articles.title: Google to Allow One-Tap Android App Installs From Approved Third-Party Stores Outside U.S.
articles.text:
Third-party Android app stores can now apply to Google for permission to install apps with one tap, without Android's usual confirmation screens, and to update them in the background.
To qualify, a store must pass identity checks and send Google its full catalog, along with every new app and update, for ongoing malware scanning. Approved stores get the features from December 1, but only on devices running Android 17 QPR2 or later in supported countries, which do not include the US.
Today, a user installing apps from a third-party store must first enable the store to install apps, then confirm each install and each update. From December 1, a store in Google's Registered App Stores program gets that permission automatically once it is approved, and its updates run in the background under the user's own update settings.
Google announced the program in March, alongside changes it said resolved its disputes with Epic Games. Joining is optional, and stores that stay out will continue to operate as they do today.
Under Google's rules, the store must still get the user's explicit consent for each install and "must not install apps silently without user consent." Large downloads and background installs must show a visible notification while they run.
If an install is started on another device, the store must show a notification that does not close automatically.
IT administrators can block registered stores from being installed on managed devices. Google's program pages do not say whether the block also applies to a store that is already installed.
Beyond the catalog scanning, Google's requirements say a store must:
- be registered as an organization and keep its developer identity verified under Android developer verification, Google's identity check for app developers
- send every version of its own app to Google for malware screening, exactly matching the version it publishes on the web and through other channels
- work to keep malware and other potentially harmful apps out of its catalog
- fix major security flaws that come to its attention
- not block other app stores from being installed, interfere with them, or hide or change Android's security notifications
- pay a $10,000 yearly fee, due before Google starts its review
Each store stays responsible and liable for everything in its catalog. Google won't moderate the content in registered stores.
If more than 1% of install attempts or more than 2% of a store's apps are found to be potentially harmful over a 30-day period, Google charges additional fees to screen and clean up the catalog.
A store that fails to meet any requirement, including paying on time, can be removed from the program until the issue is resolved. Google gives notice and a chance to fix it first.
Google's program pages do not describe how submitted apps are scanned, how quickly new uploads are checked, or what results the checks produce.
Registered stores also get a Google tool, the Android Developer ID API, to check whether each app in their catalog comes from a verified developer and can be installed. Google recommends that stores block installs of apps that fail the check.
Android developer verification is a separate Google program, now in its first phase with seven app stores. Since September 30, certified Android devices in Brazil, Indonesia, Singapore and Thailand have checked that apps from those stores come from verified developers, according to Google. Google plans to extend the checks worldwide in 2027.
Availability follows each user's home country. Short trips to unsupported countries do not turn off one-tap installs or automatic updates.
Android 17 QPR2 is one of Android's quarterly platform releases (QPRs). Its latest version, released October 16, is still a beta, and Google's release notes give no date for the final release.
In the US, a separate Google program for distributing third-party stores through Google Play has been in effect since July 22.

articles.title: Kylian Mbappé: qué pasó con el futbolista del Real Madrid, qué estudios tiene y más preguntas trend de Google
articles.text:
Kylian Mbappé volvió a ser noticia mundial, pero no por un gol ni por un título. Un comentario informal sobre un meme que usaba su rostro junto al de Mao Tse-tung desató una crisis diplomática con China, obligó a Javier Tebas a disculparse en nombre de LaLiga y terminó con el propio futbolista pidiendo perdón públicamente.
En paralelo, su nombre domina las búsquedas de Google por otros motivos: su formación académica, su lugar entre los mejores del mundo y su relación con la actriz Ester Expósito.
Qué pasó con Kylian Mbappé
Todo comenzó con una frase que Mbappé pronunció de manera casi informal. “Con el meme que más me he reído es con ese en el que usan mi cara creo que con un dictador chino. Lo utilizo mucho con mis amigos en línea”, dijo el delantero, en referencia a una imagen que suele compartir con su círculo cercano sobre Mao Tse-tung, uno de los mayores genocidas del siglo XX.
La palabra elegida por el francés, dictador, resultó ser el punto de quiebre. El régimen de Beijing considera ese término inaceptable cuando se aplica a la figura de Mao, y la respuesta no tardó en llegar.
China suspendió las emisiones de LaLiga en su territorio y ordenó a corporaciones locales cancelar los contratos millonarios que mantenían con Mbappé. El régimen de Xi Jinping instruyó además a la cadena estatal CCTV borrar al delantero de sus transmisiones y rescindir los acuerdos televisivos vigentes.
La magnitud de la respuesta encendió las alarmas en el negocio del fútbol, un ámbito que suele izar banderas en defensa de los derechos humanos. Javier Tebas, presidente de LaLiga, salió de inmediato a pedir disculpas en nombre del fútbol español. “No podemos permitir que unas declaraciones individuales empañen la relación”, afirmó el dirigente.
La postura de Tebas dejó al delantero del Real Madrid sin margen de maniobra. Mbappé terminó disculpándose a través de un comunicado: “Tengo un profundo respeto por el pueblo chino y su historia, estoy sinceramente arrepentido”, escribió.
Qué estudios tiene Kylian Mbappé
Entre las preguntas que más se repiten en los buscadores sobre el delantero del Real Madrid aparece su formación académica. Mbappé concentró su desarrollo juvenil en academias deportivas, lo que marcó el rumbo de su educación desde una edad temprana.
Su recorrido futbolístico arrancó en el AS Bondy y continuó en el INF Clairefontaine, la academia de la Federación Francesa de Fútbol dedicada a jóvenes talentos. En 2013 se incorporó al centro de formación del AS Mónaco, donde terminó de formarse antes de debutar como profesional.
En el plano escolar, Mbappé cursó la secundaria y obtuvo el Baccalauréat, el equivalente al bachillerato francés, en la especialidad de Ciencias y Tecnologías de la Gestión y Administración (STMG). El futbolista no cuenta con estudios ni títulos universitarios.
¿Es Mbappé el mejor jugador del mundo?
Otra de las búsquedas frecuentes vinculadas al atacante francés tiene que ver con su ubicación dentro de la jerarquía mundial del fútbol. Definir si Mbappé es “el mejor del mundo” responde a un criterio subjetivo que varía según cada aficionado o periodista, aunque su pertenencia a la élite absoluta del fútbol actual no admite discusión.
A fecha de octubre de 2026, varios hitos recientes respaldan ese estatus. En la edición 2026 del Balón de Oro, Mbappé terminó en el segundo lugar de las votaciones, por detrás del delantero inglés Harry Kane.
A mediados de octubre también fue distinguido por la revista francesa Onze Mondial con el premio Onze d’Or al mejor jugador de la temporada 2025-26. El reconocimiento llegó con el 48,2% de los votos de los lectores, por encima de João Neves y Khvicha Kvaratskhelia.
Quién es la pareja de Kylian Mbappé
La vida personal del futbolista también concentra buena parte del interés en los motores de búsqueda. A fecha de finales de 2026, la pareja de Kylian Mbappé es la actriz española Ester Expósito.
La relación salió a la luz a principios de este año. Ambos procuraron mantener su vínculo en privado, aunque el romance se hizo público y notorio durante el verano de Italia, especialmente después de que se los viera de vacaciones juntos en Cerdeña.
La presencia constante de Expósito en los estadios, donde acompañó a Mbappé durante el Mundial de 2026, terminó de confirmar la relación ante la opinión pública.

articles.title: Nahdet El Mahrousa and GIZ support 12 green scaleups with EGP 57.5 million
articles.text: Egypt's Nahdet El Mahrousa and Germany's GIZ have marked the graduation of 12 green businesses from the GreenShift accelerator, which provided a combined EGP 57.5 million in investment to support their growth and production capacity. The graduation took place at the GreenShift Summit in Cairo on October 27, 2026. Implemented by Nahdet El Mahrousa in partnership with GIZ, and co-funded by the European Union and the German Federal Government, the programme supports green businesses in commercialising sustainable solutions and scaling their operations. The 12 graduating businesses operate across climatetech, circular economy, recycling, sustainable materials and waste management. They include TileGreen Tech, Tilestic, Green Cycle, EGYMAG Biotechnology, Extractor Co., Mycelium, Up-Fuse, ZEE, Yadawee, Mrkoon, PLANQ Electronics and VeryNile. GreenShift received 1,353 applications, trained 46 fellows through approximately 160 hours of training and consultations, and provided EGP 1.3 million in productive assets to 18 fellows. It also supported eight of the 12 funded businesses in completing licensing and formalisation procedures. Press release: Nahdet El Mahrousa (NM), the first incubator for early-stage social enterprises in Egypt and the Middle East, hosted the GreenShift Summit on Tuesday, 27 October, bringing together more than 150 industry leaders, policymakers, investors, development partners, and entrepreneurs to explore what it takes to turn promising green businesses into scalable companies and how their growth can drive change across industries. The summit spotlighted the journeys of 12 green scaleups based in Greater Cairo and the Delta, which received acceleration support and a total of EGP 57.5 million in investment through the GreenShift Program. Implemented by Nahdet El Mahrousa in partnership with the Deutsche Gesellschaft für Internationale Zusammenarbeit (GIZ) GmbH and co-funded by the European Union and the German Federal Government, the program supports green enterprises in commercializing their solutions and scaling their impact. Emphasizing the importance of empowering startups to drive sustainable economic growth, Dr. Mona Shehab, Director of the National Solid Waste Management Programme, said: “Startups play an important role in building a stronger, more sustainable national economy by generating innovative ideas and creating new opportunities that contribute to economic growth and help advance the country’s future development plans.” At the operational level, Mostafa Ashraf, private sector advisor at GIZ, highlighted one of the key challenges these businesses face as they work to scale: access to equipment financing. “One of the biggest challenges facing these businesses is the high upfront cost of equipment. The GreenShift program helps address this challenge by financing machinery, enabling companies to continue developing their operations and improve their production processes.” The graduating scaleups operate across a range of sectors, including climate action, the circular economy, and waste management and recycling. They are: ● TileGreen Tech: Transforms hard-to-recycle plastic waste into durable building materials using patented technology. ● Tilestic: Converts single-use plastic waste into tiles, paving stones, and roof tiles. ● Green Cycle for Waste Management: Collects and processes post-consumer plastic waste into certified raw materials for local manufacturers. ● EGYMAG Biotechnology: Uses black soldier fly larvae to convert organic waste into protein, oil, and fertilizer. ● Extractor Co.: Produces essential oils through a circular process that returns plant residues to the soil. ● Mycelium: Uses mushroom-based technology to transform agricultural waste into mushrooms and plastic alternatives for packaging and construction. ● Up-Fuse: Creates everyday products by repurposing plastic and textile waste through a slow-fashion approach. ● ZEE: Produces circular footwear from discarded shoes and other waste materials. ● Yadawee: Produces and exports handmade Egyptian crafts created by local and refugee artisans. ● Mrkoon: Operates a B2B marketplace connecting businesses with verified buyers and sellers of scrap and surplus materials. ● PLANQ Electronics: Develops upgradable computers using recycled materials and repurposed laptop batteries. ● VeryNile: Works to protect the Nile through cleanup initiatives, recycling, environmental education, and community development. Islam Salah, founder of PLANQ Electronics, emphasized the program’s role in helping the company develop a viable business model around its recycling operations. “The funding mattered, but so did the expertise and guidance we received. The program gave us the confidence to pursue opportunities we might not have explored otherwise,” he added. Echoing this sentiment, Dr. Tarek Makram, founder of Extractor Co., said the funding and expert guidance he received through GreenShift helped accelerate the factory setup process. “GreenShift stood out because it offered more than advice, combining funding with training, advisory services with hands-on support.” The GreenShift Program received 1,353 applications and trained 46 fellows through approximately 160 hours of training, consultations, and a retreat. It also provided EGP 1.3 million in productive assets to 18 fellows and supported eight of the 12 funded scaleups in licensing and formalizing their businesses. Held under the theme “Rethinking Tomorrow: From Green Businesses to Changing Industries,” the one-day summit convened stakeholders from government entities, NGOs, development agencies, financial institutions, research and academia, corporations, and entrepreneurship support networks. Participants included representatives from the Ministry of Local Development and Environment, the National Solid Waste Management Programme, and the Industrial Development Authority, alongside ّGIZ, United Nations Industrial Development Organization (UNIDO), the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD), Sawiris Foundation for Social Development, Injaz Egypt, Finance in Motion, Dar Ventures, Hassan Allam Holding, Orascom Development, Flat6Labs, and AUC Venture Lab, among other ecosystem partners. The “GreenShift” summit opened with a welcome and keynote session, followed by “The GreenShift Program: What Twelve Ventures Revealed,” highlighting the experiences, achievements, and key lessons of the green scaleups supported by the program. Discussions then turned to investment readiness and growth through “Will You Invest? What Makes a Green Business Worth Backing” and “Ready to Scale. Now What?”, examining what makes green businesses commercially viable and what they need to expand. Sector-focused panels explored how sustainable materials could transform construction and how bio-based alternatives could reshape traditional agricultural practices. “Public-private partnerships are at the heart of Egypt’s sustainability agenda. The GreenShift Summit underscored the importance of cross-sector collaboration in advancing environmental, social, and governance (ESG) practices, strengthening sustainable value chains, and accelerating Egypt’s transition to a greener economy. Building on this collaborative approach, the GreenShift Program supports green enterprises at different stages of development, helping early-stage innovators commercialize their solutions while enabling growing companies to scale their impact. Together with our public- and private-sector partners, we aim to nurture the next generation of climate entrepreneurs and accelerate the adoption of sustainable solutions across industries,” said Jackie Kameel, Managing Director of Nahdet El Mahrousa.

articles.title: GPD Confirms Intel Arc G3 Extreme-Based Win Mini Ultra Handheld Coming Soon
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
GPD Confirms Intel Arc G3 Extreme-Based Win Mini Ultra Handheld Coming Soon
GPD is no stranger to powerful gaming handhelds, having previously launched the very expensive GPD Win Max 3 in August 2026, and the company has recently confirmed via a Weibo post that it is working on an Intel Arc G3 Extreme-powered version of its Win Mini gaming handheld. 
Prior versions of the GPD Win Mini were available with up to the AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 with its Radeon 890M iGPU, which put the system more or less on the same level as other popular handhelds, like the Lenovo Legion Go 2, while a Win Mini Ultra with the Intel Arc G3 Extreme CPU could perform significantly faster—about as well as an entry-level dGPU, thanks to the onboard Intel Arc B390 iGPU with 12 full Xe3 cores.The Weibo post quotes a discussion on the Handhelds United podcast about the upcoming Arc G3 handheld, referencing a leaked spec sheet for the Win Mini Ultra. The spec sheet features a traditional clamshell design typical of the Win Mini devices of yore and tips dual USB4 V2 Type-C ports, a USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A port, a microSD card slot, a 3.5 mm audio combo jack, a power button with a built-in fingerprint reader, Hall-effect triggers, and capacitive joysticks. The GPD Win Mini Ultra will also feature a glossy 9.8-inch, 120 Hz IPS display, with AdaptiveSync and AMD FreeSync with a range of 48-120 Hz and a peak brightness of 575 nits, and a built-in keyboard and touchpad. Curiously, as the podcast crew notes, the Arc G3 Extreme supports Thunderbolt 4, and the leaked spec sheet officially cites USB4 V2 instead.Unfortunately, it doesn't seem as though the display on the Win Mini Ultra will have a 2-in-1 hinge, but the handheld PC will have up to 32 GB of LPDDR5x memory and built-in Bluetooth 5.4 and Wi-Fi 6E. It will also support a replaceable M.2 2280 PCIe 5.0 ×4 SSD, and it will have a 54 Wh battery with 100 W USB PD 3.0 fast charging. 
The Weibo post reads:
GPD WIN Mini Ultra: An Unexpected Performance Beast?
The GPD WIN Mini Ultra with Intel Arc G3 Extreme Graphics is coming soon! Plus, GPD's "big move" on GPD WIN Max 3 has not been finished yet. In this issue of "Speedcast", welcome to our guests to discuss the latest exposure of GPD WIN Mini Ultra, GPD WIN Max 3!

articles.title: DuckDuckGo Privacy Pro data removal service review
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
I recommend DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle for anyone seeking to maximize their online privacy. The drawbacks are the relatively high price and that features are only compatible with the DuckDuckGo browser.
Reasons to buy
- + Robust feature set
- + Advanced VPN
- + Identity theft protection
Reasons to avoid
- - Short free trial
- - Exclusive to the DuckDuckGo browser
- - Some features are US-only
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
Staying safe online is as imperative as ever, especially since AI has inadvertently increased the volume of cyber attacks. Good online safety leans more on preventing attacks from happening in the first place than on countering them, and certain tools help you do that.
DuckDuckGo is most famous for its privacy-focused search engine and browser (we've reviewed it here), but it also provides other tools that help users surf the web without giving out their identities. These tools are offered under a single, cost-competitive Pro bundle. It's a VPN, AI tool, and data removal service all in one.
I’m reviewing the DuckDuckGo Pro bundle to help you decide if it’s worth adopting for your online security. Read on to learn what this bundle offers, its pros, cons, and how it compares to the competition.
DuckDuckGo: Plans and pricing
DuckDuckGo follows a simple pricing system, which I like - you can see all the plans by clicking here. A monthly subscription costs $19.99 and unlocks access to all Pro features. An annual subscription is discounted to $200, equivalent to $17 per month instead of the $19.99 paid on a month-to-month basis. This discount is quite small compared to what I’ve seen on rivals, but is a discount nonetheless.
The pricing varies slightly for users who live outside the U.S. For example, U.K.-based users pay 19.99 pounds monthly and 200 pounds annually. Converted to the U.S. dollar, that sums up to $27 per month and $273 annually (inclusive of value-added tax). Other countries have similar pricing variations, so you may pay more (or less) than the sticker price mentioned.
DuckDuckGo offers a 7-day free trial for its Pro plan. This is shorter than the 14 to 30-day free trials I’ve used on various online security platforms, but still provides an opportunity to test the features before deciding whether to pay.
Subscriptions can be cancelled anytime, but DuckDuckGo’s website doesn’t mention a specific money-back guarantee period. It seems that refunds can be requested, but it’ll take a lot of back and forth, which I consider a drawback.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
DuckDuckGo: Setup
Setting up DuckDuckGo Privacy Pro isn’t as straightforward as most security software bundles I’ve reviewed. You’ll need to first download the DuckDuckGo browser on your PC or smartphone (you can’t use Pro features on Chrome, Firefox, or Edge). The privacy-focused browser is the foundation of DuckDuckGo’s Pro package: it blocks ads, trackers, and cookies that pose privacy risks. The browser is free, but the Pro bundle unlocks enhanced security features, which are the focus of this review.
After paying for a Pro subscription, the first feature to take note of is the VPN. This VPN, built into the DuckDuckGo browser, routes your traffic through remote servers to prevent third-party tracking. Your location, IP address, and browsing history get hidden from third parties, like advertisers or, at worst, malicious actors.
There’s a limitation, though. DuckDuckGo’s VPN servers are concentrated in the U.S. and Europe, with few outside these locations. If you’re surfing the web from, let’s say, the Middle East, connections can get a bit slower because of the server distance. DuckDuckGo’s VPN isn’t like full-fledged VPNs that let you choose from dozens of countries.
On the bright side, DuckDuckGo’s VPN has a default kill switch, which automatically cuts off your internet connection if the VPN malfunctions, ensuring your data doesn’t leak because of a slight network mishap. I checked thoroughly, but didn’t find any button to turn off this kill switch, which is a plus in my perspective. Turning off a kill switch poses privacy risks during network lapses.
The VPN coverage can be used on five devices simultaneously. For example, you can install it on your work PC, home PC, and smartphone via the DuckDuckGo browser. Your traffic gets encrypted on all connected devices.
Another key feature offered under DuckDuckGo Pro is quite unique: identity theft restoration. If you face any incident of identity theft, you can work with an expert to mitigate the effects. For example, the expert helps identify fraudulent transactions that your card may have been used for and then files reimbursement claims with your bank. You'll also get help in fixing any credit report errors from fraudulent transactions.
There’s a catch, though: DuckDuckGo doesn’t offer identity theft restoration services directly. Rather, it has partnered with Iris, a prominent ID protection platform, to provide this service. You’ll be working with Iris’ experts if you use this service.
In this AI era, you’ll hardly find a security platform that doesn’t offer an AI-centric feature. For Pro subscribers, DuckDuckGo offers advanced chatbots (based on ChatGPT and Claude) with active privacy protection. This way, you won’t have to pay separately for the premium versions of Claude and ChatGPT, as DuckDuckGo offers access under the Pro bundle.
Overall, DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle is feature-rich and effective at maximizing online privacy. However, with plans starting at $19.99 per month, I think it’s quite pricey.
DuckDuckGo: Ease of use
DuckDuckGo is a mixed bag when it comes to ease of use. Its features are exclusive to the DuckDuckGo browser, not the more popular Chrome, Firefox, and Edge browsers.
For most people, paying for the Pro bundle means learning to use a new browser on Windows, macOS, iOS, or Android. I didn’t find it difficult to get adapted to the DuckDuckGo browser, but it took some time because the browser worked differently from the ones I was used to.
DuckDuckGo: Security and privacy
DuckDuckGo offers a very effective online privacy suite, starting with a browser that doesn’t allow cookies, trackers, or anything that keeps a trail of the sites you visit. The built-in VPN encrypts your online traffic and prevents third-party prying eyes.
Identity theft restoration is another valuable service, and so is the bonus of interacting with advanced chatbots. You’ll be a lot safer online when using DuckDuckGo’s Pro bundle.
DuckDuckGo: Support
DuckDuckGo offers decent support resources. You can start with the help page, which lists answers to frequently asked questions (FAQs). I liked the breakdown of questions people often ask about DuckDuckGo’s privacy features and the detailed answers provided.
Users who need direct help can contact DuckDuckGo’s support team via email or by filling out a support form. There’s also an option to interact with DuckDuckGo’s staff via a dedicated forum on Reddit. However, there’s no telephone or live chat support, which I consider a major drawback given the price of a DuckDuckGo Pro subscription.
DuckDuckGo: Competition
Given the many features offered under DuckDuckGo Pro, it’s hard to pinpoint an exact competitor. Instead, I’ll highlight some competitors to key DuckDuckGo Pro features.
For the private browser, Brave is a notable option. After using both, I’ll say Brave offers more privacy controls and is more advanced in general. For instance, Brave supports browser extensions just like you’ll find on Chrome, but the DuckDuckGo Browser doesn’t.
For DuckDuckGo’s VPN, I’ll say any dedicated VPN app like Surfshark and Windscribe would be a better option, with broader server locations to choose from.
However, the point of DuckDuckGo Pro is to kill multiple birds with one stone: you won’t get the best of each feature, but, overall, you’ll get a good deal.
DuckDuckGo: Final verdict
A DuckDuckGo Pro bundle maximizes your online privacy, preventing third parties from tracking your online activities. If you want to surf the web without leaking data that’ll stay on the internet for a long time, I highly recommend it. However, you’d need to be ready to switch to a new browser and pay a significant amount, which I would see as drawbacks.

articles.title: La CAF en panne ? Le site et l'application ne répondent plus ce mercredi soir
articles.text:
Le site interne de la Caisse d'allocations familiales (CAF), ainsi que l'application mobile, ne sont plus inaccessibles ce mercredi soir. Les bénéficiaires n'arrivent plus à accéder à leur compte.
À peine quelques jours après un arrêt contraint et forcé dû aux failles PHP, la CAF connaît de nouveau un empêchement informatique, pour ne pas dire une « panne ». Ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026, on nous signale que le site internet et l'application mobile de la Caisse d'allocations familiales ne sont plus accessibles. Dans le détail, c'est l'espace Mon Compte qu'il est impossible de consulter, comme Clubic a pu le consulter.
Le site de la CAF est en panne, l'application également en rade
Effectivement, il y a un gros souci du côté de la CAF. Il y a quelques jours, les opérations de maintenance liées aux failles PHP qui exposaient de nombreux sites internet étaient prévues, et une certaine communication avait été faite, même si les soucis avaient pu s'étirer au-delà de ce que certains avaient imaginé. Ce soir, c'est différent.
De nombreux signalements sont en train de remonter, d'un peu partout, pour signaler une impossibilité de se connecter à son espace. Cela concerne aussi bien l'application mobile que le site internet de la CAF. « L'application ne s'ouvre même pas, je suis bloquée sur le logo et c'est tout », explique Angèle. Un allocataire confirme qu'il est « impossible de se connecter via le site et l'application aussi », quand un autre écrivait, à 19h49, qu'il n'arrivait pas à se connecter « depuis une heure environ ».
Pour l'heure, la CAF n'a pas communiqué sur ce nouvel incident, qui pose d'autant plus problème qu'il intervient à une heure où beaucoup vont vouloir se connecter à leur compte.

articles.title: Researcher Reveals How Logic Bugs Alone Cracked Microsoft Edge in $175,000 Pwn2Own Win
articles.text:
A chain of logic flaws, with no memory corruption, can turn a malicious web page into code running on a Windows computer outside Microsoft Edge's sandbox, a security researcher has shown.
Orange Tsai of DEVCORE published the full method on October 28, five months after the chain won $175,000 at the Pwn2Own Berlin contest in May. Microsoft fixed the Edge bugs the day after the contest, so an up-to-date browser is not at risk.
A browser sandbox is the wall that keeps a web page's code inside the browser and off the rest of the computer. Breaking out of it, and then running a program, is what turns a web bug into full control of the machine.
Browser escapes like this almost always rely on memory corruption. This one used none. In his write-up, Tsai describes a chain built solely from logic errors in how Edge and Windows handle ordinary features, and he says the whole exploit is under 100 lines of code.
The result is a universal cross-site scripting (UXSS) primitive: a way to run JavaScript on any website, bypassing the content security policy meant to prevent it.
Because the attack starts from the browser's own process, it can reach sites like google.com that an ordinary web bug cannot touch. Tsai calls this a new attack surface rather than a one-off bug.
This was a competition exploit, not an attack seen in the wild. Tsai demonstrated it on stage at Pwn2Own; there is no evidence it has been used against real users, and the public CVE records list exploitation as none. One step in the chain restarts the browser, which Tsai notes is a convenience for the contest and not needed in a real attack.
The chain begins with an Edge feature for business sign-ins called a conditional access navigation throttle. Tsai found that triggering it lets the browser's own process start a new navigation that is not tied to the page that asked for it, so Edge attaches it to whichever tab is open. That mismatch is the first bug, and it produces the UXSS.
Making it run without a click took four more weaknesses. Edge checked that the request came from a trusted Microsoft site, but Tsai bypassed the check by opening the request from a second window. Edge's popup blocker should have stopped that window, but Edge carried a hardcoded list of allowed addresses, and one of them opened the popup.
The attack also required the victim to be already signed in, which the Edge auto-sign-in feature provides on its own when the user visits a Microsoft site. Lastly, the chain reads the victim's email address from a Microsoft site, assets.msn.com, which returned it to any website due to a misconfigured cross-origin setting.
Running JavaScript everywhere is still not in control of the computer. To escape the sandbox, Tsai used Edge's reading mode, Immersive Reader, which runs under a custom read:// address that Microsoft left off the list of pages barred from running scripts.
From there, the chain called an internal Edge function meant to zip up diagnostic logs and abused it to write a file with an attacker-chosen name and content anywhere on disk.
That file write is turned into code execution in two steps. The chain overwrites a configuration file that controls which websites may launch which protocol handlers, then restarts Edge so the file is read. It then launches a telnet:// link; because Windows does not ship a telnet program by default, it searches the system path for one and runs an attacker-planted copy from a folder the low-privileged user can write to.
Microsoft shipped the fix on May 15, the day after the contest, in Edge Stable version 148.0.3967.70. That release carried three Edge-specific fixes, tracked as CVE-2026-45492, CVE-2026-45494, and CVE-2026-45495. The first is recorded as a security feature bypass, and the second as a spoofing bug, both affecting Edge versions before 148.0.3967.70.
Microsoft's records rate the first two at 5.4 on a 10-point scale, a medium score that reflects a single bug in isolation, not the full chain that strings them into code execution. DEVCORE said the fix came within 24 hours of the disclosure.
Updating Edge closes this chain. Because the fix shipped in May, a browser on automatic updates has long since received it, and no separate action is needed.
Tsai built the chain by hand, over about two months, without any AI help, and frames the work as a point about where human research still matters. "The hard part is finding them, and once you find them all, chaining is the easiest part," he writes of the logic bugs. The research won the 2026 Pwnie Award for Epic Achievement.

articles.title: Amazon despidió a unos 250 empleados de su área de dispositivos tras semanas de lanzamientos
articles.text:
Amazon despidió el miércoles 28 de octubre a hasta 250 empleados de su unidad de dispositivos y servicios, la que fabrica los Kindle, las tabletas y los altavoces Echo. Los recortes llegan después de semanas de lanzamientos de productos, según informó la agencia Reuters, y la empresa los confirmó.
Una persona al tanto del asunto dijo a Reuters que los recortes afectaron a no más de 250 puestos, principalmente en desarrollo de software. Amazon no precisó el número ni las áreas.
“Tomamos la difícil decisión de eliminar un pequeño número de puestos”, afirmó un portavoz de la empresa tras la consulta de la agencia. Agregó que los despidos ayudarán a “operar con más eficiencia” y a alinear la estructura con la hoja de ruta de productos.
Como es habitual en Amazon, los trabajadores se enteraron por mensajes de texto y correos electrónicos enviados temprano. Reuters vio uno firmado por Cherie Robinson, vicepresidenta de Recursos Humanos de dispositivos y servicios, que hablaba de una “revisión a fondo de nuestra estructura”.
Un mes de anuncios de hardware
El mismo miércoles, Amazon presentó cinco dispositivos con Alexa, su asistente de voz. El Echo Time es un reloj despertador que cuesta USD 199,99 y, según la empresa, puede despertar al usuario en una fase de sueño ligero, dentro de una ventana de 10 a 60 minutos antes de la hora programada.
El Alexa Photo Frame es un marco digital con pantalla táctil de 10 pulgadas que parte de USD 199,99 y toma las fotos de Amazon Photos. Incluye 90 días de Alexa+, la versión del asistente con inteligencia artificial que Amazon ofrece con la suscripción Prime.
La línea suma un Echo Show 16, una pantalla inteligente de 16 pulgadas con Fire TV integrado, un Echo Dot rediseñado y un Echo Studio con cámara. Según The Verge, Alexa+ está disponible para todos en Estados Unidos desde febrero.
Dos semanas antes, el 8 de octubre, Amazon había presentado tres tabletas Alexa que reemplazan a la línea Fire y permiten descargar aplicaciones de Google Play. La Tablet 8 parte de USD 230, la Tablet 11 de USD 330 y la Tablet 12 Pro cuesta USD 500, según Engadget.
Las tabletas salieron a la venta el 14 de octubre en Estados Unidos, México y Canadá, y el 19 de octubre en varios países de Europa, según TechCrunch.
Engadget registró además nuevos Kindle, equipos de Ring y un Fire TV Stick 4K. Amazon no hizo un evento único, sino presentaciones escalonadas durante semanas. Panos Panay, jefe de dispositivos de Amazon, dijo a Engadget que el año pasado solo dos productos recibieron atención.
Otro recorte de Amazon en 2026
A comienzos de este mes, Amazon ya había eliminado cerca de 1.000 puestos en su división principal de comercio minorista, según Reuters.
Según un comunicado de la compañía, en enero de 2026 Amazon había despedido a 16.000 empleados corporativos en todo el mundo como parte de una reorganización interna iniciada en octubre de 2025. El plan buscaba simplificar la estructura, reducir la burocracia y acelerar la adopción de la inteligencia artificial en sus operaciones.
Esa ronda se sumó a un ajuste previo que había afectado a cerca de 14.000 puestos administrativos y de gestión, con lo cual el plan completo apuntaba a eliminar unos 30.000 empleos corporativos, equivalentes al 10% de la plantilla global. Las áreas más golpeadas fueron AWS, la unidad de computación en la nube, y Prime Video, además de Recursos Humanos y otras funciones centrales. Los recortes no alcanzaron a los trabajadores de centros logísticos ni de almacenes.
El nuevo ajuste de octubre ocurre un día antes de que la compañía publique sus resultados del tercer trimestre, tras el cierre de la bolsa del jueves 29 de octubre.

articles.title: TikTok USDS eyes 4 gigawatts of new power for advanced AI models
articles.text:
TikTok is on the hunt for a huge compute capacity upgrade — so is it replacing Oracle, or just exploring its options?
TikTok explores massive 4GW computing expansion for 2030s AI push
- TikTok could require 4 gigawatts of computing capacity by the early 2030s
- Oracle remains TikTok's primary American cloud provider despite expansion plans
- TikTok's growing AI ambitions could increase demand for computing infrastructure
A potential requirement for 4 gigawatts of computing power has prompted TikTok's American business to investigate additional infrastructure arrangements beyond its current resources.
The company has reportedly contacted potential suppliers about future capacity, although its existing partnership with Oracle remains central to American operations.
TikTok has denied any suggestion of an impending replacement, maintaining that its principal cloud services remain the same.
A massive computing requirement raises supplier questions
“Oracle will continue to be our primary cloud infrastructure provider,” said a TikTok spokesperson.
However, the company did not disclose whether it intends to obtain the additional computing capacity from other providers.
The proposed expansion concerns computing resources that TikTok might need during the early 2030s, rather than capacity already secured through contractual agreements.
According to CNBC, two sources familiar with TikTok's infrastructure discussions confirmed that the company was exploring opportunities to secure additional computing capacity.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
One source estimated that TikTok could require approximately 4 gigawatts by the early 2030s, although potential suppliers and agreements remain undisclosed.
The reported scale comes amid increasing demand for electricity and computing equipment as companies develop more resource-intensive artificial intelligence systems.
TikTok's American business already depends heavily on Oracle, whose cloud operations generally use data center buildings leased from third parties.
That arrangement allows Oracle to provide computing services without necessarily owning the physical facilities containing the servers and supporting electrical equipment.
Machine learning ambitions add another dimension
Beyond operating its social media platform, TikTok is recruiting specialists to develop artificial intelligence applications that could require additional processing infrastructure.
Several vacancies advertised by its American organization concern machine learning, while another describes work involving sophisticated AI models and automated content creation.
The latter position concerns a commercial AI offering designed for business customers, involving model inference and software capable of generating creative material.
These recruitment activities establish ongoing technical development, although the company has not connected individual projects to its reported multigigawatt infrastructure requirement.
TikTok's American operations also face specific computing responsibilities arising from changes to the platform's ownership and handling of domestic user information.
Established in 2026, TikTok USDS Joint Venture followed an executive order from President Donald Trump requiring changes to ByteDance's American ownership arrangements.
ByteDance retained 19.9% of the resulting enterprise, while Oracle, Silver Lake and MGX became managing investors with individual ownership stakes of 15%.
Additional financial backing came from Michael Dell's family investment office, which joined the ownership arrangement following the restructuring of TikTok's American business.
In January, the company announced that its recommendation algorithm would undergo domestic training and evaluation using information collected from users in America.
Oracle was designated to host the algorithm within its American cloud infrastructure, giving the provider an established role in handling TikTok's recommendation technology.
The company has not specified whether its potential 4-gigawatt expansion would support these algorithmic operations, commercial AI development, or other computing requirements.

articles.title: Oman's Phaze Ventures launches two AI funds targeting over $75 million
articles.text: Oman-based Phaze Ventures has launched two venture capital funds targeting more than $75 million combined, securing over $40 million in investor commitments to date. The funds will invest in artificial intelligence and deeptech startups in Oman and international markets. Phaze Ventures Fund II is anchored by ITHCA Group, a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority, as well as Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation. The second vehicle, Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, is backed by Future Fund Oman and will focus on domestic AI-enabled businesses. Founded in 2018 by Abdullah Al Shaksy, Mohammed Al Wahaibi and Masoud Al Rawahi, Phaze Ventures invests in early-stage AI and deeptech companies, with a focus on the GCC and North America. The firm has offices or team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh. The two funds have made 10 investments, including Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal. Phaze Ventures manages capital for more than 50 investors, including sovereign entities, corporations and family offices across the Gulf and other markets. Press release: Oman-headquartered Phaze Ventures announced the launch of two new venture funds targeting over $75 million. Phaze Ventures Fund II, anchored by ITHCA Group (a subsidiary of Oman Investment Authority), Ominvest and Oman LNG Development Foundation, continues the firm’s global AI and deeptech investment mandate, while Phaze Ventures Oman Fund, anchored by Future Fund Oman, establishes a dedicated capital pool for homegrown AI-enabled businesses. Together, the two-fund venture platform has secured over $40 million in investor commitments, with ongoing discussions to grow the funds to $75 million. The announcement comes as Oman builds the International Financial Centre of Oman, a new hub for international companies and investors. “AI is the most disruptive technology shift of our generation. Oman and the Gulf can’t afford to be spectators, and our participation can’t be limited to playing catch-up through investments in hyperscalers, data centres and public market offerings. We need to invest in the founders disrupting industries at home and across the globe, and we need to be a part of that disruption early,” said Abdullah Al Shaksy, Co-founder and CEO of Phaze Ventures. The new funds’ first 10 investments include Arabic.AI, Sully.ai, Andromeda Surgical, Boardy.ai and Metal, with co-investors including a16z, 8VC, Standard Capital, Y Combinator and Baidu Ventures. “We back founders who combine domain expertise with strong engineering and learn from every real-world deployment,” said Masoud Al Rawahi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures. Nour Al Hassan, Founder and CEO of Arabic.AI, said: “Getting to know the Phaze Ventures team convinced me they were the right partners. They shared our ambition to build AI our region can own and our long-term commitment to make it happen.” Arabic.AI develops Arabic-language enterprise AI, supported by investment from Saudi Arabia’s HUMAIN and a partnership with Qualcomm Technologies. Ahmed Omar, Co-founder and CEO of Sully.ai, said: “Phaze Ventures understood early how Sully could leverage AI to bring more capacity and real returns to the global healthcare system. They backed us every step of the way as we scaled globally, and were able to connect us with healthcare providers who could put our product to work.” NVIDIA highlighted Sully.ai in a case study showing a 90% reduction in inference costs and a 65% improvement in response times for medical workflows. That early conviction extends to Andromeda Surgical, which Phaze Ventures backed before its US$15 million Series A led by Standard Capital. Nick Damiano, Co-founder and CEO of Andromeda Surgical, said: “Phaze Ventures didn’t shy away from a frontier problem like building the autonomous AI-guided future of robotic surgery. They recognised our team’s rare combination of medical and autonomy expertise, backed us early, and have been proactive in opening doors through their regional network.” The new fund platform has backed players in the capital markets ecosystem, including Metal and Boardy.ai. Phaze Ventures invested in Metal’s seed round alongside Y Combinator and a16z. Metal’s AI fundraising platform helps hundreds of founders manage their capital raise uses AI to connect founders with investors, customers and talent. Usman Gul, Founder and CEO of Metal, said: “In today’s venture landscape, slow capital is expensive. I’ve raised from some of the world’s leading venture firms, and Phaze Ventures brings the same speed and foresight. They moved quickly to back us early and became committed partners as we rapidly scaled Metal’s AI-driven operating system for founders raising venture rounds.” A two-time founder, Usman previously raised US$120 million from investors including First Round Capital and 20VC. With team members in Muscat, Dubai and Riyadh, Phaze Ventures manages capital for over 50 investors, including sovereign entities, listed companies, corporates, family offices and business families across Oman, Saudi Arabia, Bahrain, India and beyond. “Investors across Oman and the Gulf want a stake in the next generation of AI companies while they are still taking shape. This platform is our answer” said Mohammed Al Wahaibi, Co-founder and Partner at Phaze Ventures.

articles.title: G.SKILL and Newegg Offer Limited-Time AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D Combo Deals Featuring AMD EXPO ULL DDR5 Memory
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
G.SKILL and Newegg Offer Limited-Time AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D Combo Deals Featuring AMD EXPO ULL DDR5 Memory
G.SKILL, a leading manufacturer of high-performance memory and PC gaming peripherals, is teaming up with Newegg to offer a series of limited-time PC hardware combo deals, featuring the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor, G.SKILL Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5 memory, and select AMD AM5 motherboards. These specially priced bundles offer PC enthusiasts and gamers an opportunity to build or upgrade their systems with high-performance components while enjoying additional combo savings.
The promotion features eight different hardware combinations, pairing the AMD Ryzen 7 9800X3D processor with a 32 GB (2x 16 GB) G.SKILL Trident Z5 NeoX RGB DDR5-6000 memory kit and a choice of motherboards from ASUS, MSI, GIGABYTE, and ASRock. articles.title: PHP2Shell Attack Roots 25 Servers, Breaches U.S. Government-Affiliated Network
articles.text:
Cybersecurity researchers have disclosed details of what appears to be an artificial intelligence (AI)-assisted attack orchestrated by a suspected China-nexus threat actor that has leveraged the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities to breach exposed systems.
The activity, which was observed on October 25, 2026, involved an attacker combining PHP2Shell with a kernel privilege escalation exploit to root 25 servers, including three systems in a U.S. government-affiliated environment.
"The affected devices run specific versions of a large vendor's firewall software," cybersecurity firm Dream said. "The attacker then launched attacks against Active Directory. The recovered artifacts confirm credential extraction and directory enumeration."
The name of the affected vendor was not disclosed, but the Israeli company said it notified the entity. The attack chain essentially brings together two sets of vulnerabilities impacting PHP and the Linux kernel -
- PHP2Shell, a pair of flaws tracked as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 (CVSS scores: 9.2) that could result in unauthenticated remote code execution
- Fragnesia, a Linux kernel local privilege escalation vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-46300 (CVSS score: 7.8)
"The implementation we recovered is a custom, non-public build, not a copy of any known public exploit for PHP2Shell," Dream researchers explained. "It follows the same underlying concept but appears to have been independently developed and tailored specifically for the targeted firewall platform."
"The vulnerability targets PHP's session.upload_progress mechanism on the firewall's appweb management server. The firewall OS uses PHP 8.0.30 with a high memory limit that enables the memory corruption stages of the attack."
The custom weaponization of the PHP2Shell exploit chain, coupled with CVE-2026-46300, is said to have rooted 25 servers across the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea.
Artifacts discovered by Dream indicate that the operation started with exploit development in a lab environment before obtaining persistent access to a U.S. government organization's internal Active Directory domain.
"Once rooted, the attacker zeroed in on three specific servers in a U.S. government-affiliated environment," the company noted.
The links to AI-assisted tooling stem from evidence pointing to the installation of Anthropic's Claude Code in the attack infrastructure, along with the presence of API keys for FOFA and an AI-powered offensive security platform called aiscan configured with large language models (LLMs) from DeepSeek and Kimi.
What's more, the code structure, commenting style, and consistency across nearly 40 scripts suggest the use of AI to augment the development process. The entire operation, per Dream, unfolds as follows -
- Attacker uses FOFA to identify approximately 19,000 internet-facing firewalls with exposed management interfaces worldwide.
- A custom version scanner is executed to determine which among those devices are online and what operating system version they are running. About 5,000 devices respond with the version information.
- The attacker filters the servers to those located in the U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea, and then limits the scope to systems that match newer release branches running PHP 8.0.30. This step yields 240 targets.
- The target list is fed as input to an automated batch runner that exploits the PHP2Shell-Fragnesia chain, plants a PHP web shell on a publicly accessible directory on the firewall, verifies root access, and logs the target's hostname and IP to a CSV file. This step allows the attacker to gain root access to 24 servers.
- Two of the successfully compromised systems are identified as belonging to a U.S. government-affiliated organization. One of them crashes shortly after it was rooted on October 23, 2026, at 6:14 p.m. UTC and never comes back online. The attacker carries out a dedicated campaign to successfully root a second system on October 24, 2026, at 10:09 a.m. UTC.
- The attacker exploits the second system to build a persistent channel into the internal network via a reverse SSH tunnel connecting the compromised firewall back to the operator's infrastructure. At 11:35 a.m. UTC, a third government server is compromised using the same method, the only difference being that this was an internal firewall management server only reachable through the tunnel. The total number of rooted servers reaches 25.
- The attacker targets Active Directory to decrypt the LDAP service account password, enumerate users, and spray passwords against every user account using organization-themed passwords in an attempt to extract credentials. The operation also attempts to create backdoor Active Directory accounts.
It's unclear if the activity allowed the threat actor to successfully find valid credentials or create backdoor accounts. As a result, the full extent of the compromise remains indeterminate.
"Since [the] U.S., Japan, Taiwan, and South Korea are the four primary strategic adversaries and intelligence targets for Chinese state-aligned cyber operations in the Pacific theater, this indicates potential nation-state adversary efforts," Dream said.
"The operation illustrates how an exposed management interface can become a path into an organization's identity infrastructure. The 22 other rooted firewalls remain parked with active web shells. The persistent tunnel into the US government organization is likely still running. And the attacker still has 19,000 fingerprinted targets they can revisit as they develop profiles for additional OS versions."
The disclosure comes as the PHP2Shell vulnerabilities have witnessed only limited exploitation in the wild, with threat actors highlighting the challenges in converting a proof-of-concept (PoC) into a reliable attack vector against real targets despite integrating them into their campaigns.
"In practice it's unexploitable crap. To exploit real targets you need the offsets from libphp.so, which are unique to every build and impossible to brute-force. You can reproduce it on your own test bench, or if you already have access to the target's file system," a member who goes by the handle c0d3x on the XSS forum said, according to Flare.

articles.title: Écran OLED, Dynamic Island et châssis affiné... mais puces M5 Pro / Max : Apple dévoile son premier MacBook Pro tactile
articles.text:
Après des années de fuites éparses, de rumeurs incessantes et de spéculations à tout va, Apple présente enfin son tout premier MacBook Pro à écran tactile. L’appareil s’appuie, comme prévu, sur un châssis affiné et passe à la technologie d’affichage OLED. Voici ce qu’il faut retenir de ce nouveau produit.
On savait que ces 27 et 28 octobre 2026 seraient chargés en matière de nouveaux Mac, ils le sont effectivement. Après avoir dévoilé hier ses iMac M6 et MacBook Pro M6, aux designs inchangés, Apple dégaine aujourd’hui un tout nouveau MacBook Pro qui fera date : il est en effet le premier à intégrer un écran OLED tactile. Une particularité à laquelle le géant de Cupertino s’était jusqu’à présent refusé, et qui propulse donc, pour la première fois, macOS dans l’univers de la commande du bout des doigts.
Un MacBook Pro OLED plus léger, avec Dynamic Island et logo lumineux… Mais sans nouveauté côté puces
La grosse nouveauté de ce nouveau modèle est donc l’écran choisi par Apple : une dalle tandem-OLED (avec deux couches de pixels auto-émissifs) de 14,2 ou 16,3 pouces, avec prise en charge des commandes tactiles et jusqu’à 2000 cd/m2 de luminosité maximale en SDR.
Fidèle à ses habitudes en la matière, Apple donne à cet écran, qui s’annonce d’ores et déjà comme l’un des plus beaux du marché, une dénomination marketing bien particulière : PROLED XDR. Cette dalle organique promet quoi qu’il en soit d’afficher jusqu’à 10 000 000:1 de taux de contraste tout en délivrant une gamme de couleurs toujours plus riche, couvrant cette fois aussi bien le gamut DCI-P3 que le spectre Adobe RGB (ou l’espace de couleurs Rec. 2020, qui sera pour sa part géré à plus de 80 %)… et ce, tout en continuant d’offrir la technologie de rafraîchissement dynamique ProMotion de manière à osciller entre 10 et 120 Hz en fonction des contenus affichés.
Apple annonce aussi exploiter, sur cet écran PROLED XDR, un moteur d’affichage capable de gérer indépendamment chaque pixel, en tenant compte de l’usure, de la température et du contenu. On apprend aussi que des préréglages de référence seront au menu pour le cinéma, la photo et même l’imagerie médicale, tandis que le traitement nano-texturé de l’écran restera proposé en option, mais avec une nouveauté : la nano-texture étant désormais gravée directement dans le verre.
Fonction tactile oblige, Apple explique enfin avoir revu la charnière de son nouveau MacBook Pro pour la rendre moins souple afin d’éviter au maximum les vibrations lorsque l’on interagira de manière tactile avec l’appareil. La firme indique par ailleurs avoir travaillé à une réduction de la latence pour permettre des commandes tactiles extrêmement réactives.
Autre petit détail qui tend à prouver qu’Apple a soigné sa copie, on apprend que la webcam 12 Mpx de l’appareil (désormais logée dans une Dynamic Island et non plus dans une encoche) dispose d’une stabilisation vidéo pour que l’image ne tremble pas quand on touche l’écran durant une visioconférence.
Quant à macOS, il a été calibré pour convertir automatiquement les touchers en clics, avec de nouvelles animations et de nouvelles API proposées aux développeurs pour exploiter toujours mieux ces nouvelles commandes tactiles / gestuelles.
Lancement le 6 novembre prochain, à partir de 3299 euros
Côté design, il y a bien de la nouveauté aussi, mais elle saute un peu moins aux yeux. On retrouve globalement les lignes des précédentes générations de MacBook Pro Apple Silicon, mais avec un châssis légèrement affiné et allégé.
Apple évoque notamment un châssis plus léger : 1,38 kg pour le modèle de 14 pouces et 1,82 kg pour celui de 16 pouces. Pour le formuler autrement, comptez 230 grammes de moins pour nouveau MacBook OLED de 14 pouces et 320 grammes en moins pour son grand frère par rapport à la génération précédente. Quant à leur châssis, il s’amincit de 0,5 mm en 14 pouces et 1 mm en 16 pouces grâce à la finesse induite par la technologie OLED, qui permet aussi de basculer sur des bordures d’écran plus fines. Les deux moutures du MacBook Pro PROLED XDR resteront par contre proposées en noir sidéral et en argent.
Autre nouveauté, le retour d’un logo Apple illuminé sur le capot. La marque a toutefois peu communiqué là-dessus à ce stade, on ignore donc si ce rétroéclairage sera visible uniquement au démarrage (en même temps que le son de lancement de macOS), ou s’il sera persistant, à l’instar de ce que proposaient les MacBook d’il y a une bonne quinzaine d’années.
On notera enfin qu’Apple ne mise pas sur de nouvelles connectiques pour ses MacBook Pro PROLED XDR, qui conservent en l’occurrence trois ports Thunderbolt 5, une sortie HDMI, un port d’alimentation MagSafe 3, un lecteur SDXC et une prise casque.
Comme cela avait été pressenti, le géant californien s’en tient par ailleurs aux puces M5 Pro et M5 Max que l’on connaît depuis le début d’année. Ces nouveaux MacBook Pro ne passent donc pas une génération, ce qui laisse même à penser que les puces M6 Pro et M6 Max sont encore loin d’être prêtes… Et qu’Apple n’a pas souhaité les attendre pour dégainer ses nouveaux MacBook Pro à écran OLED tactile.
On retrouve quoi qu’il en soit une puce M5 Pro pouvant embarquer jusqu’à 18 cœurs CPU, 20 cœurs GPU et 64 Go de mémoire unifiée ; ou un processeur M5 Max combinant cette fois 18 cœurs CPU et jusqu’à 40 cœurs GPU pour un maximum de 128 Go de mémoire unifiée. Apple positionne d’ailleurs clairement cette version 128 Go comme une solution faite pour la gestion locale de très grands modèles de langage. Une manière de faire un joli pied de nez à NVIDIA et ses premières machines RTX Spark… qui ne tiennent pas toutes leurs promesses.
Apple explique enfin avoir doublé les vitesses de ses SSD pour permettre d’accroître encore un peu plus la réactivité du système et doper les transferts de fichiers en grands volumes. Les pros apprécieront. Pour le reste, ces nouveaux Mac sont censés tenir jusqu’à 24 heures sur batterie, se recharger à 50 % en 30 minutes et intégrer de nouveaux haut-parleurs offrant des graves plus profonds. Nous avons hâte de tester tout ça sur Clubic.
Reste le prix de ces nouveaux modèles. Il fait mal, comme on pouvait s’y attendre : 3299 euros en prix de départ pour le modèle de 14 pouces et 3899 euros pour la version de base du modèle de 16 pouces. Comptez d’ailleurs plus de 16 000 euros si vous voulez mettre la main sur le MacBook Pro 16 PROLED XDR le mieux équipé (M5 Max 40 cœurs GPU, 128 Go de RAM et 16 To de SSD). Les deux moutures de l’appareil sont quoi qu’il en soit attendues sur le marché français le 6 novembre prochain.
Source : Communiqué de presse Apple

articles.title: Chrome podrá buscar en Gmail números de vuelo, pedidos y direcciones para llenar formularios
articles.text:
Google anunció el miércoles 28 de octubre una versión avanzada del autocompletado de Chrome que busca en el correo de Gmail del usuario los datos necesarios para llenar formularios en línea, según informó el sitio tecnológico TechCrunch. La función se despliega en Estados Unidos, en computadoras y en las aplicaciones de Gemini en Chrome para iOS y Android.
Hasta ahora, el autocompletado del navegador solo usaba la información guardada en Chrome, como direcciones o tarjetas. La nueva versión puede sugerir datos que están en los mensajes recibidos: un número de confirmación de vuelo, un número de socio, un código de seguimiento de un envío, un número de pedido, una dirección, un teléfono o una tarjeta de crédito.
La función amplía Personal Intelligence, el sistema de Google que conecta sus aplicaciones con el asistente Gemini para recuperar datos y responder preguntas complejas. Cada usuario decide si activa el autocompletado mejorado desde los ajustes de Chrome; Google asegura que los datos sensibles se cifran.
En enero, Google había anticipado en su blog que llevaría Personal Intelligence a Chrome “en los próximos meses”, con la posibilidad de conectar y desconectar las aplicaciones en cualquier momento. Según el sitio especializado Android Authority, ese sistema pasó a la versión gratuita de Gemini en marzo, después de haber sido un beneficio exclusivo para suscriptores de pago.
La función en pruebas
La función ya se había visto en julio dentro de Chrome Canary, la versión experimental del navegador, con el nombre “Find and Fill with Gemini”. Windows Report y Android Authority informaron el 20 de julio que se activaba desde Autocompletar y contraseñas, en el apartado de autocompletado mejorado.
En esa versión de prueba, el usuario podía invocarla escribiendo “@@” en un campo de texto o con un clic derecho y la opción “Buscar y completar desde cualquier lugar”. También podía definir otro atajo y elegir qué aplicaciones conectaba. Además de Gmail, la prueba incluía datos de Google Fotos.
Esos detalles corresponden a la versión Canary. TechCrunch no precisó si el lanzamiento de esta semana mantiene el atajo “@@” ni si incluye Fotos, y no cita un comunicado de Google con esos puntos.
Qué datos recibe Google
Android Authority recogió que Google reconoce que los títulos y las direcciones web de las páginas donde se usa la función “se envían a Google y pueden ser revisados por personas”. Ese punto aparece en la documentación de la versión de prueba.
La información que Gemini inserta en el formulario no es visible para nadie ni se usa para entrenar modelos de inteligencia artificial. Windows Report añadió que Chrome registra si el usuario acepta, edita o descarta cada sugerencia para mejorar la experiencia.
Android Police, que cubrió la prueba en julio, señaló que ese envío de títulos y direcciones era el aspecto más delicado de la función. Para desactivarla, el usuario debe entrar en los ajustes de Chrome, abrir Autocompletar y contraseñas, elegir autocompletado mejorado y apagar el interruptor.
TechCrunch relacionó la novedad con una función de Apple que muestra sobre el teclado los códigos de verificación recibidos por mensaje de texto. A su juicio, aunque parezca menor, puede dar a los usuarios otra razón para seguir en el navegador de Google y en su ecosistema de inteligencia artificial.
Otras novedades en Chrome
Google incorporó en Chrome una advertencia específica para sitios “sospechosos”, distinta de la alerta roja destinada a páginas identificadas como “peligrosas”, con el objetivo de ampliar la detección de riesgos sin bloquear de forma automática sitios sobre los que existe menor certeza.
La función, disponible por ahora para quienes activaron la Protección Reforzada, se complementa con mejoras en Gemini para detectar estafas de soporte técnico, falsos antivirus y supuestas actualizaciones del navegador. Además, el navegador sumó defensas contra las estafas ClickFix, que inducen a copiar comandos maliciosos en el equipo, y envía esos textos —sin datos personales— a Safe Browsing para su evaluación.

articles.title: Egyptian climatetech NoorNation secures $1.05 million seed funding
articles.text: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, backed by agribusiness group Linah Farms, along with climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses and underserved communities. Its flagship product, LifeBox, provides solar-powered electricity and water solutions for off-grid operations. Linah Farms' investment follows projects involving solar-powered irrigation at its agricultural operations, renewable energy systems at its agricultural school and a solar installation at its Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. The investment comes as NoorNation develops pay-per-use solar irrigation solutions for Egyptian farmers, aiming to reduce reliance on diesel-powered pumping systems. Press release: Egypt-based climatetech startup NoorNation has closed a $1.05 million seed funding round, with agricultural group Linah Farms joining its shareholder base after deploying the startup's renewable energy solutions across several of its operations. The round saw participation from climate tech investor Catalyst Fund and Saudi firm KBW Ventures. The investment marks a shift in the relationship between the two companies, with Linah Farms moving from a commercial customer to an investor following projects involving solar-powered agricultural irrigation, an agricultural school and a hotel in Sharm El Sheikh. Founded in 2021 by Ragy Ramadan and Mohamed Khaled, NoorNation develops decentralised clean energy and water infrastructure for agricultural businesses, rural communities and other off-grid users in Egypt and Sub-Saharan Africa. Its flagship product, LifeBox, is a self-contained, solar-powered system designed to provide electricity and water for irrigation, desalination and other applications in areas with limited access to conventional infrastructure. The company has previously attracted investment from KBW Ventures , the investment firm founded by Saudi Prince Khaled bin Alwaleed, which backed NoorNation in 2024 for an undisclosed amount. From customer to investor NoorNation and Linah Farms have worked together on several renewable energy projects, including solar irrigation systems at agricultural operations in Egypt's Bahariya Oasis, a solar-and-battery installation at Linah's agricultural school and a solar power system at Sultan Gardens Resort in Sharm El Sheikh. According to NoorNation founder Ragy Ramadan, the solar-powered irrigation system at Linah Farms' Bahariya Oasis operations has generated more than EGP 3 million in diesel savings, while the installation at Sultan Gardens Resort has reduced electricity costs by more than EGP 2.2 million. The companies have also announced an agreement covering five additional solar installations with a combined capacity of approximately 1.13 MWp across the Bahariya Oasis and West Minya. The projects include solar irrigation systems and a hybrid power station. The agreement brings the combined capacity of projects delivered and under implementation for Linah Group to approximately 1.71 MWp, according to NoorNation. Expanding solar-powered irrigation The funding comes as NoorNation develops a pay-per-use solar irrigation model aimed at farmers who continue to rely on diesel-powered water pumps. Linah Farms is also expected to support financing for this model, extending the partnership beyond its existing energy installations. The approach seeks to make solar-powered irrigation more accessible to agricultural businesses while reducing their exposure to fuel costs. NoorNation's latest investment adds to growing interest in decentralised clean energy solutions for Egypt's agricultural sector, where access to affordable power and water remains a challenge for farms operating outside established infrastructure networks.

articles.title: The touchscreen MacBook Pro uses a 'Tandem OLED' panel — so why is its 'PROLED XDR' display different to the iPad Pro's 'Ultra Retina XDR' Tandem OLED panel? Let's dig into the specs
articles.text:
What's the tech inside the touchscreen MacBook Pro's 'PROLED XDR' screen? Here's why the 'tandem' OLED panel is important
The first OLED MacBook Pro screen has a weird name — here's what's behind it
Apple has unveiled its first OLED MacBook Pro laptops, and that means we've got a new bit of display branding: PROLED XDR. You can have the laptop in 14-inch or 16-inch variants, pre-orders are open now for shipping on or after the 6th of November — and we've gone hands-on with them. Literally, because they're also the first touchscreen Macs.
The name 'PROLED XDR' is a new piece of jargon that Apple's debuting with this machine. So what actually is it?
The short answer is that it's a 'Tandem OLED' panel, which means that it uses multiple layers of organic light-emitting diodes — in this case, two layers. Two OLED layers are better than one because the result is considerably brighter than a single-layer OLED: you literally have two OLEDs firing per pixel. It also boosts longevity, because each of the two layers doesn't have to work as hard, so they have a longer lifespan and are more likely to avoid burn-in.
Apple has stayed away from OLED for its MacBook Pro displays in the past, and clearly that's changed. According to Apple that's because PROLED XDR "finally" overcomes the traditional limitations of OLED: low and variable brightness, off-axis color shift and the risk of burn-in from displaying the same interface elements, such as toolbars and palettes, whenever the screen is on.
The confusing thing, however, is that this isn't Apple's first use of Tandem OLED. It used the technology in its shift to OLED in the iPad Pro, but those aren't branded as PROLED XDR. Those are called 'Ultra Retina XDR' displays.
So let's look at the performance differences listed by Apple that put the 'pro' in PROLED.
What's so special about PROLED XDR displays
The Tandem OLED inside the new MacBook Pros is very bright, delivering up to 2,000 nits of peak HDR brightness (ie, in a small area of the screen for a short time) and up to 1,000 nits of sustained fullscreen brightness (ie, across the entire screen at once, without having to dim quickly).
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The iPad Pro (2025)'s display is also capable of 1,000 nits of fullscreen brightness, but has a rated peak brightness of 1,600 nits — so the MacBook Pro is 25% brighter. That will bring a nice extra boost to clarity in bright HDR scenes, but won't make a huge difference really — the fullscreen brightness is the most important factor, and that's the same on both.
Because it's OLED, it gives you the blackest of black tones — there's no backlight to leak light into areas it shouldn't go — and a very high contrast ratio, in this case 10,000,000:1. That again is an interesting difference from the iPad Pro, which has a claimed contrast ratio of 2,000,000:1.
Why a 5x difference if the brightness is only 25% different? Apple hasn't explicitly said, but it must come down the lowest level of brightness that can be measured on the screen. Doing the math on the iPad's 1,600-nit display with a 2,000,000:1 ratio gives us a lowest brightness of 0.0008 nits. On the PROLED XDR's display, a 2,000-nit panel with a 10,000,000 contrast ratio gives us a lowest brightness of 0.0002 nits.
We can assume this is down to the new panel design, aimed at "minimizing internal reflections common in traditional OLED designs" — so less light is reflected within the panel itself, which could be the difference between those two different black levels.
But if you're looking at 0.0008 nits and 0.0002 nits and thinking the difference must be indistinguishable, then… yes, correct. They will both appear totally black to the human eye when they're supposed to. But it produces a big difference in contrast ratio, because multiplication is overdramatic.
There are other indications that the MacBook Pro's PROLED XDR display might beat the iPad Pro's in other areas. Apple says it can achieve over 80% of the BT.2020 color gamut, which suggest it's likely to hit close to 100% of the DCI-P3 color gamut — the iPad Pro was measured by our lab at around 82% of DCI-P3, so that would be a clear jump here.
The screen is powered by a display engine that's been built into the M5 Pro and M5 Max chips, which Apple says "continuously compensates each pixel for content, usage, temperature, and ambient conditions".
Refresh rates are variable from 10Hz to 120Hz (with discrete options for film-makers: 47.95Hz, 48Hz, 50Hz, and 59.94Hz), and as we've seen with other Apple products there's a nano-texture glass option for people who'll be working in overly bright environments.
The big selling point here is reference monitor accuracy that you can take wherever you go, making these MacBook Pros ideal for video pros and mobile creatives of all kinds.
So do you need it? If you're making the next Wildwood — go see this movie, it's incredible — or working with high-res, high-quality video then these are by far the best Mac mobile laptops that Apple has ever made. But I suspect most of them will end up with people who aren't video pros, but who really like really good displays. I'd love to see Cyberpunk 2077 on one of these.
If you're technically minded Apple has put together a full technical paper on the new displays, and you can read it right here.

Contributor
Writer, broadcaster, musician and kitchen gadget obsessive Carrie Marshall has been writing about tech since 1998, contributing sage advice and odd opinions to all kinds of magazines and websites as well as writing more than twenty books. Her latest, a love letter to music titled Small Town Joy, is on sale now. She is the singer in spectacularly obscure Glaswegian rock band Unquiet Mind.
