articles.title: Instagram monetizará videos largos: “exploramos opciones para que los creadores reciban pago”, afirma director de la app
articles.text:
Adam Mosseri, director de Instagram, reaccionó a los videos de larga duración que la plataforma comenzó a probar y afirmó que exploran opciones de pago para quienes produzcan ese tipo de contenidos.
“Entendemos que la economía es muy importante, y estamos explorando múltiples opciones para ayudar a los creadores de videos de formato largo a recibir pago”, señaló en Threads.
La iniciativa se vincula con Features, la nueva función con la que Instagram permitirá publicar videos horizontales de hasta 90 minutos.
Por ahora, la herramienta está en fase de prueba y solo está disponible para un grupo de creadores de contenido en Estados Unidos. Mosseri advirtió que el despliegue será gradual. “Esto va a tomar tiempo para que esté bien, pero estamos emocionados y comprometidos”, explicó.
Además, indicó que las características todavía no fueron lanzadas por completo y que la compañía amplía lentamente el acceso mientras recopila comentarios.
Cómo funciona el nuevo formato de video en Instagram
Features está diseñada para que los usuarios puedan pasar de clips breves a contenidos extensos sin salir de Instagram.
Los Reels funcionarán como adelantos: si un creador vincula un video corto con una producción completa, quienes encuentren ese fragmento podrán pulsarlo y continuar la reproducción.
El formato apunta a contenidos como entrevistas, episodios de pódcast y videopodcast, que requieren más tiempo de reproducción.
Hasta ahora, muchos creadores usaban Instagram para compartir extractos y dirigir a su audiencia hacia otras plataformas para ver el material completo.
La prueba inicial se desarrolla en dispositivos móviles. Según la información difundida sobre la función, Instagram prevé llevar posteriormente la experiencia a pantallas grandes mediante una aplicación para televisores, aunque todavía no informó una fecha ni los dispositivos compatibles.
Cómo reaccionaron los usuarios al nuevo formato de video de Instagram
Los usuarios reaccionaron con reservas al nuevo formato de videos largos de hasta 90 minutos que Instagram comenzó a probar. Algunos cuestionaron que la plataforma se aleje de su función original como red social para compartir fotografías entre amigos.
“¿No podemos recuperar el viejo Instagram, cuando era una aplicación para compartir fotos con amigos? ¿Y cuando mis amigos realmente veían mis publicaciones?”, escribió uno de los usuarios en respuesta a la novedad.
Otros señalaron que Instagram debería priorizar la monetización de quienes ya producen contenido breve. “Con todo respeto, si no van a monetizar como YouTube, deberían seguir siendo una plataforma de formato corto, porque eso es lo que hacen bien”, comentó un usuario.
La posibilidad de que Instagram explore formas de pago para los creadores de videos largos también generó críticas. “¿Qué tal si primero les pagan a los creadores de formato corto?”, planteó otro usuario.
Qué otras nuevas funciones hay en Instagram
Además de Features, Instagram ha incorporado herramientas para modificar la experiencia de consumo y creación de contenidos.
Una de ellas es Your Algorithm, que permite revisar y ajustar los temas que la plataforma utiliza para recomendar publicaciones en el feed, Reels y Explorar. La función ofrece mayor control sobre los intereses que influyen en las sugerencias.
Para los creadores, Instagram reforzó Edits, su aplicación de edición similar a CapCut, con opciones para crear carruseles, organizar proyectos y aplicar efectos. También sumó herramientas para reemplazar el audio de publicaciones ya difundidas y editar miniaturas después de publicar un video.
Otra novedad es Instants (o Instantáneas), una opción para compartir fotos temporales y sin edición con Amigos cercanos o seguidores recíprocos.
La plataforma además amplió las etiquetas para perfiles generados con inteligencia artificial y las normas de originalidad para fotos y carruseles, con el objetivo de priorizar contenidos propios en las recomendaciones de usuarios que los descubren.

articles.title: Un Tesla Semi brûle tout seul sur une autoroute américaine, et pendant des heures !
articles.text:
Un camion Tesla Semi a pris feu seul aux USA. Et il a vraiment mis le temps pour finalement s'eteindre !
Tesla veut pouvoir compter plus que des voitures dans son catalogue de produit. C'est ainsi que la société a, après de très nombreuses années, finalement lancé la commercialisation en masse de son camion poids lourds électrique Tesla Semi à la rentrée dernière. Une prouesse technologique intèressante, mais qui peut aussi avoir ses mauvais côtés, comme on le voit avec cette histoire qui s'est passée aux États-Unis !
Un Tesla Semi prend feu seul sur la route à San Francisco
Hier, en Californie, un véhicule Tesla Semi prenait feu sur la route I-880. Et ce qui ne serait qu'un petit inconvénient, s'il s'agissait de la plupart des autres véhicules, a cette fois entraîné la fermeture de la route.
L'autoroute I-880 a en effet dû être fermée à la fois au niveau des voies du nord et du sud. Les autorités ont pris cette décision en raison du risque potentiel de fumées chimiques dangereuses qui pouvaient être émises par le camion en flamme - et qui avait brûlé tout seul.
Une batterie en lithium est beaucoup plus difficile à éteindre
Car ici, aucun accident en vue. Les témoins indiquent simplement avoir vu un feu éclater seul dans le Tesla Semi. Pour le moment, Tesla n'a pas encore apporté de commentaires sur ce sujet. Mais il a fallu être patient pour avoir un retour à la normale.
L'ensemble des voies n'a en effet été dégagé qu'au bout d'une dizaine d'heures. Il faut dire que si les voitures électriques ont moins tendance à prendre feu que les thermiques, elles sont aussi sujettes à l'emballement thermique. Ce phénomène est une réaction chimique en chaîne incontrôlable qui fait qu'une cellule ayant chauffé transmet de la chaleur résiduelle à des cellules qui n'avaient pas encore brûlé, alors même que cette même cellule est en train d'être éteinte. Ainsi, pour éviter ce problème, les pompiers doivent effectuer un refroidissement massif, qui consiste souvent à l'utilisation de grosses quantités d'eau des heures durant.
Source : Electrek

articles.title: Hackers Target Critical Oracle E-Business Suite RCE Flaw Days After Security Patch
articles.text:
Threat actors are beginning to probe for a newly patched critical vulnerability in Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS), according to threat intelligence firm Defused Cyber.
The vulnerability in question is CVE-2026-101767 (CVSS score: 9.8) , a case of improper authentication in the Oracle Application Object Library of Oracle E-Business Suite. It was patched by Oracle last week as part of its Critical Patch Update.
Security researchers Brandon Peterson, Jimi Sebree, and Noah King of Horizon3.ai have been credited with discovering and reporting the flaw to Oracle on July 24, 2026.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, October 27," Defused Cyber said in an X post.
In an advisory for the vulnerability, Horizon3.ai described it as an unauthenticated SQL injection vulnerability that could be chained to achieve remote code execution.
"The vulnerability allows an attacker with network access to the affected Thin Client Framework (TCF) servlet to execute SQL as the APPS database user, then run operating system commands as the EBS application account," the cybersecurity company said.
Specifically, an attacker can issue a crafted request to the vulnerable TCF servlet at "/OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer" to run SQL with the privileges of the APPS database user and ultimately enable system command execution with the privileges of the EBS application account.
Successful exploitation of CVE-2026-101767 can permit an attacker to read or modify application data accessible to APPS and execute commands on the application host.
"Depending on the deployment, affected data may include financial, payroll, HR, and procurement records. Operating system access is governed by the permissions of the compromised EBS application account," Horizon3.ai warned.
While internet-facing EBS deployments present the most risk, internal EBS systems can also be exploited if an attacker can reach the vulnerable servlet from a compromised system or another accessible network segment.
Users are advised to update to the latest version as soon as possible. If immediate patching is not an option, the following workarounds can be applied -
- Remove /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer, associated with oracle.apps.fnd.tcf.SocketServer, from the EBS URL firewall allowlist.
- Restrict access to the EBS web tier to trusted networks.
- Monitor the EBS application host and database for signs of compromise.
Horizon3.ai has also shared the below indicators of compromise -
- Unauthenticated POST requests to /OA_HTML/AppsTCFServer that instantiate the Gantt data-server class (oracle.apps.jtf.gantt.server.GanttDataServer), followed by backend database activity.
- SQL reconnaissance shortly after unauthenticated web requests (database version, current user, directory objects).
- Unexpected files in $APPLPTMP and the oracle account spawning /bin/sh via the Concurrent Manager to run OS commands.
Vulnerabilities in EBS are a hot target for attackers. Over the past year, two critical flaws in the same product (CVE-2025-61882 and CVE-2026-46817, CVSS scores: 9.8) have come under active exploitation, with the former leveraged by the Cl0p ransomware and extortion crew.

articles.title: No Man's Sky Forsaken Update Adds "Spooky Biomechanical Ships" and Wealth of New Exploration Content
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
No Man's Sky Forsaken Update Adds "Spooky Biomechanical Ships" and Wealth of New Exploration Content
No Man's Sky had a rough start to life, with Hello Games having had to put in nearly a decade's worth of work to right the ship and get the game to "Very Positive" reviews on Steam. Now, following a handful of significant gameplay and content updates since that success, Hello Games has announced the Forsaken update, a new content update to No Man's Sky that builds on the game's exploration, building, and research mechanics.
The Forsaken update, officially version 7.10 of the game, adds a minimal HUD mode for a more immersive experience, minimizing the compass, hazard protection bars, and mission notifications. Hello Games says this mode is especially suited for experienced players. On the gameplay and content side of things, however, the update also introduces "Haunting Mementos," a new set piece that sees gamers searching the abandoned wrecks, infested outposts, and derelict freighters in deep space for "bizarre, horrifying biological samples."Building on the "spooky" encounters in the aforementioned Haunting Mementos game mechanic, the Forsaken update also adds new biomechanical corvette modules that players can construct to give their ships a "touch of the sinister." There is also a new Vantage-Class cockpit that gives players a panoramic view of the outdoors while providing a minimalist interior, in addition to several other cockpit designs and new interior designs. On the topic of cosmetics, the new larva tank helmet also allows players to have fun with their player character customization by replacing their head with a parasitic larva in a glass tank.Another headline feature in the update is seamless interstellar travel with new warp travel capabilities. There are also new space courier contracts that reward players handsomely for interplanetary package deliveries. Off-planet bases can now also be uploaded to the shared server, allowing players to visit other players' orbital space stations. There is also now detailed guidance for space scavenging, and the Holo-Arena creature battles have now been added to deep-space outposts.The No Man's Sky Forsaken update trailer follows.

articles.title: DPI Venture Capital closes Nclude Fund at over $112 million
articles.text: DPI Venture Capital has announced the final close of its Nclude Fund at over $112 million, to invest in technology startups across Africa and the Middle East. Established in Egypt in 2022, Nclude came under DPI Venture Capital's investment advisory management in 2025 following a restructuring. The fund focuses on fintech, financial inclusion, AI and technology-enabled businesses, investing between $500,000 and $10 million per company, from Seed to Series C. Egypt remains its core market, with 30% of the fund's investment mandate allocated to opportunities outside the country. Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East, including Egyptian startups Nawy, Paymob and Money Fellows, UAE-based FlapKap, Senegal-focused healthtech Kera and Accord Partners, which targets AI applications in accounting and auditing. The final close will support new investments and the regional expansion of portfolio companies, particularly businesses scaling between Egypt, the Gulf and other African markets. DPI Venture Capital is led by Managing Partner Ashley Lewis, alongside General Partner Mohamed Aladdin. Press release: DPI Venture Capital, Development Partners International’s venture capital platform, today announced the final close of the Nclude Fund at over $112 million, supporting its next phase of investment across Africa and the Middle East. Nclude was established in 2022 as a fintech-focused venture capital fund in Egypt. DPI became investment adviser to the fund in 2025 following a restructuring transaction, alongside the launch of DPI Venture Capital, its dedicated venture capital platform. Since then, DPI Venture Capital has selectively broadened the LP base with additional strategically aligned investors. Nclude’s strategy focuses on fintech, fintech-enabled businesses and financial inclusion, and supports companies at the intersection of fintech, AI and emerging technology. The fund invests from seed through Series C, with investments ranging from $500,000 to $10 million, allowing it to back businesses at different stages of their growth. Egypt is a core market for Nclude and a launchpad for businesses with the potential to scale across Africa and the Middle East. The fund also invests across the wider Africa region and the Middle East, with 30% of its mandate available for investment outside Egypt, backing businesses with the potential to expand between markets and build regional scale. To date, Nclude has invested in 15 companies across Africa and the Middle East. The portfolio includes: ● Nawy, the Egyptian proptech company that raised a $52 million Series A as it expands across MENA; ● Paymob, the Egyptian payments business with operations across the UAE and wider Gulf that raised $35 million in a pre-Series C round led by Mubadala and EBRD; ● FlapKap, a UAE-based fintech that raised $34 million in a pre-Series A round to support SME finance and GCC expansion; ● Money Fellows, which raised $13 million to support financial inclusion and expansion across North Africa, including Morocco; ● Kera, a health access AI company operating across Senegal and Côte d’Ivoire; ● Accord Partners, an AI roll-up venture focused on the accounting and auditing space with an immediate focus on Saudi Arabia and the broader MENA region. Ashley Lewis, Managing Partner and Head of DPI Venture Capital, said: “When we became adviser to Nclude, we took stewardship of an existing fund with a strong investment thesis, rooted in improving financial inclusion across Africa and the Middle East. We have grown a portfolio aligned with that central thesis and have built on those foundations by activating more of the fund’s mandate across the region. This has included expansion into themes such as affordable insurance and healthcare access, unlocking credit access for SMEs, and helping individuals save and invest for the future. At the same time, we have selectively broadened the fund’s investor base with additional strategically aligned LPs.” Lewis added: “At over $112 million, we believe Nclude is appropriately sized for today’s market, giving us the firepower to invest with discipline and support ambitious founders as they grow from strong local businesses into regional technology leaders.” Mohamed Aladdin, General Partner at DPI Venture Capital, said: “Across our portfolio, we are seeing ambitious technology businesses increasingly look beyond their home markets as they scale. The growing links between Africa and the Middle East create opportunities for companies to access new customers and markets, whether expanding from Egypt into the Gulf, across North Africa or into Egypt from elsewhere in the region. Companies including Nawy, Paymob, Money Fellows, and FlapKap demonstrate the potential to build regional technology leaders from these markets.” Sofiane Lahmar, Chief Executive Officer of Development Partners International, said: “As one of Africa’s leading investment firms, DPI has a long track record of backing high-growth African businesses through different stages of growth. By institutionalising venture capital as a core part of our platform, we can combine DPI Venture Capital’s specialist expertise with the networks, capabilities and investment experience of the wider firm. This strengthens our ability to support ambitious technology businesses as they scale across Africa and the Middle East and deliver strong returns for our investors while advancing financial inclusion across the region.”

articles.title: LiberNovo's $1299 office chair solves the big-and-tall ergonomics problem
articles.text:
TechRadar Verdict
If you can stomach the price tag, the LiberNovo Maxis is an exceptional chair. Specifically engineered for big and tall users, its broad seat, stylish design, and range of features including motorized lumbar support marks it out as a pro choice for professionals who want a comfortable, supportive sitting experience. I found it perfect while working all day. It's more office chair than most people need - the top model even has a cooling fan under the seat and a back massager. but it's that premium price that'll determine if this is the desk chair for you.
Reasons to buy
- + Properly designed for big and tall users
- + Incredibly comfortable all-day
- + Electric lumbar support
- + Built-in fan and decompression massager
- + Highly adjustable and ultra-stylish
- + Comes in three models and a range of bundles
Reasons to avoid
- - Premium pricing
- - Not suitable for small and average-sized users (the LiberNovo Omni series is)
Why you can trust TechRadar
We spend hours testing every product or service we review, so you can be sure you're buying the best. Find out more about how we test.
- Engineered for users 5'10" to 6'7"
- Reinforced frame with weight load up to 399 lbs
- Motorized lumbar support and bionic FlexFit backrest
- Built-in fan and OmniStretch massager
- Controlled recline with Dynamic Support
I get it. Most people won’t need the LiberNovo Maxis. Most people will see the price, baulk, and close the website. It’s expensive, its headline features run on a rechargeable battery, and it’s more chair than your everyday hybrid or remote worker needs.
But it’s also ergonomic, stunningly designed, cleverly engineered, and built for big and tall users without the usual flabby, foamy designs that I see for half or even a quarter of the price of the Maxis. It’s also one of the best office chairs I’ve tested. If you're over 5'10", you'll want to check this out.
On top of that, the model I’m reviewing here - the Maxis Airflow - includes a cooling fan in the seat, electric lumbar adjustments, and a back massager called the OmniStretch designed for relieving tension.
So, this is not your everyday office chair. It’s an elite seat for professionals who prize all-day comfort, a stylish ergonomic design, supportive top-end features, and don’t mind paying a fair chunk of change for that.
LiberNovo Maxis: Price & availability
The LiberNovo Maxis is available direct from the maker, and I’m also seeing it at online retailers including Amazon and Best Buy.
I’ve danced around that price tag enough. In the US, the LiberNovo Maxis has a list price of $1299; from the UK site, it’s £1099. At the time of review, both are discounted to $1119 / £1002.
And that’s for the base manual model. The Maxis Electric, which includes the electric adjustments to the lower back support sends the price to $1799 / £1579, while the Maxis Airflow reviewed here is priced at $1859 / £1699 (although again, at time of review, they are discounted by around two-hundred bucks).
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
On top of that, you can buy the chair in three different bundles: the standalone chair, the Standard pack which comes with a footrest, and the Premium Bundle which also adds a spare rechargeable battery. Unless you’re using the electric features constantly, I’d recommend either the Basic or Standard bundle.
All in all, the Maxis is firmly in the premium price bracket, alongside top-tier brands in the office furniture world like Herman Miller and Steelcase. I can understand why, in terms of build quality and design.
| Seat depth | 20.47in / 52cm | 
| Backrest shoulder span | 16.93in / 43cm | 
| Backrest waist span | 20.47in / 52cm | 
| Headrest vertical range | 5.51in / 14cm | 
| Headrest horizontal range | 4.72in / 12cm | 
| Weight limit | Up to 399 lbs | 
| User height | 5'10" - 6'7" | 
- Value: 4 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Assembly
This beast of a chair came in two massive boxes (three, if you count the footrest).
As ever, I recommend building this in the room you’ll use it in because this one is heavy and unwieldy to move. The gouges and marks on my wall as I struggled to move it upstairs are evidence of that.
All told, it took me around 40 minutes from unboxing to fully built chair. That’s on the longer side, but LiberNovo makes assembly as easy as possible. Forget your little instruction manuals with walls of text. This one comes with a massive sheet of card that pictorially guides you through each and every step.
It’s also the first office chair I’ve ever tested that includes white gloves for handling it. Maybe that’s over the top, but can bet I pulled them on and wore them throughout the assembly process.
- Assembly: 5 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Design & build
Build quality and design are superb. The pieces feel weighty, and I experienced no creaking or squeaking as I swivelled, reclined, and generally made a nuisance of myself at my desk.
This is a premium chair across the board, right down to the wide single-piece aluminum base that feels like it will capably and confidently support anyone up to the recommended weight of 399 lbs (181kg).
Being built for big and tall users, the Maxis is designed for those between 5'10” and 6'7”. Now, I’m an inch shy of the minimum recommended height and yes, it is slightly too large for me - particularly in the broad seat, which provides ample width and depth. I had to dial down the adjustability on the headrest and armrests to its minimum settings to stay comfortable and snug. Effectively, my negative experience here is a positive for larger, taller body types.
In terms of design, I had one thought: This is like an office chair designed by HR Geiger with its Xenomorph-like exoskeleton on the tapering backrest. Unlike so many I test, it’s a real executive statement piece.
- Design & build: 5 / 5
LiberNovo Maxis: Performance & features
I always judge office chairs chiefly on two factors: comfort and support. Here, the LiberNovo Maxis is an easy win. I used this chair for eight hours a day while working and it stayed comfortable from first to last hour. After that, I spent a few extra hours in it, feet up on the footrest, while gaming. I still didn’t tire of the chair or feel fatigue or numbness that some cheap chairs can inflict on me.
And then, of course, there’s that back massager. Actually, I’m not sure ‘massager’ is the right word here. LiberNovo calls it the OmniStretch, billing it as a way to lean back and decompress. I’d liken it to having a couple of fists kneading deep into your lower back while the whole backrest quickly but gently vibrates. That may not sound comfortable, but I promise you it is. It runs for a set five minutes at the press of a button. My pregnant wife has been using it daily for relaxation and pain relief.
Now, I generally avoid foam and fabric office chairs. I run hot, and prefer breathable mesh. And while the seat can get warm when sitting down all day, I found the two-speed cooling fan - only available on the Airflow model - was a very good solution that actually helped maintain a cooler body temperature.
Adjustability is excellent on this chair, and I found it easy to fiddle around with the headrest, seat elevation, recline tension, and swivel armrests. However, the standout mechanism is the motorized lumbar support buttons located below the left armrest. So, I’m not constantly reaching under or around the chair to adjust the positioning for continued support.
What’s notable is the Dynamic Support, so when I reclined back, the seat stayed stable while the armrests dropped back with me so I could feel supported in any position. I appreciated the steady recline system in place here, too. As you lean back, it won’t suddenly fall back, but eases itself into position. The tension can be altered using the under-seat knob, while the recline can be set to lock at different angles depending on how far you want to lean back.
Where it lacks adjustments is the seat depth, which is fixed at a larger-than-average 52cm, which makes it more suitable for taller users. I would’ve also liked lockable armrests. Like a lot of office chairs, they’re directional, moving laterally and swinging in and out without much pressure. That’s fine if you’re getting up and moving around a lot, but not if you’re locking in for longer work sessions. But I appreciate this may be a me problem - I had the same complaint with the Boulies EP600 I recently reviewed.
As I say, it’s a lot of chair for the money - the only one I’ve tested that comes with a rechargeable battery. And not every professional, whether in the office or working hybrid/remote, will need a seat at this level. But I can’t fault the comfort or design at all.
- Performance & features: 5 / 5
Should I buy the LiberNovo Maxis?
✅ Buy it if...
You’re built bigger or taller. The Maxis is specifically engineered for larger body types without compromising on style, comfort, or support.
You want all the bells and whistles. This high-quality office chair does it all. If you’re going to splurge out, it might as well be one with a massager and fan.
❌ Don't buy it if...
You don’t need the extra features. You're paying for well-designed ergonomics and features most office chairs will never have.
You’re under 5’10”. I’d recommend the LiberNovo Omni or LiberNovo Omni Pro if you want the same design ethos.
How I tested the LiberNovo Maxis
For two weeks, the LiberNovo Maxis Airflow became my daily driver chair. Eight hours a day, minimum, I've been sitting on it at work. And, once the work laptop was closed, I carried on using it, both while gaming and using the OmniStretch massaging feature multiple times throughout the testing period (when I could get my wife to stop using it!). During those times, I tended to pair it with LiberNovo's adjustable footrest for the added relaxation.
Steve is B2B Editor for Creative & Hardware at TechRadar Pro, helping business professionals equip their workspace with the right tools. He tests and reviews the software, hardware, and office furniture that modern workspaces depend on, cutting through the hype to zero in on the real-world performance you won't find on a spec sheet. He is a relentless champion of the Oxford comma.

articles.title: Qué es Media Fabric y por qué lo usarán emisoras de radio y apps streaming como Netflix
articles.text:
Una plataforma streaming como Netflix necesita producir contenidos, adaptar anuncios para públicos distintos y sostener la reproducción cuando una gran cantidad de usuarios ve el mismo evento. Oracle Media Fabric apunta a reunir esas tareas en una sola plataforma para facilitar la gestión.
Oracle anunció que la herramienta está diseñada para ayudar a empresas de medios, proveedores de streaming y marcas a reducir los tiempos y costos de producción de contenido, además de distribuir y transmitir video de alta calidad a gran escala.
La propuesta combina inteligencia artificial con infraestructura de distribución de video para facilitar la creación, edición y entrega de contenidos. Permite desarrollar publicidad dirigida a audiencias específicas, programación personalizada y experiencias de visualización compartida.
Clay Magouyrk, director ejecutivo de Oracle, explicó que la herramienta integra la creación de contenido y el streaming en un mismo flujo de trabajo.
Según indicó, el objetivo es que los creadores aprovechen mejor su material existente y adapten las experiencias de visualización para diferentes audiencias en tiempo real.
Qué compone a Oracle Media Fabric
Oracle Media Fabric reúne Oracle Creative Studio, Oracle AI Media Models y Oracle Video Edge. Además, incluye Oracle Adaptive Media Platform, que conecta la creación con la distribución de contenidos.
Oracle Creative Studio está pensada para que equipos de medios y creadores conviertan ideas en guiones gráficos, escenas, videos cinematográficos, efectos visuales y personajes virtuales.
La herramienta combina modelos de inteligencia artificial de Oracle y de terceros, que pueden elegirse según requisitos de seguridad, procedencia, costos y protección de la propiedad intelectual.
Oracle AI Media Models se enfoca en la generación y edición de videos e imágenes. También permite procesar grandes volúmenes de material audiovisual, realizar búsquedas y clasificar contenidos, además de personalizar modelos dentro de Oracle Cloud Infrastructure.
La plataforma incorpora medidas para proteger la propiedad intelectual de los clientes y reducir el riesgo de que el contenido generado infrinja los derechos de terceros.
Oracle Video Edge está dirigida a emisoras y proveedores de streaming que transmiten eventos en vivo. La plataforma utiliza información de red y reproducción en tiempo real para coordinar la capacidad disponible y dirigir a los espectadores a ubicaciones de distribución adecuadas.
El objetivo es sostener video de alta calidad y baja latencia cuando la audiencia alcanza sus niveles máximos.
La herramienta busca que la reproducción comience rápido y continúe de forma fluida a través de Oracle Cloud Infrastructure, redes de distribución de contenido y redes de proveedores de internet participantes.
Por su parte, Oracle Adaptive Media Platform permite desarrollar publicidad específica para cada audiencia, programación personalizada y experiencias de visualización compartida.
Las marcas pueden generar variantes de un anuncio base dentro de sus directrices y reglas de aprobación, sin tener que crear cada versión desde cero.
Oracle señaló que Media Fabric puede ayudar a emisoras y plataformas de streaming a comprender cómo responde el público a la programación y a la publicidad. La empresa prevé que la plataforma esté disponible en los próximos 12 meses.
Sale jefa de contenidos de Netflix
Netflix anunció la salida de Bela Bajaria, su responsable de contenidos durante los últimos tres años, un día después de comunicar el despido de cerca de 1.000 empleados, el 6% de su plantilla global. Bajaria, que llevaba una década en la compañía, será reemplazada por Peter Rice, exejecutivo de Fox y Disney.
Durante su gestión estuvo vinculada a producciones como El juego del calamar, Merlina, Adolescencia y Bridgerton.
Los recortes alcanzarán distintas áreas y regiones, con mayor impacto en producto, tecnología, asuntos legales y recursos humanos.
Netflix sostiene que seguirá invirtiendo en áreas de alto impacto mientras busca crecer en publicidad, eventos en vivo, deportes, videojuegos, contenidos infantiles, formatos cortos y herramientas basadas en inteligencia artificial.

articles.title: Bosch veut vendre son usine de Vendôme, ses salariés répondent avec une grève illimitée
articles.text:
Les salariés de l’usine Bosch de Vendôme, dans le Loir-et-Cher, sont en grève illimitée depuis mardi. Lors d’un référendum, 60 % des votants ont demandé l’arrêt de la vente du site, faute de repreneur jugé fiable.
Une grève illimitée a débuté le mardi 27 octobre 2026 à l’usine Bosch de Vendôme, dans le Loir-et-Cher, où une majorité de salariés a cessé le travail. Le mouvement fait suite à un référendum interne, lors duquel 60 % des 198 votants ont réclamé l’arrêt de la vente du site, qui produit notamment des colonnes de direction (la pièce qui relie le volant au reste du système de direction), engagée par l’équipementier automobile allemand en juin 2025. En cause, des repreneurs que les syndicats jugent insuffisamment fiables, rapporte France 3 Centre-Val de Loire.
Les salariés de l’usine de Vendôme lancent une grève illimitée pour bloquer la vente de leur site
Le lundi 26 octobre fut mouvementé du côté de Vendôme, où les salariés ont été consultés par référendum sur l'avenir de leur site. Sur les 198 votants, une grande partie a réclamé l'arrêt du processus de vente. Un résultat nourri à la fois par l'usure et l'agacement. Les salariés disent être « menés en bateau » depuis des mois par une direction qui ne leur inspire plus confiance. Dès mardi, la majorité d'entre eux s'est mise en grève illimitée, un mouvement que les syndicats jugent tenable.
Le fond du problème, ce sont les candidats au rachat. Benoît Freudenreich (CFDT) et Patrick Pigoreau (CGT) assurent qu'ils n'étaient pas opposés à l'idée d'un repreneur au départ. Mais une fois les dossiers étudiés avec l'aide d'un cabinet d'expertise, le constat fut amer. Les garanties sur l'emploi ne sont pas toujours au rendez-vous, ou se résument à de belles promesses.
Le couperet est tombé la semaine dernière, avec la visite d'un nouveau repreneur. D'après les syndicats, elle aurait eu lieu à la demande du géant Stellantis, le client qui pèse le plus lourd dans la production du site. Sans retour à leur demande de plan de relance, les salariés ont d'abord débrayé, c'est-à-dire cessé le travail pour une courte durée. Bosch France dément d'ailleurs que Stellantis soit à l'origine de cette visite. Selon l'entreprise, le candidat avait simplement besoin de revenir sur place avant de retravailler son projet de relance.
Bosch maintient le cap jusqu'au verdict de décembre
La direction, elle, n'entend pas céder si facilement. Elle rappelle que 40 % des votants ne souhaitent pas arrêter la vente et que tout le monde n'a pas voté, à commencer par les intérimaires. Les syndicats écartent cet argument, puisque selon eux, ces intérimaires ne font pas vraiment partie de l'entreprise, car rattachés à une agence d'intérim. Bosch dit respecter le droit de grève, mais prévient qu'un mouvement prolongé pourrait fragiliser la confiance des clients et des repreneurs potentiels.
Selon Bosch France, les discussions sont pourtant en bonne voie. Les projets des différents candidats seront présentés le 3 décembre, et une décision sur la reprise est attendue une grosse dizaine de jours plus tard, le 15 décembre. D'un côté, on a donc une direction décidée à mener la vente à son terme. De l'autre, une majorité de votants qui refuse de signer un chèque en blanc. Les semaines à venir s'annoncent tendues.
Le site de Vendôme est assez symptomatique de ce que subit l'entreprise. Bousculé par une électrification plus lente que prévu et par la montée des concurrents chinois, le premier équipementier automobile mondial réduit peu à peu ses effectifs et revoit son organisation. Il a par exemple annoncé l'an dernier quelque 13 000 suppressions de postes d'ici 2030, en majorité en Allemagne. Le 22 octobre, il a ajouté la transformation de sa branche Mobility allemande et de trois unités de services en filiales distinctes, une réorganisation qui touchera pas moins de 62 500 salariés outre-Rhin à partir d'août 2027.

articles.title: System76 Unveils Thelio Prime 11-Liter Linux Desktop PC
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
System76 Unveils Thelio Prime 11-Liter Linux Desktop PC
System76 has announced the Thelio Prime, a compact 11-liter (288 x 148.9 x 281.9 mm) desktop built at the company's Denver facility. The chassis is made from milled stainless steel and aluminium parts. To add a bit of finesse, there's a smoked-glass front panel and tool-free magnetic side panels. The interior is designed with two thermal chambers, separating the CPU and GPU. As for performance, System76 describes it as "An 11-liter Linux desktop that fits almost anywhere, without giving up on performance." Users can choose from an AMD Ryzen 9000 processor (up to Ryzen 7 9850X3D) with integrated Radeon graphics or go for a discrete AMD or NVIDIA GPU (up to RTX 5070), depending on configuration. The system can have up to 96 GB of dual-channel DDR5 and up to 8 TB of storage across its M.2 slots (one PCIe 5.0 and one PCIe 4.0).
Front I/O offers a USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-C, a USB 3.2 Gen 1 Type-A, and the audio jack. The rear adds two USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-A ports, one USB 3.2 Gen 2 Type-C, one USB 3.2 Gen 1, four USB 2.0 ports, a BIOS Flashback button, and audio line-out. Networking covers 2.5 GbE, Wi-Fi 6E, and Bluetooth 5.2. Display outputs depend on the GPU. Integrated graphics get HDMI 2.1 and USB-C with DisplayPort 1.4. A discrete GPU option typically adds three DisplayPort outputs and one HDMI. Power comes from a 600 W 80 Plus certified supply with at least 90% efficiency. The system comes preinstalled with Pop!_OS 24.04 LTS with COSMIC Desktop Environment or with Ubuntu 24.04 LTS. The Thelio Prime is expected to launch November 18, starting at $1,599.

articles.title: Critical 16-Year-Old UEFI Flaw Can Run Code Before Secure Boot on Network-Booting Servers
articles.text:
A critical 16-year-old flaw in EDK II, the open-source code that most hardware makers use to build UEFI firmware, can allow an attacker to run code on a machine before its operating system loads, but only while the machine is booting over the network.
UEFI firmware is the software that runs first when a computer is switched on, before the operating system. An attacker who can reach the machine with a crafted network message during such a network boot can hang the boot, or, with work tailored to the exact firmware build, run their own code before Secure Boot and other startup defenses load.
An attacker needs no password and no existing access to the machine, but does need to reach it over the network during the short window when it is booting this way.
Red Hat and SUSE, which both ship the affected code, rated the flaw as one an attacker exploits from an adjacent network position rather than across the open internet.
TianoCore, the project behind EDK II, published an advisory on October 22 and rated the flaw, tracked as CVE-2026-97631, 9.5 out of 10. A code fix exists, but no stable release of EDK II contains it yet, and the advisory still lists no patched version, so most users have nothing to install today.
What the Flaw Lets an Attacker Do
The flaw is a buffer overflow in EDK II's network-boot code, known as PXE. During a PXE boot, a machine loads its startup image from the network instead of from a local disk.
As part of this, the PXE driver listens for ICMP error messages and the small status messages that network devices send back, and copies each one into a fixed 504-byte area of memory.
The size checks in that copy are wrong in both the IPv4 and IPv6 versions of the code, so a message longer than 504 bytes spills past the area and overwrites nearby memory with data the attacker chose.
To set this off, an attacker only has to send one crafted error message to the machine's address while it is in the middle of a network boot. No password or existing access to the machine is needed.
The simple result is a crash: the boot hangs, and the machine fails to start. Getting code to run is much harder and far less reliable. The advisory says that an attacker who knows the exact firmware build can plant a "counterfeit event" that causes the firmware to run the attacker's own code, so an exploit has to be built for a specific build.
When code runs, it executes within the firmware, before Secure Boot and other boot-time checks have verified anything. That timing is what makes the flaw serious.
Code planted this way runs only once and does not survive a reboot by itself. That single run is still enough to install other code that does start on every boot.
Who Is Affected
The bug sits in EDK II up to and including edk2-stable202608, the newest stable version, dated August 21. EDK II is the reference code that nearly every UEFI firmware vendor builds on, including the independent BIOS makers AMI, Insyde, and Phoenix, as well as Microsoft's hardened fork, Project Mu.
The flawed copy loop has been in the code since a commit added in November 2010, The Hacker News found by tracing the project's history.
PXE network boot is turned on by default in EDK II's standard build. The flaw does not affect home or office users who boot only from a local disk. It applies to organizations whose machines boot over a network, primarily servers and data center equipment.
How many shipping products carry the vulnerable code is not known. Intel told Ars Technica that none of its "commercial products currently under security support" are known to be affected, and that it "does not include the affected EDK2 functionality in its reference code," though an OEM board vendor or system maker could add it.
Arm said the flaw "is not directly applicable to Arm's product portfolio." Both companies' own firmware draws on EDK II.
Linux distributions also ship the code. Red Hat lists its edk2 package in Red Hat Enterprise Linux 8, 9, and 10 as affected and not yet fixed, and SUSE and Debian mark their equivalent packages the same way.
AMD, Phoenix Technologies, AMI, Microsoft, and Amazon did not answer the tech news site's questions before publication, and TianoCore did not respond either, so the status of their products remains unclear.
Is There a Fix?
A fix has been merged into the EDK II source code. It rewrites the faulty copy so an oversized message is cut off at 504 bytes instead of spilling over, and it reached the main development branch on October 15.
No stable release of EDK II includes that fix yet. The Hacker News checked the project's release tags on October 28 and found the newest, edk2-stable202608, predates it, and the advisory still lists the patched version as "Not patched currently." Microsoft's Project Mu has already pulled the fix into its release branches, and cut tagged builds on October 26.
Even with the fix public in source, a server operator has nothing to install until the maker of their firmware ships a BIOS or UEFI update built from it. That step is at least straightforward, Jesse Michael, a principal researcher at the firmware security firm Eclypsium, told Ars Technica: unlike Secure Boot bypasses such as BootHole and BlackLotus, the flaw "can be fixed with a basic code fix" and does not require certificate or key revocations.
Until that update arrives, the advisory lists no workaround. Because the flaw can only be reached during a network boot, operators who do not need PXE can disable it to reduce exposure. Ars also advised watching boot-time network traffic and logs for signs of attempts.
How It Became Public
The flaw was found by Alex Matrosov of Anthropic and Dan Holmes-Mitra of Google, the advisory credits. A coordinated disclosure had been planned for January 2027.
That plan was overtaken on September 28, when a pull request to EDK II, signed off by an AMI engineer, publicly described the flaw by its CVE number and included the fix. Once the people who found it saw the post, TianoCore published its advisory on October 22, weeks before the planned date.
With the patch public, Ars noted that skilled attackers can study it to determine how the flaw is triggered and build working exploits.
There is no sign the flaw has been used in an attack. It was not in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog as of its October 27 update, and no researcher has reported seeing it exploited.
The flaw is also not, on its own, a way into a network, Ars Technica reported after putting questions to several firmware researchers. The realistic attacker is an insider, or someone who has already gained a low-level foothold on the local network and wants to dig deeper.
"An attacker intent on compromising a nearby endpoint or server could use this bug to hijack program flow at a point where the boot process still has access to sensitive components, like the endpoint's TPM," said HD Moore, the creator of Metasploit and chief research officer at the security firm Dragos, in comments to Ars Technica.
"This could be used to break disk encryption for cases where an attacker has short-term network access (and it would be even easier in a theft scenario)."
It is not the first serious flaw in EDK II's network-boot code. In January 2024, researchers disclosed PixieFail, a set of nine flaws in the same part of EDK II, also reachable during PXE boot. Ars reported that fuzzing projects started after PixieFail to find more bugs in the code did not catch this one.

articles.title: Poussé par l'IA, Fujifilm va multiplier par cinq sa production... de bandes magnétiques
articles.text:
On les croyait reléguées aux archives de l’informatique. Pourtant, les bandes magnétiques connaissent un regain d’intérêt spectaculaire grâce à l’intelligence artificielle. Au point que Fujifilm prévoit d’investir 57 millions d’euros pour multiplier par cinq ses capacités de production d’ici à 2028.
Qui aurait imaginé que l’intelligence artificielle, avec ses GPU surpuissants et ses centres de données dernier cri, remettrait au goût du jour les bonnes vieilles bandes magnétiques ? C’est pourtant ce qui se passe chez Fujifilm, qui s’apprête à réaliser son plus gros investissement dans cette technologie depuis une vingtaine d'années.
Selon le quotidien économique japonais Nikkei, le groupe prévoit de consacrer 10 milliards de yens, soit environ 57 millions d’euros, à l’agrandissement de son usine d’Odawara, près de Tokyo. L’objectif est de multiplier par cinq sa capacité de production par rapport à l’exercice 2025, mesurée en volume de données stockables, d’ici à l’exercice 2028.
Des cartouches capables de stocker jusqu’à 100 To
Fujifilm n’a jamais vraiment abandonné les bandes magnétiques. Engagé dans la recherche sur les bandes magnétiques depuis 1954, le fabricant japonais a simplement vu leur utilisation évoluer, des enregistrements audiovisuels vers la sauvegarde et l’archivage professionnels.
Aujourd'hui, ses cartouches LTO-10 peuvent contenir 40 To de données sans compression, et jusqu’à 100 To avec compression (2,5:1, selon la nature des données stockées). Une capacité considérable pour un support aussi compact, qui trouve naturellement sa place dans les gigantesques infrastructures informatiques.
Car si l’IA a besoin de mémoire vive et de SSD rapides pour fonctionner, elle génère et exploite également d’immenses quantités de données qu’il faut conserver pendant des années. Et toutes ne nécessitent pas d’être accessibles instantanément.
Pourquoi la bande magnétique peut battre les disques durs
Les bandes magnétiques conservent un avantage de poids face aux supports de stockage modernes : leur coût. Selon Nikkei, conserver des données sur bande peut revenir jusqu’à quatre fois moins cher que sur disque dur, dans certaines configurations d'archivage.
Elles consomment également très peu d’électricité une fois stockées, puisqu’une cartouche n’a pas besoin de rester alimentée. Mieux encore, elle peut être retirée de son lecteur et conservée hors réseau, ce qui offre une protection supplémentaire contre les ransomwares.
Le revers est connu. Contrairement aux SSD ou aux disques durs, la bande magnétique impose un accès séquentiel aux données. Retrouver un fichier précis peut donc prendre beaucoup plus de temps. Mais pour les données rarement consultées, les fameuses cold data, cet inconvénient pèse finalement assez peu face aux économies réalisées.
Fujifilm n’est pas le seul à profiter de cet appétit pour les données. Kioxia et Sandisk prévoient également d’investir massivement dans la mémoire flash, alors que Toshiba cherche à augmenter sa production de disques durs, tout comme Seagate et Western Digital qui planchent sur la densité des plateaux de leurs HDD. Avec la gourmandise de l’IA en mémoire et capacité de stockage, il n’y a plus de petites économies…
Source : Nikkei via Computerbase

articles.title: Apple tiene nueva versión del MacBook Pro y ahora es táctil: hasta 24 horas de batería
articles.text:
Apple presentó una nueva versión del MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil, hasta 24 horas de batería y una tecnología OLED en tándem llamada PROLED XDR. La computadora estará disponible en modelos de 14 y 16 pulgadas, incorpora los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max y suma cambios en diseño, conectividad, audio y herramientas basadas en inteligencia artificial.
La llegada de funciones táctiles representa un cambio en la línea profesional de Apple. Hasta ahora, la Mac se había apoyado en el teclado, el trackpad y accesorios externos como principales vías de interacción. Con este modelo, los usuarios podrán desplazarse, ampliar imágenes, mover archivos y utilizar aplicaciones creativas directamente sobre la pantalla.
La pantalla PROLED XDR incorpora tecnología OLED en tándem
El nuevo MacBook Pro estrena la pantalla PROLED XDR, basada en dos capas de píxeles autoiluminados. Apple indica que esta tecnología alcanza hasta 2.000 nits de brillo máximo tanto en contenido HDR como SDR, con una relación de contraste de 10.000.000:1.
La compañía señala que el panel busca ofrecer negros profundos, mayor detalle en las zonas oscuras y reflejos más intensos sin los halos que pueden aparecer en otros sistemas de iluminación. La frecuencia de actualización variable llega hasta 120 Hz mediante ProMotion y puede bajar hasta 10 Hz para reducir el consumo energético.
La pantalla incluye compatibilidad con los espacios de color P3 y Adobe RGB, una característica dirigida a fotógrafos, diseñadores, coloristas y editores de video. También ofrece una cobertura superior al 80% de Rec. 2020 para la edición de contenido HDR.
El equipo contará con una opción de nanotextura para reducir reflejos y deslumbramientos en lugares con iluminación intensa. Según Apple, el panel se calibra en fábrica para mantener precisión en luminancia, punto blanco y gama cromática.
El MacBook Pro permite tocar, arrastrar y dibujar en la pantalla
Las capacidades táctiles llegan por primera vez a la línea MacBook Pro. La pantalla responde a gestos como desplazarse por páginas, pellizcar para ampliar fotografías, arrastrar elementos entre ventanas y tocar dos veces para maximizar una aplicación.
El sensor táctil está integrado en el panel, sin una capa externa superpuesta. Apple sostiene que este sistema reduce la latencia y hace que la interacción se sienta más directa. Una bisagra rediseñada busca aportar estabilidad cuando el usuario toca la pantalla.
Los diseñadores podrán utilizar la pantalla como lienzo, los músicos tocar instrumentos virtuales y los desarrolladores probar gestos para aplicaciones de iPhone y iPad. La interacción táctil convivirá con los atajos de teclado y los gestos del trackpad.
La empresa indica que macOS traducirá automáticamente los toques en clics para muchas aplicaciones existentes. También se mencionan herramientas compatibles como Notion, Canva, Zoom, Microsoft Word, Excel, PowerPoint, Outlook, Adobe Lightroom, DaVinci Resolve, Blender, Cinema 4D, ZBrush, Shapr3D y djay Pro.
La Isla Dinámica se integra en la computadora
Otra de las novedades es la llegada de la Isla Dinámica a la Mac. Este espacio funcionará como acceso a Spotlight, Actividades en Vivo y Siri AI. Desde allí, el usuario podrá consultar información, responder llamadas, controlar música o revisar actualizaciones en tiempo real.
La computadora ejecutará macOS 27 Golden Gate, que incorpora Apple Intelligence y una nueva versión de Siri AI. Según Apple, el asistente podrá utilizar contexto personal para buscar información en mensajes, correos y fotografías, además de realizar tareas entre aplicaciones.
M5 Pro y M5 Max apuntan a flujos de trabajo exigentes
La nueva MacBook Pro incluirá los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max, con hasta 128 GB de memoria unificada y hasta 16 TB de almacenamiento. Apple enfoca estas configuraciones en edición de video ProRes 8K, modelado y animación 3D, composición musical, programación y ejecución local de modelos de lenguaje.
El sistema incorpora tres puertos Thunderbolt 5, HDMI, lector de tarjetas SDXC, MagSafe y conector para audífonos. El modelo con M5 Pro puede conectar hasta tres pantallas externas y la versión M5 Max, hasta cuatro. También suma Wi‑Fi 7, Bluetooth 6 y carga rápida hasta el 50% en 30 minutos.
El modelo de 14 pulgadas pesa 1,36 kilogramos y el de 16 pulgadas, 1,81 kilogramos. Apple abrirá las reservas el 28 de octubre y prevé que los equipos estén disponibles desde el viernes 6 de noviembre.
La incorporación de una pantalla táctil modifica la relación histórica entre la Mac y sus usuarios. Apple mantiene el teclado y el trackpad como herramientas centrales, pero añade una interacción más directa para creación, edición y consulta de contenido. El resultado dependerá de si las aplicaciones profesionales adoptan esos gestos como parte habitual de sus procesos.

articles.title: I tried Apple's new touchscreen MacBook Pro, and touching a MacBook screen feels wonderfully natural
articles.text:
Apple's Touchscreen MacBook Pro is finally here, and yes, touching a MacBook screen feels totally and wonderfully natural
Why no M6
Confirming one of Apple's worst-kept secrets, Apple finally unveiled its first-ever touchscreen MacBook Pro in 14-inch and 16-inch models on Wednesday, October 28, in Los Angeles. The news comes just days after Apple unveiled M6-class MacBook Pros. Notably, the new PROLED touchscreen laptops are running M5 Pro and M5 Max Apple silicon.
Apple CEO John Ternus didn't waste much time on stage, quickly announcing the laptops and running through key innovations like the tandem OLED (PROLED) screens and relatively lightweight (3lbs for the 14-inch model and 4lbs for the 16-inch one) before leaving the stage and directing the assembled group of media, analysts, creators, and Apple execs to an adjacent space where I got my first experience ever with a touchscreen MacBook.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
You've been waiting for this
If you read no further, know this: it felt totally natural to tap, swipe, gesture with three fingers, pinch, zoom, and more on a MacBook Pro display. It feels like I've been waiting my whole life to do this on a MacBook (or at least as long as I've been using MacBooks).
As a former Windows user, and more specifically a longtime Surface Pro fan, I'm actually quite used to touching a screen, though maybe not one quite as beautiful as this.
For those unfamiliar with tandem OLED technology, which Apple first introduced a few years ago with the iPad Pro, it sandwiches two ultra-thin, light-emitting OLEDs together. This increases the brightness while maintaining incredibly inky blacks (they're gorgeous). It also allows for a far thinner display panel because you don't need a backlight.
Though there now is a "backlight of a sort. This touchscreen MacBook Pro lineup marks the return of the glowing Apple logo on the back of the display. It lights up when you open the laptop and turns off when you close it (people at the Hollywood, California, event were cheering for that).
I played mostly with the larger, 16-inch model, which still features the expansive, backlit Magic Keyboard and a huge ForceTouch Trackpad, which honestly is gonna get a little bit less use now that a touchscreen is just inches away.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
A pair of large speaker grills sits on either side of the keyboard, though I couldn't hear them over the din of the demo room. As with previous MacBook Pros, there's still an SD Card slot, three Thunderbolt 5 ports, one USB-4 port, HDMI, and the headphone jack.
In my hands, the 4 lb, 16-inch model felt a tad lighter than previous 16-inch MacBook Pros, though the 14-inch (which might be my preference) felt lightweight at 3lbs.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Touch it, touch it, please say you want to
Let's talk, though, about using the touchscreen.
I tried a 3D design app where I used a couple of fingers to spin a model of a guy in battle armor and then a single finger to paint gold on some of the armor.
I opened Maps and used two fingers to spin the map, then pinch-and-zoom.
I used three fingers to swipe through desktops.
I could use two fingers to grab a window, flip it to one side of the screen, and watch it instantly dock itself as a half-screen app (yes, I've done something very similar on a Surface Pro).
I played touchscreen piano with all my fingers.
At no moment did I hesitate and wonder how I did this or that thing. It's obvious. It never felt uncomfortable, and my arm never got tired. Put another way, a touchscreen is a perfect fit for the MacBook Pro family,
Now, you cannot take the screen and flip it all the way to the back of the laptop (something many touchscreen Windows laptops can do). That might be a shame because I could also use my finger to paint and, though I haven't done it yet, draw.
Speaking of which, there is no indication that the touchscreen MacBook Pro supports the Apple Pencil. Honestly, if it can't fold back at least flat, there's no point in this support anyway.
There is, by the way, a Dynamic Island that's basically copied from the iPhone, but I didn't see it do very much.
As I used the touchscreen MacBook Pro, I was not only reminded of my time with the Microsoft Surface Pro but of my initial weeks and even months with the MacBook after I switched platforms. Yes, I found myself touching the inert MacBook screen and had to retrain myself to stop doing it.
Point is, touch was something I reflexively used on the Surface Pro, and I am now certain I will happily use it on the touchscreen MacBook Pro. You probably will, too.
You will pay for the privilege of touch. The 14-inch MacBook Pro with touch starts at $2,899 / £2,899 / AU$4,599, and the 16-inch model starts at $3,399 / £3,399 / $5,499. Pre-orders are live today, and the laptops ship on November 6.

A 38-year industry veteran and award-winning journalist, Lance has covered technology since PCs were the size of suitcases and “on line” meant “waiting.” He’s a former Lifewire Editor-in-Chief, Mashable Editor-in-Chief, and, before that, Editor in Chief of PCMag.com and Senior Vice President of Content for Ziff Davis, Inc. He also wrote a popular, weekly tech column for Medium called The Upgrade.
Lance Ulanoff makes frequent appearances on national, international, and local news programs including Live with Kelly and Mark, the Today Show, Good Morning America, CNBC, CNN, and the BBC.

articles.title: Phantom Blade Zero Launches Today For GeForce RTX & RTX Spark
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Phantom Blade Zero Launches Today For GeForce RTX & RTX Spark
Today, at 7pm PT, the much-anticipated Phantom Blade Zero launches with DLSS 4.5, ray tracing and path tracing, playable on GeForce RTX and RTX Spark. The Blood of Dawnwalker can now be upgraded to DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation via the NVIDIA app.
NVIDIA RTX Remix 1.6 has been added to the Half-Life 2 RTX demo and Portal with RTX, introducing support for DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, and upgrading DLSS Ray Reconstruction and DLSS Frame Generation with our latest AI models. And our beta RTX Remix mod for Minecraft: Java Edition has been released.Metro 2033 Redux and Metro: Last Light Redux have received free updates that enhance the audio and visuals of the two critically acclaimed games, and add support for our latest version of DLSS Super Resolution.
The Boss Gangster: Criminal Empire is available now with DLSS Super Resolution. And the Killing Floor 3: Halloween Horrors update is out now.
Phantom Blade Zero Launches Today With DLSS, Ray Tracing & Path Tracing
S-GAME's Phantom Blade Zero launches today at 7pm PT on Steam and the Epic Games Store. You play as Soul, a swordsman framed for murdering his master. Gravely wounded in the heart and left with just sixty-six days to live, he roams the Wulin alone and hunted, determined to unravel a conspiracy that has ensnared the martial world. 
On GeForce RTX PCs and laptops and RTX Spark devices, you can enhance Phantom Blade Zero with immersive and realistic ray-traced and path-traced lighting, accelerated and enhanced by the complete suite of DLSS 4.5 technologies, including Ray Reconstruction and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation.
Like other recent RTX-enhanced releases, Phantom Blade Zero has received critical acclaim from reviewers, and PC reviews have once again highlighted the game-changing inclusion of DLSS and path tracing on GeForce RTX, and RTX Spark.
- "On my PC, equipped with an RTX 5090…the game ran like a dream" - The Outer Haven
- "With Path Tracing on, Phantom Blade Zero is one of the best-looking games on PC" - DSOGaming
- "NVIDIA's RTX technologies really bring out the best in the game." - Wccftech
- "A GOTY contender with combat that looks as good as it feels" - GamesRadar
Experience Unprecedent Image Quality In Phantom Blade Zero
NVIDIA has teamed up with S-GAME Studio and S-GAME Publishing to bring PC-exclusive path tracing enhancements to Phantom Blade Zero, building upon the fidelity of the game's extensive suite of ray-traced effects.
Path tracing offers a unified lighting solution, with greater levels of detail and additional effects, further improving image quality and immersion.
With path tracing activated in Phantom Blade Zero, Reservoir-based Spatiotemporal Importance Resampling Global Illumination (ReSTIR GI) replaces Unreal Engine's hardware-accelerated, ray-traced Lumen Global Illumination, adding more accurate bounced lighting and color bleeding between surfaces. ReSTIR GI also provides finer indirect shadowing and occlusion, bringing greater detail and depth to the lighting, helping objects appear more naturally grounded in the scene.Across Phantom Blade Zero, ray-traced reflections enhance the appearance of suitably reflective surfaces, and more subtlety, the entire environment. Off-screen detail will be accurately reflected at high levels of detail, objects will self-reflect detail, and game elements will look and feel more realistic and grounded.Ray-traced shadows greatly enhance Phantom Blade Zero's environments adding accurate contact hardening and softening shadows, most noticeably for foliage and terrain, elevating image quality significantly.Ray-traced water caustics are only available with path tracing enabled. Caustics simulate the real-life effect whereby light rays are reflected and refracted by water, curved surfaces and objects, creating unique patterns of light on nearby surfaces, such as river beds. With path tracing, the effect can be accurately and realistically recreated, subtly enhancing realism and immersion in Phantom Blade Zero.To ensure path-traced lighting looks its absolute best, Phantom Blade Zero includes support for DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction, enabling all GeForce RTX gamers to receive the definitive path-traced experience.
DLSS Ray Reconstruction is a neural rendering technique that replaces traditional hand-tuned denoisers, using an NVIDIA supercomputer-trained AI network to generate higher-quality pixels in the noisy parts of a path-traced frame where rays were not sampled. The model unifies denoising and Super Resolution into a single model, intelligently analyzing temporal and spatial engine data to reconstruct sharper, more stable, and higher-fidelity high-resolution images.Multiply Phantom Blade Zero Frame Rates With DLSS 4.5
Enabling Phantom Blade Zero's path tracing automatically activates DLSS Ray Reconstruction on GeForce RTX GPUs, enhancing the fidelity of path tracing and accelerating frame rates with its unified Super Resolution AI model.
For players wanting higher, faster, smoother frame rates, Dynamic Multi Frame Generation enables players to activate up to 6X Frame Generation, or to have the X factor adjusted on the fly to hit a player-selected target frame rate, based on the demands of the current scene, optimizing frame rates and PC latency.
Using a fixed 6X multiplier, GeForce RTX 5090 owners will accelerate frame rates by up to 9X, giving them the definitive Phantom Blade Zero experience. With setting maxed and path tracing enabled, gameplay runs at up to 320 frames per second, and up to 240 frames per second on the GeForce RTX 5080, enabling players to max out the capabilities of today's best 120 Hz and 240 Hz OLED displays.At 2560x1440, GeForce RTX 50 Series owners accelerate frame rates by an average of 7.8X when using DLSS 4.5 with Multi Frame Generation and DLSS Ray Reconstruction, and the other technologies and hardware accelerating and optimizing path-traced performance in the background. GeForce RTX 5090 players can experience max setting, path-traced Phantom Blade Zero at up to 450 frames per second, with GeForce RTX 5080 performance hitting 320 FPS, GeForce RTX 5070 Ti performance up to 300 FPS, and GeForce RTX 5070 performance up to 240 FPS.At 1920x1080, our suite of RTX technologies boost frame rates by an average of 7.9X, enabling GeForce RTX gamers to play max setting path-traced Phantom Blade Zero at up to 600 frames per second. On the GeForce RTX 5080, frame rates exceed 430 FPS, on the GeForce RTX 5070 Ti, 410 FPS, the GeForce RTX 5070, 350 FPS, the GeForce RTX 5060 Ti, 270 FPS, and the GeForce RTX 5060, 230 FPS.On GeForce RTX 5090 Laptop GPUs, DLSS Ray Reconstruction, 6X Multi Frame Generation, and other RTX enhancements enable on-the-go, High preset, path-traced, 2560x1440 Phantom Blade Zero gameplay at up to 280 frames per second.And at 1920x1080, GeForce RTX 50 Series Laptop GPUs can run Phantom Blade Zero with High preset path tracing at up to 390 frames per second.NVIDIA Reflex Reduces PC Latency By Up To 49%
NVIDIA Reflex is a game-changer, reducing PC latency on RTX Spark and GeForce graphics cards, desktops and laptops so your actions occur quicker, giving you a competitive edge in multiplayer matches, and making single-player titles more responsive and enjoyable.
Since its debut in September 2020, NVIDIA Reflex has reduced PC latency in hundreds of games, including virtually all of the most popular competitive shooters, over 90% of GeForce gamers have activated Reflex, and those gamers enhanced over 10 billion hours of gameplay in one year alone.
In Phantom Blade Zero, GeForce RTX and RTX Spark gamers can decrease PC latency in the game's high-speed, high intensity battles by up to 49%, making gameplay even more responsive and thrilling.
Phantom Blade Zero GeForce Game Ready Driver Available Now
For an optimum experience in Phantom Blade Zero, with the high frame rates shown above, be sure to download and install our Phantom Blade Zero Game Ready Driver from our website or the NVIDIA app.METRO 2033 Redux & METRO Last Light Redux Next-Gen Updates Add DLSS Super Resolution
It's time to journey once more into the haunting tunnels of the Moscow Metro in METRO 2033 Redux and METRO Last Light Redux because a new, free "Next-Gen Update" is now available for both games, upgrading textures, adding richer environmental detail, enhancing animation fidelity, adding higher-quality audio, and refining lighting and shadows, bringing greater depth and atmosphere to the haunting world of the METRO franchise, ahead of the February 4th release of METRO 2039.
Additionally, GeForce RTX and Spark RTX players can accelerate performance with the newly-added DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution!
Upgrade The Blood of Dawnwalker To DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation Via The NVIDIA App
Rebel Wolves and Bandai Namco Entertainment's The Blood of Dawnwalker is a critically acclaimed open-world dark fantasy action RPG set in 14th-century Europe. Bloody conflicts sweep the lands, and the Black Death comes for the survivors. Vampires seize their opportunity to walk out of the shadows and claim what they've been denied for centuries: freedom, and the power that comes with it. Other creatures of the night follow their lead. Legends turn into reality, and history as we know it will never be the same.
You play as Coen, a young man turned into a Dawnwalker, forever treading the line between the world of day and the realm of night. Fight for your humanity or embrace the cursed powers to save your family. Whatever your choice, the question stands: is your soul worth the lives of those you love?
The Blood of Dawnwalker launched with DLSS Super Resolution and Frame Generation, and now they can be upgraded to DLSS 4.5 Super Resolution and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation via the NVIDIA app, enabling all GeForce RTX and RTX Spark gamers to further enhance image quality and accelerate frame rates.
Additionally, Rebel Wolves has released the massive v1.1 update, enhancing gameplay, introducing new features, and much more.
NVIDIA RTX Remix 1.6 Now Available
We recently introduced significant improvements to rendering quality, performance, and cross-platform compatibility in RTX Remix, our modding platform that enables enthusiasts to remaster classic games with path tracing and DLSS.
RTX Remix version 1.6 equips modders with new AI capabilities, including DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, 6X Multi Frame Generation, ComfyUI agent-assisted workflows, and adds native support for RTX Spark.
These enhancements are now available in Portal with RTX and our Half-Life 2 RTX demo. Both now include our complete suite of DLSS technologies, including DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, DLSS Frame Generation Performance Mode (Preset C) beta, and DLSS Multi Frame Generation up to 6X. Press Alt+X in-game to open the RTX Remix settings, and then click the "Developer Settings Menu" button to access all of the new additions.
Additionally, we've released an RTX Remix mod for Minecraft: Java Edition, enabling you to transform worlds with DLSS-accelerated path tracing.
The beta release includes a sample world from Blockworks and a high resolution physically-based rendered materials resource pack from NVIDIA Lightspeed Studios. Players can use these samples to experience the stunning path-traced mod, and creators can use them as a starting point for building their own breathtaking, path-traced world.
The Boss Gangster: Criminal Empire Available Now with DLSS Super Resolution
Build a criminal empire from the streets up. Commit crimes in third-person, run and automate illegal businesses, recruit your own crime family, fight rival organizations, and take control of a seamless open-world city in The Boss Gangster: Criminal Empire from BEF Games and Tripwire Presents.
Killing Floor 3: Halloween Horrors Update Is Out Now With DLSS
Tripwire Interactive's Killing Floor 3 is the latest installment in the legendary co-op action-horror FPS series. Set 70 years after the events of Killing Floor 2, megacorp Horzine has produced the ultimate army: an obedient horde of bio-engineered monstrosities called Zeds. Now, the only thing standing between these infernal creations and the future of humanity is the rebel rogue group known as Nightfall. This intense first-person shooter puts players in the role of a Nightfall specialist, joining forces with up to five teammates as they battle through a war-ravaged, dystopian future, surviving unrelenting waves of Zeds, unlocking new skills, and building the ultimate arsenal.
Now, there's even more content to experience thanks to the Killing Floor 3's Halloween Horrors update that brings the Halloween season to 2091, with a new Haunted Hotel map filled with deadly tricks and Halloween-themed Zeds, plus new single-weapon Gunslinger primary weapons, a new Supply Pass and store cosmetics, and much more. And until November 5th, there'll be new Halloween models for all base Zeds and the recently added Moorcroft boss on all maps, inspired by classic horror movies, and a completely redecorated player Stronghold to set the stage for this spooktacular time of year.
Killing Floor 3 players can accelerate performance with DLSS Super Resolution and Multi Frame Generation. Via the NVIDIA app, Super Resolution can be upgraded to our latest models for improved image quality, and Dynamic Multi Frame Generation can be activated, for the absolute highest frame rates when blasting waves of Zeds.
Head Back Soon For Even More RTX Games
There are even more DLSS integrations arriving soon for a whole host of games.
