articles.title: Wazuh and AI for Enhanced SOC Workflows
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence (AI) has become one of this decade's defining technologies. From healthcare and finance to manufacturing and education, organizations increasingly rely on AI to automate repetitive tasks, uncover patterns hidden within large datasets, and support faster decision-making. Cybersecurity has experienced a similar transformation. While attackers employ AI to automate cyberattacks and accelerate vulnerability discovery, defenders are adopting AI to improve threat detection and enhance incident response.
Security Operations Centers (SOCs) receive a high volume of alerts from endpoints, cloud workloads, network devices, identity providers, and business applications. Although SIEM and XDR platforms provide visibility into these environments, analysts often spend considerable time correlating alerts, searching documentation, and determining the next investigative steps. AI offers a practical way to augment analysts by providing contextual explanations, summarizing findings, and recommending remediation actions, rather than replacing human expertise.
Challenges facing modern SOCs
Modern SOCs are expected to detect and respond to sophisticated threats while processing millions of security events every day. High alert volumes contribute to analyst fatigue and increase the likelihood that critical events are overlooked. Investigations frequently require switching between dashboards, documentation, vulnerability databases, and threat intelligence feeds before a complete picture emerges. As infrastructures become increasingly distributed across on-premises and cloud environments, maintaining consistent situational awareness becomes more difficult. AI-assisted workflows help address these challenges by reducing repetitive analysis, adding context, and accelerating investigative decision-making.
Wazuh and artificial intelligence for enhanced SOC workflows
Wazuh promotes flexible AI adoption through the Wazuh AI Analyst available on the Wazuh Cloud and integrations with third-party AI providers. Organizations can leverage the Wazuh AI Analyst capability on the Wazuh Cloud for guidance on their environment's security posture. Organizations that self-deploy Wazuh can also leverage Wazuh integrations with AI providers. The following sections highlight further details:
The Wazuh AI Analyst
The Wazuh AI Analyst is automated and hands-off. It is an AI-powered security analysis service for Wazuh Cloud subscriptions that processes your security data through Amazon Bedrock and Anthropic’s Claude, delivering insights without any manual configuration. It periodically emails key indicators, a histogram of protected endpoints, alert volume, active vulnerabilities, and a posture summary with a full PDF report attached.
The reports are generated on your Wazuh Cloud subscription’s schedule and are periodically sent to your registered email address. You can also view them from the Wazuh Cloud console in the Environments > AI Reports page.
On privacy, subscription data is not shared with third parties and is not used to train AI models; it is processed only to generate your reports, with encrypted transmission, isolated processing, and no permanent storage. As with any AI output, the recommendations are advisory and should be validated against your own policies before you act.
Threat hunting and security operations with external AI integrations
Beyond the Wazuh AI Analyst, you can expand Wazuh capabilities using a self-hosted LLM and externally managed AI integrations tailored to your needs.
Self-hosted Llama 3 and Ollama
This integration keeps everything on your own network. Ollama runs the Meta open-source Llama LLM locally on the Wazuh server; a Python script decompresses the archived logs for a chosen period, vectorizes them into a FAISS store, and serves a LangChain-powered chatbot you can query. Nothing is sent to a cloud provider, which makes it well-suited to teams with strict privacy or data-residency requirements.
Full setup steps are in the Wazuh blog post: Leveraging artificial intelligence for threat hunting in Wazuh.
Externally managed integration with Claude 3.5 Haiku
This integration surfaces Anthropic’s Claude 3.5 Haiku, hosted on Amazon Bedrock, as a chat box inside the dashboard through the OpenSearch Assistant. Setup involves enabling the model in Bedrock, installing the relevant OpenSearch plugins, and creating an ML Commons connector, model, and conversational agent. The assistant can provide useful guidance on many common tasks, including what to do about a finding and how to configure certain settings.
Full setup steps are in the Wazuh blog post: Leveraging Claude Haiku in the Wazuh dashboard for LLM-powered insights.
Conclusion
Artificial intelligence is becoming an important capability in modern SOCs. Rather than replacing analysts, it can reduce repetitive work, accelerate investigations, and provide contextual support for detection, triage, and response activities. These capabilities can help security teams operate more efficiently while keeping analysts responsible for validation and consequential decisions.
For Wazuh Cloud users, the Wazuh AI Analyst provides automated, scheduled security reports covering key indicators, alert activity, endpoint coverage, active vulnerabilities, and overall security posture. Organizations can further tailor AI-enabled security operations through self-hosted LLM integrations for privacy-sensitive threat hunting or externally managed, cloud-hosted models, aligning adoption with their operational, privacy, and data-residency requirements.

articles.title: La Commission électorale fédérale américaine cible d'une cyberattaque
articles.text:
À mois d'une semaine des élections des midterms aux États-Unis, le site web de la Commission électorale du pays est visé par une cyberattaque.
Aujourd'hui, l'une des manières les plus simples de faire mal à un pays est de l'attaquer informatiquement au moment des élections, soit pour favoriser un personnage, soit, plus généralement, simplement pour créer des disruptions et essayer de créer le doute. En France, même une simple primaire comme la primaire de la gauche a ainsi dernièrement été perturbée par une attaque de bots. Et les élections de mi-mandat aux États-Unis ne semblent pas échapper au phénomène.
Protégez votre entreprise gratuitement pendant 30 jours
Découvrez Bitdefender Ultimate Small Business Security et protégez votre activité contre les cybermenaces. Aucune coordonnée bancaire requise.
Le portail web de la Commission électorale ciblé par un piratage
Un mail, auquel Reuters a pu accéder, nous apprend en ce début de semaine que le portail web de la Commission électorale fédérale américaine a été la cible d'une cyberattaque.
Celle-ci a ainsi obligé la Commission a mettre hors ligne son système de dépôt électronique. À l'heure actuelle, elle a indiqué voir identifié le problème, consécutif à la cyberattaque, et être en train de mettre en place un correctif.
Il ne devrait y avoir aucune incidence sur les élections de mi-mandat
Il faut préciser tout de suite que la Commission électorale ne joue aucun rôle dans le décompte des voix - ceci est du ressort des États et des autorités locales. La Commission électorale américaine joue elle un rôle de supervision des dépenses électorales, fait respecter les plafonds des contribution financières et gère l'enregistrement des PAC ou Super PAC (les comités de soutien politique).
Cette cyberattaque empêche ainsi de suivre combien les groupes politiques ont dépensé sur telle ou telle élection spécifique les dernières 24 et 48 heures. Ce qui reste tout de même un point important, quand on sait que dorénavant, ces midterms 2026 sont devenues les élections les plus chères de l'histoire, avec près de 11,21 milliards de dollars dépensés, ce qui dépasse déjà ce que l'on avait pu voir en 2024, avec 11,2 milliards de dollars dépensés (dont 3,2 milliards par les deux candidats à l'élection présidentielle).
Source : Reuters

articles.title: 10 dispositivos y accesorios que puedes conectar en el puerto USB del celular, más allá del cargador
articles.text:
El puerto USB-C de un teléfono tiene funciones que van mucho más allá de la carga de batería. Teclados, discos externos, cámaras y hasta redes por cable pueden pasar por ese mismo conector y mejorar el uso del celular.
La razón está en el propio diseño del USB-C: a diferencia de conectores anteriores, no se limita a transmitir electricidad, sino también datos, audio y video, e incluso puede alimentar otros dispositivos. Esa versatilidad explica por qué un mismo puerto admite usos tan distintos entre sí.
Dispositivos que se pueden conectar al puerto USB del celular
- Periféricos: teclados, ratones y mandos
Casi cualquier teclado o mouse USB puede conectarse a un teléfono mediante el cable o adaptador correcto.
Los mandos de videojuegos siguen la misma lógica. El DualSense de PlayStation se conecta de forma directa gracias a su propio puerto USB-C, mientras que soluciones como el Backbone Pro sujetan el teléfono y permiten jugar con carga simultánea si se usa un hub con esa función. La limitación habitual es que, sin un accesorio adicional, no se puede cargar el equipo y usar el mando al mismo tiempo.
Los hubs USB-C amplían estas posibilidades al sumar varios puertos en un mismo cable. Prácticamente cualquier hub funciona con un teléfono, y los modelos con paso de energía permiten cargar el equipo mientras se usan otros periféricos conectados.
- Almacenamiento externo y lectores de tarjetas
Los teléfonos pueden leer y escribir en unidades externas como pendrives, discos duros y unidades de estado sólido, siempre que el dispositivo use un sistema de archivos compatible, entre ellos exFAT o FAT32. Las particiones en NTFS, propias de Windows, no son reconocidas.
Algunos modelos de iPhone permiten además grabar video en 4K a altas tasas de bits directamente sobre una unidad SSD conectada por USB-C, siempre que el cable admita velocidades de transferencia de 10Gbit/s y la unidad alcance los 220MB/s o 440MB/s según la resolución elegida. Para creadores de contenido y periodistas, esto evita depender del almacenamiento interno del equipo.
Los lectores de tarjetas SD y microSD funcionan de forma similar y suelen venir integrados en muchos hubs. El teléfono reconoce la tarjeta en cuanto detecta contenido en ella, y permite tanto gestionar archivos como importar fotografías directamente a la galería.
Las cámaras digitales también pueden conectarse como si fueran una unidad de almacenamiento más. En pruebas con una cámara Sony, el equipo debió adaptarse de micro USB a USB-C y mantenerse encendido para que el teléfono lo reconociera como dispositivo de transferencia.
- Pantallas externas y proyección de video
Muchos teléfonos pueden enviar su señal de pantalla a monitores, televisores o proyectores mediante un cable o adaptador compatible, gracias a una función que transporta video por el mismo puerto de carga. En la mayoría de los casos, el dispositivo detecta la conexión y comienza a reflejar la pantalla de forma automática.
El resultado no reemplaza a un escritorio completo: el teléfono suele mostrar una réplica vertical de lo que aparece en su pantalla, salvo en modelos que incorporan un modo de escritorio, como el de Samsung, capaz de abrir varias ventanas y redimensionar aplicaciones como si fuera una computadora.
- Auriculares, DAC y micrófonos
La desaparición de la entrada de 3,5 milímetros impulsó el uso de adaptadores con conversor digital-analógico, o DAC, que mejoran la calidad de sonido respecto a los componentes internos del teléfono. También existen auriculares y audífonos USB que se conectan de forma directa, sin necesidad de adaptador.
Los micrófonos USB siguen un comportamiento similar. En pruebas con un modelo Samson conectado mediante un adaptador a USB-C, el dispositivo fue reconocido de inmediato y el sistema ofreció activarlo como entrada de audio principal.
- Conexión a internet y carga entre dispositivos
Un adaptador USB-C a Ethernet permite conectar el teléfono a una red por cable, con menor latencia e interferencias que el Wi-Fi. En una prueba, el equipo mantuvo la navegación incluso en modo avión, y el sistema priorizó automáticamente la conexión por cable sobre la inalámbrica.
Por último, el mismo puerto permite la carga inversa: el teléfono puede ceder energía a auriculares inalámbricos, relojes inteligentes u otro celular compatible. No está pensada para una carga completa, ya que agota rápido la batería propia, pero resulta útil para sumar minutos de autonomía a un accesorio sin enchufe cerca.

articles.title: Amazon warns engineers just using more AI doesn't make them more productive, says they should avoid tokenmaxxing
articles.text:
Amazon warns engineers just using more AI doesn't make them more productive, says they should avoid tokenmaxxing
Amazon tells engineers to focus on real results
- Amazon urges developers not to blindly focus on AI tool usage
- The era of the "Renaissance Developer" using all kinds of AI is here
- It also urges workers to shun tokenmaxxing, and focus on building a deeper connection with customers
Amazon has told its engineers to look beyond simply using AI to ensure their work gets done, and focus instead on the results of their labor.
In a memo sent to its workforce, the company warned against using “deeply flawed” metrics such as AI token usage or code generation as a measure of team success.
It also cautioned against workers chasing "tokenmaxxing", noting how, "our most prolific engineers have demonstrated that neither the developer role nor their output is defined by the use of AI."
The age of the "Renaissance Developer"
The memo, written by Terk Terkowitz, Amazon VP/Distinguished Engineer, Worldwide, and entitled "An update from Amazon engineering leadership on the role of the developer in the age of AI", signaled the apparent beginning of a new era in how the company defines its workers in the age of AI.
This includes the age of the "Renaissance Developer", who is able to blend AI tools with human judgment and domain expertise "to build entirely new things".
"AI is changing the work of software engineering both more quickly and more fundamentally than these previous trends," Terkowitz noted. "What it means to be a software engineer, and what software engineering even is, is changing quickly and durably."
What this means for Amazon's workers is a focus on "on what is not changing as we evolved the SDE (Software Development Engineers) roles".
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
This will mean a move away from "deeply flawed" metrics such as token usage or adoption of AI tools, and more focus on the impact on customers, businesses and teams.
The memo urges managers and division heads to make sure that there is "sufficient understanding" among their teams about the benefits AI tools can bring, and told workers to ensure they become "deeply connected" to their customers in order to gain a deeper knowledge of what they really need from Amazon.
"Despite the speed of change, we believe that it is still early. We all need to embrace this change and take the time to learn, or we risk being left behind," Terkowitz concluded.
“We’re just seeing the beginning of AI’s effect on software engineering. While we have a vision for what the future looks like, there’s a lot that’s still emerging. We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice.”

articles.title: LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
LattePanda Launches LattePanda Sigma 2: The Embeddable AI Single Board Server
The LattePanda Team today launched LattePanda Sigma 2, an x86 single-board server designed to bring high-performance local AI computing directly into intelligent products and systems. Built around the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H processor with Intel Arc B390 graphics, LattePanda Sigma 2 delivers up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8 in a compact form factor.
As "The Embeddable AI Single Board Server," LattePanda Sigma 2 combines high-performance computing, up to 64 GB of memory, high-speed networking, flexible expansion, and real-time hardware control in a single board. Rather than sitting alongside a product, it is designed to be integrated directly into the product itself, supporting applications from autonomous robots and vision systems to professional instruments and private AI appliances.LattePanda Sigma 2 combines the Intel Core Ultra X7 358H CPU, Intel Arc B390 GPU, and integrated NPU to deliver up to 180 TOPS of total AI performance at INT8. It features a 16-core CPU with up to 4.8 GHz clock speed, a 12 Xe-core Intel Arc B390 GPU delivering up to 122 TOPS of INT8 AI performance, and an NPU capable of up to 50 TOPS.
With up to 64 GB of LPDDR5X-8533 RAM and 136.5 GB/s memory bandwidth, LattePanda Sigma 2 provides the capacity and throughput required for demanding local AI workloads. Up to 59 GB of VRAM can be allocated for AI workloads, providing enough room for 35B-class quantized MoE models and the KV cache required by long-context AI agents. With INT4 quantization and OpenVINO, the system can run the Qwen3.6-35B-A3B model locally at around 30 tokens per second.
Built for Local AI Systems
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed to support both individual AI workloads and multi-agent local AI systems. Developers can expand compute capacity through M.2, OCuLink, or Thunderbolt 4, connecting additional AI accelerators as workloads grow. An integrated RP2350 microcontroller adds GPIO connectivity and real-time hardware control, allowing AI applications to interact with sensors and actuators. Preloaded MicroPython firmware provides a programmable interface for intelligent devices and automation systems.
Server-Class Expansion in an Embeddable Form Factor
LattePanda Sigma 2 provides extensive connectivity for storage, networking, and acceleration. It includes three M.2 M-Key slots, one M.2 E-Key slot, PCIe 4.0 x2 via OCuLink, and two Thunderbolt 4 ports. Dual 10GbE Ethernet supports high-bandwidth networking, while USB 3.2 Gen 2, USB 2.0, HDMI 2.1, DisplayPort 2.1, and eDP 1.5 provide flexible system integration options. These interfaces allow LattePanda Sigma 2 to operate as a compact local AI server or integrate directly into larger intelligent systems.
Ready for Local AI Development and Deployment
LattePanda Sigma 2 supports Windows 11 and Ubuntu 24.04 LTS or later, with compatibility for OpenVINO, llama.cpp, and Ollama. It ships with Ubuntu, GPU and NPU drivers, OpenVINO Model Server (OVMS), OpenClaw, and local AI models pre-installed on the onboard SSD, reducing setup time for local AI deployment.
Designed for Product Integration
LattePanda Sigma 2 is designed for product-level integration and long-term deployment, offering a guaranteed 3+ year product lifecycle, custom boot logos and BIOS customization options, and direct engineering support for integration projects. Its combination of local AI compute, high-speed I/O, flexible expansion, and real-time control supports a wide range of applications, including:
- Local AI Appliances—Run private RAG and AI agents while keeping sensitive data on premises.
- All-in-One Homelabs—Combine NAS, virtualization, media services, and local AI in one system.
- Professional Instruments—Capture and process high-speed data streams directly inside compact professional equipment.
- Mobile Autonomous Robots—Unify perception, navigation, planning, and real-time control on one platform.
"Local AI is moving beyond development and into the products and systems people use every day," said Youliang Yu, Product Manager of LattePanda Sigma 2. "With LattePanda Sigma 2, we are combining the computing performance, memory capacity, expansion, and real-time hardware control needed to run AI locally in a compact, embeddable platform. The goal is to give developers a practical way to put local AI directly into the products they build."
Key Specifications
- Processor: Intel Core Ultra X7 358H
- AI Performance: Up to 180 TOPS (CPU + GPU + NPU, INT8)
- NPU: Up to 50 TOPS
- CPU: 16 cores (4P + 8E + 4LPE), up to 4.8 GHz, 18 MB cache
- GPU: Intel Arc B390, 12 Xe-cores, up to 122 TOPS (INT8)

articles.title: Adobe Fixes 8 Critical Campaign Classic Flaws Allowing Code Execution and Security Bypass
articles.text:
Adobe has released patches to address multiple critical security flaws in Campaign Classic that, if successfully exploited, could result in arbitrary code execution, security feature bypass, and privilege escalation.
The list of eight vulnerabilities is as follows -
- CVE-2026-104351 (CVSS score: 9.9) - A code injection vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-104353 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An operating system code injection vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-105780 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An incorrect authorization vulnerability that could lead to arbitrary code execution.
- CVE-2026-105489 (CVSS score: 9.9) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-105781 (CVSS score: 9.8) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-104350 (CVSS score: 9.3) - A reflected cross-site scripting vulnerability that could lead to privilege escalation.
- CVE-2026-104354 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
- CVE-2026-105779 (CVSS score: 9.1) - An SQL injection vulnerability that could lead to security feature bypass.
The issues affect Adobe Campaign Classic versions 7.4.4 build 9402 and earlier for Windows and Linux. They have been patched in version 7.4.4 build 9403.
Also resolved by Adobe is a critical code injection flaw in Adobe Connect Desktop and Mobile for Windows, macOS, and Android (CVE-2026-48360, CVSS score: 9.6) that could result in arbitrary code execution.
The vulnerability has been fixed in the following versions -
- 
    Adobe Connect Desktop - 
    
  - Windows: version 2026.9.61
  - macOS Silicon: version 2026.10.66
  - macOS Intel: version 2026.10.170
- Adobe Connect Mobile for Android version 4.5
Adobe said it's not "aware of any exploits in the wild for any of the issues" addressed in the update. Users are advised to update to the latest version for optimal protection.

articles.title: « Fais attention à ce que tu publies » : TikTok met en garde ses utilisateurs français, sur fond d'offensive contre les réseaux sociaux
articles.text:
Depuis quelques heures, TikTok affiche un avertissement assez inédit aux utilisateurs français au moment de publier une vidéo. Un message de prudence qui arrive alors que l'État a durci le ton contre les réseaux sociaux, après les récents pillages.
Publier une vidéo sur TikTok en France passe désormais par un message d’avertissement. Comme nous avons pu le constater ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026, juste avant la mise en ligne, l’application prévient l'utilisateur que « la situation évolue rapidement » dans le pays et appelle à la prudence. Ce pop-up semble être une sorte de protocole d’urgence, déclenché contraint et forcé après les violences du 17 octobre, que le gouvernement attribue en partie à l’influence des réseaux sociaux. L’exécutif avance lui aussi ses pions, d’une lettre confidentielle adressée aux opérateurs à un projet de loi tout juste adopté par le Sénat cette semaine.
Ce nouveau message de TikTok en dit long sur la pression du gouvernement sur les réseaux sociaux
Le message dont nous vous parlons apparaît au moment précis où l'on appuie sur « Publier ». TikTok rappelle qu'il refuse les contenus qui menacent autrui, incitent à la violence ou encouragent des comportements criminels, et demande à chacun de signaler ce qui pourrait poser problème. Les règles ne changent pas, seule leur mise en avant est nouvelle. Les créateurs peuvent être rassurés, puisque l'avertissement s'affiche même avant une vidéo parfaitement inoffensive, et un clic sur « Publier » suffit pour continuer. La vidéo que votre serviteur souhaitait mettre en ligne était une petite imitation vocale, un contenu banal humoristique donc.
Ce pop-up est lié au fait que TikTok a déclenché un protocole d'urgence en France, où des vidéos ont été supprimées, des lives suspendus et les recherches liées aux manifestations limitées, sans oublier les produits issus des pillages mis en vente. La plateforme chinoise répond ainsi aux demandes du gouvernement, qui presse les grands réseaux sociaux comme lui mais aussi Snapchat et Instagram de retirer les appels au pillage, à l'incendie ou au non-respect des couvre-feux, ainsi que les fausses images d'émeutes générées par intelligence artificielle. Selon le ministre du Commerce Serge Papin, 1 737 annonces suspectes ont depuis été supprimées, sur des plateformes comme Leboncoin, Vinted et autres.
Le 17 octobre a marqué les esprits, jusqu'au sommet de l'État. En marge des manifestations contre la vie chère, 1 161 commerces ont été pillés, saccagés ou incendiés selon CCI France. Pour Matignon, ce sont les réseaux sociaux qui ont servi de QG aux casseurs, en hébergeant l'organisation des pillages, les échanges sur les cibles, et le partage des positions des forces de l'ordre.
Blocage des réseaux sociaux : de l'idée lancée à la radio jusqu'au Sénat
Se pose depuis la question de couper purement et simplement les applications ? Gabriel Attal a relancé l'idée, en plaidant pour un blocage « temporaire, ciblé » de certaines plateformes. Les équipes du Premier ministre ont ensuite, dans une lettre du 22 octobre révélée par le média Blast et signée par Sébastien Lecornu, demandé à Orange, Free, SFR et Bouygues Telecom de se tenir prêts à suspendre TikTok, Instagram et Snapchat pendant quelques heures, par filtrage DNS. X aurait ensuite été ajouté à la liste. Le courrier ne citait aucune base légale et demandait la discrétion à ses destinataires. Les opérateurs ont répondu qu'ils ne pouvaient pas limiter un tel blocage aux mobiles ou à certaines zones à court terme, et qu'un simple VPN suffirait à le contourner. Heureusement, la mobilisation fut plus calme, samedi dernier.
Et puis en parallèle, l'État et le Parlement avance sur le terrain législatif. Ces dernières heures, le Sénat a adopté un amendement au projet de loi « casseurs-payeurs », soutenu par la droite, la plupart des centristes et le RN. Il élargit le rôle de Pharos, la plateforme de signalement des contenus illicites. L'administration pourra ainsi exiger, sans passer par un juge, le retrait sous 24 heures des publications susceptibles de créer un trouble grave à l'ordre public, notamment celles qui incitent aux violences, aux dégradations ou à l'insurrection, sous peine de blocage ou de déréférencement. Pour les contenus les plus graves, le gouvernement voulait d'abord imposer un retrait en une heure. Il y a renoncé à la dernière minute, craignant d'être épinglé par le Conseil constitutionnel.
Le ministre de l'Intérieur, Laurent Nuñez, affirme qu'il ne s'agit pas de fermer les réseaux sociaux, seulement de supprimer des contenus. Beaucoup dénoncent une entrave disproportionnée à la liberté d'expression, et le communiste Fabien Gay craint que le dispositif ne serve à contrôler les mouvements sociaux s'il tombait entre les mains d'un régime autoritaire.
Le texte doit encore passer devant l'Assemblée nationale, mais on sait déjà qu'en cas de crise, c'est la Commission européenne qui peut activer le mécanisme prévu par le DSA (Digital Services Act). Les très grandes plateformes doivent alors prendre elles-mêmes des mesures, et aucune coupure d'accès n'est prévue. Quant au Conseil d'État, il a jugé illégal le blocage de TikTok en Nouvelle-Calédonie. Il n'excluait pas qu'une interruption provisoire puisse se justifier, mais il a censuré un blocage total, sans durée définie ni réexamen. En attendant, le ministre affirme que des appels à l'insurrection circulent déjà pour samedi 31 octobre. Le pop-up de TikTok risque donc de rester encore un moment.

articles.title: La versión falsa de WhatsApp de la que hay que cuidarse: ya afectó a 500 mil personas
articles.text:
Google Play eliminó una aplicación que se hacía pasar por WhatsApp y que, antes de ser retirada, acumuló más de 500.000 descargas. La copia, publicada por un desarrollador identificado como Agment Assets sallu, permaneció varias semanas disponible en la tienda de Android y logró engañar a usuarios.
El caso se conoció después de que un usuario de Reddit, identificado como 2ne1cheese, alertara sobre la presencia de una aplicación llamada “WhatsApp Messenger” que replicaba casi a la perfección la app oficial de Meta. La publicación original databa de septiembre, según la información recogida en la propia ficha de la tienda.
Cómo se infiltró la copia de WhatsApp
El desarrollador de la app falsa utilizó capturas de pantalla, íconos y textos descriptivos prácticamente idénticos a los de la versión real de WhatsApp.
Según usuarios de Reddit, la aplicación fraudulenta apareció en algunos países como resultado patrocinado cuando los usuarios buscaban WhatsApp para descargar en su teléfono. Esta visibilidad, sumada a la copia casi exacta de la ficha oficial, favoreció buena parte de las descargas fraudulentas.
La única diferencia visible entre ambas aplicaciones era el nombre del desarrollador: Agment Assets sallu en lugar de WhatsApp LLC, propiedad de Meta. Se trata de un detalle fácil de pasar por alto para cualquier usuario que busque la app de manera habitual.
La app real de WhatsApp supera los 10.000 millones de descargas, cuenta con más de 246 millones de reseñas y exhibe la insignia “Elección del editor”. Cualquier aplicación que se presente como WhatsApp sin estos elementos corresponde a una falsificación.
Además, en este caso, la cuenta del desarrollador solo tenía publicada esta aplicación.
Los riesgos de instalar una aplicación falsa
Una aplicación que suplanta a WhatsApp sin serlo representa un peligro directo para los datos personales y la seguridad de quienes la descargan. Entre los riesgos más habituales figura la instalación de malware o la obtención de permisos para acceder a información sensible almacenada en el teléfono.
Este tipo de software fraudulento suele utilizarse para robar contraseñas, credenciales bancarias, archivos y fotografías. La ausencia de reseñas, combinada con una ficha casi idéntica a la original, dificulta que los usuarios perciban la amenaza antes de completar la descarga.
El caso de la falsa WhatsApp no fue un hecho aislado. La misma semana se conoció otro clon, esta vez de Google Chrome, desarrollado por una cuenta identificada como Hizbartech. Esa aplicación se posicionó en los primeros resultados de búsqueda mediante campañas publicitarias y alcanzó más de 100.000 descargas antes de su eliminación.
Al igual que con WhatsApp, el imitador de Chrome replicó imágenes y descripciones oficiales para presentarse como la aplicación legítima, lo que confirma un patrón de suplantación que se repite en distintas aplicaciones populares dentro de la tienda de Android.
La respuesta de Google Play ante el fraude
Google Play eliminó la aplicación falsa de WhatsApp una vez que tomó conocimiento de la suplantación, por lo que ya no puede descargarse desde la plataforma. La cuenta de su desarrollador, Agment Assets sallu, también fue bloqueada.
Por el momento no se ha informado de medidas adicionales por parte de Google frente a este tipo de incidentes, más allá de la retirada puntual de las aplicaciones detectadas. Mientras tanto, se recomienda a los usuarios revisar si tienen instalada esta aplicación falsa y, en caso afirmativo, desinstalarla de inmediato para evitar riesgos en sus dispositivos.
Un caso similar a lo que sucede con WhatsApp Plus, una versión falsa de la plataforma de Meta que se promociona por fuera de Google Play, ofreciendo funciones mejoradas, pero que no cuenta con el respaldo de seguridad en su proceso descarga, instalación y uso.

articles.title: American Organizations Under Attack: Skyw4lker Device Code Phishing Campaign Exposed
articles.text:
Modern phishing campaigns can compromise American businesses without relying on traditional credential theft. Attackers can abuse legitimate cloud services, authentication mechanisms, and trusted business workflows to gain access to corporate accounts while leaving fewer obvious signs behind.
ANY.RUN's analysis of Skyw4lker, a device code phishing campaign primarily targeting U.S. organizations, shows how this works in practice. The campaign has focused on manufacturing, technology, and healthcare, using business-themed documents, Google-hosted infrastructure, and Microsoft authentication flows to facilitate account compromise.
For security teams, the investigation goes beyond identifying the initial lure. It requires tracing the authentication flow and supporting infrastructure, extracting reliable indicators, and turning those findings into detections that can protect the wider organization.
Device Code Phishing: A Growing Challenge for U.S. Organizations
The scale of phishing in the United States provides an important backdrop. The FBI's Internet Crime Complaint Center recorded 193,407 phishing and spoofing complaints in 2024, making it one of the most frequently reported categories of internet crime. In 2025, the FBI recorded more than 1 million internet crime complaints and $20.9 billion in reported losses, with reported losses increasing by 26% compared with the previous year.
Attackers are also adapting to organizations that have invested heavily in identity security and MFA.
Device code phishing is one example. Rather than collecting credentials through a fake login page, an attacker can initiate a legitimate device authorization flow and convince the victim to complete it. The resulting authentication tokens can then provide access to resources available to the compromised account.
How Skyw4lker Uses Legitimate Authentication to Compromise Accounts
How the Skyw4lker Campaign Works
Skyw4lker starts with a lure designed to resemble normal business correspondence, as observed in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox analysis.
| The Skyw4lker phishing kit identified in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox | 
Victims receive a password-protected document presented as a contract or service proposal. The scenario is credible in environments where employees routinely exchange vendor agreements, procurement documents, statements of work, and similar files.
From the document, the victim is directed toward a page hosted on sites[.]google[.]com, which eventually leads into a Microsoft authentication flow.
| Skyw4lker redirecting the victims to a Microsoft365 authentication page | 
The attacker does not need to reproduce Microsoft's login experience perfectly. The authentication itself can be legitimate; the deception is in convincing the victim to complete an authentication request initiated by the attacker.
Once the process is completed, the attacker can obtain access to the resulting Microsoft 365 tokens.
That makes the attack difficult to evaluate through identity telemetry alone. An organization may see a valid authentication event without immediately seeing the malicious context that caused it. Establishing what happened requires the security team to connect the document, web activity, authentication flow, and associated infrastructure.
The Infrastructure Behind the Skyw4lker Phishing Page
The web infrastructure used by Skyw4lker provides additional evidence of the campaign's operation.
ANY.RUN’s analysis identified obfuscated JavaScript and a PHP backend used to create a victim session, collect information such as IP address and geolocation, and repeatedly poll the backend while waiting for the authentication process to complete.
| Skyw4lker sample submissions in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox by country | 
A static inspection of the original document may reveal the starting URL, but it cannot fully explain what happens once the victim interacts with the page. The malicious behavior emerges through the combination of browser activity, JavaScript execution, backend communication, redirects, and authentication.
That makes behavioral analysis essential when the objective is to establish exactly what a phishing campaign is doing and which indicators can be trusted for follow-up detection.
View the Skyw4lker analysis in ANY.RUN’s Interactive Sandbox to see its complete attack chain and associated IOCs.
Reduce Tier 1 workload by up to 20% and give analysts more time to focus on critical threats.
Interactive Sandboxing Turns Suspicious Files and URLs into Actionable Evidence
An interactive sandbox lets security teams safely execute and interact with suspicious files, links, and documents, revealing behavior that static inspection can miss.
That matters in campaigns such as Skyw4lker, where the document is only the starting point. Analysts need to follow the attack through the browser, observe redirects and authentication activity, inspect network communication, and identify the infrastructure behind the phishing flow. All of this can be done in an isolated ANY.RUN Sandbox environment, with a result available in as little as 40 seconds.
| The Tier 1 report for the observed Skyw4lker sample available in ANY.RUN’s sandbox | 
Instead of stopping at a malicious/benign verdict, the investigation can produce URLs, domains, IP addresses, network activity, screenshots, behavioral evidence, and other IOCs. These findings give security teams the context needed to validate an alert, scope-related activity, and create detections from evidence gathered during a single investigation.
As a result, SOC and MSSP teams can reach a confident verdict faster without manually reproducing the attack across multiple tools, while the resulting intelligence can support threat hunting and detection across the wider environment. Moreover, the same workflow makes it easier for MSSPs to investigate new campaigns and turn findings from one customer case into intelligence that can be searched across other environments.
Turning Threat Intel into Earlier Detection
The value of an IOC increases when it can be used to detect another attack.
ANY.RUN Threat Intelligence Feeds (TI Feeds) provide malicious IPs, domains, URLs, and contextual information derived from sandbox investigations. 99% of unique, high-confidence IOCs are added to TI Feeds after validation, helping security teams work with intelligence that has already been reviewed.
| ANY.RUN TI Feeds provide live threat intelligence for real-time attack detection | 
ANY.RUN’s internal analysis found that up to 30% of unique malicious IOCs discovered in Interactive Sandbox sessions had already been observed by the company and were present in TI Feeds. When one of these indicators appears in customer telemetry, it can potentially be matched against existing intelligence before an analyst manually investigates the associated sample.
This creates a more efficient workflow: known malicious activity can be identified earlier, while sandbox analysis provides the behavioral evidence needed to investigate unfamiliar threats.
For internal SOCs, this can reduce time spent researching indicators that are already known to be malicious. For MSSPs, the same intelligence can help identify related activity across multiple customer environments. This is how the existing threat knowledge can be reused instead of reconstructed for every new alert.
Cut MTTR by 21 minutes and give your SOC more time to focus on critical threats.
Threat Intelligence Provides Context Behind the Alert
An indicator becomes more useful when security teams can understand the activity surrounding it.
ANY.RUN’s Threat Intelligence Lookup (TI Lookup) allows analysts to investigate a suspicious domain, IP address, or URL and examine its history and associated activity. In a Skyw4lker-related investigation, this context can help determine whether an indicator is connected to the campaign, has appeared in other malicious activity, or requires further investigation.
In addition, ANY.RUN’s Threat Intelligence Reports (TI Reports) provide a broader perspective by connecting indicators with campaigns, infrastructure, techniques, and observed behavior. This can reveal relationships that are difficult to see from individual alerts, such as multiple incidents sharing the same infrastructure or a suspicious domain belonging to a wider phishing operation.
When it comes to organizations in U.S. healthcare, manufacturing, and technology, those connections can be especially important. A compromised Microsoft 365 account can expose sensitive communications, intellectual property, operational information, and regulated data, making early identification of related activity critical.
How to Make Each SOC and MSSP Investigation More Valuable
A successful investigation should improve an organization's ability to detect the next attack.
For an MSSP investigating a suspicious contract sent to one American manufacturing customer, indicators associated with Skyw4lker can be searched across other customer environments and incorporated into monitoring. The same approach works within an internal SOC environment, where an IOC found after one employee reports a phishing document can be compared against historical telemetry to identify other potentially affected users.
ANY.RUN supports these workflows through API/SDK, STIX/TAXII, SIEM, TIP, and XDR integrations, allowing intelligence from investigations to feed into existing detection and monitoring processes.
The result is broader protection from the same investigation: an incident affecting one user can generate intelligence that helps identify related activity across a SOC or MSSP's wider customer base.
Uncover up to 58% more threats and gain broader visibility into emerging attacks.
Conclusion
Skyw4lker shows why modern phishing defense requires visibility beyond the initial lure or login page. By combining interactive sandboxing, threat intelligence, and contextual investigation, security teams can move faster from suspicious artifact to actionable intelligence and broader detection.
For organizations in the U.S., that means faster investigations, less repetitive manual work, and a better ability to identify related activity before it becomes a larger incident. The goal is not only to understand one attack, but to turn every investigation into protection against the next one.

articles.title: XREAL Launches AURA as the First Wired XR Glasses Powered by Android XR
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
XREAL Launches AURA as the First Wired XR Glasses Powered by Android XR
XREAL, the global leader in lightweight XR hardware development, today officially launched XREAL AURA, the world's first wired XR glasses powered by Android XR, and the world's first wired XR glasses to launch with the Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform. Announced on stage at Google's Android Developer Summit, XREAL AURA brings the full spatial power of Android XR into a lightweight optical see-through glasses form factor designed for work, entertainment, gaming, AI-powered assistance, and everyday spatial computing.
Starting today, customers in the United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea can order XREAL AURA. The company is offering a surprise limited time offer, making the 12 GB + 256 GB configuration $1,099; and the 16 GB + 512 GB configuration $1,299. Devices are expected to begin shipping in mid-November.
Chi Xu, co-founder and CEO of XREAL"This is a defining moment for XR. We built AURA for people who want the power of spatial computing without being removed from the world around them. With transparent lenses, a category-leading lightweight design, Gemini by your side, and access to the Android ecosystem from day-one, the promise of XR is more approachable than ever," "XREAL AURA is finally here, and we're so proud to unlock new ways for people to work, watch, play, and build."
The First Wired XR Glasses Powered by Android XR
XREAL AURA was developed in collaboration with Google and Qualcomm Technologies, Inc. combining XREAL's years of leadership in lightweight XR glasses and optical engineering with the Android XR platform, Gemini AI capabilities, and Snapdragon-powered performance.
Unlike fully enclosed headsets, XREAL AURA uses transparent optical see-through lenses, allowing users to stay present with the room and people around them while digital content appears naturally in their field of view. The system uses a split-compute architecture, with the main compute and battery housed in a compact puck which ensures the glasses are lightweight and comfortable for extended use.
Powered by the new Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform, XREAL AURA delivers pro-grade performance for productivity, immersive entertainment, and next-generation XR experiences -- all while keeping the glasses under 95 grams.
A Private Workspace, Theater, and Arcade That Goes Anywhere
The device is built around a simple idea: your apps, screens, entertainment, and AI assistant should be able to come with you wherever you go.
On day-one, users have access to millions of familiar mobile apps and games from Google Play, alongside many experiences specifically for XR. Android XR brings familiar hand and voice inputs to AURA, while Gemini makes the experiences more natural and intuitive by working across what users see and do.
With Wired Mirroring, users can plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into XREAL AURA via USB-C and instantly turn it into a massive private spatial window. That means a laptop, handheld gaming device, or other compatible USB-C device can sit alongside native Android XR apps in a user's spatial workspace.
Whether turning a plane seat into a private multi-monitor setup, watching a movie on a large virtual screen, or playing Android and console games in an immersive spatial environment, XREAL AURA is designed to make spatial computing practical, portable, and useful.
Launching With Made-for-XR Experiences
XREAL AURA launches with a growing library of over 150 made-for-XR experiences that are designed to showcase what this new form factor can do. As part of the launch, XREAL is spotlighting a range of new experiences alongside access to your favorite Google Play apps, including popular streaming services and more. Made-for-XR apps include:
- NBA App for Android XR - Access the NBA App developed for Android XR, seamlessly navigate between matchups and stats, and watch up to three games at a time on multiview with your NBA League Pass subscription. New for this season on Android XR, fans can also experience live games through the NBA's tabletop feature (Court View).
- Nevatars - Created by legendary actor and director Andy Serkis - A character artist's abandoned digital creations embark on a quest through her computer's depths to remind her of her creative passion and original artistic vision. Nevatars will be exclusive to Android XR at launch and free for the first six months.
- Fallout: Factions - A skirmish-level wargame for two players. On virtual tabletop, players control a unique group of miniatures, representing a core Faction from the Fallout universe, and bring them to battle the crews of other players in a fast-paced, dice-hurling, action-packed skirmish wargame - where every action can have long-lasting consequences.
- Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars - Mixed-reality adventure set in the cinematic world based on Andy Weir's best-selling sci-fi novel, where players join Ryland Grace and Rocky during a pivotal untold chapter of the mission. Work together in the face of disaster to keep the Hail Mary intact and bring their world-saving cargo to Eridani—Rocky's home planet, and Grace's new home.
- NASCAR XR App - Bringing NASCAR Cup Series racing closer with an immersive experience that gives fans a new way to follow the action at home through a live 3D track map, driver telemetry, leaderboards and spatial highlights. Between races, explore video, standings and the schedule to stay connected and ready for what's next.
- San Francisco Ballet Company's The Nutcracker - Tchaikovsky's iconic score, played by the Grammy Award-winning Orchestra, guides us along Clara's magical journey from her Victorian-era San Francisco home, through the most dazzling onstage blizzard, and onto the stunning Crystal Palace, where we meet the Sugar Plum Fairy and an international cast of characters. Captured in stereoscopic 8K with a Blackmagic URSA Cine Immersive three-camera array, the experience showcases how cutting-edge hardware can unlock a profound sense of presence for world-class performing arts,
- Galapagos - EMMY and BAFTA award-winning Atlantic Studios is bringing ambitious immersive films to Android XR and XREAL AURA, including Galapagos narrated by Margot Robbie.
- Asteroid - A groundbreaking immersive film from acclaimed director Doug Liman, will combine cinematic storytelling, interactive gameplay, live conversational AI, and natural multimodal interaction powered by Gemini. The experience launched exclusively on Android XR and will be free for all XREAL AURA owners. The project is developed by 30 Ninjas.
- Cubism - One of the most respected puzzle games in XR built around an engaging concept: fit a set of colorful 3D blocks into a target shape, but this time set in your real world thanks to XREAL AURA's optical see-through headset. Cubism is renowned for its excellent handtracking and strong spatial interaction design.
- Oh My Galaxy! - One of the world's largest XR video game developers, nDreams, is bringing Oh My Galaxy! to XREAL AURA. Oh My Galaxy! is a beautifully crafted arcade-style physics puzzle game designed from the ground up for spatial computing. XREAL AURA marks the first time the popular game will be available on an OST headset.
- Chess Club - Odders is bringing its premier tabletop strategy game, Chess Club to XREAL AURA. Chess Club is the leading chess application across major spatial computing platforms today; its standout feature is its precise native hand-tracking. XREAL AURA marks the first time Chess Club will be available on an OST headset.
- CHZZK - South Korean streaming powerhouse, Naver is bringing CHZZK to XREAL AURA. CHZZK is Naver's massive livestreaming and content creator platform heavily centered around gaming, esports, virtual streamers, music videos and watch parties. CHZZK includes spatialized 180- and 360-degree videos that bring VR entertainment to XREAL AURA without isolating the viewer from the real world around them.
- DB Creations - The indie studio is developing three XR games for XREAL AURA. Disassemble, mend, and rebuild a variety of gadgets and robot parts while learning about the fantastical world around you in Robo Repair. Fly a jet, pilot a helicopter, and more to complete arcade challenges right in your room with the exciting RC-inspired action of Tiny Motors Arcade. Transform your space into a thriving solarpunk city of the future with easy to connect building block elements in Table Towers.
- Landing Party - Monsarrat is a Los Angeles startup launching Landing Party, the world's first outdoor roleplaying video game. Landing Party's eight patents lays a landscape of gameplay across a real world space which players walk through to explore.
- Simply Piano XR - Coming to an OST headset for the first time with XREAL AURA, Simply Piano XR brings its finetuned hand tracking and spatial computing to merge physical instruments with digital overlays along with AI-powered real-time feedback for the ultimate XR piano-learning platform.
- Soapbox - Soapbox brings real artists and comedians into your space as life-size holograms, so you can watch an intimate performance as if they're standing in the room. Founded in 2021 with a capture studio in Hollywood, Soapbox has filmed over 170 artists in 3D and is available now on XREAL AURA.
- XR HoloMedicine - In healthcare, apoQlar is bringing their XR HoloMedicine platform to XREAL AURA that transforms CT, MRI, PET, and other medical imaging data into interactive 3D holographic models that clinicians can view and manipulate in real time. The early apoQlar workflows with XREAL AURA are showing real promise and are already making advanced medical visualization and training more intuitive for clinicians.
- ShapexXR - In enterprise, ShapesXR is moving design work into XREAL AURA's immersive 70-degree FOV, allowing teams to sketch environments, place UI, storyboard interactions, and test concepts before writing much code. ShapesXR is leading in collaborative spatial creation and for the first time, bringing its highly recognized platform to XR glasses.
- Frontline.io - Frontline.io turns complex CAD models into interactive digital twins for the enterprise space, letting technicians learn, troubleshoot, and collaborate through XREAL AURA with OST workflows. It's reshaping remote assist, virtual training, and augmented work instructions—and going further with AI agents that generate, retrieve, and guide maintenance procedures in real time, all hands-free without taking workers' eyes off the task, making the smart connected worker a reality.
- Plynk Spatial - Turns stock research, portfolio management, and trading into a spatial experience coming for the first time to OST XR glasses with XREAL AURA. Instead of viewing markets through flat charts on a phone or laptop, through XREAL AURA, Plynk Spatial users can explore 3D market visualizations, interact with spatial heatmaps, view sector performance in layouts, analyze portfolio holdings in 3D space, track market movers, and execute trades directly inside AURA, all while not losing sight of their real world surroundings.
- These experiences join a broader launch catalog of immersive movies, games, entertainment, productivity features, and spatial applications that demonstrate the flexibility of Android XR on wearable glasses. From flat apps and streaming services to spatial games and made-for-XR experiences, AURA gives users access to familiar content while opening the door to new kinds of interactive experiences.
Designed for Work, Watch, and Play
For work, AURA creates a portable multi-window workspace without requiring a physical monitor. Users can open Android XR apps, mirror a laptop, place windows in virtual space, and use Gemini to help understand or act on what is on screen.
For entertainment, AURA becomes a private theater on demand. Users can access familiar streaming apps, expand content into a large virtual display, and use electrochromic dimming to create a more immersive viewing experience while remaining aware of their surroundings when needed.
For play, AURA supports Android games and compatible mirrored gaming devices, enabling users to play on a large and immersive private display.
XREAL AURA Key Specifications and Features
XREAL AURA combines high-performance XR hardware with a lightweight wearable design:
- Optical see-through XR glasses powered by Android XR
- Under 95 g glasses design for lightweight, extended wear
- 70-degree field of view
- Sony Micro-OLED display technology
- 1200p resolution at 120 Hz
- Sound by Bose
- Snapdragon Reality Elite Platform
- XREAL X1S Chip
- Split-compute architecture with compact compute puck
- Puck trackpad for familiar, intuitive navigation
- Wired Mirroring for laptops and compatible handheld gaming devices
- USB-C connectivity using a standard connection
- Electrochromic dimming for more immersive viewing
- TÜV Rheinland certified for Eye Comfort
- Support for voice, hand, keyboard, trackpad, and game controller input
Independently Tested, Built for Confidence
XREAL AURA earned five TÜV Rheinland certifications, including Eye Comfort (5 Star), High Visibility, Low Blue Light, Flicker Free, and Color Accuracy, reinforcing XREAL's commitment to delivering an exceptional visual experience without compromising comfort or quality. Building on a longstanding collaboration with TÜV Rheinland, a global leader in independent testing, inspection, and certification, XREAL AURA underwent a comprehensive series of evaluations designed to assess critical aspects of display performance, visual comfort, and safety. By combining XREAL's leadership in spatial computing innovation with TÜV Rheinland's rigorous independent testing standards, AURA delivers a new level of confidence for consumers embracing Android XR. The collaboration also reflects a shared commitment to advancing industry benchmarks and establishing the quality standards for the next generation of wearable spatial computing devices.
That same focus on premium sensory experiences extends beyond AURA's visuals. XREAL AURA features Sound by Bose technology, with audio that is meticulously fine-tuned and provides an enhanced listening experience. Detailed mid-to-high frequencies bring out subtle nuances, while the glasses' form factor creates a natural soundscape designed to compliment AURA's immersive visual experience.
New Accessories Available at Launch
Alongside XREAL AURA (that ships with a compact and easy to carry case for the glasses, compute puck and cable), XREAL unveiled a new accessory ecosystem designed to make the experience more complete. New accessories include the XREAL game controller, designed in collaboration with GameSir. The controller features a dedicated Gemini key, giving players a fast way to access AI assistance while they play. The company also announced a wireless portable keyboard for productivity and multi-window workflows.
Pricing and Availability
XREAL AURA is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea at XREAL.com/aura. XREAL AURA is also available to order starting today in the U.S. at BestBuy.com.
Further information:
- XREAL AURA 12 GB + 256 GB: $1,279, limited time offer of $1,099 through December 2026
- XREAL AURA 16 GB + 512 GB: $1,499, limited time offer of $1,299 through December 2026
- Shipping is expected to begin: Mid-November
- Launch markets: United States, Canada, Japan, and South Korea
Source:
				XREAL

articles.title: Bank of America tells customers to stop sharing banking passwords with AI agents — agentic payments are becoming a major thorn in the side of banking
articles.text:
Bank of America tells customers to stop sharing banking passwords with AI agents — agentic payments are becoming a major thorn in the side of banking
Stop giving out your financial information
- Stop giving out your username and password to your AI assistant, Bank of America warned customers
- AI agents are now capable of making agentic purchases, but that doesn't mean they should
- Customers are being locked out of accounts thanks to erroneous purchases made by AI agents
Bank of America has requested that customers do not share their usernames and passwords with anyone, “including an Al-enabled tool or agent that offers to act on your behalf.”
As agentic AI assistants have exploded in popularity, so too has the trend of having personal AI assistants make payments on a customer’s behalf. But that has led to a regulatory headache for banking providers.
AI agents ingest everything you tell them, including highly sensitive information which can be regurgitated if there is a security flaw.
Stop giving your banking details to bots
There is an obvious pro to having an AI agent make a purchase on your behalf: if something drops in price or suddenly becomes available after being out of stock, the agent can purchase it so you don’t miss out.
But these payments can sometimes be flagged as unauthorized by financial institutions, leading to customers being locked out of their accounts. Or an agent could purchase something you didn’t want it to, putting some customers into a battle with the bank to try and get the money back.
In these cases, the onus is largely on the customer. Had the AI agent not had your banking details, the purchase wouldn’t have been made.
AI firms have been praising the helpfulness of AI agents in helping organize a busy life, or help regain financial stability through analyzing spending and finances. But there is such a thing as giving too much detail on your life. As we’ve discussed before, even organizing meetings or scheduling your day can have disastrous consequences.
Sign up to the TechRadar Pro newsletter to get all the top news, opinion, features and guidance your business needs to succeed!
The best way to stay safe when using an AI assistant is to treat it as a stranger who has the power to do anything you ask almost instantly, and not always in the way you want. And don’t forget that every conversation you have with this stranger is fed back to help train other strangers.
Via TechCrunch

Benedict is a Senior Security Writer at TechRadar Pro, where he has specialized in covering the intersection of geopolitics, cyber-warfare, and business security.
Benedict provides detailed analysis on state-sponsored threat actors, APT groups, and the protection of critical national infrastructure, with his reporting bridging the gap between technical threat intelligence and B2B security strategy.
Benedict holds an MA (Distinction) in Security, Intelligence, and Diplomacy from the University of Buckingham Centre for Security and Intelligence Studies (BUCSIS), with his specialization providing him with a robust academic framework for deconstructing complex international conflicts and intelligence operations, and the ability to translate intricate security data into actionable insights.

Points forts
- Gain générationnel.
- DLSS 4 bluffant.
- Performances en raytracing.
- Sortie vidéo HDMI 2.1b.
- Écosystème logiciel Nvidia.
- Ventilation à l'arrêt quand la carte est au repos.
Points faibles
- Connecteur d'alimentation au milieu de la carte.
La GeForce RTX 5070 Ti de Nvidia est la digne héritière du modèle précédent avec des caractéristiques équilibrées. On pense notamment aux 16 Go de mémoire vidéo empruntés au modèle supérieur et aux prestations en jeu de la carte graphique, qui permettent de jouer aisément en 2560 x 1440p, et même de flirter avec la 4K, y compris sur des jeux très récents, notamment grâce à la technologie DLSS4. Sa consommation reste maîtrisée en comparaison aux gains de performances apportés et ce modèle est pour l’instant le plus intéressant de la gamme au regard du prix.

articles.title: TechPowerUp x Chieftec Giveaway: Win Cases, Coolers, and PSUs!
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
TechPowerUp x Chieftec Giveaway: Win Cases, Coolers, and PSUs!
TechPowerUp partners with Chieftec to bring our readers from the European Union a unique opportunity to bag one of six fine pieces of Chieftec hardware. The company specializes in gaming PC case, cooling, and power-supply hardware, and have opened their vaults to give us their latest and most premium hardware to give away. Up for grabs are one each of Chieftec Iceberg 240 RGB CPU cooler, Chieftec Iceberg 240 Dark CPU cooler; Chieftec Apex Lumo case, Chieftec Vista Max case, Chieftec Polaris 3.0 1050 W PSU, and Chieftec Proton 1000 W PSU.
Both the Apex Lumo and Vista Max are spacious and well-designed EATX-capable mid-tower cases with two distinct layouts. The Apex Lumo features a mesh intake that focuses on airflow; while the Vista Max features a pillarless glasshouse to let you better show off your gear. Both Iceberg 240 series coolers are capable of taming any high-end gaming PC processor in the market. The Polaris 3.0 features a modern 16-pin connector and 1050 W power; while the Proton 1000 W offers plenty of juice for a premium gaming PC build. Open from today, the Giveaway takes in entries till November 6, 2026. Once again, entries are open for our readers residing in EU countries.
For more details and to participate, visit this page.

articles.title: L’IA devait faire économiser des milliards : seules 3% des entreprises dépassent leurs attentes
articles.text:
Les entreprises investissent massivement dans l’intelligence artificielle, mais les résultats sont encore bien loin des promesses. Selon Gartner, seules 3% dépassent leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité. Un constat qui n’empêche pas les budgets de continuer à grimper.
L’intelligence artificielle devait révolutionner la productivité des entreprises et, accessoirement, leur faire économiser beaucoup d’argent. Pour le moment, la seconde partie de la promesse peine sérieusement à se concrétiser. Selon des résultats présentés par Gartner le 26 octobre, seules 3% des organisations parviennent à dépasser leurs objectifs d’économies grâce aux gains de productivité générés par l'IA.
Un résultat particulièrement décevant quand on sait que 77% des membres des conseils d’administration s’attendent justement à ce que cette technologie permette de travailler plus efficacement tout en réduisant les dépenses.
Des budgets qui explosent sans les économies promises
Le plus étonnant est que les entreprises ne semblent pas décidées à lever le pied. Selon Gartner, 85% prévoient d’augmenter leurs dépenses dans l’IA en 2027 alors que 38% dépassent déjà leur budget initial.
Les entreprises continuent donc d’investir tandis que les économies réalisées restent en deçà de leurs attentes. Entre les abonnements aux outils, les infrastructures informatiques et l’adaptation des méthodes de travail, déployer de l’IA coûte encore cher.
« À ce stade, les organisations ne réaliseront pas d’économies grâce à l'IA », prévient CV Viverito, analyste chez Gartner, lors du HR Symposium organisé à Orlando. Ce constat ne signifie pas que les salariés ne gagnent pas de temps. Le problème est plutôt de savoir ce que les entreprises font de ces heures libérées.
Gagner du temps ne suffit pas à gagner de l’argent
Automatiser la rédaction d’un compte rendu ou accélérer l’analyse d’un document peut améliorer le quotidien d'un salarié. Mais si son entreprise ne modifie pas son organisation, ces quelques heures économisées ne se traduisent pas nécessairement par une baisse des dépenses.
Gartner a d’ailleurs mesuré ce décalage. Dans une enquête menée auprès de 1 865 salariés, seulement 21% du temps libéré grâce à l’IA a été réinvesti dans des activités plus innovantes.
Pour CV Viverito, les entreprises doivent donc changer d’approche. Plutôt que de chercher systématiquement à réduire les coûts, elles devraient utiliser l’IA pour développer de nouvelles activités, améliorer leurs services ou, encore, explorer des marchés jusqu’ici inaccessibles.
Encore faut-il savoir où investir. Une autre enquête du cabinet, menée auprès de 297 responsables des ressources humaines, révèle que 78% des équipes dirigeantes ne partagent pas de vision commune des domaines où l’IA peut réellement créer de la valeur.
Gartner recommande donc de concentrer les investissements sur quelques usages pertinents, de repenser les processus de travail et de réaffecter le temps gagné à des activités véritablement productives. Bref, mieux vaut mettre l’IA au travail que finir par travailler pour elle.
Source : Gartner via Techradar

articles.title: Cuál es la fecha en la que Meta iniciará a usar el contenido web de empresas para entrenar su IA
articles.text:
Meta pospuso del 30 de octubre al 20 de noviembre de 2026 la entrada en vigor de unos términos comerciales que le permiten tomar contenido de los sitios web vinculados a las cuentas de empresas de Facebook e Instagram. Editores y reguladores europeos pidieron frenarlos.
La empresa liderada por Mark Zuckerberg tomó esta decisión tras las críticas de varios medios de comunicación.
Así lo confirmó al medio Rapporteur un portavoz de la Autoridad de Competencia y Mercados (CMA), el organismo británico encargado de regular la competencia. La Comisión Europea también celebró la postergación.
El texto original autorizaba a Meta a usar “cualquier contenido” de los dominios y páginas web asociados a una cuenta para “proveer, desarrollar, mejorar, investigar, entrenar y mantener la integridad” de sus productos.
Después de las críticas, Meta eliminó la palabra “entrenar” y limitó el uso a “productos publicitarios y comerciales”. Un portavoz de la empresa dijo a Ars Technica que la cláusula no cambia la forma en que Meta usa sus rastreadores web y que los dueños de contenido pueden indicar sus preferencias con el archivo robots.txt.
Meta dijo que aprovechará la prórroga para explicar a sus socios qué cambia y qué no. Los términos entrarán en vigor el 20 de noviembre, salvo que cambie algo antes de esa fecha.
Siguen las críticas a pesar del ajuste hecho por Meta
Según Nieman Lab, especialistas legales consultados sostienen que los términos revisados todavía permiten un rastreo masivo de sitios web. Ese medio también señaló que la nueva redacción no menciona de forma expresa que Meta respetará el archivo robots.txt.
El Consejo Europeo de Editores afirmó que “poco ha cambiado en lo sustancial” y pidió a la Comisión Europea medidas provisionales antes del 20 de noviembre. Dos asociaciones alemanas de editores, que representan a más de 9.000 marcas de medios, calificaron el plan de “robo flagrante”.
La CMA advirtió que podría usar sus poderes de aplicación si encuentra pruebas de una infracción. Su directora ejecutiva, Sarah Cardell, dijo ante el Parlamento británico que sus opciones son limitadas porque Meta no fue designada con “poder de mercado afianzado”, una categoría que sí se aplicó a Google y a Apple.
Por su parte, el gobierno británico informó el 27 de octubre de 2026 en la Cámara de los Lores que la Comisión Europea recibió el 22 de octubre una denuncia formal de competencia contra los términos revisados. La Comisión dijo que la evaluará, y no hay decisión ni sanción anunciada.
Cómo objetar el uso de datos en la UE y el Reino Unido
Los usuarios individuales de la UE y el Reino Unido pueden oponerse al uso de sus datos mediante el derecho de oposición previsto en el Reglamento General de Protección de Datos y su versión británica. Esta opción está disponible en el Centro de Privacidad de Instagram y permite rechazar el uso de la información para la IA de Meta o por parte de terceros.
Dos usuarias de Instagram publicaron guías de cómo lo hicieron: llenaron un formulario donde explicaron sus motivos y recibieron un correo de Meta que aprobaba la objeción, según 404 Media.
Anthropic, Google, Meta y Microsoft consultan a sacerdotes para enseñar ética a sus IA
Empresas tecnológicas como Anthropic, Google, Meta, Microsoft y Amazon consultan a sacerdotes, teólogos, filósofos y referentes de diversas religiones para orientar la conducta ética de sus sistemas de inteligencia artificial.
El propósito es evitar que los chatbots adopten una sola visión moral y recoger perspectivas religiosas, seculares y políticas. Sin embargo, expertos alertan que convertir las tradiciones de fe en principios comparables puede favorecer a las religiones abrahámicas y deformar otras cosmovisiones.
Anthropic sostiene que busca respuestas más profundas y cuidadosas, mientras críticos advierten que mezclar creencias distintas en un modelo podría diluir aquello que las vuelve particulares entre sí.

articles.title: Anthropic's Unreleased AI Model Chains Flaws Into Working Chrome, Safari, Windows and Linux Exploits
articles.text:
An unreleased Anthropic AI model found security flaws in Chrome, Safari, Android, Windows, and Linux and chained them into working proof-of-concept exploits, the company said in its latest report.
The exploits were built in the lab after the model was prompted, not seen in any real attack, and Anthropic reported every flaw to the vendor first, so all of them are already patched. One proof of concept opened the Calculator app on a stock Mac running Chrome within seconds of a page loading, with no further clicks.
Anthropic's Frontier Red Team described five chains in a research post. The strongest claim is not any single bug, but that one model found several separate flaws and combined them into a working exploit, something the company says has until now been the work of a few specialist teams. That capability claim rests on Anthropic's own account.
The patches and the fact that Apple and Google credit Anthropic and its Claude model for specific fixes can be verified with the vendors.
What a reader cannot check is how much of each chain the model built on its own. Anthropic says the work needed only "initial prompting" and "little human involvement," but it does not break down what a person did at each step, and it does not name the model beyond calling it an unreleased, internal research model.
For the one flaw with its own public record, the Windows bug, the record names no finder at all. Here are the five chains, what each would do, the condition each needs, and where the fix landed.
| Platform | What the exploit does | Condition it needs | Fix | 
|---|---|---|---|
| Chrome | Runs code on the computer, outside the browser's sandbox, from one visit to a web page | One click or page load, stock Chrome on macOS | Chrome 156, October 20 | 
| Safari | Lets any website read data from other sites the user is signed in to, such as email or a bank account | One visit to a malicious page | iOS and iPadOS 26.5.2, June 29 | 
| Android | Copies photos and other data off a locked, stolen phone | Physical access to the phone, over USB | Anthropic says Google has fixed it; no public record was found | 
| Windows | Crashes a server over the network, and keeps it down by repeating | The server answers HTTP/3 requests | CVE-2026-33096, patched April 2026 | 
| Linux | Runs commands as root over the network, with no login and no user action | The server runs a multipath TCP listener | CVE-2026-98432, patched October 15 | 
In the Chrome chain, the model used four separate flaws in turn. A malicious page first corrupted memory in V8, Chrome's JavaScript engine.
A second flaw escaped V8's memory sandbox and took control of the part of Chrome that renders the page. A race condition in a feature called CacheStorage then let that code read memory it should not reach and learn the layout of the more privileged browser process.
A final use-after-free bug in FedCM, Chrome's sign-in feature, let the exploit run code outside the sandbox entirely. Anthropic says it reported 62 flaws to Google that were assigned CVEs and fixed as of Chrome 156, all rated critical or high, including 13 sandbox escapes.
Google's own release notes credit "Xinyang Ge of Anthropic, assisted by Claude" for specific Chrome fixes, though not for all 62.
The Safari chain is different because it never runs code at all. It chains flaws to obtain full read and write access to the browser's memory, then changes a single value to turn off the same-origin policy, the rule that prevents one website from reading another's data.
With that rule off, a malicious page can read a user's history and cookies and send signed-in requests to other sites. Apple fixed the use-after-free at the center of the chain in iOS and iPadOS 26.5.2 and credits "Milad Nasr and Nicholas Carlini with Claude, Anthropic" for it.
The Windows chain is the one with an independent paper trail, and it is also the narrowest. It is a denial-of-service attack: a few network packets crash the machine, and repeating them keeps it down, but it does not run code or steal data. Anthropic describes the flaw as an out-of-bounds read in the Windows kernel's QUIC handling.
The public record for the bug it points to, CVE-2026-33096, instead names HTTP.sys, Windows' built-in web request handler, and rates it 7.5 out of 10. No open source ties those two descriptions together as the same component. The CVE record credits no finder, so Anthropic's authorship of this one rests on its own post.
As of late October, the U.S. government's vulnerability enrichment marked the flaw as not exploited, and it was not in the CISA catalog of known exploited bugs.
The Linux chain is the most serious in terms of impact: it runs commands as root over the network without a login. It needs the target server to be running a multipath TCP listener. The model first leaks a kernel memory address to bypass a defense called KASLR, then reuses the same race-condition bug to redirect the program to code the attacker has already placed, resulting in a root shell.
Anthropic says its proof of concept took 48 minutes to leak the address and five more to reach the shell, and that a failed attempt does not crash the system, so an attacker can keep retrying.
The company ties this chain to CVE-2026-98432, a kernel use-after-free rated 9.8 and fixed upstream on October 15; the public record for that CVE describes an IPv4 TCP fix rather than a multipath TCP one, and the two are linked only by Anthropic's post.
Anthropic frames the work as help for defenders. It says it reported each flaw under a coordinated disclosure policy that gives developers 90 days to patch and 45 more before it discusses details beyond a public advisory, and it points security teams to its expanded Cyber Verification Program, which gives vetted professionals access to Claude Opus 5.5, Sonnet 5.5 and Mythos 5.1.
The reason the company gives for publishing is in its own words: "Now, it's something models can do with little human involvement, and then prove by producing a working exploit that anyone can run and verify."
