articles.title: KLEVV Unveils All-New CRAS V RGB Prime DDR5 Memory
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
KLEVV Unveils All-New CRAS V RGB Prime DDR5 Memory
KLEVV, the leading consumer memory and storage brand introduced by Essencore, today unveils the all-new CRAS V RGB PRIME DDR5 Gaming/OC Memory. Purpose-built for elite gaming rigs and demanding creative workloads, this new premium memory unleashes ultra-low CAS latency down to CL26 at 6000 MT/s and blazing overclocking speeds of up to 8000 MT/s at CL38, dressed in a striking black-and-gold finish and armed with dual-platform overclocking support for gamers, PC builders, and performance enthusiasts who demand nothing but the best.Refined Flagship Design and Craftsmanship
Building on the aluminium heat spreader design of the flagship CRAS V RGB, winner of both the Red Dot and iF Design Awards, the CRAS V RGB PRIME introduces a striking new black-and-gold interpretation of the series' signature look.
An advanced hard-anodizing process, combined with a specialized surface treatment, gives the modules a smooth, piano-lacquer-like sheen that adds depth and sophistication from every angle. The result is an understated yet luxurious aesthetic that offers users a fresh, premium design choice while preserving the refined craftsmanship of the original CRAS V RGB.
High-Speed Performance with Lower Latency
The CRAS V RGB PRIME further advances KLEVV's DDR5 overclocking memory lineup with tested speeds of 6000, 6400, and 8000 MT/s and CAS latencies of CL26, CL28, and CL38, respectively.
The 6000 MT/s configuration features tested timings of 26-36-36-76, while the 6400 MT/s configuration delivers timings of 28-38-38-78. For users seeking extreme frequencies, the 8000 MT/s models operate at tested timings of 38-48-48-128. All configurations are tested at 1.4 V.
The 6000 and 6400 MT/s configurations are available in dual-channel kits ranging from 32 GB (16 GB x 2), 64 GB (32 GB x 2), to 128 GB (64 GB x 2), while the 8000 MT/s models are offered in both 32 GB (16 GB x 2) and 48 GB (24 GB x 2) kits. This diverse range gives users greater flexibility to select the ideal balance of speed, latency, and capacity for their systems.
Next-Generation AMD EXPO Technology: Featuring Ultra Low Latency
"AMD EXPO Technology: Featuring Ultra Low Latency" is the latest evolution of AMD's established memory overclocking technology. The new AMD EXPO ULL profile incorporates optimized memory sub-timing settings designed to reduce latency and improve overall performance on compatible AMD platforms. As the first product in KLEVV's overclocking memory lineup to adopt this technology, the CRAS V RGB PRIME delivers a more responsive gaming and overclocking experience.
The 6000 MT/s and 6400 MT/s 32 GB (16 GB x 2) configurations are certified for AMD EXPO Ultra Low Latency. According to AMD, certified Ultra Low Latency memory can deliver an average 4% improvement in FPS compared with non-ULL AMD EXPO memory on compatible systems.
Broad Intel and AMD Platform Support
Offering broad support across the latest desktop platforms, the CRAS V RGB PRIME is compatible with AMD Ryzen processors on the AM5 platform and Intel Core Ultra 200S Plus processors.
Each kit comes preloaded with both Intel Extreme Memory Profile and AMD EXPO Technology overclocking profiles, allowing users to unlock high-speed performance through a simple BIOS setting on compatible motherboards with supported BIOS versions. With both profiles included, users can confidently choose their preferred speed and capacity without the hassle of selecting separate Intel- or AMD-specific models.
Premium Components for Uncompromising Stability
The CRAS V RGB PRIME features rigorously screened, high-quality memory ICs from a leading Korean manufacturer, ensuring consistent high-speed performance and exceptional stability under demanding workloads.
Paired with a high-density 10-layer PCB, the modules deliver enhanced signal integrity and greater resistance to interference during high-speed operation. Integrated PMIC and on-die ECC technologies further support stable power management and long-term reliability, creating a robust foundation for gaming and overclocking performance.
To ensure broad compatibility, the CRAS V RGB PRIME has also been validated on the QVLs (Qualified Vendor Lists) of four major motherboard manufacturers. Its RGB lighting supports ASUS Aura Sync, GIGABYTE RGB Fusion, MSI Mystic Light Sync, and ASRock Polychrome Sync, allowing users to seamlessly coordinate lighting across compatible components and systems.
A Complete DDR5 Gaming/OC Memory Lineup
The introduction of the CRAS V RGB PRIME further expands KLEVV's comprehensive DDR5 Gaming/OC memory portfolio.
With the CRAS, URBANE, BOLT, and FIT series available across a wide range of designs and specifications, KLEVV continues to provide flexible memory choices for different performance requirements, system configurations, and aesthetic preferences.

articles.title: Apple event live — the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is official and we're in LA to try it
articles.text:
Apple 'Pro and Tell' event live — the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display is official
Apple's launched its first touchscreen laptop — and we're in LA to see if it lives up the hype
It's been a busy week for Apple, with the launch of the M6 iMac and MacBook Pro M6 following Monday's OLED iPad Mini reveal — but it saved the biggest news for last today with the launch of the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display, its first touchscreen laptop.
TechRadar's Editor at Large Lance Ulanoff is at Apple's event in LA, and will be bring you all of our first impressions of Apple's flagship MacBook, which Apple is calling the "world's best pro laptop".
Here's everything that happened during the launch of Apple's most significant Mac launch of the year...
Apple 'Pro and Tell' event: the story so far
- Apple has just announced the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display
- Apple launched the OLED iPad mini on Monday, October 26
- Yesterday we saw the M6 iMac and MacBook Pro M6 announced
It's time to try one...
Right, that's enough about specs and pricing — it's time for TechRadar's Editor at Large Lance Ulanoff to get his hands on the MacBook Pro PROLED XDR and see if it lives up the hype of being the "world's best pro laptop", as Apple calls it.
MacBook Pro PROLED: pricing
Let's take a closer look at the slightly less exciting part of Apple's new flagship MacBook Pro — its price.
The 14-inch versions starts at $2,899 / £2,899 / AU$4,599, while the base 16-inch versions comes in at $3,399 / £3,399 / $5,499. You can pre-order today, with deliveries starting on November 6.
Naturally, moving up to an M5 Max chip or boosting memory and storage will quickly ramp up that price tag. A fully maxed-out 16-inch version with all the bells and whistles? That will set you back a hilarious $14,549 / £14,549 / AU$22,424.
Still, your sweet spot will likely be somewhere in the memory and storage options below – starting with those for the 14-inch model...
And these are the memory and storage options for the 16-inch version...
The launch as it happened
There was no livestream for today's touchscreen MacBook Pro event, but want to see the reveal as it happened? Here's how Apple CEO John Ternus introduced it in LA...
The first YouTube promo
Here's Apple's first video promo for the MacBook Pro with PROLED XDR Display — tagline 'the first-ever Mac with Touch'.
Apple sells the laptop as being a "totally portable reference monitor", with up to 2,000-nits peak brightness and a 24-hour battery life for your "all-nighter". No, not that kind of all-nighter, the work-based ones...
About that touchscreen
Apple has revealed a little more about the OLED MacBook Pro's touchscreen. It supports all the usual Multi-Touch gestures (scroll, pinch, rotate, draw and more).
Why? Apple says you can use it to manipulate 3D objects or play virtual instruments. There are also classic use cases like pinching-to-zoom on photos, docs or web pages, or sketching and annotating on the screen.
Apparently the touchscreen is on this very high-end MacBook so that designers can interact with 3D prototypes, or developers can test how touch feels in their iOS apps. All very nice, but these don't sound like revolutionary use cases for touch on a laptop — perhaps our hands-on demos will make us think otherwise...
MacBook Pro with 'PROLED XDR Display': specs
The Wi-Fi at Apple's event is wobbling, but the new flagship MacBook Pro (with the dubiously-named PROLED XDR display) is already live on Apple's website.
It's available in 14-inch and 16-inch variants, with M5 Pro (16-core GPU or 20-core GPU) or M5 Max (32-core GPU or 40-core GPU) chips. Base storage starts at 1TB (going up to 16TB on the M5 Max versions), while base RAM is 24GB (going up to 128GB on the top model).
You can pre-order it now with availability starting on November 6. As rumored pricing starts at $2,899 for the 14-inch version and $3,399 for the 16-inch model...
The touchscreen MacBook Pro is official
The 'All New MacBook Pro' (as it appears to be called) is officially here.
We don't have all the specs yet, but it has a tandem OLED display and weighs 3lbs...
John Ternus has hit the stage — and the touchscreen MacBook Pro is official!
Unusually, there's no live stream for this Apple event — but fortunately, we're inside the building in LA to bring you all the news as it happens.
We've been promised multiple floors of experiences — exactly how many floors you need to experience a touchscreen MacBook Pro remains to be seen...
5 minutes to go...
It seems those rumors about a 10am PDT / 1pm ET / 5pm GMT announcement were correct, judging by the number of people inside Apple's event.
We've been told that the whole experience, not just the products, should be special. It won't be long till we find out if that's classic Apple hype or hyperbole...
How will Apple explain this?
Apple loves to jokingly talk up its “crack marketing team,” but they’ll have their work cut out trying to frame this one, given company co-founder and patron saint Steve Jobs’ long-standing opposition to touchscreen laptops.
Sure, Apple could tell us about all the innovative software features it’s built into macOS or how the touchscreen will increase your productivity (in conjunction with Siri AI, most likely). But the fundamentals remain that same as they did years ago: this is going to involve some degree of holding your arm horizontally in a way that Jobs would said will make it want to fall off.
How is Apple going to address that elephant in the room? I’ve got no idea, but it’s going to be fascinating to see how they spin it...
15 minutes to go
We've found one of the few seats available in Apple's very dark space. Unfortunately it's behind a lot of less fortunate standing people.
Earlier, our Editor at Large Lance Ulanoff managed to get this very angelic shot under the Apple logo. Not long to go now, folks...
Why no M6 Pro and M6 Max chips?
The MacBook Pro released yesterday has Apple's M6 chip, but today’s touchscreen MacBook Pro is expected to get the M5 Pro and M5 Max, not the M6 Pro and M6 Max. What gives?
According to Bloomberg, Apple is working on AI upgrades in the M7 generation that it deems so important that it has decided to skip the M6 Pro and M6 Max (and M6 Ultra) and jump right ahead to the M7 Pro and M7 Max in late 2027.
That suggests the company ditched the high-end M6 chips and moved development resources over to the M7 equivalents, but presumably also decided it was worth launching the entry-level M6 anyway.
Confusing, we know. But here’s one way to look at it: like pretty much everything these days, AI is the likely reason.
We're in!
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
We're inside Apple's event, and it's not quite on the scale of the company's bigger keynotes.
For one, there's basically no seats, which suggests this announcement could be more about the hands-on experiences than a long presentation.
The rumors suggest that a 10am PDT / 1pm ET / 5pm GMT announcement is possible, so we might be just 40 minutes away from the official news...
Can Apple convince the skeptics?
We've asked for your opinion on the concept of a touchscreen MacBook Pro in our poll below. But what do TechRadar's resident experts think of the idea?
I asked Alex Blake, an Apple veteran and TechRadar contributor, for his thoughts on what we might be seeing today.
"I’ve long been a touchscreen laptop doubter and agree with Steve Jobs’ pronouncement that they make your arm want to fall off. So I’m going to take some convincing that Apple’s latest effort is worth the outlay, especially when they’re rumored to cost an eye-watering $2,899 and up," he said.
"I’m also wondering why Apple is making this move now. The MacBook Pro is already the best laptop in the world without a touchscreen, so Apple must feel like it’s got something really special — as it often does — with this latest product," he added.
"Perhaps if Apple had decided to make a 2-in-1 instead of a fixed laptop, I might be more tempted. But that’s apparently not what we’re getting — and if we were, the price would be even sillier than it’s already expected to be," he said.
It's time for a vote!
Okay, we've filled you in on the rumors, so now it's time to get a temperature check on your thoughts — are you interested in buying a touchscreen MacBook Pro? Let us know in the poll below...
The Dynamic Island could be a dark horse
I’m a fan of the Dynamic Island on my iPhone 16 Pro, and despite its awkward name, it feels like a genuinely useful addition to my phone. It's a rumored addition to the new OLED MacBook Pro, and I’m intrigued to see how it plays out on a Mac.
Over the years, many developers have built their own versions of the Dynamic Island for macOS, and most of them have added handy functionality in one way or another. Now it’s Apple’s turn to show us its own take on the concept.
But really, all the Dynamic Island needs to be is an upgrade over the useless notch, which won’t be difficult. That alone could be enough to convince Mac fans of its utility, even if it doesn’t blow anyone away.
Apple has gone full Hollywood
TechRadar's Lance Ulanoff is in LA for Apple's event today and is feeding me his first photos and thoughts.
As you can see, Apple's event is very much in the heart of Hollywood. The event's building has a lot of history too — CBS Columbia Square was built in 1938 and served as the home of CBS radio and television until 2007.
Passes are being handed out, we're just waiting to head inside...
OLED MacBook Pro: a pricing headache?
The MacBook Pro M6 is already expensive, starting at $1,999 / £1,999 / AU$3,199. So how much can we expect to pay for a touchscreen OLED model with an M5 Pro or M5 Max chip?
The latest speculation from Bloomberg suggests the 14-inch version (with M5 Pro) could cost $2,899, which would be the highest-ever starting price for a new MacBook model. The 16-inch version, meanwhile, is tipped to cost at least $3,399.
Of course, those are just starting prices, with extra like RAM upgrades taking the prices further skywards — Apple currently charges an extra $600 / £600 to double RAM from 24GB to 48GB, for example. In other words, we should expect this to be the premium iPhone Duo of the MacBook world...
OLED MacBook Pro: what can we expect?
Perhaps thanks to the legacy of Steve Jobs’ famous hatred of them, Apple’s never done a touchscreen laptop before. With a new one set to launch today, what should we be looking out for?
Obviously, there’s touchscreen functionality, and Apple is rumored to have built an updated version of macOS to accommodate touch gestures. We’re also expecting an OLED panel — likely dubbed Super Retina XDR by Apple — with a built-in Dynamic Island and thinner bezels.
There will likely be both 14-inch and 16-inch models and options for M5 Pro and M5 Max chips. Whichever size you buy, the chassis could also come in slightly thinner than existing MacBook Pro devices.
All very impressive, but this is also likely to come at a serious cost...
What’s Apple announced so far?
The touchscreen MacBook Pro won't be the first device Apple has set loose on the world this week. Yesterday we saw the entry-level 14-inch MacBook Pro get a new version with the M6 chip that Apple says “delivers up to 30 percent faster graphics and up to 25 percent faster AI workloads” versus the M5. There’s also a new N1 wireless chip that enables Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6.
The iMac also got a spec bump with the same M6 and N1 upgrades as the MacBook Pro, and it can also support two external 4K displays at 165Hz instead of 144Hz.
Finally, Apple added AI features to its Creator Studio subscription, including Generate Fill in Pixelmator Pro and the addition of OpenAI models alongside existing Apple Intelligence options. Notably, Final Cut Pro got MotionVFX templates, graphics, transitions and more.
An impressive list, but Apple's biggest news is still likely to come...
A 'Ternus teaser'
Apple CEO John Ternus posted this Batman-style teaser two hours ago — and it doesn't reveal a whole lot.
The biggest social media theory is that it points to the return of the glowing Apple logo, which we haven't seen on a MacBook Pro for over a decade.
That glowing logo was more of a translucent cut-out rather than a separate LED, but it appears that Apple's found a way to bring it back without compromising its flagship MacBook's structural integrity.
It'd certainly give this probably-very-expensive laptop an extra bit of stardust over the rest of the lineup...
Welcome to our 'Pro and Tell' liveblog
Hello, Mark Wilson here (TechRadar's Managing editor of News, UK) and I'll be counting us down to Apple's big news today — which is expected to be an OLED touchscreen MacBook Pro.
I've been a MacBook user for 20 years (yes, I'd paid extra for the matte black MacBook in 2007), so I have lots of thoughts on these surprising rumors. I'll also be bringing you the latest from our Editor at Large, Lance Ulanoff, who's in LA right now for Apple's event.
Bur first, let's it's time for a recap of what's happened so far and a closer look at those rumors, to help warm us up...

articles.title: MrBeast dará asesoría financiera a creadores de contenido para que desarrollen sus propios proyectos y negocios
articles.text:
Jimmy Donaldson, conocido como MrBeast, pasó de publicar videos en YouTube a construir una comunidad global y una empresa que abarca medios de comunicación, productos de consumo, plataformas tecnológicas y servicios móviles y financieros.
Ahora, el creador de contenido con más suscriptores del mundo será una figura central en la alianza entre Mastercard y Beast Industries, la compañía que fundó. La propuesta busca acercar herramientas, experiencias y formación a quienes quieren convertir una idea en un proyecto propio.
Mastercard y Beast Industries lanzarán programas de tarjetas de marca compartida, beneficios exclusivos y recursos para consumidores y creadores.
La iniciativa apunta a que más personas puedan transformar su presencia en línea en oportunidades económicas.
Qué trae esta colaboración con MrBeast
La colaboración entre Mastercard y Beast Industries, la empresa de MrBeast, incluirá beneficios para seguidores, herramientas para creadores y programas de educación financiera.
Entre las iniciativas previstas se encuentran:
- Promociones conjuntas, beneficios exclusivos y experiencias para acercar a los tarjetahabientes al mundo de MrBeast.
- Herramientas y recursos para que los creadores puedan gestionar y ampliar sus proyectos, especialmente quienes ya contratan equipos, lanzan productos y llegan a clientes de distintos lugares del mundo.
- La combinación de la red de pagos, las capacidades digitales y la experiencia en fidelización de Mastercard con el ecosistema de creadores de Beast Industries.
- Educación financiera práctica y recursos comunitarios, a través del Centro Mastercard para el Crecimiento Inclusivo y Beast Philanthropy.
“En Beast, innovamos con audacia y constantemente intentamos cosas nunca antes vistas. Hacer posible lo imposible, a la vez que fomentamos la bondad, es un pilar fundamental de nuestra marca”, afirmó Jeff Housenbold, director ejecutivo de Beast Industries.
“Por eso esta alianza es tan importante: nos brinda la oportunidad de soñar en grande sobre cómo podemos ayudar a las personas a adquirir habilidades prácticas, fortalecer su confianza y llevar sus ideas “imposibles” más allá“, añadió.
“La próxima generación está dando forma a la cultura y creando nuevas formas de comercio al mismo tiempo”, afirmó Jill Kramer, directora de marketing y comunicaciones de Mastercard.
“A través de nuestra colaboración con Beast Industries, nos acercamos a las personas, vinculando cultura y comercio, y abriendo nuevos caminos que transforman ideas e influencia en oportunidades económicas significativas”, agregó.
MrBeast pide un Tesla Roadster volador a Elon Musk
Jimmy Donaldson, conocido como MrBeast, pidió a Tesla un Roadster con capacidad de vuelo para usarlo en uno de sus videos. El creador publicó el mensaje en X el 17 de octubre y dirigió la solicitud a la empresa de Elon Musk, tras la presentación del nuevo deportivo eléctrico.
“¿Puedo tener uno de esos Roadster voladores para un video, por favor?“, escribió MrBeast. Hasta el momento, ni Musk ni Tesla respondieron públicamente a su pedido.
La publicación generó reacciones entre los usuarios, que imaginaron una posible colaboración entre el youtuber y la compañía de autos eléctricos.
Algunos sugirieron que Tesla le prestara el vehículo, mientras que otros bromearon con que MrBeast podría estrellarlo contra una de las estructuras de gran escala que suele construir para sus producciones.
El modelo que despertó el interés de Donaldson es el Tesla Roadster Rocket, una versión monoplaza que solo estará disponible por invitación.
Tesla todavía no informó su precio ni habilitó reservas para este vehículo, aunque su costo podría alcanzar cifras muy elevadas si se toma como referencia el Roadster Thrust.
La línea Roadster incluye tres modelos. La versión Performance, de dos asientos y pensada para circular por carretera, exige un depósito de reserva de USD 50.000.
El Thrust incorpora propulsores de SpaceX y requiere un depósito de USD 250.000. En tanto, el Rocket incorpora 10 propulsores de gas frío, alerones activos y un sistema de succión bajo la carrocería.
Tesla aseguró que el Rocket puede volar, pero no estará autorizado para circular en vías públicas. Además, Musk advirtió que el deportivo no fue optimizado para la seguridad.
Musk anticipó la construcción de una pista de pruebas con loopings en la sede de Tesla en Texas, Estados Unidos. Allí, los propietarios del Roadster podrían probar algunas de las maniobras anunciadas, incluso con funciones autónomas para realizar determinados trucos sin controlar manualmente el vehículo.

articles.title: Apple anuncia MacBook Pro com tela OLED sensível a toques; veja preços • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Apple anuncia MacBook Pro com tela OLED sensível a toques; veja preços
MacBooks Pro de 14 e 16 polegadas agora podem ser equipados com a nova tela ProLED XDR, com painel "touch".
Semana movimentada na Apple. Depois de anunciar o iPad Mini com tela OLED, além do MacBook Pro e do iMac com chip M6, a companhia de Cupertino revelou, nesta quarta-feira (28/10), versões do MacBook Pro de 14 e 16 polegadas que contam com tela OLED sensível a toques, confirmando os rumores. No Brasil, os preços começam em R$ 34.999.
É a primeira vez que um modelo da família Mac recebe uma tela “touch” (isso se desconsiderarmos os notebooks com Touch Bar, é claro). Embora tecnologias do tipo existam há anos, a Apple vinha resistindo à proposta.
A mudança de ideia pode ser uma resposta à demanda de usuários que entendem que esse tipo de recurso é útil para tarefas que envolvam design, edição de fotos ou ilustrações, por exemplo. Nesse sentido, a Apple explica que os toques na tela podem ser usados para ampliar imagens com gesto de pinça, arrastar elementos, alternar conteúdo, entre várias outras ações.
As dobradiças foram reforçadas para evitar que os toques empurrem a tela de modo a atrapalhar o usuário.
Para ser exato, a Apple chama a nova tela de ProLED XDR. Trata-se de um painel OLED Tandem, que usa duas camadas emissoras de luz. O componente pode ainda alcançar 2.000 nits de brilho (pico) e taxa de contraste de 10.000.000:1. A taxa de atualização pode chegar a 120 Hz. Aqui, a tecnologia aparece em modelos com 14 e 16 polegadas de tamanho, como já informado.
Por dentro, o MacBook Pro pode ser equipado com o chip M5 Pro ou o M5 Max. Na linha, o chip M6 está disponível somente para o MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas anunciado ontem, pelo menos por enquanto.
O equipamento pode contar também com até 128 GB de memória RAM unificada, bem como com até 16 TB de armazenamento interno.
A Apple destaca ainda que reformulou o design dos novos MacBooks Pro para torná-los mais leves e, no quesito bateria, afirma que o componente pode alcançar 24 horas de autonomia com uma recarga completa.
Outros atributos de destaque incluem:
No Brasil, os novos MacBooks Pro com tela sensível a toques têm os seguintes preços iniciais, sem considerar descontos ou promoções:
Ambas as versões podem ser complementadas com um vidro “nano-texture”, que reduz os reflexos para melhorar a percepção de qualidade de imagem, mas gera custo adicional. Considere também que há duas opções de cores: prateado e preto espacial.
Apesar de os novos MacBooks Pro já aparecerem no site brasileiro da Apple, a companhia ainda não informou a previsão de lançamento por aqui. Nos Estados Unidos, a pré-venda já começou e o lançamento oficial está previsto para 6 de novembro.
Vale relembrar que, no início da semana, a Apple lançou o iPad Mini com tela OLED e chip A20 Pro. Ontem, a companhia anunciou um MacBook Pro de 14 polegadas e um iMac de 24 polegadas com chip M6.

articles.title: Amazon tells engineers to stop ‘tokenmaxxing’ to look productive — says AI will be central to software development, but usage is not the goal, new guidelines claim
articles.text:
Amazon tells engineers to stop ‘tokenmaxxing’ to look productive — says AI will be central to software development, but usage is not the goal, new guidelines claim
Amazon still expects AI to sit at the center of software engineering, but says usage alone is not proof of productivity
Amazon wants its engineers to quit chasing token counts, warning that heavy AI usage does not automatically mean better work. In updated engineering guidelines published on October 27, the company laid out how developers and managers should gauge AI’s real impact — and the takeaway is blunt: consuming more tokens is not the same as delivering more value. Amazon is not backing away from the technology, though. “We are certain that whatever future best practices are, AI will be at the center of software engineering practice,” the company wrote.
The guidance targets ‘tokenmaxxing,’ a practice where employees deliberately inflate their AI usage to look productive on internal dashboards. According to the memo, metrics such as AI adoption rates, token consumption, code changes, and code reviews become ‘deeply flawed’ when they are disconnected from actual results. Turning them into targets, Amazon says, encourages wasteful behavior that clashes with its emphasis on ‘frugality and simplicity’ and can raise both compute bills and software complexity.
The company’s preferred yardstick is long-term results. “We believe that it is best to measure, and be measured by, long-term outcomes,” Amazon wrote. That does not mean managers should ignore usage data altogether, as input metrics remain useful when examined ‘with care and judgment’ alongside other indicators. Amazon suggests looking at both the teams using AI the least and those using it the most to determine whether adoption is translating into better delivery.
The push comes as Amazon, under CEO Andy Jassy, has been weaving AI deeply into its sprawling operations. Jassy said earlier this year that the technology will ‘change the scope and speed’ of everyday work, and he has suggested that automation could shrink the company’s corporate workforce over the next few years — though he also expects it to create ‘other jobs.’
The memo also pushes back on the idea that every task needs an AI tool. If current tooling does not benefit someone’s work, Amazon says, that is ‘a finding, not a failing.’ Engineers who can explain where today’s tools fall short are demonstrating judgment rather than reluctance to adopt AI.
In May, it emerged that Amazon employees were using AI unnecessarily to boost internal usage scores, amid pressure to use the company's tools. Workers reportedly used MeshClaw, an internal AI agent capable of handling tasks such as deploying code and interacting with Slack, to inflate their token counts.
Notably, Amazon is not the only company rethinking how it spends on AI. Uber president and COO Andrew Macdonald said in May that higher token usage has yet to translate into useful consumer features. “That link is not there yet,” he said. The remark stands out because Uber’s CTO previously revealed that the company had burned through its entire 2026 Claude Code budget by April.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
Accenture appears to also be wrestling with the same problem on behalf of its clients. Leaked audio obtained by 404 Media in June captures executives acknowledging that token spending is climbing fast as companies move from simple chatbots to agentic workflows, and that nobody can reliably predict what a given task will cost or whether it was worth the money. Accenture’s agentic AI strategy lead described it as ‘not a niche problem,’ and the firm is reportedly building an advisory tool called ‘Token IQ’ to help customers manage the bill. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman has previously acknowledged that AI token costs had become 'a huge issue', as companies faced mounting bills from heavy AI use.
Amazon, however, says it has not imposed token caps on its employees. According to CNBC, however, it shut down an internal leaderboard in May after workers were found gaming it to climb the rankings — an early example of the behavior the new guidelines are meant to discourage.
Follow Tom's Hardware on Google News, or add us as a preferred source, to get our latest news, analysis, & reviews in your feeds.
Newton Gitonga is a tech journalist covering gadgets, PC hardware, AI, data centers, and the wider tech industry. His interest in technology started early, taking apart things around the house to see how they worked, often to his dad’s frustration. His curiosity sometimes got the better of him, including a few failed attempts to fix laptops, one of them a gifted Dell XPS. He has previously written for Notebookcheck, ZyCrypto, CoinCentral, and Crypto News Flash.

It's why you have people asking for high scores on surveys after their work, for example (actual work doesn't reflect the spreadsheet). Or why people close tickets before the work is actually done (making the spreadsheet ticket time look good is more important than actually doing the work it was meant to track). And on and on. Reply

articles.title: Pour ne pas revivre le fiasco de l’IA, Intel s’offre une pépite du quantique à 2,3 milliards
articles.text:
Après avoir pris du retard dans l’intelligence artificielle, Intel ne compte pas laisser passer la prochaine révolution informatique. Le géant américain a annoncé ce lundi 26 octobre le rachat de Classiq, une start-up israélienne spécialisée dans les logiciels quantiques, pour un montant qui atteindrait les 2,3 milliards de dollars.
Intel semble bien décidé à ne pas reproduire les erreurs du passé. Alors que NVIDIA a largement profité de l’explosion de l’intelligence artificielle, le fondeur américain prépare déjà son offensive sur un autre marché prometteur, celui de l’informatique quantique. Pour accélérer, le géant de Santa Clara vient de signer un accord en vue du rachat de Classiq Technologies, une entreprise israélienne dont les logiciels pourraient devenir une pièce maîtresse de sa stratégie.
Selon Reuters et Bloomberg, l’opération atteindrait 2,3 milliards de dollars, un montant qu’Intel n’a pas officiellement confirmé. Le rachat doit encore obtenir les autorisations réglementaires nécessaires, avec une finalisation espérée au premier semestre 2027.
Classiq veut simplifier la programmation des ordinateurs quantiques
Faire fonctionner un ordinateur quantique reste une affaire de spécialistes. Contrairement aux machines traditionnelles, ces systèmes reposent sur des qubits dont le comportement impose des méthodes de programmation particulièrement complexes.
C'est précisément ce problème que cherche à résoudre Classiq. Fondée en 2020, la start-up a développé une plateforme capable de transformer automatiquement des algorithmes de haut niveau en circuits quantiques sans obliger les développeurs à maîtriser les particularités de chaque processeur.
L'autre intérêt de cette technologie est son indépendance vis-à-vis du matériel. Elle peut fonctionner avec différentes architectures quantiques dans un secteur où plusieurs approches se disputent encore la première place. De quoi séduire les entreprises qui souhaitent expérimenter cette informatique sans miser immédiatement sur un fabricant de puces.
Intel veut réunir les puces et les logiciels
Le quantique n’est pas un terrain inconnu pour Intel. Depuis plus de dix ans, le groupe travaille notamment sur des qubits de spin en silicium, une technologie qui pourrait tirer parti de ses compétences historiques dans la fabrication des semi-conducteurs.
Avec Classiq, le fondeur entend désormais réunir ses processeurs expérimentaux, ses systèmes de contrôle et les outils logiciels nécessaires pour les exploiter. Une approche dite full-stack, qui doit lui permettre de proposer à terme une solution complète plutôt qu’une simple collection de composants.
« Notre rapprochement avec Classiq transforme notre division quantique en une activité couvrant l’ensemble de la chaîne technologique », explique Lip-Bu Tan, le patron d'Intel.
L'ambition est claire. Après les CPU, les GPU et les accélérateurs spécialisés, Intel espère pouvoir ajouter les processeurs quantiques, ou QPU, à son catalogue. Encore faudra-t-il que cette technologie trouve des applications commerciales suffisamment convaincantes.
Classiq continuera de travailler avec les concurrents d’Intel
L'acquisition par un fabricant de puces pourrait inquiéter les clients de Classiq qui utilisent d’autres architectures quantiques. Intel assure toutefois que la plateforme conservera sa compatibilité avec les matériels concurrents.
Une promesse essentielle pour préserver l’intérêt de ses logiciels, mais dont la mise en pratique devra être suivie une fois le rachat finalisé. Nir Minerbi, cofondateur et patron de Classiq, estime par ailleurs que cette alliance permettra « d’accélérer l’adoption de l’informatique quantique » en la rendant plus accessible aux développeurs et aux entreprises.
Car, malgré les investissements et les annonces, l’ordinateur quantique capable de transformer réellement les usages industriels reste encore largement à construire.
Un qubit est l’unité de calcul d’un ordinateur quantique, capable de représenter des états quantiques qui ne se limitent pas à 0 ou 1 de façon strictement binaire. Cette particularité permet certains gains théoriques, mais rend les opérations très sensibles au bruit et aux erreurs (décohérence). Programmer un calcul quantique consiste souvent à définir une suite d’opérations (portes quantiques) formant un circuit, puis à composer avec les contraintes du matériel (connectivité entre qubits, taux d’erreur, temps de calcul). À l’inverse, la plupart des développeurs sur CPU/GPU peuvent s’appuyer sur une exécution plus déterministe et sur des abstractions logicielles très stabilisées.
Un circuit quantique est une représentation bas niveau d’un programme quantique, décrite comme une séquence de portes appliquées à des qubits. Partir d’un algorithme haut niveau revient à exprimer l’intention (par exemple une optimisation ou une simulation) sans se lier immédiatement aux détails d’un processeur quantique donné. La conversion automatique implique généralement de la synthèse et de l’optimisation : réduire le nombre d’opérations, respecter la topologie de la machine et limiter l’impact des erreurs. L’enjeu est de rendre la mise au point plus rapide et de diminuer la barrière d’entrée, car écrire des circuits à la main devient vite impraticable dès que la taille du problème augmente.
Une approche full-stack vise à maîtriser toute la chaîne : le processeur quantique (QPU), l’électronique et les systèmes de contrôle, le compilateur/outil de mapping, et les bibliothèques logicielles utilisées par les développeurs. Cette intégration peut améliorer les performances réelles, car le logiciel peut être optimisé pour compenser les limites du matériel (erreurs, connectivité, contraintes de calibration). En parallèle, une plateforme logicielle dite “agnostique” du matériel cherche à fonctionner sur plusieurs types de QPU, ce qui évite d’enfermer les utilisateurs dans une seule technologie. C’est un point clé tant que le secteur n’a pas convergé vers une architecture dominante et que les entreprises veulent tester des cas d’usage sans parier trop tôt sur un unique fournisseur.

articles.title: Discord Makes Content on Discoverable Servers Searchable on Google and Other Search Engines
articles.text:
Wednesday, October 28th 2026
Discord Makes Content on Discoverable Servers Searchable on Google and Other Search Engines
Discord has apparently realized that more and more companies and game studios have moved content, like announcements, guides, and product support, that would ordinarily have been hosted on blogs and forums to official Discord servers, effectively locking that content behind a Discord account and making it extraordinarily difficult to find in some cases. In response, the chat service provider has officially announced the roll-out of Server Web Pages in an effort to make discoverable Discord servers—those publicly available servers often used for support and announcements—more easily discoverable using search engines, like Google and DuckDuckGo.
Prior to Discord's launch, message boards were common, ranging from community-driven forums to official ones run by game studios. These message boards excelled at hosting long-form, structured conversations about helping people, theory crafting, and more. While they still exist today, many have moved into Discord servers. This has led to valuable information being locked in Discord conversations, inaccessible to the wider internet. We want to fix this.
Server Web Pages have been around for a while on Discord, and they have traditionally served as a way to find out why a Discord server exists before joining it. The new Server Web Pages update just expands on that functionality by adding a brief automated summary of ongoing conversations to the Server Web Page, along with other content that admins can push to the Server Web Page. These new changes will start rolling out on November 16, 2026, and admins of discoverable servers can opt out by labelling the server as a community server instead.
We expect this to help different types of communities in various ways:
- For fandoms, you can make specific channels an easy-to-find resource that answers the top questions new players ask.
- For content creators, you can more easily promote events and new content drops.
- For indie game developers, you can use public channels, including forums, to share updates and wiki-style information about your games.
Discord will also make actual messages and channels discoverable to search engines via the new Server Pages, and server and channel admins will have the ability to share certain content exclusively. Users will also be able to share or hide their content from public searches.
From mid-December 2026, answers to questions your members sent in public channels can be found in a web search, in their own words. Server admins decide which channels take part, and server members can choose whether their own messages appear. Usernames and avatars will not be shown alongside these messages
Source:
				Discord

I presume that age-gated channels are wholly exempt from any kind of public listing, so this still remains a wrinkle that won't be worked out. I know many purely informational servers have age restrictions to help combat bot waves and genuine underage accounts from entering channels meant for specialized and professional discussion.

articles.title: Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
articles.text:
Info Edge reports steady business growth ahead of leadership transition
Revenue from operations grew 12% YoY, while net profit was up 87%. Growth was driven by recruitment business, 99acres, and matchmaking services.
Info Edge (India), which owns and operates internet-led businesses, delivered steady business growth in the second quarter ended September 30, 2026. Consolidated revenue from operations rose 12.2% year on year (YoY) to Rs 903.9 crore, while profit after tax was up 87% YoY at Rs 649.8 crore.
Growth was supported by the recruitment business, faster expansion at property portal 99acres, and continued momentum in the matchmaking business. However, the education segment remained under pressure.
Profitability improved as expenses grew more slowly than revenue, although higher other income also contributed to the increase in reported profits.
There is also a leadership transition in the offing. Hitesh Oberoi is due to leave the full-time role of Managing Director and CEO on December 2 this year, after nearly 27 years with the company. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani is slated to assume an expanded executive role from December 3, subject to shareholder approval.
Operating growth improves
Info Edge operates the brands Naukri (online recruitment), 99acres (property listings), Jeevansathi and Aisle (matchmaking), and Shiksha (education services). It also invests in other businesses. So its financial results reflect both operating performance and changes in investment values.
Consolidated total income, including other income, increased 37.7% YoY to Rs 1,332.3 crore. Other income rose 164.8% to Rs 428.4 crore from Rs 161.8 crore, while total expenses increased 4.5% to Rs 588.6 crore from Rs 563.5 crore. Profit before tax, before exceptional items, rose 85.2% to Rs 747.7 crore.
Consolidated PAT reached Rs 649.8 crore, up 87% YoY from Rs 347.5 crore. This includes profits attributable to non-controlling interests in subsidiaries. The portion attributable to Info Edge’s shareholders was Rs 479.7 crore, up 51.6% from Rs 316.4 crore.
Based on consolidated revenue, expenses, depreciation and finance costs, operating EBITDA (earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation) comes at approximately Rs 354 crore, up 27.4% YoY, with a margin of 39.2%, compared with 34.5% a year earlier.
Standalone revenue from operations rose 12.8% to Rs 841.7 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 29.8% to Rs 347.3 crore. Its margin expanded to 41.3% from approximately 35.9%.
Standalone PAT, however, fell 92.9% to Rs 333.8 crore from Rs 4,720 crore. The previous year’s quarter included an exceptional gain of Rs 5,200 crore arising from an unrealised investment valuation gain following the amalgamation of Makesense Technologies with PB Fintech. The decline therefore does not represent a comparable deterioration in operating performance.
Revenue streams diverge
Recruitment remained the largest revenue contributor. The company's earnings presentation, which includes acquired businesses in its operating-business breakdown, puts recruitment revenue at approximately Rs 682 crore, or 75.4% of the total. Standalone recruitment revenue grew 13.3% YoY to Rs 632 crore, while operating profit before tax increased 19.9% to Rs 374 crore. Its operating margin reached 59.1%.
Recruitment billings grew 12.6% in Q2 and 14.9% in the first half of FY27. Candidate Services billings increased 37%, while AI and data products for recruiters and job seekers accounted for a high single-digit share of recruitment topline.
Real estate contributed approximately Rs 134 crore, or 14.8% of revenue. 99acres revenue grew 16.7% YoY, while billings increased 21.2%. Property enquiries rose over 33% and app daily active users grew 25%. Operating losses narrowed 93% to Rs 1.6 crore, while cash from operations rose to Rs 22 crore from Rs 2.3 crore. These figures indicate improving business economics, although sustained operating profitability remains a test.
Matchmaking contributed around Rs 53 crore, comprising Rs 40 crore from Jeevansathi and Rs 13 crore from Aisle. Jeevansathi revenue grew 16.5% and it reported operating profit of Rs 2 crore. Aisle revenue increased 35.1% and billings rose 40%, but it recorded an operating loss of Rs 3 crore. Combined matchmaking billings grew 23.1% YoY.
Education remained the weakest business. Shiksha generated approximately Rs 35 crore in revenue, down 8.5% YoY, while billings fell 27.2%. The company attributed the pressure to AI-related traffic headwinds, declining Google-referred search traffic and subdued student interest in studying in the US, with preferences shifting towards the UK, Australia and Europe. The business reported negative operating cash flow of Rs 16 crore.
Cash and transition
Standalone cash generated from operations before tax rose 27.4% YoY to Rs 372.8 crore. The company reported a cash balance of approximately Rs 4,976 crore as at September 30, 2026, including balances held by wholly owned subsidiaries.
The company board has declared an interim dividend of Rs 3 per share and approved an investment of approximately Rs 150 crore in wholly owned subsidiary Redstart Labs. It has also approved exits from the stakes in Medcords and Unnati Online, investments that had been fully impaired in earlier years.
Edited by Swetha Kannan

articles.title: Anthropic ha diseñado un peculiar sistema de poder para evitar que sus accionistas la controlen después de su salida a bolsa
articles.text:
Anthropic no es una sociedad mercantil tradicional. Desde su constitución, el 26 de enero de 2021, este laboratorio de inteligencia artificial (IA) está registrado como una PBC (Public Benefit Corporation o Corporación de Beneficio Público). Esta declaración de intenciones significa que sus administradores tienen la obligación de equilibrar los intereses económicos de los accionistas con los de las personas afectadas por la actividad de la empresa. Además, sus estatutos recogen que su objetivo es contribuir al beneficio público.
Dario Amodei, el director general de Anthropic, y otros portavoces de esta compañía han pregonado en muchas ocasiones que su razón de ser es desarrollar y mantener sistemas de IA de una forma responsable y garantizando el beneficio de la humanidad a largo plazo. Todo esto suena muy bien, pero la salida a bolsa de este laboratorio, que está prevista para mediados del próximo mes de noviembre, podría dar al traste con los principios a los que se aferraron sus fundadores cuando salieron de OpenAI y lo constituyeron.
La cúpula directiva de Anthropic tiene un plan para mantener el poder de decisión cuando esta empresa cotice en bolsa. La presión de los accionistas podría amenazar sus principios constituyentes, y para evitarlo los siete cofundadores, entre los que se encuentran los hermanos Daniela y Dario Amodei, han diseñado una estructura que les permitirá controlar conjuntamente el 50,1% de los derechos de voto en determinadas decisiones corporativas. El instrumento que van a utilizar para llevar a cabo su propósito es muy ingenioso.
Siguiendo los pasos de Palantir
Anthropic va a separar el control administrativo y estratégico de la empresa de la propiedad económica de sus acciones. El mecanismo que va a hacer posible este plan gira en torno a la Founder LLC (Founder Limited Liability Company o Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada del Fundador), una sociedad de responsabilidad limitada que agrupará a Dario Amodei, director general de Anthropic, a su hermana Daniela Amodei, presidenta de la compañía, y a los otros cinco cofundadores.
Este diseño encaja como un guante con el compromiso de los fundadores de donar el 80% de su participación económica a organizaciones benéficas
Esta entidad va a recibir una sola acción de clase F, que no es otra cosa que una acción especial que aglutinará el 50,1% del poder de voto en las decisiones sometidas a los accionistas. Este mecanismo se parece mucho al que usa Palantir para proteger el control de sus fundadores, por lo que, en realidad, no se trata de una estrategia nueva, aunque es relativamente inusual. Dario Amodei tendrá una participación económica relativamente modesta, pero la estructura de voto le permitirá ejercer una influencia muy superior a la que le correspondería por su porcentaje de propiedad.
Por otro lado, este diseño encaja como un guante con el compromiso de los fundadores de donar el 80% de su participación económica a organizaciones benéficas. Además, Anthropic está contemplando la posibilidad de entregar a sus empleados un tipo especial de acciones que les serviría para deshacer empates en las votaciones que estén igualadas. Esta decisión, si finalmente la lleva a efecto, respaldará el equilibrio de su estructura de gobierno, aunque el control de los fundadores seguirá siendo un elemento central.
Sea como sea, el plan de Anthropic implica riesgos. La retención férrea del control del laboratorio que planean mantener los fundadores podría disuadir a algunos posibles accionistas, a los que quizá no les convenza tener una capacidad de influencia muy limitada. Por otro lado, la salida a bolsa no eliminará la tensión entre la necesidad de ser rentable y la de preservar la seguridad de la IA. Su estructura persigue permitir a la cúpula directiva renunciar a oportunidades comerciales para priorizar la seguridad, pero no está claro cómo encajarán los accionistas que este tipo de decisiones perjudiquen sus resultados financieros a corto plazo.

articles.title: Avant le Black Friday, ce Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy tombe à 329€
articles.text:
Les offres « Black Friday » anticipées se multiplient sur les aspirateurs Dyson depuis ce lundi, un mois avant l’événement. Le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy passe ainsi à 329 € à la Fnac, son prix le plus bas sur trois mois, pour un balai de 2018 pensé d’abord pour les sols durs et dont l’autonomie dépend beaucoup du mode choisi.
Lancé en 2018, le Cyclone V10 a précédé les V11, V12 et V15 dans la gamme de balais sans fil de Dyson. Sa version Fluffy se distingue par sa brosse principale à rouleau doux, conçue pour le parquet, le carrelage et les autres sols durs. La Fnac le vend à 329 € au lieu de 449 €, soit 120 € de moins que son prix barré, qui correspond aussi au plus haut relevé sur trois mois par LeDénicheur.
Ces 329 € sont le tarif le plus bas observé par le comparateur sur la période, et l’offre est vendue par la Fnac elle-même. Elle vise surtout les logements où dominent les sols durs.
Le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy est proposé à 329 € au lieu de 449 € par la Fnac, son prix le plus bas relevé sur trois mois.
Pourquoi choisir le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy ?
- Une brosse pensée pour les sols durs : Son rouleau en nylon doux, garni de fibres de carbone antistatiques, ramasse poussière fine et débris plus gros sur le parquet ou le carrelage, sans abîmer les revêtements délicats selon Dyson.
- Jusqu’à 60 minutes en mode normal : La batterie à sept cellules suffit pour faire le tour d’un appartement à puissance modérée. Comptez environ 3 h 30 de recharge sur la station murale fournie.
- Un balai qui devient aspirateur à main : Le corps se détache du tube pour le canapé, les marches ou la voiture, avec la mini brosse motorisée et le suceur long livrés. Le bac de 0,76 litre se vide d’un geste, sans toucher la poussière.
Du parquet du salon aux sièges de la voiture
Le Cyclone V10 Fluffy se prête surtout à un ménage rapide et fréquent sur sols durs. Son moteur numérique monte à 125 000 tours par minute et ses 14 cyclones séparent la poussière de l’air, pour une aspiration annoncée à 150 AW en mode Boost. Trois modes de puissance permettent de doser l’effort, de l’entretien courant au tapis plus encrassé. La filtration associe HEPA, mousse et technologie multicyclonique pour retenir une grande partie des particules fines.
Le profil type est celui d’un foyer en appartement, avec du parquet ou du carrelage dans la plupart des pièces. Il est moins pertinent pour une maison couverte de moquette, car la brosse principale livrée est la Fluffy, prévue pour les sols durs. L’autonomie annoncée suppose aussi le mode normal : en puissance maximale avec une brosse motorisée, le Journal du Geek n’a mesuré qu’une vingtaine de minutes lors de son test du V10 Absolute. Enfin, à environ 77 dB, il reste bruyant.
Face aux balais sans fil plus récents, à budget proche
Le Cyclone V10 date de 2018 et n’a pas le capteur de détection de poussière des générations plus récentes de Dyson. Dans notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs balais, le Dyson Gen5 Detect Absolute occupe la première place, mais il s’affiche autour de 649 €, soit près du double. À l’opposé, le Dreame V20 Pro y est retenu comme meilleur rapport qualité-prix autour de 299 €, un peu moins cher que cette offre. À 329 €, le V10 Fluffy se défend pour qui privilégie la brosse douce de Dyson sur sols durs plutôt que les fonctions récentes.
✅ Les points forts
- Brosse Fluffy à rouleau doux adaptée au parquet et au carrelage
- Jusqu’à 60 minutes d’autonomie en mode normal
- Conversion rapide en aspirateur à main, avec mini brosse motorisée
- Vidage du bac sans contact avec la poussière
- Prix le plus bas relevé sur trois mois par LeDénicheur
❌ Les limites
- Une vingtaine de minutes en puissance maximale, selon un test indépendant
- Bruyant, autour de 77 dB
- Bac de 0,76 litre à vider souvent sur de grandes surfaces
- Pas de détection de poussière, contrairement aux Dyson récents
Vendu directement par la Fnac, le Cyclone V10 Fluffy revient à 329 €, quand sa marketplace le propose à partir de 408,89 €.
À 329 €, le Dyson Cyclone V10 Fluffy devient une option sérieuse pour un logement surtout en sols durs, avec l’appoint d’un aspirateur à main. La baisse de 120 € est réelle : le prix barré de 449 € a bien été pratiqué ces trois derniers mois, selon l’historique de LeDénicheur. Son âge se voit pourtant : pas de détection de poussière, et une autonomie qui fond vite en mode Boost.
Si votre logement compte surtout de la moquette, ou si le bruit vous gêne, mieux vaut regarder les modèles de notre comparatif. Pour un appartement en parquet ou en carrelage, le V10 Fluffy couvre en revanche l’essentiel du ménage courant. Et avec les offres Dyson anticipées avant le Black Friday, garder un œil sur les prix des prochaines semaines reste un bon réflexe.

articles.title: Cyber recovery planning must include storage in the AI era - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Infinidat brings storage into cyber recovery planning
Cyber recovery planning depends on the ability to restore critical data after an attack. As enterprises adopt agentic AI, the systems and information they need to protect are expanding.
That expansion is reshaping how enterprises approach AI trust and cyber resilience. AI models, agents and the software supporting them create additional targets for attackers, according to Eric Herzog (pictured), chief marketing officer of Infinidat Ltd., a Lenovo company.
“We would argue that … anything to do with AI dramatically expands the attack surface,” Herzog said. “Everything you’re doing — the [large language models], the [small language models], that AI software stack you deploy — the cyber criminals are going to go after all of that. Instead of shrinking the attack surface, you’ve actually increased it.”
Herzog spoke with theCUBE Research’s Christophe Bertrand for the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit, during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed cyber recovery planning and why storage belongs in an AI-era cybersecurity strategy. (* Disclosure below.)
Putting storage in cyber recovery planning
Infinidat’s answer is InfiniSafe, a set of cybersecurity capabilities embedded in the company’s InfuzeOS storage operating system. It includes immutable snapshots, logical air-gapping that separates the management plane from the data plane and a fenced forensic environment for examining suspect data. About 90% of the most valuable data at global Fortune 500 companies sits on enterprise storage, which makes that layer a logical place to build defenses, Herzog noted.
“You tell it what you want to do, and the storage then responds to this data center-wide cybersecurity software or the SOC and automatically starts taking action,” Herzog said. “You don’t want to waste a minute if you think you’re having a cyberattack.”
Detection comes next. InfiniSafe Cyber Detection uses AI and machine learning to scan block data, file data and VMware data stores for anomalies, rating each snapshot’s risk as high, medium or low. Some customers scan daily snapshots twice a week, while others use the tool reactively until they reach a known good copy, according to Herzog. Infinidat offers a recovery-time guarantee of one minute or less for immutable snapshots on its InfiniBox platforms.
“That guarantee is an RTO of 1 minute or less no matter how big the dataset size,” Herzog said. “Last July, we did one of our Experts Live events … If you were on that event, you would have seen us recover 9.8 petabytes in 5 seconds.”
Attackers also go after backups and replicas, which is why Infinidat works with data protection companies such as Veeam Software Group GmbH and Commvault Systems Inc., Herzog explained. He pointed to PwC’s latest CEO survey, which ranked cyber as the No. 1 business risk, as a reason to win board-level buy-in.
“What they should do is practically deploy enterprise-wide cyber storage, integrate it with the SOC or the [security incident and event management] or [security orchestration, automation and response] technology so it works together as a team,” Herzog said. “I would argue that from a big enterprise perspective, a cyberattack is a disaster.”

articles.title: Canada launches roadmap to improve telecom competition
articles.text:
The Government of Canada has launched the Telecom Competition Roadmap to improve competition and increase the choices for Canadians.
The roadmap outlines actions that the government will implement:
More choice – to increase competition and give consumers more choices, the government will make it easier for competitors to access existing networks and expand their networks.
Better prices- to help Canadians take advantage of more affordable plans, the Canadian government will spotlight competitive offers, make it easier to shop around and switch providers and eliminate unnecessary fees.
High-quality networks – the Canadian Government will make sure consumers benefit from high-quality services across the country, and the government will help companies deploy the latest fibre-optic networks, experiment with new technologies and strengthen access to reliable connectivity in rural and Indigenous communities.
The government will monitor the progress using indicators such as pricing, switching behaviour, network speeds, coverage and consumer complaints. The Government of Canada says that parts of the roadmap have already been underway, offering benefits for consumers.
Why this roadmap is important
When you think telecoms in Canada, everyone thinks of the Big Three: Bell, Telus and Rogers, and even if you think of a sub-brand like Koodo or Lucky Mobile, those are also owned by the Big Three. And while there are other options like Freedom Mobile, owned by Quebec’s Videotron, the lack of competition and options in the country has led to incredibly expensive phone plans, especially compared to other countries.
In November of 2025, the federal budget detailed the country’s plan to increase telecom competition. This includes the ‘dig once’ policy approach to help speed up deployment and allow telecoms to work together and share more of their fibre optic networks.
Source: Government of Canada

articles.title: HBO va ressusciter ce classique d'Alfred Hitchcock dans une nouvelle série prestigieuse
articles.text:
HBO va ressusciter ce classique d'Alfred Hitchcock dans une nouvelle série prestigieuse
La nouvelle Les Oiseaux de Daphné du Maurier, devenu un film culte signé Alfred Hitchcock, s'apprête à devenir une prestigieuse série produite par HBO.
Amis ornithophobes, mauvaise nouvelle pour vous : Les Oiseaux, la célèbre nouvelle signée Daphné du Maurier, va avoir les honneurs d'une nouvelle adaptation. Plus de 60 ans après le chef-d'œuvre d'Alfred Hitchcock, HBO développe en effet une nouvelle série avec l'actrice Sarah Snook en tête d'affiche.
Par le scénariste de The Leftovers
L'actrice vue dans la série acclamée Succession, mais aussi dans les films Prédestination et Steve Jobs, y jouera le rôle de Myra Massey tenu précedemennt par Tippie Hedren. Tout comme le film d'Hithcock, cette mini-série HBO se présente comme une adaptation livre de la nouvelle de Daphné du Maurier.
La série racontera ainsi l'histoire d'une femme qui vient juste de gagner la garde de sa fille, et qui repart avec elle dans sa ville natale. Mais "alors qu’un tueur est en liberté et que les menaces personnelles se multiplient, elle se bat pour protéger sa fille face à une nouvelle menace terrifiante : des attaques d’oiseaux féroces et mortelles, inexplicablement liées au crime", précise la description du projet.
Cette mini-série est écrite par Tom Spezialy (The Leftovers, Ash vs Evil Dead) et produite par Universal Television, le producteur David Heyman et Sarah Snook elle-même pour la chaine HBO et donc pour la plateforme de streaming HBO Max.
Publiée en 1952, Les Oiseaux fut adaptée en 1963 par le réalisateur Alfred Hitchcock, qui en a fait un véritable classique de l'horreur. Malgré des critiques mitigées à sa sortie, le film a été un succès en salles avec 11,4 millions de dollars récoltés pour un budget de 3 millions.
Les Oiseaux est reconnu aujourd'hui comme l'un des chefs-d'œuvre du cinéaste, aux côtés de Pyschose, La Mort aux trousses et Sueurs froides.
- Regardez la bande-annonce du film Les Oiseaux :

articles.title: Galaxy A57 despenca 58% para quem busca custo-benefício • Tecnoblog

Galaxy A57 despenca 58% para quem busca custo-benefício
Galaxy A57 (128 GB) tem tela Super AMOLED+ e câmera wide de 50 MP; celular acessível da Samsung sai muito mais em conta no Pix com cupom no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy A57 de 128 GB está saindo por R$ 1.583 no Pix com cupom VALETECH no Mercado Livre. O smartphone acessível da Samsung, equipado com câmera de 50 MP e tela Super AMOLED+ de 120 Hz, recebe desconto de 58% sobre o atual preço base de R$ 3.799, recentemente reajustado pela fabricante.
O Galaxy A57 possui uma tela de 6,7″ Super AMOLED+, evolução sutil da Super AMOLED que oferece melhor qualidade de imagem. A taxa de 120 Hz e o brilho de até 1.900 nits entregam imagens com cores vibrantes e alta fluidez nas transições em apps e games, além de garantir a visibilidade em qualquer lugar.
Seu chip Exynos 1680 e os 8 GB de RAM dão conta de apps em multitarefa e games, além de algumas funções da suíte Galaxy AI. Os 128 GB de espaço interno podem ser expandidos com planos de armazenamento na nuvem.
O kit principal de câmeras do celular custo-benefício da Samsung inclui wide de 50 MP com OIS e uma ultrawide de 12 MP, que captam belas imagens ao ar livre, e uma macro de 5 MP para aproximações de elementos pequenos. A frontal de 12 MP tira ótimas selfies. Todas filmam em 4K.
O corpo de alumínio do A57 é revestido de ambos os lados pelo vidro Gorilla Glass Victus+, resistente a arranhões e pancadas. A certificação IP68 confere proteção extra em cenários como poeira intensa e mergulhos acidentais.
Sua bateria de 5.000 mAh resiste por até dois dias de uso, segundo a fabricante. O suporte ao carregamento rápido de 45 W via cabo USB-C permite receber uma carga de 60% em 30 minutos, evitando que o usuário fique na mão com um celular sem energia durante o corre-corre diário.
O Galaxy A57 de 128 GB (R$ 1.583 no Pix com cupom VALETECH) está sendo atualizado para o Android 17 e é elegível a mais cinco updates do sistema operacional. O celular custo-benefício da Samsung conversa com redes 5G, Wi-Fi 6E, Bluetooth 6.0 e NFC.

articles.title: Apple recorta puestos de gestión en hardware mientras reorganiza sus equipos de ingeniería
articles.text:
Apple eliminó algunos puestos de gerentes de programas de hardware mientras reorganiza áreas de ingeniería y busca reducir niveles de gestión.
Los cambios, reportados por Bloomberg y difundidos por MacRumors, se producen durante una etapa de ajustes internos que también incluye nuevos nombramientos, salidas de directivos y despidos permanentes registrados en California.
La medida importa porque afecta a una estructura clave para el desarrollo de productos de Apple. La compañía no anunció una reducción de plantilla para toda la empresa ni precisó cuántos gerentes fueron desvinculados. Sin embargo, los datos disponibles muestran una revisión de áreas técnicas mientras la inversión en investigación y desarrollo sigue en aumento.
La división de hardware cambia puestos directivos y equipos de pantallas
Según la información publicada el 25 de octubre, John Ternus y el responsable de hardware, Johny Srouji, impulsan una estructura con menos niveles de gestión. Las salidas reportadas ocurrieron en las últimas semanas y forman parte de una reorganización que no se limita a los gerentes de programas.
El área de desarrollo de pantallas también tendrá modificaciones. Wei Chen y John Zhong, ambos con cerca de 30 años de trayectoria dentro de Apple, pasarán a funciones de asesoramiento más acotadas. Victor Yin asumirá la supervisión de una parte importante del desarrollo de pantallas.
La empresa promovió además a tres líderes de ingeniería a puestos de vicepresidencia:
- Rajesh Ambati
- Louie Sanguinetti
- Derek Shaeffer
Sus responsabilidades abarcan componentes de conectividad de hardware y software. Los informes no detallan el alcance de sus nuevas funciones ni si la reestructuración se extenderá a otros equipos de producto.
California registró 147 despidos permanentes en tres sedes
Los documentos del Departamento de Desarrollo del Empleo de California muestran 147 despidos permanentes en tres ubicaciones de Apple. La notificación se presentó el 20 de agosto de 2026 y fijó el 19 de octubre como fecha de entrada en vigor.
Los puestos se distribuyeron de esta manera:
- 79 empleos en One Apple Park Way, en Cupertino.
- 40 empleos en 605 W. Maude Avenue, en Sunnyvale.
- 28 empleos en 599 N. Mathilda Avenue, también en Sunnyvale.
De acuerdo con TheStreet, la presentación incluyó perfiles técnicos como ingenieros de desarrollo de software, especialistas en aprendizaje automático e inteligencia artificial, profesionales de visión por computadora, gerentes de programas de ingeniería y desarrolladores de realidad aumentada y virtual.
No existe confirmación de que los gerentes de programas de hardware mencionados en los informes de octubre formen parte de esos 147 despidos. Ambos datos corresponden a conjuntos de información distintos, por lo que no deben sumarse como un único total de recortes.
La reorganización se suma a ajustes previos en Vision Pro y Siri
Un reporte anterior, publicado el 29 de septiembre, señaló que la dirección buscaba apoyarse más en los equipos de ingeniería existentes. Algunos directores y gerentes de programas habrían perdido sus puestos, aunque recibieron varias semanas para intentar reubicarse dentro de Apple.
Ese mismo informe se vinculó con una reducción previa de cerca de 200 puestos. Según la información difundida, alrededor de 100 correspondían a la organización de Vision Pro y otros 100 a los equipos de Siri y software.
También se conoció que Apple evaluó recortar unos 5.000 empleos de apoyo ante la posibilidad de que agentes de inteligencia artificial atendieran parte de las consultas telefónicas y web. La propuesta quedó suspendida de forma indefinida, por lo que no avanzó como un plan de reducción confirmado.
La información disponible no establece que la inteligencia artificial haya provocado directamente las salidas en la gestión de hardware. Los posibles ajustes en puestos de apoyo y los cambios en ingeniería corresponden a procesos distintos.
La reorganización deja abiertas preguntas sobre el alcance de los cambios y la estructura que Apple busca consolidar en sus equipos técnicos. Por ahora, las salidas de gerentes, los relevos en el área de pantallas y los despidos registrados en California muestran movimientos paralelos, pero no permiten establecer un único plan de recortes ni atribuirlos de forma directa a la inteligencia artificial.
La evolución de los próximos meses permitirá determinar si la empresa mantiene estos ajustes en áreas específicas o si amplía la revisión de su organización de ingeniería.

articles.title: The UK Government is considering incentivizing vehicle-to-grid tech to turn EVs into 'powerplants on wheels'
articles.text:
The UK Government is considering incentivizing vehicle-to-grid tech to turn EVs into 'powerplants on wheels'
It could help the country transition away from fossil fuels
- Ministers are considering incentivizing vehicle-to-grid (V2G) tech
- It could allow carmakers to earn credits for installing V2G capabilities
- Critics say carmakers would produce more polluting cars as a result
UK ministers are reportedly considering giving manufacturers extra incentives to add vehicle-to-grid (V2G) technology to cars as part of its review of the zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) mandate.
The technology, which was arguably pioneered by Nissan in Japan in the early 2010s, supports bidirectional power transfer, allowing electric vehicles to not only be charged from a domestic charger, but also feed energy back into the grid.
Early demonstrations with Japan’s CHAdeMO charging standard showed that something like a Nissan Leaf could provide power to a home during natural disasters, and also help decrease the load on the grid during peak consumption hours.
According to supporters of the technology, increasing the amount of V2G-enabled EVs on UK driveways could help the transition away from fossil fuels to renewables, balancing the grid when wind and solar generation is lower than electricity demand.
According to a report in The Guardian, in order to incentivize manufacturers, ministers are considering offering additional Zero Emission Vehicle credits to those companies that can successfully increase the prevalence of V2G tech.
Currently, the ZEV system sees manufacturers earn credits for every fully electric or hydrogen fuel cell vehicle they register, with annual targets set for the percentage of electric cars sold each year.
Companies that fall short of their annual sales quota must either buy surplus credits from other manufacturers, borrow against future targets, or pay non-compliance penalties.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
While increasing the amount of vehicles that are capable of bi-directional charging could indeed help balance out the grid in times of peak demand, some critics claim that offering additional credits to manufacturers could lead to an increase in the production of polluting petrol and diesel models.
“Vehicle to grid is exciting technology that could help balance the grid and cut bills, but carmakers should only be rewarded if it’s actually used, not just for fitting it,” Ben Nelmes, the chief executive of New AutoMotive, a think-tank tracking the transition to electric cars, told The Guardian.
Analysis: simplicity is key
Vehicle-to-grid technology is nothing new, and the idea of the 'virtual powerplant', where the grid can give and take energy from thousands of vehicles all connected to the grid, has been on the minds of automotive manufactures for well over a decade.
Right now, Renault and Alpine offer V2G services in France through Mobilize and The Mobility House projects, while the Volkswagen Group's Elli sub-brand announced a packaged V2G offer in June for its German customers, targeting compatible VW, Volkswagen Commercial Vehicles and Cupra models.
In the UK, Octopus Energy already offers its Power Pack, which it claims is the first vehicle-to-grid tariff that could save a typical V2G driver £620 per year compared to the company’s other flexible tariffs.
However, as someone who owns a house with EVs, solar, battery storage and inverters, I know first-hand just how complex it is navigating the various energy tariffs, and calculating whether or not it makes financial sense to sell excess solar back to the grid.
Not only does this typically require several apps and a good grasp on the software that manages all of the various systems, it also demands an in-depth knowledge of energy tariffs and dynamic pricing.
Vicky Edmonds, the chief executive of the Electric Vehicle Association England, which represents drivers, told The Guardian: “These technologies have enormous potential, but consumers are still getting to grips with more immediate questions around the cost of their car, the cost of charging, and whether an EV meets their day-to-day needs”.
So, while some believe that the electricity supplied by V2G cars could add up to the equivalent of a power station by 2030, the process would have to be as simple as possible to encourage already confused motorists to adopt the technology.

Leon has been navigating a world where automotive and tech collide for almost 20 years, reporting on everything from in-car entertainment to robotised manufacturing plants. Currently, EVs are the focus of his attentions, but give it a few years and it will be electric vertical take-off and landing craft. Outside of work hours, he can be found tinkering with distinctly analogue motorcycles, because electric motors are no replacement for an old Honda inline four.

articles.title: Cloudera expands its AI ecosystem with partnerships and packaged blueprints - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Cloudera expands its AI ecosystem with partnerships and packaged blueprints
Cloudera Inc. Tuesday announced an expansion of its enterprise artificial intelligence ecosystem, introducing preconfigured AI applications built with Nvidia Corp. technology and expanding partnerships with Neo4j Inc. and Mistral AI SAS.
Cloudera said the initiatives are intended to help enterprises move AI projects into production while maintaining control over their data, infrastructure and deployment costs. Announced at the company’s Evolve26 conference in New York, the offerings reinforce Cloudera’s strategy of bringing AI processing to enterprise data rather than requiring organizations to move sensitive information into centralized cloud environments.
“We’ll bring AI to where the data is and where the data lives,” Wim Stoop, Cloudera’s senior director of product marketing, said in an interview at the conference.
The centerpiece of the announcements is Cloudera Blueprints, a portfolio of ready-to-deploy AI packages that combine Nvidia’s AI reference workflows with Cloudera’s data management, security and governance capabilities.
Built using Nvidia Agent Toolkit and deployed through the Cloudera AI development platform, the blueprints are intended to reduce the integration work involved in turning experimental AI applications into production systems.
The initial portfolio includes applications for financial transaction analysis, automated clinical documentation, telecommunications network configuration and synthetic video detection. They incorporate technologies including Nvidia NIM microservices, Nemotron models and graphics processing unit-accelerated data processing.
Stoop said enterprises increasingly understand AI’s potential but struggle with the operational and financial implications of deployment.
“The biggest challenge for a lot of organizations seems to be how to go from a pilot to something that actually operates in production without incurring horrific costs,” he said.
Cloudera also announced an expansion of its Enterprise AI Ecosystem, adding Neo4j’s graph technology to help AI agents understand relationships among enterprise data.
Neo4j’s knowledge graphs provide semantic context that can help agents connect information about customers, transactions, products and business processes. Combined with Cloudera’s governed data infrastructure, the technology is intended to support AI systems that can reason about enterprise information and take actions.
The expanded ecosystem also includes partnerships with Mistral AI and Vast Data Inc., giving customers additional options for AI models and infrastructure.
Cloudera executives said the Mistral relationship is particularly important to its sovereign AI strategy, which emphasizes customer control over data, models and infrastructure.
Organizations increasingly want the flexibility to use open-weight models within their own environments instead of relying exclusively on externally hosted proprietary systems, Stoop said. “Our partnership with Mistral is a great example of that,” he added, citing the ability to deploy models locally and customize them with proprietary enterprise information.
That flexibility matters in Europe, where data privacy requirements, geopolitical concerns and regulations are pushing companies to examine where AI workloads run and who controls them. However, Stoop cautioned that sovereign AI goes beyond keeping data within national boundaries. Organizations must also establish control over model execution, data lineage, infrastructure and operational processes.
Cloudera said its approach preserves deployment flexibility across public clouds, private clouds, on-premises infrastructure and edge environments, allowing customers to choose configurations that match their requirements.
Stoop said flexibility could also help organizations manage the economics of AI inference, where computing costs can grow substantially as applications scale. The goal isn’t to move every workload into a sovereign environment, but to let organizations choose the most appropriate deployment model, he said. “It’s important for organizations to have that flexibility to be able to choose the right infrastructure for the right job,” he said.
Cloudera is betting that combining reusable AI applications, broader technology partnerships and consistent governance across environments will help enterprises overcome the technical and economic barriers separating AI experimentation from production.
