articles.title: FCC rebuffs TP-Link again as it attempts to sell Wi-Fi 8 gear in the US — FCC alleges inaccurate documentation and out-of-spec power levels for routers
articles.text:
FCC rebuffs TP-Link again as it attempts to sell Wi-Fi 8 gear in the US — FCC alleges inaccurate documentation and out-of-spec power levels for routers
“The FCC won’t let me be”
TP-Link has been trying everything in its power to gain conditional approval from the Federal Communications Commission (FCC). According to a new Bloomberg report, the FCC is citing discrepancies in power levels in TP-Link routers as the latest roadblock on its path to selling new Wi-Fi 8 products stateside.
In letters dated October 15, 2026, the FCC Office of Engineering and Technology made some damning claims about TP-Link's reporting practices. Specifically, the FCC alleged that TP-Link "included false or incorrect information in its applications” related to equipment authorizations for four individual router models (including high-end Archer models).
For a company that truly needs to dot every "i" and cross every "t" when it comes to a Trump administration that is increasingly skeptical of TP-Link's past ties and motives, any perceived missteps are even more magnified. However, in addition to the alleged wonky product information provided to the FCC, perhaps more troubling is that three of the four routers under scrutiny also had higher-than-allowed power usage levels.
In addition to power limits, the FCC's testing regimen for routers includes evaluations of electromagnetic compatibility (EMC), radio frequency (RF) emissions, and national security compliance. The latter has been a big sticking point with the FCC and the U.S. Department of Defense given the proliferation of TP-Link networking gear in civilian and governmental capacities.
We reached out to TP-Link about the FCC’s findings and were provided with the following statement:
"Routine spot checks have been a standard FCC practice across the consumer electronics industry for many years, and individual product test results can occasionally vary.
TP-Link Systems fully supports the FCC’s Office of Engineering and Technology and its role of ensuring that all manufacturers adhere to prescribed specifications for their certified products. We remain fully committed to working collaboratively with the FCC to resolve any technical questions that arise — and if necessary, address any confirmed technical issues as swiftly as possible."
It will likely take a lot more convincing to appease the FCC, which has so far given TP-Link the cold shoulder. And it’s not just the FCC; members of Congress and multiple state attorneys general have filed their grievances with TP-Link over alleged consumer privacy violations and Chinese ties.
For its part, TP-Link has made some significant moves to get in the good graces of the U.S. government, even while competitors like Amazon, Asus, and Netgear have sailed through compliance checks to gain conditional approval to sell wireless products in the U.S. Besides moving its U.S. headquarters to California, the company earlier this month announced a $1 billion joint venture with Key Tronic to manufacture Wi-Fi 8 routers in the U.S.
Brandon Hill is a senior editor at Tom's Hardware. He has written about PC and Mac tech since the late 1990s with bylines at AnandTech, DailyTech, and Hot Hardware. When he is not consuming copious amounts of tech news, he can be found enjoying the NC mountains or the beach with his wife and two sons.

articles.title: GTA 6 : une fuite annonce un téléchargement colossal sur PS5, commencez à faire de la place
articles.text:
Une fuite donne une première indication du poids de GTA 6 sur PS5, et votre SSD risque de se sentir à l’étroit. Rockstar n’a pas encore confirmé ce chiffre, mais les joueurs vont peut-être devoir arbitrer entre Vice City et leurs jeux déjà installés.
Les joueurs comptent les jours avant de retrouver Vice City (plus que 22 à l’heure où nous écrivons cet article), mais certains pourraient aussi devoir compter les heures devant une barre de progression. À quelques semaines du lancement, une nouvelle fuite donne une première indication du volume de données à récupérer sur PS5. Et votre connexion aura du travail.
Un téléchargement de 210 Go annoncé sur PS5
Dans une publication du 27 octobre reprise par Insider Gaming, le compte spécialisé PlayStation Game Size annonce un téléchargement de 210 Go pour GTA 6. Le média affirme avoir recoupé cette information, sans détailler sa méthode de vérification.
La prudence reste de mise : ce chiffre ne constitue pas une confirmation officielle de Rockstar. Il concerne la version PS5 et ne permet pas de déduire le poids de celle destinée aux Xbox Series X et Series S.
Autre nuance : la publication parle bien de taille de téléchargement. Cela ne suffit pas à établir précisément l’espace libre nécessaire pendant l’installation, ni la place occupée après celle-ci. Une éventuelle mise à jour au lancement pourrait également ajouter des données à récupérer, mais rien ne permet pour l’heure d’en annoncer le volume.
Le préchargement laissera une semaine pour se préparer
Pour se représenter ce que pèsent ces 210 Go, quelques calculs donnent un ordre d’idée. Avec un débit constant de 100 Mb/s entièrement consacré au téléchargement, il faudrait environ 4 h 40 pour tout récupérer. À 10 Mb/s, l’attente grimperait à 46 h 40, contre 28 minutes avec une connexion maintenant réellement 1 Gb/s.
Ces durées sont théoriques : elles ne prennent en compte ni les autres usages de la connexion, ni les variations de débit, ni les limites éventuelles des serveurs. Même avec la fibre, le débit annoncé par votre opérateur ne garantit pas celui obtenu sur la console.
Rockstar confirme toutefois que le préchargement commencera le 12 novembre à minuit, heure locale, une semaine avant la sortie du 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S. Les précommandes numériques pourront en profiter, tout comme les acheteurs de la version boîte une fois leur code reçu et activé.
La version boîte ne vous évitera d’ailleurs aucun téléchargement : elle contiendra un code, sans disque. Avec une connexion modeste, le préchargement dès le 12 novembre sera donc précieux. Après des années à attendre GTA 6, autant éviter de passer la soirée du lancement à attendre les derniers gigaoctets.

articles.title: Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
articles.text:
Info Edge’s Hitesh Oberoi to step down as MD and CEO; founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani to take over
After nearly 27 years with Info Edge, Hitesh Oberoi will step down from his full-time executive role in December 2026. Founder Sanjeev Bikhchandani will take over as MD and Group CEO, subject to shareholder approval, as investors watch how the leadership transition shapes the company's next phase.
Hitesh Oberoi, Managing Director and Chief Executive Officer of Info Edge, will step down from his full-time executive role on December 2, 2026, after nearly 27 years with the company, including more than 16 years as MD. The parent of Naukri.com announced the leadership change alongside its second-quarter FY27 results.
Sanjeev Bikhchandani, the founder of Info Edge, will take over as Executive Vice Chairman, Managing Director and Group CEO from December 3, 2026, subject to shareholder approval. The move will see Bikhchandani return to an active management role after serving as Executive Vice Chairman. According to the company's regulatory filing, his term will run until April 26, 2031.
Oberoi, however, will continue to be associated with the company. Subject to shareholder approval, he will remain on its board as a Non-Executive, Non-Independent Director. Info Edge said he had chosen to step back from his full-time executive role to devote more time to education, entrepreneurship, institution building, investing and philanthropy, while spending more time with his family.
In a statement, Oberoi said that after nearly 27 years, he felt it was the right time to begin transitioning out of his full-time operating role. He added that he would miss the colleagues and teams who had made those years special. Bikhchandani said the two had built Info Edge together over more than 27 years.
Oberoi's tenure spans much of Info Edge's growth. According to a report citing the company's filing, its market capitalisation increased from Rs 2,500 crore to Rs 80,000 crore during his tenure. Oberoi formally took over as CEO and MD in 2010, when Bikhchandani moved into the role of Executive Vice Chairman. The company said it has a strong institutional foundation, supported by senior leaders who have been with Info Edge for more than 20 years.
Investors will be watching how the leadership change affects Info Edge’s core recruitment business and broader strategy. The move comes after CFO Chintan Thakkar stepped down in November 2025, with co-promoter Ambarish Raghuvanshi taking over as interim CFO.

articles.text:

Un ejemplo: a mitad de 2024 compré yo mismo 32 GB de memoria RAM DDR5 de Corsair a 125,99 euros en Amazon. Hoy mismo, también en Amazon, valen más de 600 euros.
Tarjeta Gráfica Zotac Gaming GeForce RTX 5090 SOLID OC White Edition 32GB GDDR7 DLSS4

MSI RTX 5090 32G Gaming Trio OC Tarjeta Gráfica Gaming, 32 GB GDDR7, 512 bits, Rendimiento Extremo: 2497 MHz, DisplayPort x3 2.1a, HDMI 2.1b, NVIDIA Blackwell Architecture
¿Y el mercado de segunda mano?
Cuando buscamos algo tech y buscamos ahorrar, los reacondicionados son una opción a tener en cuenta (aunque no vale cualquiera). ¿Hay alguna RTX 5090 reacondicionada en estas tiendas? La respuesta es sí, pero realmente no merece la pena. El único ensamble que hemos encontrado de este tipo está en PcComponentes (de hecho, es la única GPU de este tipo que vende la propia tienda murciana) y su precio no es mucho mejor: cuesta 8.079 euros.
También tenemos la alternativa de buscar en aplicaciones de segunda mano, como puede ser Wallapop. Es cierto que es un componente caro y delicado (por lo que conviene revisar bien el vendedor y su estado), pero es una alternativa que está ahí... aunque con un panorama similar: no hay demasiadas disponibles y están en torno a los 6.000 o 7.000 euros si miramos vendedores con buenas valoraciones.
Entonces, ¿qué hacer si quieres una de estas RTX 5090? Algunas acaban en manos de entidades que no las quieren para jugar y, aunque no está confirmado, hay rumores que apuntan a que NVIDIA habría dejado de producirla. Es una situación complicada, pero lo cierto es que es difícil recomendar una de estas tarjetas con los precios a los que están disponibles hoy en día. Aunque, por desgracia, la cosa puede ir a peor en los próximos meses.

articles.title: Check Point is turning network firewalls into cloud-based subscriptions
articles.text:
WTF?! AI agents are increasingly becoming a driving force behind large-scale cyber-swatting campaigns and dangerous security incidents. Israeli cybersecurity company Check Point believes an AI-powered firewall could be the answer to this emerging agentic threat – and hopes customers will keep paying for it indefinitely.
Check Point recently introduced its new Firewall-as-a-Subscription offering, giving organizations access to comprehensive network protection designed for the AI era. The Israeli cybersecurity company says customers no longer need to purchase expensive hardware appliances before getting started with the new platform. However, they'll be locked into monthly or annual payments for at least three years before they can switch to something else.
Put simply, Check Point has turned one of the most basic networking services into a cloud-based subscription – and expects customers to be grateful for it, too. The Firewall-as-a-Subscription service is based on R82.20, Check Point's latest firewall platform, which is designed to provide enhanced protection and management capabilities for bots, chatbots, and AI agents.
The R82.20 platform includes an "agentic console" for managing firewall devices and services. Check Point is using AI-powered technology to fend off AI-powered attacks, a strategy that's becoming a common refrain among organizations facing increasingly aggressive AI agents and bots.
The Firewall-as-a-Subscription package also includes additional features, such as Check Point Force hardware firewalls tailored to an organization's needs, SandBlast's AI-powered threat prevention, and security updates that can be applied on the fly. The company also promises "premium" support, which should mean having a (competent) human employee available to respond to customer support tickets.
Check Point's pitch for subscription-based firewalls revolves around the rising cost of hardware. Organizations are seeing their budgets shrink, while security appliances often go for long periods without significant upgrades. If an up-to-date AI firewall can be bundled into a single subscription with predictable monthly expenses, Check Point suggests, companies will be more inclined to upgrade and take advantage of the latest capabilities offered by its all-in-one R82.20 platform.
Avi Rembaum, Check Point's president of global technical sales, said that "with Firewall-as-a-Subscription, we are making our most advanced AI security, threat prevention and agentic management available through one simple subscription, so organizations can secure their AI transformation today."
According to the company, customers must commit to the firewall subscription for at least 36 months. In return, they can expect significant feature upgrades – and potentially hardware upgrades – throughout the same period.
Check Point's subscription-based approach to network security might sound bonkers, but AI agents are becoming a real threat that internet services must address one way or another. Big tech companies such as Amazon and Meta are clashing over agents' ability to shop online freely, while Nvidia is proposing a safety platform to keep rogue AI agents in check. AI agents are hammering servers at some of the internet's most popular services, including Wikipedia. Meanwhile, someone in Delaware thinks letting AI agents run entire companies sounds like the best idea in the world.

articles.title: Rogers limits auto pay discount to Rogers credit cards, pre-authorized debit
articles.text:
Rogers has changed how customers can get its Automatic Payments discount.
The discount now requires using either a Rogers Bank credit card or a pre-authorized debit card for automatic payments. While this applies to new customers, existing customers will also have to change if they make adjustments to their plan.
A screenshot of an email posted to the r/rogers subreddit, shows the telecom giant asking customers to update their payment method following a plan change.
Notably, a Rogers support page offers some additional information about the auto-pay discount, noting that customers who already receive the discount on an eligible payment method and don’t change their plan should keep the existing discount. However, customers who make changes after July 23, 2026 (for home services) or Sept. 15, 2026 (for mobile) will need to adjust their payment method to continue receiving the discount.
Rogers clarified in an email to MobileSyrup that it’s emailing customers who changed their plan, and the email shared in the Reddit post is one such case. Further, the November deadline in that email is specific to that customer.
You can still use other payment methods like your regular credit cards or direct deposit — but you won’t get the Automatic Payments discount.
This comes right as Rogers posted a notice on its support site that it will start charging a 1.6 per cent credit card processing fee on Jan. 17, 2027. Convenient, as the Rogers Bank credit card is now the only discount-eligible credit card that can be used for payments.
Interestingly, Rogers also announced in August that it would replace the 1.5x cash back rewards redemption for eligible Rogers purchases with the ability to earn five per cent cash back rewards on eligible Rogers purchases (for every dollar, you earn $0.50 in cash back rewards), adding insult to injury.
To summarize all of this, Rogers is now making customers who want the Automatic Payments discount switch over to its own Rogers Bank credit card to get a discount. Worse, the card’s cashback benefits are now significantly reduced thanks to the slashed features and new processing fee.
Or you could use a pre-authorized debit card, but I don’t really trust giving Rogers pre-authorized access to my debit card.
Update Oct. 28, 2026, at 6:41 p.m. ET: Added some additional clarification from Rogers and fixed a few typos.
Update Oct. 28, 2026, at 2:35 p.m. ET: Added additional details from a Rogers support site.

articles.title: From a brand new Echo Time to an Echo Studio with a camera, here are 8 Alexa devices just announced by Amazon
articles.text:
8 new Echo and Alexa gadgets that Amazon just announced — from an upgraded Echo Dot to an Echo Studio with a camera attached
Lots to look at here
Amazon often likes to unveil a plethora of products at the same time, and it's done so again: we've got eight different product announcements to talk about today, and they cover smart displays, smart speakers, and the wider Amazon ecosystem.
Most of these products are available now, though some can only be preordered at the moment. Read on for all the details and pricing — at the time of writing international pricing is slowly rolling out, so we'll add that here as it gets announced.
1. Echo Dot
The brand new Echo Dot — the speaker for "everywhere you can imagine" as Amazon puts it, from the kitchen to the living room — gets a host of upgrades. There's a new full-range driver here for improved audio and 50% more bass, the addition of a fourth microphone so it can hear you better, and room temperature detection.
There's some custom Amazon silicon inside in the form of the AZ3 chip, which should make Alexa+ faster and more responsive, and the smart speaker is now both a smart home hub as well as an Eero Wi-Fi extender. It's available now in Graphite, Glacier White, Agave Green, and Coral Pink for $99.99 / £94.99 / AU$199.
2. Amazon Kids Echo Dot
If your kids are after their own Echo Dot, Amazon has you covered here too. There's everything you get in the regular Dot, with a choice of either Octopus and Penguin designs, and a year of Amazon Kids+ (featuring podcasts and audiobooks, usually $7.99 / £6.99 a month if you've got Prime). The Amazon Kids Echo Dot is yours for $109.99 / £104.99.
3. Echo Studio with Home Camera
The Echo Studio is the Echo speaker you go for if you want the best audio possible, and the newly unveiled model adds a feature called Advanced Room Adaptation that "tunes the sound to your space". There's also now Adaptive Volume, so audio adjusts as you move about the room to maintain a steady level.
Also — surprise! — there's now a camera embedded in the speaker. Amazon says you could use it to check in on pets or make sure you've switched the lights off. The camera can also be used with Alexa+, to get info on whatever you're holding, and with Fire TV devices if you want to put video calls on your television.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
As always, you can turn off the camera whenever you like. The new Echo Studio with Home Camera is now available in Graphite for $249.99 / £239.99 / AU$479, and the existing Echo Studio (without the camera or extra audio features) remains on sale for $219.99.
4. Echo Time
The Echo Time is a brand new smart speaker series from Amazon, and looks to be a more premium version of the existing Echo Spot. Yes, it's basically an Echo Dot with a clock on the front, but there's also smart alarm functionality here to wake you up at the best point during your sleep cycle, and routine settings for winding down at the end of the day too.
With a 3.2-inch touchscreen, you've got a bit of extra control when interacting with Alexa+ and other features, and Amazon says it's been specifically designed for the bedroom (there's no camera, you'll be pleased to know). The speaker is available now for $199.99 / £184.99 / AU$379, in Graphite, Glacier White, and Coral Pink.
5. Amazon Kids Echo Time
There's a kid-friendly version of the Echo Time available as well for $209.99 / £194.99, in either Galactic Grape or Cosmic Lime. As with the Echo Dot, the version for youngsters bundles in a year of Amazon Kids+ (usually $7.99 / £6.99 a month if you also subscribe to Prime), so there's lots of audio content to explore, plus wind-down content curated especially for kids.
6. Echo Show 16
Amazon is going big with the Echo Show 16, which boasts a screen measuring 16 inches from corner to corner (as you may have guessed from the name). Amazon says its the "most advanced, versatile smart display" it's put out yet: there's a refined design, Fire TV functionality built in, and a choice of three new Screen Styles.
These Screen Styles are basically different widget layout options, focusing on smart home controls, displaying photos, or acting as a family organizer (with calendars front and center). The device is faster than previous Echo Shows, Amazon says, and the 13MP camera lets you use it as a security camera and video calling device too.
Amazon is opening up preorders for the Echo Show 16 now, and it'll be available "later this year". The standard smart display costs $499.99, while one with a special anti-glare Nanomatte layer (as used in the Alexa Tablet 12 Pro) is yours for $569.99.
7. Alexa Home Map
Alexa Home Map is exactly what it sounds like: a map of your home, rendered in 3D. The idea is you can see at a glance how your smart lights, speakers, displays, and cameras are set up, and control them with a tap on the map. You can start setting up the map through the Alexa+ app on your phone, though it's not rolling out until later this year.
8. Alexa Photo Frame
The Alexa Photo Frame tasks the Alexa AI with picking out the best shots from your Amazon Photos library, and displaying them on the 10-inch touchscreen — though you can also manually specify albums and people you want to see. New photos can show up automatically if you want, as they're added to your library.
Alexa is always on hand if you want to request a particular image, and you can even add voice notes to pictures and send them to friends and family with their own Alexa Photo Frames. The digital frame is available now for $199.99 in Black, and $229.00 with a real Birch or Walnut wood frame.

Dave is a freelance tech journalist who has been writing about gadgets, apps and the web for more than two decades. Based out of Stockport, England, on TechRadar you'll find him covering news, features and reviews, particularly for phones, tablets and wearables. Working to ensure our breaking news coverage is the best in the business over weekends, David also has bylines at Gizmodo, T3, PopSci and a few other places besides, as well as being many years editing the likes of PC Explorer and The Hardware Handbook.

articles.title: Corsair Warthog case review: A rugged, military-themed chassis with plenty of airflow
articles.text:
Tom's Hardware Verdict
The Warthog’s rugged military looks are the standout feature of this mid-tower, but its higher price and noise-normalized cooling performance on the video card keep it from soaring above the rest
Reasons to buy
- + Military theme
- + Rugged construction
- + Roomy interior for components
- + Designed for high airflow
- + Cool-looking front panel IO
- + Built-in GPU support bracket
- + Light over rear IO panel
Reasons to avoid
- - Cost
- - Below average noise-normalized cooling for GPU
- - Can’t mount rads in front and side simultaneously
Why you can trust Tom's Hardware
Our expert reviewers spend hours testing and comparing products and services so you can choose the best for you. Find out more about how we test.
Fractal arguably kicked off the wood accent PC trend with the North line, and the company says its new Summit case is built for “...expressive, high-performance systems combining distinctive Scandinavian design and advanced cooling potential.” The chassis sports FSC-certified wood (timber verified to come from responsibly managed, socially beneficial, and economically viable forests) for details like the front surround and solid wood feet. There’s no doubt it’s a good-looking case, but if you want to show off the wood, you’ll want to stick to the Chalk White or Black versions, as it blends in with the Blackout SKU we tested.
Corsair’s latest case, the Warthog, is a military-inspired chassis that resembles a fuel canister (jerry can) you’d see on military vehicles. Based loosely on the Vengeance C70 case from 2012, which looked more like an ammunition container, the new Warthog evolved into a much better-looking, more functional chassis for today’s hardware in either of the two colorways.
The Warthog does resemble its predecessor, and Corsair borrowed some features from the C70 while updating the design with “...even more rugged exterior, significantly more expansion options, and an emphasis on excellent airflow throughout the chassis,” and the company largely succeeded.
The Warthog updates include the InfiniRail Fan Mounting System for flexible fan mounting, a pegboard motherboard tray for custom cable management, room for today’s massive video cards (plus built-in GPU support), and three mounting locations for 360mm radiators and 13 120mm fans. It even has bump guards on the front I/O for that all-in military aesthetic. The fighter jet-style front IO includes USB ports, one fast USB 3.2 Gen2x2 (20 Gbps) Type-C port, plus an on/off button for a unique integrated light on the back of the case that illuminates the rear IO area and down.
If you’re into the military look, the Corsair Warthog ($179) and Warthog RS ($199 with fans) absolutely nails it, with plenty of other features that make it a compelling mid-tower chassis. We'll cover more details inside and outside the chassis, showcasing the features and any issues we encounter during the build. We'll also run the case through thermal and noise testing to show how it performs compared to others and whether it could make our best PC cases list. Below are the case's specifications from Corsair.
Corsair Warthog Product Specifications
| Type | Mid-Tower | 
| Dimensions (H x L x W) | 21.4 x 21 x 11.1-inches (546 x 534 x 284mm) | 
| Motherboard Support | Mini-ITX, Micro ATX, ATX, E-ATX | 
| Back-connect Motherboard Support | Yes | 
| Color | Olive Drab Black | 
| Storage Support | (1) 3.5-inch (2) 2.5-inch | 
| PCIe Expansion Slots | 7 | 
| Fan Support | Top - 3x120/2x140mm Front - 3x120/2x140/2x200mm Bottom - 3x120mm Side: 3x120/2x140mm Rear - 1x120/140mm | 
| Pre-installed fans | (3) RS Series (120mm rear, 2x200mm front) | 
| Radiator Support | Front - 360/280/240mm Top - 360/280/240mm Side - 360/280/240mm Rear - 140/120mm | 
| CPU Cooler Clearance | 190mm | 
| GPU Clearance | 393mm (w/ front fans) 405mm (w/o front fans) | 
| Vertical GPU Support | Yes (requires riser card) | 
| PSU Length | 200mm | 
| Dust Filters | Front, Bottom, and Side | 
| Other features | 3x pre-installed fans, integrated GPU support, Infinrail system, light on rear I/O, Military theme | 
| MSRP | $179.99 (w/o fans) $199.99 (w/pre-installed fans) | 
| Warranty | 2 Years | 
Features of the Warthog
▶️ External Features
Externally, the Warthog doesn’t look like many other cases. Sure, it has the general shape of a classic mid-tower, but the front and windowed panel break up the monotony we’re used to, with bars resembling a fuel tank breaking up the window pane and front of the chassis. The front and side panels also use Corsair’s steel 3D-Y perforations (also found on the 4000) for increased airflow, and they look different from most other cases. It also has a military-inspired front I/O, sturdy built-in steel handles, and the familiar army olive drab color (it also comes in black). It just screams military industrial design.
Get Tom's Hardware's best news and in-depth reviews, straight to your inbox.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Looking more closely at the front of the case, we get a better view of the door that covers the front panel fans. We get a close-up of the contrasting black 3D-Y perforations, which not only look better than the typical circular holes, but are said (by Corsair) to allow 12% better airflow. Next to the red handle, Corsair stamps the model WX-01 in white on a thin crossmember in the upper-right corner (it’s WX-02 for the black SKU). Pull the red tab on the left, and it opens via two hinges on the right, revealing the magnetically attached dust filter.
At the bottom of the front panel is the fighter-jet-inspired I/O panel, complete with bump guards and a flip-up cover over the reset button. On flight control panels, the guards prevent accidental activation of critical or dangerous switches. A flip-up toggle would be cool here, too. Port-wise, it has everything you could want. On the left is a 3.5mm audio jack for headphones and a microphone. Next to it is the recessed power light that glows red when powered on. Next to it is the USB 3.2 (20 Gbps) Type-C port. Between the bump guards are a square power button, the cool flip-up reset button, and the light button. All buttons feel solid under my fingers and not wobbly or cheap. On the right are two USB 3.2 (5 Gbps) Type-A ports. What’s here is typical fare, but it looks a lot cooler than most front IOs.
The tempered-glass side panel doesn’t offer a full view inside. Instead, diagonal, crossmember-like ribs break it into one main viewable area, with two smaller triangles at the ends. On military vehicles, this reinforces the weaker glass while still allowing visibility. On the Warthog, it just adds to the rugged look, and maybe lets you get away with a little less time managing cables — I kid, clean up those cables! The panel is secured to the frame with two tabs at the bottom and four ball-and-socket joints at the top, two on each side. Pull toward you at the top to release, then pull up to remove. Simple, and it felt secure.
The other side panel is solid, except for side venting. The venting matches the front and top panels with the 3D-Y pattern, but here it’s olive drab instead of the black we see everywhere else. Inside is another magnetically attached dust filter. The ‘service panel’ (stenciled in the upper-right corner) is secured the same way as the front, using tabs on the bottom and ball-and-socket joints on top.
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
At the top of the case, there’s not much to see—just more 3D-Y perforations for airflow. Many cases let you easily remove the top for easier access to the Infinirail fan/radiator mounts, and the Warthog does too. Loosen the thumbscrews on the back, remove both side panels, and pull the nylon strap.
Flipping the case around, we see the power supply sits at the bottom, and Corsair includes two captive screws for tooless mounting. Above it, seven vertical expansion slots offer plenty of room for large graphics cards and other expansion. The Warthog also supports vertical GPUs up to three slots wide, but you need a riser card accessory. Above that is space for up to a 140mm fan (120mm RS fan included for RS model), and to the left is the IO area. Corsair installed a small light above that shines down on the rear of the case, illuminating the rear IO area and back of the case, which is certainly useful when plugging in cables.
On the bottom of the case, there isn’t too much going. The Warthog does have a removable dust filter that slides out from the windowed side of the chassis. I prefer this location because, if the filter pulls out from the rear, you'll likely need to move your heavy case to get it out.
▶️ Internal Features
Inside the case, we see a single-chamber design with visual separation only between the power supply area at the bottom and the rest of the case. You won’t find a fancy air guide to feed the video card, but we do spy the small (but effective) adjustable GPU support strut. Beyond that, there’s nothing special at first glance.
The motherboard tray has plenty of cutouts for wiring, but there isn’t much space to route connectors through. Sometimes you need to flex the frame a bit to get larger ones through, like the ATX connector. That’s not ideal, but it isn’t a big deal, even with a motherboard already mounted. The good news is there are no rubber grommets to pull through the holes. While we’re here, we also get a better look at the pegboard feature, which lets you custom-manage cables on the back side. For those planning to build a PC with rear-connect motherboards, the Warthog supports all of them (Asus BTF, Gigabyte Stealth, MSI Project Zero).
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
View Original
Looking at the front of the case from the inside, we see the massive pre-installed 200mm RS fans that come with the “RS” version of the chassis. Corsair says the magnetic half-dome-bearing fans spin up to 1,000 RPM and move up to 135 CFM of air at a low 36.5 dBA. They are quiet and move a fair amount of air. The front area supports up to 3x120mm fans or radiators.
Looking up at the ceiling from below, you'll see Corsair’s Infinirail system (also on the front, but hidden by the fans), which lets you slide and position fans and radiators where you need them. Although the case fits up to 3x120mm radiators here, they will protrude into the case and can cover the top of your motherboard in many cases. Be sure to mount your motherboard and connect the EPS plugs before you install a top radiator.
At the bottom rear, you can see the power supply area, along with space to route cables for any headers along the bottom of the motherboard. The bottom chamber is also vented into the rest of the chassis. It won’t radiate much heat, since the power supply draws filtered, cool air from below.
Opening up the other side of the chassis gives a better look at the side fan/rad mounts and the default cable-routing options. There is 50mm between the motherboard tray and the outside panel, which is plenty of room to route cables, even with reckless abandon. The pegboard motherboard tray, part of Corsair’s RapidRoute 2.0 cable management system, gives you plenty of freedom to move the cable-ratcheting strap mounts.
From the back, we can see the motherboard tray mounting for your SSD and HDDs. Corsair uses a combo drive plate connected via a thumbscrew. You can install two 2.5-inch drives and one 3.5-inch drive on the combo plate, which should be enough for most users in 2026. Note that to access the back of your motherboard (to mount a cooler, for example), you need to remove this combo plate.
Overall, I do like the look of this rugged, military-themed case, particularly in the olive drab colorway. The fighter jet-inspired front IO panel and jerry can-like look stand out among the played-out designs we’re used to, without looking like a failed attempt at abstract art. Inside, there’s plenty of room for components, even multiple radiators. That said, it is polarizing. Either you like the look, or you don’t. There isn’t much in between.
Joe Shields is a staff writer at Tom’s Hardware. He reviews motherboards and PC components.

articles.title: SK Hynix Reports Record Q3 Results Driven by AI Memory Surge - EE Times
articles.text:
SK Hynix posted third-quarter revenue of 104.62 trillion won (~$78 billion), exceeding 100 trillion won (~$75 billion) for the first time. Operating profit reached a record 83.33 trillion won ($62 billion), with an operating margin of 80%. Net profit was 39.78 trillion won ($30 billion), while net cash expanded to 98.7 trillion won (~$74 billion).
“SK Hynix’s third-quarter results are very significant in terms of hitting record-high earnings and delivering on shareholder value,” MS Hwang, research director at Counterpoint Research, noted. “First and foremost, operating profit beat expectations again, coming in at 83 trillion won [~$62 billion] versus the consensus of 77 trillion won [~$57 billion].”
DRAM pricing jumps to $2/Gb
According to Counterpoint Research, standard DRAM pricing surged from 20 cents to 30 cents per Gb to $2 per Gb, driving financial momentum and expanding the global DRAM market to $200 billion. “The driving force behind this is rising prices,” Hwang said. “Prices that used to sit around 20 to 30 cents per Gb have now soared to $2.” He also argued that HBM4 will see its unit price jump even further to $4 per Gb.
Additionally, Nvidia resolved initial HBM4 bottlenecks. “Over the past few months, the market has been plagued by two major misconceptions and concerns regarding HBM: That SK was facing technical hurdles in supplying HBM4 to Nvidia, and that HBM adoption volumes per chip might decrease,” he added. “As of October, both concerns have proven to be fake alarms or have been largely resolved.”
Supply shortage and long-term agreements
As AI expands into enterprise computing, robotics, and autonomous vehicles, SK Hynix projects a structural memory shortage that will persist through 2030. The issue stems from the manufacturing complexity of 10 nm-class, sixth-generation DRAM, and 321-layer NAND.
To secure revenue, SK Hynix said it has signed long-term agreements (LTAs) with 14 tech giants, covering over 50% of capacity for 2027 to 2028. “Today, more than half of the memory industry’s capital expenditure goes into infrastructure,” Hwang said. “This shift in corporate governance leading to stricter capital discipline could ultimately rewrite the traditional memory business cycle.”
Solidigm IPO canceled and shareholder return program
SK Hynix said it had discontinued its review of a potential U.S. IPO for its flash memory and solid-state drive subsidiary, Solidigm. “The IPO was intended to raise external capital for the expansion of Solidigm’s production facilities,” SK Hynix CEO Kwak Noh Jung said. “However, after carefully considering recent financial market conditions and other factors, we concluded that proceeding at this time would not be the best way to achieve the originally anticipated outcome. We have therefore discontinued our review.”
Hwang commented, “The Solidigm IPO raised issues around a dual listing… If the returns aren’t flowing back to shareholders, it’s very difficult to re-rate the stock.” Additionally, SK Hynix unveiled an expanded fiscal year 2026 shareholder return program of 100 trillion won (~$75 billion), including cash dividends over 30 trillion won (~$22 billion) and buybacks exceeding 60 trillion won (~$45 billion), supported by Kioxia investment gains.
Solidigm is currently in talks with the U.S. Commerce Department to invest $45 billion in a new U.S. chip plant, according to a Bloomberg report citing people familiar with the negotiations. Before committing to what would be the first new major flash-memory chip production facility on American soil, Solidigm is seeking U.S. government permission to send equipment to upgrade an existing plant in Dalian, China.
Data center pullback and Samsung catching up
Counterpoint Research warned of risks such as pullbacks in cloud spending. “The single most severe threat would be a scenario reminiscent of 2018, where cloud service providers simultaneously pull back on their order volume,” Hwang said. “We anticipate that Samsung will surpass SK Hynix from the HBM4 generation, leading the market share in 2027.”
SK Hynix management said it expects to preserve its market lead through proprietary packaging and customer partnerships.

articles.title: El minuto a minuto del accidente de Toledo: la reconstrucción de un siniestro "inexplicable" entre un tren AVE y un tren Iryo
articles.text:
"Es inexplicable". Es como Óscar Puente, ministro de Transportes, ha calificado el accidente que esta mañana del 28 de octubre de 2026 se ha producido en Urda (Toledo). Allí un AVE de Renfe ha arrollado a un Iryo que se encontraba detenido en la vía. Es el segundo accidente grave en lo que llevamos de año, después del accidente de Adamuz (Córdoba) el pasado mes de enero.
Pero, ¿qué ha pasado esta vez? Reconstruimos minuto a minuto lo que ha sucedido para entender las claves.
07:54. El Iryo 6076 sale de Atocha hacia Sevilla con 147 personas a bordo.
08:00. Seis minutos después sale el AVE 2080, con el mismo destino y 397 pasajeros. Los dos circulan por la misma vía y en el mismo sentido.
08:30. Cae el sistema de seguridad LZB por un problema informático.
El tráfico se detiene. Automáticamente, caído el sistema LZB, el tráfico se detiene de inmediato. El problema afecta a un tramo de 69 kilómetros en el que se encuentran, según las primeras investigaciones, seis trenes. Óscar Puente, en su declaración ante los medios, admitía que no descartaba que hubiera más trenes detenidos en ese tramo.
El CRC toma el mando. Con el tráfico detenido, es el centro de control de Atocha el que toma el control. En los minutos siguientes los trabajadores dan la orden a los trenes de continuar la marcha "con normalidad".
8:36. El AVE 2080 recibe la orden de continuar la marcha "con normalidad". El maquinista tiene ante sí una señal roja pero desde el centro de control le dan la orden de seguir adelante. El protocolo manda que lo haga "marcha a la vista". Es decir, que circule lo suficientemente despacio como para detener el tren en una frenada de emergencia. Sin embargo, recibe la orden de circular con normalidad.
Una correción. La orden de "marcha con normalidad" se da a todos los trenes afectados. Sin embargo, uno de los maquinistas alerta al centro de control de que esto no puede ser así. En el centro de control corrigen y le confirman que tiene que ser "marcha a la vista". Es decir, mucho más despacio.
El Iryo se mantiene parado. Una de las grandes preguntas es por qué el tren de Iryo se mantuvo parado sobre las vías. En la rueda de prensa, Óscar Puente señaló que creen que a este maquinista también se le dio la orden de continuar pero que no podía confirmarlo. Es algo que todavía tiene que resolverse.
8:36-8:53. El AVE 2080 recupera poco a poco la velocidad de circulación normal. Recorre 25 kilómetros sin ser avisado de que el Iryo que lo precedía se mantiene parado sobre la vía.
8:53. Hora todavía por precisar con exactitud. El AVE 2080 alcanza el Iryo 6076. Le golpe a una velocidad todavía no confirmada aunque algunas informaciones apuntan a haber superado los 100 km/h. Ambos trenes descarrilan y algunos coches caen terraplén abajo.

articles.title: Data discovery and classification anchors AI governance - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
AI gets keys to unmapped data: theCUBE’s AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit day-two kickoff analysis
Data discovery and classification are becoming important considerations as enterprises bring AI into their operations. Security teams need to understand what information is available to AI systems and how access is governed.
Data discovery and classification are becoming important considerations as enterprises bring AI into their operations. Security teams need to understand what information is available to AI systems and how access is governed. Turning AI trust and cyber resilience principles into practical controls presents a challenge for organizations, according to Jon Oltsik (pictured, right), principal analyst in residence at SiliconANGLE and theCUBE.
“A policy is a policy,” he said. “You write a policy down, you put it on a piece of paper, you educate people. But then when it comes to policy enforcement, that becomes much more difficult. That’s where your controls have to be in place.”
Oltsik and theCUBE Research’s Krista Case (left) provided a day-two kickoff analysis at the AI Cybersecurity and Resilience Summit during an exclusive broadcast on theCUBE, SiliconANGLE Media’s livestreaming studio. They discussed turning AI policy into enforceable controls, starting with data hygiene. (* Disclosure below.)
Data discovery and classification as AI’s first line of defense
A central concern for chief information security officers is controlling AI inside their own organizations. But none of it is entirely new since organizations have long used role-based access control and least privilege to protect regulated data, Oltsik noted.
“Now we have to adjust it to a very dynamic, non-deterministic world of AI, and we have to do that at a pace that keeps up with the scale and speed of AI,” Oltsik said. “None of that is easy.”
How much autonomy to grant agents depends on each organization’s risk tolerance.
The European Commission has issued draft guidance on classifying high-risk AI systems under the EU AI Act, according to Oltsik. Agents that touch sensitive data or act autonomously still warrant human oversight, much as early intrusion prevention tools once did.
“What we have to do is ease into those decisions, understand what actions agents or models are taking and then, over time, develop a comfort level,” he said.
Enterprises should get the basics right, starting with data discovery and classification, identity and access management and audits of overly permissive accounts, including those held by agents, Oltsik noted. Security leaders also need to participate in decisions about how the business adopts AI.
“The security team can’t be the division of ‘no,’ or the [chief information security officer] cannot be Dr. No,” he said. “How do you do that? How do you make sure that you go into AI with business objectives and business goals, but the right type of risk management and risk mitigation?”

articles.title: Após vazamento, Smart Sampa terá reconhecimento facial para acessar sistema • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Após vazamento, Smart Sampa terá reconhecimento facial para acessar sistema
Prefeitura de São Paulo anunciou nova camada de autenticação após exposição de credenciais.
Após a exposição de dados de câmeras de monitoramento, o Smart Sampa passará a exigir reconhecimento facial dos servidores autorizados a acessar a plataforma da Prefeitura de São Paulo. A nova forma de autenticação foi anunciada pelo prefeito Ricardo Nunes (MDB) nesta terça-feira (27/10).
O anúncio ocorreu durante a assinatura de acordos de cooperação entre a Prefeitura e o Ministério Público de São Paulo. A exigência começa a valer imediatamente.
A medida é o desdobramento da revelação, na semana passada, de que credenciais do sistema de videomonitoramento da Prefeitura de São Paulo ficaram disponíveis em um repositório público na internet.
De acordo com o UOL, informações restritas ficaram acessíveis publicamente por meses, permitindo a reproduçao de interfaces que possibilitavam visualizar em tempo real as imagens das câmeras conectadas ao programa.
Segundo Nunes, não houve falha de segurança: um servidor da Guarda Civil Metropolitana (GCM) teria compartilhado indevidamente uma senha de acesso. Ainda assim, a situação mostrou a facilidade com que os dados do Smart Sampa poderiam ser expostos através do acesso a credenciais de servidores.
Após a divulgação do caso, a administração também adotou autenticação de dois fatores. O Ministério Público registrou uma notícia de fato para avaliar as informações apresentadas pela reportagem, enquanto a Agência Nacional de Proteção de Dados (ANPD) pediu esclarecimentos à Prefeitura.
Um dos acordos anunciados durante o evento permitirá que nove promotores do Grupo de Atuação Especial de Repressão ao Crime Organizado de São Paulo (Gaeco) utilizem informações e imagens do Smart Sampa em investigações relacionadas ao crime organizado.
A própria Prefeitura confirmou que o acordo prevê o uso de dados técnicos da plataforma e ma tividades de investigação, prevenção e repressão de crimes.
O segundo convênio integra o sistema a ações de proteção de mulheres. Câmeras poderão auxiliar na localização de homens com medidas protetivas de urgência que ainda não tenham sido encontrados para receber a notificação judicial. A prefeitura afirma que o Smart Sampa já contribuiu para a captura de 3.628 foragidos e a localização de 284 pessoas desaparecidas.

articles.title: Anthropic entra a la medicina: compra empresa biotecnológica que investiga la distrofia muscular y enfermedades raras
articles.text:
Anthropic adquirió Mithril Medicine, una empresa de biotecnología de una sola persona con sede en Cambridge, Massachusetts, que utilizaba Claude para coordinar experimentos, datos y logística con 11 laboratorios externos. La operación se concretó en julio y fue anunciada por la compañía el 27 de octubre.
El fundador de Mithril, Cody Tranbarger, dirigía a científicos consultores a tiempo parcial y a laboratorios subcontratados que producían anticuerpos, medían su unión a objetivos biológicos, realizaban ensayos celulares y llevaban adelante estudios con ratones.
Tras la adquisición, sus programas para dos formas raras de distrofia muscular se convirtieron en los primeros proyectos internos de desarrollo de fármacos de Anthropic.
La empresa trabaja en tratamientos para la distrofia muscular congénita relacionada con LAMA2 y la alfa-distroglicanopatía.
El primer programa busca reparar las conexiones debilitadas entre las fibras musculares y el tejido circundante mediante anticuerpos biespecíficos, diseñados para unirse a dos dianas y formar un puente molecular.
El objetivo de Anthropic con la adquisición
Anthropic incorporó Mithril como parte de una estrategia para ampliar el uso de Claude en todas las etapas del desarrollo de medicamentos: desde la identificación de dianas terapéuticas y el diseño de moléculas hasta la fabricación, la documentación regulatoria y la planificación de ensayos clínicos.
La compañía sostiene que los obstáculos para acelerar la creación de fármacos se distribuyen a lo largo de todo el proceso, no solo en el diseño inicial de nuevas moléculas.
Por eso, busca involucrar a Claude en programas reales de investigación y desarrollo, en distintas áreas terapéuticas y etapas de avance.
Además de Mithril, Anthropic colaboró con seis organizaciones que desarrollan medicamentos: BigHat Biosciences, Bristol Myers Squibb, Divergence Labs, Enveda, Generate Biomedicines y The Column Group.
Según la empresa, estas asociaciones le permiten evaluar las fortalezas y limitaciones de sus modelos en tareas científicas y operativas.
El sistema utilizado por Mithril recibió el nombre de “Pipeline-in-a-Person”. Durante una semana elegida por el equipo como ejemplo, Claude sintetizó un informe de producción de 341 páginas sobre 113 construcciones de anticuerpos en menos de ocho minutos.
Asimismo, revisó un plan experimental para incluir 89 de esas moléculas en cuatro minutos, después de que un integrante del equipo descartara una recomendación previa.
Sin embargo, el uso de la inteligencia artificial también produjo errores. El equipo revisó seis fallas de Claude y al menos tres llegaron a laboratorios externos mediante correos electrónicos editados y enviados por personas.
Una de ellas pedía menos material por tubo del requerido, aunque fue corregida antes de que comenzara el llenado; otras dos, vinculadas con datos de producción, pasaron inadvertidas durante más de cuatro días.
Qué medicamentos podrían adelantarse
El principal programa de Mithril está dirigido a la distrofia muscular congénita relacionada con LAMA2, una enfermedad causada por mutaciones en el gen que codifica la proteína laminina-α2. Estas alteraciones debilitan las conexiones entre las fibras musculares y el tejido que las rodea.
Anthropic afirmó que Mithril alcanzó una prueba de concepto en ratones en menos de 18 meses.
El informe técnico, aún pendiente de revisión por pares, detalla que siete ratones tratados con un formato de anticuerpo mostraron, aproximadamente a las seis semanas de edad, casi el doble de fuerza de agarre y fuerza máxima del tríceps que cuatro ratones que recibieron una solución de control.
Los resultados, no obstante, presentan limitaciones. Los investigadores asignaron el tratamiento por camada, sin aleatorización, y evaluaron al grupo que recibió anticuerpos entre 126 y 161 días después del grupo de control, con un traslado de colonia en el medio.
El propio informe recomienda repetir los experimentos de manera simultánea y a ciegas.
Mithril apunta a seleccionar candidatos a fármacos en 2027. Si el desarrollo posterior tiene éxito, el programa para LAMA2 podría comenzar ensayos clínicos en humanos a finales de 2028, mientras que el proyecto para la alfa-distroglicanopatía tiene como objetivo iniciar estudios clínicos en 2029.

articles.title: Gartner report finds just 3% of organizations say they've hit productivity and savings goals from using AI
articles.text:
Gartner report finds just 3% of organizations say they've hit productivity and savings goals from using AI
Gartner report finds many firms falling behind
- Gartner report finds many firms aren't seeing benefits from AI
- Just 3% of businesses have hit their targets on AI
- This is despite many firms expecting AI technology to have a significant effect, and spending big to do so
New research has claimed barely any organizations are seeing real success when it comes to the results of heavily implementing AI in their workplace.
A report from Gartner found just 3% of organizations have hit their targets around productivity and efficiency, as well as trying to cut costs across their business using AI.
This is despite three quarters of leaders expecting AI technology to have a significant effect in their organization, with 85% set to spend more on AI in 2027, despite 38% of them already being over budget.
AI benefits to come?
"Ultimately, organizations will not generate cost savings from AI at this point," CV Viverito, senior director analyst for Gartner's HR practice, told attendees at the firm's HR Symposium.
"The greater opportunity is to use AI to do things that weren't possible before, such as shifting employee time into new capabilities, outcomes, and sources of growth."
Moving forward, Gartner says businesses should look to focus their AI efforts where the technology can make a tangible effect in key areas. It also advised organizations to spread AI knowledge across the business, with C-suite as important as entry-level workers when it comes to identifying new use cases and benefitting from such improvement.
“There isn’t a struggle to create capacity, that’s happening already as organizations redesign work,” claimed Viverito. “What organizations are struggling with is how to make that capacity usable and redirecting it to what is valuable.”

articles.title: US Marines join NATO mission in the Baltic Sea to protect undersea cables from sabotage as Russia continues to lurk — 'around four dozen' recon and intel specialists deployed to deter seabed threats
articles.text:
US Marines join NATO mission in the Baltic Sea to protect undersea cables from sabotage as Russia continues to lurk — 'around four dozen' recon and intel specialists deployed to deter seabed threats
The U.S. military is supporting a NATO mission to protect European undersea infrastructure
A team of around four dozen U.S. Marines is joining a NATO-led operation in the Baltic Sea to help protect undersea internet cables and gas pipelines in the area. In a press release, the U.S. Marine Corps shared its plans to deploy a "specialized team" to support NATO's Enhanced Vigilance Activity Baltic Sentry operation. The move comes amid a backdrop of growing undersea cable interest, movements of Russia's shadow fleet, and fears of sabotage.
The U.S. Marines are being sent from Marine Corps Base Camp Lejeune in North Carolina to provide "advanced expeditionary surveillance and tactical reconnaissance capabilities" to the region in support of Finnish and other NATO allies. Marines from 2nd Reconnaissance Battalion, 2nd Marine Division, and the II Marine Expeditionary Force Information Group are joining the mission.
Capt. Johan Tillander, Chief of Operations for the Finnish Navy, explained that the "experience, skills, and systems of the U.S. Marine Corps are perfectly suited" for the operation, including "monitoring of the Baltic Sea."
While the press release stresses that the Marines are serving in a "supportive, enabling capacity," with European nations taking the lead, the Marines are there to provide "highly specialized, agile force multipliers."
Maj. Gen. Daniel Shipley, Commander of U.S. Marine Corps Forces, Europe and Africa, shared that its participation shows its ability to "rapidly project specialized capabilities where they are most effective," and as a result, "ensuring we can operate seamlessly as a cohesive, lethal team to deter hybrid threats" in the area.
The U.S. deployment means that the operation will be able to "leverage... unique capabilities of Reconnaissance Marines, including small Unmanned Aerial Systems and littoral sensors, to feed vital data directly" to NATO.
The Baltic Sea is the frontline in potential assaults against European undersea infrastructure. Several attempts have been made to sabotage cables in the area, and two cables were cut between Finland, Sweden and Europe back in 2024. Meanwhile, Finland's own concerns about shadow fleet operations led it to set up a dedicated maritime surveillance center earlier this year to monitor activity in the Baltic Sea.

Russia isn't mentioned in the U.S. press release, but the authoritarian nation is one of Europe's biggest threats in the region, and has had worsening relations with European nations for several years, particularly since it went to war with Ukraine in 2022. Over 500 incidents of Russian fishing boats loitering near undersea cables in Europe have been seen in the last four and a half years, showing a persistence in mapping and identifying, if not directly interfering, with global data links in the area.

articles.title: Proton veut des équipes prêtes pour l'IA et s'explique après la fuite d’un email interne
articles.text:
Proton a envoyé à ses salariés un email annonçant de nouveaux entretiens pour évaluer l’usage de l’IA en interne. Après la fuite du message, l’entreprise affirme vouloir des équipes à l’aise avec ces outils, sans s’en servir comme prétexte à des licenciements.
Selon 404 Media, Proton a prévenu ses salariés lundi qu’ils pourraient être « re-interviewés » sur leur usage de l’IA, avec des conséquences possibles sur leur poste. L’entreprise a depuis répondu dans un commentaire épinglé sur Reddit, où elle publie le message en entier.
Re-interviews du 4 au 11 novembre : Proton veut savoir comment ses équipes s’adaptent à l’IA
Proton n’entend pas louper le virage de l’IA et à en juger par ses travaux portés sur Lumo et sa feuille de route, l’entreprise entend bien se positionner face à OpenAI et Anthropic avec son approche de chiffrement de bout en bout. Mais L'IA change la donne à bien des niveaux et dans son email, la direction explique que cela affecte aussi la manière de concevoir les produits et de travailler. Andy Yen, le PDG, a déjà rencontré la semaine dernière plus de 40 responsables seniors des équipes Ingénierie et Produit. Les entretiens s’étendent maintenant à d’autres collaborateurs.
Chaque salarié convoqué échangera avec quelqu’un d’extérieur à son équipe et à sa ligne hiérarchique. Cet interlocuteur sera choisi parmi des responsables à l’aise avec l’IA, qui se sont mis d’accord sur les critères d’évaluation. Plus qu’une simple liste d’outils, il faudra donner des exemples concrets en spécifiant ce qui a changé dans son travail, les résultats obtenus ou encore ce qui n’a pas fonctionné.
Sur Reddit, Proton affirme ne pas licencier en prenant l’IA comme prétexte. L’entreprise explique au contraire manquer de talents et recruter dans toutes ses équipes. Elle décrit la démarche comme un état des lieux pour voir comment chacun s’adapte, de quel soutien le salarié a besoin et qui pourrait piloter ce changement. Certains salariés pourraient obtenir davantage de responsabilités. Proton ajoute que l'IA doit être utilisée avec discernement, en tenant compte de la confidentialité, de la sécurité, de l’exactitude et de l’intérêt réel de l’outil.
Il n’empêche qu’en interne, les salariés sont assez perturbés pour avoir transféré cet email à 404 Media, lequel mentionne bel et bien :
Ces nouveaux entretiens auront des conséquences. Les enquêteurs consigneront leurs évaluations, qui alimenteront la revue plus large de notre organisation et de nos talents. Cette revue peut entraîner des changements concernant les rôles, les responsabilités et le maintien dans l’emploi. Les résultats individuels seront communiqués directement une fois les décisions arrêtées.
Ce processus nous aidera aussi à identifier les personnes prêtes à assumer un périmètre plus large et des responsabilités de direction à mesure que Proton évolue.
Proton reconnaît que cette période crée de l’incertitude et promet de communiquer clairement les décisions individuelles dès qu’elles seront prises. Reste à savoir si cette démarche vise simplement à privilégier les personnes à l’aise avec l’IA ou si l’entreprise saura mettre en place une forme de tutorat pour accompagner celles qui le sont moins.
- storageStockage de 500 Go

- alternate_emailSupport nom de domaine

En proposant de centraliser les versions premium de Proton Mail, Proton VPN, Proton Calendar, Proton Drive et Proton Pass, l'offre Unlimited s'avère particulièrement intéressante au niveau du tarif. On note quelques lacunes concernant le calendrier et le Drive, mais le Mail, le VPN ou le gestionnaire de mots de passe sont plutôt réussis. Après une décennie à plancher sur Mail, l'équipe propose une messagerie solide et moderne. Au travers de nos tests poussés le VPN a fait ses preuves, tandis que Pass évolue très rapidement et c'est plutôt bon signe. On regrette simplement que Proton semble avoir mis le calendrier aux oubliettes et que le Drive accuse encore plusieurs lacunes de jeunesse.

articles.title: How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
articles.text:
How to get corporate gifting right across multiple cities
From managing recipient lists and budgets to coordinating packaging and deliveries, here's how businesses can make large-scale festive gifting more organized and efficient.
Sending Diwali gifts to a handful of employees or clients is relatively simple. Sending hundreds of gifts to recipients spread across different cities is another matter. Addresses need to be verified, budgets finalized, packaging standardized and deliveries timed to arrive before the festival. A missed shipment, incorrect address or last-minute change can quickly complicate the exercise.
For businesses managing large-scale Diwali gifting, the key is to plan early, coordinate the details and ensure that every recipient has a consistent experience, regardless of location.
Start with a detailed recipient list
The first step is to organize all recipient information in one place. This should include names, delivery addresses, contact numbers, and any other information required to complete the delivery. For employee gifting, it may also be useful to group recipients according to city or office location. Client and partner lists can be organized separately so that different gifting requirements are easier to manage. Checking the information before placing the order is important. Incorrect or incomplete addresses can create delivery problems, particularly when gifts are being sent to several cities.
Personalize where it matters
Large-scale gifting does not have to feel completely impersonal. Businesses can add small details that make gifts feel more thoughtful. A personalized greeting card, recipient name or company message can add a sense of occasion without making the process significantly more complicated. For key clients or long-term partners, businesses may choose a more customized gift, based on the relationship. The goal is to find the right level of personalization for each recipient group while keeping the overall process manageable.
Use bulk ordering to simplify the process
When a business is managing a large number of recipients, placing individual orders can quickly become time-consuming. Bulk ordering can make the process more organized, particularly when the same or similar gifts are being sent to multiple locations. A single gifting plan can cover product selection, quantities, packaging, and delivery requirements. This also makes it easier for the internal team to monitor the overall budget and track the progress of the campaign. Businesses planning corporate Diwali gifts can also establish recipient categories in advance, making it easier to decide which gift goes to which group.
Keep packaging consistent
Packaging plays an important role in professional Diwali gifting. When gifts are being sent to different cities, consistent packaging can create a unified brand experience. The same box style, colour scheme, greeting card or branding element can be used across the entire order. This helps ensure that recipients receive gifts that feel like part of the same Diwali campaign, even if they are in different locations. Packaging should also be practical enough to protect the contents during transportation. Fragile products or items sensitive to heat may need additional consideration.
Set a clear budget
Diwali gifting costs can increase quickly when the recipient list is large. Setting a budget before selecting products helps businesses narrow down suitable options. The budget can be divided by recipient category. For example, employee gifts may have one price range, while client or business-partner gifts may have another. It is also useful to account for packaging, delivery, and personalization costs rather than looking only at the product price.
Track every shipment
Once the Diwali gifts are ordered, tracking becomes one of the most important parts of the process. A simple tracking sheet can include the recipient, city, order status, and delivery status. This allows the business team to quickly identify delayed or unsuccessful deliveries and take action where required. For larger gifting programmes, having one person or team responsible for monitoring the campaign can make communication much easier. It also prevents different departments from working with separate or outdated recipient lists.
Decide what the gift should include
The next step is deciding what will go into the Diwali gift. Businesses have several options, from traditional sweets and dry fruits to chocolates, snacks, candles and curated hampers. The choice can depend on the recipient group. Employee gifts may follow one format, while important client or partner gifts may have a different product mix. A consistent selection across cities can make large-scale gifting easier to coordinate. At the same time, businesses can create different categories of gifts based on the relationship with each recipient. This balance can help maintain consistency without making every gift identical.
Plan for different delivery locations
Sending gifts across multiple cities requires attention to delivery coverage and timelines. Businesses should confirm whether the selected gifting provider can deliver to all the required locations and understand how long each delivery may take. This becomes especially important during Diwali because demand for gifting and delivery services can increase significantly around the festival. Businesses can group orders by city and create a delivery schedule before placing them. This makes it easier to track which gifts have been dispatched, which are in transit, and which have already reached the recipients.
Start planning before the festive rush
One of the easiest ways to make multi-city Diwali gifting smoother is to start early. Early planning gives businesses more time to finalize recipient details, compare gifting options, approve designs, and schedule deliveries. It also leaves room to handle unexpected issues, such as an incorrect address or a product becoming unavailable. Waiting until the last few days can limit the available options and put additional pressure on both the business team and the delivery network.
Making multi-city Diwali gifting easier
Diwali gifting across several cities requires more planning than a small personal gifting exercise, but the process becomes manageable when it is treated as a structured campaign. A clear recipient database, suitable gifts, consistent packaging, planned delivery schedules, and proper tracking can help businesses coordinate gifting across locations. The aim is not simply to send gifts to as many people as possible. It is to create a consistent and thoughtful festive experience, even when recipients are spread across different cities.

articles.title: Apple dévoile son premier MacBook Pro avec écran tactile... à prix stratosphérique
articles.text:
Ce mercredi 28 octobre, Apple a levé le voile sur ses nouveaux MacBook Pro de 14 et 16 pouces lors d’un événement organisé à Los Angeles. Pour la première fois, un Mac est doté d’un écran tactile. C’est un véritable revirement pour Apple, qui a refusé l’idée d’un Mac tactile…pendant près de vingt ans. Steve Jobs, l’illustre fondateur d’Apple, estimait en effet qu’un écran tactile ne sert à rien sur un ordinateur portable, parce que le bras de l’utilisateur fatigue trop vite. Vingt ans plus tard, Apple a changé d’avis et présente son MacBook avec écran tactile comme « un pas en avant monumental pour le Mac ».
 We’re glowing with excitement over the new MacBook Pro. You’ve gotta touch it to believe it. pic.twitter.com/BLiGkGaefL
— John Ternus (@johnternus) October 28, 2026
À lire aussi : Apple lance le MacBook Pro M6 : prix, date de sortie, fiche technique… voici tout ce qu’il faut savoir
Un écran OLED tactile, une première sur Mac
C’est la grande nouveauté de cette génération. Le MacBook Pro passe enfin à l’OLED, des années après l’iPhone, l’iPad Pro et l’Apple Watch. Sur le papier, l’écran hérite d’un contraste bien supérieur à celui du mini-LED des MacBook Pro actuels. Apple appelle sa dalle PROLED XDR et la présente comme « le meilleur écran d’ordinateur portable au monde ». Elle repose sur une technologie OLED dite « tandem », qui superpose deux couches de pixels lumineux, comme sur l’iPad Pro.
L’écran grimpe jusqu’à 2 000 nits de luminosité, en HDR comme en SDR. Il affiche un taux de contraste de 10 000 000:1 et un taux de rafraîchissement variable, de 10 à 120 Hz. L’option d’écran nano-texturé, qui réduit les reflets, est toujours proposée.
Étant donné que l’écran est tactile, vous pouvez désormais toucher l’écran pour contrôler l’interface. On peut faire défiler une page web d’un glissement du doigt, pincer pour zoomer sur une photo ou glisser une diapositive d’une présentation à une autre. Le capteur tactile est intégré directement dans la dalle, et non posé par-dessus, ce qui réduit la latence. Sans surprise, Apple a adapté macOS 27 pour l’occasion. Les applications d’Apple sont optimisées pour le tactile, et de nombreuses applications existantes fonctionnent d’emblée, car macOS traduit automatiquement les touchers en clics. Microsoft Word, Excel, Zoom, Canva, Adobe Lightroom ou encore Blender prendront aussi en charge le tactile d’ici la fin de l’année.
Le tactile vient s’ajouter au clavier et au trackpad, sans les remplacer. Les raccourcis clavier et les gestes du trackpad fonctionnent donc toujours. L’écran tactile ouvre surtout de nouveaux usages. Par exemple, les graphistes peuvent dessiner sur toute la surface de l’écran.
Le design de l’appareil évolue également. L’encoche qui abritait la webcam disparaît. Comme sur l’iPhone, Apple la remplace par une Dynamic Island, un poinçon qui affiche des informations et des alertes autour de la caméra. Sur Mac, elle accueille notamment Spotlight, les Activités en direct et Siri AI. D’un simple toucher, on peut accepter un transfert AirDrop ou mettre un morceau en pause. Côté webcam, Apple mise sur une caméra de 12 mégapixels.
À lire aussi : Avec son écran tactile, le prochain MacBook Pro ne serait vraiment pas comme les autres
Le retour des puces M5 Pro et M5 Max
Sous le capot, on ne trouve pas de nouvelle puce. Les MacBook Pro tactiles recyclent les puces M5 Pro et M5 Max lancées en mars dernier. Apple aurait en effet renoncé aux déclinaisons Pro et Max de la puce M6. Selon les futies, le géant de Cupertino aurait pris la décision de se concentrer sur la génération M7. La puce M5 Pro embarque jusqu’à 18 cœurs de processeur et 20 cœurs graphiques, tandis que la M5 Max peut bénéficier jusqu’à 40 cœurs graphiques. La mémoire unifiée grimpe jusqu’à 128 Go, et le stockage peut désormais atteindre 16 To. Bref, c’est un appareil monstrueux pour les professionnels exigeants.
Côté autonomie, Apple promet jusqu’à 24 heures de lecture vidéo sur le 16 pouces, et jusqu’à 22 heures sur le 14 pouces M5 Pro. La connectique comprend trois ports Thunderbolt 5, un port HDMI, un lecteur de cartes SDXC, une prise casque et un connecteur MagSafe. Le Wi-Fi 7 et le Bluetooth 6 sont aussi de la partie. Selon Apple, les six haut-parleurs offrent des basses 50 % plus profondes. Comme sur les autres MacBook Pro, l’adaptateur secteur est vendu séparément en France.
Un design plus fin et plus léger
Apple explique avoir entièrement repensé le système de refroidissement du MacBook. Grâce à l’OLED, dont la dalle est plus compacte, l’ordinateur est aussi un peu plus fin, et surtout nettement plus léger que ses prédécesseurs. Les bordures autour de l’écran sont aussi plus fines.
Apple a aussi conçu une nouvelle charnière pour accompagner l’écran. Celle-ci doit éviter que l’écran vacille quand on le touche, l’un des défauts les plus agaçants des ordinateurs portables tactiles. Le MacBook Pro est proposé en noir sidéral et en argent. Il conserve le lecteur d’empreintes Touch ID, logé dans le bouton d’allumage.
Prix et date de sortie des MacBook Pro tactiles
Comme attendu, l’OLED et le tactile font grimper la facture. En France, le MacBook Pro 14 pouces tactile est proposé à partir de 3 299 euros. Le 16 pouces démarre à 3 899 euros. Les précommandes ouvrent ce mercredi 28 octobre, pour une disponibilité le vendredi 6 novembre. L’écran nano-texturé est facturé 165 euros de plus sur tous les modèles. Voici tous les tarifs en France :
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces, M5 Pro, 24 Go de RAM, 1 To : 3 299 euros
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces, M5 Pro, 48 Go de RAM, 1 To : 4 199 euros
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces, M5 Max, 36 Go de RAM, 2 To : 5 199 euros
- MacBook Pro 14 pouces, M5 Max, 48 Go de RAM, 2 To : 5 859 euros
- MacBook Pro 16 pouces, M5 Pro, 24 Go de RAM, 1 To : 3 899 euros
- MacBook Pro 16 pouces, M5 Pro, 48 Go de RAM, 1 To : 4 559 euros
- MacBook Pro 16 pouces, M5 Max, 36 Go de RAM, 2 To : 5 599 euros
- MacBook Pro 16 pouces, M5 Max, 48 Go de RAM, 2 To : 6 199 euros
Sur le 16 pouces M5 Pro, passer de 24 à 48 Go de RAM coûte 660 euros. Les plus exigeants peuvent monter jusqu’à 128 Go de RAM et 16 To de stockage. Tous ces prix s’entendent avec l’écran standard. Les modèles sont proposés en noir sidéral et en argent, au même tarif.
Sans grande surprise, ces nouveaux modèles ne remplacent pas les MacBook Pro actuels. Apple continue de vendre les versions mini-LED, moins chères, pour toucher tous les consommateurs. Les MacBook Pro mini-LED démarrent à 2 899 euros en 14 pouces et à 3 399 euros en 16 pouces. Il faut donc compter 400 euros de plus pour le 14 pouces tactile, et 500 euros de plus pour le 16 pouces.
Ces MacBook Pro tactiles ne sont qu’une première étape pour la gamme d’ordinateurs Apple. D’après le journaliste Mark Gurman, Apple prépare déjà des PC tactiles animés par des puces M7 Pro et M7 Max pour l’automne 2027.

articles.title: Nouvelles heures creuses dès le 4 novembre : comment vérifier si vous êtes concerné par le changement d'horaires d’EDF
articles.text:
Nouvelles heures creuses dès le 4 novembre : comment vérifier si vous êtes concerné par le changement d'horaires d’EDF
Dès le 4 novembre, EDF basculera 9,3 millions de foyers vers de nouvelles heures creuses en journée. Voici comment savoir si votre contrat électrique s’apprête à changer.
Lancée en novembre 2025 par la Commission de régulation de l’énergie (CRE), la grande réforme de l’option heures pleines/heures creuses entre dans sa seconde et dernière phase. Après une première vague ayant touché 1,7 million de ménages au printemps dernier, EDF amorce le déploiement final dès ce mercredi 4 novembre. Jusqu’en novembre 2027, près de 9,3 millions d’abonnés verront ainsi leurs créneaux tarifaires évoluer pour soulager le réseau et absorber le surplus de production photovoltaïque en journée.
Des tarifs réduits en plein après-midi pour profiter du surplus d’énergie solaire
Avant toute chose, le principe de base demeure intact avec huit heures quotidiennes facturées à prix réduit. Au Tarif Bleu d’EDF, le kilowattheure s’affiche ainsi à 0,1589 € TTC en heures creuses contre 0,2142 € TTC en heures pleines, soit une économie de 26 %. La véritable nouveauté réside dans l’instauration d’une saisonnalité des horaires, orchestrée par Enedis selon les contraintes locales.
Toute l’année, chaque foyer conservera au minimum cinq heures creuses consécutives la nuit, entre 23 h et 7 h, idéales pour recharger une voiture électrique ou lancer les appareils énergivores (lave-linge, lave-vaisselle, sèche-linge). Les deux à trois heures restantes basculeront désormais l’après-midi, entre 11 h et 17 h, surtout durant la période estivale d’avril à octobre, afin d’absorber le pic de production solaire. En hiver, certains foyers garderont toutefois l’intégralité de leurs créneaux la nuit.
Pour savoir si votre logement fait partie des foyers concernés, inutile de chercher midi à quatorze heures. En consultant votre espace client, EDF rappelle que “si vos heures creuses incluent une plage horaire entre 7 h et 11 h ou entre 17 h et 23 h, vos horaires seront modifiés”. Quant à ceux qui disposent déjà d’heures creuses en journée, ils en conserveront au moins deux en période estivale.
À noter que seuls les abonnés n’ayant pas bénéficié d’un nouveau créneau entre le 1er novembre 2025 et le 31 mai 2026 sont visés. Vous serez prévenus par votre fournisseur au moins un mois avant la bascule. Puisque ces modifications s’étaleront du 4 novembre 2026 au 30 novembre 2027, chacun disposera donc du temps nécessaire pour anticiper au mieux. Quant aux nouveaux clients abonnés depuis le 6 octobre 2026, leurs contrats intègrent déjà directement ces nouvelles plages horaires saisonnalisées.
