articles.title: Apple announces touchscreen MacBook Pro with OLED display
articles.text:
LOS ANGELES—Apple today announced and gave a first glimpse of its first major MacBook Pro redesign in more than five years. As rumored, it includes an OLED display and, for the first time on macOS, a touchscreen—a change Apple has long debated. (Former CEO Steve Jobs famously was opposed.)
Apple’s demonstration video showed users interacting with applications by reaching up to touch the screen, including file dragging and multi-touch gestures like pinch-to-zoom. It does not appear to be a 2-in-1 convertible design, though; all the footage was of people reaching up to touch the screen in a normal laptop configuration.
The OLED display (which Apple is, of course, calling the PROLED XDR) seems to be the real highlight here, compared to earlier models: It can achieve 2,000 nits in terms of maximum brightness, and Apple says it has a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio. References were made to burn-in protection, but details on which approach it’s taking for that weren’t yet shared. The display retains the 120 Hz variable refresh rate of its predecessors.
Beyond that, the design is largely similar to the existing one, but there are a few notable differences. First, it’s much lighter. Apple said when announcing it that the 14-inch model is just 3 pounds, down around half a pound from the previous model, depending on configuration.

articles.title: The Download: dead startups fueling AI and interspecies communication
articles.text:
The Download: dead startups fueling AI and interspecies communication
Plus: Hackers have disrupted the US Federal Election Commission’s website.
This is today's edition of The Download, our weekday newsletter that provides a daily dose of what's going on in the world of technology.
AI labs are buying data from dead startups to train their models
When Keelan Miskell began winding down his crypto startup, he didn’t think its data was worth much. But he’s since turned the company’s digital archives into tens of thousands of dollars, selling its codebase and workspace data.
He’s part of a growing market in which companies that help shut down startups sell their data to AI labs. Demand has grown as training labs hit the limits of public and synthetic datasets, with buyers seeking real-world records to help train AI agents. But the sales raise legal and ethical questions.
Read the full story on the AI labs buying up the remains of failed startups.
—Matthew King
Are we there yet? Interspecies communication
Humans are far from the only species with a gift for gab, and our furry, feathered, and finned friends could have a lot to tell us.
Decoding how animals communicate with one another could reveal the inner lives of other species—and give humans a window onto how they see the world. A growing arsenal of devices and advances in AI have made it easier to study their howls, squeaks, and clicks, but making sense of it all remains complex.
Find out how close we are to interspecies communication.
—Cassandra Willyard
This story is part of “Are we there yet?”, our series that takes stock of six technologies that have long promised to change the world—and scores them on a progress meter. We’re exploring each one in The Download, so stay tuned, and subscribe to read the rest of the stories in our new Impossible issue.
MIT Technology Review Narrated: what it would take to build a city on the moon
The US and China are racing to build bases on the moon, with NASA hoping to establish a small lunar city by the end of the century. But the moon is a tremendously hostile place to set up camp.
A sprawling lunar base must be safe for its inhabitants, protected from falling asteroids, endless cosmic radiation, razor-sharp lunar dust, and torturous temperature swings. It also must be somewhat self-sustaining.
That will require autonomous robots, nuclear power, and a way to use the moon’s resources to keep the base operating. But the chief obstacle may be one of political will.

articles.title: A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
articles.text:
A hacker stole a trove of personal information from the Department of Homeland Security (DHS). The breach exposes the names, job titles, phone numbers, email addresses, and office locations of more than 41,000 employees, including those in US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP), according to TechCrunch and Wired. The data also linked the agencies to specific surveillance tools.
A hacker stole more than 40,000 DHS employee records
The names, job titles, phone numbers, and emails of thousands of ICE, CBP, and other DHS employees were compromised in a massive hack.
As reported by TechCrunch, a hacker known as “Department of Peace” gained access to the data through Okta, an identity and access management service used by the DHS. Around 21,000 records pertain to CBP employees, and nearly 7,000 belong to staff at ICE. The data also includes records from the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA), US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS), and Homeland Security Investigations (HSI).
The DHS has worked to conceal the identities of CBP and ICE agents, who have carried out anti-immigration raids around the US, while also tracking down online critics. “They have our information, so it’s only fair that we have theirs,” the “Department of Peace” hacker said, according to TechCrunch. This leak comes just weeks after hackers stole data from the FBI on its employees and job applicants.
The leaked DHS information was reportedly given to cybersecurity researcher maia arson crimew, who shared it with Distributed Denial of Secrets (DDoSecrets), a nonprofit organization that’s now hosting the leaked “Icepick” dataset. The leak also reportedly includes information about DHS groups that have access to tools that can be used for surveillance, such as the facial recognition app Mobile Fortify and PenLink, which can collect and analyze data from phones and online services.
The DHS didn’t immediately respond to The Verge’s request for comment.

articles.title: ¿Cuánto cuesta el MacBook Pro táctil más caro? Prepárate para llorar
articles.text:
Los MacBook Pro ProLED XDR de 14 y 16 pulgadas, que estrenan pantalla OLED y táctil, son oficiales. Apple finalmente ha implementado la tecnología multitáctil en sus portátiles más avanzados, que también implementan un rediseño que los hacen más livianos y delgados.
Quienes busquen un MacBook Pro táctil pueden elegir entre los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max, como los que ya estaban disponibles en los modelos convencionales. Cada SoC tienen dos variantes:
- CPU de 15 núcleos y GPU de 16 núcleos, o CPU de 18 núcleos y GPU de 20 núcleos en el caso del M5 Pro;
- CPU de 18 núcleos y GPU de 40 núcleos, o CPU de 18 núcleos y GPU de 40 núcleos en el caso del M5 Max.
Vale aclarar que los ordenadores se pueden configurar en cualquiera de las cuatro opciones recién mencionadas si se trata del modelo de 14 pulgadas. En el de 16'' solo está disponible la opción más potente de M5 Pro.
En materia de memoria unificada, los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil inician en 24 GB, y se pueden configurar con hasta 128 GB. Mientras que la gran sorpresa está en el almacenamiento, pues si bien mantienen 1 TB como opción base, ahora es posible configurarlos con hasta 16 TB; es decir, el doble de lo que se ofrecía antes.
Dicho todo esto, está más que claro que los MacBook Pro con pantalla tándem OLED y táctil no son baratos. El modelo más económico se inicia en los 3.349 euros, que de barato no tiene nada. Pero ese número puede multiplicarse con facilidad a medida que se va explorando el configurador de Apple.
Cuánto vas a pagar por los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil más caros
En el caso del MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil de 14 pulgadas, la versión más cara es la que lleva chip M5 Max con CPU de 18 núcleos y GPU de 40 núcleos, con 128 GB de RAM y 16 TB de almacenamiento. Esta variante incluye el vidrio nanotexturizado para la pantalla y un adaptador de corriente de 96 vatios y cuesta ni más ni menos que 16.059 euros.
Si te sientes todavía más atrevido, puedes inclinarte por la opción de 16 pulgadas. Aquí, el modelo con M5 Max de 18 núcleos y 40 núcleos núcleos, 128 GB de memoria, 16 TB de almacenamiento, vidrio nanotexturizado y adaptador de corriente de 140 vatios se consigue a cambio de 16.433 euros.
Estos precios contemplan solamente el hardware de los nuevos MacBook Pro ProLED XDR con pantalla táctil. Ambas cifras se pueden hacer todavía más grandes si decides comprar las licencias de Final Cut Pro (+349,99 euros) y Logic Pro (+229,99 euros) para que lleguen preinstalados. Y si optas por añadir AppleCare+ en su póliza de pago al contado, que brinda tres años de cobertura, tienes que añadirle 479 o 579 euros más a la cuenta, según el modelo que elijas.
Así las cosas, el MacBook Pro táctil más caro que puedes comprar cuesta 17.117,98 euros para la versión de 14 pulgadas y 17.591,98 euros para la de 16 pulgadas. The more you know... ¯\(ツ)/¯

articles.title: Investable.Africa launches platform to connect African startups with investors - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
African startup funding platform Investable.Africa has launched in open beta, giving founders access to a database of more than 4,000 investing firms and investors free access to deal flow from all 54 African countries.
Investable.Africa grew out of a WhatsApp group founder Craig McLeod – who also runs online store builder BoxCommerce – has run for the past decade as both a venture capitalist and a founder. The group brings African founders and VCs together with three aims – increasing funding into Africa, eliminating bad term sheets, and helping founders build the networks they need.
“For 10 years I’ve watched great African founders struggle to reach the right investors, and sign terms they didn’t need to accept,” said McLeod. “The group showed what happens when founders and investors talk openly. Investable.Africa takes that to every founder on the continent, not just the ones who already have the right phone numbers.”
The platform allows founders to build a profile covering their problem, solution, traction, team and current round, with every profile checked by the Investable.Africa team before going live. Founders can upload a pitch deck, which only approved investors can open, and a data room, with founders deciding who sees which folders.
Founders can search the investor database by stage, cheque size, sector, lead or follow, ownership target, founder focus and location, with each firm’s partners and contact routes listed. The database is built from public lists, which are credited openly. Founders can also connect Claude, ChatGPT or another AI assistant to the database to shortlist firms that fit their round and draft personalised outreach for review.
Founders can see who has viewed their profile, opened their deck or read a file, post updates to investors following them, and receive messages from investors addressed to the whole founding team.
Investors use the platform for free, and are vetted before they can see full profiles and decks. They can filter startups by region, country, sector, stage, round type and raise size, or view only companies currently raising. A deal flow overview brings together matching startups, open access requests, data rooms and updates, while investors can request data rooms with a short note explaining their interest and follow startups to receive founder updates by email.
Investors can also list their own firm in the database, and can buy vouchers to sponsor a founder’s listing for a year, with credit as the sponsor.
Founders can build a profile for free, with a listing costing US$99 a month or US$299 per year. Investable.Africa takes no share of any raise and does not handle investment money.

articles.title: DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite : une station électrique de 2 kWh qui se recharge au soleil comme en voiture
articles.text:
Six mois après la Power 1000 Mini, DJI est de retour sur le segment de l’énergie avec la Power Auro 2000 Elite. Cette station électrique de 2 kWh (2 016 kWh précisément) est présentée par le géant des drones comme la plus compacte de sa gamme à cette capacité. La station électrique s’inspire en effet de ces aînés pour offrir un volume de 25 litres et un poids d’environ 19 kg, ce qui lui permet d’être 24 % moins volumineuse et 14 % plus légère que la DJI Power 2000. Quant à son encombrement, il se veut proche de celui de la Power 1000 V2, qui ne stocke pourtant que 1 kWh.
Avec ses 456 × 225 × 245 mm, elle se montre aussi un peu plus compacte que l’Anker Solix C2000 Gen 2 que nous avons testé (459 × 250 × 257 mm), pour un poids équivalent. DJI précise toutefois qu’elle ne remplace pas la Power 2000, qui reste sa référence pour les usages les plus gourmands.
La Power Auro 2000 Elite délivre jusqu’à 2 000 W en continu sur ses trois prises secteur, avec un signal sinusoïdal pur, et peut alimenter certains appareils d’environ 2 200 W. Elle compte aussi deux ports USB-C de 65 W, deux ports USB-A et, plus original, un câble USB-C rétractable de 140 W. Celui-ci s’enroule automatiquement dans le boîtier, de quoi recharger un ordinateur portable ou un smartphone sans chercher de câble. Dans le but de faciliter l’accès, toutes les prises sont regroupées sur une seule face.
Un chargeur solaire et un chargeur de voiture intégrés
La principale nouveauté avec ce modèle tient à sa conception tout-en-un. DJI a intégré dans le boîtier un régulateur solaire MPPT et un chargeur de voiture, là où la concurrence passe souvent par des accessoires. La station d’Anker demande, par exemple, un chargeur d’alternateur optionnel de 800 W pour se recharger rapidement en voiture.
Le port propriétaire de DJI et bien présent et les deux ports SDC de la Power Auro 2000 Elite acceptent chacun jusqu’à 600 W, pour un total de 1 200 W. Dans ces conditions, DJI évoque une recharge complète en 2,7 heures environ au soleil et 4 heures en voiture. Les câbles nécessaires sont en revanche vendus à part.
Sur secteur, avec un simple câble d’alimentation et le mode de recharge rapide activé dans l’application, la batterie accepte jusqu’à 2 000 W et passerait de 0 à 80 % en une heure, pour une charge complète en 75 minutes. Elle peut aussi combiner le secteur avec le solaire ou la voiture, toujours dans la limite de 2 000 W.
Une batterie qui vise aussi la maison
DJI met également en avant un usage domestique pour les cas de coupure, avec un mode onduleur qui bascule sur la batterie en 0,01 seconde. Cela doit permettre de garder une box internet ou un ordinateur allumés. À faible charge, la station resterait sous les 30 dB, suffisamment discrète pour fonctionner la nuit, et l’application DJI Home permet de suivre en temps réel l’énergie consommée et stockée.
Associée à des panneaux solaires et à un micro-onduleur, vendus séparément, elle peut aussi injecter jusqu’à 800 W dans le circuit électrique de la maison, à la manière d’une batterie solaire domestique, pour consommer le soir l’énergie produite en journée. Cette fonction n’est toutefois proposée que dans certains pays, précise le fabricant. DJI avance qu’avec cinq batteries d’extension, l’ensemble pourrait fournir plus de 1 000 kWh par an, avec un retour sur investissement en 3,5 ans pour l’unité principale seule. Comme toujours, ces estimations sont à prendre avec prudence, puisqu’elles dépendent largement de l’installation solaire, de l’ensoleillement et du prix de l’électricité.
La capacité de la station pourra justement être étendue jusqu’à 12 kWh avec cinq batteries d’extension de 2 kWh, présentées comme les plus compactes de DJI, mais dont la commercialisation n’interviendra que plus tard. Côté sécurité, la Power Auro 2000 Elite repose sur des cellules LFP, réputées plus stables, qui conserveraient plus de 70 % de leur capacité après 6 000 cycles, soit une dizaine d’années d’utilisation quotidienne selon DJI.
Fidèle à son écosystème, le fabricant permet enfin de recharger rapidement ses batteries de drones via les ports SDC, jusqu’à 240 W avec le câble dédié. Une batterie de DJI Air 3 passerait ainsi de 10 à 95 % en 30 minutes. La DJI Power Auro 2000 Elite est disponible dès aujourd’hui au prix de 1 099 euros.

articles.title: When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
articles.text:
When content becomes infinite, what makes people pay attention?
At TechSparks 2026, leaders from HT Media Labs, Inshorts, and Eloelo Group discuss why credibility, human creativity, and audience-first formats will matter as content creation scales.
We are living in a world where content is no longer scarce. There is more news, more videos, more creators, and, AI that can generate almost anything we ask for. But this abundance brings a new challenge: when everyone is creating content, how do you get someone to stop scrolling, pay attention, and come back?
On the sidelines of TechSparks 2026, Avinash Mudaliar, Co-founder and CEO of HT Media Labs and the creator of Saregama Carvaan; Deepit Purkayastha, Co-founder and CEO of Inshorts; and GSN Aditya, COO of Eloelo Group, came together for a discussion titled The Format Is the Product: When Content Becomes Infinite.
The conversation explored how formats shape the way audiences consume content, what makes a format resonate in an increasingly crowded digital landscape, and why the format itself can be as important as the content it carries.
What is the differentiator in all this: the format, distribution, personalisation or the relationship with the consumer?
“Actually, the four items you mentioned aren't rivals. They are congruent; they co-exist. And all of them need to be married in a particular combination to get a person to come back. Right now, the problem is not content. Content has become infinite. Time has become finite,” said Mudaliar.
He explained that when he was building Carvaan, he had a clear target audience: people who didn't want to open an app, create a playlist, log in, pay, go through the entire rigmarole just to listen, and then go to a search bar and search for a song.
Carvaan put in 5,000 songs in a fully digitised, personalised product, without advertising itself as digital. Instead, it recreated the experience of listening to old-time radio, limiting the choices available and allowing listeners to immerse themselves in the music. With OTT Play, the focus was primarily on personalisation, helping users decide what to watch, where to watch it and how.
Purkayastha said that when he started Inshorts 12 years ago, people were beginning to consume content on smartphones, but no app was truly innovating on how they consumed news and information on these devices.
“Today, people come to us because they want a reliable, factual source of information. They want to stay updated on the world, but they don't want the noise and provocativeness of social media. We are a source reliable enough that they can use it during their digital detox,” he said.
For Eloelo, the micro-drama format unlocked the ability to tell many more stories faster and reach a wider audience.
“I think people's tastes continue to change, and while there is infinite content, the top 5% is often where most of the eyeballs go. So it comes down to your ability to keep reinventing the story arc, tell new stories, and deliver them through state-of-the-art data science to personalise content so people always see what they want to see,” said Aditya.
The role of AI
There's a general perception that AI can create everything, so what will audiences actually value?
Purkayastha says that while AI platforms are increasingly meeting consumers’ on-demand information needs, people still want real-time updates.
“AI can't imagine what's happening at TechSparks right now. Someone has to feed it into the system. That is live content generation, and that is news. Summaries and articles are the collateral that emerge from it.
“When an event happens, the question is which sources and distributors will be trusted. Trust becomes the most interesting capital they build, and I think LLM agents will value it too.”
Aditya believes AI will accelerate content creation but cannot replace human creativity. “It's a great enabler for people to tell stories, but I don't think it will substitute for human creativity,” he says, pointing out that despite the money and data invested in Hollywood and Bollywood, no deterministic system can predict whether a story will be a hit.
“People's tastes continuously change, and their expectations change. That can only be solved by human creativity.”
He added that AI would speed up storytelling workflows, while creativity and inspiration would remain human-driven.
Trust and verification
Mudaliar points to trust and verification as key differentiators in an AI-driven content ecosystem.
“There's a very interesting concept we're trying out at HT Tech right now. HT is already a trusted source for most LLMs for India-oriented news and beyond, simply because we've been around for the last 100 years. We take pride in our journalism, and we put out verified stories. We are now building another ecosystem within HT called HT Verify,” he explained.
“For example, our team member here is capturing this event, creating a video out of it that will also be made into social content, and writing maybe 3,000 words on it, written to the schema AI LLMs prefer and made citable by the AI. So you are literally training the AI that this content is not only trustworthy, it's also verified and ready for consumption. That results in your content being cited and picked up, and then transmogrified for the user,” he added.
For Purkayastha, understanding audiences beyond urban India meant identifying a gap in trustworthy local content. When Inshorts began exploring consumption patterns in smaller cities in 2019, as mobile internet use surged following Jio's arrival, the team realised that local news from smaller towns often went unreported.
“We realised that the biggest gap in those markets was that content generation wasn't happening in a trustworthy way,” he says.
The company addressed this gap with Public, a platform featuring verified creators who report on their towns and cities. Launched in 2019, it has since reached about 80 million users.
For Aditya, micro-drama economics have created opportunities to tell stories for more specific audiences rather than chase mass appeal. With lower production costs and shorter turnaround times, creators can experiment with stories rooted in particular regions and communities.
“I no longer have to make storylines that only appeal to a large catchment of people. I can now talk about storylines relevant to, say, a district in Uttar Pradesh, and the P&L still works. So we're now able to tap into Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala, each of these,” he said.
Mudaliar believes the industry still has a long way to go in designing products for India's diverse linguistic audiences. Despite the emphasis on building for Bharat, he argues, many products continue to draw inspiration from platforms designed primarily for urban consumers.
“98% of India consumes in a local language. He doesn't know how to search; he doesn't know how to write in English; he's trying. For him, voice search is the first point of contact because he doesn't know how to type. That's why even Google Maps, even your Uber drivers, use voice. So why aren't we building voice-first products for India?” he asked.

articles.title: El sistema LZB que ha fallado en el accidente de Toledo debería haber sido sustituido en su totalidad por ERTMS-2 en 2026
articles.text:
El 21 de abril de 1992, España asiste al primer viaje comercial en una línea de alta velocidad. Es el Madrid-Sevilla construido, entre otras cosas, para dar servicio a la Expo 1992 que se va a vivir en la ciudad andaluza. Quedan 11 años para que se abra la siguiente línea de alta velocidad española, el tramo Madrid-Zaragoza-Lleida del corredor Madrid-Barcelona.
Durante esa década se produce un cambio clave en la extensión de las líneas de alta velocidad en Europa. Esa segunda línea, llega ya con el sistema de seguridad ERTMS que viene a sustituir el sistema LZB, instalado en la línea Madrid-Sevilla. Un corredor que estaba siendo modernizado con este sistema generalizado en Europa y cuya implantación definitiva se esperaba para abril de 2026. El accidente de Urda (Toledo) se produce justo durante este proceso de renovación y antes de que se complete del todo.
El ERTMS es un sistema de seguridad que utiliza protocolos diferentes que el LZB. Ambos están considerados como de máxima seguridad pero desde hace tiempo se ha dado la orden desde la Unión Europea de modernizar las líneas al primero de ellos y abandonar el LZB para armonizar todos los lenguajes de seguridad.
Con motivo del accidente ferroviario de Adamuz (Córdoba), en La Vanguardia recogían que en Europa hay hasta 25 sistemas de seguridad diferentes, con 227.000 kilómetros de vías no operables porque no utilizan el mismo sistema de seguridad. Aunque debería ofrecer un nivel de seguridad muy similar, este sistema LZB ya se puso en el punto de mira en enero aunque posteriormente se supo (las investigaciones siguen adelante) que la causa principal del accidente se debió a un fallo en la infraestructura de la vía que hizo descarrilar a un tren Iryo y éste fue golpeado por un Alvia de Renfe.
Un buen ejemplo de esa falta de operabilidad entre sistemas la hemos vivido en España. El corredor andaluz es el único en el que se sigue utilizando el sistema LZB, en lugar del ERTMS. Esto hizo que Ouigo retrasara su llegada a Andalucía porque estaba teniendo problemas para homologar los trenes, que hasta entonces sólo funcionaban con este segundo sistema de seguridad más moderno.
Una vía en proceso de renovación
Para evitar este tipo de situaciones, desde la Unión Europea se dio la orden de cambiar al nuevo sistema ERTMS-2, la evolución del ERTMS. En abril de 2025, el Ministerio de Transportes anunciaba que la línea estaba siendo modernizada para adaptarse a este sistema (de hecho, en los mapas de Adif se muestra que la línea está "en proceso de renovación") y que esperaban que al finalizar 2026 la línea estuviera completamente renovada. Es decir, entre otras actuaciones, con el sistema ERTMS-2 activo.
Este sistema ERTMS-2 funciona de manera diferente al LZB. Este último se basa en un cable zigzagueante que envía la información relativa a la posición del tren, su velocidad de paso y los metros que quedan hasta el próximo cambio en el límite de velocidad.
El sistema, además, cuenta con que el tren interrumpe este circuito cerrado, señalando al CRC (el centro de control de Adif) dónde está cada tren para que dos trenes no circulen por un mismo cantón (tramo ferroviario de kilómetros que se utiliza como sistema de seguridad para una frenada de emergencia). El propio sistema puede gestionar una frenada de emergencia para que un tren no "invada" un cantón donde ya hay un tren situado.
Si el sistema sufre cualquier tipo de avería, como se ha indicado con las primeras informaciones del accidente de Urda (Toledo), el maquinista debe prestar atención al sistema ASFA, el cual indica mediante señales físicas situadas a los lados de las vías si tiene o no permitido el paso y la velocidad máxima a la que puede circular.
El sistema ERTMS-2 funciona de manera diferente. Lo que hace, a grandes rasgos, es simplificar el proceso y el equipamiento. La conexión del tren se realiza por GSM-R y las balizas quedan como sistema redundante para localizar el tren.
Con este sistema, se utiliza un equipo de radio que comunica al tren con el Movement Authority o MA (Autoridad de movimiento), explican en Cómo funcionan los trenes. Esa MA es la encargada de decirle al conductor la velocidad máxima a la que puede circular y durante cuántos kilómetros pero incluye una mayor cantidad de información como restricciones de velocidad temporales, lo que facilita cumplir con los límites.
Explican estos expertos que el sistema tiene la ventaja de que si un tren sufre un problema pero ya no puede detenerse, puede pasar por un enclave a una velocidad adecuada sin riesgo a descarrilar y solo aplica el frenado de emergencia cuando la situación es segura. Al contrario, cierra el paso de todos los trenes al instante para que no se produzca un choque. Se considera que el sistema es más seguro porque cuenta con mayor información, sistemas redundantes y las decisiones se toman más rápidamente.
Además, esa simplificación y modernización de los componentes es clave. En 2020, el Consejo de Ministros y Adif autorizaron la renovación de la línea con una adjudicación de 108 millones de euros tal y como se había adelantado meses antes. En los pliegos técnicos se especificaba que se había llegado al final de la vida útil del sistema y que el soporte técnico se había complicado porque Siemens y Thales/Hitachi, los proveedores de componentes, han venido reduciendo la producción de los mismos por lo que se corría el riesgo de no encontrar repuestos en caso de rotura del sistema.
Los plazos de ejecución pasaban por tener lista esta renovación en 2025, recogía elEconomista a principios de la década cuando se hizo público el contrato de renovación. También Cinco Días recogía un plazo similar, necesitándose 52 meses para ejecutar la renovación. Sin embargo, este cambio en el sistema de seguridad se ha ido retrasando ligeramente.
El año pasado, ABC recogía que la renovación completa se esperaba que fuera efectiva "a lo largo de 2026". Explicaban que parte de los retrasos se debían a que aunque la modernización fue anunciada a principios de 2020, no fue hasta noviembre de ese mismo año cuando se dio por bueno el contrato definitivo. Y fue en septiembre de 2021 cuando las obras comenzaron. Estas obras se estaban realizando por la noche para no afectar al tráfico o hacerlo lo menos posible.
A pesar de ello, en abril de 2025, Transportes ponía una fecha más concreta para la renovación de la línea: "el objetivo es que celebre su 34 aniversario completamente renovada y contando con la tecnología más moderna del mercado, como el sistema ERTMS 2". Es decir, el cambio debía haberse producido por completo antes de abril de 2026.
Hay que recordar que el accidente de tren en Adamuz (Córdoba) mantuvo el corredor ferroviario durante meses. Eso sí, el salto a este sistema de seguridad más moderno ya debería haber llegado antes de enero de 2026, cuando éste se produjo. En aquella ocasión se debió a un problema en la infraestructura de la vía pero el sistema debía estar renovado para entonces.
En resumen, la renovación del sistema obedece a varias causas. La Unión Europea busca mayor operabilidad de las compañías en todo el continente para que la liberalización de las vías sea menos costosa y eficiente. Pero también apuesta por un sistema que tiene menor dependencia de componentes físicos y, por tanto, que presentan un desgaste más rápido y un mayor riesgo de rotura.
También por un sistema sensiblemente más seguro aunque, hay que recordar, el sistema LZB está considerado como uno de los más robustos y se utiliza en miles de kilómetros en otros países de Europa.

articles.title: « On avait du mal à toucher la population active » : dans la Sarthe, une mairie fait un bond technologique pour être ouverte 24h/24
articles.text:
À Marolles-les-Braults, dans la Sarthe, les habitants peuvent effectuer leurs démarches en ligne à toute heure. Derrière cette mairie qui se présente comme « ouverte 24h/24 », il y a surtout une volonté de simplifier le quotidien des usagers et de libérer du temps pour les agents.
Trouver un créneau pour aller en mairie quand on travaille toute la semaine relève parfois du casse-tête. À Marolles-les-Braults, commune sarthoise d’environ 2 000 habitants, c’est précisément ce public que l’on espère mieux accompagner. « On a du mal à toucher la population active, on ne la voit pas beaucoup en mairie », explique à Numerama Jonathan Cholet, directeur général des services.
Avec l’entreprise Nouvelle Époque, la commune a développé un espace citoyen permettant de déposer un dossier d’urbanisme, de réserver une salle des fêtes ou de gérer les inscriptions à la cantine depuis son ordinateur ou son téléphone.
Elle revendique ainsi le titre de « première mairie de France ouverte 24h/24 et 7j/7 ». Une formule à comprendre au sens numérique : les agents ne passent pas leurs nuits derrière le guichet, mais les habitants peuvent engager leurs démarches sans attendre son ouverture.
Digitaliser la première mairie de France
Le projet ne répond pas, au départ, à une demande explicite des administrés. Il naît du constat que les horaires des services municipaux s’accordent mal avec ceux d’une partie de la population, et d’une rencontre sur les réseaux sociaux.
« Nouvelle Époque avait un projet de digitaliser en totalité la première mairie ou ville de France », raconte Jonathan Cholet. Son intérêt pour les nouvelles technologies et le soutien du maire font le reste. Après un premier contact fin juillet, le travail commence véritablement fin août. Deux mois plus tard, la commune dispose d’un outil commun aux habitants et aux agents.
La commune affirme avoir transposé en ligne l’ensemble des démarches proposées à son guichet, dans les limites de ce que permet la réglementation. Cela ne signifie pas que toutes peuvent être achevées à distance, ni qu’une demande déposée le dimanche sera immédiatement validée. Certains dossiers nécessitent toujours un examen par les agents et certaines formalités, une présence physique. « Demain pour se marier, il va bien falloir encore venir physiquement en mairie », ironise Jonathan Cholet.
À la cantine, deux heures de tâches administratives en moins
Pour comprendre ce que change le dispositif, il faut aussi regarder du côté des agents. La mairie indique avoir regroupé dans une seule interface des tâches auparavant réparties entre plusieurs logiciels. L’objectif est notamment d’éviter de recopier les mêmes informations d’un outil à l’autre.
L’exemple le plus concret se trouve à la cantine scolaire. Les parents peuvent désormais signaler l’absence de leur enfant jusqu’à 8 h 30 le matin. Le nombre de repas à préparer est ensuite transmis automatiquement aux équipes, avec une répartition par service et par classe. Les informations nécessaires à la comptabilité suivent le même chemin.
« On avait une responsable de cantine qui passait une heure le matin à relever les présents et les absents dans les classes, et une heure l’après-midi à transmettre à la comptabilité », rapporte Jonathan Cholet. Selon lui, ce temps peut désormais être consacré aux enfants ou à des projets axés sur le contact humain.
À l’échelle de la mairie, qui compte six personnes, le directeur général des services estime que ces automatisations permettront de dégager l’équivalent du travail d’au moins deux agents. Il s’agit d’une estimation des gains à venir, avec un impératif qu’il tient à préciser : « Il ne s’agit pas du tout de supprimer des postes. » Le temps libéré doit permettre de mieux accompagner les habitants, notamment les familles en deuil ou les personnes qui constituent un dossier d’urbanisme.
Cette transformation passe aussi par des agents qui ont connu plusieurs générations d’outils. Jonathan Cholet prend l’exemple d’Isabelle, qui a « connu la machine à écrire ». À deux ans de la retraite, elle propose d’elle-même des améliorations pour la plateforme, raconte-t-il : « Ça balaie un peu les préjugés. » Pour le directeur général des services, l’âge des équipes ne saurait être un frein à la modernisation.
L’intelligence artificielle, elle, occupe une place très mesurée. Selon la collectivité et Nouvelle Époque, elle intervient uniquement via un chatbot propulsé par les modèles français de Mistral AI pour répondre aux questions basiques des usagers. Pour le reste, il s’agit d’automatisation classique de flux et de génération documentaire.
L’inspiration Apple : fermer l’écosystème pour verrouiller les données
Sur le volet technique, Nouvelle Époque assume une approche radicale : bâtir un environnement hermétique. Avant cette refonte, le site municipal tournait sous WordPress, une plateforme jugée trop exposée aux attaques automatisées. L’entreprise a donc développé son propre code propriétaire modulaire, déployé sur un serveur dédié par collectivité et hébergé chez OVH en France.
« On a imaginé l’écosystème d’Apple, où la marque a un système fermé, protégé et maîtrise toute la chaîne », détaille Alison Tartary, directrice générale de Nouvelle Époque. Pour pousser cette logique d’isolation, la société indique avoir banni Microsoft 365 ainsi que les solutions tierces non française, et prévoit même de déployer prochainement un système d’exploitation propriétaire sur mesure pour verrouiller les postes de travail municipaux. Il ne s’agit pas d’une condition pour bénéficier de leurs services, mais cela est encouragé par l’entreprise.
Selon celle-ci, la réduction de la surface d’attaque passe également par la suppression des comptes locaux : la mairie ne stocke ni identifiants ni mots de passe. L’authentification citoyenne repose exclusivement sur FranceConnect, tandis que les agents utilisent ProConnect. « Les données appartiennent à la mairie, les logiciels qu’on fait appartiennent à la mairie », martèle Alison Tartary, rappelant que chaque serveur dispose d’une sauvegarde et d’une machine de secours en cas d’incident. Si ce cloisonnement élimine de nombreuses failles courantes, un code fermé conçu par une structure restreinte ne garantit pas pour autant une inviolabilité absolue.
Côté budget, la commune rémunère la prestation sous la forme d’un abonnement annuel. Jonathan Cholet assure que la résiliation des huit contrats antérieurs compensera largement la facture. Les montants précis n’ayant pas été communiqués, il reste toutefois impossible de chiffrer l’économie nette réalisée à ce stade.
Le guichet reste ouvert, lui aussi
Reste l’enjeu de la fracture numérique : que deviennent les administrés réfractaires aux écrans ou dépourvus de connexion ? Jonathan Cholet insiste sur le maintien de l’accueil physique.
Pour éviter les décrochages, la commune a installé une grande tablette tactile munie d’un clavier à l’accueil de la mairie. Les usagers en difficulté y sont guidés par un agent. « On ne fait pas à leur place », souligne le responsable territorial. L’objectif est d’accompagner l’apprentissage pour rendre l’administré autonome sur d’autres portails publics, comme Ameli ou les impôts.
Marolles-les-Braults espère désormais faire figure d’exemple auprès d’autres collectivités. L’expérimentation montre qu’une petite commune peut revoir ses processus informatiques de fond en comble, à condition d’accompagner les agents comme les citoyens dans la transition. Nouvelle Époque indique de son côté être en contact avec « 5 à 6 » communes souhaitant franchir le cap d’ici la fin d’année.

articles.title: ChatGPT peut désormais fouiller dans vos mails iCloud, et nous avons essayé
articles.text:
ChatGPT accueille les mails et les calendriers iCloud, avec la promesse de simplifier quelques corvées du quotidien. Les utilisateurs Apple vont pouvoir en profiter, mais certains réglages méritent leur attention avant de laisser l’assistant fouiller dans leur correspondance.
Retrouver un mail reçu il y a trois semaines, vérifier l’heure d’un rendez-vous ou remettre la main sur une réservation noyée au milieu de dizaines de messages… On a tous connu ce petit moment de solitude devant sa boîte mail. OpenAI aimerait justement nous épargner ces recherches, parfois interminables, en laissant ChatGPT s’en charger directement. Après Gmail et Google Agenda, c’est au tour des services iCloud d’entrer dans la danse. Et pour une fois, nous avons pu vérifier assez simplement ce que cela change au quotidien.
ChatGPT s’invite dans les mails et les calendriers d’Apple
Depuis le 27 octobre, OpenAI propose deux nouveaux connecteurs permettant de relier ChatGPT à iCloud Mail et iCloud Calendar. Comme le rapporte MacRumors, ils sont accessibles aux utilisateurs gratuits comme payants, notamment en France, depuis le Web, les applications pour ordinateur et iOS.
L'idée n’est pas simplement de demander à ChatGPT de résumer un mail que l’on vient de copier dans une conversation. Le chatbot peut directement rechercher des messages dans votre boîte de réception, consulter votre agenda ou encore préparer des réponses. Le connecteur Mail annonce également la possibilité d’envoyer des messages et de gérer les brouillons, tandis que celui du calendrier permet de modifier des événements.
Prenons un exemple : vous avez reçu une confirmation de réservation il y a plusieurs jours, mais impossible de retrouver le message. Plutôt que de multiplier les recherches dans Mail, vous pouvez demander à ChatGPT de remettre la main dessus. Même principe pour consulter vos prochains rendez-vous, sans avoir à ouvrir Calendrier.
Précisons toutefois que le connecteur Mail accède uniquement à votre messagerie iCloud. Les comptes Gmail ou Outlook que vous avez éventuellement ajoutés à l’application Mail d’Apple ne deviennent pas automatiquement accessibles. Il faudra installer les plugins Google dédiés pour tout centraliser.
L'intérêt est surtout de pouvoir enchaîner les opérations dans une même conversation, sans multiplier les allers-retours entre les applications. Une approche qui peut sembler familière aux utilisateurs de Siri, mais qui prend ici une autre dimension grâce aux capacités conversationnelles de ChatGPT.
Nous avons essayé, et les brouillons arrivent directement dans Mail
Pour connecter sa messagerie, il faut se rendre dans les paramètres de ChatGPT, sélectionner iCloud Mail puis générer un mot de passe spécifique aux applications depuis son compte Apple. La connexion du calendrier s’effectue séparément.
Une fois cette petite formalité accomplie, nous avons demandé à ChatGPT de retrouver les messages reçus pendant la nuit. Le chatbot a pu consulter notre messagerie, puis préparer un brouillon de réponse à partir de l’un des échanges.
Et c’est là que l’intégration devient intéressante : le brouillon était directement disponible dans l’application Mail sur notre Mac. Pas de copier-coller, pas de transfert manuel, simplement un message prêt à être relu et éventuellement envoyé. Pour une tâche aussi banale que répondre à un correspondant, c'est plutôt pratique.
Nous n’avons toutefois pas testé l’envoi direct de messages ni la création ou la modification de rendez-vous. Impossible, à ce stade, de juger la fiabilité de ces opérations.
Reste évidemment la question de la confidentialité. Donner accès à sa messagerie personnelle à un assistant IA n’est pas tout à fait anodin, surtout lorsqu’elle contient des informations professionnelles, des factures ou des échanges privés.
Avant d’activer les connecteurs, mieux vaut donc jeter un œil au réglage « Améliorer le modèle pour tous » dans ChatGPT. Sur les offres grand public, les données récupérées par ces connecteurs peuvent être utilisées pour entraîner les modèles lorsque cette option est activée.
Il est possible de déconnecter les services depuis ChatGPT et de révoquer le mot de passe dédié dans son compte Apple. Attention néanmoins : couper l’accès à iCloud n’efface pas automatiquement les informations déjà reprises dans les conversations ou conservées en mémoire.
Un détail à garder en tête avant de confier à ChatGPT les clés de sa boîte mail.
- Chat dans différentes langues, dont le français
- Générer, traduire et obtenir un résumé de texte
- Générer, optimiser et corriger du code

articles.title: Volt Typhoon hides zero-day attacks using 'Silent Train' framework
articles.text:
Chinese state-sponsored hacking group Volt Typhoon has been using a framework that relies on rotating chains of connected devices compromised on demand, including for zero-day attacks targeting high-value systems.
The framework has been dubbed Silent Train because the threat actor uses it against select targets, cleans it up after each operation, and refreshes it continuously.
Researchers at Black Lotus Labs, the threat research division of communications company Lumen, have been tracking Silent Train for three years and confirmed that Volt Typhoon exploited at least four zero-day vulnerabilities in attacks targeting edge and management infrastructure.
Targets include telecommunication firms, government agencies, defense contractors, educational institutes, utilities/critical infrastructure, satellite service providers, IT firms, MSPs, transportation, aviation, and emergency services.
Black Lotus Labs’ observations indicate the most targeted regions are California, Texas, and Hawaii, suggesting a focus on Indo-Pacific matters.
Volt Typhoon previously targeted U.S. critical infrastructure, including communications, energy, transportation, and water systems, with CISA warning that it seeks to establish access for potential disruption during a future crisis or conflict.
According to the researchers, Silent Train's deployment was partly fueled by the FBI's disruption of KV-Botnet, a botnet that Volt Typhoon used to evade detection when attacking critical infrastructure in the US.
Silent Train relay network
Silent Train is practically a relay infrastructure formed of compromised devices that Volt Typhoon uses to hide the origin of its attacks.
The operators route their activity through VPS infrastructure outside the United States, then pass it through hacked devices such as routers that act as intermediate relays before launching attacks.
Black Lotus Labs says Intelbras modems served as overseas relays, while Netgear Orbi devices acted as hops in the U.S.
The threat actor's use of Silent Train involves exploiting vulnerabilities, stealing credentials, exfiltrating data, and maintaining persistent remote access to compromised systems.
By monitoring Silent Train activity, the researchers were able to observe zero-day exploits for the following products:
- CVE-2026-16812 – VeloCloudOrchestrator
- CVE-2026-20127 – Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN
- CVE-2025-8875 and CVE-2025-8876 – N-able N-central
- CVE-2024-39717 – Versa Director
- Quest KACE (suspected zero-day)
Compromising these platforms gives threat actors broad administrative control, enabling credential theft, remote access, and reach into downstream customers without the “noisy” lateral movement that might trigger detection.
“To construct these sessions, its operators exploit exposed web interfaces on SOHO, IoT, and other relay devices, then deploy only the tooling needed to enable chained SSH access through the compromised node,” Black Lotus Labs explains in a report today.
“This included temporary SSH services, keys, configuration files, and “live off the land” utilities.”
After the session ends, typically in under 8 hours, the threat actors remove all their tooling, keys, and configuration files from the disposable relays.
By early 2025, researchers noticed that the framework become hybrid, using disposable relays alongside compromised enterprise systems thaat were retained between one and three months.
Black Lotus Labs believes Silent Train was reserved for high-value targets and careful, hands-on operations conducted on China Standard Time (CST) timezone. The use of zero-days against those targets further strengthens the assumption.
The researchers recommend strengthening security around centralized management systems, restricting internet access to administrative interfaces, rapidly patching vulnerabilities, and centralizing logs with longer retention.
They also advise monitoring for unusual administrative activity, reviewing trusted connections that could expose customer or partner networks, and following CISA and NCSC guidance on Volt Typhoon.

articles.title: Juegos de PS Plus Essential para noviembre: calendario de anuncios, rumores y favoritos
articles.text:
Sony se prepara para revelar este 28 de octubre la lista de juegos esenciales de PlayStation Plus correspondiente a noviembre, con la llegada de los nuevos títulos programada para el martes 3 de noviembre. La selección de octubre, compuesta por F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896 y Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2, dejará de estar disponible el lunes 2 de noviembre.
Mientras se aguarda el anuncio oficial, circulan predicciones, pedidos de la comunidad y un repaso de lo que la plataforma ofreció en meses de noviembre anteriores.
Calendario oficial de PS Plus para noviembre de 2026
La dinámica de PlayStation Plus se mantiene constante: Sony anuncia la lista de juegos esenciales el último miércoles antes del cambio de mes y los títulos se activan el primer martes siguiente. Para noviembre, ese cronograma se traduce en una presentación el miércoles 28 de octubre y un lanzamiento el martes 3 de noviembre.
El plazo para reclamar los juegos de octubre vence el lunes 2 de noviembre, justo un día antes de que ingrese la nueva tanda. Además, se espera una revelación adicional vinculada a los niveles Extra y Premium el miércoles 11 de noviembre, con su correspondiente lanzamiento fijado para el martes 17 de noviembre.
Este esquema confirma que noviembre sigue el patrón habitual de la suscripción, sin alteraciones respecto al funcionamiento que Sony mantiene desde hace años para ordenar sus catálogos mensuales y extendidos.
Filtraciones y rumores previos al anuncio de noviembre
Hasta el momento no se registran filtraciones confiables sobre los juegos que integrarán el catálogo esencial de noviembre. La fuente más habitual en este tipo de adelantos suele ser el usuario billbil-kun, de Dealabs, quien en ocasiones anteriores reveló listados de PlayStation Plus con antelación a los anuncios oficiales de Sony.
Esas filtraciones no siguen un patrón fijo: algunas veces aparecen casi una semana antes de la presentación oficial, mientras que en otros meses se conocen apenas un día antes. Por ahora, no hay información concreta que permita anticipar los títulos de noviembre con certeza.
Ante la ausencia de datos filtrados, el análisis se apoya en los listados de noviembre de años anteriores y en los juegos relevantes que todavía no se incorporaron al servicio, dos variables que suelen ofrecer pistas sobre el tipo de selección que Sony podría preparar.
Qué trajeron los noviembres anteriores de PS Plus
El repaso histórico muestra que noviembre no tiene una identidad temática definida, a diferencia de octubre y su tendencia hacia el terror. En 2022, los suscriptores recibieron Nioh 2, LEGO Harry Potter Collection y Cuerpos Celestiales. En 2023 llegaron Mafia II: Definitive Edition, Dragon Ball: The Breakers y Aliens: Fireteam Elite.
El año 2024 sumó Ghostwire: Tokyo, Hot Wheels Unleashed 2: Turbocharged y Death Note Killer Within, mientras que en 2025 el catálogo incluyó Stray, EA Sports WRC 24 y Totally Accurate Battle Simulator.
La variedad de géneros, desde el combate exigente de Nioh 2 hasta la propuesta narrativa de Stray, sugiere que Sony utiliza noviembre para ofrecer una mezcla amplia de experiencias, sin apostar por un único tipo de juego o franquicia.
Favoritos para la lista de PS Plus de noviembre
Entre las predicciones aparece Stellar Blade, el juego de acción desarrollado por Shift Up que ya acumula más de dos años en el mercado desde su lanzamiento como exclusivo de PS5. Ese tiempo transcurrido lo coloca en el momento habitual en que los grandes exclusivos suelen integrarse al catálogo esencial.
Street Fighter 6 también figura entre las opciones consideradas, en un contexto marcado por el estreno reciente de su adaptación cinematográfica. Sin embargo, se señala que si Sony hubiera buscado aprovechar ese lanzamiento como promoción, es probable que ya lo hubiera incluido en octubre.
Blue Prince, el juego de puzles ambientado en una mansión cambiante, completa el grupo de favoritos. El título ya está disponible en el nivel Extra, pero existen antecedentes de juegos similares que luego se sumaron al nivel Essential, lo que abre la posibilidad de que repita ese recorrido en noviembre.
Pedidos de la comunidad para el catálogo essential
Más allá de las predicciones concretas, existe una lista de juegos que los usuarios esperan ver en PS Plus Essential, aunque su inclusión resulte menos probable. Resident Evil 4 Remake encabeza ese grupo: ya había sido mencionado como candidato para octubre y finalmente no se concretó.
Atomfall, el RPG de acción y supervivencia de Rebellion ambientado en una Gran Bretaña alternativa tras un desastre nuclear, también aparece en los pedidos. Lanzado en 2025, tuvo un desempeño sólido sin convertirse en un éxito masivo.
Fallout 4: Edición Aniversario se suma a la lista en un momento de popularidad renovada para la franquicia, impulsada por la adaptación televisiva de Amazon. Marvel’s Spider-Man 2 cierra el grupo de deseos, aunque su llegada se considera poco probable en el corto plazo tras el reciente lanzamiento de Marvel’s Wolverine.
Todos los juegos esenciales de PS Plus lanzados en 2026
El recorrido completo del año muestra la diversidad de títulos entregados mes a mes. Enero incluyó Need for Speed Unbound, Disney Epic Mickey: Rebrushed y Core Keeper, mientras que febrero sumó Undisputed, Subnautica: Below Zero, Ultros y Ace Combat 7: Skies Unknown.
Marzo trajo PGA Tour 2K25, Monster Hunter Rise, Slime Rancher 2 y The Elder Scrolls Online: Gold Road Collection. En abril llegaron Lords of the Fallen, Tomb Raider I-III Remastered y Sword Art Online: Fractured Daydream.
Mayo incorporó EA Sports FC 26, Nine Sols y Wuchang: Fallen Feathers. Junio sumó Grounded: Fully Yoked Edition, Nickelodeon All-Star Brawl 2 y Warhammer 40,000: Darktide. Julio ofreció Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III, For the King II y CrossCode.
Agosto incluyó Dying Light 2 Stay Human: Reloaded Edition, Big Walk y Signalis. Septiembre sumó Sniper Elite: Resistance, MLB The Show 26, Wobbly Life y Chained Echoes. Octubre cerró con F1 25, Hunt: Showdown 1896 y Earth Defense Force: World Brothers 2.
Precios actuales de las suscripciones de PS Plus
La estructura de precios de PlayStation Plus en Estados Unidos mantiene tres niveles. El plan Básico cuesta 10,99 dólares mensuales, 27,99 dólares por trimestre y 79,99 dólares en su modalidad anual.
El nivel Extra tiene un valor de 16,99 dólares al mes, 43,99 dólares trimestrales y 134,99 dólares de forma anual. El nivel Premium, el más completo, se ubica en 19,99 dólares mensuales, 54,99 dólares por trimestre y 159,99 dólares en el pago anual.
Las tarifas mensuales y trimestrales de los tres niveles registraron un incremento a comienzos de este año, mientras que los precios de las suscripciones anuales permanecieron sin modificaciones.

articles.title: Introducing Build-A-Chip-Bench: From Workload Specification to GDS
articles.text:
Home >
                                                                    Systems & Design >
                                                                Introducing Build-A-Chip-Bench: From Workload Specification to GDS                                                    
Systems & Design
                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Evaluate AI agents from workload specification through GDS layout, using open-source tools and an open-source PDK to assess their ability to complete the chip-design workflow.
								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: ChipAgents
								
							
Existing chip design benchmarks test isolated steps, such as writing RTL from a specification, and are increasingly saturated. ChipAgents is developing Build-A-Chip-Bench with contributions from Nvidia to the benchmark suite and scoring rubric. The benchmark evaluates AI agents from workload specification through GDS layout, using open-source tools and an open-source PDK to assess their ability to complete the chip-design workflow. Each design must pass a hard gate, covering functional correctness against a hidden verification IP as well as routability, hold timing, and DRC, and designs that pass are scored on PPA against the task’s constraints. The best agent passes the hard gate on 65% of tasks and reaches an overall score of 16.6%. Frontier agents struggle to revisit earlier decisions, protect working behavior while optimizing, and plan around slow tool runs.

articles.title: Flutterwave CEO on why African fintechs are trying to become banks
articles.text:
In April, Flutterwave, a pan-African fintech unicorn, secured a national microfinance banking licence through its acquisition of open banking startup Mono. It joined a growing group of Nigerian fintechs moving into regulated banking. In January, Paystack acquired Ladder Microfinance Bank, while Moniepoint secured a microfinance banking licence in 2025.
African fintechs are moving from only processing payments to holding deposits, providing credit and offering other banking services. For Olugbenga “GB” Agboola, cofounder and CEO of Flutterwave, African fintechs are becoming banks because payments alone are no longer enough.
Speaking at Moonshot in Lagos on Wednesday, Agboola said Flutterwave’s decision to obtain a national microfinance banking licence was driven by the need to control more of the infrastructure behind its payments business.
“What we’ve seen is you cannot provide a great payment experience if you don’t control the entire stack, or at least a big piece of the stack,” Agboola said. “And in most of those large stacks, it’s easy to source a third party who does not share the same level of focus that you have.”
Flutterwave has processed more than $40 billion in lifetime payments, giving it a large existing payments business to build its banking strategy around. The company has also said that more than 2 million businesses use its platform. Agboola said the scale of the payments business also exposed the limitations of relying on third-party financial institutions. If a partner bank goes down, parts of Flutterwave’s payment infrastructure can go down with it.
“We didn’t choose to do banking for the sake of banking,” Agboola said. “We chose to do banking to create more depth for our customers.”
The move into banking also gives Flutterwave a path into lending, an area where the company believes its existing transaction data could give it an advantage. Agboola said Flutterwave can see how businesses and consumers use its payment infrastructure, including when customers attempt transactions without sufficient funds or when businesses have receivables but need working capital immediately.
However, Flutterwave’s lending strategy is not immediately focused on becoming a mass-market lender. Agboola said the company is starting with liquidity and working-capital infrastructure, including pre-funding payouts for companies that need to make payments in Africa before receiving their own funds.
In June, Flutterwave raised a Series E round at a $3.25 billion valuation after Ripple invested an undisclosed amount in the company. The partnership also integrated Ripple’s RLUSD stablecoin into Flutterwave’s payment infrastructure.
The deal was part of a larger stablecoin strategy that followed the company’s partnership with Turnkey and Nuvion to launch stablecoin balances and embedded wallets supporting USDC and USDT. In June, it also partnered with Tempo to build stablecoin-powered payment and settlement infrastructure for African payments.
Agboola said the company is seeing businesses encounter stablecoins as a practical payment option, particularly when paying international suppliers.
“We’ve built what I call the largest deployment of stablecoins in Africa, where we support all the blockchains and stablecoins,” Agboola said.
The expansion is happening against a backdrop of rising competition between fintechs and traditional banks for control of customers’ financial relationships. Flutterwave says it currently operates across more than 35 countries and has more than 50 global licences.

articles.title: GitHub debuts Copilot Fusion, a new model selection & orchestration system that beats Claude Code for half the API cost
articles.text:
GitHub debuts Copilot Fusion, a new model selection & orchestration system that beats Claude Code for half the API cost
GitHub has debuted GitHub Copilot Fusion, a new system that handles model selection and orchestration for coding tasks so developers don’t have to.
Combining the advanced runtime model orchestration from Project HydraFusion with Copilot Auto Model Selection, Copilot Fusion can now handle both model selection and orchestration. GitHub says Fusion Max delivered comparable benchmark performance to Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max at about half the average API cost and in about 40% less time per task.
Generally available now, GitHub Copilot Fusion is part of GitHub’s new vision to make GitHub “the most comprehensive software delivery system in the world,” with developers delegating model choices while retaining responsibility for the direction and outcome of the work.
GitHub announced the news on Wednesday at GitHub Universe in San Francisco, the company’s flagship developer event.
GitHub Copilot Fusion is the decider now
For tasks involving reasoning, code generation, debugging, or tool use, GitHub says developers can delegate decisions about which models to use and how they work together. Its instructions: “choose Copilot Fusion and let Copilot intelligently route and orchestrate which models it uses for you.”
That sounds like a time-saver, since different tasks benefit from different models based on capabilities and cost. With Copilot Fusion working as the “model picker,” developers don’t have to weigh performance and price for every task.
More compelling is the idea that developers can use Copilot Fusion to strategically switch models mid-workflow, letting the system jump between models based on what best suits each step.
After analyzing what the task requires and choosing a model, the system orchestrates the next steps based on what makes the most sense. That may be a single model doing everything, a “cascading” workflow where a quality check evaluates one model’s response and then decides to accept it or escalate it, or a “critique” workflow where one model reviews another’s work.
That could reduce the mental load for developers who may inadvertently choose inefficient models when their attention drifts.
As Hari Pokhrel, principal software engineer at AT&T, describes in a statement for GitHub: “Previously, developers would often choose a more powerful model for a complex task and forget to switch back for everyday activities.”
So, what do developers get to decide for themselves?
Mostly, the effort level.
While Copilot Fusion handles model selection and orchestration, developers choose the effort level: Fusion Standard for everyday coding; Fusion High for more challenging tasks and deeper reasoning; Fusion Max for the most demanding, complex work.
That’s if you’re free and comfortable letting GitHub’s systems take the lead. If you prefer, developers can implement other controls.
Per GitHub, enterprise administrators can control which models Copilot Fusion can choose from, disabling certain models for Copilot Fusion without disabling them for the entire developer team. Administrators can also adjust the policy state for each model independently and set whether Copilot Fusion is or isn’t the default model for Copilot users.
The case for letting Copilot Fusion be your guide
According to GitHub and Pokhrel’s statement, offloading model selection and orchestration to the new fusion system is the smarter route for developers, letting you balance performance and cost without the friction of choosing between models.
GitHub says it has improved performance since launching Project HydraFusion as a research preview in September 2026. On the Artificial Analysis Coding Agent Index, GitHub reports that Copilot Fusion Max scored 60, within two points of Claude Code with Opus 5.5 Max. GitHub says Fusion Max delivered that result at about half the average API cost per task, using about half as many tokens and taking about 40% less time per task.
In the statement supplied to The New Stack by GitHub, Pokhrel credits Copilot Fusion Standard with improving token efficiency at AT&T, reducing unnecessary spending, and preserving capacity for higher-value work.
Model routing is becoming the default
Copilot Fusion is one piece of GitHub’s future vision, released alongside a slew of other products at the conference, including the GitHub Copilot app, Copilot Projects, and Copilot Automations.
By deferring model selection to its system, GitHub thinks developers will have more time and brainspace to focus on other work.
It looks like everyone is moving that way. This month, Ramp described moving model selection into Open SWE, its open-source coding agent. In the summer, Replit did the same, making its “intelligent model routing” system the default across every account.

articles.title: Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
articles.text:
Scientists overcome a hidden obstacle to more powerful quantum computers
- Date:
- October 25, 2026
- Source:
- RIKEN
- Summary:
- Scientists have discovered a way to operate multiple silicon qubits simultaneously with remarkable accuracy, overcoming a major challenge in scaling up quantum computers. Their new technique maintained accuracy of approximately 99.9% even when all five qubits were running at once, opening the door to larger and more powerful quantum processors.
- Share:
Silicon spin qubits could play a major role in the future of quantum computing because they can be produced using the same semiconductor manufacturing methods that make today's computer chips. However, researchers have faced a significant challenge. When multiple silicon qubits are controlled at the same time, their operations tend to become less accurate. Building practical, large quantum computers will require scientists to control many qubits simultaneously while keeping errors to a minimum.
Researchers at the RIKEN Center for Emergent Matter Science and their collaborators have now made important progress toward solving this problem. In a study published in Nature Physics, the team demonstrated highly accurate control of several silicon spin qubits operating simultaneously. Their experiments used an array of five qubits connected to a shared microwave control line. By identifying a major cause of errors during simultaneous operation, the scientists developed a technique to reduce those errors and maintain precision.
Leon Camenzind, a RIKEN research scientist and co-first author who supervised the experiments, explains the significance of the results: "This shows that high-fidelity control can be maintained even when several qubits are operated at the same time and represents an important step toward scaling up silicon-based quantum processors."
Scientists Identify a Hidden Source of Quantum Computing Errors
Unlike conventional computers, which store information as bits representing either 0 or 1, quantum computers use quantum bits, or qubits, that can exist in combinations of both states. Silicon spin qubits store this information using the spin of individual electrons confined within silicon. Performing reliable quantum calculations requires extremely precise control over these electron spins.
Microwave signals provide that control, but operating multiple qubits simultaneously can create unwanted effects that interfere with their accuracy. The researchers traced much of this problem to a phenomenon called the AC Stark shift.
This effect occurs when microwave control signals alter a qubit's effective energy levels, producing changes in the phase of its quantum state. Those phase shifts can disrupt the intended operation of individual qubits, particularly when several are being controlled at once.
To counteract the problem, the team created a calibration method that compensates for these unwanted shifts. Rather than separately calibrating every possible combination of qubits, the technique relies on calibrations performed between pairs of qubits. This makes the approach more practical for systems containing larger numbers of quantum bits.
"Rather than requiring an entirely separate calibration procedure for every possible combination of qubits, our method uses calibrations between pairs of qubits to compensate for the unwanted phase shifts," explains Yi-Hsien Wu, the first author who carried out the experiments as part of his PhD research.
Quantum Qubits Achieve Accuracy Above 99.99%
The researchers combined their calibration technique with an improved device design and carefully adjusted microwave control pulses. Their results showed that exceptionally high accuracy could be maintained even when multiple qubits were operating simultaneously.
When the five qubits were tested individually, each achieved single-qubit gate fidelity well above 99.99%, with the highest approaching 99.999%. Fidelity describes how closely a quantum operation matches its intended result.
The team then tested how well the system performed when several qubits were active together. With as many as three qubits operating simultaneously, fidelity remained above 99.99%. Even when all five qubits were controlled at once, accuracy stayed at approximately 99.9%, approaching the levels needed for practical fault-tolerant quantum computing.
Although the calibration method greatly reduced errors, it did not eliminate them entirely. The researchers found that the remaining loss of accuracy was linked to drive-induced decoherence, an effect caused by the greater microwave power required to operate multiple qubits simultaneously.
Unlike the unwanted phase shifts corrected by the new technique, decoherence involves the loss of the delicate quantum coherence needed for reliable operations.
According to Camenzind, "This is a limitation, but further improvements to device design could help mitigate this source of error."
A New Path Toward Larger Quantum Processors
The findings show that controlling several silicon spin qubits at the same time does not necessarily require a major sacrifice in accuracy. By correcting a key source of errors, the researchers have demonstrated a promising approach for operating more qubits through shared microwave control lines.
This is especially important for the development of large quantum processors. Giving every qubit its own independent control system would make increasingly complex devices difficult to manage. Shared control lines could offer a more practical way to expand these systems while maintaining the precision needed for quantum calculations.
"By addressing a key source of control errors through pairwise calibration," says Camenzind. "Our study supports the use of shared control lines as a practical approach to scaling up quantum processors. Combined with silicon's compatibility with established semiconductor manufacturing, we believe that this advance could help pave the way toward larger quantum processors capable of performing increasingly complex computations."
The broader objective is to develop quantum computers that can reliably perform calculations despite the errors and disturbances that affect quantum systems. Such machines, known as fault-tolerant quantum computers, will require precise, dependable control over large numbers of qubits.
"Our long-term goal is to build a fault-tolerant quantum computer based on silicon spin qubits, and reliable parallel control is an essential step toward that goal," adds Seigo Tarucha, project manager of a silicon quantum computing project under JST's Moonshot Goal 6.
Story Source:
Materials provided by RIKEN. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Yi-Hsien Wu, Leon C. Camenzind, Patrick Bütler, Ik Kyeong Jin, Akito Noiri, Kenta Takeda, Takashi Nakajima, Takashi Kobayashi, Giordano Scappucci, Hsi-Sheng Goan, Seigo Tarucha. Simultaneous high-fidelity single-qubit gates in a spin qubit array. Nature Physics, 2026; DOI: 10.1038/s41567-026-03466-2

articles.title: Watch this autonomous drone chase a person through a forest without GPS, maps, or cloud computing
articles.text:
Why it matters: Plenty of off-the-shelf drones can tail a cyclist down a trail these days, but most of them still lean on GPS to keep track of where they are. That's a problem in a forest, where a thick canopy can make the signal pretty unreliable. A lab at Purdue University has now shown off a drone that chases a person through the woods with no GPS at all.
Purdue computer science professor Aniket Bera posted the 44-second video on LinkedIn last Friday. It shows a quadcopter from his IDEAS Lab weaving between trees to keep a person in frame. And the drone works it all out on its own computer, without a map of the forest to rely on. Bera says skipping the cloud matters because a drone banking hard around a thin branch can't afford to wait on a server somewhere.
The person also keeps disappearing behind trunks, of course. For that, Bera's post lists an occlusion prediction step. It has the drone guess where its target is headed until they come back into view.
Navigating without GPS is also exactly the kind of autonomy the US military has been pouring money into. Last November, Purdue announced that the Army Research Laboratory had signed a five-year, $1.5 million deal with Bera's lab to build drones and ground robots that can find their way through hostile terrain without satellites. That said, the LinkedIn post doesn't say whether that money paid for the forest flights.
In the same post, Bera wrote that his team built every layer of the drone from scratch, from the 3D-printed carbon fiber frame to the software on the chip. As DroneXL noticed, though, the charts overlaid on the video label the drone's motion planner "SUPER" and its altitude estimate "FAST-LIO."
Those names belong to two open-source projects from the University of Hong Kong's MaRS Lab. SUPER is the lab's own LiDAR-guided drone. In a Science Robotics paper early last year, the team had it flying through unfamiliar terrain at more than 20 meters per second, or about 45 mph. A few weeks after that, the lab put the frame's design files online for free, including designs for 3D-printed parts and carbon fiber plates.
The Hong Kong lab doesn't get a mention in Bera's post, even though SUPER's code page asks anyone who builds on it to cite the team's papers. There's no paper covering the forest demo on the IDEAS Lab's publications page yet, either.
For now, anyone who wants to try building a similar drone can grab HKU's SUPER code as a free download. The lab's hardware kit lists every part needed, too, from the Livox Mid-360 LiDAR on top to the Intel NUC mini PC that runs the software.

articles.title: Amazon confirma “crediário” no Brasil; pagamento chega a 12 parcelas • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Amazon confirma “crediário” no Brasil; pagamento chega a 12 parcelas
Nova modalidade oferecida pelo e-commerce pode ser acessada pelo aplicativo. Usuários podem ativar diretamente no aplicativo.
A Amazon confirmou ao Tecnoblog que começou a oferecer um novo parcelamento sem cartão diretamente no aplicativo. O e-commerce se junta a concorrentes como Mercado Livre e Shopee, que já liberam uma espécie de “crediário” para realização de compras. A modalidade está em fase de implementação e pode não aparecer para todos os consumidores.
O Amazon Crédito é apresentado diretamente no site e app da Amazon. Apenas titulares podem solicitá-lo e a operação passa por análise de crédito. A documentação da Amazon indica a cobrança de taxas e de juros, mas os detalhes só são apresentados diretamente ao cliente final.
No fim das contas, trata-se de um empréstimo. Um exemplo fornecido pela Amazon cita o crédito de R$ 100 em 5 meses, com parcelas de R$ 27,74, totalizando R$ 138,70 com os juros. O Custo Efetivo Total (CET) fica em 12% ao mês. A Amazon nos explicou que a modalidade chegará em etapas, e recomendou que os interessados chequem periodicamente se a opção está disponível.
O Amazon Crédito é uma alternativa às compras no cartão de crédito. A ideia é aumentar o leque de opções para adquirir produtos, a exemplo do que já acontece em apps concorrentes. A Shopee, por exemplo, tem o SParcelado.
A ativação do Amazon Crédito pode ser feita da seguinte maneira:
O limite de crédito e a quantidade de parcelas mudam de acordo com o cliente. Nem todos terão direito às 12 vezes num primeiro momento. Isso pode mudar conforme o uso e o pagamento em dia.
O Tecnoblog apurou que o Amazon Crédito não é operado pela Amazon. Na realidade, o consumidor assina o compromisso financeiro com a Celcoin Sociedade de Crédito Direto, que está inscrita sob o CNPJ 48.632.754/0001-90. Esta instituição financeira tem autorização do Banco Central.
Há alguns requisitos básicos para os titulares que desejarem o Amazon Crédito. Segundo a empresa, é necessário ter idade entre 21 e 75 anos, renda mensal de pelo menos R$ 1.500 e documentação válida, assim como endereço no Brasil. Todos os clientes com conta ativa na Amazon podem pedir o Amazon Crédito. Além do cadastro, é necessário passar por uma análise de crédito antes de começar a usar.
Depois de aprovado, o “crediário” é exibido na Amazon. Não é possível utilizá-lo para empréstimos ou compras em outros sites, por exemplo. Uma vez ativo, basta selecionar a modalidade nas opções de pagamento.
