articles.title: TLS Flaws Found in GoAhead Web Server Used in Hundreds of Millions of Devices
articles.text:
Cybersecurity firm FoxIO has disclosed three vulnerabilities in GoAhead’s handling of TLS. They could keep revoked client certificates working, let eavesdroppers decrypt some traffic, or help attackers get around a cap on certificate chain length.
GoAhead, a lightweight web server made by EmbedThis, runs the management interfaces of networking equipment, printers and industrial systems. According to FoxIO, it is present on hundreds of millions of devices across the IoT, OT, firewall and military sectors.
FoxIO’s Sébastien Féry, who documented the flaws this week, said each one affects only a subset of deployments. Which GoAhead devices are at risk depends on the TLS library the manufacturer built into the firmware and how it configured certificate checks.
The critical flaw, CVE-2026-115881 (CVSS score of 9.1), impacts GoAhead 3.4.5 through 6.1.0 when built with OpenSSL or a compatible library and configured for mutual TLS (mTLS) with a certificate revocation list (CRL). The server reads the list but never tells OpenSSL to consult it.
On these builds, a certificate an administrator has revoked, such as one tied to a stolen or compromised device, is still accepted, even with issuer verification switched on. Nothing at startup warns that revocation checks are inactive.
The eavesdropping risk comes from the second bug (CVSS score of 5.9, no CVE), found in GoAhead 4.0.2 through 6.1.0 builds that use Mbed TLS. A coding error weakens the encryption of some TLS 1.2 connections enough that recorded sessions can be decrypted offline, but only if the client accepts the flawed parameters.
The chain-length bypass, CVE-2026-115884 (CVSS score of 7.4), affects GoAhead up to version 6.1.0 built with LibreSSL 3.2.x or 3.3.2 through 3.3.6. It only works against servers that require client certificates but accept them from any issuer, so the length cap is the only safeguard attackers get past.
“None of these defects prevents the affected handshake from completing,” Féry wrote.
GoAhead 6.1.1, released on Aug 2, resolves the OpenSSL and Mbed TLS issues, and advisories for all three flaws were published on Oct 12. Mbed TLS builds can also be protected by turning off finite-field DHE cipher suites or moving to the OpenSSL backend.
For the LibreSSL issue, FoxIO recommends enabling issuer verification with a trusted CA bundle, or switching to OpenSSL or LibreSSL 4.x.
The firm has also released proof-of-concept code and fingerprints that defenders can use to spot internet-facing GoAhead servers and determine which TLS library they rely on.
In a post on X, FoxIO founder and CTO John Althouse named Palo Alto Networks, Comcast, D-Link, HP, Canon, Honeywell, GE, Oracle, Siemens, Rockwell, Digi, Lockheed Martin and Boeing among the companies whose devices rely on GoAhead. FoxIO has not specified whether any of their products use a vulnerable configuration.
Althouse cautioned that the availability of an upstream fix “doesn’t mean there’s a patch available for the devices yet — that’s up to the manufacturer.”

articles.title: Inference cloud startup General Compute reels in $100M, despite broader AI funding fears - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Inference cloud startup General Compute reels in $100M, despite broader AI funding fears
Neoclouds are supposed to be under pressure, with the likes of Gartner Inc. and Elon Musk both predicting a bloodbath in the nascent cloud infrastructure segment in the not-too-distant future, but apparently nobody told General Compute Inc.
The cloud infrastructure startup said today it has just raised $100 million in a Series A round of funding led by Blackbird and Abstract Ventures, with participation from Fuse Venture Partners, Village Global and other investors, bringing its post-money valuation to $800 million.
The round may have raised some eyebrows because General Compute’s rivals in the neocloud industry are enduring a challenging time at the moment. That’s best illustrated by the biggest neocloud of all, CoreWeave Inc., whose stock recently fell to a 12-month low amid incessant talk that investors are getting weary of funding what seems like an endless, multibillion-dollar artificial intelligence infrastructure buildout.
Musk echoed those fears last weekend when he posted on X that his space rocket-come-AI company Space Exploration Technologies Corp. had managed to secure $40 billion in new debt. However, he warned that he was only able to get the money because his company has alternative revenue streams. “200+ neoclouds are going to see guppy-level death and consolidation,” Musk said. “Some will make it through, but not many.”
Musk’s comments came a couple of weeks after the respected analyst firm Gartner Inc. said that up to 80% of all neoclouds could disappear by the end of the decade. Some smaller neoclouds are already feeling the pressure. Earlier this month, Microsoft Corp. cancelled a multibillion-dollar deal with a startup called Nscale Global Holdings Ltd., in a move that now calls into question that company’s plans for an initial public offering.
Despite all of the negative headlines, General Compute co-founder and Chief Executive Finn Puklowski told TechCrunch in an interview that he’s not worried about what anyone else is doing. He said Musk’s comments are likely an effort to drive down the prices of the graphics processing units he wants to buy, saying that fears of a chip industry collapse are “massively overstated,” based on the demand his company is seeing.
General Compute also has a different business model than most neoclouds. Rather than focusing on general-purpose GPUs, it specifically only buys inference chips from other chipmakers such as Cerebras Systems Inc, SambaNova Systems Inc. and Positron AI Inc.
Its customers never have to manage the hardware either. They simply set up a workload and hit the start button, and General Compute routes it to the most suitable chip. Customers can choose between dedicated bare metal servers or a guaranteed tokens-per-second service level agreement.
Moreover, General Compute isn’t interested in building data centers of its own, Puklowski said. Instead, it rents space in facilities that belong to other companies, which care of all of the networking, power delivery, cooling and maintenance work.
The startup also has money to play with. In addition to today’s funding round, it secured $400 million in debt financing in July, and most of that has not yet been spent.
Puklowski said the company has been running some workloads for customers, but its first large-scale chip deployments won’t go live until the first quarter of next year. It has more than 75 megawatts of capacity planned for next year, and has already struck one large deal that will bring in over $100 million in annual recurring revenue.
Blackbird’s James Palmer said silicon is no longer the major bottleneck in the AI industry. Rather, what companies need is power. “Both power and silicon supply chains are slow to scale,” he added. “Finding creative ways through those constraints will decide who wins. Finn and his team are the ultimate coalition builders, and they think in decades, not days.”
The startup has also been praised by the three chipmakers that supply it with inference chips. “It understands that inference performance depends on how the full system is deployed and operated,” said Cerebras Chief Technology Officer Sean Lie. “We value their approach and commitment to fast execution at scale.”

articles.title: "My grandfather fell and remained on the floor for an entire day" - Magic Vision raises €600k for monitoring tech | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Magic Vision, an Italian DeepTech startup developing AI and computer vision technologies to monitor and support older people and vulnerable individuals, has closed a €600k funding round.
Investors include SixS, the Italian company behind Gecos, a management software platform for the nonprofit sector, alongside a group of Italian business angels with expertise in law, compliance and business development.
“Population ageing is putting pressure on care systems, which must meet growing needs with increasingly limited resources and staff. Technology can make a practical contribution by enabling continuous monitoring and timely intervention when needed,” says Lorenzo Mauri, co-founder and CEO of Magic Vision.
Magic Vision’s funding comes alongside several European investments in technology-enabled care during 2026.
Germany’s Patronus raised €11 million for its elderly emergency-response technology, while Spain’s Tucuvi secured €17 million for AI-powered nursing follow-up and Portugal’s Hope Care closed a €6 million round for remote patient monitoring.
Together with Magic Vision, these account for approximately €34.6 million in funding. In Italy, Rome-based VoiceMed reported reaching €1 million in cumulative funding for its device-free respiratory monitoring technology.
“Wearable devices, emergency buttons and other available systems had significant limitations. We therefore decided to use our expertise in artificial intelligence to develop technology capable of recognising risks without requiring a person to wear a device or call for help,” adds Federico Lanzani, co-founder and CTO of Magic Vision.
Magic Vision is an Italian startup founded in 2023 by six co-founders with expertise in AI and computer vision. Based in Meda, in the province of Monza and Brianza, it develops Silver Eye, an environmental monitoring system for older people and vulnerable individuals, designed to support their independence and assist families and care professionals.
Silver Eye uses proprietary AI and computer vision algorithms to analyse people’s activity and rest patterns , identify behavioural anomalies and detect critical events such as falls. Operating through environmental sensors without wearable devices, the system enable individual behavioural monitoring even in dynamic, shared settings, including senior living facilities, cohousing and private homes.
The technology is designed to protect privacy: data is processed locally using edge AI, without storing or transmitting images. Rather than functioning as a video surveillance system, it analyses the information needed to identify potential risks, alerting caregivers only when necessary.
The aim is to support prevention and help older people maintain their independence, providing technology for care models ranging from shared housing and home care to traditional residential and nursing care facilities.
During its growth journey, the startup has benefited from incubation at PoliHub and support from ComoNExT’s NExT Accelerator and Paradigma Exponential Hub , which helped connect the founders with investors. It has also received a €30k award from the Milan Monza Brianza Lodi Chamber of Commerce through the Switch2Product programme.
The funding has enabled Magic Vision to complete development and bring Silver Eye to market.
Already deployed in pilot and commercial projects with Italian care providers, Silver Eye has more than 200 sensors installed, with a target of monitoring over 100 people by the end of 2026.
“The idea for Silver Eye came from a personal experience: when my grandfather fell and remained on the floor for an entire day, I started looking for a solution that could prevent something similar from happening again,” says Federico.
The company is also preparing a €1.5 million funding round to accelerate commercial growth, build a network of partners and distributors across Italy, and begin its European expansion, with the aim of securing its first international customer within 24 months.

articles.title: Apple launches its new touchscreen MacBook Pro | TechCrunch
articles.text:
After years of resisting, Apple today launched a MacBook Pro with a touchscreen starting at $2,899. The release comes nearly 10 years after the company first tried integrating touchscreens on its laptops, with its Touch Bar on a MacBook Pro, which it later went on to remove.
The new MacBook Pro more fully embraces the touchscreen, offering a new PROLED XDR Display in both 14-inch and 16-inch screen sizes. The device is powered by M5 Pro and M5 Max chips as options to choose from, along with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 16TB of storage. The display has 2,000 nits peak HDR and SDR brightness and a 10,000,000:1 contrast ratio.
To make the new MacBook easy to use, Apple designed a hinge that stabilizes the screen when users touch it. This also helps to stabilize the camera when you are on a video call and trying to access content on the display.
In addition, the screen will include a Dynamic Island-style cutout instead of the notch that’s present on most of the current MacBooks. Plus, the new MacBook features a six-speaker array with a new woofer design for better sound.
The 14-inch Pro weighs 3.0 pounds (1.38 kg), and the 16-inch Pro weighs 4.0 pounds (1.82 kg) — lighter than its non-touch predecessors.
Both feature three Thunderbolt 5 ports, an HDMI port, an SDXC card slot, MagSafe, and a headphone jack. Users can hook up three external displays on the M5 Pro variant and up to four displays on the M5 Max variant.
The Touchscreen MacBook Pro 14-inch starts at $2,899, and the 16-inch version starts at $3,399.
Consumers can place a preorder for the new touchscreen MacBook Pro from October 30, and the device will be available starting November 6.
The new Touchscreen MacBook marks two marquee product launches for new CEO John Ternus, who also introduced the company’s first foldable, the iPhone Duo, in September. Various Apple executives, including Steve Jobs and Tim Cook, have scoffed at the idea of a touchscreen Mac in the past. Jobs famously called the idea “ergonomically terrible” at one point. However, rumors of the company working on such a variant started circulating nearly three years before today’s introduction.
The launch follows yesterday’s unveiling of a new standard MacBook Pro with the M6 chip in 14-inch size starting from $1,999.

articles.title: IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs — includes 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping
articles.text:
IT vendor lists massive $60 million AI supercomputer on eBay with 9,600 Nvidia A100 GPUs and 4,200 AMD EPYC CPUs, plus free shipping — 300 racks of decommissioned GPUs on offer
If you ever wanted to own your own supercomputer or data center while earning eBay cashback, Core 4 Solutions has the perfect opportunity. The company is selling a 300-rack AI supercomputer on eBay for $59.7 million, complete with $50 overnight shipping, or free shipping if you're willing to go with FedEx Ground. The cluster packs 9,600 Nvidia A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, enough to jump-start your own sovereign AI nation.
Nvidia and AMD have moved to newer architectures like Blackwell, Vera Rubin, and EPYC Turin. Nonetheless, A100 (codenamed Ampere) accelerators and EPYC Rome processors remain highly relevant for many computing tasks, including AI, machine learning, and scientific research. With the modern Blackwell and Vera Rubin racks from Nvidia, like the GB300 NVL72 and VR200 NVL72, costing up to $6.5 million and $7.8 million per unit, respectively, the A100 has turned into a legitimate budget alternative that can also circumvent the long waitlists and supply chain delays on Nvidia's newer AI hardware.
The cluster's sheer specifications are truly jaw-dropping. Each rack has four compute nodes and three management nodes. Each compute node has two AMD EPYC Rome 64-core processors, eight Nvidia A100 40GB SXM4 accelerators, and 1TB of DDR4-2933 memory. The management nodes are no less impressive. Each features two EPYC 64-core chips and 192GB of DDR4 memory.
When you sum it all up, the cluster comprises up to 9,600 A100 accelerators and 4,200 AMD EPYC Rome processors. With 64 Zen 2 execution cores per chip, the entire cluster boasts 268,800 cores. Memory capacity is equally impressive, with up to 1,401.6 TB or 1.4 petabytes for the entire cluster.
At first glance, $59.7 million sounds like a fortune, and it certainly is, but it seems like a reasonable valuation for the cluster. A rough estimate would be about $24 million for the A100S, $3 million for the EPYC Rome chips, and about $1.1 million for the DDR4 memory. That is about $28.1 million in crucial components, before factoring in other hardware like racks, cooling, power supplies, Nvidia Mellanox ConnectX-6 SmartNICs, etc.
Listing a 300-rack supercomputing cluster on eBay sounds absurd, but given today's AI-driven world, it is not as surprising as it may seem. After all, a broker once sold a 405-foot luxury Gigayacht for $168 million on eBay, so there is no reason why Core 4 Solutions cannot move a $59.7 million cluster. As AI farms and data centers expand, some enterprise clients out there will recognize the value and opportunity in the listing.
Shipping that many racks will be a logistics nightmare, and as funny as it sounds, Core 4 Solutions offers free local pickup or FedEx Ground delivery directly to your home. There is even an option to pay for a $25 two-day or $50 overnight delivery. Imagine FedEx casually dropping off 300 server racks at your front porch.

The cluster seems to have already drawn attention, with 11 people reportedly watching the eBay listing and one prospective buyer already letting it sit in their cart. I guess the real question is not whether it will sell, but whether the buyer will choose $50 overnight shipping.

articles.title: Buckle up for more body-swapping hijinks in Jumanji: Open World trailer
articles.text:
Let’s face it, the mid-December box office will be dominated by Avengers: Doomsday and Dune: Part Three, but for those seeking fun holiday family fare, Jumanji: Open World opens the very next week on Christmas Day. Sony Pictures just released a new trailer for director Jake Kasdan’s sequel to his 2019 hit, Jumanji: The Next Level, teasing the usual wacky hijinks with a twist that calls back to the original 1995 film.
As previously reported, Kasdan gave the franchise a welcome major overhaul with the release of 2017’s Jumanji: Welcome to the Jungle, updating the original board game into a vintage video game and giving us a hugely entertaining action-adventure. Welcome to the Jungle racked up over $960 million at the global box office and spawned the equally successful 2019 sequel Jumanji: The Next Level.
A third film was always in the cards: The Next Level featured a tantalizing mid-credits scene in which a heater repairman (Lamorne Morris) visits Spencer Gilpin’s (Alex Wolff’s) house, sees the broken video game console, and inadvertently triggers the game. The COVID-19 pandemic paused the third film’s development, but things picked up again in 2024, and here we are. Per the official synopsis:
This Christmas, Dwayne Johnson, Kevin Hart, Jack Black, and Karen Gillan are reunited in Jumanji: Open World, the hilarious final installment of the globally beloved action-adventure trilogy. Our heroes have escaped the perilous jungles of Jumanji before, but this time Jumanji breaks free of its console, unleashing its chaos into our world.
Star Dwayne Johnson—who plays in-game avatar Dr. Xander “Smolder” Bravestone—let slip in 2019 that The Next Level‘s in-game villain, Jurgen the Brutal (Rory McCann), was actually the avatar of another unknown real-world player.

articles.title: Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 feels like the future of Alexa, with a slimmer design and a smarter interface
articles.text:
Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 has a thinner design, a better screen, and a clever new way to organize Alexa conversations
It's pricey, though
- Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 starts at $499.99 and boasts a fresh design
- Alexa+ gets a redesigned interface with interactive Cards
- You can even get the 16-inch smart display with a NanoMatte finish
Amazon’s new Echo Show 16 looks like a big step forward for its smart displays. With a slimmer design, upgraded audio, and a redesigned Alexa+ interface, it feels like Amazon’s hardware and software are finally working in tandem.
It has a thinner, more modern look, almost mimicking that of an iMac, with a brighter, more vibrant display that can be treated with the special anti-glare NanoMatte coating. It also boasts a redesigned interface that feels tailor-made for the larger screen.
At $499.99 with a standard display and $569.99 with NanoMatte, the new Echo Show 16 is very much a premium smart display. It’s also only available in the United States for now and is up for preorder ahead of a mid-December launch. You can also save by preordering, with $100 off either finish.
Like the refreshed Echo Show 8 and Echo Show 11, this Echo Show 16 feels like Amazon’s device design team, led by Panos Panay, has hit its stride. I only spent a handful of minutes with it, but I can already see that the design and software are working in tandem, and this could be the template for future Echo Show smart displays.
Amazon has redesigned the entire build, including the internals, from the ground up, packing everything into an anodized aluminum frame that’s 40% slimmer than that of the Echo Show 15 or 21. The audio team has also built out eight custom micro-woofers on the sides and two tweeters for robust audio. In the demo space, it got pretty loud with no noticeable muddiness. It can also adjust playback in real time using the onboard microphones, sensors, and custom algorithms to ensure sound stays clear.
There are four microphones as well, so Alexa can clearly hear you when you make queries, but they also help if you’re on a video call, letting whoever you’re speaking to hear you without extra background noise. Two forward-facing microphones sit next to the wide-angle 13MP camera, and two are on the rear.
The 16-inch display is Full HD, and I’m especially loving the NanoMatte finish, particularly for a device that might be wall-mounted or used with the separately sold swivel stand. Either way, it could be exposed to varying degrees of natural sunlight, and glare can be an issue with smart displays.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
Of course, Alexa — specifically Alexa+ — is central to this, and the Show 16’s new Cards, which organize your conversations with the assistant, offer a new way to interact with and revisit those conversations. Panos described the interface as a combination of user interface and AI, and explained how the two work together.
When you open a Card from a previous Alexa conversation, you’re presented with the original prompt, condensed, alongside jumping-off points on the right and more detailed information next to it. You can easily tap on those suggestions or pull up the original conversation. Alexa's new conversation design is also reminiscent of how conversations are organized in the Siri app. The new look is also rolling out to the Alexa mobile app.
The whole interface feels a bit cleaner, and you can finally choose between different Screen Styles for the Echo Show 16. These include a Family Organizer for calendars and family plans, a Smart Home view for controlling connected devices — think the Echo Hub on steroids — and a Photos option that turns the display into a digital picture frame.
A more focused Echo Show
After spending a little time with the Echo Show 16, I came away most impressed by the cohesive feel of the hardware and software. The slimmer frame, more capable audio setup, NanoMatte display option, and redesigned Alexa+ experience all serve the same goal: making a large smart display more useful in the home.
The new Cards could be particularly interesting as Alexa+ becomes more capable, giving conversations a life beyond the moment you ask a question. And with Screen Styles that cater to different household needs, the Echo Show 16 feels less like a screen that simply sits on a counter or wall and more like a hub for organizing your home.
I’ll need to spend more time with it to see how well those features work in everyday use, but my first impression is that Amazon has made a more considered, cohesive smart display. If the new Alexa+ experience delivers on its promise, the Echo Show 16 could be one of the more compelling examples of where Amazon wants its smart home devices to go next.

articles.text:
Samsung ha lanzado un nuevo integrante de su familia de auriculares. El gigante surcoreano presentó los Galaxy Buds On, sus primeros auriculares con diseño abierto que buscan ofrecer una experiencia diferente a los tradicionales modelos intraaurales. Samsung ha puesto el foco en la comodidad y en la integración con funciones de inteligencia artificial.
Si no estás familiarizado con los auriculares de diseño abierto, estos dispositivos están pensados para escuchar el entorno mientras disfrutas del audio. A diferencia de los Galaxy Buds4 Pro, que priorizan el aislamiento y la cancelación de ruido, los Galaxy Buds On utilizan un formato de clip que se apoya en la oreja sin introducirse en el canal auditivo. Esto permitirá estar al pendiente de lo que ocurre a tu alrededor mientras escuchas música, atiendes una llamada o interactúas con el asistente de IA.
Según Samsung, el diseño de sus nuevos auriculares utilizó más de 119 millones de puntos de datos relacionados con la forma de las orejas. Con la ayuda de simulaciones físicas y optimización por IA, la compañía refinó la estructura del auricular y la banda de sujeción para conseguir un equilibrio entre comodidad y estabilidad. Los Galaxy Buds On pueden llevarse todo el día, ya que cada auricular pesa apenas 6,65 gramos.
38 horas de autonomía, Gemini Live y nuevas funciones de IA
En términos de funciones, los Galaxy Buds On ofrecen controles táctiles y pueden configurarse para ajustar el volumen automáticamente según el entorno. Los auriculares cuentan con tecnología de reducción de fugas de audio, que busca minimizar el sonido que escapa hacia el exterior. Esto es uno de los puntos débiles de los auriculares abiertos, por lo que Samsung usó ondas inversas para que nadie escuche tu música o conversaciones mientras te encuentras en un espacio público.
Las llamadas también reciben mejoras, gracias a tres micrófonos y una unidad de captura de voz que puede detectar vibraciones asociadas al habla. La compañía señala que estos componentes se combinan con algoritmos de aprendizaje automático, los cuales se entrenaron para filtrar ruidos de fondo. Si estás en medio del tráfico o pasas cerca de una obra en construcción, el sistema impedirá que estos sonidos se cuelen durante la conversación.
Por último, los Galaxy Buds On tienen compatibilidad con Gemini Live, a quien podremos invocar a través de comandos de voz. Entre sus funciones se encuentra la posibilidad de crear notas de voz rápidas y controlar ciertas acciones mediante movimientos de cabeza, como aceptar o rechazar interacciones. En cuanto a autonomía, Samsung ha prometido hasta 9,5 horas de reproducción continua y hasta 38 horas de uso total, eso sí, combinando los auriculares con el estuche de carga.
Los Galaxy Buds On estarán disponibles a partir de hoy a un precio de 229 dólares. Por el momento se desconoce el precio o disponibilidad en España y otros países de América Latina, aunque un reporte de SammyGuru menciona que varias tiendas europeas los venderán durante la primera mitad de diciembre.

articles.title: Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
articles.text:
The MPC Sample Key isn’t even formally announced yet, but Akai is already showing off what the modding community is cooking up through vibe coding. Akai has decided to embrace the explosion of hackers and custom firmware developers by giving them early access to the device, which will have open-source firmware.
Akai is embracing vibe-coded mods with an open-source MPC
The MPC Sample Key will be an open-source 37-key take on its budget-friendly MPC Sample.
It will likely run some version of the same software found on the MPC Sample, but with tweaks to accommodate the traditional keyboard, pitch, and mod wheels. Unlike the higher-end MPC Key 37, however, the Sample Key doesn’t have pads. Instead, you play back samples with the keys.
In the short Instagram Reels posted last night and today, Akai shows a number of vibe-coded mods that add synths, including Native Instruments Massive, to the device, as well as virtual analog and FM synths. One is even shown running a completely custom OS, with “several different synths in it.”
According to the clips, the same “community” features will come to the regular MPC Sample, which is also shown running a few vibe-coded synths built by Claude. That could mean Akai plans to open-source the entire MPC Sample platform.
CEO Jack O’Donnell told The Verge that inMusic brands, especially Akai, would be looking to embrace the modding community by seeding early devices to developers. These efforts will also include open-sourcing some software and providing an SDK.

articles.title: Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
articles.text:
In partnership withAVEVA
Pairing industrial AI autonomy and human control
Living digital twins are helping industrial plants run more like living systems, and setting the stage for industries that work in sync.
Most people associate industrial environments with cold steel and clockwork machinery. Functionally, though, a plant or factory is more like a living thing: It has a pulse, even a metabolism. It goes through wear and tear as it ages, and signs of deteriorating health often show up as barely perceptible irregularities.
Digital twin technology has long aimed to mirror that dynamism and model anomalies that may be symptomatic of larger problems. But earlier implementations were a few beats behind physical reality; they were incapable of real-time analysis and unable to proactively address any issues detected. They focused more on simulation, observation and what-if scenario planning, rather than closed-loop execution. Rather than serving as a digital mirror of reality that can spot anomalies or suggest optimizations, a living digital twin combines a dynamic, high-fidelity digital representation of complex operations with the capacity to intervene in the physical world through operations and control systems.
AI is at the center of this change. Rob McGreevy, chief product officer at AVEVA, likens newer, AI-infused digital twins to organisms that grow and evolve. These “living” versions are adaptive, evergreen models of a plant’s assets and processes. Because they keep pace with live conditions and connect systems that once ran in isolation, they provide a previously missing layer of visibility and orchestration that better reflects the organic rhythms of the facility itself.
Now, agentic AI is also enabling industrial systems to move beyond diagnostics or suggestions and act of their own accord. As the technology progresses toward greater autonomy, it’s starting to develop the reflexes for a kind of industrial homeostasis, in which small, constant adjustments keep a plant or factory healthy and humming.
All that said, human judgment and operator oversight still play an instrumental role by defining what healthy looks like to begin with—and flagging when AI systems are falling out of alignment. Living digital twins provide the means for human engineers to monitor what AI is doing and ensure execution is on track.
The technologies that keep digital twins in sync
Living digital twins link engineering and design information with real-time operational data through a digital thread, or a connected record of an asset that follows it through its lifecycle. A couple of notable technological shifts have helped string this thread together: Sensors (which have gotten more affordable in recent years) now stream telemetry from IoT devices and industrial control equipment, and software platforms bring that information into user-friendly interfaces. Predictive and physics-based models can also provide AI-enriched insights into how a machine or process might behave.
The lenses through which operators view digital twins have evolved in turn. “You can look at the digital twin through the lens of sustainability: What are my emissions?” says McGreevy. “Or, through the lens of maintenance: Is this asset performing in a healthy way? Or, through a performance metric: Is it producing the number of widgets I need?”
Setting boundaries for semi-autonomous systems
The next phase is letting AI act on select insights those lenses illuminate. For their part, manufacturers are eager for this chapter: In a 2026 Manufacturing Leadership Council survey of manufacturers (opens in new tab), 66% said they are using or plan to use agentic AI in their operations, and 40% expect some degree of factory autonomy by 2030. At the same time, they’re wary of the potential risks: In Deloitte’s 2025 smart manufacturing survey (opens in new tab), 65% of executives ranked operational risk, including the potential for business disruption, among their top concerns.
Manufacturers are accelerating toward agentic AI and greater factory autonomy
Source: MIT Technology Review Insights with data from Manufacturing Leadership Council (opens in new tab), 2026
“There is a lot more refinement to be done, a lot more proof points, testing, and validation needed,” McGreevy says about the ongoing process of making AI autonomous. In the near term, McGreevy expects agentic AI to follow the path seen in other industrial technologies like SCADA systems. “The ‘S’ in SCADA means supervisory, and supervisory means there’s a human in the middle,” he says. He sees AI working mostly in that advisory mode for the foreseeable future, with full autonomy limited to narrow, highly repetitive tasks.
As for the role human operators play, the day-to-day is evolving. Workers who once specialized in a single process line or maintenance task can now take on multiple disciplines. They can spend less time and effort approving routine actions one by one, and more on defining acceptable operating limits. Because AI can reinforce patterns in the data it receives, catching missteps early is a core part of the job. Human knowledge and experience in interpreting what AI is seeing and doing is instrumental.
Governance on a company- and industry-wide scale, too, needs to adapt to the times. Organizations must establish clear guardrails for which decisions AI can make on its own and how its actions are monitored and audited. Still, many have yet to set up comprehensive safeguards: In a recent study from AVEVA and IMD (opens in new tab), 43% of organizations said AI has changed decision-making and accountability across ecosystem partners only slightly or not at all, while just 23% reported a significant or fundamental change. (Only 27% reported sharing data substantially or extensively with partners.)
In the meantime, regulators are starting to define some of the rules. The EU AI Act classifies certain AI safety components used in critical infrastructure as high-risk and imposes requirements for human oversight. Companies are setting up their own structures as well; AVEVA, for one, has a responsible AI governance board and a published set of principles for how AI is developed and deployed.
Agentic AI and living digital twins: Real-world case studies
Inside the semi-autonomous systems already running, that oversight looks different from one deployment to another. In some cases, an operator approves every action; in others, AI acts on its own while people oversee and define the boundaries it can operate within. McGreevy cites several examples of what machine autonomy and human-plus-machine collaboration looks like among AVEVA customers:
- At Saudi Aramco’s Yanbu refinery, optimization algorithms adjust production in a closed loop, with operators overseeing as needed. At its Ras Tanura refinery, the algorithms recommend changes, and operators decide whether to implement them.
- Nestlé uses AI optimization at Nesquik plants to tune the industrial dryers used to produce powdered beverage ingredients. In a landmark test, this tuning reduced energy use by 16%, while improving quality and yield.
- At Thailand’s SCG Chemicals, an AI-supported digital twin spanning engineering, operations, and maintenance monitors asset health and flags potential failures. The company reports 99% plant reliability and a ninefold return on investment within six months.
- The National Laboratory of the Rockies in the U.S. has built a generative AI model for grid control rooms to provide oversight at scale. The model supports operators with renewable energy forecasting and estimates of grid conditions.
Looking to the future
The same synchronization that was once missing from individual plants’ technology systems has also been lacking on a larger scale. “Manufacturing and critical infrastructure have operated as siloed systems for the last 50 years,” says McGreevy. But certain emerging technologies, he suggests, are creating opportunities for more holistic coordination.
On an enterprise level, this might involve the integration of physical AI: systems that pair robotics and sensing technologies with AI-powered decision-making. Drones that fly over pipelines and power lines, for instance, can feed visual inspection data to algorithms that spot gas leaks and other hazards. Not only does this create a more accurate and interconnected flow of information, but it spares humans from needing to physically enter potentially dangerous environments. “The robotics-meets-software convergence will mean fewer incidents, fewer outages, and a more sustainable way of operating,” McGreevy predicts.
A bigger-picture version extends beyond any one plant or process to entire industrial networks, something McGreevy dubs the “integrated value chain.” “Living digital twins make digital manifestations of the entire value chain possible,” he says. “This allows companies to react quickly to supply chain changes, demand changes, tariffs, and material availability.”
Amid today’s realities of turbulent geopolitics and shifting regulatory demands, such resilience will be “an absolute necessity,” adds McGreevy. “Without it, it will be very hard to run an effective business.”

                        WHITEPAPERS
		
Make every layer of your hardware PDN-aware and reach your maximum compute density.
								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: Movellus
								
							
In an AI datacenter, 50 mV of voltage margin can be worth about 270 racks of compute per gigawatt of input electricity. To show how, this paper models two facilities that run the same Vera Rubin NVL72 racks at the same clock speeds, one at 0.80 V and one at 0.75 V. On published Vera Rubin power figures, the second draws about 8% less power per GPU and about 17 kW less per rack.
Margin is the supply voltage added above what the silicon needs to cover the worst-case voltage droop. Evolving AI workloads make that margin larger and harder to predict. As a result, platform and silicon teams often over-margin to compensate, costing them compute density and token throughput, while teams that margin too little see failures in the field.
Power delivery network (PDN) design in the age of AI takes a systematic approach to power management. This paper distills the foundation of that approach into four axioms, drawn from work with customers in AI and high-performance computing (HPC).
AXIOM 1: Test error must be minimized
AXIOM 2: Power envelopes must factor in both evolving workloads and PDN dynamics
AXIOM 3: AI systems require reactive or preemptive Ldi/dt (droop) mitigation
AXIOM 4: Co-architected control loops are a necessity for systems
Movellus addresses the four axioms in one stack through its Aeonic platform. The platform helps teams set the foundation of proper power architecture in the age of AI.

articles.title: El MacBook Pro estrena pantalla táctil y OLED: Apple rompe su gran tabú
articles.text:
Más de 16 años después del recordado discurso de Steve Jobs explicando por qué las pantallas táctiles en los ordenadores portátiles no funcionaban, Apple rompió su gran tabú. "Las superficies táctiles no quieren estar en vertical. [...] No funcionan, son terribles ergonómicamente", dijo el cofundador y exCEO de la compañía en octubre de 2010, y a partir de hoy sus sucesores lo van a poner a prueba con el nuevo MacBook Pro OLED con pantalla táctil.
Apple acaba de completar su semana de lanzamientos con el estreno del MacBook Pro de por primera vez con pantalla táctil como método de entrada. Este cambio llega de la mano de la adopción de paneles OLED, lo que garantiza negros más profundos y optimizaciones en materia de brillo, contraste y colores más vívidos.
Puede parecer que Apple ha dado el brazo a torcer con la inclusión de una pantalla táctil en los MacBook Pro OLED, tras años de negarse a hacerlo. Sin embargo, se ha dado el gusto de hacerlo a su manera. Es que, más allá de las posibilidades que desbloquea poder controlar el ordenador con los dedos, la realidad es que los de Cupertino mantienen el teclado y el ratón como los métodos de input principales. Los comandos táctiles para interactuar con macOS se presentan como un complemento y no como un reemplazo de los elementos ya convencionales.
Nuevo MacBook Pro OLED con pantalla táctil, disponible en 14 y 16 pulgadas
Con el nuevo MacBook Pro OLED, Apple no solo da el salto a una pantalla táctil, sino que traer un cambio muy esperado. La empresa finalmente se despide del notch e introduce la Isla Dinámica, que brinda un funcionamiento idéntico al que vemos en el iPhone.
El MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil incorpora un panel tándem OLED que Apple llama ProLED XDR. Este presume de un brillo pico de 2.000 nits (HDR), tasa de refresco de 120 Hz y una relación de contraste de 10.000.000:1. Al igual que con los modelos convencionales, los de Cupertino ofrecen su nuevo portátil en dos tamaños: 14 y 16 pulgadas. Vale mencionar que, en realidad, las pantallas miden 14,2 y 16,3 pulgadas, respectivamente.
Apple ha dotado a sus portátiles con un diseño renovado que les da bordes de pantalla más delgados y los hace más ligeros. El MacBook Pro táctil de 14 pulgadas pesa 1,38 kilos, mientras que la versión de 16'' queda en 1,84 kilos. Como comparación, los modelos con pantalla convencional pesan 1,6 y 2,1 kilos, respectivamente. El dato curioso de estos portátiles es que traen de regreso un ícono de los Mac de antaño: el logo de la cubierta que se ilumina.
Los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil son también un poco más delgados. Es por ello que los de Cupertino han implementado un nuevo sistema de refrigeración que ayuda alejar el aire caliente de la pantalla, sin necesidad de sacrificar rendimiento.
Chips M5 Pro y Max, y hasta 128 GB de memoria y 16 TB de almacenamiento
En su modo de hacer las cosas "a lo Apple", los de la manzana prometen desterrar uno de los problemas más complejos de los portátiles con pantalla táctil: los sacudones que da la pantalla al pulsarla. Es por ello que han diseñado una bisagra especialmente pensada para minimizar ese movimiento que puede resultar tan molesto. A esto se suma una estabilización avanzada de vídeo para evitar que la imagen se sacuda cuando se usa el input táctil en una vídeollamada.
El portátil llega impulsado por los chips M5 Pro y M5 Max ya disponibles en los modelos sin panel táctil, así que no hay sorpresas en tal sentido. En materia de RAM y almacenamiento, el MacBook Pro táctil de 14 pulgadas se inicia en 24 GB y 1 TB, mientras que el modelo de 16 pulgadas se puede configurar con hasta 128 GB de memoria unificada y 16 TB de espacio interno.
En materia de conectividad y puertos, el MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil soporta WiFi 7, Bluetooth 6 y Thread gracias al chip N1 de Apple. Llega con tres puertos Thunderbolt 5, HDMI, un lector de tarjetas SD, conector de 3,5 milímetros para auriculares y MagSafe 3. En materia de autonomía, promete hasta 24 horas de uso y soporta carga rápida, pudiendo recuperar el 50 % de la batería en 30 minutos.
Disponibilidad y precio de los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil
Apple ha abierto las reservas de los MacBook Pro con pantalla táctil, que comenzarán a llegar a los compradores el 6 de noviembre. Los portátiles estarán disponibles en los dos colores tradicionales: negro espacial y plata.
Como puedes imaginar, los MacBook Pro ProLED XDR no serán nada baratos. articles.title: Applications open for Cape Venture Bridge programme for Western Cape startups - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Western Cape tech startups are invited to apply for the first cohort of the Cape Venture Bridge, a new programme run by AfricArise that aims to prepare them for international VC and market expansion.
AfricArise, part of the AfricArena network, is delivering the six-month programme with support from the Western Cape Government’s Department of Economic Development and Tourism (DEDAT).
Twenty startups will be selected for cohort one, to receive training on market entry beyond South Africa, cross-border finance and regulation; and investor pitching, as well as at least 12 hours of one-on-one mentorship and ZAR125,000 (US$7,500) in tech credits through programme partners. All participants will also take part in a public pitch event in Cape Town.
The top five startups will join a fully funded delegation to GITEX Africa in Morocco, which takes place in April next year, with investor and partner meetings arranged ahead of their arrival.
“Cape Town founders are building companies ready to compete well beyond our borders. The Cape Venture Bridge gives them the investment readiness, the mentorship, and for the top five, a seat at GITEX Africa in Morocco, where investors and partners are looking for exactly what the Western Cape has to offer,” said Dan Mabbyalas, director of programmes at AfricArise.
He said the programme was particularly keen to receive applications from women and young founders across the province.
Tim Parle, chief director for the digital economy at DEDAT, said the Western Cape was home to some of the continent’s most innovative technology businesses.
“DEDAT welcomes initiatives of this nature that contribute to entrepreneurship, economic growth and job creation in the province. We are particularly encouraged by efforts to broaden participation by women-owned and youth-owned businesses, as well as entrepreneurs from across the Western Cape,” he said.
The programme is open to technology or innovation-driven startups registered and operating in the Western Cape, across sectors including SaaS, climate-tech, agritech, fintech, e-commerce and e-health. Applicants must be planning to enter international markets within the next 12 months, and must be led by at least two co-founders or full-time team members able to attend programme activities.
Over its first 12 months, the Cape Venture Bridge aims to support 40 startups across two cohorts, deliver more than 80 pre-arranged investor meetings and 50 business-to-business introductions, and help facilitate over ZAR3 million (US$180,000) in capital.
Applications are here until November 15.

articles.title: GTA 6 pèse 210 Go sur PS5, mais vous allez pouvoir le précharger à partir de cette date
articles.text:
Attendu le 19 novembre au prix de 79,99 euros pour l’édition standard, GTA 6 fait parler de lui via le compte PlayStation Game Size, qui a déniché l’information du poids du jeu directement sur le PlayStation Store. Ce sera donc 210 Go, avec une ouverture des serveurs à minuit. Les joueurs impatients pourront lancer le téléchargement en avance dès le 12 novembre grâce au système de préchargement, une option qui n’est pas du luxe compte tenu de la taille du jeu.
Faites de la place sur le SSD de votre PlayStation 5
Le téléchargement de 210 Go représente une part importante de l’espace disponible sur une PS5 Slim dont le SSD de 825 Go ne laisse que 667 Go réellement exploitables. Vous allez donc peut-être devoir anticiper l’installation en faisant de la place dans vos jeux pour vous éviter d’avoir une mauvaise surprise le jour J ou de devoir désinstaller un jeu que vous n’avez pas encore terminé.
 🚨 Grand Theft Auto VI
– 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB
– 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99)
Pre-Load : November 12
Release : November 19
𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight https://t.co/5vXkgnqfC7
— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) October 27, 2026
Depuis le premier aperçu de GTA 6, on pouvait se douter que le jeu ne serait pas léger. La promesse d’un monde ouvert extrêmement dense, bardé de lieux à explorer et d’activités annexes, demande de charger beaucoup d’éléments. La taille exacte de Grand Theft Auto VI sur Xbox Series X et S reste encore à officialiser. Pour cette dernière, qui a un disque dur plus petit que celui des autres consoles, il faudra probablement compter chaque gigaoctet pour ne pas avoir de mauvaises surprises.
Des jeux toujours plus lourds
GTA 6 bat largement les précédents jeux de Rockstar. À titre de comparaison, GTA 5 pesait environ 100 Go sur PS5, Red Dead Redemption 2 pesait de son côté autour de 120 Go pour sa version numérique, et le vénérable GTA 4 n’occupait quant à lui à peine 20 Go.
Notez que le poids de 210 Go n’est probablement pas définitif, la taille du jeu reste susceptible d’évoluer d’ici au lancement. On pense évidemment à un « patch day one » pour peaufiner l’expérience de jeu. Enfin, la vitesse de téléchargement dépendra directement de votre connexion à internet. Pour ceux qui n’ont pas un énorme débit descendant, le préchargement à partir du 12 novembre reste votre meilleur allié, en attendant la sortie officielle le 19 novembre à minuit.

articles.title: GitHub saw 7.4B commits in September, adding 4M CPU cores and 160 PB of storage to keep up
articles.text:
GitHub saw 7.4B commits in September, adding 4M CPU cores and 160 PB of storage to keep up
GitHub is seeing unprecedented demand and is updating its core infrastructure to keep pace.
In August, GitHub said it was seeing 2.9 billion commits per month, up from 1.4 billion in April. At its GitHub Universe conference on Wednesday, the company announced that it is now seeing 7.4 billion commits per month. To put that into perspective, developers pushed 65 million monthly commits to the platform in 2024.
That kind of growth is a great problem to have, but the company’s outages have become something of a recurring theme. The reason is rapid usage growth, driven mostly by “agentic demand,” as the company puts it.
4 million more CPU cores
In August, GitHub CTO Vlad Fedorov announced that the platform had added 3 million CPU cores — mostly on Azure — to support this growth. Now, GitHub says it has added 4 million CPU cores, plus 160 petabytes of high-speed storage and more compute power for GitHub Actions so far this year
The company also added 50 Tb/s of network capacity to keep all of this data flowing.
A new GitHub architecture is coming
GitHub also used this announcement to reiterate its commitment to rearchitecting its platform to separate compute and storage. It first talked about this earlier this month. At that time, the company noted that its internal benchmarks show that this new architecture can deliver up to 35x higher write throughput, for example.
“Agents are changing the volume and shape of software development. Adding capacity matters, but capacity alone won’t get us there. We’ve also had to change the architecture,” Jay Parikh, the EVP for Core AI at Microsoft, writes in the announcement.
Separating compute and storage isn’t exactly radical in 2026, but it shows GitHub was trying to scale on a legacy foundation. Moving to Azure and its services was essentially the only option, especially as the company’s own data center was out of capacity.

articles.title: Exclusive: Prophecy launches DataGPT to run data workflows inside ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot - SiliconANGLE
articles.text:
Exclusive: Prophecy launches DataGPT to run data workflows inside ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot
Data preparation startup Prophecy Inc. today launched DataGPT, a new service that allows business analysts to run complete data workflows from inside OpenAI Group PBC’s ChatGPT, Anthropic PBC’s Claude and Microsoft Corp.’s Copilot.
Each answer arrives with a visual map of the steps that produced it. The service goes after a workaround that has become common in finance and operations teams: An analyst uploads a spreadsheet to a chatbot, often without sign-off from the information technology department, and asks it to reconcile a quarter of transactions. The chatbot answers by writing a script of its own.
Most people in those jobs cannot read code, according to Prophecy, so they end up taking the numbers on trust. Closing the chat wipes the logic, along with whatever revenue definitions or approved exceptions the user explained during the session. Prophecy cites a January forecast from Gartner Inc. that half of all organizations will adopt a zero-trust posture for data governance by 2028 as unverified data generated by artificial intelligence spreads.
Raj Bains, Prophecy’s founder and chief executive, said software developers already have AI that helps them write code and take it all the way to production. “Business data users got question answering, and nothing changed,” he said. DataGPT is meant to put those users on the same footing, with the workflow behind every result in a form they can verify and change.
In a single DataGPT conversation, an analyst can load a messy Excel file and cross-check it with an audit list and records held in SharePoint or Snowflake Inc.’s data cloud. A pricing rule for discounted product bundles might come next. Prophecy’s own walkthrough ends with that workflow set to run again every month without anyone rebuilding it.
No workflow goes on a schedule until a person has looked it over. DataGPT lays out each stage on screen beside its results, and an analyst who spots a problem can fix that stage before approving the whole thing.
Every workflow is backed by open code in Git. Because reruns follow that code exactly and never go back to the AI model, they carry no added AI cost. Signed-off workflows also feed a knowledge graph Prophecy builds for each customer from its own business rules and data catalogs.
Prophecy is also pitching DataGPT as a way to bring shadow AI under IT’s control. Uploaded files never sit inside the chat. They go through Prophecy to the organization’s own data platform, where IT staff and the people who run that platform can see every workflow and govern it like anything else they manage. Scheduled runs happen on Snowflake, Databricks Inc.’s data platform or Google LLC’s BigQuery, whichever the customer already owns.
DataGPT is available today through the connector marketplaces in ChatGPT, Claude and Copilot. Companies that have not yet approved those AI tools can run it in Prophecy’s own app. Individuals can start with a free account, and the product can also be rolled out centrally by an administrator.
Prophecy has raised more than $100 million since its founding in 2017, most recently a $47 million Series B extension led by Smith Point Capital in January 2025. SAP SE, HSBC Holdings plc and Pfizer Inc. are among the customers it names.

articles.title: C'est le moment d'acheter un aspirateur robot puisque ce Roborock est bradé par Amazon
articles.text:
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est un aspirateur robot laveur qui aspire les poussières et nettoie vos sols sans que vous n’ayez à intervenir tandis que la station de lavage se charge de l’entretien. En ce moment, le produit de Roborock est disponible pour 330 euros de moins sur Amazon.
Avec des températures qui se rafraîchissent de plus en plus, on a de moins en moins envie de nettoyer nos sols de fond en comble. La solution est donc d’investir dans un aspirateur robot. Justement, Amazon brade le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 avec une réduction de 38 %. Malgré cette remise, il faudra dépenser plus de 500 euros pour s'offrir les services de cet engin.
Sur Amazon, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 passe de 889,99 euros à 549,99 euros
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 ?
- Une cartographie précise : Grâce à l’intelligence artificielle, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 offre une navigation précise et il pourra éviter la plupart des obstacles. L’engin peut également franchir des seuils pour pouvoir passer d’une pièce à l'autre.
- Un nettoyage intelligent : Sur l’application, il est possible de définir les horaires de passage et les zones où le robot doit passer. En action, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 peut lever ses brosses lorsqu'il arrive à proximité d’un tapis afin de ne pas l'humidifier.
- Une station qui se charge de l’entretien : Pour limiter les interventions humaines, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 s’entretient tout seul. La station d'entretien vide le bac à poussière. Elle nettoie les serpillières à l'eau chaude et les sèche à l'air chaud.
Un aspirateur robot qui n’oublie aucune zone
Roborock a apporté un soin tout particulier au design de son Qrevo Edge 2. D’abord, cet aspirateur robot n'est pas très haut avec seulement 7,98 cm de hauteur. Un détail qui n'est pas anodin puisqu’il permet à l’engin de passer sous la plupart des meubles.
Autre point fort, sa technologie FlexiArm. Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 dispose d’un petit bras extensible pour atteindre les coins ou passer le long des plinthes. Un double système anti-emmêlement est présent pour aspirer les poils et les longs cheveux sans qu’ils ne s’emmêlent autour de la brosse. Côté aspiration, il faut compter une puissance maximale de 25 000 Pa. C’est suffisant pour aspirer tous les éléments qui traînent au sol.
L'aspirateur robot emporte aussi des brosses pour le lavage des sols. Le résultat sera convaincant dans la plupart des situations, même si un second passage sera nécessaire pour les taches les plus tenaces. À noter que ces serpillières peuvent se lever pour ne pas humidifier les tapis.
Une navigation (presque) parfaite
Avant de pouvoir profiter de toutes les qualités de ce Roborock Qrevo Edge 2, il faut qu’il effectue un premier passage afin de cartographier votre intérieur. Une fois cette première étape effectuée, vous pourrez personnaliser le nettoyage. Par exemple, il sera possible de créer des zones interdites ou de définir des heures de passage.
Cet aspirateur robot possède un système de détection des obstacles qui s’appuie sur l’intelligence artificielle. Roborock affirme que son engin peut reconnaître plus de 280 obstacles. Cependant, pour les objets les plus fins comme les câbles, le robot peut présenter quelques difficultés.
Au terme de ses opérations de nettoyage, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 rejoint sa station d’entretien. Elle se charge de vider le bac à poussière et de laver les serpillères à l’eau chaude. Pour éviter les mauvaises odeurs, la station sèche les serpillères à l’air chaud.
✅ Les points forts
- Un robot pas très épais pour passer sous les meubles
- Un bras extensible pour atteindre les zones les plus difficiles d'accès
- Un double système anti-emmêlement contre les cheveux longs et les poils
❌ Les limites
- Une détection par IA qui peut montrer des limites face à des objets fins comme des câbles
- Plusieurs passages peuvent être nécessaires pour éliminer les taches les plus tenaces
Le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est actuellement disponible pour 549,99 euros au lieu de 889,99 euros
Le prix élevé de ce Roborock Qrevo Edge 2, même après la réduction d’Amazon, se justifie par toutes les qualités offertes par ce robot. Il se charge de nettoyer vos sols et s’entretient seul pour limiter les interventions humaines. Pour trouver des défauts, il faut les chercher et le seul qui peut être dérangeant concerne les faiblesses de l’IA pour détecter des câbles. Hormis sur ce point, le robot nettoiera votre intérieur de fond en comble grâce à son petit format qui lui permet de passer sous les meubles.

articles.title: Wegen KI: Proton-Mitarbeiter müssen erneut zum Bewerbungsgespräch
articles.text:
Mitarbeiter:innen des bekannten Schweizer IT-Unternehmens Proton, das auf Sicherheitssoftware spezialisiert ist, sollen in einem neuen Bewerbungsgespräch erklären, wie sie KI-Technik einsetzen. Das berichtet das investigative IT-Magazin 404 Media unter Berufung auf ein internes Rundschreiben. Darin heißt es, das Interview könne „zu Änderungen hinsichtlich der Aufgaben, Zuständigkeiten und der weiteren Beschäftigung“ führen.
Das Unternehmen benötige Menschen, die KI-Fähigkeiten in bessere Produkte und neue Arbeitsweisen „übersetzen können“, zitiert 404 Media aus dem Schreiben. Die Gespräche führen demnach nicht die direkten Vorgesetzten der Betroffenen. Zuständig sei stattdessen eine Gruppe „hochrangiger Beschäftigter“, die „starke KI-Fähigkeiten“ bereits unter Beweis gestellt haben soll.
Nicht alle bei Proton sind betroffen
Laut 404 Media treibt Proton-Chef Andy Yen den KI-Einsatz im Unternehmen schon länger voran. Dem Rundschreiben zufolge befragte er zuletzt mehr als 40 Führungskräfte, um die KI-Interviews vorzubereiten. Proton steht hinter Online-Diensten wie Proton Mail, Proton VPN und dem Passwortmanager Proton Pass. Nach den jüngsten verfügbaren Zahlen aus dem Jahr 2024 beschäftigt die Firma rund 500 Menschen.
Allerdings: Nicht alle müssen erneut zum Rapport. Wie genau sich dies zusammensetzt, blieb zunächst unklar. Wo es zu den KI-Interviews kommt, seien die Gespräche „von großer Bedeutung“, heißt es in dem Schreiben. Das Unternehmen räumt demnach ein, dass die Ankündigung Unsicherheit auslösen könnte, und will die „Ergebnisse“ der Gespräche so schnell wie möglich individuell mitteilen. Die KI-Interviews sollen zwischen dem 4. und 11. November stattfinden.
Proton widerspricht – ein bisschen
Zu dem Rundschreiben und den Bewerbungsgesprächen selbst wollte sich Proton gegenüber 404 Media nicht äußern. Später erklärte das Unternehmen, es baue keine Stellen ab und nutze KI auch „nicht als Vorwand“ dafür. Im internen Schreiben klingt das aber nicht unbedingt so.
Allerdings geht es bei Proton offenbar nicht um die seit Monaten diskutierte Sorge, KI könne Arbeitsplätze ersetzen. Stattdessen sollen Mitarbeitende offenbar dazu gedrängt werden, die Technik stärker zu nutzen. Proton-Boss Yen wünscht sich dem Schreiben zufolge Beschäftigte, die die Veränderungen durch KI „mit Neugier, Urteilsfähigkeit und Dringlichkeit“ angehen.

articles.title: OPINION: Scaling is the real test of Europe’s AI boom | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Europe’s AI funding boom is not benefiting every part of the market equally. Recorded Series A–C investment rose by approximately 66% in the first nine months of 2026, yet funding in rounds worth €22.2 million to less than €88.9 million declined by around 8%.
This middle segment is particularly important for AI startups moving beyond their first customers. Expanding internationally, hiring teams and securing larger enterprise contracts can require substantial capital, even for companies operating on a much smaller scale than Europe’s leading AI developers.
The contrasting funding trends raise questions about how Europe’s next generation of AI companies will finance their expansion. While overall investment continues to grow, the more important test may be whether startups can progress from early funding rounds to sustainable businesses without becoming overly dependent on their next investment.
The findings are based on an analysis of Crunchbase funding-round data for the first nine months of 2025 and 2026, using consistent dates and funding stages and correcting identified data issues. The original dollar-based categories were retained, with euro thresholds rounded for readability. Figures follow Crunchbase’s classifications and currency conversions and may differ from public announcements.
How Europe’s AI funding splits across the market
The adjusted Crunchbase sample recorded approximately €15.04 billion in announced Series A–C funding in the first nine months of 2026, up from €9.06 billion a year earlier. The number of recorded funding events increased from 203 to 232. Of these, 196 events in 2025 and 218 in 2026 were included in the round-size breakdown. These figures cover companies tagged as Artificial Intelligence by Crunchbase and do not represent all European AI funding stages.
The growth was concentrated in larger transactions. Rounds worth €88.9 million or more increased from 18 to 33, accounting for approximately 74% of disclosed funding in 2026, up from 59% the previous year. Although the ten biggest investments represented about half of the total, funding outside these transactions also grew.
Smaller rounds became more frequent, increasing from 108 to 124 for investments below €22.2 million. The middle of the market, however, moved in the opposite direction. The €22.2–88.9 million segment saw its share of disclosed funding fall from approximately 29% to 16%. Across all rounds below €88.9 million, recorded funding barely increased, growing by just 2.7% to €3.86 billion.
This uneven growth suggests that Europe’s AI investment boom has not been felt equally across different funding sizes. While more smaller rounds were recorded and large investments attracted substantial capital, the segment between them contracted.
Some of the largest announcements also require caution. NEURA Robotics announced a Series C of up to €1.24 billion, while Multiverse Computing described a round targeting up to €500 million. Excluding both amounts reduced the sample’s overall funding growth from approximately 66% to 47%.
The increase therefore remained substantial even without these transactions, but the headline amounts should not be interpreted as confirmation that all the funding had already been received.
From €98 million to €3 billion: The different costs of scaling AI
Taktile, a Berlin-founded company developing decision technology for financial institutions, raised approximately €51 million in a Series B in February 2025. By June 2026, it had secured another approximately €98 million in Series C funding. The company operates in enterprise software, where expansion means winning more customers and making its technology work inside complex banking systems.
Mistral raised €3 billion in a Series D in September 2026. Developing frontier AI models requires enormous computing resources and research investment. The financing needs of these two companies differ considerably, yet their announcements contribute to the broader picture of an AI funding boom. These examples provide context separately from the statistical sample: Taktile is absent from the European-headquartered export, and Mistral’s Series D falls outside the stages analysed.
Funding activity also increased across all three stages. Series A events rose from 133 to 148, Series B from 51 to 58, and Series C from 19 to 26. Median round sizes grew at every stage, with the most pronounced increase at Series C, where the median rose from €49.3 million to €93.3 million.
These figures do not indicate a broad decline in Series B or C activity. However, they cannot show how easily individual companies secured funding or what conditions investors attached to their investments.
Taktile shows that companies can successfully move through successive funding stages. For other founders, planning that transition means making expensive decisions before they know when the next round will arrive or what terms investors will offer.
The cost of depending on your next funding round
A company may raise capital to enter new markets, hire sales teams and expand its customer base. These plans often assume that another funding round will follow once the business reaches its next growth targets. But expansion can become expensive long before the company reaches those targets.
For an enterprise AI business, new contracts may require extensive customisation and ongoing engineering support. Revenue grows, yet the company spends more than expected to deliver it. Hiring commitments and operating costs continue even when progress falls behind the original plan.
This leaves founders in a difficult position. If they need fresh capital to maintain operations, they have less control over the timing of fundraising and the terms investors offer. A more measured expansion strategy may look less impressive in the short term, but it gives management greater freedom to choose when and how to raise its next round.
The next test for Europe’s AI boom
The next test for Europe’s AI funding market will come in 2027 and 2028, when some of the startups raising smaller amounts today will need substantially more capital to expand. Whether they can secure investments of €27 million, €44 million or more on favourable terms will help determine their ability to grow.
The current data does not show how many companies sought funding unsuccessfully, how long fundraising took or how much capital they needed. It therefore cannot establish a shortage of growth capital across Europe.
The next stage will also put more pressure on business fundamentals. Enterprise AI companies that can retain customers and expand without a corresponding rise in operating costs should have an advantage when seeking further investment. Others may face difficult choices about how quickly they can grow and how much capital they can afford to raise.
It will be worth following the companies that secured smaller rounds in 2025 and 2026. Their progression to larger investments, the time between funding rounds and the terms they receive will help establish whether Europe has a genuine growth-capital constraint.
Europe may continue setting AI investment records. The more consequential development over the next few years will be how many of today’s funded startups manage to reach the next stage and build sustainable businesses. That is where the depth of Europe’s AI funding market will become much clearer.

articles.title: Microsoft urges Entra ID admins to migrate users to passkeys
articles.text:
Microsoft again asked Entra ID administrators to migrate users to phishing-resistant methods to avoid sign-in disruptions before it retires SMS and voice authentication in February 2027.
This retirement process applies only to Microsoft Entra ID workforce tenant authentication scenarios and not to Azure AD B2C or Microsoft Entra External ID customer identity scenarios.
Before Microsoft retires SMS and voice authentication, admins should ensure all users in their organizations use a phishing-resistant method, since they will no longer be able to use them to complete multifactor authentication and log in to their accounts.
Admins can choose from passkeys, QR code authentication, FIDO2 security keys, and other Entra ID-supported sign-in methods.
"Microsoft-provided SMS and voice authentication will retire starting February 1, 2027. Complete your migration before rollout begins to avoid interrupting users' sign-in experience," Microsoft said in a Microsoft 365 Message Center update on Tuesday.
"SMS and voice are vulnerable to phishing and SIM-swap attacks. Microsoft recommends passkeys for stronger, phishing-resistant protection. You can also migrate to another supported authentication method or retain SMS and voice by configuring a customer-managed telecom provider (CYOT) through the Microsoft Security Store."
As Microsoft noted in a previous reminder issued in September, admins with the Authentication Policy Administrator, Global Reader, or Security Reader roles can find users with SMS or voice authentication with the Entra SMS/Voice Policy Scanner PowerShell script.
Organizations that must use phone-based authentication have to configure third-party telecom providers through the Microsoft Security Store.
Passkeys now the default Entra ID auth method
In July, Microsoft announced that passkeys will start rolling out as the default authentication experience for the Entra ID enterprise identity service starting in September.
"As the rollout reaches each organization, users enabled for SMS or voice authentication will automatically be enabled for passkeys, and the next time they perform multifactor authentication, they'll be prompted to register a passkey," Microsoft said.
"Following this transition, on February 1, 2027, Microsoft will retire Microsoft-provided telecom delivery for SMS and voice authentication and will no longer offer SMS and voice as a native Microsoft Entra capability."
Microsoft also retired SMS first-factor sign-in for Microsoft Entra ID Free tenants in August due to phishing, fraud, and account compromise risks, and stopped enabling it for newly created tenants.
Detailed guidance on deploying and managing phishing-resistant passwordless authentication in Entra ID is available on this dedicated Microsoft documentation page.

articles.title: Plus léger qu'un MacBook Air 15 pouces : le tour de force du MacBook Pro tactile — Frandroid
articles.text:
Apple a présenté ce mercredi 28 octobre son premier MacBook Pro à écran tactile, sur un châssis inédit, le premier depuis 2021.
Le point de comparaison le plus juste est le MacBook Pro à écran Mini LED, qu’Apple continue de vendre avec les mêmes puces M5 Pro et M5 Max : seuls le châssis et l’écran changent.
220 grammes de moins sur le 14 pouces, 320 sur le 16
Le 14 pouces avec puce M5 Pro pèse 1,38 kg, contre 1,60 kg pour le modèle Mini LED : 220 grammes de moins, soit 14 %. Le 16 pouces passe de 2,14 kg à 1,82 kg, soit 320 grammes (15 %) de moins. La puce M5 Max ajoute 20 grammes sur chaque taille.
Le 14 pouces tactile devient ainsi plus léger que le MacBook Air 15 pouces M5 (1,51 kg), et que le MacBook Pro 14 pouces M6 présenté ce mardi 27 octobre (1,55 kg). Il reste nettement plus épais que l’Air : 1,50 cm contre 1,15 cm.
L’épaisseur bouge peu : un demi-millimètre de moins sur le 14 pouces, 0,8 millimètre sur le 16 pouces. Grâce à des bordures d’écran plus fines, l’empreinte rétrécit surtout en profondeur, de près de 5 millimètres sur le 14 pouces et de 4 millimètres sur le 16 pouces. Le 16 pouces en profite pour passer de 16,2 à 16,3 pouces de diagonale ; le 14 pouces reste à 14,2 pouces.

|---|---|---|---|---|
| Poids (M5 Pro) | 1,38 kg | 1,60 kg | 1,82 kg | 2,14 kg | 
| Épaisseur | 1,50 cm | 1,55 cm | 1,60 cm | 1,68 cm | 
| Largeur × profondeur | 31,08 × 21,63 cm | 31,26 × 22,12 cm | 35,55 × 24,42 cm | 35,57 × 24,81 cm | 
| Écran | 14,2″ | 14,2″ | 16,3″ | 16,2″ | 
| Batterie | 72,6 Wh | 72,4 Wh | 100 Wh | 100 Wh | 
Source : Apple.
La batterie n’a pas fondu
Premier réflexe devant un portable qui maigrit : regarder la batterie. Elle ne perd rien : 72,6 Wh sur le 14 pouces, contre 72,4 Wh sur le modèle Mini LED, et toujours 100 Wh sur le 16 pouces, la limite pour l’emporter en cabine d’avion sans l’accord de la compagnie.
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
Les autonomies annoncées sont identiques à celles des modèles Mini LED : jusqu’à 22 heures de vidéo en streaming sur le 14 pouces M5 Pro et 24 heures sur le 16 pouces, d’après des mesures faites par Apple sur des machines de présérie.
Apple n’a donc pas acheté la légèreté en rognant sur l’autonomie, du moins sur le papier. Ce sera à vérifier en test, d’autant que l’écran OLED grimpe jusqu’à 2 000 nits en SDR, contre 1 000 nits sur le modèle Mini LED.
Où sont passés les grammes ?
Apple ne détaille pas. Première piste, l’écran : une dalle OLED produit sa propre lumière, pixel par pixel, quand le Mini LED s’éclaire par derrière avec des milliers de petites LED et plusieurs couches de diffusion. Apple attribue la finesse du nouveau modèle à cet empilement plus léger, et Wired, qui a pu voir la machine, y voit l’une des raisons de la perte de poids.
Deuxième piste, l’intérieur : selon Bloomberg, Apple a miniaturisé et réorganisé les composants, refroidissement compris.
Apple parle d’une « architecture thermique entièrement repensée ». Elle promet les mêmes performances soutenues que sur les modèles Mini LED, M5 Max compris, malgré le châssis allégé, et assure que l’air chaud est désormais dirigé loin de l’écran.
Ce point compte sur une machine qu’on touche : un écran tiède sous les doigts serait désagréable, et Johny Srouji, patron du matériel d’Apple, cite justement cet objectif au magazine Wired. Selon Mark Gurman, de Bloomberg, l’air circule désormais par la charnière.
Apple n’a communiqué ni le nombre de ventilateurs, ni l’emplacement des sorties d’air, ni le niveau de bruit. La promesse de performances identiques dans un châssis plus léger devra être vérifiée en test, surtout avec la puce M5 Max.
Une charnière qui ne bascule pas
Quand on touche l’écran d’un portable, on appuie sur un panneau tenu uniquement par sa base, qui a tendance à basculer. Apple a redessiné la charnière pour que l’écran reste stable sous le doigt ; Johny Srouji reproche d’ailleurs aux PC tactiles concurrents leur écran qui vacille.
Apple a tout de même ajouté une stabilisation de la caméra, qui lisse l’image en visioconférence quand on touche l’écran, signe que la dalle bouge sans doute encore un peu.
Disparue en 2016, la pomme lumineuse revient sur le capot. L’ancienne était éclairée par le rétroéclairage de l’écran ; l’OLED n’en a pas, Apple a donc dû trouver une autre solution, sans préciser laquelle.
Le reste évolue par petites touches : nouveaux woofers et tweeters pour les six haut-parleurs, verre nano-texturé (option à 165 €) désormais gravé directement dans la vitre, deux coloris, noir sidéral et argent. La connectique ne change pas : trois ports Thunderbolt 5, HDMI, lecteur SDXC, MagSafe 3 et prise casque. Les puces non plus : ce sont les M5 Pro et M5 Max lancées en mars.
Prix et disponibilité
Le MacBook Pro tactile est en précommande depuis ce mercredi, pour une sortie le vendredi 6 novembre. Il démarre à 3 299 € en 14 pouces et à 3 899 € en 16 pouces, soit 400 € et 500 € de plus que les modèles Mini LED à puce identique.
Le MacBook Pro Mini LED reste au catalogue, à partir de 2 899 € en 14 pouces et 3 399 € en 16 pouces. Les 400 € d’écart sur le petit modèle paient l’écran OLED tactile et un châssis plus léger, à puce et autonomie annoncée identiques.
À l’autre bout de la gamme, la facture d’un 16 pouces toutes options cochées dépasse les 16 000 €, comme on l’a calculé dans notre récap du nouveau MacBook Pro.
