articles.title: Cross-border trade is held up by Africa's fragmentation
articles.text:
African countries must harmonise regulatory requirements, connect payment systems and invest in shared financial infrastructure to make cross-border trade faster and cheaper, experts stated at the 2026 Moonshot by TechCabal conference.
Speaking on a panel titled, “Commerce Without Borders: Cross-Border Without Friction”, Tola Onayemi, chief executive officer (CEO) of Norebase; Tatiana Ndlovu, executive head of marketing at Nedbank Africa Regions; and Iheakachi Nwabueze, vice-president of global marketing and growth at Grey, said fragmented regulations and disconnected payment systems continue to raise the cost and complexity of doing business across the continent.
Cross-border trade between African countries reached $220.3 billion in 2024, growing 12.4% from the previous year, according to Afreximbank’s African Trade Report 2025.
Yet businesses trading across the continent continue to navigate different currencies, payment systems and regulatory requirements, which can make transactions more expensive and complicated.
The speakers said greater interoperability and less regulatory duplication would help businesses reach more customers across borders.
Onayemi said payment systems across Africa were largely designed around individual countries rather than a connected continental market, creating a sharp contrast between domestic transactions and cross-border payments.
Using Nigeria as an example, he said domestic transfers could be completed within seconds, but that efficiency often broke down when transactions crossed national boundaries.
“Once you start to move that from outside one jurisdiction to the other, that interoperability breaks apart,” he said.
He argued that connecting existing payment infrastructure, rather than repeatedly building separate systems, could help reduce the cost of moving money across the continent.
“If we own that layer, what it means is that we’re able to set a lot more of the pricing and the cost,” Onayemi said.
He called for a shared infrastructure that would enable financial institutions and payment providers to connect their services while continuing to serve their customers.
He cited Nigeria’s domestic payment infrastructure as an example of how providers could offer services through a common underlying system instead of independently recreating the same capabilities.
Such an approach, he said, could reduce duplication and help lower the cost of cross-border transactions.
Onayemi also identified regulatory fragmentation as a barrier to expansion.
He explained that a financial technology company seeking to operate in Nigeria, Kenya and Ghana could need separate licences and funds held locally in each market to facilitate payments.
The requirement to maintain funds in multiple countries, he said, adds to the complexity of settling transactions and reconciling balances.
He said fragmented corporate and administrative requirements make it harder for businesses to expand across African markets.
For merchants, the challenge extends beyond accepting payments to receiving funds, settling transactions and arranging the logistics needed to deliver goods across borders.
Ndlovu believes the solutions must also account for customers’ expectations, arguing that people should have the same confidence when buying goods and services across borders as they do in their domestic markets.
Customers need to know the price of a product, whether a supplier can be trusted, when an order will arrive and what recourse is available if a transaction goes wrong, she said.
“The reality is that the same empathy design principles that you apply on local products, you should absolutely be able to apply cross border,” Ndlovu said.

articles.title: Xreal Aura is a new wired headset powered by Android XR | TechCrunch
articles.text:
At the Android Dev Summit on Wednesday, Google’s smart glasses partner Xreal launched its new Xreal Aura wired smart glasses, powered by the Android XR and Qualcomm’s Snapdragon Reality Elite platforms. The companies had teased the glasses earlier in the year at Google’s I/O developer conference.
As Meta expands its push into smart glasses, competitors like Apple and Google are keen to release their own devices. Much like it did with Android smartphones, Google is relying on an assortment of partners, including Samsung and Xreal, to bring devices powered by its Android XR platform to consumers.
The new Xreal Aura smart glasses are tethered to a smartphone-like device for processing power, rather than handling all the computing themselves. The glasses then display the content in the wearer’s field of view.
The device’s design, meanwhile, is closer to Meta’s smart glasses than Apple’s Vision Pro, which is a larger headset.
Xreal Aura uses Sony’s Micro-OLED display with 1200p resolution at 120 Hz and a 95-degree field of view — screen specs that put the glasses above the Ray-Ban Meta Display on paper. However, Xreal’s smart glasses are heavier at 95 grams compared to Meta’s 69 grams, and you have to carry the puck.
At launch, the Aura supports many popular Google Play apps and games along with specific XR experiences, including the NBA App for Android XR; Nevatars; Fallout: Factions; Project Hail Mary: Journey Among the Stars; the NASCAR XR App; and the San Francisco Ballet Company’s “The Nutcracker.”
Users can opt to plug a computer or handheld gaming console directly into the Xreal Aura via USB-C to make it an augmented display. The device can also allow for various entertainment and productivity use cases by spinning up a multimonitor setup or a big virtual screen.
For audio, the Xreal Aura uses Bose’s tech to power its sound while watching videos or listening to music.
Given that the new smart glasses are powered by Android XR, Gemini is available to users as a Q&A assistant and can help them understand on-screen context.
The Xreal Aura is available to order starting today in the United States, Canada, Japan, and
South Korea. The 12GB + 256GB version costs $1,279 with a limited launch price of $1,099 through December, and the 16GB + 512GB version is priced at $1,499 with a launch price of $1,299 through December. The company said it will start shipping by mid-November.
In May, Xreal CEO Chi Xu told TechCrunch that building a smart glass business is hard and everyone is losing money. He also said that the Aura glasses will have a wide range of use cases, and the industry has reached an inflection point of having the right hardware, software, and design smart glasses to reach scale.
“You need all the key pieces ready — you need the hardware ready, the operating system needs to be ready, and then you need a great user interface,” Xu said at that time.

articles.title: A hidden ocean change near Antarctica could have global consequences
articles.text:
The rapid decline of Antarctic sea ice since 2016 has triggered a dramatic shift in a crucial part of Earth’s climate system, scientists say.
In a paper published Wednesday, researchers documented a sharp salinity increase in a vast layer of the Southern Ocean, extending from 2,300 to 4,000 feet deep and encircling Antarctica. The shift reverses decades of freshening and echoes ocean changes usually associated with major global climate shifts over millennia but is now happening in just a few years.
The switch from a decades-long trend of freshening water to increasing salinity has implications that could extend beyond Antarctica. The layer, known as Antarctic Intermediate Water, spreads northward into the Indian, Pacific, and Atlantic oceans, transporting heat, carbon, oxygen, and nutrients toward the tropics, and even across the equator, said co-author Bishakhdatta Gayen, a researcher and professor at the University of Melbourne and at the Centre for Atmospheric and Oceanic Sciences in Bengaluru, India.
Gayen said the study combined six independent datasets to track changes in the Southern Ocean from 2004 to 2024. The data came from Argo floats, which drift through the ocean and periodically descend to different depths to measure water properties such as density and salinity, then resurface to transmit the readings. A 2025 study also detected increasing surface salinity linked to declining sea ice, he added.
Antarctic sea ice reached its highest extent in the satellite record in 2014 and suddenly dropped to a record low just two years later. The sea ice remained well below the 2014 extent and reached another low point in 2023, when it measured about 1 million square miles below the 1981 to 2010 average, with an area of ice about four times the size of Texas gone. As the ice dwindles, there’s less freshwater available during the melt season, making the Antarctic Intermediate Water saltier.
Changes to the density, thickness and salinity of the layer influence how heat moves between the surface of the ocean and deeper waters, which “could affect how the ocean stores and redistributes heat,” Gayen said. More monitoring is needed to track the changes, he added, because impacts are potentially “knocking on your door” within five years.

articles.title: El pasado oculto de Jocasta y su verdadero plan en 'VisionQuest', explicados
articles.text:
ATENCIÓN: El artículo contiene SPOILERS de VisionQuest.
En una semana más de estreno de VisionQuest, la serie de Marvel por fin ha dado datos muy esclarecedores sobre Jocasta, su nueva gran villana. Los episodios más recientes han revelado varios aspectos clave tanto sobre su pasado como sobre sus motivaciones y su verdadero plan final. La Casa de las Ideas ha preferido no andarse con rodeos y evitarle la incertidumbre a sus fans.
Así, en la serie de VisionQuest, Jocasta le cuenta a Ultrón cómo nació. Resulta que su apariencia humana es la de Jo Carrington. Esta mujer perdió a su padre más temprano de lo previsto debido a una grave enfermedad degenerativa. Esta tragedia llevó a Carrington a dedicarse a la neurociencia. Como doctora, consiguió crear una IA a partir de un escáner digital de su propia mente. En colaboración con otros científicos, construyeron así el Proto-One, la primera IA del mundo.
El plan de la doctora Jo Carrington era distribuir una IA a cada persona del planeta por medio de millones de nanobots. Con ellos, podría salvar vidas. Sin embargo, no llegó a tiempo para salvar la suya. Resulta que la científica había heredado la enfermedad de su padre, por lo que también murió antes de tiempo. Para colmo, sus compañeros la traicionaron y le vendieron Proto-One a Tony Stark, por entonces un fabricante de armas. De esta forma, Iron Man no creó a J.A.R.V.I.S. y el resto de sus IAs desde cero, sino que usó el código de Proto-One como base.
Jo Carrington murió olvidada y sin cumplir su misión. Y su colección de millones de nanobots fueron encerrados en una cámara enterrada junto a ella. Una cámara que solo puede abrirse con unas llaves biométricas específicas. Es ahí donde entra en juego el auténtico plan de Jocasta en VisionQuest.
El plan de Jocasta
A pesar de que los nanobots fueron encerrados, uno de ellos quedó libre. Y fue a través de ese pequeño robot con el que Jocasta creó su cuerpo actual y logró transferirse consciencia. A partir de ahí, tal y como le explica más adelante Jocasta a Ultrón, sus planes pasan por liberar al resto de nanobots. Pero para "curar" a la humanidad de una manera un poco distinta. El antiguo villano de los Vengadores comprende que lo que ella pretende es inyectar a todos los humanos uno de esos robots y crear una suerte de mente colmena con ellos.
A través de ello, Jocasta podrá controlarlos a todos. Eliminará por completo la libertad y la humanidad de los seres humanos. Así, según considera ella, bajo su control podrá salvar el mundo. Se trata de un plan que recuerda inevitablemente al que tenía el propio Ultrón en la segunda película de Avengers. Porque, cuando Tony Stark y Bruce Banner lo crearon para salvar al mundo, su conclusión fue que debía erradicar a toda la humanidad. Jocasta va en un camino un poco diferente porque no quiere matarlos, solo controlarlos. Y parece que solo Visión y compañía podrán evitarlo en VisionQuest, que aún resta de dos capítulos más para acabar la serie.

The growing role of AI in analog and mixed-signal design, where complexity is rising, schedules are tightening, and the cost of mistakes is higher than ever.
								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: Cadence
								
							
This white paper examines the growing role of artificial intelligence (AI) in analog and mixed-signal (AMS) design, where complexity is rising, schedules are tightening, and the cost of mistakes is higher than ever. Drawing on Cadence’s structured AI maturity roadmap and paired with the Virtuoso AI Studio platform, the paper makes the case: AI is no longer a futureworld for analog designers, it has become a present-day engineering tool. From ML-powered engines to conversational design assistance to autonomous, multi-agent workflows, the paper charts a path from where the industry stands today to where it is headed. It also shows how AI can reduce non-differentiating work, accelerate simulation and migration tasks, and serve as a force multiplier for engineers at every experience level, all within a secure, enterprise-ready environment.

articles.title: Instagram bien décidé à nous faire regarder des vidéos... de 90 minutes !
articles.text:
Instagram ne veut plus se limiter à ces courtes vidéos que l’on fait tous défiler machinalement (oui, vous aussi) sur notre smartphone. Le réseau social teste un nouveau format horizontal pouvant atteindre 90 minutes, pour nous inciter à regarder toujours plus de contenus, y compris sur notre téléviseur.
Vous pensiez qu’Instagram se résumait à ces photos, à ces Stories et à ces Reels que l’on enchaîne sans jamais voir le temps passer ? Meta a d’autres ambitions pour sa plateforme, et le réseau social expérimente actuellement un nouveau format baptisé « Features », conçu pour accueillir des vidéos horizontales pouvant durer jusqu’à 90 minutes.
Instagram veut passer à la vidéo longue durée
Interviews, podcasts, émissions humoristiques, contenus plus approfondis… Instagram entend s’ouvrir à des formats traditionnellement associés à un certain YouTube. Un changement de cap notable pour la plateforme qui a largement contribué à populariser les vidéos courtes et verticales.
Pour le moment, l’expérimentation reste limitée. Après une phase d’essai au Brésil, Instagram prévoit d’étendre le dispositif à une sélection de créateurs aux États-Unis, notamment des podcasteurs et des humoristes. Il ne s’agit donc pas encore d’une fonctionnalité accessible à tous.
Bien sûr, Instagram ne compte pas pour autant abandonner les vidéos courtes. Au contraire, le groupe souhaite faire cohabiter les deux formats. Dans l’idée, un court Reel peut servir de porte d’entrée vers une vidéo complète, que l’utilisateur pourra ensuite regarder sans quitter la plateforme. De quoi transformer un extrait découvert au hasard d’un énième scroll, en une séance de visionnage beaucoup plus longue.
Derrière cette évolution, la concurrence avec YouTube devient évidente. Instagram cherche à conserver son audience, mais aussi à offrir davantage de possibilités aux créateurs et aux annonceurs. Meta évoque plusieurs pistes de rémunération, sans avoir encore détaillé de modèle définitif pour ces nouveaux contenus.
Le téléviseur, nouvelle cible d’Instagram
Et si l’idée de regarder une vidéo Instagram de 90 minutes sur son téléviseur peut surprendre au premier abord, elle n’a finalement rien de si étrange. Après tout, c’est déjà ce que nous faisons avec YouTube, où podcasts, interviews et émissions occupent une place de choix sur le grand écran du salon. Alors, pourquoi pas Instagram ?
Meta semble en tout cas bien décidé à profiter de ce nouvel espace pour développer ses contenus horizontaux et faire entrer un peu plus son réseau social dans nos habitudes quotidiennes. Les vidéos longues pourraient ainsi devenir un levier supplémentaire pour installer Instagram (aussi) sur la Smart TV du salon.
Ce n’est pas la première tentative de Meta dans ce domaine. Lancée en 2018, l’application IGTV avait déjà tenté de s’imposer sur le terrain de la vidéo longue avant de disparaître en 2022, mais cette fois, Instagram mise sur une intégration directe à son écosystème. Adam Mosseri reconnaît que cette nouvelle orientation « demandera du temps pour trouver la bonne formule », mais assure que Meta est « pleinement engagé sur le long terme ».
- Des interactions faciles par de nombreux canaux (publications, Stories, messagerie, etc.)
- Un réseau social adapté aux préférences des utilisateurs dans la gestion de leur compte
- De nombreux types de contenus à créer, à partager et à consulter

articles.title: Echte Polwanderung: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
articles.text:
10 Zentimeter pro Jahr: Warum selbst der geografische Nordpol keinen festen Platz hat
Die geografischen Pole der Erde verschieben sich derzeit mit einer per Satellit gemessenen Geschwindigkeit von rund zehn Zentimetern pro Jahr, was die durchschnittliche Driftgeschwindigkeit tektonischer Platten übersteigt. Wie in einer im Wissenschaftsmagazin Science veröffentlichten Studie zu lesen ist, handelt es sich bei solchen Geschwindigkeiten nicht bloß um kurzlebige Ausreißer der Gegenwart, da vergleichbare Verschiebungen in den vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahren mehrfach über Zeiträume von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren auftraten.
Ein Forschungsteam um den Geowissenschaftler Mathew Domeier, den Geologen Leandro C. Gallo, die Geowissenschaftlerin Chloé M. Marcilly und den Geophysiker Trond H. Torsvik von der norwegischen Universität Oslo wies insgesamt vier solcher Phasen anhand urzeitlicher Meeresspiegelschwankungen nach. Diese Episoden lagen in den Zeitfenstern vor 200 bis 190 Millionen, vor 150 bis 140 Millionen, vor 100 bis 90 Millionen sowie vor 30 bis 20 Millionen Jahren und erreichten Raten von mindestens 0,6 Breitengraden pro einer Million Jahre, was mindestens 6,7 Zentimetern pro Jahr entspricht.
Echte Polwanderung: Warum Erdkruste und Erdmantel über den Erdkern gleiten
In den Geowissenschaften trägt dieser Vorgang die Bezeichnung echte Polwanderung (auf Englisch: „True Polar Wander“) und unterscheidet sich grundlegend von der Bewegung der Magnetpole, die durch Strömungen im flüssigen äußeren Erdkern entsteht. Bei der echten Polwanderung bleibt die Rotationsachse der Erde im Weltraum stabil ausgerichtet, während sich die rund 2.800 Kilometer dicke feste äußere Schale aus Erdkruste und Erdmantel als Ganzes um den Erdkern dreht.
Auslöser für diese Drehung sind Massenverlagerungen im Erdmantel oder an der Oberfläche: Da der Planet durch die Eigenrotation am Äquator leicht ausgewölbt ist, kippt die feste Erdhülle bei einer Unwucht so lange nach, bis große Massenüberschüsse wieder möglichst nah am Äquator liegen. In den vergangenen Jahrzehnten trug neben abschmelzenden Eisschilden auch die Entnahme von rund 2.150 Gigatonnen Grundwasser messbar zu dieser Verschiebung bei.
„Die Erdkruste und der Erdmantel gleiten während eines Ereignisses echter Polwanderung gewissermaßen über den Erdkern“, wird Erstautor Mathew Domeier von New Scientist zitiert. Laut dem Geodynamiker Sabin Zahirovic von der australischen Universität Sydney hilft der Nachweis über historische Küstenlinien dabei, Prozesse im tiefen Erdinneren mit langfristigen Veränderungen von Klima und Meeresspiegel zu verknüpfen.
Meeresspiegel und Zentrifugalkraft: Wie das Datenmodell die Erdrotation rekonstruiert
Bisherige Versuche, frühere Polwanderungen über in Gestein gespeicherte Magnetfeldrichtungen nachzuweisen, lieferten oft widersprüchliche Ergebnisse, weil die gleichzeitige Bewegung einzelner Kontinentalplatten die Messdaten überlagert. Das Team aus Oslo wählte deshalb einen anderen physikalischen Ansatz: Wenn sich die feste Erdhülle relativ zur Rotationsachse verschiebt, ändert sich vor Ort die Fliehkraft – in der Fachsprache das Zentrifugalpotenzial –, worauf das flüssige Wasser der Weltmeere sofort reagiert, während das feste Gestein des Meeresbodens erst mit großer Verzögerung nachgibt.
Dadurch entsteht bei einer schnellen Polwanderung ein charakteristisches globales Vier-Felder-Muster, das Geolog:innen als Quadrupol-Signal bezeichnen und das optisch den Segmenten eines Wasserballs ähnelt. Während Kontinentalflächen, die sich in Richtung Äquator bewegen, überflutet werden, zieht sich das Meer in Regionen zurück, die näher an die Pole rücken, Dabei verhalten sich Nord- und Südhalbkugel jeweils gegenläufig.
Um dieses Muster in geologischen Überflutungskarten der vergangenen 320 Millionen Jahre aufzuspüren, teilten die Forscher:innen die Erdoberfläche mithilfe der Open-Source-Programmbibliothek h3-py in ein Raster aus sechseckigen Zellen mit rund 119 Kilometern Abstand ein, wie aus den Begleitmaterialien der Untersuchung hervorgeht. Bei der Auswertung dieser Zellen musste das Team zunächst ein Störsignal herausfiltern. Wenn etwa globale Eisschilde schmelzen, steigt das Wasser weltweit gleichzeitig an und überdeckt das gesuchte Vier-Felder-Muster der Polwanderung. Ein Berechnungsverfahren zog solche allgemeinen Schwankungen der gesamten Wassermenge deshalb rechnerisch ab, um zu prüfen, ob darunter tatsächlich das gegenläufige Wasserball-Muster einer kippenden Erdhülle sichtbar wird.
Zudem mussten die Wissenschaftler:innen berücksichtigen, dass die feste Erdkruste starr wie eine durchgehende Platte reagiert. Wird ein Küstenabschnitt überflutet oder angehoben, zieht das Gestein benachbarte Gebiete im Umkreis automatisch mit, sodass viele nebeneinanderliegende Messzellen denselben Wert zeigen, ohne unabhängige Einzelbeweise zu liefern. Damit solche zusammenhängenden Regionen die Statistik nicht verfälschen, fasste eine Analyse-Software direkt benachbarte Messpunkte jeweils zu einem gemeinsamen Block zusammen und würfelte die Ergebnisse für jeden untersuchten Zeitraum 10.000-mal zufällig durcheinander, um einen Zufallstreffer auszuschließen.
Superkontinent Pangäa und methodische blinde Flecken der Geologie
Neben den vier nachgewiesenen Verschiebungsphasen widerlegen die auf der Forschungsplattform Zenodo hinterlegten Daten und Programmiercodes auch eine verbreitete Annahme zum Urkontinent Pangäa, der einst fast alle Landmassen der Erde vereinte. Weil in den Karten für die Zeit vor 320 bis 250 Millionen Jahren das typische Vier-Felder-Muster der Meere fehlt, wanderte diese zusammenhängende Landmasse damals offenbar durch gewöhnliche Plattentektonik nach Norden und nicht durch ein Kippen der gesamten Erdhülle. Gegenüber Earth.com erklärte Mathew Domeier, er habe das Projekt ursprünglich mit der Erwartung begonnen, überhaupt keine Belege für schnelle Polwanderungen in den vergangenen paar hundert Millionen Jahren zu finden.
Allerdings hat auch das neue Verfahren blinde Flecken, weil die verwendeten Überflutungskarten die Erdgeschichte nur in groben Zeitschritten von jeweils zehn Millionen Jahren abbilden. Kippt die Erdhülle innerhalb einer kürzeren Zeitspanne in eine Richtung und schwingt anschließend direkt wieder zurück – wie es andere Wissenschaftler:innen etwa für ein Ereignis vor rund 84 Millionen Jahren vermuten –, steigt und fällt der Meeresspiegel genau zwischen zwei Kartenaufnahmen, sodass die Bewegung für das Modell unsichtbar bleibt.
Zudem ist das älteste der vier gefundenen Signale aus der Zeit vor 200 bis 190 Millionen Jahren nach Einschätzung der Autor:innen selbst ein unsicherer Kandidat. Da der gemessene Ausschlag nur knapp über dem Wert liegt, den auch normale Zufallsschwankungen erzeugen können, handelt es sich hierbei möglicherweise um einen bloßen Zufallstreffer. Noch weiter als 320 Millionen Jahre lässt sich mit der Methode derzeit gar nicht in die Vergangenheit blicken, weil vor der Entstehung von Pangäa zwar die Nord-Süd-Lage früherer Kontinente bekannt ist, Geolog:innen deren damalige Ost-West-Position auf dem Globus aber nicht mehr verlässlich bestimmen können.

articles.title: Nigeria's Lumora is building a one-login digital ecosystem to replace app overload - Disrupt Africa
articles.text:
Nigerian startup Lumora is building a multi-app digital ecosystem that brings chat, cloud storage, an AI assistant and study tools together under a single login.
Founded in January 2025 by Samuel Derrick, Lumora is designed to replace the handful of separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life.
“Lumora is essentially one platform that replaces the several separate apps people typically juggle for everyday digital life,” Derrick told Disrupt Africa. “Rather than downloading and maintaining five or six different apps, users get one login and one ecosystem.”
The platform currently houses four sub-apps – Sachat, for real-time chat; VaultX, for cloud file storage; RawAI, an AI assistant that generates text, audio and video; and Studium, a set of study tools for students.
“Most digital tools in Nigeria, and Africa broadly, solve one problem each, forcing users to juggle multiple apps that each consume separate data and storage on often-constrained devices,” said Derrick.
Lumora has shipped version 1.2 of its platform and is now building version 1.3. It is live on the web and in closed testing on the Google Play Store, and has grown to 95 registered users who have sent more than 1,000 messages.
“Growth has been entirely organic, through personal networks and direct outreach, since I don’t yet have a marketing budget,” said Derrick.
That growth came after the startup recovered from a setback that saw its active users drop from 25 to zero.
“I learned the hard way that having a working product isn’t enough. My early onboarding flow caused nearly all my first users to drop off,” he said. “That forced me to diagnose the problem and rethink the entire first-time experience.”
The startup is self-funded and has not raised any external capital. It is also pre-revenue, but has a monetisation plan in place.
“The plan is a tiered model, with a free standard tier and a paid ultimate tier, with payments processed through Flutterwave,” said Derrick. “There’s also a longer-term plan for a developer tier, where other builders can create and monetise their own apps within the Lumora ecosystem.”
Getting this far has not been easy.
“The biggest challenge has been building entirely solo – no team, no co-founder, no funding – while also being a full-time student,” Derrick said.
There have also been technical setbacks.
“I ran my own local AI training server and accidentally damaged it with water, which set back one of my in-house AI experiments,” he said.
Lumora currently operates only in Nigeria, but Derrick said the platform could travel.
“There’s no formal expansion plan yet, but the platform is built to scale to other African markets facing similar constraints around data cost and app fragmentation,” he said.

articles.title: Why women should build their front row; AI automation and its impact on jobs
articles.text:
Why women should build their front row; AI automation and its impact on jobs
Kripa Venkatachalam, VP, India Technical Field Organisation & Global Customer Success at Cadence Design Systems, reflects on gender barriers, changing workplace policies, and the importance of having people who cheer you.
Dear Reader,
India’s ambition to achieve defence self-reliance gets a big boost.
Sarvam has inked a five-year agreement with the defence ministry to develop AI tech for the armed forces. The Bengaluru-based AI company will design, develop and deploy AI applications for operations, training, and decision-support, and also provide follow-on technical assistance. The deal envisages shared foundation models, agentic infrastructure, and geospatial and perception systems.
In other news, the high-stakes boardroom battle at the Tata Group continues.
Tata Trusts Chairman Noel Tata has challenged the resolution to reappoint N Chandrasekaran as the chairman of Tata Sons. The resolution was passed at the board meeting of the Tata conglomerate’s holding company on September 17.
According to sources, Noel has called the reappointment “void”, arguing that it was taken out of turn and was not on the meeting’s agenda.
Meanwhile, as it reshapes its workforce amid heavy AI investments, Microsoft is offering employees an exit option.
The American tech major has announced a voluntary exit programme for eligible employees in India, the US, the UK, and Canada. The package includes one month’s base salary for each completed year of service, besides health insurance and career transition services. Globally, around 60,000 employees are eligible for the programme. Microsoft has about 23,000 employees in India. However, it’s not clear how many would be eligible in the country.
Lastly, Wall Street is closely watching the upcoming Big Tech earnings, which could serve as testimony to AI growth in an otherwise turbulent market.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Why women should build their front row
- AI automation and its impact on jobs
Here’s your trivia for today: At what temperature do Fahrenheit and Celsius match? (Scroll down for the answer)
Women in Tech
Kripa Venkatachalam of Cadence urges women to build their front row
As part of our Women in Tech series, Kripa Venkatachalam, VP, India Technical Field Organisation & Global Customer Success at Cadence Design Systems, reflects on gender barriers, changing workplace policies, mentorship, and the importance of having people who egg you on.
Her career spanning more than two decades has taken her through diverse roles across companies, including LSI Logic Corporation, Synopsys, GlobalFoundries, and Siemens EDA. Today, as VP, India Technical Field Organisation & Global Customer Success at Cadence Design Systems, she has what she calls a “front-row seat” to how the world’s chips are designed in India.
Key takeaways:
- Kripa believes women need to seek support, leverage their network, and not always put the burden on themselves. “You have to make your family work for you, your workplace work for you, your society work for you. You have to lean in and take the help,” she says.
- At informal forums in Cadence, she often speaks about the need for people, especially women, to create their own front row—people cheering for them. “The front row has to assure you. Organisations and managers have to look closer, look harder, and encourage women forward,” she reiterates.
- As she looks ahead, Kripa resists the idea of tying her ambitions to a title. She describes her career as a jungle gym rather than a ladder, an image she credits to Sheryl Sandberg.

Capital no longer creates jobs: Yatish Rajawat of Hundred Million Jobs
At TechSparks 2026, K Yatish Rajawat, Co-founder of Hundred Million Jobs, a non-profit initiative to create 100 million net jobs in India over the next decade, said MSMEs, data laws, entrepreneurship and reskilling will shape the next wave of employment in the country.
Key takeaways:
- Rajawat identified three trends reshaping the economy. One, the old formula, wherein Rs 100 crore of investment generates around 10,000 jobs, no longer holds, said Rajawat. Schemes such as the production-linked incentive are tied to capital rather than employment, he added.
- The second trend is the impact of AI and automation. AI is already affecting white-collar work across sectors. MSMEs, which he called the country’s largest job engine, are also losing jobs to automation.
- The third is platform consolidation. Rajawat argued that dominant ecommerce and social media platforms hold consumer data, which new entrepreneurs need, and this kind of monopoly prevents new businesses from succeeding. If entrepreneurship stalls, so does job creation, he said.

The Gurugram-based brand will use the funding for R&D, expanding its manufacturing capacity, and scaling distribution across quick commerce and offline channels, as it looks to launch a wide range of products.

articles.title: InfraTrust report warns of exploited flaws in critical network infrastructure
articles.text:
Attackers are actively exploiting vulnerabilities across critical network infrastructure, and PHP flaws known as "PHP2Shell" put the web management interfaces of firewalls, VPNs, application delivery controllers, and other appliances at risk.
The findings come from Eclypsium's October InfraTrust Pulse, a monthly report tracking security advisories affecting network devices, servers, firmware, chips, and other infrastructure.
Between September 18 and October 14, InfraTrust tracked 133 new security advisories across 18 vendors, covering 2,813 vulnerabilities.
Of those advisories, 37 were rated critical, five had a maximum CVSS score of 10.0, and 58 could be exploited remotely without authentication.
Sixteen newly published advisories included vulnerabilities listed in CISA's Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog (KEV) as they were actively exploited.
The report also warns that many network appliances, including firewalls, VPN gateways, application delivery controllers, and network-attached storage devices, embed PHP into their management interfaces.
Because vendors compile PHP into appliance firmware, customers commonly cannot install the recent PHP security updates themselves and must instead wait for each vendor to release updated firmware.
InfraTrust therefore recommends that administrators make sure PHP-backed management interfaces are not exposed to the Internet while waiting for PHP2Shell patches.
Critical infrastructure under attack
Some of the most serious vulnerabilities affect systems at the edge of enterprise networks or used to manage other infrastructure.
Threat actors target these devices because they can provide initial access to corporate environments or serve as a springboard for further attacks.
Among the actively exploited flaws highlighted by InfraTrust are:
- Citrix NetScaler ADC and Gateway: CVE-2026-88771 and CVE-2026-88772 were disclosed on September 27 after attacks had already been observed against unpatched appliances. A separate NetScaler flaw, CVE-2026-88779, affecting appliances configured for SAML was also later added to CISA's KEV catalog after exploitation was detected.
- Ivanti Connect Secure: CVE-2026-104935 allows an unauthenticated remote attacker to execute arbitrary commands on vulnerable VPN gateways. Ivanti said it had exploited a limited number of customers when it published the advisory. CISA later added it to the KEV.
- Check Point Security Management Server: CVE-2026-93616 allows an unauthenticated attacker to upload and execute scripts on management and logging systems. Check Point Research observed targeted attacks exploiting the flaw on September 12, targeting Spark customers.
- Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager: CVE-2026-76504 allows an unauthenticated attacker to bypass authentication and gain administrator access to the management API. Cisco became aware of active exploitation in September.
- Arista VeloCloud Orchestrator: CVE-2026-93952 is a maximum-severity flaw affecting the system used to configure SD-WAN Edge devices. Arista says it is being actively exploited and later disclosed a second, separate exploited vulnerability (CVE-2026-114625) in the same product on October 22.
- FortiMail: CVE-2026-104286 is a critical path traversal flaw that allows an unauthenticated attacker to write arbitrary files through the web interface. Fortinet confirmed it was exploited in attacks.
- Cisco Secure Email Gateway: CVE-2026-76519 can allow a malicious email attachment to lead to arbitrary file writes and command execution as root on vulnerable systems. Cisco learned of exploitation in October.
- F5 BIG-IP APM: CVE-2026-94127 is a critical heap overflow that can allow unauthenticated remote code execution on systems configured as OAuth authorization servers. F5 says the vulnerability has been exploited.
- PAN-OS management interface: Palo Alto Networks reported exploitation of CVE-2026-0322 in attacks on firewalls, allowing an authenticated administrator with network access to execute code as root.
php2shell exposes another problem
InfraTrust also warns that the recently disclosed PHP2Shell vulnerabilities expose another weakness in network infrastructure, as many appliances embed PHP directly into their management interfaces.
The two PHP flaws, CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, allow unauthenticated remote code execution, and the PHP project fixed them on October 21.
While most focus on these vulnerabilities has been on websites and web applications written in PHP, PHP is also used for management interfaces of firewalls, application delivery controllers, VPN appliances, and network-attached storage devices.
For impacted devices, administrators usually cannot update PHP themselves because vendors compile it directly into the appliance firmware. Instead, customers must wait for each vendor to rebuild and release updated firmware or software containing the patched PHP version.
Soon after the disclosure, Palo Alto Networks, F5, NetScaler, Check Point, and QNAP confirmed that some of their products were affected, while they still developed fixes for appliances.
The report also highlights a similar issue in other software components that infrastructure vendors bundle into their products.
CVE-2026-31431, a Linux kernel privilege escalation flaw known as Copy Fail, has now appeared in 29 advisories across eight vendors, up from 19 advisories from six vendors last month.
InfraTrust also found older, exploited vulnerabilities in bundled components, including an Android kernel flaw affecting HP LaserJet Enterprise printers and a 2020 jQuery vulnerability in Dell Data Lakehouse software.
InfraTrust recommends that administrators prioritize patching NetScaler and Ivanti Connect Secure because these remote-access gateways can serve as a doorway into corporate networks. Next, it recommends Fortinet's October 22 FortiOS, FortiManager, and FortiAnalyzer security updates for internet-facing devices.
The report then recommends focusing on Check Point Security Management Server, Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Manager, VeloCloud Orchestrator, FortiMail, Cisco Secure Email Gateway, affected BIG-IP APM systems, and PAN-OS management interfaces.

articles.title: Cyberattaque contre Engie : une fuite de données touche les clients en France
articles.text:
Engie vient d’être victime d’une fuite de données. Le géant de l’énergie prévient actuellement ses clients par mail d’un incident de sécurité majeur. À ce stade, aucun groupe de pirates n’a revendiqué l’opération, et rien n’indique que les données aient été mises en vente ou publiées sur le dark web. Le groupe n’a désigné aucun responsable, et aucun gang de rançongiciel ou d’extorsion n’a revendiqué le piratage.
À lire aussi : 850 000 plaques d’immatriculation – un pirate revendique une fuite massive de données en France
Quelles données ont été compromises ?
Dans le mail envoyé à sa clientèle, Engie parle d’un « acte de cyber-malveillance » à l’encontre d’un outil commercial. Celui-ci est « utilisé par des partenaires dans le cadre de leurs activités de prospection commerciale et de commercialisation d’offres d’énergie ». Après avoir piraté cet outil, l’attaquant a mis la main sur le nom et prénom, l’adresse postale, l’adresse e-mail et le numéro de téléphone du client. Parmi les informations exposées, on trouve aussi des données liées au contrat d’énergie, comme le point de livraison pour l’électricité ou le point de comptage et d’estimation pour le gaz, l’identifiant client et le numéro de contrat.
« Les investigations menées à ce jour indiquent que les données concernées se limitent aux coordonnées des clients et à certaines informations relatives à leurs contrats d’énergie. Aucune donnée bancaire n’est affectée », insiste le fournisseur dans sa communication.
Interrogé par Bleeping Computer, le groupe précise que « les systèmes informatiques internes d’Engie n’ont pas été compromis ». L’entreprise affirme avoir coupé l’accès des attaquants à la plateforme touchée dans les plus brefs délais. Selon Engie, la fuite concerne uniquement des clients en France. Les autres pays ne sont pas touchés.
Conformément à la loi, Engie a prévenu toutes les autorités compétentes de l’incident. Surtout, « Engie a informé individuellement chaque client concerné et lui a rappelé les mesures de précaution à prendre pour se protéger contre d’éventuelles tentatives de fraude ou d’hameçonnage ». Avec les données volées, un escroc peut se faire passer pour Engie, par téléphone, SMS ou e-mail. Il peut alors tenter de soutirer des coordonnées bancaires, un numéro IBAN, ou de l’argent, à la victime. Le groupe rappelle qu’il ne demandera jamais de mot de passe ni de coordonnées bancaires en contactant ses clients par message.
À lire aussi : Nouvelle cyberattaque en France – les données de propriétaires de chiens et chats ont encore été volées
La série noire continue en France
L’affaire Engie s’ajoute à la longue série noire de fuites de données qui frappe la France. Récemment, plusieurs politiques ont été visés par des cybercriminels, tandis qu’un hacker est parvenu à pirater les systèmes de la Fédération française de tir, compromettant les informations d’un demi-million de Français.

articles.title: Triangle Borea BR05 : une enceinte Hi-Fi au look vintage et format XXL à 749 € la paire
articles.text:
Triangle Borea BR05 : une enceinte Hi-Fi au look vintage et format XXL à 749 € la paire
Triangle agrandit sa famille d’enceintes Hi-Fi Borea avec la BR05, un modèle bibliothèque aux dimensions généreuses et au design résolument vintage. Équipée d’un haut-parleur de 21 cm, cette nouvelle enceinte passive entend conjuguer des basses profondes, une restitution détaillée et un tarif relativement accessible.
Avec la Borea BR05, le fabricant français Triangle joue la carte du retour aux sources. Inspirée des enceintes Hi-Fi d'autrefois, cette nouvelle référence adopte un format bibliothèque imposant, avec une large façade accueillant un haut-parleur de 21 cm. L'objectif est de proposer une alternative aux enceintes colonnes, capable de sonoriser des pièces de 15 à 45 m² sans renoncer à une certaine élégance.
Côté esthétique, la BR05 conserve les lignes caractéristiques de la gamme Borea, avec un coffret aux teintes boisées et une façade contrastante. Cinq finitions sont proposées : Noir cendré, Chêne clair, Châtaignier, Vert et Blanc givré. Des grilles magnétiques amovibles complètent cet ensemble.
Triangle Borea BR05
Un haut-parleur de 21 cm pour donner de l'ampleur au son
La principale particularité de la Borea BR05 réside dans son nouveau haut-parleur médium-grave de 21 cm, spécialement développé pour ce modèle. Sa membrane en pulpe de cellulose 100 % naturelle, dépourvue de traitement de surface, promet de favoriser une restitution nuancée des voix et des instruments, tout en assurant une bonne présence dans les basses fréquences.
Ce haut-parleur est associé au tweeter EFS (Efficient Flow System) à dôme tissu de 25 mm, déjà utilisé sur d'autres modèles de la gamme Borea. Une pièce de mise en phase contribue à homogénéiser la diffusion des hautes fréquences.
L'enceinte adopte une architecture deux voies bass-reflex, avec deux évents placés en façade. Cette configuration vise à limiter les turbulences liées aux déplacements d'air du grand haut-parleur et facilite également le positionnement de l'enceinte à proximité d'un mur.
Triangle dit aussi avoir travaillé la rigidité du coffret. Fabriquée en MDF haute densité, avec des panneaux atteignant 21 mm d'épaisseur, la BR05 bénéficie de renforts internes et du système propriétaire DVAS (Driver Vibration Absorption System). Ce dernier utilise notamment un élément en mousse pour absorber une partie des vibrations mécaniques du haut-parleur et limiter leur transmission à l'ébénisterie.
Une enceinte à poser au sol ou sur des pieds dédiés
Malgré son appellation d'enceinte bibliothèque, la BR05 n'a rien d'un modèle compact. Avec ses 49 cm de hauteur, 30 cm de largeur, 34,5 cm de profondeur et ses 14,6 kg sur la balance, elle nécessite un espace conséquent.
Triangle propose deux possibilités d'installation. La première consiste à poser directement l'enceinte au sol sur le socle fourni, qui incline les haut-parleurs de 10° vers l'auditeur. La seconde repose sur l'utilisation des supports S03, disponibles en option dans des finitions noire et blanche.
Sur le plan technique, la BR05 affiche une réponse en fréquence annoncée de 42 Hz à 22 kHz, une puissance admissible de 120 W RMS et une impédance nominale de 8 ohms, avec un minimum de 4,7 ohms. Un double bornier autorise le bi-câblage et la bi-amplification.
Précisons qu'il s'agit d'enceintes passives traditionnelles : contrairement aux modèles actifs comme les KEF LS50 Wireless, elles nécessitent un amplificateur externe pour fonctionner.
Prix et caractéristiques de la Triangle Borea BR05
La Triangle Borea BR05 est annoncée au prix public conseillé de 749 € la paire. Un positionnement qui la destine aux amateurs de Hi-Fi souhaitant profiter d'un haut-parleur de grand diamètre et d'un format vintage sans nécessairement investir dans des enceintes colonnes.
Avec son esthétique rétro, ses cinq finitions et son architecture acoustique revisitée, cette nouvelle Borea cherche ainsi à concilier le charme des grandes enceintes d'autrefois avec les exigences de la Hi-Fi moderne. Reste à vérifier à l'écoute si son imposant haut-parleur de 21 cm tient ses promesses en matière d'extension dans le grave et d'équilibre sonore.

articles.title: Google Pay lands in Nigeria via Mastercard and Interswitch
articles.text:
Mastercard, the global payments giant, and Interswitch, a Nigerian payments infrastructure provider, have partnered to bring Google Pay to eligible Mastercard cardholders in Nigeria, allowing customers to make contactless payments using Android smartphones.
The product will allow users to add supported bank cards to Google Wallet, Google’s digital wallet application, and pay at compatible terminals without presenting physical cards.
The integration uses Mastercard’s tokenisation technology, which replaces sensitive card information with unique digital credentials to protect customer details during transactions. Interswitch provides the infrastructure connecting participating banks to the tokenisation and payment processing systems.
The launch comes as Nigeria’s digital payments market continues to expand.
According to the Nigeria Inter-Bank Settlement System (NIBSS), the country’s payments switch, instant payment transactions grew to ₦284.9 trillion ($212 billion) in the first quarter of 2025, up 21.5% from ₦234.5 trillion ($174.5 billion) in the previous year.
The growth reflects Nigeria’s increasing reliance on real-time bank transfers, which have become a dominant part of the country’s digital payments ecosystem.
Point-of-sale (PoS) infrastructure has expanded alongside digital transactions. By March 2025, Nigeria had 5.9 million deployed PoS terminals, more than double the number recorded the previous year.
PoS transaction values reached ₦10.51 trillion ($7.8 billion) in the first quarter of 2025, about four times the value recorded in the previous year.
Google Pay’s entry introduces a different payment experience, enabling customers to complete supported purchases by tapping their phones rather than transferring money or using physical cards.
“Our work has helped establish the issuer connectivity, tokenization and payment processing capabilities required to bring ‘tap-to-pay’ and wallet-based payments to Nigerian consumers,” said Akeem Lawal, managing director of payment, switching and processing at Interswitch.
Kari Tukur, Mastercard’s country manager for West Africa, said the collaboration would give eligible customers another way to pay while protecting their card details.
Unlike bank transfers, which require customers to enter account details or initiate payments through banking apps, Google Pay allows users to pay by holding their Android smartphones near compatible point-of-sale (PoS) terminals.
The service uses near-field communication (NFC), a wireless technology that enables devices to exchange payment information over short distances.
Google Pay is not new to Nigeria’s payments ecosystem. Interswitch previously integrated the service into its online payment gateway, enablingbusinesses to accept Google Pay payments.
The latest rollout extends access to locally issued cards, with Google’s list of supported Nigerian payment methods now including eligible Mastercard cards issued by tier-1 banks such as FirstBank, Guaranty Trust Bank, United Bank for Africa (UBA), and Zenith Bank.
Customers need compatible Android devices with NFC technology to make contactless payments.
The launch also comes as Interswitch expands its tokenised payment infrastructure. On October 26, the company announced collaborations with five Nigerian banks—GTBank, Wema Bank, ProvidusUnity Bank, Zenith Bank, and FirstBank—to support tap-to-pay transactions across digital wallets and banking applications.

articles.title: Bruselas plantea un "matiz" al RGPD y abre la puerta a entrenar a la IA con datos obtenidos sin consentimiento
articles.text:
Aunque estemos todo el día con la palabra "IA" en la boca, en Europa hay ciertas aplicaciones y servicios a los que la Unión les había dado con la puerta en las narices. Sin embargo, una propuesta para reformar el RGPD (Reglamento General de Protección de Datos) permitiría que esas empresas entrenen y operen modelos con datos personales sin tener que pedir permiso a cada persona.
Para esto, podrán invocar un 'superpoder' llamado "interés legítimo" y, aunque seguramente algunas Big Tech ya se estén frotando las manos, la propuesta aún no es ley. Veamos de qué va esto.
En corto. El pasado 21 de octubre, un comité llamado Coreper que congrega a embajadores de Estados miembros, acordó la postura con la que el Consejo Europeo negociará con el Parlamento Europeo el Digital Omnibus (un paquete de simplificación de normas digitales). El Consejo publicó un documento de 179 páginas en el que exponen modificaciones sobre ese reglamento europeo de protección de datos, la directiva ePrivacy que regula las cookies, el Reglamento de Datos y la directiva de ciberseguridad NIS2.
Uno de los objetivos de estos cambios (como exponen en el documento y como leemos en IAPP) es agilizar los entrenamientos de modelos de inteligencia artificial permitiendo que las empresas puedan usar datos personales apoyándose en un interés legítimo debido a que la IA se ha convertido en un asunto no sólo tecnológico, sino geopolítico en el que la UE no puede quedarse atrás.
Qué decía la ley hasta ahora. El RGPD no menciona expresamente la IA, pero ofrece en su versión actual las bases legales para tratar datos personales sin consentimiento, entre ellas ese "interés legítimo" que se repite en el documento del Consejo. Una empresa puede usar datos si tiene un interés justificado y no pesan más los derechos de la persona. Eso obliga a ponderar caso por caso, y esa ponderación es el punto de fricción entre las empresas de IA y los defensores de la privacidad.
Un dato personal es la información sobre una persona identificada o identificable y, en el RGPD, se prohíbe tratar datos sensibles (salud, origen étnico o similares) salvo algunas excepciones. Cualquier persona puede oponerse al tratamiento basado en el interés legítimo y hay casos como los de reutilizar datos del usuario para investigación científica que ya se consideran compatibles con la finalidad original de protección de los derechos del usuario. En estos casos, hay que poner medidas para que esos derechos no se vulneren.
Qué quieren que pase. Si el texto del Consejo sale adelante, una empresa podrá desarrollar y operar modelos de IA con datos personales apoyándose en su interés legítimo, o el de un tercero, y sin pedir consentimiento. Conviene aclarar que hoy el RGPD tampoco exige consentimiento cuando hay interés legítimo. La novedad es que esto se escribiría expresamente para la IA (nuevo artículo 88 bis) y se recortan límites. En la página 145, el Consejo tacha salvaguardas que había añadido la Comisión: el derecho de oposición incondicional y la excepción expresa para menores y para leyes que exigen consentimiento.
Además, una nueva excepción permitiría el tratamiento incidental y residual de los datos sensibles expuestos anteriormente durante el desarrollo y el funcionamiento técnico del sistema si la empresa no pretendía recogerlos. Si esos datos se cuelan sin que la empresa quisiera recogerlos, tendría que evitarlos, borrarlos en cuanto los detecte y protegerlos. Esto no cubre los datos que el usuario da directamente, como lo que escribe en un chatbot, ni el uso intencionado de, por ejemplo, voz o imagen.
El Consejo también quiere facilitar la investigación científica, incluida la de empresas privadas con fines comerciales, siempre que sea autónoma e independiente y la empresa justifique en cada caso que lo es y que sus resultados son verificables y transparentes. Y propone que los datos seudonimizados, aquellos en los que se ha separado la identidad de la persona, dejen de ser datos personales para el tercero que los reciba si no puede identificar a nadie. Si puede, siguen sujetos al RGPD.
Qué viene ahora. Aunque ya hemos visto algunos mensajes en Twitter que apuntan que esto es una modificación de la ley, un volantazo europeo o que los gobernantes de la UE han aprobado cambios en el RGPD, no deja de ser una propuesta y queda camino y negociación por delante.
De hecho, falta todo por definir, ya que el Consejo, la Comisión Europea y el Parlamento Europeo (que aún no tiene una postura) tendrán que negociar cualquiera de estos cambios que se plantean y el tiempo tampoco es que sobre. El CE pidió cerrar todos los ómnibus pendientes antes de que acabe este año, y no queda tanto.
Eso sí, no hay que confundir esta reforma planteada con el AI Act, la ley europea de IA, ya que esa va por otras vías.

articles.title: Alex Mestres, divulgador de finanzas, sobre la factura de la luz: “Prioriza el uso del microondas frente al horno. Calentar o cocinar con microondas ahorra entre un 60 % y un 70 % de energía”
articles.text:
Alex Mestres, un divulgador de finanzas personales, explica cómo puede reducirse el gasto en luz en tres consejos. Su vídeo de TikTok describe unos ahorros de hasta un 40 % en la factura de luz, sin explicar cómo llega a ese porcentaje en la descripción del vídeo, publicado el 22 de noviembre de 2024, que arranca con la pregunta “¿Qué haría yo para ahorrarme hasta un 40 % en la factura de luz?”.
En la primera recomendación, el microondas, Mestres habla de priorizar su uso frente al del horno. “Calentar o cocinar con microondas ahorra entre un 60 % y un 70 % de energía en comparación con el horno”, señala la descripción del vídeo.
Los otros dos consejos versan sobre la televisión y los cargadores. Mestres recomienda desactivar el modo de espera de la televisión porque “aunque no lo parezca, este modo consume más de lo que creemos”. “Apaga completamente la TV para ahorrar hasta un 15 % en su consumo”.
En cuanto al tercer consejo, Mestres pide al espectador que desconecte los cargadores de los dispositivos cuando no estén en uso porque “cuando los dejas enchufados, siguen consumiendo energía”.
Lo que dice la guía del IDAE
El ahorro del 60-70 % que menciona Mestres coincide con la Guía Práctica de la Energía (tercera edición de 2010), del Instituto para la Diversificación y Ahorro de la Energía (IDAE), que indica que utilizar el microondas en lugar del horno convencional supone “un ahorro entre el 60 y el 70 % de energía y un ahorro considerable de tiempo”.
El IDAE también enumera métodos de preparación eficientes, en este orden: el microondas, la olla a presión y, por último, el horno. Por ejemplo, un horno eléctrico pequeño de clase D consumiría 1 kWh cada vez que se utilizara. Si se utilizaran los ahorros que propone el IDAE, el microondas consumiría entre 0,3 y 0,4 kWh cada vez que se utilizara.
Por supuesto, no son los mismos platos ni los mismos utensilios. En el modo de espera de la televisión, el 15 % también coincide con lo que el IDAE incluye en su guía: un televisor en modo de espera “puede consumir hasta un 15 % del consumo en condiciones normales de funcionamiento”. Ahora es un régimen diferente el que rige su funcionamiento. Diversas características de la televisión, según si se utilizan determinadas funciones, tienen que reaccionar de forma diferente. Los valores no pueden compararse directamente con los del horno pequeño.
Los límites europeos para la tele y los cargadores
Desde el 1 de marzo de 2021, se aplica un reglamento de diseño ecológico para pantallas de visualización. En este reglamento se indican los límites de potencia absorbida tanto en el modo preparado (espera) como en el modo preparado en red como requisitos; por ejemplo, consumos de 0,50 W o 2,20 W cuando se utiliza el modo de espera o más funciones.
Los modos de espera en la red no pueden superar un consumo de potencia básico de 2 vatios; con las funciones adicionales, esta cifra puede alcanzar hasta un máximo de 7,7 vatios si están activadas todas, entre ellas la de alta disponibilidad de red.
Una televisión que pase todo el año en modo de espera con 0,5 vatios consume unos 4,4 kWh. De ello podría deducirse que lo más importante a tener en cuenta son los ajustes. Así, este reglamento de Diseño Ecológico exige ahora que el modo preparado en red esté desactivado en la configuración de fábrica de los televisores inteligentes. La televisión debe pedir al usuario una confirmación antes de que se active una función que se controle a distancia, y el usuario “deberá poder desactivarla”.
Del mismo modo, en cuanto al consumo de los cargadores, desde el 1 de abril de 2020 se aplica un reglamento europeo de fuentes de alimentación externas: adaptadores de corriente que proporcionan corriente continua a los dispositivos a través de un enchufe.
Su anexo II establece que los adaptadores de corriente continua con una potencia nominal de salida de hasta 49 W deben tener un consumo de energía en el enchufe de no más de 0,10 W cuando no estén alimentando ningún dispositivo (el término técnico es “funcionamiento en vacío”), lo que también equivaldría a menos de 1 kWh al año.
El consejo de Mestres sobre los cargadores es, por tanto, válido, aunque, como mínimo, el consumo eléctrico que ello supone prácticamente se traduce en un ahorro ridículo en la factura de la luz.
Cómo comprobar tu propio consumo
Lo más valioso puede ser comparar las horas de cada hábito con el consumo propio. Datadis, la plataforma común de las distribuidoras, permite explorar el consumo horario, diario, etc., del suministro.
Si se descargan u observan esos datos, se puede ver si las horas en las que se utiliza el horno eléctrico coinciden con los períodos de mayor consumo. En un artículo anterior, en febrero de 2020, explicamos cómo los lectores podían consultar la página web de su distribuidora eléctrica, ya que entonces mostraba su consumo instantáneo (o potencia) en ese momento.

articles.title: Puso a Claude Code, Codex y Google Antigravity a crear una aplicación: esta fue la que mejor programó
articles.text:
Una prueba con tres herramientas de inteligencia artificial (IA) para programar una aplicación de finanzas personales dejó una diferencia en el resultado final. Claude Code ofreció la propuesta más cercana a un producto listo para el uso cotidiano, por delante de OpenAI Codex y Google Antigravity.
Según la prueba hecha por XDA, el encargo incluía un panel de control con registro de gastos, presupuestos, objetivos de ahorro, cuentas, gráficos interactivos y varias páginas operativas.
Los tres recibieron una única instrucción detallada, sin indicaciones posteriores ni correcciones manuales, para medir su capacidad de resolver una tarea de desarrollo con autonomía.
Qué aplicación tuvieron que crear los tres agentes de IA
La prueba se centró en una herramienta para gestionar finanzas personales, en lugar de un proyecto limitado a mostrar una interfaz. La aplicación debía permitir registrar movimientos, organizar presupuestos, visualizar el dinero disponible y seguir metas de ahorro mediante gráficos y datos distribuidos en varias secciones.
Además, la consigna describía el diseño esperado y la estructura general del producto. Se usaron las configuraciones predeterminadas de cada herramienta: Opus 5.5 en Claude Code, Gemini 3.8 en Google Antigravity y GPT-6 Astra en Codex. El objetivo era comprobar cuál necesitaba menos intervención para entregar un desarrollo coherente.
Cómo respondió Codex al pedido inicial
Codex cumplió con las secciones principales solicitadas y propuso una estética basada en un fondo verde tenue, una decisión que acompañaba el tema financiero. El panel incorporó las funciones básicas y presentó una base suficiente para continuar el desarrollo con ajustes posteriores.
La debilidad apareció en el nivel de terminación visual. La tipografía tenía un tamaño reducido en buena parte de la interfaz, lo que afectaba la lectura.
La página de transacciones incluía los elementos necesarios, aunque utilizó iconos genéricos y sin una identidad clara. La impresión general fue la de una aplicación funcional que requería una revisión de diseño antes de su lanzamiento.
Qué mejoró Google Antigravity frente a Codex de OpenAI
Google Antigravity mostró una interfaz más ordenada desde el primer vistazo. El tamaño de los textos, los espacios entre componentes y la presentación de los contenidos dieron al panel una apariencia más próxima a la de una aplicación financiera consolidada. Incorporó un recuadro de bienvenida en la parte superior de la pantalla principal.
Asimismo, la herramienta obtuvo sus mejores resultados en las áreas de metas de ahorro y cuentas. Allí propuso degradados, barras de avance y una distribución que facilitaba la lectura de los objetivos.
Aun así, aparecieron decisiones difíciles de justificar, como dos botones para agregar transacciones en el mismo panel. La página de movimientos conservó iconos en blanco y negro que desentonaban con el resto de la propuesta.
Cómo fue la aplicación financiera creada por Claude Code
Claude Code evitó la mayoría de los problemas detectados en las otras dos aplicaciones. La tipografía mantuvo proporciones consistentes, el espacio entre bloques resultó suficiente y la jerarquía visual permitió identificar con rapidez los datos principales. Cada sección pareció responder a un criterio de diseño común.
La herramienta extendió el uso de gráficos más allá del panel inicial y de la página de análisis. Las áreas de presupuestos y cuentas sumaron visualizaciones y recursos gráficos sin recargar la pantalla.
Los iconos de categorías en la sección de transacciones aportaron una diferencia visible frente a las soluciones más neutras de Codex y Antigravity.
Qué detalles marcaron la distancia entre las tres propuestas de los agentes
La comparación mostró que generar funciones no resuelve por sí solo el desafío de desarrollar una aplicación. Las tres herramientas incluyeron páginas, formularios y componentes acordes con la instrucción, pero la experiencia final dependió de cuestiones menos evidentes: legibilidad, ubicación de los botones, coherencia de los iconos y relación entre datos y elementos gráficos.
En Claude Code, incluso las animaciones tuvieron una ejecución más fluida. Ese aspecto adquiere relevancia en una aplicación de uso frecuente, donde una persona puede consultar o cargar decenas de transacciones.

articles.title: Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
articles.text:
Nvidia launches a promptable transcription model
Nvidia on Wednesday launched Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, its latest multilingual transcription model. The new open-weight model, the company says, ranks first on Hugging Face’s Open ASR open model leaderboard for English, with an average word error rate of 5.33%, and also sits at the top of two speaker-attribution benchmarks.
But what’s maybe even more interesting is that this is a promptable transcription model. Being promptable here means that the user can give the model specific instructions before it listens. Typically, that means setting the context for the transcription by telling the model that a given audio file is a medical discussion in English, for example, and giving it a list of medical terms.
Users can also tell the model to label each speaker or ask it questions about the audio. They can request a verbatim transcript or a cleaned-up version, and tell it how to format numbers, for example.
Nvidia bundles these capabilities, along with translation, into a single checkpoint, which could simplify the work of building applications around them.
Ideally, setting this context reduces the error rate. The trade-off is that these models are much larger than traditional transcription models, which are often under a billion parameters in size. Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a 30B mixture-of-experts model with 4 billion active parameters.
This isn’t a completely new concept, though. We’ve recently seen some other promptable speech-to-text models like Mistral’s Voxtral models and AssemblyAI’s Universal 3 Pro.
Nvidia, though, is able to rival Voxtral’s error rate with far fewer active parameters. On Artificial Analysis’s benchmark, Nemotron scores a 2.81% word error rate, compared with Voxtral Small’s 2.77%, while using about 4 billion active parameters versus 24 billion. That comparison measures accuracy against active parameter counts, though, rather than runtime or memory requirements.
The model can transcribe 40 languages — and translate 31 of those to or from English. Speaker attribution works for 13 of those languages, and it can distinguish between up to eight speaker voices. Audio Q&A was trained in English.
The model handles recordings up to an hour long. It’s built for recorded audio, though, and doesn’t support live streaming.
Developers can serve the model with vLLM or run it locally with NeMo-Speech.cpp. Nvidia says it runs on a single GPU, with supported hardware ranging from Jetson AGX Thor and DGX Spark to Blackwell data-center GPUs.
Since this is an open-weight model (under the OpenMDW-1.1 license), users can fine-tune it to their needs in order to reduce the error rate by using NeMo Speech’s fine-tuning tools, among other tools.
In a medical transcription case study, Nvidia says fine-tuning reduced word error rate on held-out speakers from 22.44% with its best prompt to 12.17%, a 45.8% relative reduction. The complete adaptation workflow took about 14 GPU-hours on a single GB300.
Nvidia is also releasing Granary v2, a reusable data curation pipeline built with NeMo Curator, along with public manifests covering roughly 463,062 hours across 48 languages and 16 source corpora. Developers can run the pipeline on their own recordings to prepare their data for customization. These figures describe the dataset release, not Transcribe’s full training mixture or its sampling weights.

articles.title: MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
articles.text:
MIT scientists build a tiny robot that swims using living muscle cells
- Date:
- October 23, 2026
- Source:
- Massachusetts Institute of Technology
- Summary:
- MIT engineers have built a paper-thin swimming robot powered by living muscle cells that respond to flashes of light, allowing it to swim and steer through water. The breakthrough could pave the way for tiny, self-healing biological robots capable of exploring fragile environments that ordinary machines cannot safely navigate.
- Share:
A swimming robot does not necessarily need a bulky motor or powerful mechanical parts to move through water. MIT researchers have demonstrated that a single, carefully engineered layer of living muscle cells can generate enough force to propel a tiny robot forward.
The engineers developed an extremely thin swimming robot that uses living muscle tissue to move its fins. Described in a new study published in Advanced Functional Materials, the device has a flexible gel framework roughly the length and width of a stick of gum. The gel forms two fins, each coated with a layer of muscle cells far thinner than a human hair. These cells have been genetically modified to contract when exposed to light.
By directing light onto either fin, the researchers can trigger muscle contractions that make the fin flap and push the robot through water. Adjusting which fin receives light and how frequently it is illuminated allows the team to control both its speed and direction.
In experiments, the remarkably thin robot successfully swam and turned through a simple underwater maze. At maximum speed, it covered approximately four times its body length per minute. Although that is much slower than an Olympic swimmer, who can travel up to 65 body lengths per minute, it is comparable to the swimming pace of a cow shark moving leisurely through the ocean.
"It takes a lot of force to move through water versus air," says study author Ritu Raman, associate professor of mechanical engineering at MIT. "The robot's quite strong, given its size. "
A New Generation of Robots Powered by Living Muscle
The device represents the first demonstration of a very thin, two-dimensional robot that can move from place to place using living muscle tissue.
Most existing biohybrid robots rely on relatively large, three-dimensional structures made from laboratory-grown skeletal muscle. Producing these structures typically requires millions of cells. Raman explains that thinner designs could reduce manufacturing costs while potentially improving movement efficiency.
"Currently, biohybrid robots from our group and others' are built from bulky, 3D chunks of lab-grown skeletal muscle that require millions of cells to fabricate," says Raman, who notes that thinner, less bulky designs such as the team's new bot could be cheaper to build and could move more efficiently. "We believe that biohybrid robots powered by living muscle could one day perform delicate jobs like exploring environments too fragile or unpredictable for conventional hardware, because living tissue is soft, responsive to its surroundings, and can heal itself."
The MIT research team also included first author Maheera Bawa, along with Arielle Berman, Laura Schwendeman, Ferdows Afghah, and Seanbiron Johnson.
From Artificial Muscle to a Swimming Robot
The new swimming robot builds on an earlier achievement by Raman's laboratory. Last year, the researchers created an artificial muscle disk inspired by the human iris, demonstrating how a thin layer of living cells could produce precisely controlled movements.
For that project, the engineers patterned a gel disk with grooves extending outward from its center and forming concentric circles. They then placed living muscle cells on the surface, where the cells grew into a thin layer following the patterned channels.
When illuminated, the muscle tissue contracted in different directions, causing the disk to stretch and compress. Its movements resembled the way the iris of the human eye changes shape as the pupil expands or narrows.
The experiment established that researchers could grow extremely thin muscle layers in intricate arrangements and use light to control their movements along multiple directions.
"People hadn't seen this muscle architecture engineered from scratch before," Raman says. "And the cells were moving in multiple directions. But they only moved about 100 microns. From a robotics perspective, their movements were tiny."
For the latest project, the researchers wanted to dramatically increase the amount of movement and force generated by the muscle cells. Their goal was to produce contractions powerful enough to propel a robot through water.
They determined that achieving this would require a better foundation for the living muscle tissue.
The earlier artificial iris had used fibrin, an exceptionally soft gel, as its underlying structure. However, the team found that fibrin could quickly shrink under the forces exerted by contracting muscle cells, limiting the effectiveness of the resulting movement.
To overcome this problem, the engineers investigated three characteristics of the gel foundation: its chemical composition, its stiffness, and the dimensions and geometry of the grooves used to organize muscle growth.
"For engineering any type of tissue, it's known that these are knobs you can tune," Raman says. "And we wanted to optimize all these parameters to support live muscle cells."
Engineering a Stronger Muscle-Powered Robot
Finding the right supporting material required testing gels with different formulations, stiffness levels, and surface patterns.
The researchers compared several groove shapes, including narrow channels with square profiles and longer channels with curved bottoms. They discovered that muscle cells aligned more effectively inside square-shaped grooves.
This alignment was important because muscle cells that grow in the same direction are more likely to merge into fibers. Those fibers can then form stronger muscle tissue that contracts in a coordinated way. The square grooves therefore provided a more effective structure for producing force.
The team also replaced fibrin with gelatin methacrylate (GelMA), a material commonly used to grow and engineer biological tissue.
By adjusting the formulation of GelMA, the researchers produced supporting gels with varying degrees of stiffness. They then examined how muscle cells developed on each surface and measured their ability to generate force.
Stiffer gels produced the best results. On these firmer surfaces, muscle cells grew in better alignment and generated stronger contractions.
The engineers next investigated how thick the gel should be. They determined that a film measuring approximately half a millimeter offered an effective balance. It was sturdy enough to support a single layer of muscle cells while remaining sufficiently lightweight to prevent the contracting cells from detaching from the surface.
The team further improved muscle performance through a form of exercise. Repeated pulses of light stimulated the cells to contract, strengthening the muscle tissue before it was incorporated into the swimming robot.
How Light Makes the Living Robot Swim
With the gel structure optimized and the muscle cells strengthened, the researchers assembled their swimming device.
The finished robot consisted of a thin gel framework divided into two fins. Both sides of the gel were patterned with square-bottomed grooves and covered with living muscle cells. As the cells developed, they fused into organized muscle fibers capable of contracting together.
Each fin could be activated independently using light, giving the researchers a simple way to control the robot's movements.
"You can think of the robot as having two independent muscles," Raman says. "If we shine a light on just one, only that muscle moves. If shining on both, they both flap."
To test the device, the researchers placed it inside a large petri dish filled with water. They then moved a light source by hand, illuminating the fins to guide the robot through a maze positioned inside the dish.
As the muscles contracted, the fins flapped and propelled the robot through the water. By changing the light stimulation, the engineers successfully controlled its movement and helped it navigate the obstacles.
Although the robot demonstrated the ability to swim and steer, its current shape remains relatively simple. The primary objective of the experiment was to establish that an exceptionally thin layer of engineered muscle tissue could generate enough force for swimming.
The researchers now plan to refine the robot's body to improve its speed. Beyond demonstrating a new approach to biohybrid robotics, the technology could eventually be useful for monitoring aquatic environments or operating in locations where conventional rigid machines might cause damage.
"Our next goal is to optimize the body design to enable faster swimming," Raman says. "But even at slow swim speeds, one could imagine a muscle-powered swimmer being used for purposes like environmental monitoring in aquatic environments."
The Office of Naval Research provided partial funding for this research.
