articles.title: airtel-africa-appoints-goriola-bakare-home-broadband-lead
articles.text:
Airtel Africa has appointed Goriola Bakare as Home Broadband Experience Lead for the continent, effective October 1, 2026, after he led Airtel Nigeria’s home broadband business and completed a six-month secondment to Bharti Airtel in India.
The appointment comes as Airtel Africa expands its broadband business beyond traditional mobile data services to capture rising demand for home connectivity.
According to Airtel Africa’s 2026 annual report, the company ended its 2025/26 financial year with 903,000 home broadband customers, an 86% increase from the previous year. Home broadband revenue grew by 119% in constant currency, while average monthly usage reached 195GB per customer.
“In his new role, Bakare will help shape Airtel Africa’s Group Home Broadband experience agenda, working with operating companies to strengthen customer acquisition,” the telco said. The aim is to “improve digital engagement, support customer retention and develop scalable commercial models for broadband growth.”
The figures point to a fast-growing business that is becoming more important to Airtel Africa’s growth strategy. The group is investing in fibre and 5G infrastructure, expanding sales channels and digitising customer onboarding and service delivery to attract and retain subscribers.
Nigeria is part of that expansion. In its Nigeria mobile services report, Airtel Africa said its home broadband business continued to record strong growth during the 2025/26 financial year. The company also reported that smartphone penetration in Nigeria rose to 54.9%, from 49.6% in the previous year.
“The appointment represents a further step in Bakare’s career at Airtel,” said the telecom. “Where he has held senior responsibilities spanning commercial strategy, product development, digital innovation and business performance.”
Bakare’s appointment places him in a position to help translate that growth into a more consistent customer experience across the group’s markets. His responsibilities include identifying commercial practices that can be adapted across operating companies, improving digital customer journeys and supporting a scalable home broadband operating framework.
Before his new role, Bakare served as Acting Director of Home Broadband Business at Airtel Nigeria from October 2024 to March 2026. He oversaw revenue growth, product strategy, customer acquisition and retention, customer lifecycle management and strategic partnerships.
From April to September 2026, he was seconded to Bharti Airtel in India through the company’s Talent Exchange Programme. He worked with senior leaders and cross-functional teams to study the Indian business’s broadband strategies, operating models and customer experience practices, with a view to applying relevant lessons across Airtel Africa’s markets.
Bakare joined Airtel in 2009 after working in financial services, including roles at Skye Bank and Pacific Holdings. He holds a bachelor’s degree in Banking and Finance and an MBA in Strategic Management from Babcock University, Nigeria, and is an alumnus of Airtel Africa’s inaugural India-Africa Global Accelerator Programme.

articles.title: Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
articles.text:
Cambridge scientists create a $10 chip that could put a medical lab on your wrist
- Date:
- October 22, 2026
- Source:
- University of Cambridge
- Summary:
- Cambridge researchers have created a groundbreaking $10 optical sensor that delivers the precision of laboratory equipment in a device small enough for wearable technology. It identified foods, plastics, and medicines with 100% accuracy in tests and demonstrated the ability to monitor blood glucose, alcohol, and other health markers without invasive procedures.
- Share:
A new optical sensor costing just $10 could bring laboratory-level precision to wearable health monitors, potentially allowing people to track blood glucose without needles. The technology could also transform food testing, industrial quality control, and environmental monitoring.
Researchers at the University of Cambridge and GlitterinTech (a start-up founded by the same research group) have developed a new type of optical spectrometer that combines exceptional accuracy with a remarkably small size and low cost. Measuring just centimeters across, the device could be incorporated into portable electronics and wearable health technology. Its potential applications range from monitoring important health markers in real time to identifying materials and detecting changes in chemical composition.
Optical spectrometers work by analyzing light to reveal information about the substances it interacts with. They are essential tools in medicine, manufacturing, chemical testing, and environmental research. However, making these instruments smaller has traditionally meant compromising their performance. Compact spectrometers often have limited measurement ranges, reduced resolution, or lower accuracy, making them better suited to identifying substances than performing precise measurements.
The researchers believe their new design could overcome these limitations. Known as a convolutional spectrometer, it uses a mathematical principle called the convolution theorem to analyze light in a fundamentally different way. According to the team, this approach delivers performance that surpasses existing types of spectrometers in several key areas, including designs based on light dispersion, Fourier transforms, and computational reconstruction.
A New Way to Analyze Light With Extraordinary Precision
Traditional spectrometers generally separate incoming light into its component wavelengths or use complex calculations to reconstruct its spectrum. The new device takes another approach by performing a mathematical operation called convolution directly on the incoming light.
To accomplish this, the researchers arranged optical components with repeating spectral responses in a sequence. These components can include unbalanced Mach-Zehnder interferometers or micro-ring resonators. By adjusting them in proportion to one another, the system can shift its response to different wavelengths in a controlled, linear fashion. Fast Fourier transforms are then used to accurately recover the light spectrum.
"The key insight was to go back to the mathematics and ask whether there was a fundamentally cleaner way to retrieve spectra," said Dr. Chunhui Yao, a lead author of the study. "By using the convolution theorem directly in the optical domain, we avoid many of the limitations that have held miniaturized spectrometers back. This gives us high precision, strong noise tolerance, and very low computational overhead, all in a compact and low-cost system."
The researchers built the spectrometer using a silicon nitride photonic platform and integrated it with onboard electronics. It operates across a broad range of near-infrared wavelengths (1200-1700 nm) and can collect and process measurements in less than a second.
Another important advantage is its ability to expand its measurement capabilities without major hardware changes. Because the system uses repeating optical patterns, its spectral bandwidth can theoretically be extended almost without limit. Adding more optical components in sequence can also increase its resolution exponentially.
A $10 Sensor That Could Transform Food Testing and Healthcare
To evaluate the device outside purely theoretical measurements, the researchers tested it on a variety of materials and substances. The results demonstrated its potential for applications that normally depend on larger, more expensive laboratory instruments.
When used to identify plastics, pharmaceuticals, coffee, flour, and tea, the spectrometer achieved a 100% classification success rate in the reported tests. It also measured concentrations in water-based and organic solutions with accuracies of approximately 0.01%, exceeding the performance of commercial benchtop spectrometers in those experiments.
The healthcare demonstrations were particularly promising. Under conditions designed to reflect real physiological environments, the device accurately measured several human biomarkers, including skin moisture, blood alcohol, blood lactate, and blood glucose.
The researchers also demonstrated noninvasive glucose tracking over an extended period in one participant. Although further testing would be needed before the technology could become a practical medical product, the finding suggests a possible route toward monitoring blood sugar without repeatedly piercing the skin.
"These biomedical demonstrations are particularly exciting," said Prof. Qixiang Cheng, who led the project. "What makes this work stand out is not just performance in the lab, but technical readiness. Dr. Chunhui Yao's contribution was crucial in translating a mathematical concept into a fully packaged, robust system that operates reliably across temperature extremes and real-world conditions. That combination is what opens the door to practical deployment."
The sensor also demonstrated impressive resistance to temperature changes. It continued operating reliably between -20°C and 80°C, an unusually wide temperature range for a miniature spectrometer. This durability could be especially valuable for wearable devices, factory equipment, and sensors operating outdoors.
Why a Simpler Design Could Be a Major Breakthrough
The new spectrometer's advantages extend beyond its accuracy, size, and price. Its internal design also reduces the amount of computing power needed to analyze incoming light.
Many existing miniature spectrometers depend on complicated calibration procedures and demanding algorithms to reconstruct spectral information. These methods can become unreliable when measurements contain noise, and they often require substantial processing resources.
The Cambridge team's convolution-based approach avoids much of this complexity. Because the measurements follow a linear mathematical relationship, the system can recover spectra rapidly and consistently while using relatively little computational power.
"This is a beautiful example of how elegant engineering can unlock real impact," said Prof. Richard Penty, who contributed to the photonic system design and integration. "The architecture is simple, scalable, and manufacturable, yet it delivers precision that rivals or exceeds much larger instruments. Dr. Chunhui Yao played a central role in bringing together the photonic design, system integration, and experimental validation that made this possible."
Its relatively simple construction could also make the technology easier to manufacture on a large scale, potentially bringing sophisticated optical measurements to devices where conventional spectrometers would be too bulky or expensive.
Bringing Laboratory-Grade Measurements to Everyday Devices
The researchers envision a future in which accurate optical sensing becomes a routine feature of everyday technology rather than something largely confined to specialized laboratories.
In industrial settings, inexpensive spectrometers could be installed throughout manufacturing facilities to continuously check material composition and product quality. Similar sensors could monitor food freshness, identify substances, and analyze environmental conditions on a much larger scale than is currently practical.
Healthcare could see equally significant changes. Compact sensors might eventually enable wearables to measure hydration levels, detect signs of alcohol intoxication, track biomarkers related to physical fitness, or continuously monitor glucose levels for people managing diabetes.
"Our vision is to make spectrometry as ubiquitous as temperature or motion sensing," added Prof. Qixiang Cheng. "This work shows that high-quality spectral information doesn't have to be confined to the laboratory -- it can be embedded directly into the technologies people use every day."
As photonic technology becomes smaller and more advanced, the convolutional spectrometer provides a promising example of how mathematical insights and practical engineering can make sophisticated scientific instruments simpler, cheaper, and more accessible. By combining high precision with a device that costs around $10, the researchers have opened a potential path toward a new generation of smart sensors capable of measuring the hidden chemistry of our bodies and surroundings.

Materials provided by University of Cambridge. Original written by Michael Shuff. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.

articles.title: Finlandia ordena detener el trabajo en dos centros de datos de Google
articles.text:
Google anunció el 9 de septiembre una inversión de 13.000 millones de euros en Finlandia para el período comprendido entre 2027 y 2028. El 6 de octubre, la Agencia de Licencias y Supervisión (LVV) de Finlandia ordenó a la filial de Google Tuike Finland que detuviera los preparativos que modifican de manera significativa el entorno de dos proyectos de nuevos centros de datos, pues la evaluación de impacto ambiental de estos sigue en curso.
Los lugares afectados son Muhos y Kajaani. La intervención se produjo después de que se cortaran árboles, se retirara la tierra vegetal, se construyeran caminos y zonas de almacenamiento, y se modificaran zanjas. En el proyecto de Muhos, los datos presentados por Tuike indican que la superficie talada y preparada equivale a unas 330 hectáreas. La Asociación Finlandesa para la Conservación de la Naturaleza había pedido detener los preparativos y expresado su preocupación por la tala de áreas que el grupo consideraba que merecía la pena conservar.
La agencia fijó el 23 de octubre como plazo para suspender tales actuaciones y el 14 de octubre como fecha límite para presentar explicaciones. Google reconoció: “No hemos estado a la altura de nuestros altos estándares” y afirmó que había actuado “de buena fe conforme a la ley forestal”. Sostuvo que había realizado estudios sobre la naturaleza, protegido áreas de valor naturalista y anunciado la plantación de árboles en 130 hectáreas en Muhos.
Después de que Google comunicara el 11 de octubre a la LVV que había detenido los preparativos en ambos emplazamientos, añadió que podrían ser necesarios trabajos de estabilización para garantizar la seguridad de las obras y que solicitaría instrucciones y autorización escrita previa para ello.
Qué trabajos pueden continuar y por qué se han detenido los demás
El requerimiento que la LVV dirigió a la empresa permite la planificación, las mediciones, los estudios del suelo y otras tareas de efectos menores y fáciles de revertir. Su prohibición se aplica a la excavación, la voladura, la trituración, el movimiento de tierra y el drenaje del sitio, así como a la tala y la creación de accesos. La LVV vincula el fin de la suspensión a la finalización de la evaluación de impacto ambiental y a que las autoridades dispongan de la conclusión motivada del órgano competente.
Tommi Muilu, jefe del departamento de medio ambiente de la LVV, sostuvo que modificar el terreno antes de completar la evaluación podría socavar las alternativas que deben considerarse y las posibilidades de prevenir daños ambientales. La agencia quiere primero que la empresa resuelva autónomamente la situación; si incumple el requerimiento, contempla medidas coercitivas administrativas que pueden reforzarse con multas.
El proyecto de Kajaani-Otanmäki supone la construcción de ocho edificios de centros de datos en un área de proyecto de unas 405 hectáreas, incluidos generadores de respaldo y equipos de control de la temperatura. En Muhos, la empresa quiere construir nueve edificios de centros de datos sobre una superficie de unas 571 hectáreas. Estos tamaños representan los proyectos completos; no el terreno ya talado. También se estudiará la refrigeración mediante el uso de la aducción y devolución de agua al río Oulujoki, según indica el proyecto de Muhos.
La electricidad tiene sus propias fechas
Los 13.000 millones anunciados incluyen las inversiones en la infraestructura y los contratos necesarios en Hamina, Kajaani, Muhos y Vaala. Google asoció estas inversiones a la demanda que su buscador, Maps y Gemini generan. Para la construcción de 2027 y 2028, la empresa calculó que la inversión mencionada ayudaría a sostener más de 37.000 empleos en el país y aportaría 3.600 millones de euros al producto interior bruto anual. Se trata de las estimaciones de Google para la inversión total; no de puestos permanentes contratados para los dos centros afectados.
El plan incluiría nuevos centros de datos en Kajaani, Muhos y Vaala, así como inversiones en la instalación existente de Hamina. La energía es otra variable que contribuye a la decisión de construir centros de datos en Finlandia. Su clima frío reduce la energía necesaria para refrigerar los servidores, al tiempo que la electricidad de baja emisión de carbono resulta atractiva para empresas como Google.
Google anunció que había firmado un contrato eléctrico con Fortum con una duración de 22 años, ligado a la prolongación de la vida útil de la central nuclear de Loviisa hasta 2050. El acuerdo comenzaría a cubrir una capacidad menor en 2028 y alcanzaría el 50 % de la capacidad de generación de la central entre 2030 y 2049. La electricidad contratada tendría, por tanto, una aplicación gradual. La inversión anunciada en septiembre incluye los centros de datos y el acuerdo nuclear mencionado.
La empresa americana informó además de una batería de 94 megavatios de potencia cerca de Kajaani, prevista para finales de 2027, así como de contratos eólicos que suman 629 megavatios de nueva capacidad contratada en Finlandia. Google se propone explorar la reducción temporal de la demanda de electricidad por parte de sus centros de datos cuando la red esté sometida a presión, basándose en las pruebas que llevó a cabo en la instalación de Hamina durante la crisis energética de 2022 y 2023.
Estos contratos representan su solución para el suministro eléctrico, pero los requisitos relacionados con Muhos y Kajaani hacen referencia a la preparación del terreno antes de que se completen los estudios de impacto ambiental. El 23 de octubre era el plazo límite para detener esos preparativos; el requerimiento no indica una fecha para reanudarlos, sino que exige completar la evaluación de impacto ambiental y que las autoridades dispongan de la conclusión motivada del órgano competente sobre los efectos de los proyectos.
Imágenes | Google, Magnific (KimSunHo)

articles.title: BYD fait éclater un pneu de sa voiture électrique à 140 km/h : la vidéo montre comment elle garde sa trajectoire
articles.text:
BYD fait éclater un pneu de sa voiture électrique à 140 km/h : la vidéo montre comment elle garde sa trajectoire
Un pneu explose à 140 km/h. La petite électrique continue tout droit, sans embardée, jusqu'à l'arrêt complet. En Chine, BYD montre cette scène pour lancer la deuxième génération de la Seagull, la citadine que les Français connaissent sous le nom de Dolphin Surf. La démonstration attire le regard, mais la vraie révolution est sous la carrosserie.
Zhang Zhuo, directeur général des ventes du réseau Ocean de BYD, a publié une vidéo saisissante. Lancée à 140 km/h, une Seagull de deuxième génération, remplaçante de la citadine vendue chez nous sous le nom de Dolphin Surf, subit l'éclatement volontaire d'un pneu, puis reste dans sa voie jusqu'à s'immobiliser. Ce système de stabilisation est de série sur toutes les versions. Elle est vendue en Chine depuis le 20 octobre 2026 à partir de 65 900 yuans, soit environ 8 000 euros.
Le contrôle d'éclatement de pneu gagne les petits prix
Cette démonstration vient du constructeur lui-même, sur un parcours qu'il maîtrise. Elle ne remplace aucun essai indépendant, et BYD ne détaille ni le protocole ni le fonctionnement exact du dispositif.
En Chine, ces mises en scène sont devenues un passage obligé des lancements. Dès janvier 2023, le Yangwang U8, SUV de luxe du groupe, gardait sa ligne après un dégonflage brutal à 120 km/h. Depuis, d'après le média chinois Zhidongxi, cet équipement s'est étendu à des modèles vendus de 80 000 yuans à un million de yuans. La Seagull le fait descendre encore plus bas dans la gamme.
BYD Seagull 2 : plus grande, propulsion et recharge en 5 minutes
La sécurité ne résume pas ce changement de génération. La citadine mesure désormais 4,20 m, soit 42,5 cm de plus, avec un empattement de 2,65 m. Elle accueille cinq passagers au lieu de quatre. Le moteur passe à l'arrière : la Seagull devient une propulsion et gagne un coffre avant de 94 litres. La puissance grimpe de 55 à 95 kW (129 ch), la vitesse de pointe atteint 150 km/h, et une suspension arrière multibras remplace l'essieu à poutre de torsion.
Côté énergie, la batterie Blade de deuxième génération promet 320 ou 420 km en cycle chinois CLTC, nettement plus optimiste que le WLTP. Sur les versions hautes, la recharge Flash fait passer la batterie de 10 à 70 % en cinq minutes, à condition d'utiliser les bornes dédiées de BYD. Un LiDAR est même proposé en option, avec l'aide à la conduite DiPilot 300.
	
Dès aujourd'hui, chaque achat donne droit à douze mois de recharge Flash gratuite, sans limite d'énergie.
En France, la Dolphin Surf actuelle démarre à 19 990 euros. BYD n'a annoncé aucun calendrier européen pour cette nouvelle génération.

articles.title: Discord will make some channels and messages searchable on Google
articles.text:
In context: Discord is widely considered a relatively private communication channel compared to the open web. However, in a bid to revive the usefulness of forums, the company will start making some messages more public in the coming weeks. Server admins should now start seeing new controls to determine which chatrooms and messages can eventually appear in Google search results.
Answers posted after mid-December to questions in discoverable Discord servers can appear in search results on the open web. Usernames and avatars won't appear next to the messages, and admins can already opt out of the new policy.
Most Discord servers will remain relatively private, inaccessible to search engines and anyone without an invite. However, users can already enter certain large servers, called Discoverable servers, without an invite, and Discord aims to make information from and about these servers more visible.
Discoverable servers must have more than 1,000 members, be more than eight weeks old, and meet certain safety and privacy requirements. Discord's website already hosts links to some Discoverable servers, along with brief descriptions of them.
All discoverable servers will have web-accessible description pages starting November 16 unless admins opt out. Admins can limit public access to certain channels, but Discord will automatically generate default descriptions for discoverable servers if admins haven't written their own or adjusted the relevant settings by the deadline. The new controls can be found in Server Settings > Web Presence.
Furthermore, answers to questions posted in public channels will appear in server web pages and search results starting mid-December – if admins and users don't opt out. Channels where messages can go public will be labeled. The new system applies only to questions and answers posted after mid-December, and usernames and avatars will be hidden.
Users can opt out now by heading to User Settings > Data and Privacy. If users change their visibility settings after posting public messages, those messages will still appear on the web and in search results unless deleted. However, new messages will remain private.
The change aims to make troubleshooting solutions and other helpful advice more widely available. Although public forums still exist, many users complain that troubleshooting threads and other informative discussions have migrated to private Discord servers, making them harder to access and putting them at risk if the servers close.

articles.title: Long-Hidden Flaws Patched in EPICS Research Facility Control Software
articles.text:
Four vulnerabilities in EPICS Base could allow attackers to crash processes in control systems used at particle accelerators, fusion experiments and other large research facilities. One flaw could potentially lead to code execution.
CISA disclosed the issues in an advisory published on Tuesday, saying they impact EPICS Base 7.0.10 and earlier. The agency recommends updating to version 7.0.11.
The vulnerabilities were discovered by Cipher, an autonomous security research system made by Causal Security.
EPICS is an open source software toolkit that scientific facilities rely on to build their control systems, and EPICS Base is its central component. According to Causal, ITER’s fusion reactor control system is based on EPICS, and the Advanced Photon Source at Argonne National Laboratory makes heavy use of it.
The most severe of the bugs is CVE-2026-114595 (CVSS score of 9.8), an integer overflow that can occur when network requests are processed. According to CISA, it can lead to a wrongly sized memory allocation, and processing attacker-supplied data afterwards could corrupt memory, trigger DoS, or possibly enable remote code execution.
Exploiting CVE-2026-114596 (CVSS score of 8.2) can cause an out-of-bounds write that leaves the process unstable or causes DoS. CVE-2026-114597 (CVSS score of 7.5) is an out-of-bounds read that could crash the application and leak data from nearby memory, while CVE-2026-114598 (CVSS score of 7.5) is a type confusion issue that can be triggered with malformed network data, leading to DoS.
All four bugs are tied to the handling of Channel Access and pvAccess, the protocols EPICS uses for network communication. Shubham Raj, co-founder of Causal Security, explained to SecurityWeek what an attack would require.
“All four can be triggered without authentication or user interaction. An attacker needs network access to the vulnerable EPICS services, typically on TCP 5064 (Channel Access) or 5075 (pvAccess). This could be through an exposed service or access to a facility’s internal network,” he said.
Attacks could disrupt costly experiments
Regarding the potential operational consequences of the vulnerabilities, Raj explained, “Operationally, this could potentially mean interrupted particle beams, disrupted experiments, lost monitoring data, or expensive shutdowns of critical research equipment (by abusing remote code execution).”
Code execution has not actually been achieved, though. “Cipher demonstrated the attacker-controlled out-of-bounds heap write and process crash using AddressSanitizer,” Raj said. After that write was confirmed, he did not pursue a functional RCE exploit.
The number of internet-facing EPICS deployments is also unknown. Raj said a brief Censys check identified potential candidates based on exposed ports, but none could be verified as EPICS.
No public exploitation of the flaws has been reported to CISA.
The bugs were found in under four hours
According to Causal, Cipher needed roughly 3 hours and 49 minutes to identify the four vulnerabilities. It started with no knowledge of EPICS and was not given attack techniques designed for scientific control systems.
No human directed the first phase of the analysis. Afterward, the system received a single instruction to look more closely at whether the bugs could be exploited.
Cipher’s review of the code history shows the flaws are between approximately 14.5 and 31.5 years old. EPICS maintainers were notified on June 9 and merged patches in July and August.
Earlier this month, Causal’s research also led to disclosures in Grid Protection Alliance’s openPDC and openHistorian, which process power grid measurements, and in the FreeRTOS-Plus-TCP embedded networking stack.
Related: Maritime Coalition Launches Free Vulnerability Database for Ship and Port Systems
Related: Industrial Vendors Check Products for PHP2Shell Vulnerabilities
Related: Accenture, Dragos, SANS Launch $10M Initiative to Defend Small US Utilities

articles.title: What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
articles.text:
What happens when the agent is long gone, but its access key lives on?
Imagine: There’s a line on the credential report that no one on the platform team can explain. An IAM user called research-agent-2 has an access key created 14 months ago that was last used 11 months ago. And it’s still active.
The project it supported closed long ago, and the person who approved it doesn’t even work at the company anymore.
While this example is hypothetical, the lifecycle problem isn’t.
This doesn’t require carelessness. An agent is created for a task, the task ends, and nobody revisits its access. A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab. AWS IAM user access keys don’t expire automatically, so a forgotten key stays valid until somebody disables or deletes it.
“A departing person triggers offboarding; a finished agent just leaves a closed tab.”
OWASP puts improper offboarding first in its 2025 Top 10 for non-human identities, and the remedy reads like this series’ premise: retire what’s no longer needed, and give the rest an accountable owner. The hard part is knowing what exists.
The problem is that attackers move faster than an annual audit ever could. In September 2026, GreyNoise documented an AI-orchestrated campaign against PaperCut servers: the attacker went from an empty workspace to remote code execution at a real victim in under four hours, and once launched, the campaign compromised at least eleven organizations in 26 seconds. That wasn’t an attack using abandoned AWS IAM keys. It shows how quickly exposed access becomes useful once an attacker is in, and why slow inventory and revocation are dangerous.
An agent’s access can outlive its purpose unless someone governs its lifecycle.
The last three articles covered attaching an owner at discovery, reassigning one before a last day, and what happens when the owner is an agent. Credentials add a related problem, with one distinction. An agent’s deployment identity is what authenticates it, or the deployment platform, to a cloud account.
“A forgotten VM costs money; a forgotten credential can grant access.”
A provisioned credential is a persistent key, secret, or token that a deployment creates for some other workload; the two have different owners and revocation procedures. A forgotten VM costs money; a forgotten credential can grant access. The remedy is still a query, a policy, and a clock, each used for the part of the problem it can solve.
1. The query that finds keys no one is using
CloudQuery can sync AWS IAM credential reports into aws_iam_credential_reports when that table is enabled in the source configuration. The report lists up to two access-key slots per user. This query, written for the ClickHouse dialect CloudQuery Platform uses, takes the latest synced row for each report, turns the slots into rows, and returns active IAM user keys that are at least 90 days old and unused for at least 90 days.
SQL
WITH latest_reports AS (
    SELECT
        _cq_platform_id,
        arn,
        `user` AS principal,
        access_key1_active,
        access_key_1_last_rotated,
        access_key_1_last_used_date,
        access_key2_active,
        access_key_2_last_rotated,
        access_key_2_last_used_date
    FROM aws_iam_credential_reports
    ORDER BY _cq_sync_group_id DESC, _cq_sync_time DESC
    LIMIT 1 BY _cq_platform_id
),
keys AS (
    SELECT _cq_platform_id, arn, principal,
           1 AS key_slot,
           access_key1_active AS active,
           access_key_1_last_rotated AS created,
           access_key_1_last_used_date AS last_used
    FROM latest_reports
    UNION ALL
    SELECT _cq_platform_id, arn, principal,
           2 AS key_slot,
           access_key2_active AS active,
           access_key_2_last_rotated AS created,
           access_key_2_last_used_date AS last_used
    FROM latest_reports
)
SELECT _cq_platform_id, arn, principal,
       key_slot, created, last_used
FROM keys
WHERE principal != '<root_account>'
  AND active = true
  AND created < now() - INTERVAL 90 DAY
  AND (
      last_used IS NULL
      OR last_used < now() - INTERVAL 90 DAY
  )
ORDER BY last_used NULLS FIRST, principal, key_slot;
The active flags, access_key1_active and access_key2_active, have no underscore before the digit; the date columns do. On Platform, a table name already points at the latest complete snapshot, so the latest-row clause matters on destinations that keep history, where it can also resurface a user deleted since. 
The 90-day window is a review threshold, not a verdict: quarterly jobs have quiet keys, and a null or placeholder last-used date means investigate, not “never needed.” The report doesn’t say which agent used an account; correlate with audit logs and a named owner. The query skips the root account, whose access keys need a separate, urgent audit; AWS recommends having none.
On PostgreSQL, quote "user" with double quotes, use interval '90 days', and replace LIMIT 1 BY with DISTINCT ON. Here the ARN, which is unique per IAM user, identifies each report:
SQL
WITH latest_reports AS (
    SELECT DISTINCT ON (arn)
           arn, "user" AS principal,
           access_key1_active, access_key_1_last_rotated, access_key_1_last_used_date,
           access_key2_active, access_key_2_last_rotated, access_key_2_last_used_date
    FROM aws_iam_credential_reports
    ORDER BY arn, _cq_sync_time DESC
),
keys AS (
    SELECT arn, principal, 1 AS key_slot,
           access_key1_active AS active,
           access_key_1_last_rotated AS created,
           access_key_1_last_used_date AS last_used
    FROM latest_reports
    UNION ALL
    SELECT arn, principal, 2 AS key_slot,
           access_key2_active AS active,
           access_key_2_last_rotated AS created,
           access_key_2_last_used_date AS last_used
    FROM latest_reports
)
SELECT split_part(arn, ':', 5) AS account_id, arn, principal,
       key_slot, created, last_used
FROM keys
WHERE principal <> '<root_account>'
  AND active
  AND created < now() - interval '90 days'
  AND (last_used IS NULL OR last_used < now() - interval '90 days')
ORDER BY last_used NULLS FIRST, principal, key_slot;
The result is a prioritized review list. Next, the human question matters: who owns this credential, what still depends on it, and when should it stop working?
Other clouds raise the same concern elsewhere. In Entra ID, entraid_serviceprincipals includes credential metadata and entraid_serviceprincipal_owners shows who’s accountable; inspect identifiers and validity dates, not secret values, since Microsoft Graph returns secretText only at creation. In Google Cloud, gcp_iam_service_account_keys can inventory service-account keys if that table is enabled in your sync, but inventory alone doesn’t show use; check Google Cloud’s audit logs.
2. The policy that keeps agents from minting keys
The query cleans up what exists. An env zero approval policy can stop certain new keys at deploy time, but only where env zero governs the deployment: policies are enforced at deploy and destroy, not for credentials created in a console, by an external script, or by an env zero task, and they don’t revoke the identity authenticating a deployment. Cloud-native IAM controls, like an AWS service control policy or GCP’s organization policy for service account keys, and the inventory above still do that work.
Assign the policy to a project and every environment under it, subprojects included, inherits it. It doesn’t need to know whether a person or an agent clicked Deploy; it refuses selected long-lived credential types in Terraform and OpenTofu plans. Prefer federation where you can: env zero supports OIDC-based deployment authentication, and an AWS role issues temporary credentials that expire with the session, though the role itself doesn’t.
package env0
import future.keywords.contains 
import future.keywords.every 
import future.keywords.if 
import future.keywords.in
key_resources := {
	"aws_iam_access_key",
	"aws_iam_user_login_profile",
	"aws_iam_service_specific_credential",
	"aws_iam_signing_certificate",
	"google_service_account_key",
	"azuread_service_principal_password",
	"azuread_application_password",
	"azuread_service_principal_certificate",
	"azuread_application_certificate",
}
# A real Terraform or OpenTofu plan carries format_version, and omits
# resource_changes entirely when there is nothing to change.
tf_plan(p) if {
	is_object(p)
	p.format_version
}
standard_plan if {
	not input.plan.is_run_all
	tf_plan(input.plan)
}
run_all_plan if {
	input.plan.is_run_all == true
	is_object(input.plan.modules)
	count(input.plan.modules) > 0
	every _, m in input.plan.modules {
		tf_plan(m)
	}
}
resource_changes := object.get(input.plan, "resource_changes", []) if standard_plan
resource_changes := [rc |
	some _, m in input.plan.modules
	some rc in object.get(m, "resource_changes", [])
] if run_all_plan
deny contains msg if {
	not standard_plan
	not run_all_plan
	msg := "Unsupported plan format for the credential policy"
}
deny contains msg if {
	some rc in resource_changes
	key_resources[rc.type]
	"create" in rc.change.actions
	msg := sprintf("%s: long-lived credential prohibited", [rc.address])
}
allow if count(deny) == 0
The policy reads a standard Terraform or OpenTofu plan, or the module map from Terragrunt run-all. A plan with no changes can omit resource_changes, so an empty plan counts as valid, while an unrecognized shape is denied rather than silently allowed; attach it only to projects whose templates produce these formats, since Pulumi, CloudFormation, and Kubernetes deployments would all be denied. Replacements include a create action, so they’re caught. The resource list is an example, and the policy can’t see a hardcoded secret or a key generated outside Terraform.
The allow rule matters: with it, anything not denied proceeds without manual approval; without it, a policy that returns nothing defaults to pending, and every deployment waits for a person. Test with the full env zero input wrapper, not bare terraform show -json output, covering key creation, role-only plans, replacements, run-all, missing plan data, and destroys. ENV0_PRINT_POLICY_INPUT=true logs the exact input; ENV0_OPA_VERSION pins the OPA version. The policy runs on env zero’s default OPA (0.46.1) and on 1.x, which is why it uses future.keywords imports instead of import rego.v1.
If an integration genuinely needs a persistent key, don’t just create it in another project. Use a documented exception: a named owner, a specific workload, least privilege, a revocation deadline, secure storage, monitoring, and an approval record. IAM access keys can’t be tagged, so record ownership on the identity and in your credential inventory.
3. Make sure you give every key a finite lifespan
AWS doesn’t give IAM user access keys an expiration date, so the end date has to come from somewhere else. For Terraform-managed credentials, an environment TTL gives you a teardown point: put disposable credentials in the same environment as what they serve and set a TTL. But a TTL isn’t credential expiry.
It starts a destroy, and the key disappears only if Terraform manages it and the destroy succeeds. A failed destroy, a locked environment, a manually created key, or an identity managed elsewhere leaves access behind, so verify revocation instead of trusting the countdown. TTLs can be extended or set to infinite, and TTL limits don’t bind admins. On the Free plan, once an organization passes 250 runs in a month, TTLs are destroyed; wait for the count to reset at the start of the next month (UTC), so a key can outlive its TTL by up to a month.
Govern the trust relationship and permission scope of any OIDC federation, and rotate persistent tokens in the issuing system; destroying infrastructure doesn’t revoke the caller. Terraform-managed access keys also record their secret values in state, so protect the state backend.
For keys outside any environment lifecycle, retire them under control. The credential report doesn’t include key IDs, so look those up, check last-used metadata, confirm the owner and dependency, then deactivate the specific key:
Shell
aws iam list-access-keys \
  --user-name research-agent-2
aws iam get-access-key-last-used \
  --access-key-id <key-id>
aws iam update-access-key \
  --user-name research-agent-2 \
  --access-key-id <key-id> \
  --status Inactive
Deactivation is reversible, but it isn’t harmless: a quarterly batch or disaster-recovery job can fail long after a typical release cycle. Watch for authentication errors through an observation period matched to the workload’s schedule, get owner sign-off, then delete under your change procedure, since it isn’t reversible.
env zero’s Free plan includes custom approval policies and environment TTL, with 250 runs a month and 30 active environments. CloudQuery’s Platform has a free tier, and its CLI syncs to your own Postgres. Sync the credential report, run the query, and count the rows. It’s read-only, so the worst outcome is a list you didn’t want to see.
A credential needs an end date
A resource without an owner costs money until someone notices, and an unowned credential can grant unintended access to whoever finds it.
“An old key doesn’t need to be labeled orphaned for an attacker to use it; it only needs to be valid.”
Agents who finished last quarter’s projects won’t flag their own credentials, and the next agent to encounter one might not belong to your organization. An old key doesn’t need to be labeled orphaned for an attacker to use it; it only needs to be valid.

articles.title: As Merz visits Japan, energy startup Proxima Fusion moves to secure Germany's place in the global fusion race | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Proxima Fusion, a German stellarator fusion company, has today signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) in Japan to strengthen the industrial supply chain behind Germany’s ambition to become a global leader in fusion energy.
The MoU was signed during Chancellor Merz’s visit to Japan with Kyoto Fusioneering, a Japanese fusion technology provider, and marks the cooperation of critical technologies needed to build and operate commercial fusion power plants.
Dr. Francesco Sciortino, co-founder and CEO of Proxima Fusion, said: “The global race to fusion will be won in factories and supply chains. Japan has spent decades building world-class fusion engineering capabilities; Germany has the leading stellarator engineering in the world and knows how to industrialise. In working closely with Kyoto Fusioneering and Fujikura, we are building a new industry together, one that makes both our countries more secure.
“Japanese partners choosing to work with Germany is a direct result of the strong backing fusion enjoys from the German government and the European Union, as well as our determination to apply world-leading technology to the world’s increasing energy demands and climate challenge.”
Today’s news comes off the tail-end of a spectacular couple of years for the Munich-based startup.
EU-Startups has followed Proxima Fusion’s development since its €7 million pre-Seed round in 2023, followed by a €20 million Seed round in 2024 and a €130 million Series A in June 2025, extended by a further €15 million that September. In July 2026, the company secured another €411 million, bringing its reported funding and public grants to more than €650 million and supporting the development of its Alpha demonstration stellarator.
This progression comes amid investment in other European fusion technologies, including fellow Munich-based Marvel Fusion’s €50 million Series B extension in 2025 and Bristol-based Astral Systems’ €26 million Series A in 2026, the latter focused on medical-isotope applications.
Together with Proxima’s latest round, they represent €487 million in investment across 2025–2026, reflecting the varied European approach to fusion power.
Kiyoshi Seko, Representative Director, President and COO, Kyoto Fusioneering, said: “Germany is approaching fusion not only as a future source of energy, but as a pillar of its High-Tech Agenda to build national prosperity through advanced technology. Manufacturing and engineering are at the heart of that vision, and they are also at the heart of what Kyoto Fusioneering does. Through our cooperation with Proxima Fusion, we will bring our state of the art plasma heating.. technologies to one of the most ambitious stellarator programmes in the world, and help turn fusion into a real industry in Germany.“
Founded in 2023, Proxima Fusion is a spin-out from the Max Planck Institute for Plasma Physics. The company is developing commercial fusion power plants based on the QI-HTS stellarator concept. With Alpha, Proxima is developing a net-energy fusion demonstrator targeted for the early 2030s, paving the way for Stellaris, the world’s first commercial stellarator fusion power plant later that decade.
On the other side of the MoU sits Kyoto Fusioneering, a premier fusion technology and integrated systems developer. It delivers technologies and engineering services for plasma heating, tritium fuel cycle, and tritium breeding blanket and thermal cycle systems that are essential to advanced fusion programmes worldwide, regardless of confinement approach.
Under the MoU, the two companies will continue and expand joint work on next-generation gyrotrons for plasma heating and on fuel cycle technologies. Kyoto Fusioneering will also contribute its technologies and engineering expertise to the commercialisation and industrial deployment of fusion energy in Germany, including within the national Fusion Hubs initiative of the German Federal Ministry of Research, Technology and Space’s (BMFTR).
The German federal government has set the goal of building the world’s first fusion power plant in Germany. Turning that ambition into reality depends on secure, industrial-scale supply chains for components that, in many cases, do not yet exist at scale anywhere in the world.
Building on Proxima’s existing partnerships across the supply chain, including for high-temperature superconducting (HTS) magnets, the agreement with Kyoto Fusioneering adds key building blocks of that supply chain: the systems that heat and fuel the plasma.
The agreement brings together Japan’s long standing expertise in fusion engineering with Germany’s world-leading stellarator research and industrial capabilities. It also strengthens industrial ties between the two countries as governments and companies worldwide race to turn fusion science into a new source of firm, dispatchable and clean energy.
The partnership will support Proxima’s roadmap towards Alpha, its demonstration stellarator planned for the early 2030s, and Stellaris, its first commercial fusion power plant.

articles.title: Alberta data centre boom could lead to worker shortage: report | BetaKit
articles.text:
A report from The Information and Communications Technology Council (ICTC) is warning that Alberta’s data centre boom could cause a worker shortage if the Province doesn’t work to increase access to skilled workers and training programs.
The news: ICTC’s report, which was released on Wednesday, outlines several key findings, chief among them that if Alberta were to build 80 percent of its planned data centre capacity in the next 10 years, the province would face a shortage of roughly 5,200 construction and skilled trades workers.
ICTC is a non-partisan, non-profit organization that aims to strengthen Canada’s digital economy and workforce.
From the source: Alberta leads Canada in data centre development, with the province accounting for roughly 90 percent of the country’s planned data centre projects. The 33 proposed projects in development in Alberta would, as of press time, consume around 20,000 megawatts of power, nearly double what the province’s entire grid uses during peak demand.
The context: ICTC’s report was commissioned by the Government of Alberta in 2025 to look into the workforce requirements for the province’s planned data centre buildout. It finds that tinkering with timelines and capacity loads could reduce the shortfall to anywhere between 2,200 and 666 positions. Ultimately, however, it projects that Alberta will need to either attract new workers or invest in expanding training opportunities to meet demand.
BetaKit reached out to Alberta’s Ministry of Jobs and Ministry of Technology to ask if the Province has any plans related to hiring or training, but has yet to receive a response.
Final thought: ICTC’s report touches on an issue that is increasingly salient for Alberta’s business community: attracting skilled workers. In the recent October referendum, the Province included several immigration-related questions that some in Alberta’s tech sector have speculated could stymie attracting new talent to the province.

articles.title: Amazon corta até 250 vagas após lançar novos Kindle e tablets
articles.text:
A Amazon cortou até 250 postos de trabalho em sua divisão de dispositivos e serviços nesta quarta-feira (28), após uma série de lançamentos de produtos, incluindo novos leitores Kindle e tablets. Segundo a Reuters, os cortes atingem principalmente profissionais de desenvolvimento de software e fazem parte de uma revisão da estrutura da equipe.
A empresa confirmou as demissões após ser procurada pela agência de notícias. Em comunicado, um porta-voz afirmou que a Amazon tomou a “difícil decisão de eliminar um pequeno número de cargos”, sem detalhar quantos funcionários foram afetados.
De acordo com uma pessoa familiarizada com o assunto, ouvida pela Reuters, o número de vagas eliminadas não ultrapassa 250. A empresa justificou a medida como uma forma de operar com mais eficiência e alinhar a equipe ao planejamento de produtos.
Demissões ocorrem após lançamentos de Kindle e tablets
Os cortes acontecem depois de semanas movimentadas para a divisão de dispositivos da Amazon. A companhia apresentou novos leitores eletrônicos Kindle e computadores tablet e, nesta quarta-feira, anunciou também um despertador inteligente e uma moldura digital equipados com a assistente Alexa.
Em mensagem enviada aos funcionários, Cherie Robinson, vice-presidente de recursos humanos da divisão de dispositivos e serviços, afirmou que a empresa havia realizado uma revisão abrangente de sua estrutura e identificado a necessidade de reduzir o quadro de pessoal.
A Amazon não informou quais equipes específicas foram afetadas, nem se algum produto ou projeto será cancelado em consequência das demissões.
Leia mais:

- Amazon lança ferramenta para desafiar domínio da Nvidia em chips de IA
- Amazon já vendeu toda sua capacidade de nuvem até 2027
Amazon já havia cortado quase mil vagas em outubro
A nova rodada de desligamentos ocorre poucas semanas depois de outra redução de pessoal na companhia. No início de outubro, a Amazon eliminou cerca de mil postos de trabalho em sua divisão principal de varejo.
Na ocasião, os cortes atingiram principalmente áreas ligadas à operação comercial da empresa. A nova medida, por sua vez, concentra-se na divisão responsável por dispositivos e serviços.
A Amazon divulgará seus resultados financeiros do terceiro trimestre nesta quinta-feira (29), após o fechamento do mercado. O balanço poderá oferecer mais informações sobre o desempenho da companhia, embora a empresa não tenha relacionado oficialmente os cortes desta quarta-feira aos resultados financeiros.

articles.title: Chrome's AI-powered Autofill can now dig through your Gmail to fill out forms | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Google’s Chrome browser is getting an update that will improve its autofill capabilities using AI. On Wednesday, the company said that Chrome will get an advanced version of autofill that will help users fill out online forms with suggestions pulled from their Gmail.
That means Chrome could suggest things you might need to know, like a flight confirmation number, membership ID, tracking information, order number, address, phone number, or credit card number by referencing your email.
The update is an expansion of Google’s Personal Intelligence, which already allows users to connect their Google Apps to its AI assistant, Gemini, to retrieve certain details and then use them to answer complex questions.
Though seemingly minor, the update could make Chrome easier to use, which could give users another reason to continue to use Google’s browser and stay in its AI ecosystem. It’s reminiscent of one of Apple’s most appreciated features: the ability to automatically detect verification codes sent via text and display them above the keyboard, allowing users to enter them with a single tap.
As with other Personalized Intelligence features, users can decide whether or not to enable enhanced autofill from their Chrome settings. Sensitive data is encrypted, Google notes.
The feature is rolling out to U.S. users on the desktop, and in the iOS and Android apps for Gemini in Chrome.

articles.title: Japan experiments with autonomous AI chainsaw-wielding robots — video shows rail truck-mounted metal humanoid cutting down tree branches
articles.text:
Japan experiments with autonomous AI chainsaw-wielding robots — video shows rail truck-mounted metal humanoid cutting down tree branches
The frightening-looking mech in the demo still has a human operator, for now.
A scary-looking humanoid robot with a chainsaw arm was shown in action on Japan's ANN News recently. The rail truck-mounted mech was being used by Japanese railway firm JR East to clear tree branches that had begun to impede rail tracks. The unnamed heavy machinery robot’s chainsaw and grabber arms are remotely controlled by a human in this instance. However, JR East is broadly integrating AI and robotic technologies across its operations to enhance safety, efficiency, and round-the-clock maintenance.
In the future, this robot could become autonomous with AI-based image analysis for recognizing rail obstructions that need to be addressed. While they’re at it, why not dispose of the wheeled vehicle and add some legs and a jet pack?
JR East is the largest passenger railway operator in Japan. It is famous for operating the northern Shinkansen (bullet train) routes, but also has business interests/revenue from shopping centers, hotels, smart cards, and more. The firm has a reputation for quite aggressive AI adoption, including company-wide AI tools, designing AI programs for disaster recovery, and it is even using drones equipped with AI image analysis for rail infrastructure inspections (PDF).
The source video and report (machine translation) indicate that the chainsaw mech you see has been available to JR East engineers since March, but the TV crew took the opportunity to catch a rare glimpse of this heavy machinery in action. JR East is turning to robots like this due to labor shortages. Apparently, operating a robot like this requires some skill, but so does chainsaw work at height.
There’s also been a recent shift in rail building and maintenance work to the daytime – despite some inconvenience to customers – to the benefit of workers and safety. Perhaps that’s why we now have a video of the chainsaw-wielding truck-mounted robot for the first time.
The combination of labor shortages and advances in robotics and AI makes development of this kind of rail maintenance robot seem very timely. If the metallic humanoid can be made autonomous, it could save a lot of labor and promote safety. What could go wrong?

articles.title: ‘This is such a game-changer’: the Android Kindle app now has handwriting support — and iPads could be getting it next
articles.text:
Amazon has quietly added handwriting support to the Kindle app for Android, giving you one less reason to buy a Kindle Scribe
And iPads could get this soon too
- The Android Kindle app now supports handwriting
- This means you can use a stylus to annotate books
- A support page suggests similar functionality might soon come to Apple devices
One of the big perks of the Kindle Scribe is being able to add handwritten annotations to your books, but it’s a perk that’s no longer exclusive to Amazon’s hardware, as the Kindle app for Android now supports handwritten notes too.
With this update, you can now use a stylus to write directly onto your Kindle books, selecting from different pen styles, colors, and sizes. You can also use this feature to highlight, circle, and underline text.
This could be especially useful for studying, but if you enjoy annotating fiction books, it’s a helpful update there too. It’s not limited to large-screen devices either, with users on Reddit claiming that various standard phones, such as the Samsung Galaxy S24 Ultra, gained access to this feature as well — though it appears to only work on devices that have native stylus support.
An ereader upgrade — with iOS support possibly incoming
Still, as confirmed by some users, that also means you can access this update on some Android-powered ereaders like certain Boox models.
It’s a feature that’s largely been received positively, with comments on Reddit including “nice surprise,” “I was so happy to see this,” “this is awesome,” and “this is such a game changer.”
Right now, this feature is only available on the Android app, but an Amazon support page mentions that Active Canvas (the feature that allows you to write directly on a Kindle book) is also available on supported iOS devices — so perhaps the iPad and iPhone Duo app will get this update soon.

articles.title: Amazon presenta nuevos Echo con Alexa+, incluyendo un despertador inteligente que querrás poner en la mesilla de noche
articles.text:
Aunque la compañía ya presentó el año pasado la nueva gama de productos que probamos en Hipertextual con el Echo Studio y Echo Dot Max y que venían a redefinir el hogar inteligente de la compañía, ahora ha presentado nuevos dispositivos que se suman a los anteriores y que abren un abanico de posibilidades para todos aquellos que buscan llenar el hogar con Echos de nueva generación compatibles con Alexa+.
En total son tres nuevos dispositivos que se suman a los anteriores y que amplían el catálogo de altavoces inteligentes de la compañía para ofrecer un dispositivo en función de las necesidades de cada usuario, todos de nueva generación y preparados para Alexa+, incluyendo el rumoreado Echo con cámara. para dotar de mayor funcionalidades al ecosistema de la compañía.
El primer dispositivo es el nuevo Echo Dot: la compañía renueva su altavoz más pequeño (y más vendido) haciéndolo controlador de hogar digital integrado compatible con Zigbee, Matter y Thread y, por supuesto, compatible con Alexa+. Una funcionalidad interesante es que incluye un extensor wifi eero que añade hasta 93 m² de cobertura si usas una red eero.
Tiene un nuevo chip AZ3 para Alexa+ junto con un cuarto micrófono para las conversaciones con el asistente. Sobre el audio, incluye un altavoz rediseñado que ofrece un 50% más de graves que la generación anterior. ¿Su precio? 104,99 euros y estará disponible en Amazon.
Otro de los dispositivos nuevos de Amazon es el Echo Studio con cámara para el hogar. Es el dispositivo que probamos y el tope de gama de la compañía. Además del sonido de estudio, Dolby Atmos y sonido envolvente, y la red Zigbee, Matter y Thread, suma una cámara integrada de 13 MP para usarla con Alexa+, de forma que puede ver y entender lo que tienes delante para ayudarte en tiempo real.
Sobre la privacidad, tiene un botón específico que desactiva los micrófonos y la cámara siempre, y un LED integrado se enciende cada vez que la cámara transmite imágenes a la nube. Disponible en Amazon por 259,99 euros.
Además de estos dos nuevos modelos, Amazon también ha presentado el Echo Time, un Echo específicamente para la mesita de noche, sin cámara y nada por lo que tengas que preocuparte. Un altavoz inteligente despertador con Alexa que incluye una pantalla táctil circular personalizable y que incluye la tecnología Omnisense, de forma que las alarmas inteligentes te despiertan durante una fase de sueño más ligero, entre 10 y 60 minutos antes de la hora programada. Además, tiene un sistema que reduce la luz azul y se atenúa hasta mostrar solo la hora. Tiene un precio de 214,99 €.

articles.title: Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
articles.text:
Google parent company Alphabet says that its AI investments are leading to a big growth in searches year-over-year, as noted in its Q3 2026 earnings today.
Google says its investments in AI are driving more searches
Google’s year-over-year search query growth rate is ‘the highest it’s been in the last five years.’
“Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries,” CEO Sundar Pichai says in a statement. “In fact, our year-over-year query growth rate is the highest it’s been in the last five years.”
Alphabet’s consolidated revenues for the quarter were $127.6 billion, up 25 percent year-over-year, with its “Google Search & other” revenues up 12 percent year-over-year. Google Cloud revenue was also up 103 percent year-over-year to $30.7 billion. Alphabet also says it passed 150 million YouTube Music and Premium subscribers globally, though that figure includes trials.
The earnings follow a packed quarter for Google, including the announcement of its Gemini 4 Argon frontier model (which it released widely this month); crossing 1 billion monthly users in Gemini; the reveal of the first five Googlebook laptops; a price hike for the Google TV Streamer; renaming NotebookLM to Gemini Notebook; the launch of the Pixel 11 line of smartphones, the new Pixel Watch, and the forthcoming Pixel Tag; and a major shakeup of its top AI leadership that included former DeepMind leader Demis Hassabis stepping into a chair role.

articles.title: Reddit is the latest platform to embrace the 'For You' feed | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Reddit is the latest social platform to adopt the “For You” feed popularized by TikTok. The company announced on Wednesday that users will now see two options when opening the platform: “For You” and “Following.”
The “For You” feed combines posts from communities users have joined with recommendations tailored to their interests. Reddit says the feature will help users discover relevant communities and conversations they might not have otherwise come across. The “Following” feed only displays posts from communities they have joined.
The company says the change is designed to foster connection, participation, and belonging.
Reddit is likely hoping that the redesigned feed experience will nudge users to engage with content beyond the communities they already follow. It also brings Reddit more in line with the recommendation-driven experience that’s become standard across social media, where algorithms play a significant role in shaping what users see.
With the launch, Reddit joins a number of popular platforms that have adopted “For You”-style feeds, including Instagram, X, Threads, and Facebook.
Of course, not everyone will welcome the change, as some users may prefer the more focused feed experience of only seeing posts from communities they’ve joined, rather than having recommended content mixed into their home feed. Some users who encountered the new feed during its initial testing phase have already expressed their frustration with the change.
Reddit says users can switch between feeds and return to the one they last viewed the next time they open the platform.
It’s worth noting that although Reddit has long recommended posts from outside users’ subscribed communities, the new layout gives those recommendations their own feed on the homepage.
“This new feed experience is a first step in helping drive discovery that leads to something novel and relevant – an idea, a connection, a unique perspective, or even a new interest,” the company wrote in a blog post. “A more human internet is not just something you sit back and watch, it is something you find value in and want to participate in.”
The new feed experience is rolling out globally over the next few weeks, the company says.

Agentic solutions for RF design.
								October 28th, 2026 - 
								By: Keysight
								
							
Artificial intelligence is rapidly reshaping electronic design automation, creating new opportunities for RF and microwave engineering teams to improve productivity, preserve expertise, and accelerate innovation. As designs become increasingly complex and experienced engineers become harder to replace, organizations must find practical ways to integrate AI into existing workflows without disrupting proven design processes.
This white paper presents a strategic framework for AI adoption built around three complementary themes: Capture, Orchestrate, and Accelerate. Rather than prescribing a single transformation path, the framework enables organizations to pursue one or all three capabilities in parallel using the engineering tools they already rely on, including Advanced Design System (ADS), RFPro, RF Circuit Simulation Pro (Nexus), and Python. Capture focuses on making engineering knowledge reusable by transforming institutional expertise into accessible, repeatable workflows. Orchestrate introduces intelligent agents that automate routine engineering tasks and enable scalable design processes. Accelerate expands design exploration through machine learning, surrogate models, and measurement-correlated simulation to evaluate more design alternatives in less time.

articles.title: En 9 mois, le champion français du drone, Parrot, fait aussi bien qu'en 2025, avec un seul modèle !
articles.text:
Parrot a publié mercredi un chiffre d’affaires en hausse de 40 % au troisième trimestre 2026. Porté par ses micro-drones ANAFI UKR, le fabricant français s’apprête à dépasser pour la première fois les 100 millions d’euros dans les drones professionnels.
Le chiffre d'affaires de Parrot poursuit son envolée, porté en bonne partie par le micro-drone ANAFI UKR. En neuf mois, le groupe parisien a déjà fait mieux que sur toute l'année 2025, et sa branche drones a enfin trouvé l'équilibre sur un an glissant, comme on l'apprend ce mercredi 28 octobre 2026. Les commandes s'enchaînent pour elle, de la Suède au Canada, tandis que la filiale logicielle Pix4D réinvente discrètement sa façon de vendre, avec de vraies ambitions pour la fin de l'année.
Le micro-drone ANAFI UKR fait décoller les comptes de Parrot
Sur le seul troisième trimestre, Parrot a réalisé 23,7 millions d'euros de chiffre d'affaires, contre 17 millions un an plus tôt. La hausse atteint 40 %, ou 38 % même si l'on gomme l'effet des variations entre devises. Depuis janvier, le compteur affiche 81 millions d'euros (+60 %), soit déjà plus que les 79,8 millions de tout l'exercice 2025. Et il reste encore un trimestre à jouer.
Cette croissance, Parrot la doit entièrement à ses micro-drones professionnels. Ils ont rapporté 16,6 millions d'euros sur le trimestre (+68 %) et 58,7 millions sur neuf mois, plus du double de l'an dernier. Sur cette période, ils pèsent désormais 73 % des ventes du groupe, contre 55 % un an plus tôt.
Après la Finlande et l'OTAN, l'ANAFI UKR a enregistré de nouvelles commandes et livraisons auprès de forces de défense et d'organismes publics en Suède, au Danemark, aux États-Unis, en France et au Canada. Ses usages se diversifient aussi, avec des activités sur des acteurs comme la défense, la sécurité publique et la protection d'infrastructures. Parrot progresse par ailleurs dans les processus de sélection, de qualification et de référencement, notamment en Amérique du Nord et en Europe du Nord. Ce sont autant d'étapes qui lui ouvrent plus facilement les portes des grands programmes d'équipement publics.
Parrot touche du doigt la barre des 100 millions d'euros
L'autre bonne nouvelle, attendue de longue date, est qu'après des années d'investissements, l'activité drones atteint l'équilibre opérationnel sur les douze derniers mois. Autrement dit, ses ventes couvrent désormais ses coûts d'exploitation, même si le troisième trimestre, pris isolément, reste dans le rouge. Sur un marché où les commandes tombent par à-coups, Parrot prévoit plus de 20 millions d'euros de ventes de drones au quatrième trimestre. Cela représenterait une croissance de 20 à 30 % au second semestre, malgré une base de comparaison déjà élevée. Sur l'année, l'activité approcherait alors des 80 millions d'euros, soit plus de 65 % de hausse, et Parrot se dit confiant de la voir atteindre l'équilibre sur l'ensemble de l'exercice.
Sa filiale de modélisation 3D qui porte l'activité « Solutions pour infrastructures essentielles », Pix4D, fait en apparence du surplace, avec 7 millions d'euros au trimestre et 22,1 millions sur neuf mois, stable à taux de change constants. Mais en réalité, elle change de modèle. Les licences achetées une fois pour toutes reculent nettement, au profit d'abonnements qui progressent, notamment en Europe et sur le continent américain, et qui assurent des revenus plus réguliers à l'entreprise.
Ses logiciels de nouvelle génération se vendent désormais mieux que les anciens, et ses outils de modélisation 3D au sol gagnent du terrain. Au total, Parrot devrait atteindre environ 110 millions d'euros de chiffres d'affaires pour l'année 2026. Ce serait une première dans les drones et solutions professionnels, le créneau sur lequel l'ancien roi des kits mains libres a fait le pari de se recentrer. Verdict le 26 mars 2027, avec les résultats annuels.
