articles.title: Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore | Amazon Web Services
articles.text:
Artificial Intelligence
Building an Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore
If you’ve tried to get an agent into production, the model and tool use are not the blocker. The main bottleneck is everything around them: how many teams can build within a secure environment, which team owns each model and tool, how AgentOps and error handling stay inside a pre-defined boundary, and how platform, Workstream, and finance teams see cost and health across accounts. For a Platform team that wants to support many agentic use cases, that’s a platform product to design and operate. In this post, we refer to the team that manages the platform as the Platform team, and to the teams that build on it as Workstream teams. Workstream teams are the domain or product teams that build and own agents on the platform.
Each Workstream team needs a paved road with approved models and tools, short-lived workload identity, isolated runtime and memory, automated evaluation, rollback, telemetry, and cost attribution. These controls need to remain consistent as Workstream teams customize prompts, tools, data access, and application behavior. When every team assembles them, controls drift, shared services become a bottleneck, and ownership is difficult to audit.
In this post, we walk through the architecture and reference implementation of an enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock and Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. We cover the multi-account operating model, the Platform control plane, a repeatable per-Workstream deployment pattern, separate inference and tool gateways, and an evaluation pipeline that gates each agent before promotion to production. By the end, you should be able to deploy a governed Workstream from the companion blueprint, validate its security and lifecycle contracts, and use it as the foundation for your own agentic AI platform in the organization.
Amazon Bedrock AgentCore provides modular services for building, deploying, and operating agents at scale, including runtime, gateway, identity, memory, policy, registry, and evaluations. The Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint, built on AgentCore, adds the surrounding enterprise contracts as deployable infrastructure as code: ownership, account boundaries, software delivery, observability, cost governance, and retirement.
Architectural principles
Before diving into the solution details, it helps to understand the organizational needs that drive the platform architecture. The common challenges we have heard from customers who establish an agent platform fall into these five categories:
- Governed model access: Every untrusted inference request must pass through an approved inference gateway. The gateway applies the organization’s guardrails (for example, Amazon Bedrock Guardrails or a third-party provider), restricts which models and inference AWS Regions each Workstream can use, and enforces per-Workstream rate limits, token quotas, and budgets so that no single team can exhaust shared capacity. It also carries workload identity and emits attribution data.
- Governed tool access: Agents must discover and invoke only approved tools through an authenticated Model Context Protocol (MCP) gateway, with exact targets, least-privilege execution roles, policy decisions, and an auditable owner.
- Delegated delivery: Workstream teams (for example, product teams) need to ship and roll back independently inside pre-approved boundaries, without waiting for the platform team to deploy each application or granting developers a direct infrastructure write path.
- Fleet operations and cost: Several personas need visibility across accounts without gaining write access to team workloads. Agent operations engineers need logs, metrics, traces, and quotas. Workstream owners need cost per agent against their budgets. FinOps and finance teams need chargeback by team or business unit through AWS Cost Explorer and the AWS Cost and Usage Report (CUR). Security and governance leads need evidence of which workload called which model and tool.
- Bounded evidence and lifecycle: Every agent release needs proof at each boundary it touches: 
         
  - Model access: An approved model call succeeds, and a call to an unapproved model or Region is denied.
  - Tool access: A subscribed tool call succeeds, and a call to a tool outside the agent’s subscription is denied with the expected error.
  - Identity: A request from another workstream’s account or identity is rejected.
  - Release: The previous agent runtime version can be restored.
  - Retirement: Teardown removes the agent’s runtime, memory, tool gateway, and tool grants in dependency order, and confirms nothing is left behind.
The blueprint addresses these needs through four connected planes: developer experience, platform control, Workstream execution, and assurance and operations. The unit of scale is the Workstream cell, not a manually configured agent or one shared workload account. The blueprint README documents the responsibilities of each plane in detail. And you will read the main planes: Agentic AI Platform control plane and Repeatable Workstream cell in the later paragraphs.
Operating models and platform components
Enterprises usually adopt one of three operating models for agentic AI:
- Centralized: A single artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) team builds and runs every agent. Governance is consistent, but that team quickly becomes a bottleneck as the number of use cases grows.
- Decentralized: Each business unit builds and operates its own agents. Teams can move quickly, but without shared standards, controls tend to drift, effort gets duplicated, and cost visibility suffers.
- Federated: A central Platform team provides shared, governed services while domain teams retain ownership of their agents, tools, and data. This model balances team autonomy with consistent guardrails and is where most enterprises land.
- For assistance choosing, see the AWS Prescriptive Guidance page on Governance Models.
Following patterns we have observed in customer engagements, the blueprint implements the federated model. The Platform team is the hub, typically a Platform product manager, architect, platform engineers, agent operations engineers, and a security and governance lead. Workstream teams are the spokes, made up of agent developers, a domain tech lead, and AI/ML engineers. An executive sponsor and the CISO sit above both.
In this blueprint, the Platform team owns the definition of each component: templates, versions, policies, and admission. Each Workstream account runs its own instance of the per-team components (Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway), so a failure or rollback stays inside one team’s boundary.
Solution overview
This solution delivers a governed, multi-account Agentic AI Platform that platform teams operate, and workstream teams such as internal product and engineering teams consume through versioned, self-service interfaces.
At enterprise scale, the developer experience plane is a catalog of organization-approved, versioned agent templates. The blueprint ships reference templates for Strands, LangGraph, and CrewAI, but you can use your choice of framework when the template preserves the same inference gateway, tool gateway, identity, policy, evaluation, and delivery contracts. Application teams own prompts, agent logic, tools, and evaluation cases. The Platform team owns the common controls and release requirements.
Out of the four planes, two carry most of the architecture:
- Agentic AI Platform control plane: The Platform account publishes versioned templates and interfaces, operates AWS Agent Registry governance records and shared Inference Gateways, admits models and Guardrails, orchestrates reviewed releases, and aggregates fleet signals. Teams consume these capabilities through code, descriptors, and pipelines rather than administrator sessions or deployment tickets.
- Repeatable Workstream cell: Each product or domain receives an isolated boundary with a team-owned source repository, a Workload pipeline, and three Amazon Bedrock AgentCore capabilities: AgentCore Runtime, actor-scoped AgentCore Memory, and an AgentCore Gateway that uses AWS_IAM authorization and exposes only the approved tool targets. The cell also holds local customer managed AWS KMS keys, tags, alarms, budgets, and a CloudWatch Observability Access Manager (OAM) source link. One cell can deploy, fail, roll back, or retire without coordinating with another team’s release.
Key components
The following diagram illustrates the operating model and governed flow of the solution.
The architecture consists of the following account layers:
- Management and governance foundation. AWS Organizations, AWS IAM Identity Center, preventive policy, audit, retention, and cost policy establish the enterprise boundary. These are logical responsibilities that can map to an existing AWS Control Tower landing zone rather than requiring a duplicate account structure.
- Security, audit, and observability layer. AWS CloudTrail, AWS Config, AWS Security Hub, Amazon GuardDuty, log archive, and an Amazon CloudWatch OAM sink provide independent control-plane evidence and fleet visibility. Central operators can query shared signals without gaining write access to Workstream resources.
- Platform layer of Agentic AI Platform. Separate Platform environments own golden paths, the governance catalog, Guardrails, shared Inference Gateways, exact tool aliases, pipelines, compatibility, quotas, and common operational interfaces. Platform changes are tested against representative cells before wider rollout.
- Workstream fleet layer. Each product, domain, or regulated boundary receives one or more nonproduction and production cells. Teams own Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, tools, data, prompts, evaluation cases, application incidents, and service-level objectives (SLOs). The same baseline can be repeated across many cells while preserving account-level isolation.
Solution walkthrough
The following sections trace the key design decisions: account topology, preventive and detective controls, the AgentCore execution path, and the delivery pipeline.
Account topology and organizational units
The blueprint defines logical account roles that separate enterprise governance, shared Platform services, and team-owned execution:
| Role | Landing-zone placement | Purpose | 
| Management foundation | Root / Security and Management | Organizations, Identity Center, preventive policy, audit, retention, and cost policy | 
| Security and log archive | Security | CloudTrail, AWS Config, Security Hub, GuardDuty, and retained audit data | 
| Observability | Security or Operations | CloudWatch OAM sink and fleet logs, metrics, traces, and cost views | 
| Agentic AI Platform | Agent Platform | Golden paths, AWS Agent Registry, Guardrails, Inference Gateways, pipelines, and fleet controls | 
| Workstream cell | Agent Workstreams | Team-owned Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, tools, data, evaluation, and application SLOs | 
| Additional Workstream cells | Agent Workstreams | Repeat the same baseline per product, domain, environment, or regulated boundary | 
This topology integrates into an existing landing zone, a pre-configured, secure, and scalable multi-account AWS environment, where the Management, Platform, and Workstream labels describe responsibilities rather than a fixed three-account estate. An organization can operate multiple validated Platform environments and many Workstream account pairs. Start with one representative cell and prove onboarding, production promotion, rollback, centralized observability, and zero-residual retirement before repeating the baseline.
Service control policies
Service control policies constrain the maximum permissions available to Platform and Workstream accounts. They complement, rather than replace, IAM, gateway authorization, Guardrails, resource policies, network controls, and pipeline evidence. The blueprint renders and reviews the effective policies for the exact account and Region instead of relying on source-code intent alone.
- Model and Region admission: Organization policy and Gateway execution roles restrict inference to approved models and the supported Region. Adding a model or Region requires service availability, residency, IAM, quality, cost, rollback, observability, and denial validation.
- Guardrail and inference enforcement: Agents do not call model providers directly. Inference crosses the governed gateway, where the stage Guardrail and model allow-list are applied.
- Pipeline-only Workstream mutation: Workstream teams open pull requests and use the Workload pipeline. Direct developer deployment into Workstream accounts is outside the supported operating model, which keeps the reviewed release and evidence path non-bypassable.
- Registry and Gateway governance: Workstream Gateway synthesis fails when a subscribed Registry record is missing, changed, or not approved.
- Scoped deployment roles: Bootstrap policies are generated per account and Region, validated with AWS Identity and Access Management Access (IAM) Analyzer, and checked through effective-policy simulation. Administrator access is reserved for initial setup rather than routine pipeline execution.
- Separation of duties and adversarial proof: Platform controls model, Guardrail, Registry, and shared-service admission. Workstream teams control application behavior. Every denied path is paired with an authorized positive call and a mutation that proves the intended control caused the denial.
An administrator inside a Workstream account can’t create a supported fast path around these controls. New or changed organization policies need a sandbox or representative-cell soak, exact allow and deny tests, and a rollback plan before broad attachment.
CI/CD pipeline with evaluation gates
The blueprint uses reviewed Platform and Workload pipelines to enforce the following promotion sequence:
- Source and review: A pull request establishes the immutable source revision. The pipeline pins the intended branch so an unmerged change can’t silently build the repository default branch.
- Build and synth: The pipeline compiles code, runs tests and linting, creates the agent manifest, scans the digest-bound image, validates policies, resolves approved Registry descriptors, and inspects synthesized AWS CloudFormation and cdk-nag output.
- Stable roles and permission handoff: The Workload pipeline creates stable Workstream roles and pauses. The Platform pipeline grants exact tool aliases to the exact Gateway role, live policies are verified, and only then does the Workload pipeline continue.
- Deploy to nonproduction: The pipeline deploys Runtime, Memory, Tool Gateway, observability, alarms, budgets, tags, and application resources into the cell’s nonproduction boundary.
- Evaluate the deployed agent: The gate invokes the real Runtime and measures regression, quality, tool success, refusal behavior, first-token latency, and cost. Every authorized call is paired with an adversarial twin: the gate calls an approved model and confirms success, then calls an unapproved model and confirms the denial. The same pattern applies to tools, cross-account identity, and throttling. If an expected denial is missing, the gate fails the build.
- Human approval: A reviewer examines the deployed evidence, known limitations, and residual risk. A generic green build is not enough when a required probe, resource, or expected denial is missing.
- Promote, observe, and roll back: Production promotion uses the reviewed revision and continuity checks. Runtime sessions are sampled through update, cancellation, rollback, restore, and re-run so the pipeline proves both the forward path and recovery path.
No Workstream deployment step has a manual fast track. The Platform team owns the release contract, but Workstream teams operate their own pipeline instances and deployment cadence. Retirement follows a strict dependency order: Platform alias grants are revoked first, then Workstream Gateway and tool roles, then Runtime, Memory, and application resources. Each step is verified before proceeding, and a final inventory confirms zero residual resources remain.
Security and governance
The blueprint implements defense in depth through reinforcing identity, policy, delivery, data, and evidence controls:
- Identity and trust boundaries: AgentCore Identity, a capability of Amazon Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon Cognito provide short-lived inference credentials. AWS_IAM and SigV4 authenticate tool traffic. Exact Runtime and Gateway roles, issuer and audience checks, account and Region context, and scoped bootstrap trust limit each principal to its intended path.
- Model safety and admission: Inference flows through the governed gateway described in the Solution overview, applying Guardrails and model allow-lists before every call.
- Tool authorization: The Tool Gateway invokes only Registry-approved aliases, as detailed in the Solution overview. Cedar policies provide authorization, with a retained AWS Lambda wrapper for defense in depth.
- Tenant data protection: Workstream accounts isolate application state. AgentCore memory uses actor-scoped namespaces and customer-managed KMS keys. Tools and application data remain team-owned, and retention, deletion, and access policies are explicit rather than inherited from a shared mutable workload account.
- Software supply chain and release: Reviewed source, manifest hashing, reproducible builds, digest-bound image scanning, policy validation, cdk-nag checks, deployed-runtime evaluation, human approval, rollback, and dependency-ordered teardown form one release contract. A missing check fails closed.
- Audit, observability, and cost governance: CloudTrail and retained control-plane data corroborate pipeline evidence. OAM shares logs, metrics, and traces with central operators. Standard allocation tags, budgets, quotas, and AWS Cost and Usage Report reconciliation assign ownership without giving the agent permission to rewrite its own attribution.
The repository is a reference implementation. Developers can adjust it to address their needs. The deployment and available features are based on the eu-west-1 (Ireland) Region. A substituted component, another Region, or a wider organizational rollout requires its own availability, security, load, rollback, observability, and teardown evidence.
Conclusion
In this post, we walked through an enterprise Agentic AI Platform built on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore. The architecture separates a centrally governed Platform control plane from repeatable, team-owned Workstream cells, with distinct inference and tool gateways, and production promotion gated by deployed-runtime evaluation.
The companion repository includes a blueprint that validates these controls end to end, from pipeline gates and adversarial boundary tests through zero-residual teardown. The support claim stops at that tested boundary.
To get started, deploy one representative Workstream cell from the companion repository, prove its full lifecycle, and then automate additional cells from the same versioned baseline.
Related resources:
- Enterprise Agentic AI Platform Blueprint on GitHub
- Enterprise multi-account architecture for running agentic AI in production on AWS (Prescriptive Guidance)
- Building an Enterprise Agentic AI Platform on Amazon Bedrock AgentCore Workshop
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore documentation

articles.title: KI-Simulation in Echtzeit: So funktioniert Googles neues Weltmodell Genie 4
articles.text:
KI-Simulation in Echtzeit: So funktioniert Googles neues Weltmodell Genie 4
Google Deepmind hat sein neues Weltmodell Genie 4 als Research-Preview veröffentlicht. Laut einem Beitrag des Unternehmens soll es die bisher fotorealistischsten und interaktivsten Welten generieren können. Nutzer:innen haben die Möglichkeit, während der Simulation Eingaben zu machen, um die Szene in Echtzeit zu verändern. Google beschreibt das Modell als „von Haus aus multimodal“: Es kann neben Videos auch passende Musik, Umgebungsgeräusche und Dialoge erstellen.
Google will der Konkurrenz voraus sein
Ein Weltmodell ist ein KI-System, das weiß, wie eine Umgebung funktioniert. Dafür lernt es, welche Objekte, Zusammenhänge und möglichen Zukünfte es gibt. So kann es die Folgen bestimmter Handlungen vorab simulieren, anstatt nur auf Basis von Beobachtungen das nächste Wort oder Bild zu erzeugen. Weltmodelle spielen besonders dort eine Rolle, wo Technologie autonom handeln muss, also beispielsweise bei selbstfahrenden Autos, Robotik oder der Simulation von Wetterereignissen. Sie ermöglichen es, Risiken virtuell durchzuspielen, bevor sie auf die echte Welt übertragen werden.
Laut Techcrunch ist die Branche für Weltmodelle derzeit dabei, sich zu konsolidieren. Bisher gab es einige gut finanzierte Startups, die sich auf diesen Bereich konzentrierten. Diese werden zunehmend aufgekauft oder von großen Konzernen überholt. Die Veröffentlichung von Genie 4 könnte demnach Googles Versuch sein, in diesem hart umkämpften Feld die Nase vorn zu behalten. Laut Angaben des Unternehmens kann das neue Modell eine konsistente Szene bis zu zwei Minuten lang aufrechterhalten. Das ist doppelt so lange wie das Vorgängermodell. Zudem bietet Genie 4 eine verbesserte Physik sowie menschenähnlichere Charaktere.
Alles ist möglich: So funktioniert Genie 4
Gemini, Googles KI-Modell, ist jetzt enger in Genie 4 integriert und fungiert als eine Art KI‑Regisseur. Es plant Schritte und überprüft Einzelbilder, während Genie die visuellen Elemente erstellt. „Gemini Omni verankert die Simulationen in einem realistischen Erscheinungsbild und Verhalten, während andere Gemini-Modelle die komplexen Schlussfolgerungen liefern, die erforderlich sind, um die Kohärenz und Kontinuität einer Simulation aufrechtzuerhalten”, heißt es im Beitrag von Google Deepmind. „Auf dieser Grundlage können Sie ein Ereignis in Gang setzen und Genie 4 simuliert, was als Nächstes geschieht: Wie die Welt reagiert, wie sie klingt und wie sich die Menschen darin bewegen, reagieren und sprechen.“
In einem Video zeigt das Labor, wie sich Videos in Echtzeit anpassen lassen. Nutzer:innen verändern die Simulation per natürlicher Sprache. So können sie beispielsweise das Wetter ändern oder ein neues Objekt hinzufügen. Zwischen den Eingaben überwacht und steuert Gemini die Szene, damit sich die Welt nahtlos weiterentwickelt. Laut dem Unternehmen setzt Genie 4 dabei neue Maßstäbe für den Realismus in der interaktiven Echtzeit-Simulation. Dank eines fortgeschrittenen physikalischen Verständnisses könne es realistische Szenarien wie Aerodynamik und Kollisionen simulieren. Google Deepmind erklärt zudem, dass das Verstehen und Simulieren der Welt ein entscheidender Aspekt bei der Entwicklung einer AGI sei.
Nur für ausgewählte Tester:innen verfügbar
Bei der Entwicklung von Genie 4 hat Google eigenen Angaben zufolge mit Tester:innen aus den Bereichen Journalismus, Bildung, Gaming und Ingenieurwesen zusammengearbeitet. Ziel war es, zu verstehen, wie interaktive Weltmodelle reale Arbeitsabläufe unterstützen können. Als kommerzielle Anwendungsfälle nennt das Unternehmen interaktives Lernen und Robotik. Genie 4 ist vorerst allerdings nur für „vertrauenswürdige Tester:innen“ verfügbar. In den kommenden Wochen sollen Abonnent:innen von Google AI Ultra, Early-Access-Partner der Gemini-API und von Google AI Studio sowie Nutzer:innen von Project Genie folgen. Interessierte können sich schon jetzt für eine Warteliste eintragen.

articles.title: El Niño pourrait provoquer une nouvelle flambée des concentrations de CO2, alerte l'OMM
articles.text:
La Nasa a prévenu, nous nous dirigeons vraisemblablement vers un épisode d’El Niño « historique » dans l’océan Pacifique. Le phénomène est officiellement de retour depuis l’été, et selon l’Organisation météorologique mondiale (OMM), El Niño va se maintenir jusqu’en février 2027. Cet épisode s’annonce particulièrement intense. Une étude publiée cet été concluait même qu’El Niño est plus puissant qu’à aucun moment depuis 1 000 ans.
Une « nouvelle flambée » des gaz à effet de serre à craindre à cause d’El Niño
Ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, l’OMM a de nouveau attiré l’attention sur l’impact potentiel de ce phénomène, en lien avec un autre triste record planétaire. « Les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre ont atteint de nouveaux records, scellant ainsi une hausse des températures à long terme. L’intensification du phénomène El Niño pourrait entraîner une nouvelle flambée de ces concentrations », résume l’organisme des Nations unies sur X.
El Niño est un phénomène climatique naturel. Il se manifeste par des anomalies de températures de surface dans l’océan Pacifique équatorial. Ces températures plus chaudes que la normale peuvent entraîner une cascade d’effets sur la planète. Avec le réchauffement planétaire, ces effets peuvent être encore plus dommageables.
Dioxyde de carbone : 53 % de plus qu’en 1750, un niveau sans précédent
Le dioxyde de carbone est le principal gaz à effet de serre lié aux activités humaines, suivi du méthane en deuxième, et de l’oxyde nitreux en troisième (qu’on appelle aussi protoxyde d’azote).
L’OMM vient de présenter un nouveau rapport portant sur les concentrations de gaz à effet de serre dans l’atmosphère. Ce texte « montre que les concentrations de surface moyennes mondiales de dioxyde de carbone (CO2), de méthane (CH4) et d’oxyde nitreux (N2O) ont atteint des niveaux sans précédent en 2025 ».
En 2025, la concentration moyenne de CO2 a atteint 426,8 ppm (parties par million), contre 377,5 ppm en 2004, année du premier bulletin. Celle du méthane a atteint 1 948 ppb (parties par milliard), et celle du N2O 339,1 ppb. Par rapport aux niveaux préindustriels de 1750, cela représente une hausse de 53 % pour le CO2, de 167 % pour le CH4 et de 26 % pour le N2O.
Ko Barrett, secrétaire générale adjointe de l’OMM, a commenté ces conclusions dans le communiqué de l’organisation : « Une nouvelle année, un nouveau record. Les gaz à effet de serre retiennent une quantité de chaleur sans précédent dans l’atmosphère, ce qui alimente l’intensification des phénomènes météorologiques extrêmes et les risques qui en découlent pour nos économies et nos sociétés. »
Ce bulletin arrive à deux semaines de la COP31, qui se tiendra à Antalya, en Turquie, du 9 au 20 novembre. L’OMM le publie chaque année pour fournir des données scientifiques aux négociateurs de la conférence des Nations unies sur le climat, qui doit cette fois traduire les engagements pris en actions concrètes.
Les puits de carbone terrestres face à El Niño
Le renforcement d’El Niño attendu pour la fin 2026 et le début 2027 inquiète l’OMM, qui craint qu’il fasse encore grimper la concentration de CO2 dans l’atmosphère. « Nous pouvons nous attendre à une nouvelle hausse des concentrations en 2026, en raison de l’utilisation de combustibles fossiles et du développement d’un épisode El Niño de forte intensité, qui aura un impact sur les puits de carbone terrestres, comme cela a été le cas en 2023/2024 », selon Oksana Tarasova, responsable scientifique chargée de coordonner la recherche et la surveillance mondiale des gaz à effet de serre à l’OMM, citée dans le communiqué.
Comme le résume Reuters, El Niño devrait favoriser un temps plus sec, ce qui compliquera l’absorption des émissions par les puits de carbone. Ces puits, à savoir les écosystèmes terrestres (forêts, sols, végétation) et les océans, absorbent environ la moitié du CO2 émis chaque année selon l’OMM, le reste s’accumulant dans l’atmosphère.
Les alertes de l’OMM au sujet d’El Niño se multiplient ces derniers temps. Quelques jours plus tôt, le 21 octobre, Celeste Saulo, secrétaire générale de l’OMM, aux côtés de Tom Fletcher, secrétaire général adjoint de l’ONU aux affaires humanitaires et coordonnateur des secours d’urgence, a prévenu que l’épisode en cours pourrait atteindre une intensité sans précédent, « au point de sortir littéralement hors du cadre des graphiques de contrôle que nous utilisons depuis 40 ans ». Tous deux ont encouragé à prendre des mesures préventives, pour protéger les personnes les plus vulnérables face aux pires conséquences du phénomène (sécheresse, inondations, faim).
Et en France, quel sera l’impact d’El Niño ?
En France, le phénomène El Niño ne devrait pas avoir un impact direct sur la météo. Le phénomène réchauffe la planète entière, avec des réactions en chaîne fortes dans les territoires des tropiques. Il n’est cependant pas responsable de tous les événements qui pourraient advenir ces prochains mois en France métropolitaine. Mais, indirectement, il augmente le risque de vagues de chaleur et de douceur anormale chez nous.
Le lien entre le changement climatique et l’intensité d’El Niño reste débattu. Ce que l’on sait, c’est qu’El Niño peut amplifier les effets du changement climatique. D’où les appels de plus en plus fréquents de l’OMM à se préparer à cet épisode d’El Niño hors norme.
Toutes vos questions sur El Niño, Numerama va les poser à un expert : voici comment participer !
El Niño est un phénomène aux conséquences complexes, dont nous allons de plus en plus entendre parler ces prochaines semaines, à mesure que l’on approchera de son pic d’intensité. Pour debunker le vrai du faux, Numerama reçoit bientôt Éric Guilyardi, océanographe et climatologue au CNRS. Il est spécialiste d’El Niño, et vous allez pouvoir lui poser toutes vos questions dans une grande FAQ que nous diffuserons sur notre chaîne YouTube.

articles.title: Poland’s Autofixer raises €3 million in venture debt to scale its online car parts platform | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Autofixer, a Polish online car parts platform, has raised €3 million in venture debt financing to expand further across Europe, develop its platform and grow its team.
The financing came from Orbit Capital, a growth-stage venture debt and growth equity firm, whose portfolio includes Preply, Booksy, MEWS, Rohlik, among others. The venture debt financing allows Autofixer to access capital without diluting existing shareholders.
“The company’s rapid growth and strong business metrics demonstrate both clear product-market fit and the effectiveness of its business model. At this stage, venture debt is a natural way to support further growth, providing additional capital to scale the business without diluting existing shareholders,” said Wiktor Namysł, General Partner at Orbit Capital.
Autofixer was founded in 2021 by the team behind Renee and born2be, two e-commerce brands that were later consolidated under AZA Group. The group generated approximately €114 million in annual revenue at its peak, and the founders are bringing that expertise to the automotive parts market. The earlier growth was backed by Montis Capital, which invested in the company in both 2023 and 2025.
The premise is simple: buying car parts online is harder than it looks. The 360 million vehicles in Europe require a wide range of components, and even within a single model, parts can differ significantly across production years and trim levels. Another problem being that parts that look alike are not always interchangeable, while the information needed to identify the right component remains scattered across manufacturers and distributors.
Autofixer, as the name clearly implies, fixes this problem by combining vehicle data with parts catalogues, supplier listings, and records of previous part-to-vehicle matches. Autofixer’s platform relies on automation and AI to organise product descriptions and part numbers, helping drivers find components that are compatible with their specific cars.
“For a driver, buying the wrong part means more than returning a product. It means starting the search again and delaying the repair. We want to help drivers make an informed choice before placing an order. We bring together information about their car and the available parts so they can choose the right product without having to search through and compare multiple catalogues themselves,” said Szymon Jezierski, CEO of Autofixer.
The platform is not only designed for vehicle owners but also distributors, who can expand into new European markets without having to build a full e-commerce operation in each country. Autofixer integrates distributor listings and handles customer acquisition, marketing, and customer service.
In the first ten months of 2026, Autofixer processed more than 840k orders and expects to cross one million by the end of the year. The company has generated approximately €41 million in revenue so far this year, with full-year revenue expected to reach around €52 million. Since July, the company has recorded positive monthly EBITDA.
The €3 million will support Autofixer’s continued expansion in Europe, with Czechia as the next market and sales expected to begin within a month. The company also plans to use the fund to improve its platform technology and grow the team.
“The financing from Orbit Capital gives us the resources for our next stage of growth. We will invest in improving the platform, expanding our team and entering more European markets. As sales grow, we want to make the shopping experience more convenient for drivers too,” Jezierski added.
Autofixer plans to build AI-powered tools that guide drivers through the parts-selection process, as well as a companion app designed to support day-to-day car ownership.

articles.title: Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
articles.text:
Microsoft just posted the first quarter of its 2027 fiscal financial results. The software maker made $92.3 billion in revenue and a net income of $33.6 billion during Q1. Revenue is up 19 percent, and net income has increased by 32 percent.
Microsoft reveals strong cloud growth amid financial reporting overhaul
Windows and Xbox revenues have declined during Microsoft’s first quarter of the 2027 financial year.
It’s a new financial year for Microsoft, so the company is changing up how it reports its finances by splitting its businesses into two segments for the first time. Gone are the previous segments: Productivity and Business Processes, Intelligent Cloud, and More Personal Computing. It’s now just Agents and Infra, and Devices and Consumer.
Agents and Infra, which includes businesses like Azure, Microsoft 365 commercial and consumer, and server products, makes up 83 percent ($76.8 billion) of the overall $92.3 billion of Microsoft’s revenue and has increased 25 percent year-over-year. The big changes to Microsoft’s financial reporting also mean we will now see the company disclose Azure revenue on a quarterly basis. Azure contributed $33.17 billion in revenue this quarter, up 48 percent year-over-year.
Devices and Consumer, which includes Windows, Xbox, Surface, and Microsoft’s search and advertising businesses, makes up the remaining 17 percent ($15.5 billion) of Microsoft’s $92.3 billion in revenues this quarter — a decrease of three percent.
Windows OEM and devices revenue is down 22 percent year-over-year, amid a RAMageddon crisis that has seen the overall PC market dropped by 20 percent in the recent quarter. Microsoft blames the revenue drop on the benefit of Windows 10 end of support during the prior year, as well as OEM inventory drawdowns and a weaker PC market.
Microsoft launched Intel- and Qualcomm-powered Surface Pro 12 and Surface Laptop 8 devices just before its new financial year began, and the company even refreshed its smaller Surface Pro and Surface Laptop with Qualcomm’s X2 Plus chips during the quarter. Surface prices are higher than ever thanks to RAMageddon, and the PC market looks like it’s going to go through a very tough time during Microsoft’s 2027 financial year and beyond.
Microsoft CFO Amy Hood said on the company’s earnings call that she expects Windows OEM revenue to decline again next quarter, around “the mid 30s,” and a decline is expected to continue throughout the 2027 financial year.
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella also remarked on the company’s new hybrid AI push for Windows during the earnings call. “We are executing on our vision to bring hybrid intelligence to every desk in every home, making every PC a secure agent box,” said Nadella. “As more capable models run locally, we see an opportunity to make more intelligence effectively unmetered.”
Microsoft and Nvidia unveiled a range of RTX Spark laptops earlier this month, including the Surface Laptop Ultra. The laptops ship with up to 128GB of unified memory, and are capable of running recent frontier models locally.
Over on the Xbox side, hardware revenue has declined once again year-over-year. Xbox hardware revenue is down 14 percent. Xbox content and services, which includes Game Pass, is down 2 percent, too. Microsoft is still not giving an update on Game Pass subscriber numbers, after the company last reported it had 34 million subscribers more than two years ago. Overall Xbox revenue is down 2 percent.
The first quarter of the 2027 financial year for Xbox has been dominated by a “reset” with thousands of layoffs and studios spun off. The layoffs aren’t over yet, with rumors more could arrive in November and January. In a memo earlier this year, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma said “we will return Xbox to player and revenue growth” by the end of fiscal year 2027 (which runs through next June).
The aim, as Sharma puts it, is to “scale what works” so that by fiscal year 2030 Xbox is “halfway to our long-term daily-player goal with sustained double-digit growth in players and engagement and industry leading margins.” Sharma posted on X that Xbox was “making progress, with a lot more work ahead.” Sharma also revealed that PC platform revenue has grown in double digits this quarter, and that “console sales remain constrained by supply, with more demand than consoles available.”
Hood says Xbox hardware revenue will decline again next quarter, but Xbox content and services revenue is expected to increase in the “mid to high single digits.” Sharma says Microsoft is “working to get more consoles into players’ hands, including through our expanded refurbishment program.”
Microsoft’s cloud revenues were really the star of the earnings show again this quarter, a phrase I seem to always write every few months. Microsoft Cloud revenue contributed $63.9 billion towards Microsoft’s revenues this quarter, almost 70 percent. That’s up 30 percent year-over-year, thanks to strong demand for Azure and Microsoft 365 commercial cloud.
Microsoft 365 commercial cloud revenue itself also grew 18 percent, thanks to higher revenue per user and upselling of premium options like Microsoft 365 Copilot, E5, and E7. Microsoft 365 consumer cloud revenue has also grown by 17 percent, driven by growth in revenue per user and subscriber growth of 7 percent.
Nadella also discussed his vision for Microsoft’s own AI models on the company’s earnings call. “We also continue to make rapid progress with our first-party models,” said Nadella. “Our goal is to advance the cost to outcome frontier, which means delivering capabilities comparable to leading models within three to six months of their release at a fraction of the training cost, thereby allowing us to transfer those cost benefits to customers.”
Update, October 28th: Article updated with comments from Microsoft CFO Amy Hood, Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, and Xbox CEO Asha Sharma.

articles.title: Firefox pourra bientôt remplir automatiquement vos formulaires et surveiller vos pages Web
articles.text:
Les fonctionnalités d’IA de Firefox vont s’enrichir de deux nouveautés. Déjà capable de rechercher sur le Web grâce à l’IA, de regrouper automatiquement vos onglets ou encore de rechercher dans votre historique de navigation à l’aide d’instructions en langage naturel, l’assistant de navigation IA Smart Window du navigateur va profiter de deux nouvelles fonctionnalités.
Le remplissage des formulaires assisté par l’IA
La première nouveauté concerne le remplissage des formulaires en ligne. Très bientôt, Smart Window pourra se charger de remplir ceux-ci en prenant en compte le contexte.
Contrairement au système de remplissage automatique déjà en place qui ne gère que les données personnelles enregistrées dans le navigateur (comme votre nom, prénom et adresse), cette fonction s’appuie sur le contexte des autres onglets ouverts pour vous suggérer des réponses.
Concrètement, lorsque vous cliquerez sur un formulaire comportant au moins quatre champs de saisie, une option « remplir à partir de la source » (Fill from source) s’affiche. Vous pourrez choisir les onglets sur lesquels s’appuyer et ainsi vérifier les propositions de remplissage avant de les valider. Mozilla précise que « Smart Window ne soumettra jamais le formulaire à votre place ».
Pour proposer cette fonction qui analyse les champs et extrait les données des onglets, Mozilla s’appuie sur le modèle de Google, Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite. Cela « signifie que les informations provenant de ces pages sont partagées avec le modèle d’IA en vue de leur traitement. », tient toutefois à préciser Mozilla.
Un outil pour surveiller les changements sur les pages Web
L’autre grande nouveauté à venir dans Firefox concerne la surveillance du Web. Comme l’a fait récemment Apple avec Safari sur iOS 27 et macOS 27, vous pourrez prochainement configurer Firefox pour surveiller les modifications apportées sur certaines pages Web. Cela vous permettra, par exemple, d’être alerté d’une baisse de prix sur un article, de la disponibilité d’un produit après une rupture de stock, de la publication d’une nouvelle offre d’emploi, etc.
Pour l’utiliser, il suffira de saisir la commande /watch dans le chat Smart Window et de décrire en langage naturel ce que vous souhaitez surveiller. La fonction, qui s’appuie sur le modèle d’IA Qwen, a toutefois quelques limites. Vous ne pourrez en effet pas surveiller plus de 5 pages web par tâche, avec un maximum de 15 tâches actives en parallèle.
Le module, qui ne fonctionne que lorsque Firefox est ouvert, vous permettra en outre de choisir la fréquence de vérification quotidienne ou hebdomadaire.
Mozilla précise par ailleurs que les tâches seront mises en pause automatiquement passé 60 jours sans changement détecté et qu’elles s’arrêteront automatiquement après 90 jours.
Quid de la disponibilité de ces deux nouveautés ? Mozilla précise que ces nouvelles fonctionnalités ne sont pour l’instant accessibles qu’au sein de la version bêta de Firefox desktop, et qu’elles restent pour l’heure limitées aux seuls utilisateurs anglophones résidant aux États-Unis et au Canada. Si aucune date de disponibilité pour la France n’est à ce jour connue, Mozilla envisage d’étendre leur disponibilité à d’autres marchés dans les mois à venir.

articles.title: Hackers now scanning systems for recently-patched Oracle flaw
articles.text:
Attackers have begun probing the Internet for systems unpatched against a recently disclosed critical Oracle E-Business Suite (EBS) vulnerability.
Discovered in a core component of EBS's Application Object Library and tracked as CVE-2026-101767, this flaw lets unauthenticated threat actors with HTTP network access take over vulnerable systems in low-complexity attacks.
Oracle released security updates to address the issue in its October 2026 Critical Security Patch Update on October 20 and urged customers to patch their systems immediately.
"In some instances, it has been reported that attackers have been successful because targeted customers had failed to apply available Oracle patches," it said. "Oracle therefore strongly recommends that customers remain on actively-supported versions and apply security patches without delay."
While Oracle has not yet tagged CVE-2026-101767 as exploited in the wild, threat intelligence company Defused said on Tuesday that it already spotted threat actors scanning the Internet for vulnerable systems.
"Our Oracle E-Business Suite decoys recorded exploratory exploits against CVE-2026-101767, an unauthenticated SQL injection in EBS's Thin Client Framework servlet that chains to remote code execution, this morning, Oct 27," Defused warned.
Internet threat watchdog Shadowserver now tracks over 670 Internet-exposed Oracle EBS instances, most of them with IP addresses from the United States. However, Shadowserver doesn't indicate how many are honeypots or have already been secured against the CVE-2026-101767 flaw.
Attackers often target Oracle vulnerabilities because they let them breach enterprise systems on the networks of many Fortune 100 corporations, government organizations, and healthcare networks around the world.
For instance, since early August 2025, the Clop extortion gang has exploited another Oracle EBS flaw (CVE-2025-61882) in zero-day attacks targeting high-profile victims like Logitech, GlobalLogic, and the Washington Post, as well as US universities (including Harvard University, the University of Pennsylvania, Dartmouth College, and the University of Phoenix)
More recently, in June, Oracle released emergency mitigations for a critical PeopleSoft Suite zero-day (CVE-2026-35273) that the ShinyHunters extortion gang exploited between May 27 and June 9.
By abusing this flaw, the threat actors gained unauthenticated remote code execution on victims' systems and stole data from many organizations worldwide, including Nottingham University, Nissan, and the National Association of Insurance Commissioners (NAIC).
Since November 2021, CISA has added 46 Oracle security bugs to its list of actively exploited vulnerabilities, 13 of which have also been abused in ransomware attacks.

articles.title: Tandem Oled, 2000 nits : tout savoir sur l'écran ProLed XDR du nouveau MacBook Pro — Frandroid
articles.text:
Apple a dévoilé ce mercredi 28 octobre, dans un communiqué, un MacBook Pro en 14 et 16 pouces. C’est le premier Mac équipé d’un écran OLED, baptisé PROLED XDR. Sur le papier, cette dalle offre deux fois plus de luminosité que l’écran Mini LED des MacBook Pro actuels en usage courant, et un contraste dix fois supérieur. Elle est aussi tactile, une première sur un Mac.
Apple garde pourtant les modèles Mini LED au catalogue, et l’OLED coûte au moins 400 euros de plus à puce égale.
Un écran Tandem Oled sur MacBook Pro
Apple parle d’OLED « tandem ». Comme sur un iPhone, chaque pixel produit sa propre lumière, mais la dalle empile deux couches lumineuses au lieu d’une. Les deux couches se partagent le travail. La dalle peut donc monter plus haut en luminosité sans pousser chaque couche à fond, ce qui limite aussi leur usure. Apple utilise déjà cette technique sur l’iPad Pro depuis mai 2024, et LG Display en a même fait une appellation à part pour ses dalles de moniteurs. Côté Mac, la marque y pense depuis au moins 2019, quand elle négociait avec Samsung Display pour passer ses MacBook Pro à l’OLED.
Apple annonce jusqu’à 2 000 nits, en HDR comme en SDR. Le contraste, c’est-à-dire l’écart entre le noir le plus profond et le blanc le plus lumineux, atteint 10 000 000:1. L’écran garde ProMotion, le rafraîchissement variable d’Apple. Il monte à 120 Hz pour les contenus les plus dynamiques et descend jusqu’à 10 Hz sur une image ou un contenu fixe, afin d’économiser la batterie.
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
Côté couleurs, la dalle couvre l’espace P3, celui des écrans Apple, et désormais l’Adobe RGB, la référence des photographes et de l’impression. Apple revendique aussi plus de 80 % de la norme Rec. 2020, utilisée pour le montage et l’étalonnage de la vidéo HDR, et calibre chaque écran en usine. Grâce à une fonction baptisée Apple Color Matching Function 2026, les couleurs doivent rester identiques à celles d’un iPhone 18 Pro ou du Studio Display XDR, l’écran externe Mini LED lancé en mars. Un traitement antireflet est appliqué de série. L’option nano-texture, qui rend l’écran mat pour réduire encore les reflets, est désormais gravée directement dans le verre.
Le capteur tactile est intégré à la dalle au lieu d’être posé par-dessus, ce qui réduit la latence d’après Apple. L’encoche laisse sa place à une Dynamic Island, comme sur iPhone. Les bordures sont plus fines, et le 16 pouces passe de 16,2 à 16,3 pouces de diagonale (le 14 pouces reste à 14,2 pouces). Une dalle OLED n’a pas besoin de rétroéclairage. Les deux machines perdent donc un demi-millimètre d’épaisseur pour le 14 pouces et près d’un millimètre pour le 16 pouces. Elles s’allègent aussi, à environ 1,4 kg pour le 14 pouces (230 grammes de moins) et 1,8 kg pour le 16 pouces (320 grammes de moins).
Face au Mini LED, l’OLED gagne surtout sur le noir
Les MacBook Pro Mini LED, toujours vendus avec les puces M6, M5 Pro et M5 Max, utilisent une dalle LCD. Leurs pixels ne produisent pas de lumière. Ils filtrent celle d’un rétroéclairage fait de plusieurs milliers de minuscules LED, regroupées en zones qui s’allument ou s’éteignent séparément (le fameux local dimming.
Pourtant, chaque zone couvre des milliers de pixels. Ce qui signifie qu’un curseur blanc ou un sous-titre sur fond noir allume toute sa zone et crée un léger halo autour de lui, qu’on appelle le blooming. L’OLED éteint chaque pixel un par un, et Apple promet un affichage sans halo.
La fiche technique des modèles Mini LED annonce 1 000 nits en SDR, 1 600 nits en pic HDR et un contraste de 1 000 000:1, avec la même fréquence maximale de 120 Hz.
| Caractéristique | PROLED XDR (OLED tandem) | Liquid Retina XDR (Mini LED) | 
|---|---|---|
| Technologie | OLED tandem (2 couches émissives) | IPS + rétroéclairage Mini LED | 
| Luminosité SDR (nits) | 2 000 | 1 000 | 
| Pic HDR (nits) | 2 000 | 1 600 | 
| Rapport de contraste | 10 000 000:1 | 1 000 000:1 | 
| Gamme de couleurs | P3 + Adobe RGB | P3 uniquement | 
| Écran tactile | Oui | Non | 
| Dynamic Island | Oui | Non (encoche) | 
Une luminosité plein écran qu’Apple ne chiffre pas
Selon Apple, le Mini LED tient 1 000 nits en continu sur toute la surface de l’écran, un chiffre qui compte en montage vidéo HDR. Pour l’OLED, Apple ne publie aucune valeur de ce type et parle bien de pic, y compris pour les 2 000 nits en SDR. Or les dalles OLED baissent en général leur luminosité quand une grande partie de l’écran affiche du blanc, pour limiter la chauffe et l’usure des pixels. Il faudra donc des mesures pour savoir ce que la dalle tient sur une page web blanche en plein écran.
Les pixels OLED vieillissent aussi quand ils affichent longtemps les mêmes éléments fixes, et macOS en compte beaucoup, de la barre des menus au Dock. À la longue, ces éléments peuvent laisser une trace visible, ce qu’on appelle le marquage. Apple explique que son moteur d’affichage surveille l’usage de chaque pixel dans le temps pour préserver la qualité d’image. Par contre, la marque ne donne aucun chiffre sur la durée de vie de la dalle.
En France, le MacBook Pro OLED démarre à 3 299 euros en 14 pouces et 3 899 euros en 16 pouces avec la puce M5 Pro. Les modèles Mini LED équivalents, toujours au catalogue, étaient affichés à 2 899 et 3 399 euros juste avant l’annonce, soit 400 euros d’écart sur le 14 pouces et 500 euros sur le 16 pouces. Les précommandes sont ouvertes depuis ce mercredi, et les livraisons commencent le vendredi 6 novembre.

articles.title: Target real-life issues, Gates Foundation urges AI builders
articles.text:
Nigeria’s artificial intelligence (AI) ambitions should be judged by the lives the technology improves. Uche Amaonwu, Director of the Gates Foundation Nigeria Country Office, believes the number of AI products launched should not be the yardstick.
Speaking at Moonshot on Wednesday in Lagos, Amaonwu argued that Nigeria’s next phase of AI development should focus on practical applications in healthcare, education, agriculture, and public services. The opportunity for Gates Foundation, he noted, is to use AI to extend access to knowledge and economic opportunities for people who have historically been left behind by technological advances.
“We need to be clear-eyed between promise and impact,” he said. “The real test is whether people are going to be able to use these AI solutions and tools, whether there is an institution that can sustain those tools over time, and whether we actually see better outcomes from the use of those tools.”
McKinsey & Company, a global management consulting firm, estimates that Gen AI could unlock $61 billion to $103 billion of economic value across sectors in Africa. The Gates Foundation 2026 Goalkeepers report argues that AI could become a great equalizer by expanding access to knowledge and services It however, warns that without deliberate intervention, the technology could instead widen existing inequalities.
Amaonwu identified four areas Nigeria needs to get right to move AI from promising products to widespread adoption. Firstly, he mentioned the foundation on which AI applications will run. Nigeria’s fintech growth, he said, was driven by payments infrastructure, regulation, policy, and institutions capable of adopting technology.
“AI is going to need similar foundations for us to be able to replicate what happened with fintech,” he said. “It’s going to need reliable connectivity, trusted data, and systems that can talk to one another. Without those things, we’ll be institutions where every innovator is going to be trying to solve the same underlying ambition problems in the network.”
He also said Nigeria needs to build AI around its own realities. Amaonwu believes that much of the world’s advanced AI models are developed outside Africa and trained on data that may not adequately reflect the continent’s languages or experiences, which could limit the usefulness of that tool.
Trust is another condition for scale. AI systems will handle sensitive information, making data protection and accountability important in sectors such as healthcare. Amaonwu said these safeguards need to be built into AI from the start.
A more local approach could also determine whether AI is useful beyond the demonstration stage. Amaonwu pointed to Nigerian innovators already working on digital health, agricultural advisory tools, and language capabilities for African contexts. However, he stressed that having a working product is only the beginning.
“The hardest questions in my experience when people develop solutions comes after that solution has been frustrated and it works,” he said.
He explained that The Gates Foundation is putting some of this thinking into practice in Nigeria through its support for the Nigeria AI Building Hub, hosted by Lagos Business School in collaboration with Nigerian ecosystem partners. In September, it committed at least $1 billion over two years to expanding access to AI and AI-enabled solutions, opportunities, and knowledge, with the aim of ensuring the technology helps narrow rather than widen gaps between richer and poorer communities.
Amaonwu urged policymakers, innovators, researchers, and investors to connect their efforts rather than trying to build Nigeria’s AI ecosystem independently.
“AI gives us an opportunity to deliver outcomes,” he said. “It allows us to get there more effectively, more affordably, and at a greater scale. For me, that’s the future that is worth building, and it’s the one that we must build together.”

articles.title: "La IA no va a meterse debajo de las casas para instalar tuberías": en EEUU y Francia los oficios manuales están al alza
articles.text:
En las últimas décadas, el mensaje para millones de jóvenes fue el mismo: estudiar una carrera universitaria era la mejor forma de asegurarse un buen futuro laboral. La irrupción de la inteligencia artificial está empezando a cuestionar esa promesa. En Estados Unidos crecen las matriculaciones en formación técnica y en Francia aparecen profesionales universitarios que abandonan sus oficinas para trabajar con las manos. Hay una razón que resume bien un estudiante de fontanería de Los Ángeles: la IA puede hacer muchas cosas, pero todavía no puede meterse debajo de una casa para instalar tuberías.
La generación del cinturón de herramientas. El Wall Street Journal explicaba que en Estados Unidos ya tiene nombre: toolbelt generation, la generación del cinturón de herramientas. Son jóvenes que apuestan por aprender fontanería, electricidad, carpintería o mecánica como alternativa a la universidad. Según el National Student Clearinghouse, las matriculaciones en programas relacionados con la construcción y la mecánica aumentaron un 30% entre 2022 y 2024, hasta alcanzar cifras récord.
De hecho, en el Los Angeles Trade-Technical College (LATTC), prácticamente todos los programas técnicos de dos años tienen largas listas de espera. El atractivo combina formación asequible, oportunidades laborales y una menor exposición a la automatización mediante IA.
La IA no sabe instalar tuberías. Victor Velasco, de 26 años, contaba al diario Le Monde que estudia fontanería en Los Ángeles porque busca estabilidad profesional. Conoce a un universitario graduado en Humanidades que no encuentra empleo relacionado con sus estudios y ha terminado trabajando en Chipotle. Él, en cambio, aprende un oficio con demanda y aspira a montar su propia empresa.
Cerca de allí, Brandon, también de 26 años, construye estructuras de madera después de abandonar Geología por sus inciertas salidas laborales. Ambos han descubierto una ventaja difícil de replicar con inteligencia artificial: reparar instalaciones, manipular materiales y resolver problemas físicos en entornos reales exige habilidades que todavía resultan complicadas de automatizar.
En Francia están abandonando las oficinas. El fenómeno francés presenta una diferencia interesante: muchos jóvenes llegan a los oficios después de estudiar una carrera y trabajar durante años frente a un ordenador. Apolline Jude, de 24 años, dejó atrás Derecho y Comunicación para convertirse en pastelera cerca de París.
Durante unas prácticas en un despacho de abogados le pidieron redactar artículos utilizando ChatGPT, una experiencia que terminó alejándola de aquella profesión. Ahora cobra unos 1.689 euros netos mensuales por 39 horas semanales, menos de lo que esperaba ganar como abogada. A cambio, asegura haber recuperado la satisfacción de crear algo tangible y disfrutar de su trabajo.
Cuando la IA empieza a vaciar de sentido una profesión. Hermine, de 33 años, explicaba al medio francés que abandonó el diseño gráfico y la comunicación para formarse como mosaísta después de comprobar cómo los algoritmos transformaban su sector. Aina, de 34, pasó una década en el comercio electrónico y llegó a dirigir una unidad de IA antes de crear un taller artesanal en Madagascar que emplea a cinco mujeres.
Jonas, de 29 años, dejó una agencia donde la inteligencia artificial redactaba resúmenes, preparaba presentaciones y aceleraba una carga laboral que llegó al 180% de una jornada. Ahora es profesor y gana 1.800 euros netos mensuales frente a los casi 3.000 anteriores. Qué duda cabe, los tres representan una reacción que va más allá del miedo al desempleo, en la práctica son jóvenes que quieren recuperar el sentido de lo que hacen.
La universidad está perdiendo parte de su atractivo. En Estados Unidos, las matriculaciones universitarias de primer año registraron un ligero descenso en 2025, mientras las instituciones privadas más caras pueden costar unos 40.000 dólares anuales. A ello se suma que aproximadamente el 35% de los estudiantes abandona antes de graduarse, según las cifras citadas en un reportaje de Le Monde.
Aunque un título universitario sigue ofreciendo ventajas económicas a lo largo de la vida laboral, la inversión resulta menos atractiva para quienes temen endeudarse sin encontrar después un empleo cualificado. En el LATTC, los carpinteros pueden empezar ganando unos 45.000 dólares anuales. Sus profesores observan un cambio generacional, ya que donde antes predominaban los trabajadores de treinta o cuarenta años que buscaban reconvertirse, ahora muchos llegan directamente del instituto.
Hasta las grandes tecnológicas necesitan trabajadores manuales. En TikTok e Instagram, la etiqueta TradesVsCollege reúne vídeos de jóvenes que muestran cuánto ganan como electricistas, fontaneros o carpinteros y comparan sus ingresos con el coste de la universidad. La reivindicación de estos oficios también ha entrado en el debate político estadounidense, especialmente entre sectores conservadores críticos con las universidades.
Hay, si se quiere, una paradoja adicional: en junio de 2026, Meta anunció una inversión de 115 millones de dólares para crear America’s Workforce Academy, destinada a formar trabajadores especializados para construir centros de datos. Resulta que la expansión de la propia inteligencia artificial necesita electricistas, técnicos y profesionales de la construcción capaces de levantar y mantener sus infraestructuras.
Un cambio de mentalidad. Una encuesta de LinkedIn y Censuswide publicada en diciembre de 2025 encontró que cerca del 63% de los jóvenes de entre 18 y 28 años prefería una profesión práctica frente a un empleo de oficina, comparado con el 52% del conjunto de encuestados.
Además, el 65% consideraba que los trabajos técnicos y manuales aportaban mayor sentido personal, mientras más del 67% rechazaba pasar su vida laboral frente a una pantalla respondiendo correos electrónicos. La socióloga francesa Anne Jourdain advierte de que estas reconversiones todavía son minoritarias. La IA está acelerando una insatisfacción que ya existía entre las expectativas de los jóvenes y la realidad de muchos empleos.
El futuro puede estar donde menos se esperaba. Los oficios manuales también presentan inconvenientes: esfuerzo físico, posibles lesiones, horarios exigentes y condiciones laborales que no siempre resultan atractivas. Además, tampoco son inmunes a la automatización, ni todas las profesiones universitarias están igualmente amenazadas. Aun así, Francia y Estados Unidos parecen mostrar cómo empieza a cambiar una jerarquía profesional construida durante décadas.
Muchas familias asociaron el progreso con abandonar el trabajo físico y acceder a una oficina. Ahora, mientras las máquinas aprenden a escribir, programar y generar imágenes, algunos jóvenes están descubriendo que una de las habilidades más valiosas del futuro puede ser algo tan antiguo como saber construir una casa, un mueble o reparar una tubería.

articles.title: Nuevos buscadores inteligentes rastrean objetivos a velocidades hipersónicas sin GPS ni señales de radio
articles.text:
OKSI ha presentado cabezas buscadoras de misiles capaces de reconocer y seguir un objetivo sin necesidad de GPS, designación láser ni radio, afirmó la empresa, que cuenta con algoritmos capaces de funcionar tanto a velocidad subsónica como hipersónica.
El comunicado presentó las capacidades anunciadas por el fabricante, sin mencionar ensayos con ningún tipo de misil hipersónico.
Sensores y software de reconocimiento de objetivos
A partir de sensores electroópticos e infrarrojos, con proceso de imagen a bordo, OKSI afirma que puede reconocer y seguir un objetivo tras el lanzamiento, permitiendo al operador utilizar múltiples municiones en contra de uno o varios objetivos sin necesidad de designación externa continua, algo que su director ejecutivo, Chris HolmesParker, describió como “una vía pasiva para fijar el objetivo”.
La empresa afirmó que podía aplicarse a la lucha contra drones, armas de ataque marítimo, fuego indirecto y sistemas de interceptación, y añadió que su diseño modular permite sustituir sensores y ordenadores y actualizar el software por separado. Afirma que la familia de productos está lista para entrar en producción.
Este problema tiene su origen en la guerra electrónica. Este tipo de guerra puede interferir con los sistemas de navegación o las radios de otras armas y plataformas, reduciendo su eficacia. Procesar imágenes de sensores en el propio misil permitiría reducir esa dependencia de señales externas.
Hay que tener en cuenta que reconocer un objeto no es lo mismo que saber dónde se encuentra la plataforma, y que estos dos aspectos forman parte de diferentes módulos, según el folleto del producto de OKSI OMNISCIENCE.
OMNISCIENCE también incluye OMNItarget para la guía terminal y OMNImind para gestionar la misión utilizando lógica de programación condicional. OKSI ofrece estas capacidades en forma de módulos en un contenedor, que podrían utilizarse por separado o combinarse.
La colaboración con Qualcomm y el entorno Ubuntu Linux
La empresa OKSI anunció una colaboración con Qualcomm en 2026. Según el comunicado, el software OMNISCIENCE se ha adaptado al QCS8550 y su entorno se basa en Ubuntu Linux, con herramientas de inteligencia artificial y visión por ordenador open source, mientras que este chip aporta el cálculo y el procesamiento de imágenes necesarios para ejecutar este software de autonomía en dispositivos sin tripulación.
Este comunicado también es prueba de una vía de integración del software para la autonomía. Sin embargo, no menciona que el QCS8550 sea ni el microprocesador ni el sensor de las nuevas cabezas buscadoras anunciadas. Además, tal y como se describe en el comunicado, no hay forma de determinar si el software de OKSI sigue el principio de la programación open source, ya que esa descripción se refiere al entorno Ubuntu y a las herramientas compatibles.
Los ataques de elusión descritos en la documentación del software Dioptra, del Instituto Nacional de Estándares y Tecnología (EE. UU.), pueden modificar los datos de entrada, incluso mediante cambios en el entorno físico, para impedir que los modelos funcionen correctamente, lo que afectaría a la precisión de los modelos de inteligencia artificial, incluidos los utilizados para la visión artificial, según la documentación general sobre los ataques de elusión en sistemas de aprendizaje automático.
Los comunicados no ofrecen datos cuantitativos sobre la exactitud o la tasa de error de las nuevas cabezas buscadoras, necesarios para evaluar las afirmaciones de OKSI. Estos comunicados tampoco presentan resultados de ensayos hipersónicos.
