articles.title: Nobody Trusts the Security Questionnaire. We Rely on It Anyway.
articles.text:
Right now, people on security and GRC teams are spending their entire workday answering security questionnaires. At some companies it is a full-time role: a GRC analyst or compliance manager who arrives, opens a laptop, and works through these forms until they go home, two or three hundred of them in a year. I’ve heard the stories. The dinner missed, left a kid’s game at halftime, lost the weekend to a form asking whether the company still keeps tape backups. They do it because the questionnaire sits on the path to revenue. If the form stalls, the deal stalls with it.
There is a double standard built into the process. The same team buried under those questionnaires also sends them out to the company’s own vendors, collects the answers, and files them as proof those vendors are safe to trust. They know how little the answers are worth when they fill them out, because they have watched how little scrutiny the yeses get under deadline. They rely on them anyway when a vendor sends them back, because for a long time there was nothing better to rely on.
The same form, distrusted going out and trusted coming in
Step back and look at the whole exchange. Company A wants to sell to Company B. Before the deal closes, B sends A a questionnaire and a stack of security terms to sign: a security addendum, a data processing agreement, and now an AI addendum. Company A answers the questions, signs the commitments, and the deal proceeds. But A buys software too, so it runs its own vendors through the same exercise and weighs their answers to decide whom to trust. The form Company A knew was soft when it answered becomes, when A sits on the buyer’s side, its basis for trusting someone else. Every company in the chain is doing both at once.
Good programs already know the questionnaire is weak, which is why they also ask for a SOC 2 report, an ISO certificate, a penetration test, and sometimes an outside security rating. But look at where the weight still sits. The questionnaire is still what gates the deal and lands in the file as the record of due diligence. We have surrounded it with supplements and left it at the center. Trust between businesses runs, more than we like to admit, on a self-report: a vendor’s own account of its security, taken largely on the vendor’s word.
Why a self-reported answer stopped being evidence
An answer is not a control. A vendor writing yes does not make the thing true, and it was not true because your own team wrote yes when the roles were reversed. A questionnaire captures an intention, or a setting that was accurate on the day someone typed it, and then everyone moves on while the environment keeps changing.
If this model were working, third-party breaches should be getting rarer. They are not. Verizon’s 2025 Data Breach Investigations Report found the share of breaches involving a third party doubled in a single year, from 15 percent to 30 percent. They are not cheap, either. In IBM’s 2025 Cost of a Data Breach report, third-party and supply-chain compromise was one of the most expensive vectors at roughly $4.9 million per incident, above the global average, in a year when the overall average breach cost fell for the first time in five years. So the vendor-borne breach is getting more common and staying more costly even as breaches overall ease.
The clearest illustration is also one of the most studied breaches in the industry. Target was certified compliant with the Payment Card Industry Data Security Standard in September 2013. That December it disclosed a breach of 40 million payment cards. The certificate was real. It was also beside the point. A passing assessment tells you a vendor cleared a bar in one day. It does not tell you the vendor is secure, and that conflation is how thoroughly certified companies still end up writing breach notifications.
Stop trading promises, start trading proof
The market has started to act on this, and so have regulators. In an October 2025 industry letter, the New York Department of Financial Services (NYDFS) clarified what it expects of the firms it oversees: vet vendors up front, reassess them on a risk basis over time, obtain independent audit reports rather than rely on a vendor’s own say-so, and recognize that compliance cannot be handed off to the vendor. Stop exchanging assertions and start exchanging things the other party does not get to author. What that looks like depends on which chair you are in.
When you are assessing a vendor, start with what they cannot write for you. Before the questionnaire goes out, look at what is observable from the outside, none of which is self-reported:
- Exposed infrastructure and the state of their public-facing systems
- Breach and incident history
- Leaked or exposed credentials
It is not perfect. Anyone who has used security ratings knows the noise, the stale IP address, the subdomain that was never theirs. But it is harder to dress up than a self-graded form, and it is a better starting point than the vendor’s own account of itself. From there, concentrate your real effort on the few vendors who hold enough of your data or access to cause meaningful damage, and ask the rest for proof rather than prose: a report, a test result, or an attestation signed by someone who is not on the sales team.
When you are the one being assessed, the same principle holds. The security and data processing terms in your contracts are specific and binding in a way the questionnaire is not, and a customer is entitled to ask you to show, not assert, that you are meeting them. In practice that means being able to:
- Answer “show me you are doing what this clause requires” with current evidence
- Produce that evidence on demand, rather than re-typing the same three hundred answers into every customer’s form
- Stand behind the words as an accurate description of what is actually running, not what was true when someone last typed them
You put the promises in writing. Be able to back them the same way.
What trust between two companies should rest on
The questionnaire made sense when there was no other way to size up a vendor you couldn’t see inside. Mailing everyone a form was better than flying blind. That constraint is gone. You can observe a company from the outside, and you can produce real evidence behind your own commitments, neither of which existed at scale a decade ago.
So stop letting a self-report be the decision. Keep the questionnaire if it helps you start a conversation, but make the evidence, yours and theirs, the thing that actually settles whether there is trust. Businesses were never safe taking each other’s word for it. For a long time that was the only option. It is not anymore.

articles.title: A new report accuses Microsoft of using 10 "dark patterns" to keep you on Edge
articles.text:
A hot potato: It's no secret that when it comes to pushing its Edge browser onto users, Microsoft isn't afraid to play dirty. There have been numerous stories about the aggressive tactics the company uses, and other browser makers aren't happy about it. Now, a new report dives into the "dark patterns" Microsoft adopts to get more people onto Edge.
The Browser Choice Alliance (BCA), a group of browser makers advocating fair competition and freedom to choose a browser, commissioned the report, which was produced by the Behavioural Insights Team (BIT).
The report maps any harm to users from Microsoft's PC browser choice practices, focusing on dark patterns that are used by the company.
For those unfamiliar, dark patterns are designs that steer people into choices they wouldn't otherwise make, such as hiding a decline button or making cancellation difficult.
BIT identified 10 dark patterns that it said make it harder to choose a browser other than Edge or subvert a user's choice of an alternative browser after that decision has already been made. These are:
1. Pushing Edge ads when you search for rival browsers: Banners try to talk you out of downloading another browser and steer you back to Edge.
2. Making the switch incomplete: Setting another browser as your default still leaves files like PDFs assigned to Edge, requiring more changes.
3. Restricting alternatives through Windows S mode: Users have to leave the restricted mode before they can install competing browsers.
4. Ignoring your choice in Windows Search: Web results open in Edge even when you've chosen another default browser.
5. Sending Widgets and lock-screen links to Edge: These parts of Windows bypass your preferred browser, too.
6. Forcing News and Interests links into Edge: Clicking stories in Windows 10's news feed opens Microsoft's browser instead of your chosen one.
7. Giving Outlook and Teams separate browser settings: Links can open in Edge unless you change settings inside those apps as well.
8. Blocking tools that help you avoid Edge: Microsoft has blocked workarounds that redirect Edge-only links to your preferred browser.
9. Pulling another browser's tabs into Edge: The report describes tabs from competing browsers reopening in Edge when you sign in.
10. Pushing you back toward Edge after updates: "Recommended settings" prompts make accepting Microsoft's browser settings easier than keeping your own.
BIT also identified practices that make Edge seem easier to use and safer than rival browsers, potentially without supporting evidence, including blocking its removal and showing strong safety warnings when users leave S mode.
Source: StatCounter Global Stats - Browser Market Share
The report concludes that Microsoft's tactics work together to make switching away from Edge harder and sticking with another browser more frustrating. It says this undermines user choice, wastes time and particularly affects people without a strong browser preference.
European users face fewer barriers, but the problems haven't disappeared. In 2025, Microsoft said it had stopped nagging users in the European Economic Area to set Edge as their default browser as part of its compliance with the Digital Markets Act.
This isn't the first time BCA has called out Microsoft over Edge. It sent a letter to Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella in June demanding it stop burying rival browsers.

articles.title: MIT desarrolla software inspirado en origami para lograr construcciones más resistentes
articles.text:
Investigadores del MIT diseñaron un sistema de construcción modular basado en origami que permite erigir estructuras tridimensionales livianas y extremadamente rígidas sin necesidad de columnas de soporte interior ni equipos pesados de soldadura. El método utiliza bloques de construcción doblados a partir de láminas metálicas planas y un software que traduce diseños arquitectónicos complejos en piezas fáciles de cortar y ensamblar con herramientas manuales básicas.
“Este trabajo demuestra que doblar metal es un método listo para utilizarse en la construcción de estructuras. Podemos hacerlo lo suficientemente grande y resistente como para sacarlo del laboratorio y llevarlo al sitio de obra”, afirmó Neil Gershenfeld, director del Centro de Bits y Átomos del MIT.
El origami tradicional carece de resistencia estructural
El origami en papel es delicado. Hasta ahora, el origami aplicado a la arquitectura tampoco había logrado superar esa fragilidad. Los pliegues convencionales realizados sobre una sola lámina tienden a generar estructuras inestables, incapaces de soportar el peso que exige una construcción real.
El autor principal del estudio, Alfonso Parra Rubio, y su equipo retomaron patrones de teselado desarrollados en la década de 1960 por el artista Ron Resch. En lugar de trabajar con una única lámina de grandes dimensiones y difícil manejo, el equipo del MIT dividió el problema en bloques de construcción individuales más pequeños.
La unión de celdas tripié elimina el movimiento estructural
La clave del sistema radica en la combinación de dos celdas con forma de trípode en un solo bloque modular. Esa unión genera una unidad estructural con cero grados de libertad, es decir, que queda completamente fija y sin posibilidad de movimiento.
Cuando estos bloques se conectan entre sí formando una red entrelazada, dan lugar a una estructura tridimensional hueca de gran tamaño. El sistema no requiere columnas centrales de soporte, reduce en un tercio el uso de material y ofrece 3,5 veces más rigidez que los métodos de origami desarrollados previamente.
Un software traduce diseños complejos en piezas planas
La construcción de geometrías complejas suele generar fallas de comunicación entre arquitectos, ingenieros estructurales y trabajadores de obra. El equipo del MIT resolvió ese problema mediante el desarrollo de un software que funciona como solucionador automático: descompone visiones arquitectónicas complejas en archivos de diseño individuales y plegables.
Una fresadora de control numérico por computadora (CNC) corta estas formas precisas a partir de láminas metálicas planas. Las piezas resultantes pueden apilarse de manera compacta en camiones de plataforma o trasladarse por aire directamente a zonas de crisis.
El ensamblaje no requiere mano de obra especializada
El proceso de montaje en el terreno fue diseñado para ser simple. Las celdas modulares encajan en una única orientación correcta, lo cual elimina errores de posicionamiento durante la construcción.
Los trabajadores solo necesitan destornilladores manuales básicos para unir las piezas, sin requerir equipos pesados de soldadura ni herramientas especializadas. Este enfoque hace que la construcción sea más rápida, silenciosa y considerablemente más económica que los métodos convencionales.
Para comprobar la viabilidad del sistema fuera del laboratorio, el equipo construyó una escultura de aluminio plegado de 23 pies (siete metros) de longitud, suspendida del techo de la Biblioteca Pública de Boston. Un grupo de trabajadores sin formación formal en construcción levantó la estructura, del tamaño de una habitación, en apenas unos días.
Las aplicaciones se extienden a la industria aeroespacial
Aunque los refugios de emergencia de despliegue rápido representan la aplicación más inmediata, las implicancias del sistema abarcan otros sectores. Ingenieros aeroespaciales podrían adaptar la técnica para fabricar cascos de aviones y naves espaciales más livianos, dado que el sistema produce componentes excepcionalmente livianos y a la vez rígidos.
Arquitectos urbanos también evalúan el método para el desarrollo de paneles interiores con propiedades de aislamiento acústico, robótica modular y fachadas de edificios que reduzcan la huella de carbono asociada a su fabricación.

articles.title: Soundbar LG com 300 W RMS de potência despenca 39% na Amazon • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Soundbar LG com 300 W RMS de potência despenca 39% na Amazon

articles.title: People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
articles.text:
People are taking an unapproved weight-loss drug. AI found something surprising
- Date:
- October 21, 2026
- Source:
- University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science
- Summary:
- Researchers analyzing nearly 150,000 Reddit posts uncovered unexpected symptom reports linked by users to unapproved versions of retatrutide, including increased appetite, sleep disturbances, and elevated heart rates. The findings differ from clinical trial results and highlight how AI could help identify potential drug safety signals that warrant further investigation.
- Share:
An experimental weight-loss drug that has not yet received regulatory approval is already attracting users willing to obtain unapproved versions online. Now, scientists are using artificial intelligence to investigate their experiences, uncovering unexpected symptom reports that differ from those documented in clinical trials.
The drug, retatrutide, belongs to a new generation of GLP-1 medications designed to help regulate appetite and body weight. Although it remains under investigation and is not approved for use, people are purchasing unapproved formulations that are not intended for human consumption and discussing their experiences on internet forums.
Researchers at the University of Pennsylvania analyzed nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments from approximately 40,000 users to investigate these accounts. Their study, published in JAMA Network Open, provides the first systematic examination of potential side effects reported by people claiming to use unapproved retatrutide.
One finding stood out. Among users whose reported symptoms could be classified, increased appetite was the most common complaint. That was particularly unexpected because retatrutide is designed to suppress hunger, and its Phase 2 clinical trials primarily identified digestive problems as the most frequent side effects.
AI Uncovers Unexpected Weight-Loss Drug Reports
"Our goal is to identify hypotheses in online conversations that we could test. AI helps us find recurring patterns in people's self-reports, including experiences that may be missed by conventional drug-safety monitoring," says Sharath Chandra Guntuku, Research Associate Professor in Computer and Information Science (CIS), Director of Penn's Computational Social Listening Lab and senior author of the study.
However, the researchers emphasize that the findings should not be interpreted as proof of previously unknown side effects. Reddit users represent a very different population from clinical trial participants, and their accounts cannot establish whether the drug caused the symptoms they described.
There is also considerable uncertainty about what these individuals are actually taking. Products sold outside regulated medical channels may differ from the genuine experimental medication in their ingredients, purity, and dosage.
"We can't say that retatrutide is causing these symptoms, or even that Reddit users are actually taking genuine retatrutide, since the drug is not legally available, and gray market formulations vary," says Lyle Ungar, Professor in CIS and a co-author of the study.
Rather than confirming new risks, the research offers scientists an opportunity to identify questions that warrant more rigorous investigation.
"This is the first glimpse into the experiences of a population that is otherwise outside conventional drug safety monitoring because they are taking unapproved versions of a drug that has yet to finish clinical trials," says Neil Sehgal, the study's first author and a doctoral student in CIS.
How Researchers Analyzed 150,000 Reddit Posts
The project builds on previous research by the University of Pennsylvania team. In that earlier investigation, scientists used large language models (LLMs), the type of artificial intelligence that powers many modern chatbots, to examine more than 400,000 Reddit posts discussing semaglutide and tirzepatide.
That analysis revealed reports of possible side effects, including menstrual irregularities, that may not have been fully documented in clinical trials or official drug safety records.
"We wanted to apply the same methodology to gray-market retatrutide," says Sehgal.
Retatrutide is particularly interesting because it works differently from existing GLP-1 medications. Semaglutide acts on one hormone receptor involved in blood sugar control and appetite regulation, while tirzepatide targets two. Retatrutide activates three receptors, potentially producing a different combination of effects throughout the body.
To investigate what people were experiencing, the researchers used AI to examine nearly 150,000 Reddit posts and comments. They identified approximately 14,000 users who claimed to have personally taken an unapproved version of retatrutide.
The AI systems then extracted descriptions of symptoms that users associated with the medication and translated those descriptions into standardized medical terminology. This allowed researchers to compare reports even when different people used different words to describe similar experiences.
After excluding expected effects such as weight loss and reduced appetite, the team identified 7,823 users who reported at least one symptom that could be medically classified.
"A researcher might be able to examine a few thousand Reddit posts by hand, but looking at nearly 150,000 would be an enormous undertaking," says Sehgal. "AI makes it possible to analyze these conversations at scale, identifying patterns in what people are sharing that would otherwise be difficult to recognize."
A Surprising Appetite Paradox Emerges
The most striking difference involved hunger.
In retatrutide's Phase 2 clinical trials (the drug is currently in Phase 3 trials, the final step before FDA approval), participants most commonly experienced gastrointestinal complaints, including nausea. These effects are familiar concerns with medications that influence appetite and digestion.
But among Reddit users who reported taking unapproved retatrutide, the pattern looked different. Increased appetite emerged as the most frequently described classifiable symptom, despite the substantial weight-loss effects demonstrated in clinical testing.
The researchers also compared the new findings with their earlier analysis of semaglutide and tirzepatide.
Compared with those earlier Reddit reports, discussions involving unapproved retatrutide contained proportionally more mentions of appetite-related changes, sleep disturbances, increased heart rate, and muscle-related symptoms. Reports of nausea and other digestive complaints were proportionally less common.
These differences could reflect how retatrutide interacts with the body. However, they could also result from differences between the groups of people discussing the medications, their other drug use, or the contents of the unapproved products.
"Retatrutide works differently from existing GLP-1 drugs, so it's possible that its effects on the body are different, too," says Jena Shaw Tronieri, Senior Research Investigator at Penn's Center for Weight and Eating Disorders and a co-author of the study.
"But the people discussing it on Reddit also may be different," she notes. "Users willing to obtain an unapproved medication on the gray market likely differ from other clinical populations. Some may be taking multiple experimental peptides, and we can't verify exactly what they're taking. We need more research to understand what, if anything, these differences in self-reported symptoms mean."
Can AI Detect Drug Safety Concerns Earlier?
Beyond the findings about retatrutide, the study demonstrates how AI could potentially improve the early detection of drug safety concerns.
Traditional monitoring systems depend heavily on clinical trials, reports submitted to regulators, and information collected by healthcare professionals. People obtaining experimental medications through unapproved channels may not be represented in those systems.
Social media offers another source of information, allowing researchers to identify recurring experiences that might otherwise escape attention. However, these reports must be independently investigated before they can be considered reliable evidence of a drug-related problem.
The Penn team has already seen an example of how this approach can help guide further research.
In their previous investigation of semaglutide and tirzepatide, researchers identified online reports of menstrual irregularities. Those findings subsequently encouraged another scientific team to examine similar symptoms using the FDA's database of reported adverse drug events.
The follow-up study, published in Obstetrics & Gynecology, also detected disproportionate reports of certain menstrual changes. Although those findings did not establish causation, they provided additional reasons to investigate the potential connection.
The researchers hope their retatrutide findings will lead to similar independent studies, particularly as the drug advances through clinical development.
"That's what we hope will happen with this study," says Sehgal. "Other researchers can take what we find on Reddit and look for the same patterns in other datasets, using entirely different methods. Whether those signals hold up or not, the goal is to build a better understanding of what people are actually experiencing."
The research was conducted through the University of Pennsylvania's School of Engineering and Applied Science and Perelman School of Medicine. Benjamin Rader of Boston Children's Hospital also contributed as a co-author. Funding was provided in part by the University of Pennsylvania's Penn Medical Communication Research Institute. Tronieri disclosed receiving an investigator-initiated grant from Novo Nordisk on behalf of the University of Pennsylvania, along with consulting fees from Currax Pharmaceuticals, LLC. No conflicts of interest were reported by the other authors.
Story Source:
Materials provided by University of Pennsylvania School of Engineering and Applied Science. Note: Content may be edited for style and length.
Journal Reference:
- Neil K. R. Sehgal, Jena Shaw Tronieri, Benjamin Rader, Lyle Ungar, Sharath Chandra Guntuku. Self-Reported Adverse Effects Among Social Media Users Taking Nonapproved Retatrutide. JAMA Network Open, 2026; 9 (10): e2638929 DOI: 10.1001/jamanetworkopen.2026.38929

articles.title: AI execs may be too out of touch to build for the general public | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Former Yahoo CEO and early Google engineer Marissa Mayer is catching a lot of flak for how she uses AI. In an interview about her new app Dazzle, an AI assistant that learns from your camera roll, Mayer poses what she believes is an impressive flex for the product: It helped her come up with three bullet points about her 10-year-old daughter for a birthday presentation at school, describing her as “empathetic, creative, and an animal lover.”
It’s a vague description, like a generic horoscope — it could probably describe a lot of 10-year-olds.
Some onlookers, like progressive activist Leah Greenberg, marveled that “the fact that Marissa Mayer would voluntarily disclose this to a reporter is a pretty good demonstration of how deeply the culture of Silicon Valley has diverged from the rest of humanity.”
Perhaps Mayer drew so much backlash because we have repeatedly observed sheltered billionaires suggest that we outsource child-rearing — one of life’s greatest tests of patience, humility, and kindness — to a computer that is incapable of understanding human emotion.
We’ve been primed for this frustration. Last year, OpenAI CEO Sam Altman told Bored Ape owner and late night host Jimmy Fallon on national television, “I cannot imagine … figuring out how to raise a newborn without ChatGPT.” The public didn’t love that comment, either, but Altman wasn’t fazed by the negative feedback. A few months ago, he said on X that a “cool use case” of ChatGPT Work would be creating a podcast that talks about your kids’ upcoming birthdays or soccer games and “explain[s] your kids’ interests.” (He was brutally ratioed with comments like, “What if you just talked to your children?”)
After publication, Mayer defended herself in a long X post. She claims she was not relying on Dazzle to explain her child to her, but rather, she was testing what her prototype could do — it resurfaced photos of “forgotten kindergarten projects,” like a “snake devenomer” or “sandcat playground,” illustrating her daughter’s creativity and care for animals.
Fair enough. But Mayer remarks in the same interview that people could also use her AI to outsource the mental load of “figuring out the theme for your child’s birthday party.” She says she’s used her app to plan a playdate for her daughter, book family activities on vacation, and decide what to be for Halloween. She even proposes that her AI assistant could coordinate plans with her husband’s AI assistant. When the reporter asks her if it’s depressing to imagine this “frictionless future … planned by AI,” Mayer replies, “I haven’t really thought that through.”
These leaders seem to write off the naysayers as part of a small, angry fringe group. Yet a Pew Research Center study reports that 50% of U.S. adults think that AI will reduce people’s ability to form meaningful relationships. Only 5% of respondents said AI would make it easier to build these connections.
Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg, however, joins his Silicon Valley kin in envisioning a world where our social needs are met via AI.
“The average American I think has, it’s fewer than three friends, three people they’d consider friends, and the average person has demand for meaningfully more, I think it’s like 15 friends,” Zuckerberg said last year on a podcast. “The average person wants more connectivity, connection than they have.”
Zuckerberg predicts that it will become more socially acceptable to outsource our emotional needs to AI therapists or even AI romantic partners. “There are all these things that are better about physical connections when you can have them,” he added. “But the reality is that people … feel more alone a lot of the time than they would like.”
Zuckerberg goes on to explain how virtual-reality embodiments of AI avatars are only growing more realistic. Meta seems to be more keen on improving our relationships with these approximations of humans, rather than between the actual billions of humans who use its platforms each day.
Maybe part of this stems from the culture of the tech industry, which prizes efficiency. People try to biohack their own bodies by optimizing their sleep schedules with health trackers or injecting unregulated “peptide stacks” to maximize their productivity.
If you’re building electric vehicles or computer chips, then sure, efficiency is a clear north star. But our relationships with other people are not a tech product that we’ve been challenged to ship with as little capital as possible. Human relationships are inherently messy, but our connections with one another can be what gives our lives meaning. When we delegate those interactions to computers, we surrender the difficult, yet fulfilling experience of being people.

articles.title: NanoTess delivers wound-care treatment to Ukraine’s front lines | BetaKit
articles.text:
A made-in-Calgary treatment for wound and burn care is now treating soldiers on the front lines of the war in Ukraine.
The news: NanoTess, a Calgary biotech startup, announced at the CAN Health Network Annual Conference on Wednesday that its flagship product, NanoSALV Catalytic, is being used to treat wounds sustained by soldiers and civilians in Ukraine. The company claims NanoSALV, a topical gel that uses tiny, catalytic particles to accelerate healing, has reached more than 6,000 soldiers and civilians impacted by the war.
From the source: “Effective medical treatment in active conflict zones and during recovery is critical to our soldiers. Burns require urgent care, and complex blast wounds, typically sustained in drone strikes, are easily contaminated by debris and can quickly become infected,” Dr. Vasyl Voronets, a military surgeon working in Ukraine’s eastern front, said in a press release. “In a conflict where medical access can never be taken for granted, this support matters deeply to our soldiers and to the people we serve.”
The context: To deliver NanoSALV to the often remote and dangerous regions along the Ukrainian frontlines, NanoTess is partnering with Calgary-based charity Medical Mercy Canada, as well as the Public Health Centre of Ukraine, and the Ukrainian military’s Medical Forces Sustainment Group East. Much of the deployment is occurring via drone delivery, the company said.
Since being authorized by Health Canada in 2022, NanoSALV has gone on to be used in more than 2,500 hospitals and health facilities; it’s also available in 14,000 pharmacies. In 2023, the company received support from the CAN Health Network, a federally funded organization that connects health-tech companies with healthcare providers to launch commercialization.
Final thought: Ukraine and Canada have deepened cooperation. In September, Prime Minister Mark Carney and Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelensky signed a 100-year declaration to collaborate on defence innovation. Amid that collaboration, as well as Canada’s larger defence expansion, dual-use technology from the private sector has been prioritized. NanoTess has expanded toward dual-use capability, participating in the Department of National Defence’s (DND) Innovation for Defence Excellence and Security program, and receiving support from the DND to build out its manufacturing.
BetaKit’s Prairies reporting is funded in part by YEGAF, a not-for-profit dedicated to amplifying business stories in Alberta.

articles.title: Cronologia de Zelda: a ordem que a Nintendo só inventou 25 anos depois
articles.text:
A cronologia de The Legend of Zelda organiza os jogos em três linhas do tempo paralelas que nascem de Ocarina of Time. E aqui vai o detalhe que muita gente não sabe: essa ordem não existia enquanto os jogos eram feitos. Ela foi publicada oficialmente em 2011, no livro Hyrule Historia, quando a franquia já tinha mais de 25 anos e quase 20 títulos lançados.
Ou seja: a Nintendo não escreveu uma saga e depois a dividiu em jogos. Ela fez jogos por 25 anos e depois sentou para encaixar tudo numa linha que fizesse sentido, ou não.
Um jogo de 2011 (Skyward Sword) abre a história. O original de 1986 está lá no fim. Alguns títulos receberam pequenos ajustes de roteiro — retcons — para caberem melhor. E o quadro continua sendo atualizado até hoje: a última mudança aconteceu em setembro de 2026, junto com o anúncio do remake de Ocarina of Time.
Com os 40 anos da franquia e o remake chegando em 5 de novembro de 2026, vale entender como essa bagunça magnífica se organiza.
Preciso jogar Zelda na ordem cronológica?
Não. E essa é talvez uma ótima característica da franquia.
Cada jogo de Zelda é uma história, com começo, meio e fim próprios. Você pode começar por Breath of the Wild, por Ocarina of Time ou pelo remake que chega agora sem ter jogado absolutamente nada antes. O jogo te explica o que você precisa saber.
As exceções são poucas e óbvias: Majora’s Mask continua Ocarina of Time com o mesmo Link, Tears of the Kingdom é sequência direta de Breath of the Wild, e Phantom Hourglass segue The Wind Waker. Mesmo nesses casos, o jogo posterior se vira sozinho.
E a lore, então?
Conhecer as conexões deixa tudo mais rico, sem dúvida. Mas tem um argumento forte do outro lado: quem jogou por ordem de lançamento viveu as revelações do jeito que elas foram projetadas para acontecer.
Imagina jogar The Wind Waker em 2002, achando que é um Zelda cartunesco qualquer, e descobrir no meio do jogo que aquele oceano cobre a Hyrule de Ocarina of Time. Ou chegar em Twilight Princess e encontrar o esqueleto de um guerreiro que te ensina técnicas de espada — e perceber, pelas entrelinhas, que aquele é o Link de Ocarina, que morreu sem nunca ter sido reconhecido como herói naquele mundo.
Esses momentos não funcionam do mesmo jeito quando você já sabe. A cronologia é um mapa ótimo, mas o mapa estraga algumas surpresas.
Resumo prático: jogue na ordem que te der vontade. Use a cronologia como leitura complementar, não como pré-requisito.
Qual é a ordem cronológica oficial dos jogos de Zelda?
Tudo começa com uma maldição. Em Skyward Sword, o Rei Demônio Demise é derrotado, mas antes de morrer promete que uma encarnação do seu ódio vai perseguir eternamente quem carregar o sangue da deusa e o espírito do herói.
É a frase que sustenta a franquia inteira. Por isso a princesa sempre se chama Zelda, o herói sempre se chama Link e o vilão sempre volta. Não são os mesmos personagens — são as mesmas três almas renascendo, era após era.
O tronco comum
Quatro jogos acontecem antes da divisão:
- Skyward Sword (2011) — a origem de tudo: o primeiro Link, a primeira Zelda, o nascimento da Master Sword e a maldição de Demise. No fim, Zelda funda o Reino de Hyrule.
- The Minish Cap (2004) — o mago Vaati solta monstros sobre Hyrule e petrifica a princesa. Um novo Link forja a Four Sword para detê-lo.
- Four Swords (2002) — o selo de Vaati enfraquece e outro Link usa a mesma espada, que o divide em quatro.
- Ocarina of Time (1998) — o ponto de ruptura.
O que acontece em Ocarina of Time
Um garoto criado na floresta descobre que foi escolhido pela deusa. Ganondorf, rei das Gerudo e encarnação do ódio de Demise, dá um golpe de Estado para tomar a Triforce.
Link saca a Master Sword do pedestal, mas tem dez anos e seu corpo não suporta o poder: fica selado por sete anos. Ganondorf aproveita a brecha, alcança a Triforce e a parte em três. Sete anos depois, Link desperta adulto, vira o Herói do Tempo e vence.
E é aqui que a história se abre em três.
Ramo 1: a Era da Criança
Zelda devolve Link ao passado para que ele recupere os sete anos perdidos. Como ele volta com as memórias, avisa a família real e Ganondorf é preso antes do golpe.
- Majora’s Mask (2000) — o mesmo Link procura a fada Navi e acaba em Termina, onde a lua vai cair em três dias.
- Twilight Princess (2006) — séculos depois, um fazendeiro descendente do Herói do Tempo entra no Reino do Crepúsculo, para onde Ganondorf havia sido banido. É o único jogo em que o Ganondorf de Ocarina é derrotado de vez.
- Four Swords Adventures (2004) — Ganondorf reencarna e liberta Vaati. Fim desse ramo.
Ramo 2: a Era do Adulto
Este é o mundo que Link deixou para trás ao voltar no tempo. Um mundo sem herói.
- The Wind Waker (2002) — gerações depois, Ganon ressurge. As pessoas rezam pelo retorno do herói, e ele nunca vem: ele está em outra linha do tempo. Sem saída, as deusas inundam Hyrule inteira. O reino vira um oceano. O novo Link não nasce escolhido — ele se torna o escolhido.
- Phantom Hourglass (2007) — sequência direta, mesmo Link, mesma Tetra.
- Spirit Tracks (2009) — os dois encontram um novo continente e fundam uma nova Hyrule, interligada por trilhos de trem. Fim desse ramo.
Ramo 3: o Herói Derrotado
O mais estranho dos três, porque parte de um “e se?”. E se Link tivesse perdido a batalha final de Ocarina?
Nesse universo, Ganondorf reúne as três partes da Triforce. Os Sete Sábios conseguem selá-lo no Reino Sagrado — a Guerra do Aprisionamento — e aquele lugar se corrompe no Mundo das Trevas.
- A Link to the Past (1991) — o feiticeiro Agahnim tenta quebrar o selo de Ganon.
- Link’s Awakening (1993) — o mesmo Link naufraga numa ilha que só existe dentro do sonho de uma criatura.
- Oracle of Seasons / Oracle of Ages (2001) — dois jogos simultâneos em reinos diferentes, impedindo a ressurreição de Ganon.
- A Link Between Worlds (2013) — um mago invade Hyrule vindo de Lorule, sua dimensão espelho.
- Tri Force Heroes (2015) — aventura paralela no reino de Hytopia.
- Echoes of Wisdom (2024) — o primeiro jogo da linha principal com Zelda como protagonista jogável. Fendas engolem Hyrule e Link desaparece em uma delas.
- The Legend of Zelda (1986) — o original. Ganon ressuscita, Zelda parte a Triforce da Sabedoria em oito pedaços e um novo Link sai para reuni-los.
- Zelda II: The Adventure of Link (1987) — fim da linha, com Link despertando uma princesa adormecida há gerações.
Detalhe de colecionador: a ordem entre Link’s Awakening e os jogos Oracle mudou. O Hyrule Historia (2011) colocava Link’s Awakening depois; a Zelda Encyclopedia (2018) inverteu. A ordem acima é a vigente.
O que mudou na cronologia em 2026
Durante anos ficou uma pergunta sem resposta: onde entram Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom?
Os dois nunca foram encaixados em nenhum dos três ramos. E Tears of the Kingdom complicou ainda mais, ao mostrar que Hyrule teria sido fundada por Rauru e Sonia, da raça Zonai — o que criaria dois Ganondorf convivendo: o Gerudo de Ocarina of Time na superfície e o Ganondorf original selado no subsolo. Nunca fechou.
Em setembro de 2026, depois do Direct de 40 anos que apresentou o remake, a página japonesa do jogo trouxe um quadro revisado com uma mudança discreta e decisiva: uma segunda fundação do Reino de Hyrule, posicionada logo antes da Guerra do Aprisionamento de Tears of the Kingdom — mantendo a primeira, lá no começo, onde sempre esteve.
A leitura que a comunidade tirou disso é que a Hyrule de Rauru é uma refundação, muito à frente de toda a cronologia clássica. O lugar simplesmente voltou a se chamar Hyrule — do mesmo jeito que o herói sempre volta a se chamar Link.
No código-fonte da mesma página, criadores de conteúdo encontraram os dois jogos descritos como um epílogo compartilhado: o ponto em que os três ramos se encontram. A ideia já era defendida pelos produtores da série — Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom se passam tão adiante que as três linhas viraram lenda, e separar lenda de história ficou impossível dentro do próprio universo.
Vale a ressalva: a expressão “epílogo compartilhado” não é texto publicado pela Nintendo, e sim um achado no código da página. A leitura da refundação também é interpretação do gráfico, não declaração oficial.
As mecânicas de Zelda que a indústria inteira copiou
A cronologia é divertida, mas não é por ela que Zelda importa. A franquia importa porque, várias vezes, ela resolveu um problema que a indústria inteira tinha — e todo mundo copiou a solução.
O Z-targeting resolveu o combate em 3D
Em 1998, jogar em três dimensões era desorientador. Câmeras ruins, noção de profundidade confusa, e acertar um inimigo em movimento era quase sorte.
Ocarina of Time criou o Z-targeting: você aperta um botão, a câmera trava no inimigo e o personagem passa a se mover em relação a ele. O problema deixou de existir.
Hoje isso tem nome genérico — lock-on — e está em praticamente todo jogo de ação em terceira pessoa. De Dark Souls a Red Dead Redemption 2, a lista é enorme.
O mundo aberto
The Legend of Zelda, lá em 1986, já nasceu com uma proposta incomum: não havia ordem obrigatória. Você escolhia para onde ir e em que sequência encarar as masmorras. Shigeru Miyamoto queria o oposto de Super Mario Bros., que só ia da esquerda para a direita.
Foi também o primeiro cartucho da história com bateria interna para salvar o progresso — sem isso, a ideia de um mundo grande para explorar aos poucos simplesmente não funcionaria.
Trinta e um anos depois, Breath of the Wild refez o mesmo truque: largou o design de mundo aberto com checklist de ícones e devolveu ao jogador a liberdade de subir em qualquer coisa e ir a qualquer lugar. Foi copiado com a mesma velocidade.
O tempo como mecânica
Ocarina usou a viagem no tempo não como enredo, mas como ferramenta: você planta uma semente no passado e colhe a árvore sete anos depois. Majora’s Mask foi mais longe, com um ciclo de três dias que reinicia tudo.
Sem esses dois jogos, boa parte dos puzzles temporais que vemos hoje em jogos de ação e aventura não existiria no formato que existe.
Zelda em números: 40 anos de franquia
O primeiro The Legend of Zelda chegou ao Famicom japonês em fevereiro de 1986. São 40 anos — e poucas obras de entretenimento de qualquer linguagem chegam a essa marca ainda sendo consumidas por público novo.
| Dado | Número | Referência | 
| Breath of the Wild | 34,06 milhões de unidades | Nintendo IR, 30/06/2026 | 
| Tears of the Kingdom | 22,71 milhões de unidades | Nintendo IR, 30/06/2026 | 
| Franquia (total estimado) | mais de 160 milhões | estimativa de 2023 | 
| Jogos na linha principal | 20 títulos | contagem da cronologia oficial | 
Breath of the Wild é o jogo mais vendido da série e um dos campeões absolutos do catálogo Nintendo. E chama atenção que os dois títulos mais recentes sejam também os dois maiores em vendas: não é uma franquia vivendo de nostalgia. Ela cresceu.
O remake de Ocarina of Time chega em 5 de novembro
O remake de The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time sai em 5 de novembro de 2026, exclusivo para Nintendo Switch 2, desenvolvido pela Nintendo EPD com produção de Eiji Aonuma e Hidemaro Fujibayashi.
Ele mantém história e estrutura do original de 1998 — o que significa que o ponto de bifurcação da cronologia segue exatamente onde estava. O que muda é tudo ao redor: visual refeito, câmera livre, botão de pulo, Hyrule Castle Town explorável em vez de cenário fixo, ciclo de tempo contínuo e cutscenes dubladas.
Duas novidades chamam mais atenção. A ocarina pode ser tocada pelo microfone do console — dá para cantar as melodias. E a história é narrada por uma tapeçaria que vai sendo montada ao longo da gameplay, com personagens de traço quase de marionete. Há quem leia isso como o jogo se apresentando como uma lenda sendo contada — o que conversa bem com a ideia de que, na era de Breath of the Wild, tudo isso virou folclore.
Eu joguei a demo e escrevi as minhas primeiras impressões aqui — resumo: nunca tinha jogado o original, e o clássico envelheceu muito bem.
A corrida pelo console
O hype produziu números concretos. A Nintendo lançou um Switch 2 em edição Zelda, com Pro Controller temático, que chegou às lojas em 29 de outubro por US$ 519,99 — e esgotou em boa parte dos varejistas internacionais antes mesmo de sair.
No Brasil, a pré-venda da edição física do jogo, aberta em 16 de setembro por cerca de R$ 409, acabou em aproximadamente dez minutos. A versão digital, a R$ 329,90, seguiu disponível.
Colocar um remake de um jogo de 1998 nesse patamar de disputa diz bastante sobre o tamanho da franquia.
E tem filme vindo aí
O live-action de The Legend of Zelda estreia em 30 de abril de 2027, dirigido por Wes Ball (Planeta dos Macacos: O Reinado), com roteiro de T. S. Nowlin. A produção é da Columbia Pictures em parceria com a própria Nintendo e a OddBall Entertainment, com distribuição Sony.
Benjamin Evan Ainsworth vive Link e Bo Bragason é Zelda. As filmagens aconteceram na Nova Zelândia entre novembro de 2025 e abril de 2026.
A data já foi remarcada duas vezes — era março, virou 7 de maio e acabou em 30 de abril de 2027. É o passo mais arriscado da Nintendo desde que ela decidiu levar suas franquias para o cinema, e vem logo depois do sucesso da linha de animação do Mario.
Além do fã
Preciso ser honesta: eu não sou Zeldamaníaca. Não tenho a memória afetiva de ter jogado na infância, não sei de cor a melodia da Ocarina e, até pegar a demo do remake, eu nunca tinha jogado Ocarina of Time.
Mas trabalho com entretenimento há mais de 15 anos, e tem uma coisa que eu sei reconhecer: são pouquíssimas obras que atravessam 40 anos e continuam sendo jogadas, discutidas e esperadas por gente que nem era nascida quando elas saíram.
O que me chamou atenção no hype do remake não foi a nostalgia em si. Foi a conversão dela. Pré-venda esgotando em dez minutos no Brasil. Console em edição especial sumindo “das prateleiras” instantaneamente. Gente de 20 e poucos anos, que nunca encostou num Nintendo 64, ansiosa por um jogo de 1998.
Isso não é só saudade. É uma franquia que construiu lore suficiente para sustentar décadas de teoria, mecânicas boas o bastante para a indústria inteira copiar, e uma relação com o público forte o suficiente para transformar um remake em um dos lançamentos mais esperados de 2026.
Eu continuo não sendo Zeldomaníaca. Mas saí da demo com bem mais admiração do que entrei — e com um pouco de inveja de quem tem essa memória afetiva para reviver.
Perguntas frequentes sobre a cronologia de Zelda
Qual é o primeiro jogo da cronologia de Zelda? Skyward Sword (2011). Ele conta a origem da Master Sword, do primeiro Link e da maldição que gera todos os jogos seguintes.
Por que a cronologia de Zelda tem três linhas do tempo? Porque Ocarina of Time termina com três desfechos simultâneos: Link volta ao passado (Era da Criança), o futuro que ele deixou continua sem herói (Era do Adulto), e existe a possibilidade de ele ter perdido a batalha final (Herói Derrotado).
Preciso jogar os jogos de Zelda em ordem? Não. Cada título é uma história independente. As únicas sequências diretas são Majora’s Mask, Tears of the Kingdom e Phantom Hourglass.
Onde Breath of the Wild e Tears of the Kingdom se encaixam? No ponto final, depois de todos os ramos. O quadro atualizado em setembro de 2026 os trata como o encontro das três linhas do tempo.
Quando sai o remake de Ocarina of Time? Em 5 de novembro de 2026, exclusivo para Nintendo Switch 2.
Quando estreia o filme de Zelda? Em 30 de abril de 2027, dirigido por Wes Ball, com Benjamin Evan Ainsworth como Link e Bo Bragason como Zelda.
Quantos jogos tem a franquia The Legend of Zelda? São 20 títulos na linha principal da cronologia oficial, sem contar spin-offs como a série Hyrule Warriors.

articles.title: How Much Can Semiconductor Models Hide?
articles.text:
Advanced packaging requires models to cross company boundaries without exposing proprietary processes, but hiding too much can make the prediction break down.
Key Takeaways:
The goal seems simple — share the model without sharing the process. A materials supplier shouldn’t have to reveal a proprietary formulation just so a customer can predict how it will behave in a package, and a foundry shouldn’t have to hand over its recipe to provide a useful model of a chiplet. But advanced packaging is making that separation much harder to maintain.
For years, engineers moved much of what they needed between companies through datasheets, design rules, and qualification specs, while the manufacturing knowledge stayed with the supplier. That arrangement held as long as the pieces behaved independently, but what one company keeps inside its process now shapes how another company’s part of the package performs once everything is assembled. The process may still belong to the supplier, but its consequences no longer end at the factory gate.
“There’s been some initial work on this challenge, but how do you insert a membrane between the companies so they can share a certain amount of data, but not all,” said Greg Prewitt, director of product management for Exensio Test Operations at PDF Solutions. “Do you obfuscate it? Do you normalize it? How much do you share so both teams can solve a problem without seeing any of the IP that’s proprietary to one company or another?”
The difficulty is deciding what that membrane should let through. Hide too little and the supplier gives away process knowledge it spent years developing. Hide too much and the model may lose the behavior, variation, or limits that the engineer on the other side needs to make a useful prediction. That leaves a harder question — how much can disappear inside it before it starts hiding something the prediction actually needs?
Materials show the problem in its simplest form. Engineers may need to know how a material changes with temperature, whether a substrate will warp enough to affect assembly, or how process variation propagates into electrical performance without needing the proprietary details that produced those behaviors. A customer doesn’t need a material company’s formulation to model how one of its materials will behave, but a few static numbers on a datasheet may not be enough either.
“Although proprietary formulations cannot be shared, material characterization across the range of conditions relevant to the intended application can provide a more comprehensive representation of material behavior, allowing models to better reflect real-world conditions and improve prediction accuracy,” said Hanlin Chen, senior research associate and team lead at Brewer Science. “A digital twin that uses single fixed values for material inputs will always underrepresent real-world risk.”
The data handoff challenge
The need for more detailed models is growing because an advanced package brings together pieces whose engineering histories accumulated in different places. They may pass through several companies before the finished package reaches the system, but by then no single company necessarily has the whole history.
“Advanced packaging is enabled by a highly collaborative supply chain,” said Joon Ahn, vice president of global factory IT and automation at Amkor. “Dies, substrates, materials, and design information are contributed by multiple partners. Each participant owns unique expertise and data associated with their portion of the value chain.”
That distributed ownership becomes a problem once the design flow needs manufacturing information before everything has been built. The process can remain inside one company, but enough of its behavior has to become usable somewhere else.
What reaches the next engineer is usually enough to describe the part as designed, but not necessarily enough to explain how it will behave after assembly. Nominal dimensions and basic electrical or material properties are relatively easy to pass along. Production variation and the history behind those numbers are much less likely to make the trip.
“I don’t think we need complete data transparency to create a connected digital thread,” said CP Hung, vice president of corporate R&D at ASE. “What we really need is a trusted way to share enough information for the next engineering decision to be made.”
That doesn’t mean every upstream detail belongs in the model. Some can disappear without changing the prediction, while others matter only when something elsewhere in the package exposes their effect. For example, a chiplet’s thermal response may be enough for one analysis, but process variation can change that response in a way the downstream model can’t see.
The question therefore isn’t simply how much information can be shared. It’s which information still matters after the process itself has been hidden. A model that preserves the right behavior can protect the recipe underneath it. Hide the wrong thing, however, and the uncertainty disappears from the model even though it never disappeared from the package.
How much physics can a model hide?
Reduced-order and surrogate models solve a similar computational problem in different ways. A reduced-order model simplifies a higher-fidelity physical representation, while a surrogate approximates behavior across a sampled design or process space. Both make analysis practical when running the underlying model every time would take too long, but they don’t become more trustworthy because they run faster.
“The surrogate model can be trusted if the simulated data used to create the surrogate model is accurate,” said Eric Guichard, senior vice president and general manager of AI Manufacturing at Silvaco. “For the simulation data to be accurate and predictive, the physical models used to generate them must be calibrated. The calibration can only be done against experimental data. Those experimental data are usually available and not proprietary. Physical model calibration is only one part of the equation. The second part is the knowledge of the detailed process recipes.”
The problem splits into two very different kinds of information. Experimental measurements can provide the evidence needed to calibrate a model without revealing much about the process itself, but building a predictive representation may still require details the company would never hand directly to a customer.
What makes that workable is an asymmetry between building the model and using it. The organization creating the model may need to know enough about the process to establish why it behaves the way it does. The engineer consuming the model may only need access to that behavior. A substrate model, for example, might expose thickness, material response, and the effects of process variation without revealing how the supplier achieves those characteristics in manufacturing.
“If only some key knobs are exposed to the user of the surrogate model, we can reasonably believe that the proprietary process details are preserved,” Guichard said.
The recipe doesn’t disappear. It moves behind the model boundary. But that only relocates the disclosure problem rather than solving it, because the model builder still needs what the supplier is trying to protect.
“Availability of detailed process recipes is actually the challenge,” Guichard added.
Encryption protects proprietary data
Encryption creates a way to separate useful behavior from proprietary implementation. Synopsys’ HFSS (High Frequency Structure Simulator) supports encrypted electromagnetic models that a component supplier can share for use in a customer’s simulation without exposing the underlying geometry and material information.
“These encrypted models solve a significant but non-technical hurdle — how to share simulation models of an electronic part with your customers without revealing your trade secrets,” said Lang Lin, product management director at Synopsys.
Encryption handles the disclosure problem neatly. The engineer receiving the model can use it without gaining access to what’s sealed inside. What encryption can’t tell that engineer is whether the model is still valid for the problem being asked.
“That has always been one of the key concerns about simulation, in general,” Lin said. “How well does it actually match reality?”
A model can be secure and still be wrong for the conditions in which it’s being used. If it was built around one package or process window, the result may remain numerically precise long after the design has moved beyond those conditions. Encryption can make that harder to catch because the user can’t look inside and see where the original assumptions stop holding. The IP can stay perfectly protected while the engineering decision doesn’t.
Model sharing therefore needs something outside the encrypted model itself. The recipient may not need to know how the model works internally, but they still need to know the conditions under which it can be trusted.
When the model stops working
Materials make that problem easier to see. A datasheet can be perfectly accurate and still describe only one moment in a material’s life. Once that material is cured, assembled, and put into service, the properties used to build the model may start to move.
“A datasheet gives you a snapshot, CTE, modulus, adhesion, viscosity, measured under one set of conditions at one point in time,” said Brewer’s Chen. “Mechanical and thermal properties shift with degree of curing. Crosslink density may continue to evolve after processing, and adhesion strength is highly dependent on the specific bonding interface. CTE also varies, particularly in the temperature region near the polymer’s Tg (glass transition temperature). Treating any of these as a single static number causes a lot of simulation-to-silicon gaps.”
The supplier doesn’t have to reveal the formulation to account for that behavior. What has to survive the handoff is enough information to show how the material changes under the conditions the package is likely to see. A nominal value may be enough at one point in the design space but misleading somewhere else.
Surrogate models make the same validity problem particularly visible. They can be highly accurate inside the region represented by their training data and still return a plausible-looking answer after the user has wandered outside it. The model hasn’t necessarily failed at that point. It’s being asked a question its underlying data was never meant to answer.
“The fundamental principle is that surrogate models are reliable when interpolating within the region represented by their training data and less reliable when extrapolating beyond it,” Guichard said.
The difficulty is that nothing in the output necessarily flags the crossing. A number returned from outside the training region can look exactly like a number returned from inside it.
A useful black box therefore needs a visible envelope around it. The recipe can remain hidden, but the conditions that establish where the model applies can’t. The engineer using it needs to know when the question has moved outside the territory the model actually knows. The model builder has to make that territory visible, and the user still has to respect it.
The interfaces add complexity
The problem gets harder at the interfaces because the IP line often falls in the same place where two independently built models have to begin describing the same physical behavior.
A material, substrate, or die model may be perfectly valid for the conditions its supplier intended. The trouble starts when those models are joined and the assumptions underneath them don’t line up. One may treat a temperature, geometry, or other condition as fixed while another allows it to move.
“The challenge is that the data often comes in different formats, at different levels of detail, and with different assumptions behind it,” said ASE’s Hung. “A material property, for example, only really means something if we know how it changes with temperature, moisture, time, and process history. A component model may also work perfectly well on its own but not tell us enough about what happens once it’s integrated into the package.”
Those assumptions become harder to separate once the package is assembled. Heat generated in the die moves through the structures around it, while the resulting temperature changes material behavior and mechanical stress elsewhere in the assembly. The models may have been created separately, but the package doesn’t operate that way.
“The real challenge isn’t simply moving data from one company to another,” Hung said. “It’s making sure the physical meaning of that data doesn’t get lost along the way.”
Thermal analysis shows how quickly the information problem follows. Substrate and interposer data may exist upstream, but the downstream design flow needs it in a form that can be combined with the rest of the package.
“When you’re talking about thermal, it’s not just the dies,” said Amlendu Shekhar Choubey, senior director of product management at Synopsys. “This is an integrated problem. You need the whole stack.”
But having all the pieces still doesn’t guarantee they fit. One supplier may characterize behavior under one set of conditions while the model on the other side of the interface assumes another. Even the same nominal parameter can mean something different if it was measured at another temperature, derived from a different process state, or intended for a different range of operation.
The harder problem isn’t getting more data across the interface. The handoff has to preserve enough of the assumptions behind the data for the next model to know how to use it, or every model can be right on its own while the package they describe together is wrong.
What models need to carry
The model itself is becoming a kind of engineering contract between companies. One side doesn’t promise to expose how a process works. It promises to describe enough of what that process does for another engineer to use the result within an agreed set of conditions. The formulation, recipe, or implementation can stay hidden as long as the model exposes the behavior the next engineer actually needs. The receiving engineer still needs to know what kind of promise is being made.
“Uncertainty and model validity need to move with the model,” said Kenneth Larsen, senior director of 3D-IC product management at Synopsys. “It is not enough to exchange geometry, material properties, or simulation results. Each model also needs to carry the context that determines whether it can be trusted — where the data came from, how it was measured or calibrated, what assumptions were used, what range it is valid over, and what decisions it is intended to support.”
That context matters most when the model is abstracted or encrypted. A model useful for architecture exploration may not be trustworthy for final closure, and a surrogate built inside one process window doesn’t automatically stay predictive after the package changes. The output alone gives the engineer no indication that the original promise no longer applies.
The practical answer isn’t to demand that everything become visible. It’s to make the model’s useful behavior and its limits visible enough that the company receiving it can decide whether it applies.
Supplier boundaries won’t disappear, and neither will the competitive value of the processes behind them. In many cases those proprietary details are exactly why a customer selected the supplier in the first place. What’s changing is how much engineering information can stop at the boundary with them. A traditional black box could hide both the process and most of its behavior because the customer mainly needed a specification. A model shared into a tightly coupled package has to conceal the recipe while leaving enough of its consequences visible for someone else to make a defensible decision.
Conclusion
For years, the black box was a workable bargain. A supplier could protect how something was made, the customer could design around a specification, and enough margin usually existed between the two to absorb what neither side could see. Advanced packaging is narrowing that margin because the behavior of one piece increasingly depends on what happened to another before the two ever met.
That doesn’t make proprietary process knowledge less valuable. If anything, the process may become more valuable as packages demand materials, assembly methods, and manufacturing windows tuned to a particular architecture. But the model now has to carry something the old specification often didn’t — enough evidence about what that hidden process does, where that behavior changes, and when the representation should no longer be trusted.
The companies that solve this best probably won’t be the ones that share the most. They’ll be the ones that can turn proprietary process knowledge into models other engineers can use without being able to reconstruct what’s underneath. The recipe can stay private, but the consequences cannot.

articles.title: Google Genie 4 : créer un monde avec l'IA ne suffit plus, vous pouvez désormais le transformer en direct
articles.text:
Google DeepMind dévoile Genie 4, un modèle de monde capable de générer du son nativement et de modifier une simulation en cours avec de simples phrases. Pour l’instant, seuls des testeurs triés sur le volet y ont accès.
Avec Genie 4, taper sur son clavier « il se met à pleuvoir » ou « un passant entre dans la scène » suffit à transformer un monde simulé en direct, sans relancer la simulation. DeepMind a présenté le modèle le 27 octobre 2026, un peu plus d’un an après Genie 3, qui ne permettait pas encore ce type de retouche à la volée.
Modifier la météo, la caméra ou les personnages en pleine simulation
Le principe tient en une phrase : on navigue au clavier dans le monde généré, et des consignes écrites servent à le faire évoluer. Météo, angle de caméra, nouveau personnage, nouvel objet : Gemini adapte la consigne au contexte de la scène, puis surveille son déroulement entre deux instructions pour que l’ensemble reste cohérent. Selon Google, les expériences durent désormais environ deux minutes, contre une minute pour Genie 3.
Cette boucle repose sur Gemini 3.8 Flash, qui joue le rôle de chef d’orchestre : il découpe un objectif en étapes, examine les images à mesure qu’elles arrivent et vérifie que chaque étape a bien abouti. Autrement dit, Genie dessine le monde pendant que Gemini garde le fil de l’histoire. Dans une expérience liée à Gemini Robotics, un modèle Gemini 4 Argon a ainsi décomposé une tâche (une partie de dames jouée par le robot humanoïde Apollo d’Apptronik) en étapes simulées par Genie 4 en temps réel.
Du son natif et des dialogues qui s’adaptent à la scène
C’est la vraie rupture face à Genie 3 : Genie 4 est le premier modèle de monde temps réel de DeepMind à générer l’audio nativement. Chaque univers porte l’ambiance sonore de son décor, du vent dans les arbres aux vagues sur la plage, avec de la musique et des bruits ambiants produits en même temps que l’image. Les personnages peuvent aussi converser et réagir à vos actions ou aux événements du monde, le tout en direct.
DeepMind annonce par ailleurs une physique plus convaincante (aérodynamique, collisions) et des humains au comportement plus naturel, présentés comme le plus gros bond de cette génération. Les vidéos et l’audio produits seront marqués avec SynthID, le filigrane invisible de Google.
Accès restreint et dérive visuelle
Genie 4 est disponible en préversion de recherche pour des « trusted testers ». Il doit arriver dans les semaines à venir chez les abonnés Google AI Ultra via Project Genie, ainsi que chez des partenaires en accès anticipé de l’API Gemini et de Google AI Studio. Une liste d’attente est ouverte pour Project Genie. Aucun tarif n’a été communiqué.
Google reconnaît que les détails visuels et la permanence des objets peuvent dériver, surtout quand la simulation dure, après plusieurs retouches complexes ou en se déplaçant dans la scène. La précision de l’audio, la lisibilité des textes et la cohérence sur la durée restent des chantiers de recherche. Côté usages, les testeurs explorent la prévisualisation de films, le prototypage de jeux et la génération de scénarios pour la simulation.

articles.title: CISA warns of hackers now exploiting critical Node2Shell flaw
articles.text:
On Tuesday, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) confirmed that hackers have begun exploiting a critical Brotli vulnerability known as Node2Shell, Broccoli2Shell, and HTTP2Shell.
Tracked as CVE-2026-111497, this critical-severity flaw stems from an out-of-bounds write weakness in the Brotli decoder used to expand data compressed with Google's widely popular Brotli lossless compression algorithm.
Unprivileged attackers can use a maliciously crafted Brotli-compressed stream to trigger crashes or memory leaks and, in some cases, gain remote code execution on devices with vulnerable Brotli libraries or binaries.
The security issue was first identified in the Node.js JavaScript runtime environment, but it also affects HTTP servers and clients that rely on vulnerable Brotli implementations.
On Sunday, Microsoft also pushed an emergency .NET security update, warning that attackers could exploit it to escalate privileges on systems with a vulnerable .NET version.
CISA added the flaw to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities (KEV) Catalog on Tuesday and ordered US government agencies to patch their systems within two weeks, by November 10, as mandated by its Binding Operational Directive (BOD) 26-04.
"Google Brotli contains an unchecked return value vulnerability that allows a remote unauthenticated attacker to corrupt adjacent decoder state memory, disclose sensitive memory contents, cause a denial of service, or potentially execute arbitrary code using a crafted Brotli-compressed stream," it said.
"These types of vulnerabilities are a frequent attack vector for malicious cyber actors and pose significant risks to the federal enterprise."
While CISA's BOD 26-04 applies only to federal agencies, the cybersecurity agency urged all network defenders to prioritize patching this security flaw to block incoming attacks.
Security teams that can't apply the updates immediately should block incoming Brotli-compressed requests at the proxy or firewall level, or disable the Brotli decoding feature until they can update.
After patching, administrators must also restart affected processes and rebuild and redeploy affected container images.
Once attackers have valid credentials, only 37% of their actions are blocked
Overall prevention scores can hide what happens after initial access. Once attackers are using valid credentials, prevention drops sharply.

articles.title: Ce SUV électrique chinois devient éligible au bonus écologique en France grâce à Stellantis
articles.text:
Le constructeur chinois est bien aidé dans son implantation en Europe par Stellantis. En effet, la marque chinoise est gérée en Europe par Stellantis sous une société appelée Leapmotor International, dont Stellantis est actionnaire majoritaire. Le groupe franco-italien ne compte pas qu’importer les Leapmotor en Europe : les produire dans ses usines est aussi un projet important pour la réussite de la marque, et un modèle vient justement de profiter de cette stratégie pour devenir beaucoup plus intéressant en France et en Europe.
De nouveaux modèles produits en Espagne
Stellantis a trouvé de la place dans ses usines pour les modèles Leapmotor. L’usine espagnole de Saragosse, produisant actuellement pour le groupe la Peugeot 208, l’Opel Corsa ou encore la Lancia Ypsilon, vient de voir arriver le Leapmotor B10. Il s’agit d’un SUV compact d’origine chinoise désormais assemblé par Stellantis en Espagne pour le marché européen.
Mais ce n’est pas tout, Stellantis prévoit d’ajouter à l’usine de Saragosse dans les prochaines semaines la Leapmotor B05, une berline compacte électrique dont le prix pourrait défier toute concurrence. Pour Stellantis, cela assure l’occupation de son appareil industriel, que ce soit ses chaînes de production, mais aussi ses collaborateurs. Tandis que pour Leapmotor, cela permet d’avoir des produits plus concurrentiels en Europe, évitant les barrières à l’entrée que l’Union européenne a mises en place pour les constructeurs chinois.
Un nouveau SUV électrique chinois éligible au bonus écologique
En profitant de sa production en Espagne, le Leapmotor B10 peut prétendre désormais au bonus écologique en France, ce qui peut créer de l’inquiétude du côté des constructeurs européens qui luttent contre les nouvelles marques chinoises.
Et cela n’a pas traîné puisque le Leapmotor B10 valide déjà l’éco-score, précieux sésame pour profiter du coup de pouce CEE en France. Pourtant, cet éco-score a été pensé justement pour éviter de financer des véhicules électriques chinois, enfin davantage des véhicules électriques produits en dehors de l’Europe, visant intrinsèquement les constructeurs chinois très agressifs face aux constructeurs européens. Il y avait une volonté de la France de favoriser les constructeurs français et européens avec cet éco-score que vient de déjouer Stellantis, constructeur ayant pourtant intérêt à ne pas voir la concurrence chinoise s’installer.
En aidant à l’obtention de l’éco-score de 3 650 à 7 000 € pour le Leapmotor B10, on peut dire que Stellantis a fait entrer le loup dans la bergerie. D’autant que ce lieu de production en Espagne évite également la taxe d’importation en Europe majorée pour les voitures électriques produites en Chine. Le Leapmotor B10 passe désormais à 25 750 euros pour tous, en déduisant le bonus de 3 650 euros, ou 22 400 euros avec le bonus pour les foyers modestes.
À ce prix, le Leapmotor B10 Life Pro embarque une batterie de 60,8 kWh pour une autonomie de 400 km WLTP. Leapmotor vient récemment d’améliorer la capacité de la batterie. En haut de gamme, il y a la version Pro Max, qui utilise une batterie de 68,7 kWh pour 450 km d’autonomie WLTP. Les autonomies ne sont pas impressionnantes, mais elles sont plus que raisonnables pour les prix auxquels sont proposées les variantes du Leapmotor B10. Et pire encore pour la concurrence européenne, la Leapmotor B05 devrait également avoir droit prochainement au bonus écologique, réduisant encore son prix déjà très agressif.

articles.title: Bouygues Telecom propose une box 5G en Wi-Fi 7 sans engagement, à brancher et c’est tout — Frandroid
articles.text:
La fibre n’arrive pas encore partout, et certains logements restent coincés avec un ADSL poussif. Bouygues Telecom propose une alternative simple, la 5G box. Elle capte le réseau mobile 5G de l’opérateur et le diffuse en Wi-Fi dans le logement, sans raccordement ni intervention d’un technicien. Elle est proposée à 29,99 euros par mois pendant douze mois, puis 39,99 euros, sans engagement.
Une version avec TV existe aussi à 34,99 euros par mois la première année, et les moins de 26 ans profitent d’un tarif réduit. Cette box est actuellement bien positionnée sur notre comparateur de box internet.
Cette 5G Box en bref :
- Internet en 5G sur le réseau de Bouygues Telecom, jusqu’à 1,1 Gb/s en téléchargement et 175 Mb/s en envoi
- Wi-Fi 7 bi-bande
- Sans engagement, sans raccordement
- 29,99 euros par mois pendant 12 mois, puis 39,99 euros
- Version avec TV à 34,99 euros par mois pendant 12 mois, puis 44,99 euros
En ce moment, la 5G box de Bouygues Telecom est disponible à 29,99 euros par mois pendant 12 mois, directement sur le site de Bouygues Telecom.

Une box internet qui se passe de la fibre
Le fonctionnement de la 5G box est simple. Elle se branche sur une prise électrique et capte le réseau 5G de Bouygues Telecom, sur la bande des 3,5 GHz, pour le redistribuer en Wi-Fi. Pas de prise téléphonique, pas de câble à tirer, pas de rendez-vous avec un technicien. Bouygues Telecom annonce un débit maximum théorique de 1,1 Gb/s en téléchargement et 175 Mb/s en envoi, selon les fréquences disponibles. C’est largement de quoi regarder plusieurs vidéos en 4K en même temps, télétravailler en visio ou jouer en ligne.
Cette box intéressera d’abord les foyers qui ne sont pas encore éligibles à la fibre ou qui subissent un ADSL lent. Elle peut aussi convenir à une résidence secondaire ou à un logement occupé une partie de l’année, puisqu’elle est sans engagement. Avant de souscrire, un test d’éligibilité en ligne permet de vérifier que l’adresse est couverte en 5G. Selon le baromètre nPerf de septembre 2026, le réseau de Bouygues Telecom arrive deuxième en couverture 5G, avec un indice de 72,34 %, juste derrière SFR.
Le Wi-Fi 7, la TV en option et un tarif pour les moins de 26 ans
La 5G box est compatible avec le Wi-Fi 7 bi-bande, présenté par Bouygues Telecom comme jusqu’à deux fois plus rapide que le Wi-Fi 6. Pour la télévision, la version 5G box avec TV donne accès à plus de 180 chaînes en 4K HDR via la clé b.tv, avec plus de 30 chaînes en replay et 100 heures d’enregistrement. Un répéteur Wi-Fi 7 est fourni sur demande avec cette version. Elle coûte 34,99 euros par mois pendant douze mois, puis 44,99 euros.
Les 18-25 ans profitent d’une offre dédiée à 25,99 euros par mois au lieu de 29,99 euros, valable jusqu’à la veille de leurs 26 ans, avec le très haut débit 5G en illimité. Pour tout le monde, il faut prévoir 29 euros de frais de mise en service à la souscription, et 29 euros en cas de résiliation.

Il suffit de récupérer son code RIO en appelant gratuitement le 3179 depuis sa ligne fixe, puis de le transmettre au nouvel opérateur lors de la souscription.
