articles.title: 👨🏿🚀TechCabal Daily – Safaricom cleans house - TechCabal
articles.text:
It’s Day 1 at Moonshot 2026! ☀️
Let’s talk at Moonshot!
You’ve been reading our stories. Now, we’d love to hear yours.
If you’re attending Moonshot today, we’re inviting TC Daily readers to sit down with members of the TechCabal newsroom for a conversation.
Bring us an African tech story you’re trying to understand, a question you’ve been meaning to ask, or even a take of ours you disagree with. We’d love to talk about it.
We’re setting aside a few 15-minute slots at the TechCabal booth on October 28 and 29. Pick a time that works for you, tell us what you’d like to discuss, and we’ll see you there.
Read smart insights about Francophone Africa’s tech ecosystem—weekly.
Banking
FirstRand goes bank shopping in Kenya, again
FirstRand has spent about 14 years window-shopping Kenya’s banking sector. The South African banking group may finally be ready to buy.
What happened? FirstRand, the parent company of First National Bank (FNB) and Rand Merchant Bank (RMB), has stepped up its search for a Kenyan lender. Mary Vilakazi, the bank’s chief executive officer, said the group would rather buy a smaller bank at the right price and grow it than pay a premium for one of Kenya’s biggest lenders.
No target has been named. FirstRand is also looking beyond banking at businesses such as insurance and investment banking as it tries to build a broader East African operation.
Explain like I’m new here: FirstRand is not new to Kenya. In 2012, it opened a representative office in Nairobi, mainly through RMB, to arrange infrastructure and project-finance deals. But a representative office cannot take deposits or run a full retail bank.
Even then, FirstRand said it wanted to buy a mid-sized Kenyan lender. It never did. High valuations made acquisitions difficult, so the group spent years operating on the market’s edges instead.
Between the lines: Kenyan banks made KES 241.65 billion ($1.9 billion) in combined profits last year, up 16.3%. At the same time, smaller lenders are under pressure to build enough capital to meet a KES 10 billion ($77 million) minimum by 2032, which could create more willing sellers.
FirstRand therefore does not need to win a bidding war for a trophy bank. Buying a smaller lender would give it a banking licence, deposits, and customers, then let it add FNB’s retail products and RMB’s corporate business over time.
Zoom out: South Africa’s banks are crowding into Kenya. Nedbank has completed its 66% acquisition of NCBA, while Standard Bank already operates Stanbic and is looking for more scale.
FirstRand has watched Kenya for more than a decade. The interesting part now is whether rising consolidation finally produces a bank at a price it is willing to pay.
Upgrade your business today
Pay with OPay is live on Fincra. Customers approve payments straight from their OPay wallet, and you get confirmation back on your site. Available now for NGN collections! Upgrade your business today with Fincra pay with OPay.
Companies
Safaricom fires 118 employees over fraud
Safaricom fired 118 employees for fraud in the year to March, roughly one every three days. It is the fourth year in a row that the number has risen at Kenya’s largest telecom company and M-PESA’s operator.
What happened? Dismissals jumped from 113 in the previous year. Safaricom also issued three disciplinary warnings and referred 14 cases to law enforcement. The misconduct included theft, falsifying company records, and unauthorised access to customer call records.
Safaricom separately recovered KES 953 million ($7.4 million) in inflated commissions paid to agents after its monitoring systems flagged irregular payments. The company has not linked those recoveries directly to the 118 employees who were fired.
Explain like I’m new here: Fraud is particularly sensitive at Safaricom because the company sits on much more than phone records. M-Pesa processed KES 41.68 trillion ($323 billion) across 46.4 billion transactions in the year to March. Employees, dealers and agents can therefore access customer identities, SIM registrations and a payments network used by tens of millions of people.
Safaricom has dealt with insider fraud for years, including unauthorised system access, fraudulent SIM swaps and misuse of M-PESA processes. It has steadily added automated monitoring and machine-learning tools to catch suspicious activity.
Between the lines: More dismissals do not automatically mean fraud is getting worse. Safaricom has expanded the operations its fraud reporting covered in recent years, while better analytics can uncover misconduct that previously went unnoticed.
A more useful measure is whether actual losses and successful attacks fall. Safaricom says its new SIM-swap system, which runs 18 automated checks before a line can be replaced, has already cut fraudulent swaps by 65%.
What to watch: Safaricom is increasingly taking sensitive decisions away from individual employees and agents and putting them into automated systems. If those controls work, future fraud reports should eventually show more than people getting caught. They should show fewer successful fraud attempts in the first place.
More value with Mycoverai
You already have a great product. With MyCover.ai, create tailored insurance for your customers across fintech, e-commerce, logistics and more, built around your product, and their needs. Get started here.
Fintech
Moniepoint is restructuring its engineering and product teams
On October 19, Moniepoint, a Nigerian fintech unicorn, informed employees of an internal restructuring affecting roles across backend, frontend, mobile, quality assurance, and product management. The company says some positions will become redundant as it moves to smaller teams that own products from start to finish. Moniepoint has offered affected employees five months’ salary to leave voluntarily, while saying it will first look for suitable roles elsewhere in the business. The company has not disclosed how many employees will be affected.
Explain like I’m new here: Moniepoint became a unicorn in 2024 after raising $110 million, bought a 78% stake in Kenya’s Sumac Microfinance Bank in March, and says its subsidiaries now process more than $400 billion in annual digital payments. In October, one employee said the company hired more than 120 people, while Moniepoint has previously said it was struggling to fill hundreds of senior technical roles. However, in August, Moniepoint phased out MonieWorld, its UK-Nigeria remittance product, less than 18 months after launch.
Why the restructuring? The fintech says the restructuring is part of a regular strategic review as the business moves into its next growth stage. It is moving to a platform-group model, where smaller teams own specific product areas, and it is also creating platform architect roles to oversee the shared technology underneath those teams. The restructuring and growth reflect a company still expanding, but becoming more selective about where it puts people and money.
The bigger picture: Moniepoint is also joining a tech-industry shift towards smaller teams. Block, the parent company of Square and Cash App, cut about 40% of its workforce earlier this year, citing AI and a leaner organisational structure. Jumia and Zap Africa have also tied workforce changes to efficiency and AI. Moniepoint says AI is not the reason for this restructuring, although the company has discussed internally how AI could streamline product-management work.
Don’t miss Moonshot 2026 for anything in the world!
True scale demands moving beyond surface-level integrations to robust execution. We’ve filtered the noise out of Moonshot 2026, optimising the conference strictly for high-calibre connections between startup founders, global financial operators, enterprise leaders and individuals rewiring Africa’s technical frameworks. Join us on October 28 & 29, 2026. Get your ticket.
Funding
South Africa’s CrissCross gets Circle backing for stablecoin expansion
Stablecoins are having their moment in African payments, and Circle, the company behind USDC, is backing the infrastructure that wants to make them actually useful.
What happened? CrissCross, a South African cross-border payments company, has received an undisclosed investment from Circle Ventures, Circle’s corporate venture arm. The investment was made through CrissCross’s parent company, Stitch Group. The money will help CrissCross expand its payment connections and liquidity across Africa, while building out stablecoin settlement for enterprise customers.
Explain like I’m new here: Stablecoins such as USDC are digital tokens designed to maintain a stable value against a currency, usually the US dollar. That makes them useful for moving dollar value between markets. African fintechs are beginning to build around this idea.
Flutterwave announced a Circle Ventures investment in July and added USDC settlement to its payments platform. Onafriq has also been working with Circle on regulated stablecoin settlement across its network of more than 40 African markets. CrissCross partnered with Velocity in October to connect institutional stablecoin liquidity to local collections and FX across more than 30 African markets.
Why Circle is interested: Every new payment platform that builds USDC into its infrastructure potentially creates another route for the stablecoin to move through the financial system. Sub-Saharan Africa also received more than $205 billion in on-chain crypto value between July 2024 and June 2025.
CrissCross says it operates across more than 30 markets and supports more than 20 currencies. The investment should help it deepen those local connections and give enterprises more ways to move between stablecoins and local currencies.

articles.title: From human clicks to agentic velocity: What OpenAI’s 1.2 billion scale means for your auth
articles.text:
From human clicks to agentic velocity: What OpenAI’s 1.2 billion scale means for your auth
When OpenAI announced at DevDay that ChatGPT had crossed 1.2 billion weekly active users (WAUs), roughly 15% of the human population, most engineering discussions naturally centered on model context windows, compute clusters, and distributed GPU inference.
However, behind every chat session, API call, and model invocation sits an equally monumental infrastructure challenge: Identity and Access Management (IAM) at extreme web scale.
“Behind every chat session, API call, and model invocation sits an equally monumental infrastructure challenge: Identity and Access Management (IAM) at extreme web scale.”
Before OpenAI can serve a token from an LLM, its backend systems must authenticate the request, validate OAuth2 access tokens, inspect fine-grained permissions, and maintain secure session contexts globally. To manage this massive transaction volume without introducing latency bottlenecks, OpenAI turned to Ory, utilizing its lightweight, decoupled authentication engine and OAuth2/OIDC infrastructure.
Here is an architectural breakdown of how identity scale shifts when moving from human traffic to agent workloads, why legacy IAM platforms break at this volume, and how decoupled, edge-ready authorization handles extreme throughput.
The scale problem: human traffic vs. agentic workloads
To understand why traditional IAM platforms fail at extreme scale, consider how user authentication patterns change as architectures evolve from standard web applications to agentic AI platforms.
“When an enterprise moves from human-initiated UI clicks to autonomous AI agents… the ratio of token validations to human interactions scales non-linearly.”
When an enterprise moves from human-initiated UI clicks to autonomous AI agents (e.g., OpenAI’s Work and Codex suites), the ratio of token validations to human interactions scales non-linearly:
- Transaction velocity: A single user request to an AI agent can trigger dozens of downstream sub-tasks, database queries, and third-party API tool calls. Each step requires session verification and token introspection.
- Token introspection overhead: Legacy central identity providers (IdPs) typically validate access tokens via centralized RPCs or database lookups. At billions of requests per minute, centralized introspection introduces severe network hops and database lock contention.
- Stateless edge verification: To prevent authorization from becoming the primary bottleneck in the request path, session validation must happen synchronously at the edge using lightweight cryptographic verification (such as JSON Web Key Sets / JWKS caching) rather than stateful network calls.
Architectural comparison: modern composable IAM vs. legacy monolithic SaaS
When evaluating identity platforms for ultra-high throughput, engineering teams frequently hit performance and cost walls with traditional multi-tenant identity SaaS products (e.g., Auth0, Okta, Ping Identity).
| Architectural dimension | Legacy monolithic identity SaaS | Self-hosted composable IAM (e.g., Ory) | 
| Token validation mechanism | Centralized IdP round-trips or heavy server-side SDKs | Edge-native stateless JWT validation & local session caching | 
| Data residency & ownership | User store hosted in vendor-managed SaaS clouds | Complete data sovereignty (runs directly in your VPC / multi-cloud k8s) | 
| Database persistence strategy | Proprietary SaaS database clusters subject to vendor rate limits | Highly available distributed SQL layers (e.g., CockroachDB, Spanner, Postgres) | 
| Cost scaling model | Per Monthly Active User (MAU) or per-API request execution fees | Infrastructure-based scaling; cost correlates with compute/memory footprint | 
| Customizability & velocity | Restricted to vendor webhooks, rules, or custom code sandboxes | Go-native microservices with clean API boundaries and headless UI integration | 
“OpenAI wanted a partner that could help enable our vision for owning our identity processes, data, and success. We have a lot of partners, and Ory is one of our best.”
- Benjamin Billings, Engineering Manager, OpenAI (Case study)
Key infrastructure requirements for billion-user identity systems
Securing identity at scale requires a clear separation of concerns across the auth stack. Based on high-throughput deployments like OpenAI’s, modern identity architectures depend on four core principles:
1. Separation of identity state from business logic
Monolithic frameworks often bind user profiles, authentication state, and business roles together in single relational databases. High-throughput architectures decouple these responsibilities into distinct microservices:
- Identity storage & auth engines: Dedicated microservices handling identity lifecycle, credential hashing, and session management (e.g., Ory Kratos).
- OAuth2 / OIDC token issuance: High-performance OAuth2 server implementations capable of issuing signed access tokens and managing grant flows with minimal latency (e.g., Ory Hydra).
- Fine-grained access control (FGAC): Relationship-based access control engines based on Google’s Zanzibar model (e.g., Ory Keto) to evaluate tuple relationships (ObjectRelationSubject) in sub-millisecond execution times.
2. Distributed persistence across cloud regions
To support global edge routing, the underlying storage layer must support geo-distributed writes and low-latency local reads. Combining a self-hosted identity engine with distributed SQL engines (such as CockroachDB or cloud-native multi-region databases) ensures token-verification state can be replicated globally without split-brain risks or cross-continental network latency.
3. Agent security: transitioning from “enforce first” to “observe mode”
As enterprises deploy autonomous agents that execute commands on users’ behalf, writing restrictive IAM policies immediately can break workflows or cause silent failures. Modern security practices emphasize runtime observability before strict policy enforcement:
- Step 1: agent fingerprinting: Map every machine-to-machine (M2M) credential and agent service account operating across internal networks.
- Step 2: execution tracing: Audit tool usage, API invocations, and database queries initiated by autonomous runtimes.
- Step 3: identity delegation: Implement scoped OAuth2 Token Exchange (RFC 8693) to ensure agents operate under strict downscoped permissions tied directly to the delegating human user.
For a limited time, you can create a complimentary Ory account and turn on observe mode to learn how best to build enforcement.
“Scaling authentication to 1.2 billion weekly active users proves that identity is no longer just a security checkbox; it is a core distributed systems challenge.”
Scaling authentication to 1.2 billion weekly active users proves that identity is no longer just a security checkbox; it is a core distributed systems challenge.
As software shifts from human-driven UI interactions to high-velocity AI agent execution, engineering teams must evaluate whether their identity stack can handle exponential API volume. Decoupled, stateless-first identity engines offer the low latency, data sovereignty, and predictability modern platforms need to scale into the agentic era.

articles.title: Dona do Google fica abaixo das expectativas e acende alerta sobre gastos com IA
articles.text:
A Alphabet, controladora do Google, registrou receita de US$ 127,58 bilhões no terceiro trimestre de 2026, alta de 25% em relação ao mesmo período do ano anterior. O resultado, divulgado nesta quarta-feira (28), ficou abaixo dos US$ 128,22 bilhões esperados por analistas consultados pela LSEG. O lucro por ação ajustado também decepcionou, com US$ 2,67, ante previsão de US$ 3,02.
O balanço mostrou ainda um fluxo de caixa livre negativo de US$ 9,07 bilhões. Após a divulgação dos resultados, os papéis da Alphabet recuaram mais de 10% nas negociações após o fechamento do mercado, em meio a preocupações com os investimentos em inteligência artificial (IA) e a expectativa de retorno financeiro.
Alphabet prevê aumento dos gastos com IA em 2027
Os investimentos de capital (capex) da Alphabet somaram US$ 51,36 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, abaixo dos US$ 55,09 bilhões projetados por analistas. A empresa manteve a previsão de investir entre US$ 195 bilhões e US$ 205 bilhões em 2026, após elevar a estimativa no trimestre anterior.
Para 2027, a companhia espera um aumento significativo nos investimentos, que devem superar US$ 300 bilhões. A diretora financeira da Alphabet, Anat Ashkenazi, afirmou durante uma teleconferência com analistas que a empresa fornecerá mais detalhes sobre os planos na apresentação dos resultados do quarto trimestre.
A companhia também ampliou seu endividamento de longo prazo. O indicador chegou a US$ 125,1 bilhões no terceiro trimestre, ante US$ 21,6 bilhões no mesmo período de 2025, uma alta de aproximadamente 479%.
Receita de buscas fica abaixo das projeções
A receita da Alphabet com buscas cresceu 12% na comparação anual e alcançou US$ 63,35 bilhões. O valor, porém, ficou abaixo da estimativa de US$ 64,96 bilhões. Segundo o CEO Sundar Pichai, os investimentos em IA contribuíram para que o volume de consultas registrasse o maior ritmo de crescimento em cinco anos.
O lucro operacional foi de US$ 40,58 bilhões, abaixo dos US$ 43,19 bilhões esperados, segundo a FactSet. Já as participações acionárias da Alphabet, que haviam gerado um ganho de US$ 99,03 bilhões no segundo trimestre, passaram a representar uma perda de US$ 8,66 bilhões no terceiro.
Google Cloud cresce e Gemini chega a 1 bilhão de usuários
A divisão Google Cloud registrou receita de US$ 30,7 bilhões, mais que o dobro do valor do mesmo período do ano anterior. O resultado superou a estimativa de US$ 28,7 bilhões dos analistas e foi impulsionado pela demanda por serviços de inteligência artificial.
O CEO do Google Cloud, Thomas Kurian, afirmou que a empresa observa demanda de laboratórios de IA, instituições financeiras e outras companhias. A divisão também vem ampliando sua participação de mercado em concorrência com Amazon Web Services e Microsoft Azure.
Outro destaque foi o aplicativo Gemini, que chegou a 1 bilhão de usuários. Segundo a Alphabet, ele é o produto de crescimento mais rápido da história da companhia. Pichai também afirmou que o modelo Carbon, anunciado nesta quarta-feira, supera o Argon em quase todos os domínios, segundo avaliações internas da empresa.
Ana Figueiredo é editora de tecnologia do Olhar Digital. É formada em Jornalismo pela Universidade Federal de Uberlândia (UFU).

articles.text:
Baratinho: Galaxy Fit 3 para treinos fica abaixo dos R$ 200 em oferta
Galaxy Fit monitora mais de 100 exercícios e tem resistência à água; pulseira inteligente da Samsung recebe 66% OFF no Mercado Livre
O Galaxy Fit 3 está saindo por apenas R$ 189 no Pix no Mercado Livre. A oferta representa um desconto de 66% sobre o preço original de R$ 549 pelo smartband da Samsung, que é uma das principais opções custo-benefício para quem busca uma pulseira inteligente para monitorar os treinos na academia.
O Galaxy Fit 3 é uma das melhores opções do mercado atualmente para quem procura um relógio para treinos baratinho. articles.title: Barcelona’s Artiso raises over €3 million to scale its AI operating system for fashion teams | EU-Startups
articles.text:
Artiso, a Barcelona-based FashionTech startup building an AI operating system built for fashion teams, has raised more than €3 million in a fully equity pre-Seed round.
Criteria Venture Tech led the round and has supported the company since it emerged from stealth. Swanlaab Venture Factory and Bynd Venture Capital joined the round, alongside business angels David Tomás, co-founder of Cyberclick, and Nicolaj Reffstrup, founder and former CEO of GANNI, who invests through Look Up Ventures.
“I spent years leading creative teams that had to orchestrate every step of a collection across tools that never spoke to each other. So we built the operating system we always needed: one that knows each brand’s archive, its customers and its taste, and that is already running inside fashion companies today. AI is changing how every collection is imagined, made and shown, and with Artiso, creativity, not complexity, defines fashion’s next era,” said Sarah Iglesias Hiller, co-founder and CEO, Artiso.
Artiso was founded in Barcelona in 2025 by Iglesias Hiller, Lucas Pastur Romay (CPO) and Matthias Brenninkmeijer (CTO), former Mango executives who have worked together since 2022.
The company emerged from stealth in July 2025 and claims to be building an AI operating system for fashion that connects inspiration, design, product development, and pre-production, including tech packs, styling, and campaign imagery, on top of each brand’s own memory.
According to the Spanish startup, fashion is one of the industries where AI can make the maximum impact, as the sector designs so many products and undergoes constant change season after season.
“Artiso’s vision is to redefine how fashion brands create, end to end. Today that work is spread across disconnected tools: product lifecycle management (PLM) systems, design software, image generators, shared drives, spreadsheets and email. Every season, part of what a brand has learned is lost along the way: which shapes sold, which colours worked, what was designed two seasons ago,” the company mentioned in the press release.
Artiso claims to bring that work and that knowledge together, using agentic AI to transform the process from the first idea to the final campaign. The company says it is designed for creatives, with a visual, intuitive platform built around how fashion teams actually work.
Its agentic AI takes collections from inspiration and moodboards to design and flat sketches, product development and pre-production such as tech packs, virtual models, on-model imagery, packshots and campaign content.
“We designed Artiso for the people who make fashion: creative directors, designers, pattern makers, merchandisers. It is intuitive, it remembers each brand and adapts to how every team works, and it connects every step, from the first moodboard to the tech pack and the campaign, in one operating system,” commented Pastur Romay.
The startup says a brand memory and ontology sits beneath everything, capturing each brand’s archive, bestsellers, seasonal direction, and visual codes, so every output is hyper-personalised to the brand’s DNA.
It highlights that a complete tech pack takes around four minutes instead of two to six hours. Artiso connects the whole process end to end, with creative direction, design, pattern making, product development, visual merchandising, and marketing, all working in the same operating system.
Brenninkmeijer said, “Fashion imagery is where AI first proved its value, and Artiso takes it further: every image, sketch and tech pack is created with an understanding of the brand behind it. Our agents combine state-of-the-art generation with each brand’s own knowledge, while people stay in control of every decision. That is what turns AI from a tool into a new way of working.”
The company plans to use the new capital to accelerate development of its operating system, expand the team, and support customers’ enterprise rollouts. To do that, Artiso is hiring across fashion and technology. Its team’s expertise spans garment technology, pattern making, design, art direction, motion, and data science.
Artiso reported that it already works with mid-sized to enterprise brands with strong identities, from fast-growing players in full transformation to established category leaders and luxury houses, as well as the retailers and manufacturers behind them. Its customers span Europe, North America and Asia, with the US as a key market. The new funding will help it bring more of them on board.

articles.title: Trump DOE loans $5B to nuclear plants that will power data centers | TechCrunch
articles.text:
The Trump administration is giving Constellation Energy $5 billion in loans to expand nuclear generating capacity at eight power plants by 1.1 gigawatts.
Most or all of the additional power from seven of those facilities has already been bought by Google, Meta, or Amazon.
Constellation said it plans to use the financing to “uprate” 11 existing reactors, an industry term for expanding capacity at a reactor, often by using more highly enriched uranium and by upgrading equipment to handle the increased power levels.
The energy company said it had already committed to spending more than $7 billion to add 1,080 megawatts of nuclear capacity to deliver power to Google, Amazon, and Meta. The loan commitment, which has yet to be finalized, “could lower financing costs” for the projects, Constellation said in a press release.
The eight power plants include six in Illinois (Braidwood, Byron, Clinton, Dresden, La Salle, and Quad Cities), one in Maryland (Calvert Cliffs), and one in Pennsylvania (Limerick).
Google is already the confirmed buyer of additional power from the Pennsylvania plant and four Illinois power plants, while Amazon is buying electricity from the Maryland plant and Meta is effectively buying the entire Clinton power plant in Illinois.
On Tuesday, the Department of Energy touted the loan as supporting “affordable, reliable power to American homes and businesses,” though there is no evidence that the new nuclear capacity will lower prices for residential ratepayers. Constellation’s announcement does not say whether the projects will maintain or lower electricity rates, and the company would not confirm the government’s claim to TechCrunch.
Hyperscalers, including Google, Amazon, and Meta, have been scouring the grid for additional capacity to support their AI data centers. Tech companies are paying handsomely for energy, committing tens of billions of dollars over the coming years. Given that power has become a competitive advantage, that estimate is probably on the low end.
By lowering the cost of capital for the upgrades, the Department of Energy’s loans could boost Constellation’s bottom line, that of the hyperscalers — or both.

articles.title: Endlich Ruhe im Büro: Dieser Meeting-Simulator täuscht Video-Calls vor
articles.text:
Meeting-Simulator: So täuschst du wichtige Video-Calls vor
Wer am Freitagnachmittag vor dem PC im Büro sitzt und alle Arbeiten für die Woche abgeschlossen hat, fragt sich sicherlich: Wie bringe ich die Zeit bis zum Feierabend noch rum? Wie wäre es damit, die lieben Kolleg:innen etwas zu schocken? Etwa, indem du ein sehr wichtiges Meeting vorgaukelst, zu dem nur du eingeladen wurdest.
Funktionsweise der Meeting-Simulation für den Büroalltag
Dabei will dir die Webseite „Sorry, I’m in a meeting“ weiterhelfen. Es handelt sich im Grunde um einen Simulator für eine Reihe von wichtigen Anrufen. Diese reichen von Calls, bei denen das ganze Unternehmen für den Quartalsbericht zusammenkommt, über Meetings zu Status-Updates des aktuellen Projekts bis zu Ransomware-Krisensitzungen, weil alle Daten im Unternehmen verschlüsselt wurden.
Du trägst einfach deinen Namen in den Simulator ein, der während des Meetings in einer Videokachel angezeigt werden soll. Sobald der Fake-Termin startet, öffnet die Webseite eine Video-Call-Ansicht im Vollbild mit mehreren Fake-Personen darin. Die Videoübertragung ist dabei „deaktiviert“, sodass du nur Stimmen anderer Teilnehmer:innen hörst. Diese wurden KI-generiert. Jedes Meeting ist etwa zwölf Minuten lang, wobei du beim Starten zu unterschiedlichen Zeiten hineingeworfen wirst, sodass die Aufnahme nicht immer offensichtlich an derselben Stelle beginnt.
Anwendungsmöglichkeiten der Fake-Termine im Kalender-Management
Zudem kannst du in den Einstellungen die Option „Back-to-Back Meetings“ aktivieren. Dadurch startet nach dem Ende des ersten Meetings direkt der nächste Termin, sodass die Aufnahme nicht wieder von vorn startet. Alternativ kannst du im Meeting auf „I have to drop“ klicken. Dadurch verabschieden sich alle Fake-Teilnehmer:innen und du kannst das Meeting zu einem glaubwürdigen Ende bringen.
Die Webseite bietet sogar eine Funktion, um dir Meetings in deinem Kalender anzulegen. Du kannst im unteren Bereich der Seite ein Meeting auswählen, einen Titel sowie Datum und Uhrzeit festlegen und daraus eine ICS‑Datei oder Termineinträge für den Google-Kalender oder Outlook generieren. Dabei kannst du auch festlegen, ob ein Beitrittslink in der Mail enthalten sein soll und ob andere im Unternehmen den Terminnamen sehen können. Natürlich handelt es sich dabei um ein spaßiges Tool, das nicht wirklich aktiv zur Überbrückung der Arbeitszeit genutzt werden sollte. Aber es reicht allemal, um den anderen Kolleg:innen vorzugaukeln, man hätte ein wichtiges Meeting ohne die anderen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 16.10.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.
Gab mal eine IT-Crowd-Folge (glaub ich), wo der frisch eingestellte Manager hastig zum Telefon griff und so tat als würde er telefonieren, als jemand sein Büro betrat. Stellte sich raus, es war der Techniker, der sein Telefon anschließen sollte.

articles.title: 'VisionQuest' recupera por sorpresa a uno de los primeros villanos de Marvel: no le veíamos desde 'Iron Man'
articles.text:
ATENCIÓN: El artículo contiene SPOILERS de VisionQuest 1x06.
El estreno de los nuevos episodios de VisionQuest esta semana ha devuelto a los fans de Marvel a un personaje totalmente inesperado. La serie protagonizada por Paul Bettany sigue el camino de la nueva Visión Blanca. Atrapado en su propio conflicto interno, el personaje no es capaz de conectar emocionalmente con los recuerdos de su versión anterior. Pero no por ello dejará de intentar sentirse, de verdad, humano.
En ese camino se cruza con Tommy Shepherd, que asegura ser el hijo de Wanda y Visión. Sin embargo, el villano Paladín, cuyo nombre real es Paul Denning, le secuestra con el fin de atraer a Visión a una trampa y poder capturarle para entregárselo a su misterioso Cliente. Pero lo cierto es que esta peligrosa figura, cuya identidad sigue siendo desconocida, ha puesto punto y final al contrato que les unía.
Bajo este contexto, todos los personajes se reúnen en Madripoor. Allí, Visión y el Paladín se enfrentan en una vertiginosa escena de acción, con Tommy como recompensa. Pero, de pronto, ambos se ven sorprendidos por una banda que comienza a tirotearles. Y el líder de todos ellos no es otro que Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar. Los fans más veteranos de Marvel recordarán perfectamente a este personaje porque era el líder de la banda terrorista de los 10 Anillos que secuestraron a Tony Stark en Iron Man.
En aquella película, Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar parecía morir traicionado por Obadiah Stane, que mandaba a sus hombres para asesinarlo. Sin embargo, jamás vimos su cadáver. Y ahora, casi veinte años después, el actor Faran Tahir ha regresado como Raza en la serie de VisionQuest. Una confirmación de que este villano se ha mantenido vivo y activo en las sombras.
¿Es Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar el Cliente de VisionQuest?
Con esta impactante revelación del retorno de Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar a Marvel, muchos podrían pensar que el villano es el verdadero Cliente, el gran antagonista en las sombras de VisionQuest. Pero pronto salimos de dudas. Resulta que no, Raza no es esta misteriosa figura, sino otro de sus mercenarios.
El Cliente ha contratado a Raza y sus hombres para poner fin al desastre generado por el Paladín y, de paso, secuestrar definitivamente a Visión. De hecho, como vemos en VisionQuest 1x06, está a punto de conseguirlo. Al final, los protagonistas se salvan porque E.D.I.T.H. consigue tomar control de los drones de los terroristas. El propio Paladín es quien le da el golpe definitivo a Raza para dejarle fuera de combate.
Date de alta en Disney+ ahora y ahorra gracias a la suscripción anual, con la que podrás disfrutar de todo su catálogo de series y películas. Acceso a los últimos estrenos, al catálogo de Star y ESPN* y a los mejores documentales de National Geographic.
*ESPN solo está disponible en Latinoamérica. Ahorro respecto a 12 meses de suscripción mensual.
Tras este breve pero intenso regreso de Raza Hamidmi al-Wazar a Marvel, se desconoce si volveremos a ver al personaje en el futuro. No ha muerto, por lo que no hay nada descartado. Pero lo cierto es que todo apunta a que su retorno no era más que un guiño a los fans de la saga y una nueva manera de conectar la nueva serie al resto de la franquicia. Los dos últimos episodios de VisionQuest se estrenarán en Disney+ el 3 y el 10 de noviembre (el 4 y el 11 de noviembre en España), respectivamente.

Large-format/curvilinear masks; STCO for heterogeneous design; physical AI interactions; signing off AI-generated designs; workload profile analysis.

Arm’s Alan Chen explores how to enable source-less microarchitectural analysis using an evidence-first harness engineering approach that combines indexed workload data, bounded LLM analysis, and simulation evidence to improve optimization results.
Keysight’s Eric Yu explains why tensor parallelism is the first parallelism dimension that any scale-up fabric, whether it’s NVLink or Ethernet, must get right.

articles.title: ChatGPT, Gemini, Meta AI : l'Europe prépare un passe-droit des IA sur vos données
articles.text:
« Rien d’autre que l’expropriation numérique des Européens » : en septembre, l’association noyb, onze plaintes contre Meta AI au compteur, jugeait ainsi le projet de la présidence irlandaise du Conseil. Les Vingt-Sept sont passés outre : le mandat de négociation adopté le 21 octobre reprend la disposition, au milieu des 179 pages de l’omnibus numérique. Un futur article 88 bis du RGPD autoriserait l’entraînement et l’exploitation des IA sur des données personnelles au nom du seul « intérêt légitime », sans que les premiers concernés aient leur mot à dire.
Le droit de dire non passe à la trappe
Le périmètre couvre les publications, avis et photos accumulés depuis des années, pour le développement des modèles comme pour leur exploitation au quotidien. La Commission avait assorti sa proposition de novembre 2025 d’un garde-fou : un droit d’opposition inconditionnel, qui permettait de retirer ses données d’un entraînement sans se justifier. Le Conseil l’a supprimé. Ne reste que l’opposition classique de l’article 21 du RGPD, qu’une entreprise peut écarter en invoquant des « motifs légitimes et impérieux ». La protection particulière des enfants quitte elle aussi le corps du texte pour un simple considérant.
Santé, opinions, orientation sexuelle : les données sensibles deviennent tolérées, et leur présence dans les jeux d’entraînement ne posera pas problème tant qu’elle reste « incidente et résiduelle ». L’entreprise doit les effacer, sauf quand l’opération se révèle techniquement impossible ou exige un effort « manifestement disproportionné ». Un confinement technique suffit alors, et les CNIL européennes, qui alertaient ensemble dès le 10 février, n’ont pas été suivies.
Meta a essuyé les plâtres depuis mai 2025
Depuis le 27 mai 2025, Meta entraîne ses modèles sur les publications publiques des Européens adultes, déjà au nom de l’intérêt légitime. Des associations de consommateurs allemandes avaient tenté de bloquer la collecte en urgence : la cour d’appel de Cologne les a déboutées le 23 mai 2025, jugeant l’opération « légale, même sans le consentement des personnes concernées ». Google et OpenAI défendraient la même lecture pour nourrir Gemini et ChatGPT.
Le mandat du Conseil transforme cette interprétation disputée en règle écrite, valable pour n’importe quel acteur, de la jeune pousse au géant américain. Le volet IA s’appliquerait trois jours après la publication du règlement au Journal officiel, sans période de transition. Un considérant borne l’exercice, sur le papier : développer une IA ne constitue pas en soi un intérêt légitime, et chaque traitement s’évalue au cas par cas. Max Schrems y voit surtout « la remise totale des données européennes aux multinationales ».
Le texte reste, toutefois, une position de négociation : le Parlement européen n’a pas arrêté la sienne, et les trilogues n’ont pas de calendrier. Si l’article 88 bis survit tel quel, la logique s’inversera : vos publications passées deviendront entraînables par défaut, et dire non se plaidera dossier par dossier. Le formulaire d’opposition de chaque plateforme reste donc le levier le plus sûr, à actionner avant l’entraînement du prochain modèle. Une fois avalées par un modèle, vos données n’en ressortent plus, opposition ou pas.

articles.title: Nefilim and Hive ransomware affiliate gets 70 months in prison
articles.text:
A Ukrainian national was sentenced to 70 months in prison for his role in Nefilim and Hive ransomware attacks targeting hospitals, government entities, and high-revenue businesses worldwide between 2018 and 2021.
The sentence follows the extradition of 35-year-old Artem Aleksandrovych Stryzhak to the United States on April 30, 2025, after authorities arrested him in Spain in June 2024.
"Artem Stryzhak is a prolific cybercriminal who worked with multiple ransomware groups to target U.S. businesses and hospitals," said Brett Leatherman, the FBI's Cyber Branch Operations Director. "These groups disrupted patient care and caused more than $100 million in losses. Today's sentence reflects the seriousness of Stryzhak's crimes and demonstrates the FBI's global reach and extensive network of international partners."
According to court documents, he paid for 20% of all ransom payments collected for access to custom Nefilim ransomware and decryption keys starting in June 2021.
While active as a Nefilim affiliate until October 2021, Stryzhak used the custom-tailored malware to target large corporations in the United States, Canada, and Australia with revenues exceeding $100 million each year. However, one of the Nefilim administrators later encouraged him to focus on large companies that were generating more than $200 million annually.
To pressure victims into paying, the ransomware operation also threatened to leak data stolen during attacks on dark web "Corporate Leaks" websites managed by the Nefilim admins unless victims met the ransom demands.
Stryzhak also joined Hive ransomware as an early affiliate, breaching and encrypting the systems of seven victims, including a dentist's office, multiple law firms, and a healthcare provider during the COVID-19 pandemic.
In December 2025, Stryzhak pleaded guilty and admitted to computer fraud conspiracy charges brought by US prosecutors in connection with ransomware attacks targeting businesses in the United States, Norway, France, Switzerland, Germany, and the Netherlands.
"Disrupting a ransomware group that attacked approximately 1,500 victims worldwide and sentencing a defendant who had targeted healthcare during the COVID-19 pandemic is of significant importance to this office," added US Attorney Gregory W. Kehoe.
"Ransomware attacks like those committed by the defendant wreak enormous havoc — harming victim companies that pay millions in remediation and ransoms, preventing hospitals and other critical facilities from accessing data, and putting sensitive information in the hands of bad actors," US Attorney Joseph Nocella Jr. noted.
The US State Department also offers up to $11 million for any details that could lead to the arrest of Ukrainian national Volodymyr Tymoshchuk, one of Stryzhak's alleged accomplices, who is still at large.
Tymoshchuk is on the most-wanted lists of the European Union and the FBI, and the US Justice Department charged him in September for his roles as an administrator for the LockerGoga, MegaCortex, and Nefilim ransomware gangs. He was also allegedly involved in ransomware attacks that caused millions of dollars in damages to hundreds of companies around the world between July 2020 and October 2021.

articles.title: Apple releases iMac with M6 to make the all-in-one home computer more powerful than ever - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Apple has upgraded the iMac desktop computer with the new M6 chip to help users with everyday productivity and advanced AI performance.
The new iMac is aimed at everyday consumers and families who want a powerful home computer with remarkable capabilities to meet all your computing needs, as well as access to Apple Intelligence and Siri AI.
The iMac design has not changed – it has a 24-inch 4.5K Retina display and is still a remarkably thin and includes a keyboard and your choice of a mouse or trackpad.
It is also available in seven vibrant colours so it can transform your home or workspace.
The new M6 chip adds noticeable performance and power improvements to allow users to complete tasks like video and photo editing and play the latest games.
The display has 500 nits of brightness and the ability to display more than a billion colours.
The new iMac also has a 12MP Centre Stage camera to keep you framed and centred on video calls.
On the audio side it has two pairs of force-cancelling woofers with two tweeters that offer room-filling bold, bass-rich sound and Spatial Audio with support for Dolby Atmos you can enjoy an immersive entertainment experience.
The new iMac includes Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 along with 2.5Gb Ethernet that delivers up to 2.5 times faster wired connectivity than the previous model.
Its internal SSD (solid-state drive) has read and write performances that are two times faster than the M4 iMac.
The new iMac with M6 is available with up to four Thunderbolt 4 ports to enable fast data transfers and to connect a range of accessories, including external storage and up to two 6K external displays.
PRICING AND AVAILABILITY
The new iMac with M6 is available to preorder from October 29 and will go on sale on Friday, November 6.
Pricing for the iMac with M6 featuring a 10-core CPU and 10-core GPU starts at $2,399.

articles.title: Doblete de descuentos en el robot aspirador de Xiaomi, un Robot Vacuum H50 con base de autovaciado y navegación láser
articles.text:
Los robots aspirador son dispositivos muy prácticos para mantener una buena limpieza diaria en casa, sobre todo si tenemos un modelo completo con varias funciones de limpieza. Estos últimos suelen tener precios bastante altos, pero no tanto cuando los encontramos de oferta.
Ahora mismo Xiaomi tiene en su tienda oficial el Xiaomi Robot Vacuum H50 con un doble descuento, uno sobre el precio oficial y otro sobre su anterior oferta. Con todo ello, finalmente se queda por 299,99 euros.
Xiaomi Robot Vacuum H50
Ideal para la limpieza del día a día
El Xiaomi Robot Vacuum H50 es un robot aspirador con doble función de aspiración y fregado, lo que significa que cuenta con la capacidad de limpiar el polvo y fregar el suelo. Además, cuenta con navegación láser para mapear las habitaciones de la casa, ofreciendo así una mayor efectividad de limpieza.
Incorpora un cepillo principal y otro lateral para no dejarse suciedad en el suelo a la hora de aspirar, así como también incluye dos mopas giratorias para la función de fregado (incluye elevación inteligente para pasar por las alfombras). Para vaciar la suciedad, incluye una estación o base de autovaciado con sus propios depósitos de polvo y agua limpia y sucia.
La base de autovaciado también cuenta con función para limpiar las almohadillas de la mopa, evitando así que pueda ensuciar más que limpiar el suelo si se encontrasen sucias. Además, entre otras cosas, ofrece una potencia de succión de 10.000 Pa, cuenta con tres niveles de flujo de agua y viene con un sistema antienredos en el cepillo principal para evitar que se enrede de pelo.

articles.title: Apple dévoile son tout nouveau MacBook Pro avec Écran PROLED XDR : plus fin, plus léger et tactile — Frandroid
articles.text:
« Une catastrophe ergonomique », c’est en ces termes que Steve Jobs avait fustigé l’idée d’un écran tactile sur un PC portable lors d’une keynote d’Apple en 2010.
Seize ans plus tard, la marque désormais présidée par John Ternus a présenté son premier MacBook Pro équipé d’un écran tactile.
C’est l’aboutissement d’une longue série de présentations pour Apple. La firme a dévoilé en quelques semaines : son premier smartphone pliant, l’iPhone Duo, son premier écran connecté, Apple Homeview, sa première tablette étanche, l’iPad Oled, sans oublier les renouvellements plus classiques : l’iPhone 18 Pro, les AirPods, les Apple Watch, le Mac mini M6, l’iMac M6 ou encore le MacBook Pro M6.
Le nouveau MacBook Pro
Le MacBook Pro annoncé par Apple ce mercredi 28 octobre propose plusieurs changements majeurs.
Un nouveau design
C’est le premier changement de design depuis l’arrivée du chassis Apple Silicon en 2021 qui avait fait revenir les ports, le lecteur SD et surtout introduit l’écran mini LED Pro Motion.
Le nouveau design reprend ces forces, mais dans un design beaucoup plus léger. La version 14 pouces est annoncée à 1,38 kg, contre 1,60 kg sur l’ancien design.
Protégez votre vie numérique avec Bitdefender, la protection européenne de confiance. Bitdefender vous protège contre les arnaques et les fraudes du web. Profitez de vos activités en ligne en toute tranquillité.
La version 16 pouces passe, elle, de 2,14 kg à 1,82 kg.
Autre petit changement au niveau de design, la pomme brille à nouveau au dos du MacBook Pro.
Écran ProLED XDR
L’excellent écran miniLED des MacBook Pro laisse sa place à une dalle OLED annoncée comme particulièrement qualitative. Définition, luminosité, fréquence d’affichage : Apple pousse les curseurs à leur plus haut.
- Dalle Oled Tandem
- Jusqu’à 2000 nits
- Adobe RGB + P3
- taux de rafraichissement de 120 Hz
- Rapport de contraste de 10 millions pour 1
Le premier MacBook tactile
C’est le grand bouleversement pour Apple, le MacBook Pro est le premier Mac équipé d’un écran tactile. La précédente expérimentation en la matière d’Apple se limitait à la fameuse TouchBar.
Cette fois, tout l’écran est tactile et Apple a modifié macOS pour qu’il soit manipulable du bout des doigts. On y trouve de nouvelles animations notamment et des raccourcis pensés pour le tactile.
Dynamic Island, enfin sur Mac
Autre changement attendu, la fin de l’encoche inutile sur les MacBook. Les ordinateurs d’Apple gagnent la Dynamic Island qui permet, comme sur iPhone, d’afficher dynamiquement des widgets et des notifications.
La même puce
C’est l’élément sur lequel Apple ne bouge pas, assez étrangement pour un produit aussi novateur : le MacBook Pro continue avec les puces M5 Pro et M5 Max.
Les rumeurs avaient vu justes. Elles annoncent aussi du changement de ce côté en 2027. Le MacBook Pro passerait alors directement aux puces M7 Pro et M7 Max, sans passer par la génération M6.
Disponibilité et prix
Les précommandes ouvrent dès ce soir, pour une sortie annoncée à partir du vendredi 6 novembre.
Le prix est en très forte hausse. À partir de 3299 euros pour la version 14 pouces et M5 Pro, et à partir de 3899 euros pour la version 16 pouces.
Pour rappel, l’ancien modèle M5 Pro débutait à 2899 euros en 14 pouces et 3399 euros en 16 pouces.
En poussant toutes les options au maximum, on arrive à un MacBook Pro à 16 264 euros. C’est à dire un MacBook Pro 16 pouces équipé d’une puce Apple M5 Max avec un GPU 40 coeurs, 128 Go de mémoire unifiée et 16 To de stockage SSD.

articles.title: Anthropic rachète la biotech d'un seul chercheur qui pilotait 11 labos avec Claude pour créer un médicament
articles.text:
Dans le dessin animé Pokémon, le professeur Chen est celui qui donne à Sacha son tout premier Pokémon, Pikachu. Mais sur X, le professeur Oak (son nom anglais) avait une tout autre activité : la biotech. On ignorait tout de l’identité de la personne se cachant derrière le pseudonyme, mais il signait des analyses dans le domaine de la recherche pharmaceutique.
Et voilà que ce mardi 27 octobre 2026, on vient de découvrir qui se cachait sous ce personnage fictif : il s’agit de Cody Tranbarger, le fondateur et unique salarié de Mithril Medicine. Et si l’on en parle aujourd’hui, c’est en raison de l’actualité : Anthropic, l’entreprise américaine derrière l’intelligence artificielle Claude, a présenté de nouveaux travaux en médecine.
Au fil de l’article, on finit par comprendre le lien : Mithril Medicine a été rachetée par Anthropic plus tôt cette année. Ce que confirme l’intéressé sur X : « Surprise n°1 : Anthropic a racheté une biotech d’une seule personne. Surprise n°2 : cette personne, c’est moi ». Cody Tranbarger s’est alors lancé dans une longue explication du pourquoi du comment.
Ce rapprochement s’inscrit dans un mouvement plus large d’Anthropic. Sur X, le concurrent d’OpenAI explique que « les scientifiques d’Anthropic ont noué des partenariats de recherche approfondis avec six organisations développant de nouveaux médicaments au cours des derniers mois ». Parmi elles figurent Bristol Myers Squibb, Generate Biomedicines ou Enveda. La start-up de Cody Tranbarger n’en fait pas partie : Anthropic l’a rachetée pour mener ses propres programmes de recherche.
Et l’intérêt d’Anthropic pour Mithril Medicine se comprend au regard de ce qui a été accompli, selon Anthropic. Il est affirmé que son fondateur a confié à Claude les contrats, la logistique et le suivi d’expériences menées dans 11 laboratoires extérieurs. Objectif de la start-up : développer des traitements contre deux formes rares de dystrophie musculaire.
Le résultat revendiqué ? Mithril a réussi, en moins de 18 mois, à faire passer un traitement potentiel contre une forme de dystrophie musculaire du stade de l’idée à celui de résultats prometteurs chez la souris. Ce n’est bien sûr pas encore le bout du chemin, mais c’est un pas encourageant en vue d’un traitement d’une forme rare de myopathie de l’enfant.
« Aujourd’hui chez Anthropic, Cody poursuit ces recherches et prévoit de lancer plusieurs nouveaux programmes. Si ses candidats-médicaments continuent de donner de bons résultats, nous prévoyons qu’un médicament sera prêt à entrer en phase d’essais cliniques chez l’homme dès la fin de l’année 2028 », avance Anthropic.
Le rapport technique de 38 pages détaille la méthodologie suivie par Cody Tranbarger. Il nuance aussi un peu le discours de l’individu seul ayant tout réglé à coups de prompts bien placés. On y apprend en effet que huit consultants et conseillers rémunérés ont épaulé le fondateur, et que toutes les expériences ont été réalisées par des organismes de recherche (CRO) sous contrat.
Que fait Claude, au juste ?
Toujours est-il qu’il raconte une semaine de travail.
Claude, par exemple, a lu en 7 minutes et 53 secondes un dossier long de 341 pages envoyé par un laboratoire. Il en a tiré une synthèse visuelle qui proposait une suite à donner pour chacun des 113 anticorps candidats. Sur la semaine, il a aussi rédigé 17 e-mails techniques. Douze sont partis après relecture et correction par l’équipe, et Claude n’en a envoyé aucun lui-même.
Dans ce processus, Claude lit, calcule et rédige ; les décisions restent à l’équipe. Le rapport note d’ailleurs que ce sont les réponses des laboratoires et les arbitrages humains qui ont fixé le rythme de la semaine.
Claude a aussi proposé de tenir 24 anticorps, tous construits à partir des trois mêmes briques, à l’écart des tests sur cellules, pour des raisons de fabrication. Il voulait pourtant mesurer l’affinité des 113 candidats, et a défendu ce choix en 27 secondes quand un membre de l’équipe l’a contesté. L’équipe a tranché : les 24 anticorps ont été mis de côté, et Claude a ramené en quatre minutes son plan, la liste des tests et trois brouillons d’e-mails de 113 à 89 molécules.
Claude a aussi raccourci les temps d’attente, au prix de brouillons qu’il a fallu retravailler.
Claude a rendu une première réponse en 96 secondes, contre 8,5 heures pour le premier retour d’un laboratoire externe (un délai qui inclut des nuits, un week-end et 12 heures de décalage horaire). L’IA accélère ainsi la logistique et la clarification des protocoles. Ses brouillons ont en revanche été nettement retouchés : sur les dix e-mails comparables, les 4 938 mots rédigés par Claude sont devenus 3 409 mots envoyés, soit près d’un tiers en moins. Certaines propositions ont tout de même été gardées telles quelles, comme des contrôles expérimentaux suggérés aux laboratoires.
Un résultat encore fragile
Cela étant dit, Claude ne décide de rien. Il ne réalise aucun essai physique, ne valide aucun protocole de son propre chef et n’envoie aucun message sans approbation. L’expertise humaine reste indispensable, à ce stade, pour relire, arbitrer la sélection finale des molécules et porter la responsabilité scientifique de l’étude.
Par ailleurs, le rapport n’a pas été relu par des pairs. Les souris n’ont été ni tirées au sort ni évaluées à l’aveugle, et le résultat principal repose sur 7 animaux traités contre 4 témoins. Surtout, le groupe traité a été testé en dernier, après un déménagement de l’animalerie. Ses souris avaient aussi les pattes plus longues, ce qui peut fausser la mesure de force.
Qui plus est, le rapport lui-même a été rédigé par Claude, sous la direction de l’équipe, y compris les recherches bibliographiques ou les schémas. La start-up reconnaît un risque de biais dans la partie qui décrit le travail de l’intelligence artificielle. Le rapport n’a donc rien d’une évaluation indépendante : il est signé par un salarié d’Anthropic, qui possède désormais le programme d’anticorps.
Chez Anthropic, l’équipe de Nathan C. Frey, responsable de la recherche sur la découverte et le développement de médicaments, appelle ce modèle « pipeline-in-a-person ». Dans le jargon pharmaceutique, le pipeline désigne le portefeuille de candidats-médicaments d’une entreprise : l’idée est qu’une seule personne, épaulée par plusieurs instances de Claude, puisse en monter et en piloter un. À le lire, cette idée pourrait être étendue à d’autres programmes qui projettent de développer de nouveaux soins.
