articles.title: Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
articles.text:
Apple announced a new iPad Mini with a larger OLED display this week, and we’ve just gotten to try it out at Apple’s “Pro and tell” event.
Hands-on with the new OLED iPad Mini
We’ve gotten to play around with Apple’s next small tablet.
It’s an iPad for sure, but the new OLED on the Mini looks exceptional, and the optional nano-texture matte finish is awesome. The “Pro and tell” event venue has soft lighting that’s not the most conducive to blinding glare on displays, but the matte finish pretty much squashes it entirely.
Moving the front-facing camera to the long edge is also a welcome change, matching other recent iPad models. (The shift means that the whole iPad line has the camera that way.) The reliance on Touch ID instead of Face ID is still a bummer, though.
The 8th-generation iPad Mini, revealed on Monday, has an 8.5-inch OLED screen, thinner bezels, and a higher peak brightness of up to 1,200 nits. The display still tops out at a 60Hz refresh rate instead of hitting 120Hz. It’s equipped with an A20 Pro chip, though the 128GB and 256GB models have five CPU cores, while the 512GB model gets six. Apple has also touted the new iPad Mini’s “Acoustic Display,” which includes woofers “paired through the display to produce punchier bass and more volume.”
The new iPad Mini starts at $699 and comes in two colors: starlight and midnight. It’s available to preorder now ahead of its launch on November 6th.

articles.title: Octoverse: Commits, pushes, reach new highs in 2026 as developers build with agents
articles.text:
GitHub Staff
GitHub is the world's best developer experience and the only AI-powered platform with security incorporated into every step, so you can innovate with confidence.
See how a record year of growth reached every industry, every field, and every kind of builder in the 2026 Octoverse report.
Developers pushed code to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than in 2024 and 2025 combined.
Behind that number are developers building what interests them and what their communities need. In Nepal, one developer built a flood bulletin on GitHub Pages with verified information on roads, rescue, weather, and power. It has since grown into Gati, a Nepali-first relay of official disaster alerts that runs on GitHub Pages and Actions. Elsewhere, developers at NASA’s Jet Propulsion Laboratory are creating software designed to run programs aboard spacecraft, and fans built open-source firmware that lets people customize their e-readers. Curiosity, aimed in every direction, at a scale GitHub hasn’t seen before.
That growth happened quickly. Partway through the year, activity on GitHub bent sharply upward, just as agents went from something developers were trying out to something they were working alongside. Developers picked from more models than ever and built in industries we are highlighting in this report for the first time, from health care to agriculture.
Octoverse is our chance to step back and look at the whole picture. This year, that picture is bigger than ever. Here is what stood out most:
Underneath it all, AI models and the harnesses built around them have advanced over the past year, and developers have more to choose from. Growth is moving quickly: one year into last year’s five-year developer growth projections, every country we projected has already closed at least a fifth of its distance to 2030, and our own forecasting models no longer agree on where it will go next.
This year was all about momentum. Developers pushed code changes to GitHub 17.9 billion times in the past 12 months, more than 2024 and 2025 combined. Commits across all repo types (public and private) climbed even faster to 34.3 billion, more than three times where they stood two years ago. Merged pull requests more than tripled to 1.3 billion over the same period, an average of 3.5 million a day.
Agents were one of the tools developers leaned on hardest this year, pulling them deeper into daily work. Among repos created this year, the average repo with an agent configuration file logged eight times as many commits as the average new repo without one, sign that individuals and teams building with agents from day one are moving at a markedly different pace.
Developers also relied on automations to keep projects moving. GitHub Actions ran a job 1,440 times every second this year. This equals 124 million times a day and is more than three times last year’s total. Developers merged more than 30 million Dependabot pull requests to keep dependencies current and reduce the use of known vulnerabilities, about double 2025’s pace.
Our telemetry shows activity climbing steadily from January, then surging around June, as if developers everywhere saw new possibilities at once. Right around then, a cluster of industry-wide shifts landed: better underlying models, the harnesses and tools built around them, and the agents running on both. Agents moved from single-session tools to persistent ones that could track progress across days and orchestrate other specialized agents. Just as important, agents began making extensive use of the cloud, executing work remotely as well as on local machines.
This momentum is showing up both in brand-new repos and from developers who have been building for years. From June onwards, about 55% of all commits came from brand new repositories. But plenty more commits came from developers who’ve been around a while: developers who pushed code in the past 12 months have been on GitHub for an average of 36 months, and of those who opened a pull request in August, more than 75% pushed code in September. They are also branching out: the average developer now works across 10% more repositories than they did a year ago.
That staying power shows up in open source too. Public contributions soared to 2.5 billion in 2026, more than double last year’s total (1.12 billion). Behind those numbers are developers who keep showing up, like @kinlane, who made more than 1 million contributions across his public repositories using agentic workflows to keep a machine-readable catalog of public API information current. Another example is @kim-em, who made more than 178,000 contributions while maintaining mathlib, which is a community library of computer-checked mathematics. @andig, a maintainer of the open source EV charging controller and home energy management system evcc, contributed over 21,000 times.
These are just a few examples of the work millions of developers do every day. To all the developers doing work like this and beyond: we see you, and we’re glad you’re building.
Behind every number in this report is a developer. GitHub now serves more than 225 million of them, and the community is growing around the globe. The United States (38.3 million) and India (32 million) remain the two largest developer communities, and each added more than 10 million developers this year. Brazil added 3.28 million developers on GitHub this year, the third most of any country.
| Country | Total number of developers on GitHub in Sept. 2026 | 
|---|---|
| United States | 38.3 M | 
| India | 32.0 M | 
| China | 12.4 M | 
| Brazil | 10.2 M | 
| Japan | 7.15 M | 
| United Kingdom | 6.47 M | 
| Indonesia | 6.34 M | 
| Germany | 6.30 M | 
| Russia | 5.07 M | 
| France | 4.75 M | 
Last year, we projected that India would reach 57.5 million developers by 2030 and the United States 54.7 million. One year into that five-year window, every country in our projections has already closed at least a fifth of the distance to its own 2030 figure. The United States has closed 38.6%, and India 28.3%.
The same momentum shows up across regions, each with its own local context:
| Region | Growth driver | Market context | 
|---|---|---|
| Americas | Fintech and digital payments | • Brazil: mature, fast-growing fintech sector • Canada: steady AI and software investment | 
| EMEA | AI adoption in manufacturing and startups. Fast-growing developer community in Africa | • Morocco: fintech and startup scene • Germany: enterprise AI adoption across its industrial heartland • France and Spain: AI and deep-tech startups • Kenya, Nigeria, South Africa: fintech, agritech, and coding bootcamps | 
| APAC | Government investment in AI infrastructure and talent | • Indonesia: booming digital economy • Japan: AI infrastructure investment • South Korea: government-backed AI talent programs • Australia: AI, machine learning, and data skills | 
One year in, growth is strong against last year’s projection, and projecting the next five years is getting harder. We ran more than 40 forecasting models forward to 2031, time-series and regression models built on historical sign-up and usage data, each assuming a different pace of growth. About half call for “extreme” growth, with developer counts on GitHub more than tripling by 2031. Just under half call for “substantial” growth, doubling to tripling. Only three models expect anything close to modest, under 2x growth.
Forecasts are estimates, and a spread this wide shows how much the 2026 surge widened what is plausible by 2031. What holds steady is the shape of the trend: a developer community growing in more places at once.
In past reports, “everywhere” meant more developers and more countries, such as in the context of the top countries contributing code to public repositories:
| Rank | Country | 
|---|---|
| 1 | United States | 
| 2 | India | 
| 3 | China | 
| 4 | Brazil | 
| 5 | Germany | 
| 6 | United Kingdom | 
| 7 | Korea | 
| 8 | France | 
| 9 | Japan | 
| 10 | Canada | 
This year, it also means more fields, including industries we haven’t measured before.
We’re sharing our view of public repositories by industry using the North American Industry Classification System (NAICS), which sorts economic activity into sectors. A language model classified random samples of public repositories created each year from 2022 to 2026, assigning each to the industry it serves based on its name, description, topics, and README. We also tracked two signals: whether a repository mentions AI, and whether an agent opened a pull request against it.
The two signals do not always move together. In administrative and support services, mining, health care, and agriculture, more than four in 10 repositories mention AI, yet agent-opened pull requests are rare, less than 3 percent. Construction breaks that pattern. About a quarter of its repositories mention AI, but about 9 percent have agent-opened pull requests, the highest share of any sector, with manufacturing next.
The same classification shows how each industry’s footprint has shifted since 2022, and sectors well beyond software are climbing. Professional, scientific, and technical services rose from fourth to second place among all industries, behind only information. Agriculture, forestry, fishing and hunting climbed two spots, and finance and insurance and health care and social assistance each moved up one. Against each sector’s own 2022 baseline, mining, quarrying, and oil and gas extraction grew roughly 65 times from a small starting base, administrative and support services and construction 17 to 18 times, and even manufacturing, the slowest of these, almost tripled.
Behind these sector shifts are people who know their fields, now using AI coding agents to build. For example, in manufacturing, a small team built a way to turn a photo of your tools into a custom-fit, 3D-printable drawer organizer. A research lab in health care made it easier for scientists to analyze huge digital scans of tissue samples, the kind pathologists study to understand disease. In Copenhagen, a university lab built a pipeline that classifies video of chickens at play, from frolicking to worm chasing. A University of Waikato energy center built a toolkit that helps industrial plants find heat they can reuse, and Bulgaria’s digital ministry open-sourced a portal where anyone can trace who won a public contract and for how much. For writers, a novelist built a free app that makes a manuscript look like a book as you type. In field after field, the people closest to the problem are building the solution, with agents helping along the way.
Professional, scientific, and technical services, which grew about 5 times over its own 2022 baseline and climbed to second place, is the work of researching, engineering, and advising, and open code has long been part of how that work gets done. In biochemistry, the work behind AlphaFold earned Demis Hassabis and John Jumper a share of the 2024 Nobel Prize in Chemistry. In computer science, Tensor2Tensor accompanied the paper that introduced the Transformer, the architecture behind today’s large language models, “Attention Is All You Need.” In medicine, sars-cov-2-stability held the code and data behind one of the earliest papers on how long the virus survives in the air and on surfaces. In physics, eht-imaging was one of two open-source libraries used to reconstruct the first image of a black hole. A repository has quietly become part of the paper trail behind published research.
More developers now begin a pull request by specifying what they want and orchestrating the agents that carry it out. By September 2026, more than 40% of pull requests on GitHub started with an agent’s first draft, up from 17% in March. That is 110 million in September alone, about 6x March’s volume.
Agent-started pull requests also more often change multiple files: about 87%, compared with 79% of pull requests without detected agent involvement. They are landing quickly too. In February, 83% of agent-involved pull requests merged within two weeks, a touch behind the roughly 86% for pull requests without detected agent involvement. By September, agent pull requests were at 90%, while the comparison group held at about 86%.
Among GitHub Copilot’s monthly active users, 55% now use agentic features, up from 35% a year ago. The steepest growth is in the most hands-off mode. Copilot cloud agent, where a developer assigns a task and an agent works on it independently, grew 230% year over year, against 85% for agent chat. Developers still ask agents questions, and increasingly they hand over whole tasks.
The willingness to delegate is reflected by the kinds of tasks developers are attempting. Public repositories mentioning interoperability or reverse engineering increased more than 300% year over year, from about 30,000 created in 2025 to more than 130,000 in 2026.
Review is where developers shape what comes back, and more tooling is being built for it. Stacked pull requests, which split related work into smaller changes that are easier to review in sequence, launched as a preview on July 30, and more than 264,000 developers had used them by September. Usage of AI-assisted code review and GitHub Advanced Security both grew more than 90% year over year. The platform also helps secure that work: push protection, which screens for exposed secrets such as API keys and passwords, ran 5.8 billion scans this year, nearly four times 2025’s pace. Developers are investing in how they review code.
Developers match models to the work they hand to their agents. In September 2026, 61% of GitHub Copilot users who selected a model themselves used more than one model across their sessions, up from 50% four months earlier.
The lineup is growing too: developers on paid GitHub Copilot plans used 29 distinct models in May and 47 in September, and no single model carried more than 25% of requests that month. Some model decisions come down to cost and familiarity. Developers weigh price and functionality against need and may lean toward providers they already trust.
To see how developer choices spread, we grouped the models used in GitHub Copilot by what they are built for: deep reasoning and planning, general purpose, and fast and lightweight. We then looked at where requests went, counting only activity where a developer explicitly selected a model. That leaves out cases where GitHub Copilot picks the model (auto model selection), GitHub and Microsoft staff usage, background utility models, duplicate requests used for monitoring and testing, and requests made with a developer’s own API key.
We found that out of every 100 developer-selected requests, 38 went to general purpose models, 37 to deep reasoning and planning models, and 25 to fast and lightweight models. Developers spread their choices across models and functionality, and about 25% of requests go to a fast model.
To see how those choices shift, we looked at them as a time series over the past three months, tracking request share alongside how many developers tried each model and how many kept coming back. Three patterns stand out:
Taken together, the spread across kinds of models points to a lot of choosing: a lineup that keeps growing, a best fit that shifts from one task to the next, and all three kinds of models held in rotation. Many developers also let GitHub Copilot do some of it. In September 2026, 63% of paying GitHub Copilot developers used auto model selection at least once, letting Copilot pick the model for the task.
Planning, implementing, and checking a change each place different demands on a model, in capability, speed, and cost. Project HydraFusion, began as a research preview of model orchestration, matching models to each step of that work. In the CLI and the GitHub Copilot app, it routed almost 60,000 sessions. That work is now generally available as GitHub Copilot Fusion, which brings model orchestration together with auto model selection and chooses the right model for each step behind the scenes.
Language choice has long reflected what developers want to build, what their teams know, and what existing systems require. This year’s data raises the question of whether a fourth influence is emerging: the language an agent picks when a developer doesn’t specify one.
Last year, we reported that TypeScript had overtaken Python and JavaScript to become the most used language on GitHub by contributors. That order held in 2026, with TypeScript first, Python second, and JavaScript third. The pace picked up. From September 2025 to September 2026, TypeScript added 3.62 million monthly contributors, Python 3.23 million, and JavaScript 1.82 million, the largest gains among the top 10 languages. Rust grew fastest by percentage among the top languages, doubling in the past year.
Our forecasts extend recent trends: TypeScript and Python near 13 million monthly contributors each by September 2027, JavaScript at 7.4 million, and every other language in the top 10 below about 2.2 million.
The languages growing fastest are also where AI shows up most. We charted each language’s community growth over the past year against the share of its merged pull requests with detected AI involvement, with bubbles roughly sized to show the size of each language’s community. TypeScript, Python, and Rust, the fastest-growing communities, have the highest shares, about 40% to 44% of merged pull requests. Java, C#, and C++ sit lower, between about 21% and 34%, though AI shows up in more than one in five merged pull requests in every language shown.
The repository data adds another angle. Among repositories created in 2026, TypeScript was the primary language in 35% of those with an observed agent signal, compared to 24% without one. For repositories created before 2026, the gap was similar: 27% with an agent signal, versus 17% without. That suggests developers who work with agents gravitate toward languages where agent output is easier to check. Developers who know exactly what they want still specify the language. But when they leave the choice open, agents appear to favor a narrower set of languages, TypeScript chief among them.
This year, we split the fastest-growing and most-engaged projects on GitHub into two groups: community and independent repositories, and single-vendor or product-led ones. Community and independent projects are foundation-governed, broadly maintained, or led by an individual without a clear commercial sponsor. Single-vendor and product-led projects are open source or source-available and often take substantial community contributions, but strategic control sits with one company.
Read together, the two lists show a division of labor. The community side is mostly the foundation underneath everything else: inference engines like vLLM, SGLang, and llama.cpp, frameworks like PyTorch, languages and runtimes like Rust and CPython, and platforms like Home Assistant and Godot. The vendor side is mostly the tools developers work with directly: coding agents, editors, and the orchestration around them. Contributors are showing up for both layers. The growth list also includes places built to welcome newcomers, like first-contributions and is-a-dev/register, where many developers make their first pull request.
| Rank | Community / independent | Single vendor / product-led | 
|---|---|---|
| 1 | farion1231/cc-switch | Anthropic: anthropics/claude-code | 
| 2 | punkpeye/awesome-mcp-servers | OpenAI: openai/codex | 
| 3 | Omacom Foundation: omacom/omarchy | Anomaly: anomalyco/opencode | 
| 4 | firstcontributions/first-contributions | Microsoft: microsoft/vscode | 
| 5 | ggml-org/llama.cpp | GitHub: github/copilot-cli | 
| 6 | Eclipse Foundation: EclipseFdn/open-vsx.org | Zed Industries: zed-industries/zed | 
| 7 | sgl-project/sglang | Google: google-gemini/gemini-cli | 
| 8 | vllm-project/vllm | BerriAI: BerriAI/litellm | 
| 9 | imputnet/helium | microsoft/winget-pkgs | 
| 10 | vllm-project/vllm-ascend | Kilo-Org/kilocode | 
| Rank | Community / independent | Single vendor / product-led | 
|---|---|---|
| 1 | OpenClaw Foundation: openclaw/openclaw | Nous Research: NousResearch/hermes-agent | 
| 2 | vllm-project/vllm | Anomaly: anomalyco/opencode | 
| 3 | ggml-org/llama.cpp | Earendil: earendil-works/pi | 
| 4 | Omacom Foundation: omacom/omarchy | Stably AI: stablyai/orca | 
| 5 | farion1231/cc-switch | Ping: pingdotgg/t3code | 
| 6 | sgl-project/sglang | Microsoft: microsoft/vscode | 
| 7 | PyTorch Foundation: pytorch/pytorch | Graphify Labs: Graphify-Labs/graphify | 
| 8 | Rust Foundation: rust-lang/rust | Paperclip AI: paperclipai/paperclip | 
| 9 | Open Home Foundation: home-assistant/core | BerriAI: BerriAI/litellm | 
| 10 | Python Software Foundation: python/cpython | can1357/oh-my-pi | 
As part of our research this year, we also tracked the emoji developers used most in their repositories. Across every industry we looked at, the rocket 🚀 topped the list, by a wide margin. A fitting symbol for a year of momentum. Developers on GitHub covered more ground this year: more code, more countries, and more industries than we’ve ever measured. None of that activity changes who decides what the code should do. Someone still has to come up with the idea, whether it’s software that assesses earthquake risk, an open record of how online services change their terms and privacy policies, or an agent skill that makes an AI answer like a caveman to save on words. And someone still has to decide whether it works, whether it belongs, and whether it’s good.
What did change is how much easier it is to take an idea from a weekend thought to something real.
The tools will keep changing, and new industries will keep showing up in places we didn’t expect. What a developer chooses to build, and who they build it for, is still theirs to decide. Rocket emoji and all.
Today, we laid out our vision for GitHub as the most comprehensive, end-to-end software delivery system in the world.
AI, agents, voice, and physical controls are shifting software development from operating tools to expressing intent—and helping developers stay focused on building.
In September, we experienced two incidents that resulted in degraded performance across GitHub services.

articles.title: Women-led companies dominate top ranks of 2026 Deloitte Fast 50 | BetaKit
articles.text:
For the first time, half of Canada’s 10 fastest-growing companies are led by women, according to the 2026 Deloitte Technology Fast 50.
The annual list recognizes Canada’s fastest-growing technology companies across three categories based on their revenue growth percentage over the past three or four years, depending on the category.
The top of the flagship list featured more women-led companies than usual this year, including Toronto-based rewards platform Chexy, which placed second with a four-year revenue growth rate of 23,183 percent. Other women-led companies at the top of the list include legaltech company BorderPass, led by co-CEO Sally Daub, in third place; cleantech software WeavAir, led by CEO Natalia Mykhaylova, in fourth; AI automation platform SimplyAsk.ai, led by CEO Shuli Gortler, in fifth; and online therapy provider Total Life, led by CEO Neelam Brar, in sixth place.
Women-led companies featured more prominently than usual on this year’s list, taking spots two through six.
In a statement, Chexy CEO Liza Akhvledziani-Carew said the company has proved its rent-to-rewards model, and that the growth rate indicates it’s “onto something much bigger.” Earlier this year, the company raised a $14-million Series A round led by Khosla Ventures, one of Silicon Valley’s most reputable venture firms, to help its users earn credit card rewards on more everyday expenses.
The list’s top spot went to Toronto-based Finni Health, which sported a four-year revenue growth rate of 46,754 percent. The Y Combinator alum, founded by Canadian Bucky Khan, provides a platform for autism care providers in the United States to start, run, and grow their practices.
The average revenue growth rate of this year’s Fast 50 was 3,079 percent, a jump from last year’s average growth of 2,623 percent. Other companies on the 2026 Fast 50 include, in descending order, Toronto-based legaltech Spellbook, Québec City-based pipeline inspector Flyscan, Montréal-based digital lender Nesto, and Vancouver-based private stock marketplace Clarity (formerly known as Hiive).
In addition to the Fast 50, Deloitte also recognized 15 Canadian companies on its Enterprise—Industry Leaders ranking and another 17 on its Companies to Watch list, which showcases companies with the potential to be future Fast 50 program winners.
Richmond, BC-based last-mile delivery company UniUni topped this year’s industry leaders list, sporting a 2,143-percent four-year revenue increase. While its reported revenue increase vastly exceeded others below it on the list, UniUni has faced trouble recently. The company’s attempt to go public through a special purpose acquisition company (SPAC) fell through after the SPAC terminated the deal, citing UniUni’s deteriorating business and financial performance.
RELATED: Neo Financial completes first-ever hat trick of Deloitte Technology Fast 50 rankings
Other companies on the Enterprise—Industry Leaders list include Toronto-based FinTech firm Koho, which placed second with a 580-percent four-year revenue increase, Calgary-based PurposeMed (which is set to be acquired by Grindr) in seventh, and Ottawa-based surveillance tech firm Solink in tenth.
Ottawa-based Turbopuffer, which provides a fast data search engine, decisively took the top spot on the Companies to Watch list with a 65,443-percent growth rate, confirming founder Simon Hørup Eskildsen’s fears that he runs Canada’s fastest-growing company. In a distant second was another Ottawa-based company, defence tech firm Tactiql, with a 4,395-percent growth rate.
Companies on the flagship Fast 50 list are automatically eligible for the broader North American Technology Fast 500, which will be released on November 18. Deloitte says 80 Canadian companies made that list this year, down from 114 last year.

articles.title: Bose Sport Open Earbuds (2026) : des écouteurs taillés pour les sportifs déjà en promo
articles.text:
Il y a un mois, Bose a étoffé sa gamme d’écouteurs à conception ouverte avec deux nouveaux modèles, dont les Sport Open Earbuds. Ces derniers adoptent un format à clip, déjà apprécié des runners et adeptes d’entraînements en plein air. En bref, les Sport Open Earbuds, qui ne s’enfoncent donc pas dans le conduit auditif, permettent aux sportifs de profiter de leur musique tout en restant attentifs au monde qui les entoure. Et ils sont blindés de technologies, pour ne rien gâcher. Actuellement, les Sport Open Earbuds sont proposés à un prix inférieur à leur tarif de lancement : on les trouve à moins de 180 euros.
Les points forts des Bose Sport Open Earbuds
- Des écouteurs ouverts confortables et certifiés IP54
- La technologie Bose OpenAudio, qui limite les fuites sonores
- Jusqu’à 29 heures d’autonomie avec l’étui de charge
Initialement affichés à 199,99 euros, les Bose Sport Open Earbuds sont aujourd’hui disponibles à 179,99 euros chez Boulanger grâce au code promo BOSE20.
Si, par la suite, l’offre mentionnée dans cet article n’est plus disponible, merci de jeter un coup d’œil ci-dessous afin de dénicher d’autres offres concernant les Bose Sport Open Earbuds. Le tableau s’actualise automatiquement.
Il n’y a pas d’offres pour le moment, découvrez :
Des écouteurs confortables et résistants
Les Bose Sport Open Earbuds sont des écouteurs dits « open ear », qui peuvent convenir aux sportifs qui ne supportent pas les écouteurs intra-auriculaires trop invasifs. Chaque oreillette se compose de deux modules reliés par un arceau en silicone doux en forme de C, qui se clipse sur l’oreille et assure le maintien des écouteurs, sans obstruer le conduit auditif. Et contrairement aux modèles à conduction osseuse, les Sport Open Earbuds diffusent le son dans l’air, à proximité de l’oreille, plutôt que de transmettre des vibrations par les os du crâne. La marque l’assure : le rendu sonore est plus naturel qu’avec la conduction osseuse.
Bose assure par ailleurs que ces Sport Open Earbuds parviennent à rester stables sur les oreilles, y compris lors de mouvements brusques ou pendant des entraînements intenses. Ces true wireless sont également certifiés IP54 : ils résistent donc à la transpiration, aux éclaboussures et à la poussière. Et leurs boutons physiques texturés permettent de contrôler la musique, les appels et le volume, même avec les doigts moites en plein effort. Côté autonomie, Bose annonce jusqu’à 7 heures de lecture sur une seule charge, complétées par 22 heures supplémentaires grâce à l’étui de recharge, lequel prend d’ailleurs en charge la recharge sans fil.
Le plein de technologies
Côté connectivité, les Sport Open Earbuds sont compatibles avec le Bluetooth 5.4, prennent en charge la connexion multipoint pour se connecter à deux appareils simultanément et supportent les codecs SBC et AAC. Côté audio, les écouteurs renferment des haut-parleurs dynamiques pensés pour délivrer un son ample et équilibré. Ils sont d’ailleurs associés à la fonction Auto Volume, qui ajuste automatiquement le niveau sonore selon les variations du bruit ambiant.
Bose a inclus d’autres technologies bien pratiques, à l’image de la Bose OpenAudio, qui permet de profiter d’un son limpide directement à l’oreille tout en limitant au maximum les fuites sonores vers l’extérieur. Vous avez aussi la technologie SpeechClarity : un microphone dédié et une unité de captation vocale travaillent ensemble dans chaque oreillette afin d’isoler la voix des bruits de fond, que ce soit dans une rue animée ou en plein entraînement.
En revanche, n’espérez pas trouver la réduction de bruit active ici : ces écouteurs, comme les autres modèles open ear du marché, ont été conçus pour permettre à l’utilisateur de rester attentif à son environnement, notamment à la circulation ou aux annonces sonores. Enfin, grâce à une mise à jour du firmware, les utilisateurs pourront profiter de la localisation via Google Find Hub ou encore de l’assistant Alexa+ pour des tâches mains libres comme la réservation d’une table ou une recommandation musicale.

articles.title: Un astre jamais vu, situé encore plus loin que Pluton, pourrait rejoindre le très fermé club des cinq planètes naines du Système solaire - Numerama
articles.text:
Pour l’instant, elle ne porte qu’une désignation provisoire, 2026 ED138, mais elle pourrait à terme rejoindre les cinq planètes naines reconnues par l’Union astronomique internationale (UAI) : Pluton, Makémaké, Cérès, Hauméa et Éris. Cet astre, dont la découverte a été annoncée ce mardi 27 octobre par le Minor Planet Center, l’organisme qui recense les petits corps du Système solaire, est le premier candidat au titre de planète naine repéré par le télescope Vera C. Rubin, mis en service il y a quasiment un an et demi.
Ce type d’astre est trop gros pour être considéré comme un astéroïde et possède une forme sphérique qui le fait ressembler à une planète classique. Contrairement à la Terre, à Mars et aux autres planètes, une planète naine n’a pas fait le ménage sur son orbite : d’autres corps circulent encore sur des trajectoires proches de la sienne. C’est la nuance qui a fait perdre à Pluton son titre de planète au terme de débats houleux au sein de l’Union astronomique internationale, en 2006.
Un astre massif transneptunien
L’Union astronomique internationale ne reconnaît que cinq planètes naines dans notre Système solaire, mais on compte plusieurs centaines de candidates plus ou moins assurées de décrocher le titre. Pour ED138, il s’agit de la toute première candidate découverte par le télescope Rubin. L’observatoire, installé sur le Cerro Pachón au Chili, doit notamment dresser l’inventaire des petits corps du Système solaire, qu’il s’agisse d’astéroïdes, de comètes ou d’autres objets.
Le télescope a capté cet objet transneptunien, particulièrement brillant et jamais vu auparavant, en balayant le ciel austral avec sa gigantesque caméra. L’astrophysicien Matthew Holman, du Center for Astrophysics Harvard & Smithsonian, l’a repéré le 13 octobre dans les données collectées plus tôt en 2026, grâce à un code de recherche d’objets en mouvement qu’il a développé avec son collègue Kevin Napier. D’après les premières analyses de l’équipe de Rubin, il s’agirait d’un des astres les plus gros et les plus brillants repérés dans cette partie du Système solaire.
Il est encore trop tôt pour confirmer qu’il s’agit bel et bien d’une planète naine. ED138 montre en revanche ce dont sont capables les algorithmes du télescope, chargés de comparer des milliards de détections d’objets en mouvement pour retrouver celles qui appartiennent au même astre.
Beaucoup d’indices, mais pas de confirmation
En fouillant les données, les astronomes ont retrouvé ED138 sur d’autres images : au total, le télescope l’a observé 30 fois, sur 20 nuits, entre le 4 mars et le 11 juillet 2026. Des images d’archives de la Dark Energy Camera, montée sur le télescope Blanco, toujours au Chili, ont même permis de retrouver l’objet en remontant jusqu’en 2016. Les astronomes ont ainsi pu retracer plus de dix ans de l’orbite de la possible planète naine.
On sait ainsi qu’elle tourne bien autour du Soleil, dont elle se trouve actuellement à environ 46 unités astronomiques (UA), une UA correspondant à la distance moyenne entre la Terre et le Soleil. Pour comparaison, Pluton en est à 40 UA en moyenne. À partir de sa distance, de son éclat et de la part de lumière que sa surface est censée réfléchir, l’équipe estime son diamètre entre 600 et 1 500 kilomètres. C’est bien moins que Pluton (2 377 kilomètres), mais un corps glacé de cette taille devrait en théorie être rond.
ED138 semble assez grosse pour être ronde, elle tourne autour du Soleil (ce qui exclut qu’il s’agisse d’un satellite naturel) et partage sa région avec une foule d’autres objets transneptuniens. Autant d’indices qui portent à croire qu’il s’agirait bien d’une nouvelle planète naine. Pour en avoir le cœur net, les astronomes devront l’observer dans l’infrarouge afin de mesurer précisément sa taille. Rubin, qui doit photographier tout le ciel austral pendant dix ans, pourrait d’ici là débusquer d’autres objets de ce genre dans les zones négligées par les relevés précédents.

articles.title: “Aucun disque ne sera inclus dans la boîte” : le poids de GTA 6 vient de fuiter, et votre console va devoir faire le vide
articles.text:
“Aucun disque ne sera inclus dans la boîte” : le poids de GTA 6 vient de fuiter, et votre console va devoir faire le vide
À trois semaines de la sortie, les serveurs de Sony ont parlé : GTA 6 réclamera deux fois plus d’espace que Red Dead Redemption 2. Et puisque la boîte vendue en magasin ne contient aucun disque, tout le monde passera par la case téléchargement.
Le 27 octobre, le compte X PlayStation Game Size, qui extrait les métadonnées du PlayStation Store, a dévoilé la taille de téléchargement de Grand Theft Auto VI sur PS5 : 210 Go pour l'édition Standard à 79,99 €. Le site Insider Gaming affirme avoir recoupé l'information. Rockstar Games n'a rien officialisé, mais la source a fait ses preuves. Le préchargement ouvrira le 12 novembre à minuit, une semaine avant la sortie du 19 novembre sur PS5 et Xbox Series X|S.
🚨 Grand Theft Auto VI
- 𝐃𝐨𝐰𝐧𝐥𝐨𝐚𝐝 𝐒𝐢𝐳𝐞 : 210 GB  
- 𝐒𝐭𝐚𝐧𝐝𝐚𝐫𝐝 ($79.99)
Pre-Load : November 12
Release : November 19
𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐚𝐬𝐞 𝐓𝐢𝐦𝐞 : Midnight pic.twitter.com/5vXkgnqfC7
— PlayStation Game Size (@PlaystationSize) October 27, 2026
Le chiffre rejoint les affirmations du pirate CyberLeek, qui disait détenir une version de développement de plus de 200 Go. Le poids sur Xbox reste inconnu.
Une boîte de GTA 6 sans Blu-ray
Un tel volume serait plus facile à encaisser avec un disque. Rockstar a pourtant tranché dès juin.
	
La version physique de GTA VI contiendra un code de téléchargement utilisable pour la version numérique du jeu. Aucun disque ne sera inclus dans la boîte.
Les boîtes arriveront chez les revendeurs le 12 novembre, juste à temps pour le préchargement. Sur PS5, le code est en plus lié à la région du compte PlayStation Network. Chaque acheteur récupérera donc la totalité des fichiers sur les serveurs de Sony ou de Microsoft, en même temps que des millions d'autres joueurs, et un patch du premier jour pourrait encore alourdir la facture.
Combien de temps pour télécharger GTA 6 ?
Avec une fibre à 1 Gb/s exploitée à plein régime, comptez moins d'une demi-heure. À 100 Mb/s, il faut déjà plus de quatre heures et demie. Avec un ADSL à 10 Mb/s, toujours présent dans bien des campagnes françaises, l'attente dépasse 46 heures. Ces durées théoriques ne tiennent pas compte de la saturation du réseau.
Il faudra aussi faire de la place. Sur la PS5 de lancement, GTA 6 avalerait près d'un tiers des 667 Go utilisables. Sur la Xbox Series S, il occuperait plus de la moitié des quelque 364 Go disponibles. Le 12 novembre, mieux vaut avoir déjà fait le ménage.

articles.title: TikTok expands into restaurant guides with 'Must Eat' feature | TechCrunch
articles.text:
TikTok has long been a go-to place for discovering new spots, with viral videos helping local restaurants attract new customers. Now, TikTok is making it easier for users to find their next favorite restaurant with a new feature called “Must Eat.”
Introduced Wednesday, the community-driven guide highlights restaurants getting attention on the platform, bringing food recommendations from across the U.S. into one place.
The move puts TikTok in more direct competition with platforms like Yelp and Google Maps. But instead of relying mainly on search results, maps, and traditional reviews, TikTok is building on what it already does well: connecting people with restaurants through recommendations shared by other users.
“Must Eat” uses more than 40 million posts and comments to pull restaurant recommendations and curated lists together in one place. Users can browse restaurants by city and filter results by cuisine, price, rating, and location, making it easier to compare options before heading out.
The recommendations are split into two categories: “Everyday Eats,” featuring casual favorites and neighborhood go-tos, and “Elevated Dining,” highlighting restaurants for celebrations, special occasions, or a night out.
Additionally, select restaurants can be booked directly through TikTok via OpenTable.
The feature is launching first in New York City, Los Angeles, and San Francisco. Users can find it through the search bar, the Local feed, restaurant pages, and location links attached to videos featuring participating restaurants.

articles.title: La moda de los dispositivos sin pantalla y por qué cada vez hay más
articles.text:
La moda de los dispositivos sin pantalla y por qué cada vez hay más
La IA y el cansancio digital impulsan dispositivos que funcionan sin pantalla, sin iconos y, en algunos casos, sin necesidad de sacar el móvil del bolsillo
Durante años, la industria tecnológica parecía obsesionada con una idea: poner una pantalla en cualquier objeto imaginable; y cuanto más grande, mejor. Teléfonos, relojes, electrodomésticos, coches, altavoces e, incluso, frigoríficos se llenaron de superficies repletas de iconos y notificaciones. Sin embargo, en los últimos tiempos ha comenzado a emerger una tendencia aparentemente opuesta: la de los dispositivos que reducen o eliminan por completo la pantalla.
No se trata de un regreso al pasado, sino de una nueva forma de relacionarse con la tecnología. La inteligencia artificial generativa, los asistentes de voz y los sistemas capaces de interpretar lenguaje natural han abierto la puerta a productos que prometen ofrecer información o ejecutar tareas sin necesidad de que el usuario mire constantemente una pantalla.
Tecnología invisible
Los expertos llevan años alertando sobre la fatiga asociada al exceso de notificaciones y al tiempo de exposición a dispositivos digitales, como demuestran estudios como el llevado a cabo por investigadores de la Universidad Cornell en 2020. Frente a ello, muchas empresas han comenzado a explorar lo que algunos diseñadores denominan “tecnología ambiental” o “tecnología invisible”: dispositivos que permanecen en segundo plano y solo aparecen cuando son necesarios.
Y la llegada de la IA generativa ha dado, además, un nuevo impulso a este movimiento. Si un sistema es capaz de comprender preguntas complejas y responder de forma conversacional, la necesidad de navegar por menús o aplicaciones disminuye. Uno de los ejemplos más conocidos fue el Humane AI Pin, presentado en el Mobile World Congress (MWC) en el año 2024, un pequeño dispositivo que se llevaba prendido en la ropa y que aspiraba a sustituir parcialmente al teléfono móvil.
Su propuesta consistía en interactuar mediante voz, gestos y una proyección luminosa sobre la mano del usuario en lugar de utilizar una pantalla convencional. Sin embargo, el producto no logró convencer al mercado y fue retirado menos de un año después de su lanzamiento tras la adquisición de gran parte de la empresa por HP. Su fracaso, no obstante, no ha frenado la búsqueda de alternativas.
Los altavoces inteligentes son el caso más evidente de que es posible usar un dispositivo sin pantalla y no echarla de menos. El Amazon Echo Dot, el Apple HomePod Mini o el Google Nest Mini funcionan principalmente mediante voz y han normalizado la idea de que una interfaz puede ser invisible. De hecho, millones de usuarios se han acostumbrado a pedir música, consultar el tiempo o controlar dispositivos domésticos simplemente hablando.
De forma similar funcionan los auriculares inteligentes provistos de asistentes integrados o las gafas inteligentes. En estos productos, el usuario recibe información directamente por audio sin necesidad de tener que sacar el teléfono del bolsillo. En las últimas semanas, además, hemos visto que firmas como Fitbit han renovado su catálogo con una pulsera de actividad —Fitbit Air— con un diseño que pasa totalmente desapercibido (y sin pantalla, por supuesto) a la vez que registra todo tipo de métricas. También destaca la ēllu band, una pulsera especialmente indicada para niños y adolescentes que integra localización en tiempo real, avisos y funciones de seguridad; o Amazfit Helio Strap, un entrenador deportivo diseñado para conseguir objetivos de entrenamiento y mejorar en la recuperación.
En el ámbito doméstico, sensores, termostatos, cerraduras inteligentes o asistentes para el hogar conectado funcionan cada vez más de forma automática, sin requerir una pantalla propia. La tecnología se integra en el entorno y desaparece de la vista.
Las ventajas (y las que no lo son tanto)
La principal promesa de estos dispositivos es reducir la dependencia visual. En teoría, permiten acceder a información o realizar acciones sin interrumpir una conversación, una caminata o cualquier otra actividad cotidiana. También pueden simplificar el uso de la tecnología. Hablar suele ser más rápido que navegar por varias aplicaciones cuando se trata de tareas sencillas como consultar una cita, encender una luz o reproducir una canción. Además, algunos diseñadores consideran que estos equipos ayudan a combatir la llamada “economía de la atención”, un modelo en el que las aplicaciones compiten constantemente por captar la mirada del usuario.
Pero eliminar la pantalla también implica renuncias. Las interfaces visuales siguen siendo extremadamente eficientes para mostrar grandes cantidades de información, comparar opciones o realizar tareas complejas. Y la privacidad es otro desafío importante. Al basarse en micrófonos y procesamiento de voz, estos dispositivos generan preguntas sobre la recopilación y tratamiento de datos personales. Tanto es así que diversos estudios académicos han analizado riesgos potenciales relacionados con el tráfico de datos, la elaboración de perfiles de usuario y la seguridad de las interacciones por voz.
¿Un futuro sin pantallas?
Probablemente no. La mayoría de los expertos coinciden en que las pantallas seguirán siendo imprescindibles para multitud de tareas y, por lo tanto, lo que parece más plausible es un escenario híbrido. Así, en lugar de desaparecer, podrían convertirse en un recurso secundario. La interacción cotidiana se realizaría mediante voz, inteligencia artificial o automatizaciones, mientras que la información compleja seguiría mostrándose visualmente cuando fuera necesario.

articles.text:
O Brasil chegou a 10,2 milhões de desenvolvedores no GitHub e se consolidou como o quarto país com mais usuários na plataforma de compartilhamento de código da Microsoft. O avanço aproxima o país da China, que soma 12,4 milhões de usuários, e pode levar os brasileiros a ultrapassar os chineses até 2030, segundo projeção do GitHub.
Os dados fazem parte do relatório Octoverse 2026, divulgado nesta quarta-feira (28). Nos últimos 12 meses, 3,28 milhões de brasileiros entraram na plataforma, o dobro do número de novos usuários chineses. Apenas Estados Unidos e Índia registraram mais novos participantes no período.
O Brasil também ocupa a quarta posição mundial em contribuições para repositórios públicos. Essas contribuições incluem os chamados pushes, quando desenvolvedores enviam alterações de código para um projeto.
Segundo o GitHub, o amadurecimento das fintechs brasileiras é um dos fatores que podem impulsionar o crescimento da comunidade de desenvolvedores no país.
IA já participa de boa parte do desenvolvimento de software
O avanço brasileiro ocorre em momento de transformação na programação. O GitHub ultrapassou 225 milhões de desenvolvedores no mundo e registrou 17,9 bilhões de pushes nos últimos 12 meses — volume superior à soma dos números de 2024 e 2025.
Parte desse crescimento está relacionada à adoção de agentes de inteligência artificial (IA), capazes de executar tarefas de desenvolvimento de software.
Em setembro, mais de 40% dos pull requests aprovados e incorporados a projetos no GitHub começaram com rascunho gerado por um agente de IA. Foram 110 milhões de solicitações desse tipo em um único mês.
Um pull request é uma proposta para incorporar alterações ao código de um projeto. O fato de uma solicitação começar com rascunho produzido por IA, porém, não significa que o código tenha sido aprovado automaticamente ou dispensado de revisão humana.
Ainda assim, os números indicam que ferramentas automatizadas estão assumindo participação crescente no processo de desenvolvimento.
TypeScript lidera avanço entre as linguagens
A expansão da IA também aparece no ranking de linguagens de programação. TypeScript, Python e JavaScript continuam nas três primeiras posições, mas o TypeScript registrou o maior crescimento absoluto da plataforma: foram 3,62 milhões de novos contribuidores mensais em um ano.
O Rust também ganhou espaço e dobrou de tamanho no período.
De acordo com o relatório, a escolha das linguagens está relacionada não apenas às preferências dos desenvolvedores, mas também à facilidade de trabalhar com código gerado por IA e verificar os resultados.
Em TypeScript, Python e Rust, os agentes de IA aparecem em 40% a 44% dos pull requests incorporados aos projetos. Em Java, C# e C++, a participação fica entre 21% e 34%.
O TypeScript também está presente em 35% dos repositórios criados em 2026 com auxílio de IA, ante 24% daqueles que não utilizam a tecnologia.
Os dados sugerem que linguagens com características favoráveis à verificação do código gerado por máquinas estão ganhando espaço nesse novo cenário.
Leia mais:
- Microsoft cancela licenças do Claude Code para desenvolvedores
- Hackers invadem GitHub e roubam milhares de dados
- Microsoft oferece demissão voluntária a cerca de 60 mil funcionários
GitHub anuncia novidades para o Copilot
Durante o GitHub Universe 2026, a empresa apresentou novos recursos para o Copilot, seu conjunto de ferramentas de IA voltadas ao desenvolvimento de software.
Entre os anúncios estão:
- GitHub Copilot: aplicativo para acompanhar diferentes etapas do trabalho em um único lugar, reunindo agentes e ferramentas;
- Copilot Fusion: seleciona automaticamente o modelo de IA mais adequado para cada tarefa;
- Copilot Projects: permite coordenar trabalhos que envolvem vários repositórios;
- Copilot Code Review Max: voltado a revisões mais aprofundadas de código.
A proposta do Fusion acompanha comportamento já observado entre os usuários: 61% dos clientes do Copilot alternam entre mais de um modelo de IA durante a mesma sessão. A ideia é combinar modelos mais potentes, voltados ao raciocínio, com opções mais leves para tarefas rápidas.
Outra mudança envolve a cobrança dos recursos de IA para clientes do GitHub Enterprise. Eles passarão a acessar as novas funcionalidades sem precisar de uma assinatura separada, pagando de acordo com os créditos de IA consumidos.
Na prática, o custo ficará mais diretamente ligado ao uso dos agentes. Quanto maior o consumo de recursos de IA, maior poderá ser a cobrança.
Microsoft amplia infraestrutura para acompanhar a demanda
Para sustentar o crescimento da plataforma e o uso de ferramentas de IA, o GitHub adicionou, em 2026, quatro milhões de núcleos de processamento, 160 petabytes de armazenamento de alta velocidade e 50 terabits por segundo de capacidade de rede.
A empresa também está migrando para uma arquitetura distribuída em várias regiões da nuvem Azure, da Microsoft. A conclusão dessa transição está prevista para o início de 2027.
A infraestrutura é parte importante da estratégia para atender à expansão do número de desenvolvedores e às novas cargas de trabalho provocadas pelos agentes de IA.
GitHub está mudando a forma de programar
Adquirido pela Microsoft em 2018, o GitHub ocupa posição central na expansão das ferramentas de IA aplicadas ao desenvolvimento de software.
Em 2021, a plataforma recebeu o Copilot, criado por Microsoft e OpenAI. A ferramenta levou recursos de IA generativa diretamente ao ambiente de programação antes de o ChatGPT popularizar a tecnologia entre o público geral, em novembro de 2022.
Agora, o avanço dos agentes aponta para nova etapa: sistemas que não apenas sugerem trechos de código, mas também participam de tarefas mais amplas de desenvolvimento.
Para o Brasil, a expansão da comunidade representa oportunidade de ganhar ainda mais espaço em uma das principais plataformas globais de programação. Ao mesmo tempo, a crescente participação da IA levanta questão sobre o futuro da atividade: quanto do código será produzido diretamente por desenvolvedores e quanto ficará a cargo das máquinas?
Rodrigo Mozelli é jornalista formado pela Universidade Metodista de São Paulo (UMESP) e, atualmente, é redator do Olhar Digital.

articles.title: Meta has a new AI pet app called Waddle World | TechCrunch
articles.text:
Continuing its fast-paced experiments with AI apps, Meta has now launched a new app called Waddle World, which essentially looks like a Tamagotchi clone, but with AI. It might be a test, but it could very well be a precursor to the company’s Tamagotchi-like gadget powered by Muse.
The company has launched Waddle World in the Philippines on both iOS and Android. The app, spotted by social media consultant Matt Navarra, lets you pick and grow a virtual pet, feed it, and play with it.
We have reached out to Meta for a comment on wider availability, and will update this piece if we hear back.
Meta’s description of the app indicates that it doesn’t want the app to be a habit builder. The company’s page also says that the app is not a chatbot, and is flagged as suitable for users older than 18.
“Waddle World is a cozy 16-bit world where your pixel pet lives. Hatch a virtual pet, visit whenever you like, and let it get to know you. No pressure, no streaks to protect, no scores to chase — just a warm little escape in the cracks of your day,” the app’s description reads.
“Not a chatbot. Not an assistant. Not a productivity tool. It’s a pet, and a place. Stay two minutes or twenty — it’ll be happy either way.”
The app also doubles as a journal, letting users describe their day through voice or text. The pet listens to the user and writes up the note in its own voice as an entry with a doodle. The app also features mini-games that you can play over a few minutes, and can send you a weekly email based on what it learned about you.
Meta may be wanting to stay away from building companion apps, given companies like Character.AI and OpenAI have faced lawsuits that allege their products caused harm to teenagers.
Until now, the social media giant has released AI-centric apps like Pocket, which lets you vibe-code games, and Vibes, which lets you quickly generate videos.
Besides virtual pets, some companies have also tried making hardware AI pets.

articles.title: Thin, Light and Built for Everything: NVIDIA RTX Spark Windows Laptops Gain New Models, Agent Tools and Games
articles.text:
NVIDIA RTX Spark powers thin and light laptops built for everything that developers, creators and gamers do.
RTX Spark laptops are now available from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI. These powerful systems combine an NVIDIA Blackwell RTX GPU and an NVIDIA Grace CPU in a single superchip with up to 128GB of unified memory and up to 1 petaflop of FP4 AI performance. That puts the NVIDIA CUDA platform, RTX graphics and the capabilities of a personal AI supercomputer inside premium Windows laptops built to go anywhere.
New and expected RTX Spark updates, coming soon, include:
- NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe, an open weight speech model for transcription, speaker attribution and translation is available on RTX Spark.
- The LFM3 family of open models with day-zero support.
- Resource management controls in NVIDIA App to allocate GPU resources between foreground apps and background agents.
- Phantom Blade Zero, S-GAME’s highly-anticipated action role-playing game, launches with ray tracing and NVIDIA DLSS 4.5.
- Experience Minecraft with path tracing and DLSS with RTX Remix1.6, available now for RTX Spark.
Turn Recorded Audio Into Useful Information With NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe
Introduced today, NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe is a new, open weight speech model that turns recorded conversations into useful information. Instead of needing multiple models for transcription, speaker labels and translation, developers can use one promptable model that handles all three, plus questions about the audio. It transcribes 40 languages, including seven Indic languages.
Developers guide the model with plain-language prompts. For example, for a single recorded meeting, users can ask it to:
- “Transcribe this recording and label each speaker.”
- “Translate this audio into English.”
- “List what decisions were made in this meeting.”
Prompts can also include product terms and formatting conventions, which helps the model handle specialized vocabulary in fields like healthcare, financial services and customer service. Because the weights are open, developers can choose where audio is processed, from a desktop to the cloud.
Nemotron 3.5 Transcribe ranks No. 1 on the Hugging Face Open ASR and No. 2 among open weight models on Artificial Analysis — delivering leading accuracy with approximately 4.3 billion active parameters, 80% fewer than the No. 1 open weight model, making high-quality, intelligent transcription more practical on local hardware.
It’s available today on Hugging Face. Quantized versions are coming soon, so developers can run Transcribe locally onNVIDIA RTX Spark and DGX Spark systems, Jetson AGX Thor devices or scale up on NVIDIA Blackwell data center GPUs. NVFP4 versions will be deployable through NeMo-Speech.cpp or vLLM.
Learn more in the NVIDIA technical blog.
Control How Agents and PC Apps Share GPU Resources
On RTX Spark, users can have long-running agents working alongside their favorite applications. Both share the system’s GPU compute, and the right balance of resources depends on what matters to users at that moment.
With the new resource management feature in NVIDIA App, users can now choose how GPU resources are shared. They can prioritize their foreground app for the best performance, or give their background-running agent more resources to get work done faster.
Access control resource sharing from System > Advanced in the NVIDIA App. This feature requires hardware-accelerated GPU scheduling to be enabled in Windows Settings.
Liquid AI: One Model Family, Many Ways to Work
Liquid AI’s LFM3 provides a new generation of Liquid Foundation Models designed for specialized tasks. The family spans text, vision, audio, omni and decision models built on one shared backbone, with base and post-trained models available as open weights. The models are compact and fast: Liquid AI’s new 1.7-billion-parameter base model outperforms its previous 2.6-billion-parameter base model.
These models support local workflows such as agents running in Hermes Agent, Pi and OpenClaw to triage inboxes and manage calendars, read documents and app screens, transcribe and translate speech, answer spoken questions about handwritten math, and route support tickets or voice requests.
Developers can run LFM3 models on RTX Spark with native support through llama.cpp and vLLM, and fine-tune the models locally.
‘Phantom Blade Zero’ Launches With DLSS 4.5
S-GAME’s Phantom Blade Zero launches tonight, Oct. 28, at 7 p.m. PT on Steam and the Epic Games Store. Players can take on the role of Soul, a swordsman framed for his master’s murder, as he travels the martial world to uncover a conspiracy.
NVIDIA worked with S-GAME Studio and S-GAME Publishing to add ray-traced effects to the title. On RTX Spark laptops and GeForce RTX GPU-powered PCs, ray tracing adds more accurate bounced lighting, detailed reflections and realistic shadows on foliage and terrain. The NVIDIA DLSS Dynamic Multi Frame Generation feature boosts frame rates with up to 6x frame generation, or adjusts the multiplier on the fly to hit a player’s target frame rate.
Read more on GeForce.com.
RTX Remix Breathes New Life Into Classics
NVIDIA RTX Remix, the modding platform for remastering classic games with path tracing and DLSS, released version 1.6 last week. This update brought RTX Remix to the world’s largest gaming community: Minecraft. Both creators and players can render Minecraft Java Edition 1.21.1 through RTX Remix with DLSS-accelerated path tracing and take full advantage of realistic lighting and materials in their future creations.
The update also adds DLSS 5 with 3D-Guided Neural Rendering, up to 6x Multi Frame Generation, native RTX Spark support and agent-assisted workflows. Starting today, those upgrades come to Portal with RTX and the Half-Life 2 RTX demo. Both now support RTX Spark, with DLSS 3D-Guided Neural Rendering for more lifelike lighting and materials, a new Performance Mode for DLSS Frame Generation and new options that speed up path tracing.
RTX Remix 1.6 also makes AI-powered modding simpler. A redesigned ComfyUI workflow lets modders generate physically based materials directly inside RTX Remix, with no application programming interface setup, batch processing for full projects and presets for less technical creators. Plus, with NVIDIA agent skills, compatible AI agents can work directly with RTX Remix to help speed up remastering projects.
Learn more in the RTX Remix blog.
RTX Spark Laptops: Beautifully Designed, Built for Everything
RTX Spark laptops come in a range of designs, so users can choose one that fits how they work and play. Options include different screen sizes, colors, touchscreens, pen support and two-in-one convertibles. RTX Spark laptops are as thin as 14mm and as light as three pounds, with all-day battery life.
Such slim designs are possible because RTX Spark places the GPU, CPU and up to 128GB of unified memory on one power-efficient superchip. Creative projects and AI models draw from the same memory pool, so a laptop can take on work that used to call for a desktop workstation, even when unplugged.
Here’s what this means for:
- AI developers: Run models and agents locally on NVIDIA CUDA — the same platform that powers AI in the cloud — with a path to deploy across more than 150 million NVIDIA RTX AI PCs and NVIDIA GPUs in the cloud.
- Creators: RTX Spark can edit camera native 4:2:2 video and render 3D scenes of up to 90GB. Adobe Photoshop and Premiere offer native RTX Spark support through beta releases.
- Gamers: Hundreds of games run on RTX Spark, with NVIDIA DLSS, ray tracing, Reflex and G-SYNC delivering sharper visuals and smoother, more responsive gameplay.
RTX Spark laptops are available now from ASUS, Dell, HP, Lenovo, Microsoft and MSI, starting at $2,599, with 128GB configurations on shelves. Find a laptop on the RTX Spark product page.
#ICYMI: More Updates From NVIDIA Local AI
🦆Microducks learn to walk with help from RTX Spark: During the GTC Berlin keynote, NVIDIA founder and CEO Jensen Huang showed how AI agents running on RTX Spark can help train Hugging Face’s Microduck robot. A new NVIDIA technical blog walks through the workflow: Hermes Agent and Nemotron 3.5 Bolt plan an obstacle course on RTX Spark, Astra builds the 3D assets, NVIDIA Isaac Lab trains the navigation policy and RTX Spark validates it in NVIDIA Isaac Sim. Watch the demo and try the playbook.
⚡NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Bolt E4B 4GB is now available, enabling natural conversations and multistep agent tasks with as little as 4GB of memory. The model powers local voice assistants, game characters and embedded interfaces on RTX Spark, DGX Spark, GeForce RTX GPUs and NVIDIA Jetson devices. It supports llama.cpp, vLLM, Ollama, Unsloth and LM Studio, and works with Hermes and OpenClaw. For more demanding agent workloads, Nemotron 3.5 Bolt 74B-A9B 24GB is designed to run local agents on RTX Spark.
🖼️Black Forest Labs’ FLUX 3 Image Klein is a 5.6-billion-parameter open weights model that lets users generate and edit images locally. NVIDIA-optimized versions run on RTX GPUs with as little as 8GB of VRAM. Developers can also fine-tune the model on RTX Spark using an NVIDIA NeMo AutoModel recipe to customize it for specific creative workflows.
🖥️NVIDIA DGX Spark 64GB is now available to purchase from manufacturer partners, giving developers and researchers another way to build and run AI locally. Powered by the GB10 Grace Blackwell Superchip, it combines 64GB of unified memory with DGX OS and the NVIDIA AI software stack for agent development, inference and fine-tuning. Learn more and explore purchase options.
Follow NVIDIA RTX Spark on X, Instagram, TikTok and Facebook — and stay informed by subscribing to the NVIDIA Local AI newsletter. Follow NVIDIA Workstation on LinkedIn and X.
